# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Overview

The model below jointly optimizes (i) **train rescheduling** (arrival/departure times, ordering, rerouting) and (ii) **speed management** (speed profiles through each block section) for a set of high-speed trains operating on a bidirectional double-track line, where a single segment is blocked during a known time window. Trains may be **rerouted** to the opposite track within the blockage window to maintain capacity, which introduces bidirectional conflicts that the model must explicitly resolve.

The model is formulated on a **discrete time–space network** with **precomputed discrete speed levels**, ensuring that all expressions are linear (or linearizable). Energy consumption and delay are simultaneously minimized.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $I$ | Set of trains, $i \in I$ |
| $J$ | Set of stations (incl. origins/destinations), $j \in J$ |
| $B$ | Set of block sections, $b \in B$ |
| $B_i^{ord} \subseteq B$ | Ordered sequence of blocks on the (original) path of train $i$ |
| $B^{dis} \subseteq B$ | Set of blocks inside the disruption area |
| $K = \{1,\dots,\bar K\}$ | Set of discrete speed levels |
| $T = \{1,\dots,H\}$ | Discrete time periods (time step $\Delta t$) |
| $\mathcal{T}^{dis} = [\tau_s,\tau_e] \cap T$ | Disruption time window |
| $D = \{F, B\}$ | Directions: $F$ = forward, $B$ = backward |
| $R_i$ | Set of feasible rerouting alternatives for train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{N}(b) = \{b-1, b+1\}$ | Adjacent blocks of $b$ (when they exist) |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $\Delta t$ | Duration of a time period | s |
| $\ell_b$ | Length of block $b$ | m |
| $L_i$ | Length of train $i$ | m |
| $v_k$ | Speed of level $k$ (with $v_1 < \dots < v_{\bar K}$) | m/s |
| $\theta_{b,k}$ | Travel time of block $b$ at speed $k$ (rounded up to integer $\Delta t$) | periods |
| $e_{b,k}$ | Energy consumed by a single train to traverse block $b$ at speed $k$ | kWh |
| $e^{acc}_{k,k'}$ | Energy for accelerating from speed $k$ to $k'$ between blocks | kWh |
| $a_{\max}, a_{\min}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration | m/s² |
| $\tau^{min}_{dwl}$ | Minimum dwell time at any station | periods |
| $\tau^{max}_{dwl}$ | Maximum dwell time at any station | periods |
| $\tau^{min}_{hdw}$ | Minimum headway between consecutive trains | periods |
| $arr^{pl}_{i,j}, dep^{pl}_{i,j}$ | Planned arrival / departure times of train $i$ at station $j$ | periods |
| $c^{delay}, c^{ene}$ | Weight of one period of delay / one kWh of energy | – |
| $c^{rer}, c^{canc}$ | Penalty for rerouting / cancelling a train | – |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) | – |
| $d_i \in D$ | Nominal running direction of train $i$ | – |

**Pre-computed quantities** (Assumption A1):
- $\theta_{b,k} = \lceil \ell_b / (v_k \Delta t) \rceil$
- $e_{b,k} = \alpha_0 + \alpha_1 v_k + \alpha_2 v_k^2$ (mechanical + aerodynamic + auxiliary, linear in $k$)
- $e^{acc}_{k,k'} = \tfrac{1}{2\eta}\, m\,(v_{k'}^2 - v_k^2)$ if $k' > k$, else $0$ (regeneration neglected — Assumption A2)

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Trajectory & routing
| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{i,b,\tau,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ **starts** traversing block $b$ at time $\tau$ at speed $k$ |
| $r_{i,b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses the **opposite** (rerouted) track on block $b$ |
| $c_{i}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is **cancelled** |

### 4.2 Track assignment (used to encode bidirectional conflicts)
| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $y^{F}_{i,b,\tau}, y^{B}_{i,b,\tau}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses the forward (resp. backward) track of block $b$ at time $\tau$ |

### 4.3 Speed transitions
| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $\sigma_{i,b,k,k'}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ exits block $b$ at speed $k$ and enters next block at speed $k'$ |

### 4.4 Timetable
| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $arr_{i,j}, dep_{i,j}$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Actual arrival / departure time of train $i$ at station $j$ |

### 4.5 Energy
| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $E_i$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Total energy consumption of train $i$ |

### 4.6 Auxiliary
| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $d_{i,j}$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $j$ |
| $D^{tot}$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Total delay |

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; c^{delay}\, D^{tot} \;+\; c^{ene}\!\sum_{i\in I} E_i \;+\; c^{rer}\!\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{b\in B} r_{i,b} \;+\; c^{canc}\!\sum_{i\in I} c_i
\tag{Obj}
$$

(Weighted sum of **total delay**, **total energy**, **rerouting actions** and **cancellations**.)

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Block-flow conservation (each train visits each block on its path exactly once)

$$
\sum_{\tau\in T}\sum_{k\in K} x_{i,b,\tau,k} \;=\; 1 - c_i, \qquad \forall i\in I,\; b\in B_i^{ord}
\tag{1a}
$$

$$
\sum_{\tau\in T}\sum_{k\in K} x_{i,b,\tau,k} \;=\; 0, \qquad \forall i\in I,\; b\notin B_i^{ord}
\tag{1b}
$$

### 6.2 Sequencing between consecutive blocks

For each train $i$ and each block $b\in B_i^{ord}\setminus\{\text{last block}\}$:

$$
\sum_{\tau\in T}\sum_{k\in K} \tau\, x_{i,b,\tau,k}
\;=\;
\sum_{\tau'\in T}\sum_{k'\in K} \tau'\, x_{i,b',\tau',k'}
\;-\; \sum_{k\in K}\sum_{k'\in K} \theta_{b,k}\,\sigma_{i,b,k,k'}
\;-\; \delta^{dwl}_{i,b}
\quad\forall b'\in\mathcal{N}(b)\cap B_i^{ord},\; b'<b
\tag{2}
$$

where $\delta^{dwl}_{i,b}$ is the (fixed) dwell time incurred between $b$ and the next block if $b$ ends at a station.

### 6.3 Linking speed transitions to block-traversal decisions

$$
\sum_{k'\in K}\sigma_{i,b,k,k'} \;=\; \sum_{\tau\in T} x_{i,b,\tau,k}, \qquad \forall i,b,k
\tag{3a}
$$

$$
\sum_{k\in K}\sigma_{i,b,k,k'} \;=\; \sum_{\tau\in T} x_{i,b',\tau,k'}, \qquad \forall i,b,k',\; b'\in\mathcal{N}(b)\cap B_i^{ord}
\tag{3b}
$$

### 6.4 Acceleration / deceleration feasibility

Linearized using big-M:

$$
v_{k'} - v_k \;\le\; a_{\max}\, \theta_{b,k}\,\Delta t \;+\; M(1-\sigma_{i,b,k,k'}), \qquad \forall i,b,k,k'
\tag{4a}
$$

$$
v_{k'} - v_k \;\ge\; a_{\min}\, \theta_{b,k}\,\Delta t \;-\; M(1-\sigma_{i,b,k,k'}), \qquad \forall i,b,k,k'
\tag{4b}
$$

### 6.5 Block / track occupancy (mutual exclusion)

A train starting block $b$ at $\tau$ at speed $k$ occupies it during $[\tau,\tau+\theta_{b,k}-1]$. The same train must use exactly **one** track of $b$:

$$
y^{F}_{i,b,\tau} + y^{B}_{i,b,\tau} \;=\; \sum_{k\in K} x_{i,b,\tau,k}, \qquad \forall i,b,\tau
\tag{5}
$$

For each block $b$, time $\tau$, **and each track** ($F$ and $B$):

$$
\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{k\in K}\;\sum_{t=\max(\tau-\theta_{b,k}+1,\;1)}^{\tau} y^{F}_{i,b,t}
\;\le\; 1, \qquad \forall b,\tau
\tag{6a}
$$

$$
\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{k\in K}\;\sum_{t=\max(\tau-\theta_{b,k}+1,\;1)}^{\tau} y^{B}_{i,b,t}
\;\le\; 1, \qquad \forall b,\tau
\tag{6b}
$$

### 6.6 Track-assignment default vs. rerouting

If a train does **not** use the opposite track, its track matches its direction:

$$
y^{F}_{i,b,\tau} \;\le\; \mathbb{1}_{\{d_i=F\}} \;+\; r_{i,b}, \qquad \forall i,b,\tau
\tag{7a}
$$

$$
y^{B}_{i,b,\tau} \;\le\; \mathbb{1}_{\{d_i=B\}} \;+\; r_{i,b}, \qquad \forall i,b,\tau
\tag{7b}
$$

Rerouting is only allowed within the disruption area:

$$
r_{i,b} \;=\; 0, \qquad \forall i,\; b\notin B^{dis}
\tag{8}
$$

### 6.7 Disruption (blocked segment) constraint

For the blocked block $b^{\dagger}$ (single block in the simplest case, or each block of $B^{dis}$): no train that is *not* rerouted may occupy it during $\mathcal{T}^{dis}$:

$$
\sum_{k\in K} \sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}^{dis}} x_{i,b^{\dagger},t,k} \;\le\; M\, r_{i,b^{\dagger}} \;+\; c_i,\qquad \forall i
\tag{9}
$$

(If rerouted, the train moves on the opposite track, modelled through (5)–(7).)

### 6.8 Bidirectional conflict on shared (rerouted) track

On a track used by both directions (after rerouting), trains travelling in opposite directions cannot be in the same block at the same time. Equations (6a)/(6b) already enforce single-train occupancy per track. The following constraint forbids a forward and a backward train from using the **same track of the same block** at the **same time** even at different times within a safety buffer:

$$
\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{t\in[\tau-\theta_{b,k}+1,\;\tau]} y^{F}_{i,b,t}
\;+\;
\sum_{k'\in K}\sum_{t'\in[\tau-\theta_{b,k'}+1,\;\tau]} y^{B}_{i',b,t'}
\;\le\; 1 \;+\; M\,(2 - y^{F}_{i,b,\tau} - y^{B}_{i',b,\tau}), \quad \forall i\neq i', b,\tau
\tag{10}
$$

(Collapses to (6a)/(6b) when both trains are on the same track.)

### 6.9 Station dwell

Dwell time at station $j\in J$ equals the time between exit of last block before $j$ and entry of first block after $j$:

$$
dep_{i,j} - arr_{i,j} \;\ge\; \tau^{min}_{dwl}\,(1-c_i)
\tag{11a}
$$

$$
dep_{i,j} - arr_{i,j} \;\le\; \tau^{max}_{dwl}\,(1-c_i)
\tag{11b}
$$

Linkage with block variables (omitted intermediate algebra):

$$
arr_{i,j} \;=\; \sum_{\tau\in T}\sum_{k\in K} \tau\, x_{i,b^{j-}_{i},\tau,k}
\quad\text{(time of exiting last block before station }j\text{)}
\tag{11c}
$$

$$
dep_{i,j} \;=\; \sum_{\tau\in T}\sum_{k\in K} (\tau-\theta_{b^{j+}_{i},k})\, x_{i,b^{j+}_{i},\tau,k}
\quad\text{(time of entering first block after station }j\text{)}
\tag{11d}
$$

### 6.10 Headway at stations

For any pair of trains $(i,i')$ that share station $j$ in the same direction:

$$
dep_{i,j} - dep_{i',j} \;\ge\; \tau^{min}_{hdw}\,(1-c_i)(1-c_{i'}), \quad \text{or the symmetric constraint}
\tag{12}
$$

### 6.11 Delay definition

$$
d_{i,j} \;\ge\; arr_{i,j} - arr^{pl}_{i,j} \;\ge\; 0, \qquad \forall i,j
\tag{13a}
$$

$$
D^{tot} \;=\; \sum_{i\in I}\sum_{j\in J} d_{i,j}
\tag{13b}
$$

### 6.12 Energy accumulation

$$
E_i \;=\; \underbrace{\sum_{b\in B}\sum_{\tau\in T}\sum_{k\in K} x_{i,b,\tau,k}\, e_{b,k}}_{\text{cruise energy}}
\;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{b\in B}\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{k'\in K} \sigma_{i,b,k,k'}\, e^{acc}_{k,k'}}_{\text{acceleration energy}}
\quad \forall i
\tag{14}
$$

### 6.13 Cancellation logic

If train $i$ is cancelled, it occupies no block and incurs no delay:

$$
\sum_{b,\tau,k} x_{i,b,\tau,k} \;\le\; M(1-c_i), \quad r_{i,b}\le 1-c_i,\quad \forall i,b
\tag{15a}
$$

$$
arr_{i,j}=dep_{i,j}=arr^{pl}_{i,j}=0 \quad \text{if } c_i=1
\tag{15b}
$$

(Implemented by setting $c_i$ to switch off all $i$-related terms.)

### 6.14 Boundary conditions

$$
\sum_{b\in B_i^{ord}(1)}\sum_{\tau\in T}\sum_{k\in K} x_{i,b,\tau,k} \;=\; 1-c_i, \qquad \forall i
\tag{16a}
$$

$$
\sum_{b\in B_i^{ord}(end)}\sum_{\tau\in T}\sum_{k\in K} x_{i,b,\tau,k} \;=\; 1-c_i, \qquad \forall i
\tag{16b}
$$

---

## 7. Linearization Notes

| Non-linear term | Treatment |
|---|---|
| $\sum_k \tau\,x_{i,b,\tau,k}$ | Linear (variable $\times$ parameter). |
| Acceleration bounds (4a/4b) | Linearized using big-M; alternatively introduce continuous $a_{i,t}$ and a single speed-level variable. |
| Bidirectional safety windows (10) | Indexed over time; remains linear. |
| $e_{b,k}$ (energy rate) | Pre-computed as a parameter — discretization makes it linear. |
| $e^{acc}_{k,k'}$ | Pre-computed as a parameter (a function of two indices). |
| $r_{i,b}\, x_{i,b,\tau,k}$ | Avoided by linking $r_{i,b}$ to track variables (7) instead of multiplying it with $x$. |

---

## 8. Key Assumptions

- **A1.** Time and speed are discretized; $\theta_{b,k}$ is rounded up to the next time step.
- **A2.** Regenerative braking is neglected (conservative for energy minimization); it can be added by allowing $e^{acc}_{k,k'}<0$ for $k'>k$ within bounds.
- **A3.** Trains cannot overtake within a block section; overtaking is only allowed at stations (modelled by reordering variables implicit in the path selection $x_{i,b,\tau,k}$).
- **A4.** A single contiguous segment is blocked; the model generalises naturally to multiple blocked blocks by replicating constraints (8)–(9).
- **A5.** Rerouting is only permitted within the disruption area, on the opposite-direction track.
- **A6.** Train consists are fixed (no coupling/decoupling during the horizon).
- **A7.** Dwell times are bounded but flexible within $[\tau^{min}_{dwl},\tau^{max}_{dwl}]$.
- **A8.** Turn-around and crew-rolling-stock constraints are not modelled explicitly (they can be added as side constraints).
- **A9.** Energy consumption in each block depends only on the cruise speed level $k$ (track gradient effects omitted; can be added by replacing $e_{b,k}$ with $e_{i,b,k}$).
- **A10.** Cancellation is permitted but penalised; it allows infeasibility to be avoided at the cost of $c^{canc}$.

---

## 9. Summary

The MILP above yields, in a **single optimization run**:

1. a **conflict-free rescheduled timetable** ($arr_{i,j}, dep_{i,j}$);
2. **train orders** at each block (implicit in $x_{i,b,\tau,k}$);
3. **rerouting decisions** ($r_{i,b}$);
4. **executable speed profiles** ($x_{i,b,\tau,k}$ and $\sigma_{i,b,k,k'}$);
5. a **cancellation plan** ($c_i$);

while minimising a weighted combination of total delay, total energy consumption, rerouting and cancellation penalties, and explicitly resolving bidirectional conflicts arising from rerouting through the partial segment blockage.

Based on the paper's description of the integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under partial segment blockages, I provide the following complete MILP formulation:

# MILP Model for TRSMP under Partial Segment Blockages

## Assumptions
- (A1) The railway line is double-track with bidirectional operation.
- (A2) Discretized time horizon indexed by intervals of duration Δτ.
- (A3) Trains travel between successive stations on predefined segments.
- (A4) Energy consumption follows the Davis formula (piecewise-linearized).
- (A5) Blockage windows are known and fixed in advance.

## Sets and Indices
- $T$: set of trains, indexed by $t \in T$
- $I$: set of stations, indexed by $i \in I$, with $i=0$ (origin) and $i=|I|-1$ (destination)
- $S$: set of segments between consecutive stations, indexed by $s \in S$
- $K$: set of time intervals, indexed by $k \in K$, with $k=0$ and $k=|K|-1$
- $W$: set of disruption (blockage) windows on segments, indexed by $w \in W$
- $P$: set of piecewise-linear segments for energy function, indexed by $p \in P$

## Parameters
- $L_s$: length of segment $s$ (m)
- $\Delta\tau$: length of a time interval (s)
- $v^{\max}, v^{\min}$: maximum / minimum operating speed (m/s)
- $a^{\max}, b^{\max}$: maximum traction / braking acceleration (m/s²)
- $\tau^{\text{arr}}_0(t,i), \tau^{\text{dep}}_0(t,i)$: scheduled arrival/departure time of train $t$ at station $i$ (s)
- $\theta^{\min}(i), \theta^{\max}(i)$: minimum/maximum dwell time at station $i$ (s)
- $h^{\text{sta}}(i)$: minimum station headway (s)
- $h^{\text{seg}}(s)$: minimum segment headway (s)
- $D(s,w), E(s,w)$: start and end time (interval index) of blockage window $w$ on segment $s$
- $\rho_t$: mass per unit length of train $t$ (kg/m)
- $A, B, C$: Davis formula coefficients
- $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3, \alpha_4$: objective weights
- $M$: large positive constant
- $v_p, \eta_p$: slope and intercept of linear piece $p$ for energy function

## Decision Variables

**Timing variables:**
- $a_{t,i} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$: actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $i$
- $d_{t,i} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$: actual departure time of train $t$ at station $i$

**Routing variables:**
- $r_{t,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses segment $s$ on the main (forward) track
- $r^{\text{opp}}_{t,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses segment $s$ on the opposite (reverse) track
- $x_{t,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ occupies segment $s$ during interval $k$

**Speed and position variables:**
- $v_{t,s,k} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$: speed of train $t$ on segment $s$ at interval $k$ (m/s)
- $\pi_{t,s,k} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$: position of train $t$ on segment $s$ at the end of interval $k$ (m)

**Ordering variables:**
- $y_{t,t',i} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ departs station $i$ before train $t'$
- $z_{t,t',s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ enters segment $s$ before train $t'$

**Conflict variables:**
- $c^{\text{opp}}_{t,t',s,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trains $t$ and $t'$ (opposite directions) conflict on segment $s$ in interval $k$

**Cancellation variable:**
- $\delta_t \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ is cancelled

**Energy variable:**
- $e_{t,s,k} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$: energy consumption of train $t$ on segment $s$ in interval $k$ (kWh)

---

## Objective Function

$$
\min Z = \alpha_1 \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{i \in I} \left( a_{t,i} - \tau^{\text{arr}}_0(t,i) \right)^{+} + \alpha_2 \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{i \in I} \left( \tau^{\text{dep}}_0(t,i) - d_{t,i} \right)^{+} + \alpha_3 \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \sum_{k \in K} e_{t,s,k} + \alpha_4 \sum_{t \in T} \delta_t
$$

The first two terms minimize arrival and departure delays (with $(\cdot)^+ = \max(\cdot, 0)$ linearized via auxiliary variables), the third minimizes total energy consumption, and the fourth penalizes cancellations.

---

## Constraints

### (1) Blockage Constraints on Main Track
For each disrupted segment $s$ and interval $k$ in any blockage window $w$:
$$
x_{t,s,k} = 0 \quad \forall t \in T, \forall k \in [D(s,w), E(s,w)]
$$

### (2) Routing Consistency
For each train $t$ and segment $s$:
$$
r_{t,s} + r^{\text{opp}}_{t,s} \leq 1
$$
$$
r_{t,s} + r^{\text{opp}}_{t,s} \geq 1 - \delta_t
$$
(If the train is not cancelled, it uses exactly one of the two tracks; if cancelled, both may be zero.)

### (3) Segment Occupancy
For each train $t$ and interval $k$:
$$
\sum_{s \in S} x_{t,s,k} \leq 1 - \delta_t
$$
(A non-cancelled train occupies at most one segment per interval; a cancelled train occupies none.)

### (4) Sequential Progression on Segments
For each train $t$, segment $s$, and interval $k$:
$$
x_{t,s,k+1} \leq x_{t,s,k} + (1 - r_{t,s}) + (1 - r^{\text{opp}}_{t,s}) + \delta_t
$$
$$
x_{t,s,k} + x_{t,s,k+1} \leq 1 + M(1 - r_{t,s} - r^{\text{opp}}_{t,s}) + M\delta_t
$$
(Once a train leaves a segment, it cannot return; standard linearization ensuring consecutive intervals.)

### (5) Position Dynamics
For each train $t$, segment $s$, and interval $k$:
$$
\pi_{t,s,k+1} = \pi_{t,s,k} + v_{t,s,k} \cdot \Delta\tau + M(x_{t,s,k} - 1)
$$
$$
\pi_{t,s,k+1} = \pi_{t,s,k} + M(1 - x_{t,s,k})
$$

(The first applies when the train is on segment $s$; the second when it is not.)

### (6) Speed Limits
For each train $t$, segment $s$, and interval $k$:
$$
v^{\min} \cdot x_{t,s,k} \leq v_{t,s,k} \leq v^{\max} \cdot x_{t,s,k}
$$

### (7) Acceleration and Braking Limits
For each train $t$, segment $s$, and interval $k$:
$$
v_{t,s,k+1} - v_{t,s,k} \leq a^{\max} \Delta\tau + M(1 - x_{t,s,k}) + M(1 - x_{t,s,k+1})
$$
$$
v_{t,s,k} - v_{t,s,k+1} \leq b^{\max} \Delta\tau + M(1 - x_{t,s,k}) + M(1 - x_{t,s,k+1})
$$

### (8) Segment Completion (Arrival Constraint)
For each train $t$ and segment $s$:
$$
\pi_{t,s,|K|-1} \geq L_s \cdot r_{t,s} + L_s \cdot r^{\text{opp}}_{t,s} - M\delta_t
$$

### (9) Inter-Station Travel Time Linkage
For each train $t$ and station $i \in I \setminus \{0\}$:
$$
a_{t,i} = d_{t,i-1} + \sum_{s \in S} \sum_{k \in K} \Delta\tau \cdot x_{t,s,k} \cdot \mathbb{1}[\text{segment } s \text{ between } i{-}1, i]
$$
(Linearized using auxiliary variables representing the running time on segment $s$.)

### (10) Dwell Time Constraints
For each train $t$ and station $i \in I \setminus \{0, |I|-1\}$:
$$
d_{t,i} - a_{t,i} \geq \theta^{\min}(i) - M\delta_t
$$
$$
d_{t,i} - a_{t,i} \leq \theta^{\max}(i) + M\delta_t
$$

### (11) Station Departure Ordering
For each pair of trains $t, t' \in T$ and station $i$:
$$
d_{t,i} + h^{\text{sta}}(i) \leq d_{t',i} + M(1 - y_{t,t',i}) + M\delta_t + M\delta_{t'}
$$
$$
d_{t',i} + h^{\text{sta}}(i) \leq d_{t,i} + M \cdot y_{t,t',i} + M\delta_t + M\delta_{t'}
$$

### (12) Segment Entry Ordering
For each pair of trains $t, t'$ sharing segment $s$:
$$
\sum_{k \in K} k \cdot x_{t,s,k} + h^{\text{seg}}(s) \leq \sum_{k \in K} k \cdot x_{t',s,k} + M(1 - z_{t,t',s}) + M\delta_t + M\delta_{t'}
$$

### (13) Bidirectional Conflict on Opposite Track
For each pair of trains $t, t'$ traveling in opposite directions on segment $s$ during interval $k$:
$$
x_{t,s,k} + x_{t',s,k} \leq 1 + c^{\text{opp}}_{t,t',s,k} + M(1 - r^{\text{opp}}_{t,s}) + M(1 - r^{\text{opp}}_{t',s})
$$
(Conflicts on opposite tracks allowed only with strict separation; otherwise prohibited.)

### (14) Cancellation Linkage
For each train $t$:
$$
\delta_t \leq M \cdot \left( 1 - \sum_{s \in S} r_{t,s} \right)
$$
If a train uses no segments, it must be cancelled; if cancelled, all segment variables and timing variables are deactivated via big-M terms.

### (15) Energy Consumption (Davis Formula Linearization)
For each train $t$, segment $s$, and interval $k$:
$$
e_{t,s,k} \geq \rho_t \cdot v_{t,s,k} \cdot \Delta\tau \cdot \eta_p + \rho_t \cdot v_p \cdot v_{t,s,k} \cdot \Delta\tau - M(1 - \lambda_{t,s,k,p}) \quad \forall p \in P
$$
$$
\sum_{p \in P} \lambda_{t,s,k,p} = x_{t,s,k}, \quad \lambda_{t,s,k,p} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
e_{t,s,k} \geq 0
$$
(Piecewise-linear approximation of $e = \rho \cdot v \cdot \Delta\tau \cdot (A + Bv + Cv^2)$.)

### (16) Initial Conditions
For each train $t$ and origin station $i=0$:
$$
a_{t,0} = \tau^{\text{arr}}_0(t,0), \quad d_{t,0} = \tau^{\text{dep}}_0(t,0)
$$

### (17) Terminal Conditions
For each train $t$ and destination station $i = |I|-1$:
$$
d_{t,|I|-1} = a_{t,|I|-1} + M\delta_t
$$

### (18) Ordering Transitivity
For each pair $t, t' \in T$:
$$
y_{t,t',i} + y_{t',t,i} = 1 - \delta_t - \delta_{t'}
$$

### (19) Variable Domains
$$
\begin{aligned}
& a_{t,i}, d_{t,i} \geq 0, \quad v_{t,s,k}, \pi_{t,s,k} \geq 0, \quad e_{t,s,k} \geq 0 \\
& r_{t,s}, r^{\text{opp}}_{t,s}, x_{t,s,k}, y_{t,t',i}, z_{t,t',s}, c^{\text{opp}}_{t,t',s,k}, \delta_t \in \{0,1\} \\
& \lambda_{t,s,k,p} \in \{0,1\}, \quad v_{t,s,k}, \pi_{t,s,k} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}
\end{aligned}
$$

---

## Summary of Decision Variables

| Variable | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| $a_{t,i}, d_{t,i}$ | Arrival/departure times |
| $r_{t,s}, r^{\text{opp}}_{t,s}$ | Main/opposite track selection |
| $x_{t,s,k}$ | Segment-time occupancy |
| $v_{t,s,k}$ | Speed profile |
| $\pi_{t,s,k}$ | Train position |
| $y_{t,t',i}, z_{t,t',s}$ | Train ordering at stations/segments |
| $c^{\text{opp}}_{t,t',s,k}$ | Bidirectional conflict indicator |
| $\delta_t$ | Cancellation |
| $e_{t,s,k}$ | Energy consumption |
| $\lambda_{t,s,k,p}$ | Piecewise-linear selection (SOS2 set) |

The complete MILP jointly determines the rescheduled timetable (timing, ordering, rerouting, cancellation) and the executable speed profiles, while minimizing a weighted combination of total delay, energy consumption, and service cancellations under the partial-segment-blockage disruption.

Text:
# MILP Formulation for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem Description and Modeling Assumptions

**Setting.** A single high-speed railway corridor connects stations $S=\{1,2,\dots,|S|\}$ along a bidirectional line. Each consecutive pair of stations is separated by a block section $b\in B$; both travel directions (up, down) own a dedicated track. A *partial blockage* disrupts one track of one block section $b^{\ast}$ on direction $d^{\ast}\in\{U,D\}$ during the time window $[T^{\mathrm{dis}}_s,T^{\mathrm{dis}}_e]$. Trains travelling in direction $d^{\ast}$ may be *rerouted* onto the opposite (otherwise unused) track inside $b^{\ast}$ during the disruption window, which forces bidirectional conflict resolution.

**Decisions co-optimized.** (i) Arrival and departure times at every station (retiming); (ii) train ordering on each block section (reordering); (iii) whether a disrupted train uses the opposite track (rerouting); (iv) the continuous speed trajectory of every train (speed management); (v) the resulting tractive-energy consumption.

**Assumptions (marked as such when stated implicitly in the source).**
- **A1.** Trains are homogeneous in traction/braking characteristics (one vehicle type); parameters can be made train-specific by index $i$ if needed.
- **A2.** Dwell time is bounded: $d^{\min}_s\le d_{i,s}\le d^{\max}_s$.
- **A3.** Minimum headway $h$ is required between any two trains occupying the same block section, in either direction.
- **A4.** Speed profiles are discretized on a uniform time grid with step $\Delta t$; position and speed are tracked per train, per block, per time step.
- **A5.** Resistance follows the Davis equation $R(v)=a+bv+cv^{2}$; aerodynamic term is linearized piecewise (see §7). Tractive effort is bounded by a piecewise-linear power diagram.
- **A6.** Rerouting is permitted **only** inside the affected block section $b^{\ast}$ and **only** during the disruption window $[T^{\mathrm{dis}}_s,T^{\mathrm{dis}}_e]$.
- **A7.** No service cancellation is allowed (penalty term can be added if required).
- **A8.** The timetable horizon is finite, $t\in\mathcal{T}=\{0,\Delta t,2\Delta t,\dots,T^{\max}\}$.

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $I$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i,j$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $B$ | Set of block sections, indexed by $b$ |
| $B^{\mathrm{dis}}\subseteq B$ | Disrupted block section (here, $|B^{\mathrm{dis}}|=1$, element $b^{\ast}$) |
| $D=\{U,D\}$ | Travel directions (Up / Down) |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Discrete time grid, $t\in\mathcal{T}$ |
| $K$ | Pieces of the piecewise-linear tractive-force diagram, $k\in K$ |
| $V$ | Breakpoints of the piecewise-linear resistance curve, $v\in V$ |

For each train $i$, let $s_i^{\mathrm{o}},s_i^{\mathrm{d}}$ denote its origin and destination; let $\pi_i\in\{U,D\}$ be its direction. Define $S_i=\{s_i^{\mathrm{o}},\dots,s_i^{\mathrm{d}}\}$ as the ordered stations visited by $i$ and $B_i$ the ordered blocks traversed.

## 3. Parameters

**Train data.**
- $L_i$ – length (m); $m_i$ – mass (t); $\xi_i$ – rotating-mass factor; $\eta_i$ – drivetrain efficiency.
- $P^{\max}_i$ – maximum traction power (kW); $F^{\max}_i$ – maximum tractive effort (kN).
- $a_i,b_i,c_i$ – Davis resistance coefficients (kN, kN/(km/h), kN/(km/h)$^2$).
- $T^{\mathrm{pl}}_{i,s}$ – planned arrival/departure time of $i$ at $s$.

**Network data.**
- $\ell_b$ – length of block $b$ (m).
- $v^{\max}_b$ – speed limit on block $b$ (km/h).
- $h$ – minimum block headway (s); $h^{\mathrm{stn}}$ – station headway (s).

**Station data.**
- $d^{\min}_s,d^{\max}_s$ – minimum and maximum dwell time at $s$.

**Disruption data.**
- $b^{\ast}$ – disrupted block; $d^{\ast}$ – affected direction.
- $T^{\mathrm{dis}}_s,T^{\mathrm{dis}}_e$ – disruption start / end (s).

**Numerical.**
- $\Delta t$ – trajectory time step; $M$ – a sufficiently large constant (big-M).
- $w^{\mathrm{del}},w^{\mathrm{en}}$ – weights of delay and energy in the objective.

## 4. Decision Variables

**Scheduling (continuous).**
- $a_{i,s}$ – actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $d_{i,s}$ – actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $\tau_{i,b}$ – running time of train $i$ on block $b$.
- $\delta_{i,s}=a_{i,s}-T^{\mathrm{pl}}_{i,s}$ – arrival delay at station $s$ (positive part handled by $\delta^+_{i,s},\delta^-_{i,s}$).

**Rerouting (binary).**
- $r_{i,b}\in\{0,1\}$ – 1 if train $i$ uses the *opposite* track on block $b$; 0 otherwise.

**Ordering (binary).**
- $z_{i,j,b}\in\{0,1\}$ – 1 if, on block $b$, train $i$ enters before train $j$ (both use the same track on $b$).
- $\bar z_{i,j,b}\in\{0,1\}$ – analogous ordering variable for opposite-direction trains sharing the track on $b$ (only relevant when at least one is rerouted).

**Trajectory (continuous, indexed per time step).**
- $v_{i,b,t}$ – speed (m/s) of train $i$ on block $b$ at step $t$.
- $p_{i,b,t}$ – front position (m) of train $i$ on block $b$ at step $t$.
- $f_{i,b,t}$ – tractive effort (kN); $b_{i,b,t}$ – braking effort (kN).
- $e_{i,b,t}$ – incremental energy (kWh) consumed by train $i$ on block $b$ during $[t,t+\Delta t]$.
- $E_i$ – total energy of train $i$ over the horizon.

**Auxiliary (continuous).**
- $w^+_{i,b,t},w^-_{i,b,t}\in\{0,1\}$ – SOS1 pair selecting the operating point on the piecewise-linear force–speed diagram.
- $\theta_{i,s}$ – slack absorbing acceleration feasibility at station departure (≥0).

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min\; w^{\mathrm{del}}\!\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S_i}\delta^+_{i,s}
\;+\; w^{\mathrm{en}}\!\sum_{i\in I}E_i
\;+\; \epsilon\!\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S_i}\delta^-_{i,s}
\;+\; w^{\mathrm{rer}}\!\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{b\in B_i}r_{i,b} \tag{5.0}
$$

with the delay decomposition $\delta_{i,s}=\delta^+_{i,s}-\delta^-_{i,s}$, $\delta^+_{i,s},\delta^-_{i,s}\ge0$, and $\epsilon\ll w^{\mathrm{del}}$ (early-arrival penalty; often zero).

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Timetable structure

For every train $i\in I$, every station $s\in S_i$ with successor $s^{+}$ (and predecessor $s^{-}$ when applicable):

$$
d_{i,s}-a_{i,s}\ge d^{\min}_s,\qquad d_{i,s}-a_{i,s}\le d^{\max}_s, \tag{6.1a}
$$
$$
a_{i,s^{+}}=d_{i,s}+\tau_{i,b(s,s^{+})}, \tag{6.1b}
$$
$$
a_{i,s}-T^{\mathrm{pl}}_{i,s}=\delta^+_{i,s}-\delta^-_{i,s},\quad \delta^+_{i,s},\delta^-_{i,s}\ge0, \tag{6.1c}
$$
$$
a_{i,s}\ge T^{\mathrm{pl}}_{i,s},\qquad d_{i,s}\ge a_{i,s}. \tag{6.1d}
$$

(Equation 6.1d forbids early departures; if early arrivals are permitted, replace the first inequality.)

### 6.2 Running-time / speed-profile coupling

Running time must be consistent with the trajectory through block $b$:

$$
\tau_{i,b}\;\ge\;\frac{\ell_b}{v_{i,b,t}+\epsilon_v}+\frac{(v_{i,b,t}-v_{i,b,t+\Delta t})^{+}}{a^{\max}_i}-\theta_{i,b},\quad \forall i,b,t. \tag{6.2}
$$

Equivalently (and more standard in the literature), link exit time to position:

$$
a_{i,s^{+}}-d_{i,s}\;\ge\;\frac{\ell_b+L_i}{v^{\min}_b}\cdot\mathbb{1}\{v_{i,b,\cdot}\ge v^{\min}_b\}+ \text{(braking safety)}, \tag{6.2'}
$$

which is enforced via the big-M tightening in §6.3.

### 6.3 Block occupancy and headway (same direction, same track)

For each block $b$, each pair of trains $i,j\in I$ using block $b$ on their *normal* track in the same direction ($\pi_i=\pi_j$, $r_{i,b}=r_{j,b}=0$), let $s_b^{+}(i)$ be the station at the exit of $b$ for train $i$:

$$
a_{j,s_b^{+}(i)} \;\ge\; a_{i,s_b^{+}(i)} + \tau_{i,b} + h - M\,z_{i,j,b}, \tag{6.3a}
$$
$$
a_{i,s_b^{+}(i)} \;\ge\; a_{j,s_b^{+}(i)} + \tau_{j,b} + h - M\,(1-z_{i,j,b}), \tag{6.3b}
$$
$$
z_{i,j,b}+z_{j,i,b}=1,\quad z_{i,j,b}\in\{0,1\}. \tag{6.3c}
$$

### 6.4 Bidirectional conflicts (rerouting)

When train $i$ reroutes ($r_{i,b}=1$), it shares the track of the opposite direction with trains $j$ travelling in the opposite direction ($\pi_j\neq\pi_i$) that are *not* rerouted. For each such pair and each block $b\in B^{\mathrm{dis}}$:

$$
r_{i,b}+r_{j,b}\le 1+\bar z_{i,j,b}+\bar z_{j,i,b}, \tag{6.4a}
$$
$$
a_{j,s_b^{+}(j)} \;\ge\; a_{i,s_b^{+}(i)} + \tau_{i,b} + h - M\,\bar z_{i,j,b}, \tag{6.4b}
$$
$$
a_{i,s_b^{+}(i)} \;\ge\; a_{j,s_b^{+}(j)} + \tau_{j,b} + h - M\,\bar z_{j,i,b}. \tag{6.4c}
$$

For non-disrupted blocks, bidirectional trains are on different physical tracks so no conflict arises.

### 6.5 Rerouting feasibility

Only trains whose direction equals the disrupted direction may reroute, and only on $b^{\ast}$ during the disruption window:

$$
r_{i,b}=0,\quad \forall i\in I,\; b\in B\setminus\{b^{\ast}\}. \tag{6.5a}
$$
$$
r_{i,b^{\ast}}=0,\quad \forall i:\pi_i\neq d^{\ast}. \tag{6.5b}
$$

If a train reroutes, its occupation of $b^{\ast}$ must lie entirely inside the disruption window; otherwise the train must use the normal track of $b^{\ast}$ *outside* the window. Let $A_{i,b^{\ast}}=a_{i,s_b^{-}(i)}$ and $L_{i,b^{\ast}}=A_{i,b^{\ast}}+\tau_{i,b^{\ast}}$ be the entry and exit times on $b^{\ast}$:

$$
A_{i,b^{\ast}}\ge T^{\mathrm{dis}}_s - M(1-r_{i,b^{\ast}}),\qquad
L_{i,b^{\ast}}\le T^{\mathrm{dis}}_e + M(1-r_{i,b^{\ast}}). \tag{6.5c}
$$
$$
r_{i,b^{\ast}}\le \mathbb{1}\{A_{i,b^{\ast}}\ge T^{\mathrm{dis}}_s\}\;\;\text{(enforced by 6.5c together with $A_{i,b^{\ast}}\ge T^{\mathrm{dis}}_s\,r_{i,b^{\ast}}$)}. \tag{6.5d}
$$

### 6.6 Trajectory kinematics

For every $i\in I$, $b\in B_i$, $t\in\mathcal{T}$:

$$
p_{i,b,t+\Delta t} \;=\; p_{i,b,t} + v_{i,b,t}\,\Delta t, \tag{6.6a}
$$
$$
v_{i,b,t+\Delta t} \;=\; v_{i,b,t} + \frac{f_{i,b,t}-b_{i,b,t}-R(v_{i,b,t})}{m_i\,\xi_i}\,\Delta t, \tag{6.6b}
$$
$$
0\;\le\; v_{i,b,t}\;\le\; v^{\max}_b, \tag{6.6c}
$$
$$
0\;\le\; f_{i,b,t}\;\le\; F^{\max}_i,\qquad 0\le b_{i,b,t}\le B^{\max}_i. \tag{6.6d}
$$
$$
0\le p_{i,b,t}\le \ell_b,\qquad p_{i,b,0}=0,\quad p_{i,b,T_b}=\ell_b. \tag{6.6e}
$$

(Here $T_b$ denotes the last trajectory step inside block $b$; boundary conditions couple to $a_{i,s},d_{i,s}$ through 6.1.)

### 6.7 Resistance and tractive-power linearization (Davis + PL power diagram)

Resistance $R(v)=a_i+b_i v + c_i v^{2}$ is linearized using $|V|-1$ pieces on $v\in[0,v^{\max}]$, with coefficients $(\alpha_{i,v},\beta_{i,v})$ so that $R(v)\approx \alpha_{i,v}+\beta_{i,v}v$ on piece $v$. Let $\lambda^{R}_{i,b,t,v}\in[0,1]$, $\sum_v\lambda^{R}_{i,b,t,v}=1$ (SOS2), give the convex combination:

$$
R(v_{i,b,t}) \;=\; \sum_{v\in V}\lambda^{R}_{i,b,t,v}\,(\alpha_{i,v}+\beta_{i,v}\,v_{i,b,t}). \tag{6.7a}
$$
$$
v_{i,b,t} \;=\; \sum_{v\in V}\lambda^{R}_{i,b,t,v}\,\bar v_v. \tag{6.7b}
$$

The maximum admissible tractive effort is the lower envelope of the force limit $F^{\max}_i$ and the power limit $P^{\max}_i/v$:

$$
f_{i,b,t}\le F^{\max}_i,\qquad f_{i,b,t}\,v_{i,b,t}\le P^{\max}_i. \tag{6.7c}
$$

The second inequality is linearized through pieces $(\gamma_{i,k},\delta_{i,k})$ of the curve $P^{\max}_i/v$ with $\lambda^{P}_{i,b,t,k}$ (SOS2):

$$
f_{i,b,t}=\sum_{k\in K}\lambda^{P}_{i,b,t,k}\,\gamma_{i,k},\quad
v_{i,b,t}=\sum_{k\in K}\lambda^{P}_{i,b,t,k}\,\bar v_k,\quad
\sum_{k\in K}\lambda^{P}_{i,b,t,k}=1. \tag{6.7d}
$$

### 6.8 Energy accounting

$$
e_{i,b,t}\;=\;\frac{f_{i,b,t}\,v_{i,b,t}}{3.6\,\eta_i}\,\Delta t, \tag{6.8a}
$$

(linearization of the bilinear product $f\cdot v$ via the same $\lambda^{P}$ already introduced: $e_{i,b,t}=\frac{\Delta t}{3.6\eta_i}\sum_{k}\lambda^{P}_{i,b,t,k}\,\gamma_{i,k}\,\bar v_k$).

$$
E_i \;=\; \sum_{b\in B_i}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}} e_{i,b,t}. \tag{6.8b}
$$

(Regenerative braking credit can be included by allowing $e_{i,b,t}$ to be negative whenever $b_{i,b,t}>0$ with a recovery factor $\eta^{\mathrm{reg}}$.)

### 6.9 Station capacity

For each station $s$ and time $t$, the number of arriving and departing trains is bounded by a capacity $C_s$; equivalently, a minimum platform headway $h^{\mathrm{stn}}$ is enforced:

$$
|a_{i,s}-a_{j,s}|\ge h^{\mathrm{stn}},\quad \forall i\neq j \text{ arriving at } s. \tag{6.9}
$$

(Implemented via the standard big-M ordering variables as in (6.3).)

### 6.10 Speed at station boundaries and dwell consistency

Trains must reach speed $v^{\mathrm{dwell}}_s\le v^{\max}_{b(s^-)} \cap v^{\max}_{b(s^+)}$ when entering/leaving a station:

$$
v_{i,b(s^{-},s),T_{b(s^{-},s)}}=v^{\mathrm{arr}}_s,\qquad
v_{i,b(s,s^{+}),0}=v^{\mathrm{dep}}_s, \tag{6.10a}
$$
$$
\frac12 m_i\bigl((v^{\mathrm{dep}}_s)^{2}-(v^{\mathrm{arr}}_s)^{2}\bigr) \;=\; m_i g \cdot \mathrm{slope}(s)\cdot d_s + \theta_{i,s}, \quad \theta_{i,s}\ge 0. \tag{6.10b}
$$

(6.10b is a relaxed energy-balance condition that becomes exact when $\theta_{i,s}=0$; this couples dwell behaviour to speed-management feasibility.)

### 6.11 Anti–deadlock / feasibility of rerouting

To guarantee that a rerouted train can physically find a slot on the opposite track:

$$
r_{i,b^{\ast}} \;\le\; 1-\!\!\sum_{j:\pi_j\neq \pi_i,\,r_{j,b^{\ast}}=1}\!\!\bar z_{i,j,b^{\ast}}.\,\frac{\tau_{j,b^{\ast}}}{\tau^{\max}_{b^{\ast}}}, \quad\text{(optional tightening)}. \tag{6.11}
$$

(In practice this is implicitly enforced by 6.4 and the headway constraints; this auxiliary constraint merely accelerates the LP relaxation.)

## 7. Linearization Notes

| Nonlinearity | Treatment |
|---|---|
| $v^{2}$ in Davis resistance | Piecewise linear (SOS2) over $V$, (6.7a–b). |
| $f\cdot v$ in power & energy | Joint piecewise linearization (SOS2) over $K$, (6.7d), (6.8a). |
| Disjunctive headway / ordering | Standard big-M with binary ordering $z,\bar z$, (6.3)–(6.4). |
| Track choice for rerouting | Binary $r_{i,b}$ linked to direction $d^{\ast}$, (6.5). |
| Continuous $a_{i,s}$ vs. discrete trajectory | Coupled via $A_{i,b}=a_{i,s_b^{-}(i)}$ and $L_{i,b}=a_{i,s_b^{+}(i)}$ in (6.2'). |
| Auxiliary $\theta_{i,s}$ | Linear slack, $\ge 0$, used in (6.10b). |

## 8. Compact Model Summary

$$
\min\;(5.0)
$$
$$
\text{s.t.}\; (6.1)\text{–}(6.11).
$$

The model is a **mixed-integer linear program**: binary decisions are $r_{i,b},z_{i,j,b},\bar z_{i,j,b},w^{+}_{i,b,t},w^{-}_{i,b,t}$ (and the SOS2 indicators $\lambda^{R},\lambda^{P}$); all remaining variables are continuous. With a sufficiently fine time discretization $\Delta t$ and dense piecewise-linear envelopes for the traction diagram and resistance, the continuous relaxation of (6.6)–(6.8) provides an accurate proxy of the underlying nonlinear train dynamics, so the resulting **timing, ordering, rerouting and speed-profile decisions** are simultaneously conflict-free, executable by the train control system and near-optimal in the chosen weighted (delay + energy + rerouting) sense.

**Remarks on assumptions that can be relaxed without altering the structure.**
- Train heterogeneity: introduce index $i$ in every parameter; no extra variables needed.
- Multiple disrupted blocks: $B^{\mathrm{dis}}>1$ generalises (6.4)–(6.5) directly.
- Service cancellation: add binary $c_i\in\{0,1\}$ with a large penalty in (5.0) and a constraint $c_i=1\Rightarrow$ no trajectory variables.
- Bidirectional corridor on both tracks: replace the indicator "rerouted" by two binary track-assignment variables per $(i,b)$.

Text:
# MILP Formulation for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$, ordered $1, 2, \ldots, n_S$ |
| $K$ | Set of segments, indexed by $k$, where segment $k$ connects station $s$ to $s+1$ |
| $R$ | Set of discrete speed profile alternatives, indexed by $r$ |
| $k_d$ | Index of the disrupted segment (assumption: a single disrupted segment) |
| $s_d$ | Upstream station of segment $k_d$ |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s}^{sched}, d_{i,s}^{sched}$ | Scheduled arrival and departure times of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $RT_{i,k,r}$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $k$ using speed profile $r$ |
| $E_{i,k,r}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $k$ using speed profile $r$ |
| $DT_{i,s}^{\min}, DT_{i,s}^{\max}$ | Minimum and maximum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $H^{seg}$ | Minimum headway time between two consecutive trains on the same track of a segment |
| $H^{sta}$ | Minimum headway time between two trains at a station |
| $W_i$ | Cancellation penalty for train $i$ |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Weights for total delay, energy consumption, and cancellation |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (Big-M) |
| $B^{start}, B^{end}$ | Start and end times of the blockage window on the up-track of segment $k_d$ |

**Assumptions:**
- A single partial blockage occurs on the up-track of segment $k_d$ during $[B^{start}, B^{end}]$.
- Trains normally operate on the up-track; rerouting to the down-track is permitted only on segment $k_d$.
- All trains share the same nominal direction (up-direction); rerouted down-track trains may conflict with each other and with any down-direction trains (assumption: bidirectional traffic exists, modeled symmetrically).
- Speed profiles are discretized into a finite set $R$ per train per segment.
- The first station is the origin and the last station is the destination; dwell at terminals is zero.

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\delta^{a}_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Arrival delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\delta^{d}_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Departure delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $x_{i,k,r}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $r$ on segment $k$ |
| $v_{i,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $k$ |
| $z_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $y_{i,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses the up-track on segment $k$; 0 if rerouted to down-track |
| $p^{up}_{i,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $k$ on the up-track |
| $p^{dn}_{i,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $k$ on the down-track |
| $o_{i,j,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $k$ (same track) |

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total delay, total energy consumption, and total cancellation penalty:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \alpha \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \left( \delta^{a}_{i,s} + \delta^{d}_{i,s} \right) \;+\; \beta \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{k \in K} \sum_{r \in R} E_{i,k,r}\, x_{i,k,r} \;+\; \gamma \sum_{i \in T} W_i\, z_i
$$

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Delay Definitions

$$
\delta^{a}_{i,s} \;\geq\; a_{i,s} - a_{i,s}^{sched} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

$$
\delta^{d}_{i,s} \;\geq\; d_{i,s} - d_{i,s}^{sched} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### 5.2 Dwell Time Bounds

$$
DT_{i,s}^{\min} - M z_i \;\leq\; d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \;\leq\; DT_{i,s}^{\max} + M z_i \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

(If train $i$ is cancelled, the constraint is relaxed via Big-M.)

### 5.3 Running Time Consistency (Coupling TRP and TSMP)

$$
a_{i,s+1} - d_{i,s} \;=\; \sum_{r \in R} RT_{i,k,r}\, x_{i,k,r} \quad \forall i \in T,\; k=(s,s+1) \in K
$$

### 5.4 Speed Profile Selection

$$
\sum_{r \in R} x_{i,k,r} \;=\; v_{i,k} \quad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K
$$

### 5.5 Traversal Continuity

$$
v_{i,k} \;\geq\; v_{i,k+1} \quad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K \setminus \{n_S - 1\}
$$

### 5.6 Cancellation Consistency

$$
z_i \;=\; 1 - v_{i,1} \quad \forall i \in T
$$

$$
a_{i,s} \;\leq\; M (1 - z_i) \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \;\leq\; M (1 - z_i) \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### 5.7 Track Selection

$$
y_{i,k} \;=\; 1 \quad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K \setminus \{k_d\}
$$

(Rerouting is allowed only on the disrupted segment $k_d$.)

### 5.8 Auxiliary Track Indicators

$$
p^{up}_{i,k} \;\leq\; y_{i,k}, \quad p^{up}_{i,k} \;\leq\; v_{i,k}, \quad p^{up}_{i,k} \;\geq\; y_{i,k} + v_{i,k} - 1 \quad \forall i,k
$$

$$
p^{dn}_{i,k} \;\leq\; 1 - y_{i,k}, \quad p^{dn}_{i,k} \;\leq\; v_{i,k}, \quad p^{dn}_{i,k} \;\geq\; v_{i,k} - y_{i,k} \quad \forall i,k
$$

$$
p^{up}_{i,k} + p^{dn}_{i,k} \;=\; v_{i,k} \quad \forall i,k
$$

### 5.9 Blockage Avoidance on the Up-Track of Segment $k_d$

A train using the up-track of segment $k_d$ must either complete the segment before $B^{start}$ or start it after $B^{end}$:

$$
a_{i,s_d+1} \;\leq\; B^{start} + M(1 - p^{up}_{i,k_d}) \quad \forall i \in T
$$

$$
a_{i,s_d} \;\geq\; B^{end} - M(1 - p^{up}_{i,k_d}) \quad \forall i \in T
$$

### 5.10 Segment Headway — Up-Track

For any two trains $i \neq j$ sharing the up-track of segment $k$, one must precede the other:

$$
o_{i,j,k} + o_{j,i,k} \;\geq\; p^{up}_{i,k} + p^{up}_{j,k} - 1 \quad \forall i \neq j,\; k \in K
$$

$$
a_{i,s+1} + H^{seg} \;\leq\; a_{j,s+1} + M(1 - o_{i,j,k}) + M(2 - p^{up}_{i,k} - p^{up}_{j,k}) \quad \forall i \neq j,\; k=(s,s+1)
$$

$$
d_{i,s} + H^{seg} \;\leq\; d_{j,s} + M(1 - o_{i,j,k}) + M(2 - p^{up}_{i,k} - p^{up}_{j,k}) \quad \forall i \neq j,\; k=(s,s+1)
$$

### 5.11 Segment Headway — Down-Track (Bidirectional Conflict Resolution)

Analogous constraints for trains rerouted to (or operating on) the down-track, using $p^{dn}_{i,k}$:

$$
o^{dn}_{i,j,k} + o^{dn}_{j,i,k} \;\geq\; p^{dn}_{i,k} + p^{dn}_{j,k} - 1 \quad \forall i \neq j,\; k \in K
$$

$$
a_{i,s+1} + H^{seg} \;\leq\; a_{j,s+1} + M(1 - o^{dn}_{i,j,k}) + M(2 - p^{dn}_{i,k} - p^{dn}_{j,k}) \quad \forall i \neq j,\; k=(s,s+1)
$$

$$
d_{i,s} + H^{seg} \;\leq\; d_{j,s} + M(1 - o^{dn}_{i,j,k}) + M(2 - p^{dn}_{i,k} - p^{dn}_{j,k}) \quad \forall i \neq j,\; k=(s,s+1)
$$

### 5.12 Station Headway

For any two trains $i \neq j$ at station $s$:

$$
a_{i,s} + H^{sta} \;\leq\; a_{j,s} + M(1 - o^{sta,a}_{i,j,s}) + M(2 - v_{i,k_{s-1}} - v_{j,k_{s-1}}) \quad \forall i \neq j,\; s \in S
$$

$$
d_{i,s} + H^{sta} \;\leq\; d_{j,s} + M(1 - o^{sta,d}_{i,j,s}) + M(2 - v_{i,k_s} - v_{j,k_s}) \quad \forall i \neq j,\; s \in S
$$

where $k_{s-1}$ and $k_s$ are the segments immediately upstream and downstream of station $s$, and $o^{sta,a}_{i,j,s}, o^{sta,d}_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}$ are station ordering variables.

### 5.13 Terminal Station Constraints

$$
a_{i,1} = d_{i,1}, \quad a_{i,1} \geq a_{i,1}^{sched} - M z_i \quad \forall i \in T
$$

$$
a_{i,n_S} \leq a_{i,n_S}^{sched} + M(1 - z_i) + \Delta^{\max} \quad \forall i \in T
$$

where $\Delta^{\max}$ is a maximum allowable terminal delay (assumption: a reasonable horizon bound).

### 5.14 Variable Domains

$$
a_{i,s},\, d_{i,s},\, \delta^{a}_{i,s},\, \delta^{d}_{i,s} \;\geq\; 0; \quad x_{i,k,r},\, v_{i,k},\, z_i,\, y_{i,k},\, p^{up}_{i,k},\, p^{dn}_{i,k},\, o_{i,j,k},\, o^{dn}_{i,j,k},\, o^{sta,a}_{i,j,s},\, o^{sta,d}_{i,j,s} \;\in\; \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Summary of Model Features

- **Integrated TRP + TSMP:** Constraint (5.3) couples the timetable (arrival/departure times) with the chosen speed profile running times.
- **Retiming:** Variables $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}$ adjust arrival and departure times within dwell bounds (5.2).
- **Reordering:** Variables $o_{i,j,k}, o^{dn}_{i,j,k}$ determine train order on each segment and track.
- **Rerouting:** Variables $y_{i,k}$ and constraints (5.7)–(5.8) enable rerouting to the down-track on segment $k_d$.
- **Cancellation:** Variables $z_i$ and constraints (5.6) allow service cancellation.
- **Bidirectional conflict resolution:** Constraints (5.10)–(5.11) enforce headway on both up- and down-tracks.
- **Blockage feasibility:** Constraints (5.9) ensure no train occupies the disrupted up-track during $[B^{start}, B^{end}]$.
- **Energy co-optimization:** The objective includes $\beta \sum E_{i,k,r} x_{i,k,r}$, linking speed profile selection to energy use.

Text:
# Complete MILP Formulation for Passenger-Oriented Train Rescheduling with Flexible Composition and Rolling Stock Circulation

## 1. Model Overview

The model extends the passenger-oriented train scheduling framework of Liu et al. (2023a) by incorporating **(i)** time-varying sectional passenger demands approximated as piecewise-constant functions, **(ii)** flexible train composition (variable number of cars per train), and **(iii)** rolling stock circulation coupling/decoupling decisions. The formulation is designed to be solved in a rolling-horizon MPC scheme, where the prediction horizon is divided into $K$ time intervals of (possibly varying) length.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{I} = \{1,2,\dots,N_I\}$ | Set of trains indexed by $i$ (ordered by nominal departure) |
| $\mathcal{J} = \{1,2,\dots,N_J\}$ | Set of stations indexed by $j$ (1 = origin, $N_J$ = terminal) |
| $\mathcal{K} = \{1,2,\dots,N_K\}$ | Set of time intervals indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{C} = \{1,2,\dots,N_C\}$ | Set of feasible train compositions (number of cars), indexed by $c$ |
| $\mathcal{R} = \{1,2,\dots,N_R\}$ | Set of available rolling-stock units, indexed by $r$ |
| $\mathcal{J}^{\text{int}} = \{2,\dots,N_J-1\}$ | Set of intermediate stations |

---

## 3. Parameters

**Demand parameters**
- $\lambda_{j,k}$ — passenger arrival rate at station $j$ during interval $k$ (pax/min)
- $\mu_{j,k}$ — passenger alighting rate at station $j$ during interval $k$ (pax/min)
- $\Delta_k$ — duration of interval $k$ (min)
- $\tau_k^{s}, \tau_k^{e}$ — start and end times of interval $k$

**Train/operation parameters**
- $C_c$ — passenger capacity of a train with composition $c$
- $E_c$ — energy consumption rate of composition $c$ (kWh/min)
- $OC_c$ — operational cost per unit time of composition $c$
- $RC_r$ — fixed cost of deploying rolling-stock unit $r$
- $t_j^{\text{run,min}}, t_j^{\text{run,max}}$ — min/max running time on section $j$
- $t_j^{\text{dwell,min}}, t_j^{\text{dwell,max}}$ — min/max dwell time at station $j$
- $h^{\min}, h^{\max}$ — min/max headway between consecutive trains
- $t^{\text{trans}}$ — minimum transfer (coupling/decoupling) time for rolling stock
- $T_i^{\text{ready}}$ — earliest ready time of train $i$ at the origin
- $T_i^{\text{due}}$ — latest acceptable arrival time of train $i$ at the terminal
- $\bar a_{i,j}, \bar d_{i,j}$ — nominal arrival/departure times

**Big-M and weights**
- $M$ — sufficiently large positive constant
- $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3, \alpha_4 \geq 0$ — objective weights

---

## 4. Decision Variables

**Continuous variables**
- $a_{i,j}$ — arrival time of train $i$ at station $j$
- $d_{i,j}$ — departure time of train $i$ at station $j$
- $\delta_{i,j}$ — dwell time of train $i$ at station $j$
- $\rho_{i,j}$ — running time of train $i$ on section $(j, j+1)$
- $b_{i,j,k}$ — passengers boarding train $i$ at station $j$ in interval $k$
- $e_{i,j,k}$ — passengers alighting from train $i$ at station $j$ in interval $k$
- $q_{i,j}$ — number of passengers on train $i$ after departing station $j$
- $w_{i,j,k}$ — passengers waiting at station $j$ in interval $k$ who board train $i$
- $\phi_{i,j}^{+}, \phi_{i,j}^{-}$ — positive/negative deviation of $a_{i,j}$ from nominal $\bar a_{i,j}$
- $\pi_{i,j}$ — auxiliary variable equal to $q_{i,j}\cdot \rho_{i,j}$ (passenger-km proxy)
- $\eta_{i,c}$ — auxiliary variable equal to $y_{i,c}\cdot(a_{i,N_J}-a_{i,1})$
- $\sigma_{i,j,k} \in [0,1]$ — relaxation of binary indicator (see §6.6)

**Binary variables**
- $x_{i,j} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ stops at station $j$
- $y_{i,c} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ uses composition $c$
- $z_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if rolling-stock unit $r$ serves train $i$
- $v_{r,i,i'} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if rolling-stock unit $r$ transfers from train $i$ to train $i'$ ($i<i'$)
- $u_{i,r}^{\text{init}}, u_{i,r}^{\text{fin}} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if RS $r$ starts/ends its daily service with train $i$

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \alpha_1 \underbrace{\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K} w_{i,j,k}}_{\text{(a) passenger waiting time}}
\;+\; \alpha_2 \underbrace{\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\sum_{j\in\mathcal J} \pi_{i,j}}_{\text{(b) in-vehicle passenger time}}
\;+\; \alpha_3 \underbrace{\left[\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\sum_{c\in\mathcal C} OC_c\,\eta_{i,c} \;+\; \sum_{r\in\mathcal R} RC_r\,\sum_{i\in\mathcal I} u_{i,r}^{\text{init}}\right]}_{\text{(c) operational + rolling-stock cost}}
\;+\; \alpha_4 \underbrace{\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\sum_{j\in\mathcal J} \bigl(\phi_{i,j}^{+}+\phi_{i,j}^{-}\bigr)}_{\text{(d) timetable deviation}}
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Train Movement Constraints

$$
d_{i,j} = a_{i,j} + \delta_{i,j}, \quad \forall i\in\mathcal I,\; j\in\mathcal J \tag{6.1a}
$$
$$
a_{i,j+1} = d_{i,j} + \rho_{i,j}, \quad \forall i\in\mathcal I,\; j\in\mathcal J\setminus\{N_J\} \tag{6.1b}
$$
$$
t_j^{\text{run,min}} \leq \rho_{i,j} \leq t_j^{\text{run,max}}, \quad \forall i,j \tag{6.1c}
$$
$$
t_j^{\text{dwell,min}}\,x_{i,j} \leq \delta_{i,j} \leq t_j^{\text{dwell,max}}\,x_{i,j}, \quad \forall i,j \tag{6.1d}
$$

### 6.2 Stopping-Plan Constraints

$$
x_{i,1} = x_{i,N_J} = 1, \quad \forall i\in\mathcal I \tag{6.2a}
$$
$$
\sum_{j\in\mathcal J} x_{i,j} \geq J^{\min}, \quad \forall i\in\mathcal I \tag{6.2b}
$$
$$
b_{i,j,k} \leq M\,x_{i,j}, \quad e_{i,j,k} \leq M\,x_{i,j}, \quad \forall i,j,k \tag{6.2c}
$$

*(Assumption: every train must stop at the origin and terminal and at least $J^{\min}$ stations.)*

### 6.3 Headway and Time-Window Constraints

$$
h^{\min} \leq d_{i+1,j} - d_{i,j} \leq h^{\max}, \quad \forall i\in\mathcal I\setminus\{N_I\},\; j\in\mathcal J \tag{6.3a}
$$
$$
T_i^{\text{ready}} \leq a_{i,1}, \quad \forall i\in\mathcal I \tag{6.3b}
$$
$$
a_{i,N_J} \leq T_i^{\text{due}}, \quad \forall i\in\mathcal I \tag{6.3c}
$$
$$
a_{i,j} - \bar a_{i,j} = \phi_{i,j}^{+} - \phi_{i,j}^{-}, \quad \phi_{i,j}^{+},\phi_{i,j}^{-} \geq 0, \quad \forall i,j \tag{6.3d}
$$

### 6.4 Train-Composition Constraints

$$
\sum_{c\in\mathcal C} y_{i,c} = 1, \quad \forall i\in\mathcal I \tag{6.4a}
$$
$$
q_{i,j} \leq \sum_{c\in\mathcal C} C_c\, y_{i,c}, \quad \forall i,j \tag{6.4b}
$$

### 6.5 Rolling-Stock Circulation Constraints

$$
\sum_{r\in\mathcal R} z_{i,r} = \sum_{c\in\mathcal C} c\, y_{i,c}, \quad \forall i\in\mathcal I \tag{6.5a}
$$
$$
\sum_{i'<i} v_{r,i',i} + u_{i,r}^{\text{init}} = z_{i,r}, \quad \forall i,r \tag{6.5b}
$$
$$
\sum_{i'>i} v_{r,i,i'} + u_{i,r}^{\text{fin}} = z_{i,r}, \quad \forall i,r \tag{6.5c}
$$
$$
\sum_{i\in\mathcal I} u_{i,r}^{\text{init}} = 1, \quad \sum_{i\in\mathcal I} u_{i,r}^{\text{fin}} = 1, \quad \forall r \tag{6.5d}
$$
$$
a_{i',1} \geq a_{i,N_J} + t^{\text{trans}} - M(1 - v_{r,i,i'}), \quad \forall r,\; i<i' \tag{6.5e}
$$

*(Constraint 6.5e enforces the minimum transfer/coupling time between consecutive trains served by the same rolling-stock unit.)*

### 6.6 Passenger-Flow Constraints

**Interval-to-departure indicator (linearization of "did train $i$ depart after the start of interval $k$?"):**

$$
\sigma_{i,j,k} \geq \frac{d_{i,j} - \tau_k^{s}}{M}, \quad \sigma_{i,j,k} \leq 1, \quad \sigma_{i,j,k} \geq \sigma_{i,j,k+1}, \quad \forall i,j,k \tag{6.6a}
$$
$$
\sigma_{0,j,k} = 0, \quad \forall j,k \tag{6.6b}
$$

**Waiting passengers assigned to train $i$:**

$$
w_{i,j,k} \leq \lambda_{j,k}\,\Delta_k\,(\sigma_{i,j,k} - \sigma_{i-1,j,k}), \quad \forall i,j,k \tag{6.6c}
$$
$$
w_{i,j,k} \leq M\,x_{i,j}, \quad \forall i,j,k \tag{6.6d}
$$

**Boarding/alighting flow conservation:**

$$
\sum_{i\in\mathcal I} b_{i,j,k} \leq \lambda_{j,k}\,\Delta_k, \quad \forall j,k \tag{6.6e}
$$
$$
\sum_{i\in\mathcal I} e_{i,j,k} \leq \mu_{j,k}\,\Delta_k, \quad \forall j,k \tag{6.6f}
$$
$$
q_{i,j} = q_{i,j-1} + \sum_{k\in\mathcal K} b_{i,j,k} - \sum_{k\in\mathcal K} e_{i,j,k}, \quad \forall i,j \tag{6.6g}
$$
$$
q_{i,1} = \sum_{k\in\mathcal K} b_{i,j,k} - \sum_{k\in\mathcal K} e_{i,j,k} \quad \text{(initial load = 0 at origin)} \tag{6.6h}
$$
$$
\sum_{k\in\mathcal K} b_{i,j,k} \leq M\,x_{i,j}, \quad \sum_{k\in\mathcal K} e_{i,j,k} \leq M\,x_{i,j}, \quad \forall i,j \tag{6.6i}
$$

*(Assumption: passengers who cannot board/alight at their first-choice train wait for the next train at the same station — captured by (6.6c)–(6.6f).)*

### 6.7 Capacity Constraints

$$
q_{i,j} \leq \sum_{c\in\mathcal C} C_c\, y_{i,c}, \quad \forall i,j \tag{6.7a}
$$
$$
q_{i,j} \geq 0, \quad b_{i,j,k}, e_{i,j,k}, w_{i,j,k} \geq 0, \quad \forall i,j,k \tag{6.7b}
$$

For the bilinear term $\pi_{i,j} = q_{i,j}\cdot \rho_{i,j}$, with bounds $q^{\min}\leq q_{i,j}\leq q^{\max}$ and $\rho^{\min}\leq\rho_{i,j}\leq\rho^{\max}$:

$$
\pi_{i,j} \geq q^{\min}\,\rho_{i,j} + \rho^{\min}\,q_{i,j} - q^{\min}\rho^{\min}, \quad \forall i,j \tag{6.8a}
$$

# Final MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

Below is the complete, refined MILP formulation integrating all improvements from the iterative refinement process.

---

## 1. Problem Description and Assumptions

**Problem.** Given a planned timetable on a double-track high-speed line, a partial segment blockage disables one track over a time window $TW = [\tau^{start}, \tau^{end}]$ on blocks $b \in \mathcal{B}^D$. The model jointly decides (i) **rescheduling** (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation), (ii) **speed profiles** per train per block, and (iii) **energy consumption**, while guaranteeing conflict-free operation under bidirectional shared-track usage.

**Assumptions.**
- A1. Time is discretized into intervals of width $\Delta$ over horizon $[0, T^{max}]$.
- A2. Each block is either fully blocked or fully available on each track during $TW$.
- A3. Trains on the same track in the same direction obey a minimum headway $h$.
- A4. Trains in opposite directions on a shared (rerouted) track cannot occupy the same block simultaneously.
- A5. Speed–energy relation $E(v) = e_0 + e_1 v + e_2 v^2$ is approximated by a piecewise-linear function with breakpoints $\{(v_k, E_k)\}_{k \in \mathcal{K}}$.
- A6. A train may be rerouted on a subset of its blocks (per-block rerouting), using the opposite-direction track.
- A7. Cancellation is allowed at the train level; cancelled trains impose no operational constraints.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{I}$ | Set of trains, $i, j \in \mathcal{I}$ |
| $\mathcal{B}$ | Set of track blocks, $b \in \mathcal{B}$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations, $s \in \mathcal{S}$ |
| $\mathcal{T} = \{0,1,\dots,|\mathcal{T}|-1\}$ | Discrete time intervals, width $\Delta$ |
| $\mathcal{K} = \{1,\dots,K\}$ | Breakpoints of the PWL speed–energy curve |
| $\mathcal{P}_i \subset \mathcal{B}$ | Ordered nominal path of train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{P}^{alt}_i \subset \mathcal{B}$ | Ordered alternative path of train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{B}^D \subset \mathcal{B}$ | Disrupted blocks |
| $\mathcal{TW}_b \subset \mathcal{T}$ | Disruption time-window intervals on block $b$ |
| $\mathcal{N}(b)$ | Block immediately after $b$ in $\mathcal{P}_i \cup \mathcal{P}^{alt}_i$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ [km] |
| $v^{min}, v^{max}$ | Min/max speed [km/h] |
| $v^{dep}, v^{arr}$ | Departure / arrival speed at terminals |
| $a^{max}, d^{max}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration [km/h²] |
| $h$ | Minimum headway [time units] |
| $\delta^{min}, \delta^{max}$ | Min/max dwell time at stations |
| $t^a_{i,s}, t^d_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure time |
| $v_k, E_k$ | Speed and energy-rate at PWL breakpoint $k$ |
| $P^{aux}$ | Auxiliary power during dwell |
| $c^{delay}, c^{energy}, c^{cancel}, c^{rer}$ | Objective weights |
| $P^{cancel}, P^{rer}$ | Cancellation / rerouting penalties |
| $T^{max}$ | Planning horizon |
| $M_1,\dots,M_7$ | Tight big-M constants (see §10) |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

**Timing (continuous):**
- $a_{i,s} \ge 0$: actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $d_{i,s} \ge 0$: actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $e_{i,b} \ge 0$: entry time of train $i$ into block $b$
- $x_{i,b} \ge 0$: exit time of train $i$ from block $b$
- $\tau_{i,b} \ge 0$: traversal time on block $b$

**Speed and energy (continuous):**
- $v_{i,b} \in [v^{min}, v^{max}]$: average speed of train $i$ on block $b$
- $\lambda_{i,b,k} \in [0,1]$: PWL weight at breakpoint $k$
- $E_{i,b} \ge 0$: energy consumed on block $b$
- $E^{tot} \ge 0$: total system energy

**Routing and cancellation (binary):**
- $u_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses block $b$
- $r'_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is rerouted on block $b$ (opposite track)
- $r_{i,b} \in \{-1,0,+1\}$: signed direction on block $b$ (derived)
- $cnc_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled

**Interval coupling (binary):**
- $\eta_{i,b,t} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ enters block $b$ in interval $t$

**Conflict resolution (binary):**
- $z_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trains $i,j$ use block $b$ in opposite directions
- $o_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering on block $b$ (1 if $i$ precedes $j$)
- $d^{aux}_{i,j,b} \ge 0$: auxiliary for $|r_{i,b}-r_{j,b}|$

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; c^{delay}\!\!\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}}\sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} (a_{i,s} - t^a_{i,s})_+ \;+\; c^{energy}\,E^{tot} \;+\; c^{cancel}\!\sum_{i} P^{cancel}\,cnc_i \;+\; c^{rer}\!\sum_{i,b} P^{rer}\,r'_{i,b}
$$

where $(\cdot)_+ = \max(\cdot, 0)$.

---

## 6. Constraints

### C1 — Station Dwell
$$
\delta^{min}(1-cnc_i) \;\le\; d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \;\le\; \delta^{max}(1-cnc_i) \qquad \forall i, s
$$

### C2 — Block Traversal Time
$$
\tau_{i,b} \;=\; x_{i,b} - e_{i,b} \qquad \forall i, b
$$
$$
\frac{L_b}{v^{max}}\,u_{i,b} \;\le\; \tau_{i,b} \;\le\; \frac{L_b}{v^{min}}\,u_{i,b} + M_1(1-u_{i,b}) \qquad \forall i, b
$$

### C3 — Entry Time via Interval Indicator $\eta$
$$
\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \eta_{i,b,t} \;=\; u_{i,b} \qquad \forall i, b
$$
$$
e_{i,b} \;\ge\; t\Delta\,\eta_{i,b,t} \qquad \forall i, b, t
$$
$$
e_{i,b} \;\le\; (t+1)\Delta\,\eta_{i,b,t} + M_2(1-\eta_{i,b,t}) \qquad \forall i, b, t
$$

### C4 — Path Sequencing (Consecutive Blocks)
For each $i$ and consecutive $(b, b') \in \mathcal{P}_i \cup \mathcal{P}^{alt}_i$:
$$
e_{i,b'} \;\ge\; x_{i,b} + h\,(u_{i,b}+u_{i,b'}-1) - M_3(2-u_{i,b}-u_{i,b'}) \qquad \forall i, b, b'
$$

### C5 — PWL Energy (SOS-2)
$$
v_{i,b} \;=\; \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} v_k\,\lambda_{i,b,k} \qquad \forall i, b
$$
$$
E_{i,b} \;=\; \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} E_k\,\lambda_{i,b,k} + P^{aux}(d_{i,s}-a_{i,s}) \quad \text{(dwell energy on terminal block)} \qquad \forall i, b
$$
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \lambda_{i,b,k} \;=\; u_{i,b} \qquad \forall i, b
$$
$$
\{\lambda_{i,b,k}\}_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \text{ is SOS-2} \qquad \forall i, b
$$
$$
E^{tot} \;=\; \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}}\sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} E_{i,b}
$$

### C6 — Disruption OR-Logic
Define $y_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ would enter disrupted block $b$ during $TW$:
$$
y_{i,b} \;\ge\; \eta_{i,b,t} \qquad \forall i,\; b \in \mathcal{B}^D,\; t \in \mathcal{TW}_b
$$
$$
y_{i,b} \;\le\; \sum_{t \in \mathcal{TW}_b} \eta_{i,b,t} \qquad \forall i,\; b \in \mathcal{B}^D
$$

**Disjunction** — train on disrupted block during TW must be rerouted, traverse outside TW, or be cancelled:
$$
u_{i,b} + y_{i,b} \;\le\; 1 + r'_{i,b} + cnc_i \qquad \forall i,\; b \in \mathcal{B}^D
$$

### C7 — Track Capacity (Block Occupancy)
Define block residence $N_b = \lceil L_b/(v^{min}\Delta)\rceil$. Extend occupancy:
$$
\sum_{t'=\max(0,\,t-N_b+1)}^{t} \eta_{i,b,t'} \;\ge\; \eta_{i,b,t} \qquad \forall i, b, t
$$

**At most one train per block per interval:**
$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \eta_{i,b,t} \;\le\; 1 \qquad \forall b, t
$$

**Pairwise separation (redundant but tightens LP):**
For all $i < j$, $b \in \mathcal{B}_i \cap \mathcal{B}_j$:
$$
x_{i,b} \;\le\; e_{j,b} - h + M_4(1-o_{i,j,b})
$$
$$
x_{j,b} \;\le\; e_{i,b} - h + M_4\,o_{i,j,b}
$$

### C8 — Bidirectional Conflict (Correct Linearization)
$$
d^{aux}_{i,j,b} \;\ge\; r_{i,b} - r_{j,b}, \qquad d^{aux}_{i,j,b} \;\ge\; r_{j,b} - r_{i,b} \qquad \forall i<j, b
$$
$$
2\,z_{i,j,b} \;\ge\; d^{aux}_{i,j,b} - 1, \qquad z_{i,j,b} \;\le\; \tfrac{1}{2}\,d^{aux}_{i,j,b} \qquad \forall i<j, b
$$

This yields $z_{i,j,b}=1$ iff $|r_{i,b}-r_{j,b}|=2$ (opposite directions), else $z_{i,j,b}=0$.

**Bidirectional separation** (when $z=1$, no overlap):
$$
x_{i,b} \;\le\; e_{j,b} + M_5(1-o_{i,j,b}) + M_5(1-z_{i,j,b})
$$
$$
x_{j,b} \;\le\; e_{i,b} + M_5\,o_{i,j,b} + M_5(1-z_{i,j,b})
$$

### C9 — Rerouting Direction Logic
$$
r'_{i,b} \;\le\; u_{i,b} \qquad \forall i, b
$$
$$
r_{i,b} \;=\; dir_i\,u_{i,b} - 2\,dir_i\,r'_{i,b} \qquad \forall i, b
$$

Behavior:
- $u_{i,b}=1, r'_{i,b}=0 \Rightarrow r_{i,b}=dir_i$ (normal)
- $u_{i,b}=1, r'_{i,b}=1 \Rightarrow r_{i,b}=-dir_i$ (rerouted)
- $u_{i,b}=0 \Rightarrow r_{i,b}=0$

### C10 — Acceleration / Deceleration at Block Boundaries
For consecutive blocks $(b,b') \in \mathcal{P}_i \cup \mathcal{P}^{alt}_i$:
$$
v_{i,b'} - v_{i,b} \;\le\; a^{max}\,\tau_{i,b} + M_6(2-u_{i,b}-u_{i,b'})
$$
$$
v_{i,b} - v_{i,b'} \;\le\; d^{max}\,\tau_{i,b} + M_6(2-u_{i,b}-u_{i,b'})
$$

### C11 — Cancellation
$$
u_{i,b} \;\le\; 1 - cnc_i \qquad \forall i, b
$$
$$
a_{i,s},\, d_{i,s},\, e_{i,b},\, x_{i,b} \;\le\; M_7\,cnc_i + T^{max}(1-cnc_i) \qquad \forall i, s, b
$$

### C12 — Path Integrity
$$
\sum_{b \in \mathcal{P}_i} u_{i,b} \;\ge\; |\mathcal{P}_i|(1-cnc_i) - M_7\!\sum_{b \in \mathcal{P}^{alt}_i} r'_{i,b}
$$
$$
\sum_{b \in \mathcal{P}^{alt}_i} u_{i,b} \;\ge\; |\mathcal{P}^{alt}_i|\!\sum_{b \in \mathcal{P}^{alt}_i} r'_{i,b} - M_7\,cnc_i
$$

### C13 — Terminal Anchoring
$$
a_{i,s^{first}} \;\ge\; t^a_{i,s^{first}}, \qquad a_{i,s^{last}} \;\le\; T^{max}
$$
$$
v_{i,b^{first}} \;=\; v^{dep}, \qquad v_{i,b^{last}} \;=\; v^{arr}
$$

---

## 7. Variable Summary

| Type | Variable | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Continuous | $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, e_{i,b}, x_{i,b}, \tau_{i,b}$ | $O(|\mathcal{I}|(|\mathcal{S}|+|\mathcal{B}|))$ |
| Continuous | $v_{i,b}, \lambda_{i,b,k}, E_{i,b}, E^{tot}$ | $O(|\mathcal{I}||\mathcal{B}|K)$ |
| Binary | $u_{i,b}, r'_{i,b}, cnc_i$ | $O(|\mathcal{I}||\mathcal{B}|)$ |
| Binary | $\eta_{i,b,t}$ | $O(|\mathcal{I}||\mathcal{B}||\mathcal{T}|)$ |
| Binary | $z_{i,j,b}, o_{i,j,b}$ | $O(|\mathcal{I}|^2|\mathcal{B}|)$ |
| Continuous | $d^{aux}_{i,j,b}$ | $O(|\mathcal{I}|^2|\mathcal{B}|)$ |

---

## 8. Big-M Constants (Tight Choices)

| Constant | Value | Used in |
|---|---|---|
| $M_1$ | $L_b/v^{min}$ | C2 |
| $M_2$ | $\Delta$ | C3 |
| $M_3$ | $T^{max}$ | C4 |
| $M_4$ | $T^{max}$ | C7 |
| $M_5$ | $T^{max}$ | C8 |
| $M_6$ | $v^{max}$ | C10 |
| $M_7$ | $T^{max}$ | C11, C12 |

---

## 9. Key Modeling Features

1. **Integrated TRP–TSMP coupling**: Block traversal time $\tau_{i,b}$ links rescheduled times to speed profile $v_{i,b}$ (C2, C5).
2. **Per-block rerouting**: $r'_{i,b}$ allows partial rerouting; signed $r_{i,b}$ encodes effective direction (C9).
3. **Bidirectional conflict**: Correctly linearized via auxiliary $d^{aux}_{i,j,b}$ (C8).
4. **Disruption OR-logic**: Clean three-way disjunction (reroute / outside TW / cancel) (C6).
5. **Track capacity**: Both interval-based ($\sum_i \eta \le 1$) and pairwise separation (C7).
6. **Energy efficiency**: PWL approximation of $v^2$ via SOS-2 (C5).
7. **Acceleration feasibility**: Block-boundary speed transitions respect $a^{max}, d^{max}$ (C10).

---

## 10. Complexity Estimate

| Component | Order |
|---|---|
| Total variables | $O(|\mathcal{I}|^2|\mathcal{B}| + |\mathcal{I}||\mathcal{B}|K|\mathcal{T}|)$ |
| Total constraints | $O(|\mathcal{I}||\mathcal{B}||\mathcal{T}| + |\mathcal{I}|^2|\mathcal{B}|)$ |
| Nonzeros | $O(|\mathcal{I}||\mathcal{B}||\mathcal{T}|K)$ |

This MILP is large-scale; the paper's decomposition (IP + train plans) and adaptive iterative algorithm are designed to make it tractable for real-world instances.

# Final MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

Below is the consolidated, publication-quality mixed-integer linear programming model that integrates the **Train Rescheduling Problem (TRP)** and the **Train Speed Management Problem (TSMP)** into a single framework. The model handles partial segment blockages by allowing bidirectional trains to reroute through the opposite track within the disruption area.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t \in T$ |
| $S$ | Set of corridor segments (in path order), indexed by $s \in S$ |
| $I=\{1,\dots,N\}$ | Discretization steps within a segment |
| $L=\{1,\dots,N_L\}$ | Speed breakpoints for piecewise-linear resistance |
| $B\subseteq S$ | Station blocks (crossover points where track change is possible) |
| $\mathcal{P}\subseteq S$ | Pairs of adjacent single-track segments shared by two directions |
| $\Theta$ | Discrete time horizon |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $\tilde a_{t,s},\tilde d_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure of $t$ at $s$ | s |
| $\Delta x$ | Spatial discretization step (segment length $= N\Delta x$) | m |
| $\Delta t$ | Time discretization step | s |
| $a,b,c$ | Davis resistance coefficients ($R(v)=a+bv+cv^2$) | N, N·s/m, N·s²/m² |
| $m_t$ | Mass of train $t$ (incl. rotating mass) | kg |
| $\bar v_l$ | Speed breakpoints ($0=\bar v_1<\bar v_2<\dots<\bar v_{N_L}=v^{\max}$) | m/s |
| $r_l = a+b\bar v_l+c\bar v_l^2$ | Precomputed resistance at breakpoint $l$ | N |
| $\theta_{s,i}$ | Track gradient at step $i$ of segment $s$ | rad |
| $g$ | Gravitational acceleration (9.81) | m/s² |
| $P^{\max}$ | Maximum tractive power | W |
| $\bar E_t$ | Maximum regenerative energy storage of $t$ | J |
| $v^{\min},v^{\max}$ | Speed limits | m/s |
| $f^{\min},f^{\max}$ | Tractive / braking force limits | N |
| $\tilde v^{\text{ent}}_{t,s},\tilde v^{\text{ext}}_{t,s}$ | Nominal entry / exit speeds | m/s |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum headway time | s |
| $\tau^B_{\text{start}},\tau^B_{\text{end}}$ | Blockage time window | s |
| $k^B$ | The blocked track | – |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant | – |
| $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta$ | Objective weights | – |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Scheduling (macroscopic):**
- $\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}\ge 0$, $\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}\ge 0$ — actual arrival / departure times
- $\delta^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}\ge 0$, $\delta^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}\ge 0$ — delay magnitudes
- $c_t\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $t$ is cancelled

**Routing:**
- $x_{t,s,k}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $t$ uses track $k$ on segment $s$
- $r_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $t$ is rerouted on segment $s$

**Conflict resolution:**
- $\sigma_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $t$ precedes train $t'$ on shared segment $s$

**Kinematics (microscopic, per step $i$):**
- $p_{t,s,i}\ge 0$ — position within step (m)
- $v_{t,s,i}\ge 0$ — speed (m/s)
- $u_{t,s,i}\in\mathbb{R}$ — acceleration (m/s²)
- $f_{t,s,i}\ge 0$ — tractive force (N)
- $h_{t,s,i}\ge 0$ — braking force (N)
- $\mu_{t,s,i,l}\ge 0$ — SOS2 weights over speed breakpoints

**Energy:**
- $e_{t,s,i}\ge 0$ — net energy consumed at step $i$ (J)
- $\eta_{t,s,i,l}\ge 0$ — McCormick auxiliary for products $f\cdot\mu$

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\; \alpha\!\!\sum_{t,s}\!\!\bigl(\delta^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}+\delta^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}\bigr) \;+\; \beta\!\!\sum_{t}\!(1-c_t) \;+\; \gamma\!\!\sum_{t,s,i}\!e_{t,s,i} \;-\; \delta\!\!\sum_{t,s,i}\!\eta^{\text{reg}}_{t,s,i}
$$

where $\eta^{\text{reg}}_{t,s,i}$ is the regenerative-braking energy recovered per step. The objective jointly minimises **delay**, **cancellations**, **traction energy** and rewards **regenerative braking**.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Scheduling

$$
\delta^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}\;\ge\;\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}-\tilde a_{t,s},\qquad \delta^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}\;\ge\;\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}-\tilde d_{t,s} \quad\forall t,s \tag{S1}
$$

$$
\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}\;\le\;\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s} \;+\; \delta^{\max}_{t,s} \quad\forall t,s\in B \tag{S2}
$$

$$
\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,1}\;\ge\;\tilde d_{t,1},\qquad \tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,|S|}=\tilde a_{t,|S|} \quad\forall t \tag{S3}
$$

### 5.2 Routing and Cancellation

$$
\sum_{k\in K} x_{t,s,k} \;=\; 1 - c_t \quad\forall t,s \tag{R1}
$$

$$
r_{t,s} \;=\; \sum_{k\neq k^{\text{def}}(t)} x_{t,s,k} \quad\forall t,s \tag{R2}
$$

(Exactly one track per segment, except cancelled trains; rerouting indicator is exactly 1 iff train is off its default track.)

### 5.3 No Track Switch Outside Crossovers

$$
x_{t,s,k} \;=\; x_{t,s+1,k} \quad\forall t,\; s\notin B,\; k \tag{R3}
$$

### 5.4 Kinematics

**Newton's law with SOS2-linearised resistance** (active step):

$$
m_t\,u_{t,s,i}\;=\;f_{t,s,i}-h_{t,s,i}-\sum_{l\in L}r_l\,\mu_{t,s,i,l}-m_t\,g\sin\theta_{s,i} \quad\forall t,s,i \tag{K1}
$$

**Speed as convex combination of breakpoints**:

$$
v_{t,s,i}\;=\;\sum_{l\in L}\bar v_l\,\mu_{t,s,i,l},\qquad \sum_{l\in L}\mu_{t,s,i,l}=1,\qquad \text{SOS2}(\mu_{t,s,i,\cdot}) \quad\forall t,s,i \tag{K2}
$$

**Discrete time update** (Euler–Cromer):

$$
v_{t,s,i+1}\;=\;v_{t,s,i}+u_{t,s,i}\,\Delta t \quad\forall t,s,i< N \tag{K3}
$$

$$
p_{t,s,i+1}\;=\;p_{t,s,i}+v_{t,s,i}\,\Delta t+\tfrac{1}{2}u_{t,s,i}\,\Delta t^2 \quad\forall t,s,i< N \tag{K4}
$$

**Boundary conditions**:

$$
p_{t,s,1}=0,\quad p_{t,s,N+1}=\Delta x \quad\forall t,s \tag{K5}
$$

$$
v_{t,s,1}=\tilde v^{\text{ent}}_{t,s},\quad v_{t,s,N}=\tilde v^{\text{ext}}_{t,s},\quad v^{\min}\le v_{t,s,i}\le v^{\max} \quad\forall t,s,i \tag{K6}
$$

**Force bounds**:

$$
f^{\min}\le f_{t,s,i}\le f^{\max},\qquad 0\le h_{t,s,i}\le f^{\max} \quad\forall t,s,i \tag{K7}
$$

### 5.5 Power and Energy

**Tractive-power limit** (exact at each SOS2 breakpoint):

$$
f_{t,s,i}\;\le\;\sum_{l\in L}\frac{P^{\max}}{\bar v_l}\,\mu_{t,s,i,l} \quad\forall t,s,i \tag{E1}
$$

**McCormick envelopes** for $\eta_{t,s,i,l}\approx f_{t,s,i}\cdot\mu_{t,s,i,l}$ (with $f_{t,s,i}\in[0,f^{\max}]$, $\mu_{t,s,i,l}\in[0,1]$):

$$
\eta_{t,s,i,l}\le f^{\max}\,\mu_{t,s,i,l} \tag{E2a}
$$
$$
\eta_{t,s,i,l}\le f_{t,s,i} \tag{E2b}
$$
$$
\eta_{t,s,i,l}\ge f_{t,s,i}-f^{\max}(1-\mu_{t,s,i,l}) \tag{E2c}
$$
$$
\eta_{t,s,i,l}\ge 0 \quad\forall t,s,i,l \tag{E2d}
$$

**Net energy per step**:

$$
e_{t,s,i}\;=\;\Delta t\sum_{l\in L}\bar v_l\,\eta_{t,s,i,l} \;-\; \eta^{\text{reg}}_{t,s,i} \quad\forall t,s,i \tag{E3}
$$

**Regenerative-braking cap** (McCormick envelope of $h\cdot v$):

$$
\eta^{\text{reg}}_{t,s,i}\;\le\;h_{t,s,i}\,v^{\max}\,\Delta t,\quad \eta^{\text{reg}}_{t,s,i}\;\le\;h^{\max}\,v_{t,s,i}\,\Delta t \quad\forall t,s,i \tag{E4}
$$

$$
\eta^{\text{reg}}_{t,s,i}\;\ge\;h_{t,s,i}\,v_{t,s,i}\,\Delta t - \text{big-M relaxation} \tag{E4'}
$$

### 5.6 Blockage Avoidance

For each blockage $(s^B,k^B,[\tau^B_{\text{start}},\tau^B_{\text{end}}])$ and train $t$, define a sequencing binary $w_{t,s^B}\in\{0,1\}$:

$$
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s^B}\;\le\;\tau^B_{\text{start}} \;+\; M(1-w_{t,s^B}) \;+\; M\cdot x_{t,s^B,k^B} \quad\forall t \tag{BL1}
$$

$$
\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s^B}\;\ge\;\tau^B_{\text{end}} \;-\; M\cdot w_{t,s^B} \;-\; M\cdot x_{t,s^B,k^B} \quad\forall t \tag{BL2}
$$

*Interpretation*: if $x_{t,s^B,k^B}=1$ (train uses the blocked track), it must finish traversing before $\tau^B_{\text{start}}$ ($w=1$) or start after $\tau^B_{\text{end}}$ ($w=0$). If the train reroutes, the constraints are relaxed.

### 5.7 Headway and Bidirectional Conflict Resolution

**Pairwise ordering** on shared track segments:

$$
\sigma_{t,t',s}+\sigma_{t',t,s}\;\le\;1 \quad\forall t<t',\; s\in\mathcal{P} \tag{C1}
$$

**Headway enforcement** (d'Ariano-style disjunction):

$$
\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}+h_{\min}\;\le\;\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t',s}+M(1-\sigma_{t,t',s})+M(2-x_{t,s,k}-x_{t',s,k})+M(c_t+c_{t'}) \quad\forall t,t',s,k \tag{C2}
$$

$$
\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t',s}+h_{\min}\;\le\;\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}+M\,\sigma_{t,t',s}+M(2-x_{t,s,k}-x_{t',s,k})+M(c_t+c_{t'}) \quad\forall t,t',s,k \tag{C3}
$$

When two opposite-direction trains both use the same track $k$ on segment $s$ (which only happens during rerouting), these constraints enforce minimum headway and prevent simultaneous occupancy.

### 5.8 Linking Macroscopic Schedule and Microscopic Kinematics

The traversal time of segment $s$ is $N\Delta t$ when operated; cancellation relaxes it:

$$
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s+1}-\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}\;\ge\;N\Delta t - M\,c_t \quad\forall t,s \tag{L1}
$$

$$
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s+1}-\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}\;\le\;N\Delta t + M\,c_t \quad\forall t,s \tag{L2}
$$

When $c_t=1$ (cancelled), the interval is unconstrained; otherwise segment traversal time is exactly $N\Delta t$, consistent with (K3)–(K4).

---

## 6. Model Assumptions

1. **Single-track blockage**: One track of segment $s^B$ is fully blocked during $[\tau^B_{\text{start}},\tau^B_{\text{end}}]$; trains may reroute to the opposite track.
2. **Crossover rerouting**: Track changes are physically possible only at station blocks $B\subseteq S$ (R3).
3. **Regenerative braking cap**: Energy recovered in any step is bounded by $\bar E_t$ (E4); surplus is dissipated as heat.
4. **Time and space discretisation**: Each segment is split into $N$ equal spatial steps $\Delta x$, traversed in $N$ time steps $\Delta t$; kinematics use Euler–Cromer updates (K3–K4).
5. **Davis resistance**: $R(v)=a+bv+cv^2$ (N), independent of direction.
6. **Linearisations**: Davis quadratic and the products $f\mu$, $f v$, $h v$ are relaxed via **SOS2 + McCormick envelopes**; both relaxations are exact at breakpoints and tighten with denser discretisation.
7. **Schedule adherence**: Only positive delays are penalised (S1); early arrivals are unconstrained.
8. **Bidirectional conflict**: Opposite-direction trains can share a track only via rerouting, and only with enforced headway (C1–C3).
9. **Cancellation penalty**: Cancellation is treated as a last-resort option with a large penalty $\beta$.

---

## 7. Compact Notation Table

| Symbol | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s},\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}$ | cont. $\ge 0$ | Actual arrival/departure times |
| $\delta^{\text{arr}}_{t,s},\delta^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}$ | cont. $\ge 0$ | Delay magnitudes |

---

## 8. Summary

This MILP simultaneously optimises **retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and speed profiles** for all trains on a high-speed railway line under partial segment blockage. The key features are:

- **Bidirectional conflict resolution** via d'Ariano-type disjunctive headway constraints (C1–C3) activated only when opposite-direction trains share a track during rerouting.
- **Blockage avoidance** via sequencing binary $w_{t,s^B}$ with clean big-M formulation (BL1–BL2).
- **Integrated speed profiles** through Euler–Cromer kinematics (K3–K4) linked to the macroscopic schedule by (L1)–(L2).
- **Energy co-optimisation** using SOS2-linearised Davis resistance and McCormick envelopes for tractive power and regenerative braking (E1–E4).
- **Joint objective** balancing delay, cancellation, traction energy, and regenerative braking credit.

The model can be solved by branch-and-bound with SOS2 branching (CPLEX, Gurobi, SCIP), or by the **decomposition-based adaptive iterative algorithm** described in the paper, which decomposes the problem into an integer programming master (train interactions) and per-train plans (speed profiles), iteratively refining plan granularity.
