Text:
# Best Model: Model 2 — Complete MILP for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

After comparing the three generated formulations, **Model 2** is selected as the best because it offers the most complete and rigorously detailed formulation, with explicit separation of same-direction and opposite-direction ordering variables, a clean decomposition of running time into per-block traversal plus train-length traversal, careful constraint numbering, and explicit boundary conditions for both origin and destination stations. It captures every element described in the problem statement (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, block-level speed profiles, energy minimization, disruption handling, and bidirectional conflict resolution) within a single MILP.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Set | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t$ |
| $S=\{1,\dots,|S|\}$ | Stations; $s=1$ is origin, $s=|S|$ is destination |
| $K=\{1,\dots,|S|-1\}$ | Segments; segment $k$ connects stations $k$ and $k+1$ |
| $B_k=\{1,\dots,|B_k|\}$ | Block sections in segment $k$ |
| $I=\{1,\dots,|I|\}$ | Discrete time intervals; interval $i$ covers $[(i-1)\Delta t,\;i\Delta t]$ |
| $D\subset T\times T$ | Ordered train pairs on the **same** direction |
| $D'\subset T\times T$ | Ordered train pairs on **opposite** directions (bidirectional conflicts) |
| $R=\{1,\dots,R\}$ | Breakpoints for the piecewise-linear energy/speed model |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| $L_{k,b}$ | Length of block section $b$ in segment $k$ |
| $L_t$ | Length of train $t$ |
| $\text{dir}_t\in\{-1,+1\}$ | Direction of train $t$ ($+1$ up, $-1$ down) |
| $v_{\max},v_{\min}$ | Maximum / minimum allowed speed |
| $a_{\max},d_{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration magnitude |
| $t_{\min}^{\text{dw}},\,t_{\max}^{\text{dw}}$ | Minimum / maximum station dwell time |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum time headway between consecutive trains |
| $\Delta t$ | Length of a time interval |
| $v_r$, $E_r=E(v_r)$ | Speed breakpoint $r$ and corresponding energy-rate value |
| $T^{\text{arr}}_{t,s},\,T^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure times |
| $[T_d^{\text{st}},T_d^{\text{end}}]$ | Disruption time window |
| $k_d$ | Index of the disrupted segment |
| $\gamma_{k_d,i}\in\{0,1\}$ | 1 if interval $i$ overlaps $[T_d^{\text{st}},T_d^{\text{end}}]$ on segment $k_d$ |
| $\text{min\_int}_{k,b}=\lceil L_{k,b}/(v_{\max}\Delta t)\rceil$ | Min intervals needed at $v_{\max}$ |
| $\text{max\_int}_{k,b}=\lceil L_{k,b}/(v_{\min}\Delta t)\rceil$ | Max intervals allowed at $v_{\min}$ |
| $W_{\text{delay}},W_{\text{energy}},W_{\text{cancel}},W_{\text{reroute}}$ | Objective weights |
| $P_t$ | Priority weight of train $t$ |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |
| $T_{\text{hor}}$ | End of the planning horizon |
| $\delta_{\max}$ | Maximum allowable final-arrival delay |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{t,s}\in[0,T_{\text{hor}}]$ | Continuous | Actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{t,s}\in[0,T_{\text{hor}}]$ | Continuous | Actual departure time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $s_{t,k}\in\mathbb{R}_+$ | Continuous | Running time of train $t$ on segment $k$ |
| $\delta_{t,s}\in\mathbb{R}_+$ | Continuous | Delay of train $t$ at station $s$ vs schedule |
| $\text{ent}_{t,k,b}\in[0,T_{\text{hor}}]$ | Continuous | Entry time of train $t$ into block $b$ of segment $k$ |
| $v_{t,k,b}\in[v_{\min},v_{\max}]$ | Continuous | Average speed of train $t$ in block $b$ of segment $k$ |
| $e_{t,k,b}\in\mathbb{R}_+$ | Continuous | Energy consumed by train $t$ in block $b$ of segment $k$ |
| $\lambda_{t,k,b,r}\in[0,1]$ | Continuous | Convex-combination weight for breakpoint $r$ |
| $x_{t,k,b,i}\in\{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ occupies block $b$ of segment $k$ in interval $i$ |
| $z_{t,k}\in\{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ reroutes to opposite track on segment $k$ |
| $o_{t_1,t_2,k}\in\{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if $t_1$ traverses segment $k$ before $t_2$ (same direction) |
| $o'_{t_1,t_2,k}\in\{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if $t_1$ traverses segment $k$ before $t_2$ (opposite direction) |
| $c_t\in\{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled |
| $\alpha_{t,k}\in\{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ enters segment $k$ during the disruption window |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\; W_{\text{delay}}\!\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S} P_t\,\delta_{t,s}
\;+\;W_{\text{energy}}\!\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{b\in B_k} e_{t,k,b}
\;+\;W_{\text{cancel}}\!\sum_{t\in T} c_t
\;+\;W_{\text{reroute}}\!\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{k\in K} z_{t,k}.
$$

The objective balances four weighted components: priority-weighted delay (service quality), total energy consumption (speed-management cost), cancellation penalties, and rerouting penalties.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Station dwell and arrival–departure consistency

$$
\begin{aligned}
d_{t,s}-a_{t,s} &\geq t_{\min}^{\text{dw}}\,(1-c_t) &&\forall t,s \\[2pt]
d_{t,s}-a_{t,s} &\leq t_{\max}^{\text{dw}}\,(1-c_t) &&\forall t,s \\[2pt]
a_{t,s+1}-d_{t,s} &= s_{t,k}\,(1-c_t),\quad k=s &&\forall t,\;s\in S\setminus\{|S|\} \\[2pt]
s_{t,k} &= \sum_{b\in B_k}\frac{L_{k,b}}{v_{t,k,b}}+\frac{L_t}{v_{t,k,|B_k|}} &&\forall t,k
\end{aligned}
$$

The last equation decomposes the running time on a segment into (i) the sum of per-block traversals $L_{k,b}/v_{t,k,b}$ and (ii) the train-length traversal $L_t/v_{t,k,|B_k|}$ of the last block before reaching the next station.

### 5.2 Delay definition (relative to schedule)

$$
\begin{aligned}
\delta_{t,s} &\geq a_{t,s}-T^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}-M\,c_t &&\forall t,s \\
\delta_{t,s} &\geq d_{t,s}-T^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}-M\,c_t &&\forall t,s
\end{aligned}
$$

Together with $\delta_{t,s}\ge 0$, this gives $\delta_{t,s}=\max(0,\,a_{t,s}-T^{\text{arr}}_{t,s},\,d_{t,s}-T^{\text{dep}}_{t,s})$ for active trains.

### 5.3 Cancellation neutralizes variables

$$
\begin{aligned}
a_{t,s} &\leq M\,(1-c_t) &&\forall t,s \\
d_{t,s} &\leq M\,(1-c_t) &&\forall t,s
\end{aligned}
$$

### 5.4 Block-section capacity (space–time network)

$$
\sum_{t\in T} x_{t,k,b,i} \leq 1 &&\forall k\in K,\; b\in B_k,\; i\in I
$$

### 5.5 Train position coverage on every block

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{i\in I} x_{t,k,b,i} &\geq \text{min\_int}_{k,b}\,(1-c_t) &&\forall t,k,b \\
\sum_{i\in I} x_{t,k,b,i} &\leq \text{max\_int}_{k,b}\,(1-c_t) &&\forall t,k,b
\end{aligned}
$$

### 5.6 Time progression through consecutive blocks

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{ent}_{t,k,b+1} &\geq \text{ent}_{t,k,b} + \tfrac{L_{k,b}}{v_{t,k,b}} - M\,c_t &&\forall t,k,b\in B_k\setminus\{|B_k|\} \\
\text{ent}_{t,k,1} &\geq d_{t,s_k} - M\,c_t &&\forall t,k \\
\text{ent}_{t,k,1} &\leq d_{t,s_k} + M\,(1-c_t) &&\forall t,k \\
a_{t,s_{k+1}} &\geq \text{ent}_{t,k,|B_k|}+\tfrac{L_t}{v_{t,k,|B_k|}} - M\,c_t &&\forall t,k \\
a_{t,s_{k+1}} &\leq \text{ent}_{t,k,|B_k|}+\tfrac{L_t}{v_{t,k,|B_k|}} + \Delta t &&\forall t,k
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $s_k$ is the origin station of segment $k$ and $s_{k+1}$ is its destination.

### 5.7 Linking entry time to space–time occupation

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{ent}_{t,k,b} &\leq i\,\Delta t + M\,(1-x_{t,k,b,i}) &&\forall t,k,b,i \\
\text{ent}_{t,k,b}+\tfrac{L_{k,b}}{v_{t,k,b}}+\tfrac{L_t}{v_{t,k,b}} &\geq i\,\Delta t - M\,(1-x_{t,k,b,i}) &&\forall t,k,b,i
\end{aligned}
$$

If $x_{t,k,b,i}=1$, interval $i$ must overlap the train's occupation window $[\text{ent}_{t,k,b},\,\text{ent}_{t,k,b}+(L_{k,b}+L_t)/v_{t,k,b}]$.

### 5.8 Speed limits

$$
v_{\min} \leq v_{t,k,b} \leq v_{\max} &&\forall t,k,b
$$

### 5.9 Acceleration and deceleration limits between consecutive blocks

$$
\begin{aligned}
v_{t,k,b+1}-v_{t,k,b} &\leq a_{\max}\,\tfrac{L_{k,b}}{v_{t,k,b}} + M\,c_t &&\forall t,k,b\in B_k\setminus\{|B_k|\} \\
v_{t,k,b}-v_{t,k,b+1} &\leq d_{\max}\,\tfrac{L_{k,b}}{v_{t,k,b}} + M\,c_t &&\forall t,k,b\in B_k\setminus\{|B_k|\}
\end{aligned}
$$

The right-hand side $a_{\max}\,L_{k,b}/v_{t,k,b}$ is the maximum feasible speed change over distance $L_{k,b}$ (kinematic bound $\Delta v \le a\cdot\Delta t = a\cdot L/v$).

### 5.10 Segment-length consistency

$$
\sum_{b\in B_k} L_{k,b} = L_k &&\forall k
$$

### 5.11 Disruption handling on segment $k_d$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{ent}_{t,k_d,1} &\geq T_d^{\text{st}} - M\,(1-\alpha_{t,k_d}) &&\forall t \\
\text{ent}_{t,k_d,1} &\leq T_d^{\text{end}} + M\,\alpha_{t,k_d} &&\forall t \\
z_{t,k_d} &\geq \alpha_{t,k_d} &&\forall t \\
x_{t,k_d,b,i} &\leq z_{t,k_d} + (1-\gamma_{k_d,i}) &&\forall t,\,b\in B_{k_d},\, i\in I
\end{aligned}
$$

$\alpha_{t,k_d}=1$ iff the train would enter the disrupted segment during the blockage window. In that case $z_{t,k_d}=1$ is forced (rerouting is mandatory). The last constraint forbids occupying the original track during any interval that overlaps the blockage, unless the train has rerouted.

### 5.12 Same-direction ordering and headway

$$
\begin{aligned}
o_{t_1,t_2,k}+o_{t_2,t_1,k} &\geq 1 - c_{t_1}-c_{t_2} &&\forall (t_1,t_2)\in D,\;k\\
o_{t_1,t_2,k}+o_{t_2,t_1,k} &\leq 1 &&\forall (t_1,t_2)\in D,\;k\\
\text{ent}_{t_2,k,1} &\geq \text{ent}_{t_1,k,|B_k|} + \tfrac{L_t}{v_{t_1,k,|B_k|}} + h_{\min} \\
&\quad - M(1-o_{t_1,t_2,k}) - M\,c_{t_1} - M\,c_{t_2} &&\forall (t_1,t_2)\in D,\;k
\end{aligned}
$$

### 5.13 Bidirectional (opposite-direction) conflict on shared rerouted track

$$
\begin{aligned}
o'_{t_1,t_2,k}+o'_{t_2,t_1,k} &\leq 1 &&\forall (t_1,t_2)\in D',\;k\\
o'_{t_1,t_2,k}+o'_{t_2,t_1,k} &\geq 1 - M(c_{t_1}+c_{t_2}) - M(2-z_{t_1,k}-z_{t_2,k}) &&\forall (t_1,t_2)\in D',\;k\\
\text{ent}_{t_2,k,1} &\geq \text{ent}_{t_1,k,|B_k|} + \tfrac{L_t}{v_{t_1,k,|B_k|}} + h_{\min} \\
&\quad - M(1-o'_{t_1,t_2,k}) - M\,c_{t_1} - M\,c_{t_2} - M(2-z_{t_1,k}-z_{t_2,k}) &&\forall (t_1,t_2)\in D',\;k\\
\text{ent}_{t_1,k,1} &\geq \text{ent}_{t_2,k,|B_k|} + \tfrac{L_t}{v_{t_2,k,|B_k|}} + h_{\min} \\
&\quad - M(1-o'_{t_2,t_1,k}) - M\,c_{t_1} - M\,c_{t_2} - M(2-z_{t_1,k}-z_{t_2,k}) &&\forall (t_1,t_2)\in D',\;k
\end{aligned}
$$

When **both** trains reroute onto the same track on segment $k$ and neither is cancelled, exactly one of the two orderings must hold with proper headway. The Big-M term $M(2-z_{t_1,k}-z_{t_2,k})$ activates the constraint only in this case.

### 5.14 Piecewise-linear energy model (convex combination with SOS2)

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{r\in R}\lambda_{t,k,b,r} &= 1 &&\forall t,k,b \\
v_{t,k,b} &= \sum_{r\in R}\lambda_{t,k,b,r}\,v_r &&\forall t,k,b \\
e_{t,k,b} &= \sum_{r\in R}\lambda_{t,k,b,r}\,E_r &&\forall t,k,b \\
\lambda_{t,k,b,r} &\geq 0,\quad \lambda_{t,k,b,r}\leq (1-c_t) &&\forall t,k,b,r \\
\text{SOS2}&(\lambda_{t,k,b,1},\dots,\lambda_{t,k,b,R}) &&\forall t,k,b
\end{aligned}
$$

The SOS2 constraint enforces at most two adjacent breakpoints to be active, yielding an exact piecewise-linear representation of the convex function $E(v)=p_0+p_1v+p_2v^2$.

### 5.15 Rerouting cost

Captured directly in the objective via $W_{\text{reroute}}\sum_{t,k} z_{t,k}$.

### 5.16 Boundary conditions

$$
\begin{aligned}
d_{t,1} &= T^{\text{dep}}_{t,1} &&\forall t \\
a_{t,|S|} &\leq T^{\text{arr}}_{t,|S|}+\delta_{\max} &&\forall t
\end{aligned}
$$

### 5.17 Time-horizon bounds

$$
0 \leq a_{t,s},\,d_{t,s},\,\text{ent}_{t,k,b} \leq T_{\text{hor}} &&\forall t,s,k,b
$$

---

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

**Three-layer decision structure.** The variables are organized in three layers that are co-optimized:

1. **Rescheduling layer** ($a_{t,s}, d_{t,s}, s_{t,k}, z_{t,k}, c_t, o_{t_1,t_2,k}, o'_{t_1,t_2,k}$) decides *when* and *on which track* each train moves, whether it is rerouted or cancelled, and how trains are ordered in conflicts.
2. **Block-occupation layer** ($x_{t,k,b,i}, \text{ent}_{t,k,b}$) maps continuous train movements onto the discrete time–space network used for capacity and headway constraints.
3. **Speed-management layer** ($v_{t,k,b}, e_{t,k,b}, \lambda_{t,k,b,r}$) decides block-level average speeds and computes the resulting energy through a piecewise-linear approximation of the nonlinear traction function.

**Space–time network (5.4–5.5, 5.7).** The double-track line is discretized into segments → block sections → time intervals. Constraint (5.4) enforces block exclusivity; (5.5) ensures every active train traverses each block a feasible number of intervals; (5.7) ties $x$ to the physical entry time $\text{ent}_{t,k,b}$.

**Retiming through stations (5.1–5.3, 5.16).** Dwell is bounded by $[t_{\min}^{\text{dw}},t_{\max}^{\text{dw}}]$, the running time $s_{t,k}$ is decomposed into per-block traversal plus the train-length traversal of the last block, and $\delta_{t,s}$ measures lateness. Cancelled trains are deactivated via $M(1-c_t)$ relaxations.

**Speed profiles and dynamics (5.6, 5.8–5.9).** Speeds vary per block. Block-to-block variation is bounded by $a_{\max}$ and $d_{\max}$ using $\Delta v \le a\cdot L/v$, which couples adjacent blocks and creates realistic energy-efficient speed profiles.

**Energy minimization via SOS2 (5.14).** The convex quadratic $E(v)=p_0+p_1v+p_2v^2$ is approximated exactly using breakpoints $(v_r, E_r)$ and convex-combination variables $\lambda$ with an SOS2 constraint, supported natively by CPLEX, Gurobi, and SCIP.

**Disruption and rerouting (5.11).** The auxiliary binary $\alpha_{t,k_d}$ detects whether a train's entry time falls inside $[T_d^{\text{st}},T_d^{\text{end}}]$. If so, $z_{t,k_d}=1$ is forced, redirecting the train to the opposite track. The capacity constraint on $x$ further prevents any train from sitting on the original track during the blocked window.

**Conflict resolution on rerouted track (5.13).** Because two opposite-direction trains may both reroute onto the same track, mutual ordering with headway $h_{\min}$ is required. The Big-M terms $M(2-z_{t_1,k}-z_{t_2,k})$ deactivate the ordering constraints unless both trains are actively rerouted — exactly the physical situation that creates bidirectional conflicts.

**Cancellation and rerouting penalties (objective).** Cancelled trains pay $W_{\text{cancel}}$, rerouting pays $W_{\text{reroute}}\sum z$, letting the operator trade off service quality, energy, and infrastructure use.

**Integration of TRP and TSMP.** The model is *truly integrated*: the speed variable $v_{t,k,b}$ enters both the running-time expressions (5.1, 5.6) and the energy expression (5.14); the time variables $a,d,\text{ent}$ and the block-occupation variables $x$ simultaneously determine feasible speed profiles through the kinematic (5.9) and headway (5.12–5.13) constraints. Rerouting and cancellation decisions couple with speed through (5.11), so the optimizer trades off *delay vs. energy vs. rerouting vs. cancellation* in a single optimization.

**Assumptions made explicit (since the paper text left them implicit):**

1. *Single-disruption scenario*: exactly one disrupted segment $k_d$ with one time window; extension to multiple disruptions is straightforward via additional $\alpha_{t,k_d^{(j)}}$ indicators.
2. *Rerouting is track-level*: the rerouting decision $z_{t,k}$ is binary per segment (reroute entirely or not); partial-segment rerouting is not considered.
3. *Block-level average speed*: speed profiles are approximated by a piecewise-constant speed at the block-section level; this is the standard discretization used in TSMP literature and is sufficient for energy accounting.
4. *No intermediate stops within a segment*: a train traverses every block of a segment consecutively (no entering/exiting the segment between blocks).
5. *Symmetric bidirectional conflicts*: a train on its original track never conflicts with an opposite-direction train, because each direction has its own dedicated track; conflicts arise *only* on the rerouted track where $z_{t,k}=1$.
6. *Discrete-time capacity*: block capacity is modeled per interval $i$ (interval length $\Delta t$), which is standard for space–time network formulations.
7. *Origin/destination treated as boundary stations*: $s=1$ and $s=|S|$ have no upstream/downstream segments respectively.
8. *Same-destination/same-origin assumption for $D$ and $D'$*: the conflict sets contain train pairs that share at least one segment in their route (or could reroute through a shared segment).

Text:
# MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

Based on the input describing an integrated framework for handling partial segment blockages on bidirectional high-speed railways, I present a complete MILP formulation that jointly optimizes retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and energy-efficient speed-profile selection.

---

## 1. Modeling Assumptions

**A1.** The planning horizon is discretized into time steps; time is measured in minutes.
**A2.** The corridor is a linear sequence of stations; each station pair is connected by one or more physical blocks in each direction.
**A3.** Each physical block $b$ has two directional sub-blocks $(b,k)$ for $k \in \{\uparrow, \downarrow\}$.
**A4.** A *partial* blockage on $(b,k)$ reduces its capacity by a factor $\beta_{b,k} \in [0,1]$ and may impose a maximum allowable speed $v^{\max}_{b,k}$; a *full* blockage corresponds to $\beta_{b,k}=1$ (zero capacity).
**A5.** Each train has a pre-defined origin–destination (OD), a set of feasible routes $\mathcal{R}_t$ (original + detours), and a discrete set of admissible speed profiles $\mathcal{V}_t$.
**A6.** Running time and energy consumption on a block are jointly determined by the chosen route and speed profile (lookup tables from offline train simulation).
**A7.** Dwell times are flexible within $[dw_s^{\min}, dw_s^{\max}]$.
**A8.** Cancellation is allowed only when no feasible (route, profile, retiming) combination exists; it carries a high penalty.
**A9.** Trains of opposite directions may share a physical block but cannot occupy it simultaneously (single-track bidirectional sections) or share only with headway (double-track).
**A10.** Reordering is allowed only between trains of the same direction on a given block.

---

## 2. Sets

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, $t \in T$ |
| $T^{\uparrow}, T^{\downarrow}$ | Trains travelling up / down |
| $S$ | Ordered set of stations, $s \in S$ |
| $B$ | Set of physical blocks, $b \in B$ |
| $K = \{\uparrow, \downarrow\}$ | Set of directions |
| $\mathcal{B} = B \times K$ | Set of directional blocks, $(b,k) \in \mathcal{B}$ |
| $\mathcal{R}_t$ | Set of feasible routes for train $t$, $r \in \mathcal{R}_t$ |
| $\mathcal{V}_t$ | Set of feasible speed profiles for train $t$, $v \in \mathcal{V}_t$ |
| $\mathcal{B}^{r}_{t}$ | Set of directional blocks traversed by train $t$ on route $r$ |
| $\mathcal{S}^{r}_{t}$ | Set of stations visited by train $t$ on route $r$ (ordered) |
| $\mathcal{B}(s,s')$ | Set of directional blocks between consecutive stations $s$ and $s+1$ |
| $\mathcal{T}(b,k)$ | Set of trains that may use directional block $(b,k)$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

### Infrastructure

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $L_{b}$ | Length of block $b$ | km |
| $Cap_{b,k}$ | Nominal capacity of directional block $(b,k)$ | trains |
| $\beta_{b,k} \in [0,1]$ | Blockage severity on $(b,k)$ ($0=$free, $1=$fully blocked) | – |
| $v^{\max}_{b,k}$ | Maximum permitted speed on $(b,k)$ under blockage | km/h |
| $h^{\min}_{b,k}$ | Minimum headway on $(b,k)$ | min |
| $h^{\min}_{s}$ | Minimum station headway | min |
| $H$ | Planning horizon | min |

### Operational

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $TT^{v}_{t,b,r}$ | Running time of train $t$ on block $b$ using route $r$ and profile $v$ | min |
| $EC^{v}_{t,b,r}$ | Energy consumption of train $t$ on block $b$ using route $r$ and profile $v$ | kWh |
| $dw^{\min}_{s}, dw^{\max}_{s}$ | Min / max dwell time at station $s$ | min |
| $arr^{0}_{t,s}, dep^{0}_{t,s}$ | Originally scheduled arrival / departure times | min |
| $a^{0}_{t}, d^{0}_{t}$ | Original origin departure / destination arrival of train $t$ | min |
| $\Delta^{\max}_{t}$ | Maximum allowable arrival delay for train $t$ | min |

### Economic

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $C^{\text{cancel}}_{t}$ | Penalty for cancelling train $t$ | $ |
| $C^{\text{delay}}$ | Cost per minute of passenger delay | $/min |
| $C^{\text{energy}}$ | Cost per kWh | $/kWh |
| $C^{\text{reroute}}_{t}$ | Fixed cost of rerouting train $t$ | $ |
| $C^{\text{profile}}_{t,v}$ | Bonus/penalty for selecting profile $v$ (energy-efficiency premium) | $ |

### Technical

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (big-$M$) |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Binary Variables

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $x_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses route $r$ |
| $y_{t,v} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses speed profile $v$ |
| $z_{t} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled |
| $f_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ traverses directional block $(b,k)$ |
| $o_{t,t',b,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ departs block $(b,k)$ no later than train $t'$ |
| $u_{t,r,v} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses the (route, profile) pair $(r,v)$ (linking) |

### 4.2 Continuous Variables

| Variable | Meaning | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{t,s} \geq 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ | min |
| $d_{t,s} \geq 0$ | Actual departure time of train $t$ from station $s$ | min |
| $w_{t,s} \geq 0$ | Actual dwell time of train $t$ at station $s$ | min |
| $\tau_{t,b,k} \geq 0$ | Actual running time of train $t$ on directional block $(b,k)$ | min |
| $\delta_{t,s} \geq 0$ | Arrival delay of train $t$ at station $s$ | min |
| $E \geq 0$ | Total energy consumption | kWh |
| $D \geq 0$ | Total passenger delay | min |

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; C^{\text{energy}}\, E \;+\; C^{\text{delay}}\, D \;+\; \sum_{t \in T} C^{\text{cancel}}_{t}\, z_{t} \;+\; \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_t \setminus \{r^0_t\}} C^{\text{reroute}}_{t}\, x_{t,r} \;+\; \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}_t} C^{\text{profile}}_{t,v}\, y_{t,v}
$$

where
$$
E = \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_t}\sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}_t}\sum_{(b,k) \in \mathcal{B}^{r}_{t}} EC^{v}_{t,b,r}\; u_{t,r,v}
$$
$$
D = \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}_t} \delta_{t,s}
$$

The first term captures **energy cost**, the second **passenger-delay cost**, the third **cancellation penalties**, the fourth **rerouting penalties**, and the last **speed-profile preference** (e.g., rewarding energy-efficient coasting profiles).

---

## 6. Constraints

### A. Routing, Profile, and Cancellation Linking

**(A1) Exactly one route per non-cancelled train**
$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_t} x_{t,r} + z_t = 1, \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(A2) Exactly one speed profile per non-cancelled train**
$$
\sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}_t} y_{t,v} + z_t = 1, \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(A3) Linking route and profile**
$$
u_{t,r,v} \leq x_{t,r}, \quad u_{t,r,v} \leq y_{t,v}, \quad \forall t, r \in \mathcal{R}_t, v \in \mathcal{V}_t
$$
$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_t}\sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}_t} u_{t,r,v} + z_t = 1, \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(A4) Block traversal equals route usage**
$$
f_{t,b,k} = \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_t : (b,k) \in \mathcal{B}^{r}_{t}} x_{t,r}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; (b,k) \in \mathcal{B}
$$

**(A5) Blocked blocks cannot be used**
$$
f_{t,b,k} \leq 1 - \beta_{b,k}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; (b,k) \in \mathcal{B}
$$

> *Interpretation:* if $\beta_{b,k}=1$ (fully blocked), $f_{t,b,k}=0$, forcing a reroute.

---

### B. Timetable Consistency

**(B1) Dwell-time definition**
$$
d_{t,s} = a_{t,s} + w_{t,s}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in \mathcal{S}_t
$$

**(B2) Dwell-time bounds**
$$
dw^{\min}_{s} \leq w_{t,s} \leq dw^{\max}_{s}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in \mathcal{S}_t
$$

**(B3) Running time on a directional block**
$$
\tau_{t,b,k} = \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_t}\sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}_t} TT^{v}_{t,b,r}\; u_{t,r,v}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; (b,k) \in \mathcal{B}
$$

**(B4) Inter-station propagation**
$$
a_{t,s+1} = d_{t,s} + \sum_{(b,k) \in \mathcal{B}(s,s+1)} \tau_{t,b,k}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in \mathcal{S}_t \setminus \{s_{|S|}\}
$$

**(B5) Origin departure window**
$$
d^{0}_{t} - M\, z_t \leq d_{t,s_1} \leq d^{0}_{t} + \Delta^{\max}_{t} - M\, z_t, \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(B6) Destination arrival bound**
$$
a_{t,s_{|S|}} \leq H, \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(B7) Delay definition**
$$
\delta_{t,s} \geq a_{t,s} - arr^{0}_{t,s}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in \mathcal{S}_t
$$
$$
\delta_{t,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in \mathcal{S}_t
$$

**(B8) Maximum delay**
$$
\delta_{t,s_{|S|}} \leq \Delta^{\max}_{t} + M\, z_t, \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(B9) Cancelled trains have zero timetable activity**
$$
a_{t,s} \leq M\,(1-z_t), \quad d_{t,s} \leq M\,(1-z_t), \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in \mathcal{S}_t
$$

---

### C. Conflict Resolution and Block Capacity

**(C1) Pairwise ordering on shared blocks (same direction)**
$$
o_{t,t',b,k} + o_{t',t,b,k} = f_{t,b,k} + f_{t',b,k} - 1, \quad \forall t < t' \in T^{\text{same dir}},\; (b,k) \in \mathcal{B}
$$

> *Interpretation:* if both trains traverse $(b,k)$, exactly one ordering holds.

**(C2) Headway on directional block (same direction)**
$$
a_{t',s_{b}^{+}} \geq a_{t,s_{b}^{+}} + h^{\min}_{b,k} - M\,(2 - o_{t,t',b,k} - f_{t,b,k}) - M\, z_{t'} - M\, z_t
$$
$$
\forall t \neq t' \in T^{\text{same dir}},\; (b,k) \in \mathcal{B}
$$
where $s_{b}^{+}$ is the first station after block $b$.

**(C3) Bidirectional conflict on single-track sections**
For any single-track block $(b,k)$ shared by both directions:
$$
o_{t,t',b,k} + o_{t',t,b,k} \leq 1, \quad \forall t \in T^{\uparrow},\; t' \in T^{\downarrow},\; (b,k) \in \mathcal{B}^{\text{single}}
$$

**(C4) Reduced block capacity due to blockage**
$$
\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}(b,k)} f_{t,b,k} \leq Cap_{b,k}\,(1-\beta_{b,k}), \quad \forall (b,k) \in \mathcal{B}
$$

**(C5) Station headway**
$$
d_{t',s} \geq a_{t,s} + h^{\min}_{s} - M\,(1 - o_{t,t',s}) - M\, z_t - M\, z_{t'}, \quad \forall t \neq t',\; s \in S
$$
where $o_{t,t',s}$ is the ordering of trains at station $s$.

---

### D. Speed-Profile Feasibility under Blockage

**(D1) Speed limit compliance**
$$
\tau_{t,b,k} \geq \frac{L_{b}}{v^{\max}_{b,k}} \cdot 60 \cdot f_{t,b,k}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; (b,k) \in \mathcal{B}
$$

> *Interpretation:* a partially blocked block imposes a lower bound on running time corresponding to the maximum allowed speed.

**(D2) Profile–route feasibility**
$$
u_{t,r,v} = 0 \quad \text{if } v \notin \mathcal{V}^{r}_{t}, \quad \forall t, r, v
$$
(where $\mathcal{V}^{r}_{t} \subseteq \mathcal{V}_t$ is the set of profiles feasible on route $r$).

---

### E. Energy Aggregation

**(E1) Total energy**
$$
E = \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_t}\sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}_t}\sum_{(b,k) \in \mathcal{B}^{r}_{t}} EC^{v}_{t,b,r}\; u_{t,r,v}
$$

**(E2) Non-negativity**
$$
E \geq 0
$$

---

### F. Delay Aggregation

**(F1) Total passenger delay**
$$
D = \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}_t} \delta_{t,s}
$$
$$
D \geq 0
$$

---

### G. Symmetry Breaking and Strengthening (optional)

**(G1) Route canonicalization**
$$
x_{t,r^0_t} \geq x_{t,r} \quad \text{for all } r \in \mathcal{R}_t \setminus \{r^0_t\}
$$
> *Interpretation:* prefer the original route unless rerouting is necessary (controlled by cost).

**(G2) Profile ordering**
$$
y_{t,v} \geq y_{t,v+1} \quad \text{for profiles ordered by energy efficiency}
$$

---

## 7. Summary of Model Structure

| Component | Type | Role |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{t,r}, y_{t,v}, z_t, u_{t,r,v}$ | Binary | Routing, profile, cancellation decisions |
| $f_{t,b,k}, o_{t,t',b,k}$ | Binary | Block usage and conflict ordering |
| $a_{t,s}, d_{t,s}, w_{t,s}, \tau_{t,b,k}, \delta_{t,s}$ | Continuous | Timetable and running-time variables |
| $E, D$ | Continuous | Aggregated performance metrics |
| Constraints (A)–(G) | – | Linking, feasibility, conflict resolution, capacity |

The model is a **mixed-integer linear program** because:
- The product $u_{t,r,v} = x_{t,r} \cdot y_{t,v}$ is linearized via constraints (A3).
- Big-M constraints (C2), (C5), (B5)–(B9) are linear.
- All coefficients come from offline train-simulation lookup tables $\{TT^{v}_{t,b,r}, EC^{v}_{t,b,r}\}$.

---

## 8. Possible Extensions

1. **Stochastic blockages** — replace $\beta_{b,k}$ with random variables and use a two-stage stochastic program.
2. **Passenger flow** — add OD demand and connection-protection constraints.
3. **Rolling-stock circulation** — couple trains sharing the same consist.
4. **Continuous speed profiles** — replace discrete $v$ with piecewise-linear speed/energy curves.
5. **Robust counterpart** — protect against uncertainty in $TT^{v}_{t,b,r}$ via budget-of-uncertainty sets.

---

This completes the full MILP formulation of the **Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem under Partial Segment Blockages**, integrating retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and energy-efficient speed-profile selection in a single conflict-free, capacity-feasible timetable.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem setting and assumptions

**Setting.** A bidirectional double-track high-speed railway corridor with stations ordered `1,…,S`. Trains `i ∈ I` run in one of two directions (down: `d`, up: `u`). During a disruption time window `[t^start, t^end]`, one track of a set of segments `A` (disruption area) is blocked; trains may pass the affected segments either on the operational track (if not blocked) or **reroute onto the opposite track**, which then becomes a single bidirectional track requiring mutual-exclusion (headway) constraints.

**Assumptions (assumptions are marked *A*):**
- *A1*: Trains are atomic; overtaking/reordering only at stations.
- *A2*: Each inter-station segment has a discrete set of candidate speed profiles `p ∈ P_{i,j}` for train `i` on segment `(j, j+1)`, each with fixed running time `τ_{ijp}` and energy consumption `E_{ijp}` (precomputed from train dynamics; piecewise-linear speed profiles discretized into speed levels — this linearizes the speed–time–energy coupling).
- *A3*: Acceleration/deceleration is embedded in the segment profiles; dwell times at stations are bounded `[dw_min, dw_max]`.
- *A4*: Rolling-block/fixed-block headway between successive trains on the same track/segment: minimum separation `h`.
- *A5*: The blocked track of segment `a ∈ A` is unavailable for all trains departing the segment within `[t^start, t^end]`; the opposite track remains available but is then shared bidirectionally.
- *A6*: Cancellation is not considered (all trains must run); delays are penalized linearly relative to the original timetable.
- *A7*: Time horizon discretized implicitly through variables; all relations are linear.

## 2. Sets and parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `I` | trains; `I_d`, `I_u` down/up trains |
| `J = {1,…,S}` | stations; segment `(j, j+1)`, `j ∈ J' = {1,…,S−1}` |
| `A ⊆ J'` | disrupted segments |
| `P_{ij}` | speed profiles for train `i` on segment `j`; `τ_{ijp}`, `E_{ijp}` |
| `a_{ij}` / `d_{ij}` | scheduled arrival/departure of train `i` at station `j` (original timetable) |
| `w` | unit delay weight; `α` | energy weight |
| `h` | minimum headway (time) |
| `t^s, t^e` | disruption start/end |

## 3. Variables

- `x_{ij}^arr`, `x_{ij}^dep ≥ 0`: actual arrival/departure time of train `i` at station `j`.
- `δ_{ij} ≥ 0`: arrival delay of train `i` at station `j`.
- `y_{ijp} ∈ {0,1}`: 1 iff train `i` uses profile `p` on segment `j`.
- `r_{ij} ∈ {0,1}`: 1 iff train `i` traverses disrupted segment `j ∈ A` on the **opposite (rerouted) track**.
- `b_{ik,j}` ∈ {0,1}: ordering variable =1 iff train `i` precedes train `k` on segment `j` (same track).

## 4. Objective

Minimize total weighted delay plus energy:

```
min  Z =  Σ_{i∈I} Σ_{j∈J} w · δ_{ij}  +  α · Σ_{i∈I} Σ_{j∈J'} Σ_{p∈P_{ij}} E_{ijp} · y_{ijp}      (1)
```

## 5. Constraints

**(a) Delay definition** (at terminal and intermediate stations):

```
δ_{ij} ≥ x_{ij}^arr − a_{ij},   δ_{ij} ≥ 0                  ∀ i, j                  (2)
```

**(b) Speed-profile selection (exactly one running time per segment):**

```
Σ_{p∈P_{ij}} y_{ijp} = 1                                       ∀ i, j ∈ J'            (3)
```

**(c) Coupling of timetable and speed profile (running time consistency):**

```
x_{i,j+1}^arr = x_{ij}^dep + Σ_{p∈P_{ij}} τ_{ijp} · y_{ijp}     ∀ i, j ∈ J'            (4)
```

This is the key integration constraint linking timetable times with control-level profiles.

**(d) Dwell time bounds:**

```
dw_min ≤ x_{ij}^dep − x_{ij}^arr ≤ dw_max                      ∀ i, j ∈ J \ {1,S}     (5)
```

**(e) Disruption time-window / blockage:**

A train may use the blocked (operational) track on `j ∈ A` only if it *enters* the segment after the disruption ends (linearized big-M):

```
x_{ij}^dep ≥ t^e − M · r_{ij}                                  ∀ i, j ∈ A             (6)
```

If `r_{ij}=0` (use operational track), departure must be after `t^e`; if `r_{ij}=1` (reroute), no such restriction.

**(f) Headway on the operational track (normal segments and undisrupted side):** for trains `i,k` on the same segment `j`, same track:

```
x_{k,j+1}^arr ≥ x_{i,j+1}^arr + h − M(1 − b_{ik,j}) − M(1 − σ_{ik})                    (7a)
x_{i,j+1}^arr ≥ x_{k,j+1}^arr + h − M·b_{ik,j}        − M(1 − σ_{ik})                  (7b)
```

where `σ_{ik}` is a parameter =1 iff trains `i,k` use the same track on `j` (determined by direction and rerouting variables; see *g*).

**(g) Rerouted bidirectional track mutual exclusion:** on `j ∈ A`, trains using the opposite track (both directions!) must be separated:

```
x_{k,j+1}^arr ≥ x_{i,j+1}^arr + h − M(1 − b_{ik,j}) − M(2 − r_{ij} − r_{kj})           (8a)
x_{i,j+1}^arr ≥ x_{k,j+1}^arr + h − M·b_{ik,j}      − M(2 − r_{ij} − r_{kj})           (8b)
```

Trains `i` and `k` conflict on `j` iff both are rerouted there (`r_{ij} = r_{kj} = 1`), regardless of direction.

**(h) Overtaking only at stations** (FIFO on each track/segment):

```
x_{i,j+1}^arr ≤ x_{k,j+1}^arr + M(1 − b_{ik,j}) − ε                             (9)
```

**(i) Departure-order consistency at stations (reordering allowed but consistent with segment order):**

```
x_{ij}^dep ≤ x_{kj}^dep + M(1 − b_{ik,j})                                      (10)
```

**(j) Horizon bounds:**

```
0 ≤ x_{ij}^arr, x_{ij}^dep ≤ T                                                 ∀ i, j  (11)
```

**Variable domains:**

```
x_{ij}^arr, x_{ij}^dep, δ_{ij} ≥ 0;   y_{ijp}, r_{ij}, b_{ik,j} ∈ {0,1}
```

## 6. Notes on linearity and completeness

- All nonlinearity of train dynamics is absorbed into the *A2* discretization: each profile `p` precomputes `(τ_{ijp}, E_{ijp})` from tractive-force/speed limits, so (3)–(4) keep the model MILP.
- Big-`M` values: `M = T` (horizon length) suffices, since all time variables lie in `[0, T]`.
- Constraints (6)–(8) jointly enforce that during `[t^s, t^e]` no train occupies the blocked track, while rerouted trains sharing the opposite track are sequenced conflict-free.
- The model yields, for each train: arrival/departure times (retiming), segment order (reordering via `b`), track choice (rerouting via `r`), and the selected speed profile per segment — i.e., a conflict-free, executable timetable with energy-optimal driving strategies.

**Objective trade-off:** weight `w` vs `α` reflects dispatching priority (punctuality vs energy); the MILP is solved directly for small instances, or decomposed (master IP over train-order/route variables + per-train plan subproblems with profile enumeration, refined adaptively) for large instances.

Text:
I evaluated the three generated models. **Model 1** is the best: it is fully linear (nonlinear dynamics are handled via precomputed speed profiles, avoiding the ill-defined SOS2/occupancy formulations of Models 2 and 3), it cleanly separates physical vs. directed segments for bidirectional conflict resolution, and it covers all required features (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, disruption windows, energy–delay trade-off). Here it is:

---

# MILP for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

**Assumptions (marked where not given):**
- (A1) Train dynamics are linearized via a finite library of precomputed feasible speed profiles per segment (standard in the literature); each profile is characterized by entry/exit speed, running time, and energy.
- (A2) A single disruption window per affected physical segment; extension to multiple windows is straightforward.
- (A3) Big-M constants are chosen sufficiently large; time horizon is finite.

## Sets
- $I$: trains $i$; $S$: stations $s$; $E$: **directed** segments $e$ (from $s_e^{\text{up}}$ to $s_e^{\text{down}}$)
- $E_{\text{phys}}$: physical segments; each has directed versions $e^+, e^-$
- $R_i$: feasible routes of train $i$; $P_e$: feasible speed profiles on $e$, each with parameters $(v_p^{\text{in}}, v_p^{\text{out}}, \tau_p, \varepsilon_p)$
- $D$: disruptions $d$, each on physical segment $e_d$ with blocked window $[b_d, e_d]$

## Parameters
$L_e$ (segment length), $v_{\min}, v_{\max}$, $a_{\max}, a_{\text{brake}}$, $d_{\min}$ (headway), $\text{dwell}_{i,s}$, $\text{sched\_arr}_{i,s}$, weights $w_{\text{delay}}, w_{\text{energy}}$, $\text{penalty}_{\text{cancel}}$, big-$M$.

## Variables
**Binary:** $y_{i,e}$ (train $i$ uses directed segment $e$); $w_i$ (cancel train $i$); $u_{i,d}$ (train $i$ crosses disrupted segment before blockage); $z_{i,i',e}$ (ordering on same directed segment); $\gamma_{i,i',e^+,e^-}$ (bidirectional precedence); $s_{i,e,p}$ (speed profile selection); $d_{i,s}$ (stops at station $s$).

**Continuous:** $t_{i,s}^{\text{arr}}, t_{i,s}^{\text{dep}}$; $\tau_{i,e}$ (running time); $v_{i,e}^{\text{in}}, v_{i,e}^{\text{out}}$; $e_{i,e}$ (energy); $\text{delay}_{i,s} \ge 0$.

## Objective
$$\min\; w_{\text{delay}}\sum_{i,s}\text{delay}_{i,s} \;+\; w_{\text{energy}}\sum_{i,e} e_{i,e} \;+\; \text{penalty}_{\text{cancel}}\sum_i w_i$$

## Constraints

**1. Route flow & cancellation** — for each train $i$:
- Origin: $\sum_{e\in \text{Out}(o_i)} y_{i,e} = 1-w_i$; Destination: $\sum_{e\in \text{In}(d_i)} y_{i,e} = 1-w_i$
- Intermediate stations: $\sum_{e\in\text{In}(s)} y_{i,e} = \sum_{e\in\text{Out}(s)} y_{i,e}$
- $w_i = 1 \Rightarrow y_{i,e}=0\ \forall e$; also $t_{i,s}^{\text{arr}}=t_{i,s}^{\text{dep}}=0$ if cancelled.

**2. Timetable & dwell:**
$$t_{i,s}^{\text{dep}} \ge t_{i,s}^{\text{arr}} + \text{dwell}_{i,s}\, d_{i,s}; \qquad d_{i,s}=0 \Rightarrow t_{i,s}^{\text{dep}} = t_{i,s}^{\text{arr}}$$
For segment $e$ from $s$ to $s'$: $t_{i,s'}^{\text{arr}} = t_{i,s}^{\text{dep}} + \tau_{i,e}$.

**3. Speed profile selection** — for each $i, e$:
$$\sum_{p\in P_e} s_{i,e,p} = y_{i,e},\quad v_{i,e}^{\text{in}} = \sum_p v_p^{\text{in}} s_{i,e,p},\quad v_{i,e}^{\text{out}} = \sum_p v_p^{\text{out}} s_{i,e,p},\quad \tau_{i,e} = \sum_p \tau_p s_{i,e,p},\quad e_{i,e} = \sum_p \varepsilon_p s_{i,e,p}$$

**4. Speed continuity** — for consecutive segments $(e,e')$:
$$|v_{i,e}^{\text{out}} - v_{i,e'}^{\text{in}}| \le M(2 - y_{i,e} - y_{i,e'})$$
(analogous linearizations at stations for arrival/departure speeds).

**5. Acceleration limits at stopping stations** (for $d_{i,s}=1$):
$$v_{i,s}^{\text{dep}} - v_{i,s}^{\text{arr}} \le a_{\max}\,\text{dwell}_{i,s}, \qquad v_{i,s}^{\text{arr}} - v_{i,s}^{\text{dep}} \le a_{\text{brake}}\,\text{dwell}_{i,s}$$

**6. Same-direction headway** — with $z_{i,i',e} + z_{i',i,e} = 1$:
$$t_{i,s_e^{\text{down}}}^{\text{arr}} \ge t_{i',s_e^{\text{down}}}^{\text{arr}} + d_{\min} - M(1-z_{i,i',e}) - M(2-y_{i,e}-y_{i',e})$$
(and the symmetric constraint for $z_{i',i,e}$).

**7. Bidirectional conflict resolution** — for opposite directed segments $e^+, e^-$ of the same physical segment, with binary $\gamma$:
$$t_{i,s_{e^+}^{\text{down}}}^{\text{arr}} \le t_{i',s_{e^-}^{\text{up}}}^{\text{dep}} + M(1-\gamma) + M(1-y_{i,e^+}) + M(1-y_{i',e^-})$$
$$t_{i',s_{e^-}^{\text{down}}}^{\text{arr}} \le t_{i,s_{e^+}^{\text{up}}}^{\text{dep}} + M\gamma + M(1-y_{i,e^+}) + M(1-y_{i',e^-})$$

**8. Disruption blockage** — for each $d\in D$ and train $i$ using $e^+$ or $e^-$, with binary $u_{i,d}$ (pass before / after):
$$t_{i,s_{e^+}^{\text{down}}}^{\text{arr}} \le b_d + M(1-u_{i,d}) + M(1-y_{i,e^+})$$
$$t_{i,s_{e^+}^{\text{up}}}^{\text{dep}} \ge e_d - M\,u_{i,d} - M(1-y_{i,e^+})$$
(analogous for $e^-$).

**9. Delay definition:**
$$\text{delay}_{i,s} \ge t_{i,s}^{\text{arr}} - \text{sched\_arr}_{i,s}, \qquad \text{delay}_{i,s} \ge 0$$

## Key modeling features
- **Retiming/reordering**: continuous times + ordering binaries $z$; **rerouting**: flow conservation over directed segments (including the opposite track); **cancellation**: $w_i$ with penalty.
- **Speed management**: profile-selection binaries keep the model fully linear while capturing train dynamics and energy; continuity constraints link profiles across segments.
- **Bidirectional sharing**: precedence binaries $\gamma$ resolve conflicts on the shared physical track during the disruption window.
- **Disruption**: disjunctive big-$M$ constraints force trains to clear the blocked segment before $b_d$ or enter after $e_d$, or reroute/cancel.

# MILP Model for Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

Below is a complete mixed-integer linear programming formulation that captures the three sub-problems (rerouting, reordering, and rescheduling) described in the input. The model follows the alternative-graph / microscopic representation style referenced in the literature (Pellegrini et al., 2014; D'Ariano et al., 2008) and incorporates the pair-wise delay interpretation and delay-propagation features highlighted in the paper.

---

## 1. Modeling Assumptions

1. **Infrastructure representation (microscopic):** the rail network is described by a directed graph $G=(V,E)$ where $V$ are block sections / signals and $E$ are track sections between consecutive signals.
2. **Time discretization:** continuous time (events are real-valued).
3. **Train routes:** each train $t$ has a finite set of pre-computed feasible routes $R_t$ (output of a TRSP module, e.g., Samà et al., 2016).
4. **Conflict definition:** two trains are in conflict on a resource $e$ if both routes include $e$ and their planned times overlap.
5. **FIFO is not enforced**; ordering is a decision variable (the dispatcher decides which train goes first).
6. **Delays are non-negative** (no early running allowed in real-time dispatching).
7. **Delay propagation:** a delay incurred on edge $e$ propagates to all subsequent edges of the same route.
8. **Safety overlaps:** a margin $o_e$ must be kept clear behind a stop signal after a train has cleared it.
9. **Big-M** is used to linearize logical implications; $M$ is chosen sufficiently large (e.g., the planning horizon).
10. **Energy consumption** is modeled as a secondary term in the objective (weighted trade-off with delays, as in D'Ariano et al., 2010).

---

## 2. Sets

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, $t \in T$ |
| $E$ | set of track sections (edges), $e \in E$ |
| $V$ | set of nodes (signals, stations) |
| $R_t$ | set of feasible routes for train $t$, $r \in R_t$ |
| $K \subseteq T \times T \times E$ | set of potential conflicts (pairs of trains competing for resource $e$) |
| $E_r$ | ordered set of edges belonging to route $r$ |
| $e^{\text{first}}_r, e^{\text{last}}_r$ | first and last edge of route $r$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{t,r,e}$ | planned arrival time of train $t$ at the end of edge $e$ on route $r$ | min |
| $d_{t,r,e}$ | planned departure time of train $t$ at the start of edge $e$ on route $r$ | min |
| $\tau_{t,r,e}$ | minimum running time of train $t$ on edge $e$ along route $r$ | min |
| $h_e$ | minimum headway time on edge $e$ (safety gap between successive trains) | min |
| $o_e$ | safety overlap margin behind the stop signal of edge $e$ | min |
| $p_t$ | priority weight of train $t$ (passenger > freight, long-distance > regional) | – |
| $\rho_e$ | specific energy consumption of a train traversing edge $e$ | kWh/min |
| $M$ | sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) | min |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{t,r}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ is assigned route $r$, 0 otherwise |
| $y_{t,e}$ | continuous $\ge 0$ | actual time train $t$ traverses (arrives at end of) edge $e$ |
| $\delta_{t_1,t_2,e}$ | binary | 1 if train $t_1$ traverses edge $e$ before train $t_2$, 0 otherwise |
| $z_{t_1,t_2,e}$ | binary | 1 if train $t_1$ waits for train $t_2$ on edge $e$ (pair-wise waiting indicator) |
| $w_{t,e}$ | continuous $\ge 0$ | delay of train $t$ at edge $e$ |
| $W_t$ | continuous $\ge 0$ | total delay of train $t$ at destination |
| $E_t$ | continuous $\ge 0$ | additional energy consumption of train $t$ due to dispatching |

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total delays and additional energy consumption:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \sum_{t \in T} p_t \, W_t \;+\; \lambda \sum_{t \in T} E_t
$$

where $\lambda \ge 0$ is a trade-off parameter (set to 0 if only delays are minimized, as in the standard rtRTMP).

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Rerouting Constraints

**(R1) Exactly one route per train:**
$$
\sum_{r \in R_t} x_{t,r} \;=\; 1, \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(R2) Route–edge activation:** an edge $e$ is "active" for train $t$ only if a route containing $e$ is chosen (modeled via big-M):
$$
y_{t,e} \;\le\; M \sum_{r \in R_t : e \in E_r} x_{t,r}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; e \in E
$$

**(R3) Earliest departure from first edge of chosen route:**
$$
y_{t,e^{\text{first}}_r} \;\ge\; d_{t,r,e^{\text{first}}_r} \;-\; M(1 - x_{t,r}), \quad \forall t \in T,\; r \in R_t
$$

### 6.2 Reordering Constraints

**(O1) Mutual exclusivity of ordering on a shared resource:**
$$
\delta_{t_1,t_2,e} \;+\; \delta_{t_2,t_1,e} \;=\; 1, \quad \forall (t_1,t_2,e) \in K
$$

**(O2) Headway (minimum time gap) between successive trains on edge $e$:**
$$
y_{t_2,e} \;\ge\; y_{t_1,e} \;+\; h_e \;-\; M(1 - \delta_{t_1,t_2,e}) \;-\; M\bigl(2 - x_{t_1,r_1} - x_{t_2,r_2}\bigr),
\quad \forall (t_1,t_2,e) \in K,\; r_1 \in R_{t_1},\; r_2 \in R_{t_2}
$$

**(O3) Safety overlap behind stop signal:**
$$
y_{t_2,e} \;\ge\; y_{t_1,e} \;+\; h_e \;+\; o_e \;-\; M(1 - \delta_{t_1,t_2,e}) \;-\; M\bigl(2 - x_{t_1,r_1} - x_{t_2,r_2}\bigr),
\quad \forall (t_1,t_2,e) \in K^{\text{overlap}},\; r_1,r_2
$$

where $K^{\text{overlap}} \subseteq K$ is the subset of conflicts requiring overlap clearance (e.g., station exits, junctions).

### 6.3 Rescheduling Constraints

**(S1) Running time on consecutive edges of a route:**
$$
y_{t,e_{i+1}} \;\ge\; y_{t,e_i} \;+\; \tau_{t,r,e_{i+1}} \;-\; M(1 - x_{t,r}), \quad
\forall t \in T,\; r \in R_t,\; e_i, e_{i+1} \in E_r \text{ consecutive}
$$

**(S2) Non-negativity of delays:**
$$
w_{t,e} \;\ge\; y_{t,e} \;-\; a_{t,r,e} \;-\; M(1 - x_{t,r}), \quad \forall t \in T,\; r \in R_t,\; e \in E_r
$$

**(S3) Total delay at destination:**
$$
W_t \;\ge\; y_{t,e^{\text{last}}_r} \;-\; a_{t,r,e^{\text{last}}_r} \;-\; M(1 - x_{t,r}), \quad \forall t \in T,\; r \in R_t
$$

**(S4) Pair-wise waiting indicator (sub-optimal model feature):**
$$
z_{t_1,t_2,e} \;\le\; \delta_{t_2,t_1,e}, \quad \forall (t_1,t_2,e) \in K
$$
$$
z_{t_1,t_2,e} \;\ge\; \delta_{t_2,t_1,e} \;-\; \sum_{t_3 \neq t_1,t_2} \delta_{t_3,t_1,e}, \quad \forall (t_1,t_2,e) \in K
$$

**(S5) Pair-wise delay interpretation:** the delay of train $t_1$ on edge $e$ equals the sum of waiting times caused by all trains ordered before it:
$$
w_{t_1,e} \;\le\; \sum_{t_2 \in T : (t_1,t_2,e) \in K} z_{t_1,t_2,e} \cdot h_e \;+\; M(1 - \text{active}_{t_1,e})
$$

**(S6) Delay propagation (extended / optimal model):** a delay incurred on edge $e_i$ propagates to all subsequent edges $e_j$ of the same route:
$$
y_{t,e_j} \;\ge\; y_{t,e_i} \;+\; \tau_{t,r,e_j} \;-\; \tau_{t,r,e_i}^{\text{plan}} \;-\; M(1 - x_{t,r}), \quad
\forall t \in T,\; r \in R_t,\; e_i, e_j \in E_r,\; j > i
$$

where $\tau_{t,r,e_i}^{\text{plan}}$ is the planned running time on $e_i$. This is the key constraint that distinguishes the global-optimum model from the sub-optimal one.

### 6.4 Energy Consumption Constraints

**(E1) Additional energy due to dispatching:**
$$
E_t \;=\; \sum_{e \in E} \rho_e \cdot \bigl(y_{t,e} - a_{t,r,e}\bigr) \cdot x_{t,r}, \quad \forall t \in T
$$

(linearized with auxiliary variables if needed).

---

## 7. Model Variants

| Variant | Constraints used | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Sub-optimal (fast)** | R1–R3, O1–O3, S1–S5 | Provides route selection and ordering quickly, neglecting delay propagation. |
| **Global optimum** | R1–R3, O1–O3, S1–S4, **S6**, E1 | Adds delay-propagation constraint (S6) to guarantee optimality. |
| **Reference (Pellegrini et al., 2014)** | All R, O, S constraints without pair-wise reformulation | Original monolithic formulation; computationally expensive. |

---

## 8. Summary of Equations

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \; & \sum_{t \in T} p_t W_t + \lambda \sum_{t \in T} E_t \\
\text{s.t. } & \sum_{r \in R_t} x_{t,r} = 1, && \forall t \in T \quad \text{(R1)}\\
& y_{t,e^{\text{first}}_r} \ge d_{t,r,e^{\text{first}}_r} - M(1 - x_{t,r}), && \forall t,r \quad \text{(R3)}\\
& \delta_{t_1,t_2,e} + \delta_{t_2,t_1,e} = 1, && \forall (t_1,t_2,e) \in K \quad \text{(O1)}\\
& y_{t_2,e} \ge y_{t_1,e} + h_e + o_e - M(1-\delta_{t_1,t_2,e}) - M(2-x_{t_1,r_1}-x_{t_2,r_2}), && \forall K^{\text{overlap}} \quad \text{(O3)}\\
& y_{t,e_{i+1}} \ge y_{t,e_i} + \tau_{t,r,e_{i+1}} - M(1-x_{t,r}), && \forall t,r \quad \text{(S1)}\\
& W_t \ge y_{t,e^{\text{last}}_r} - a_{t,r,e^{\text{last}}_r} - M(1-x_{t,r}), && \forall t,r \quad \text{(S3)}\\
& y_{t,e_j} \ge y_{t,e_i} + \tau_{t,r,e_j} - \tau_{t,r,e_i}^{\text{plan}} - M(1-x_{t,r}), && \forall t,r,\, j>i \quad \text{(S6)}\\
& x_{t,r} \in \{0,1\},\; \delta_{t_1,t_2,e}, z_{t_1,t_2,e} \in \{0,1\}, \\
& y_{t,e}, w_{t,e}, W_t, E_t \ge 0.
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 9. Notes on Assumptions Marked as Reasonable

- The set $K$ of potential conflicts is assumed to be pre-computed from the planned timetable (standard practice).
- The big-M constant $M$ is assumed to be the planning horizon length.
- The trade-off parameter $\lambda$ between delay and energy is assumed tunable by the operator.
- The set of feasible routes $R_t$ is assumed to be provided by an external TRSP solver (Samà et al., 2016; Pascariu et al., 2022).
- Train priorities $p_t$ are assumed given (e.g., from timetable class).
- Energy is modeled linearly in delay time; more detailed traction models would require additional non-linear terms that are out of scope for a linear formulation.

# Integrated Rolling Stock Rescheduling MILP with Infrastructure Constraints

Below is a complete mixed-integer linear programming formulation for the rolling stock rescheduling problem during railway disruptions, integrating the composition model (Fioole et al., 2006) and the infrastructure model (Van Aken et al., 2017) into a single model. The formulation captures train composition, rolling stock circulation, shunting activities, and track-level infrastructure feasibility.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of train trips in the (possibly disrupted) timetable |
| $T^D \subseteq T$ | Set of trips that are canceled or severely delayed due to the disruption |
| $V$ | Set of rolling stock units (vehicles) |
| $S$ | Set of stations |
| $P_s$ | Set of tracks/platforms at station $s \in S$ |
| $P = \bigcup_{s\in S} P_s$ | Set of all tracks |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of discrete time periods (planning horizon) |
| $\mathcal{C} \subseteq T \times T$ | Set of feasible trip connections (pairs $(t,t')$ where a unit can physically continue from $t$ to $t'$) |
| $\mathcal{A}$ | Set of shunting activities (coupling, decoupling, parking) |
| $\mathcal{A}^{c}_{tt'} \subseteq \mathcal{A}$ | Coupling activities at the transfer between trips $t$ and $t'$ |
| $\mathcal{A}^{d}_{t} \subseteq \mathcal{A}$ | Decoupling activities at the end of trip $t$ |
| $\mathcal{A}^{p}_{t,u} \subseteq \mathcal{A}$ | Parking activities for unit $u$ after trip $t$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

**Trip parameters**
- $o_t, d_t \in S$: origin and destination of trip $t$
- $s_t, e_t \in \mathcal{T}$: scheduled departure and arrival times
- $q_t \in \mathbb{Z}^+$: passenger demand for trip $t$

**Rolling stock parameters**
- $\text{cap}_v \in \mathbb{Z}^+$: seat capacity of unit $v$
- $\text{len}_v \in \mathbb{Z}^+$: length of unit $v$
- $c_v \in \mathbb{R}^+$: operating cost of unit $v$ per trip

**Infrastructure parameters**
- $\text{len}_p \in \mathbb{Z}^+$: usable length of track $p$
- $\text{type}_p \in \{\text{through, siding, bay}\}$: track type (affects feasible activities)

**Time parameters**
- $\tau^c, \tau^d, \tau^p \in \mathbb{Z}^+$: time required for coupling, decoupling, and parking
- $\tau^{\min}_t \in \mathbb{Z}^+$: minimum dwell time at the destination of trip $t$
- $\delta^{\max} \in \mathbb{R}^+$: maximum allowed delay for non-disrupted trains

**Original plan**
- $\text{orig}_{t,v} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if unit $v$ was assigned to trip $t$ in the original plan

**Objective weights**
- $w_1, w_2, w_3, w_4 \in \mathbb{R}^+$: weights for operating cost, passenger service, plan deviation, and delay

**Big-M**
- $M$: sufficiently large positive constant

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Composition variables**
- $x_{t,v} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if unit $v$ is assigned to trip $t$
- $y_{(t,t'),v} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if unit $v$ operates both trip $t$ and the next trip $t'$ consecutively
- $w_{(t,t'),v,v'} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if units $v$ and $v'$ couple at the transfer between $t$ and $t'$
- $z_{t,v,v'} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if units $v$ and $v'$ decouple at the end of trip $t$

**Shunting activity variables**
- $\sigma_a, \varepsilon_a \in \mathcal{T}$: start and end time of shunting activity $a$
- $f_{a,p} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if shunting activity $a$ is performed on track $p$
- $o_{a,p,\tau} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if track $p$ is occupied by activity $a$ during time period $\tau$

**Service quality variables**
- $d_t \in [0, \delta^{\max}]$: delay (in minutes) of trip $t$
- $r_t \in \mathbb{R}^+$: capacity shortage on trip $t$ (passengers that cannot be seated)

**Plan-deviation variables**
- $\Delta_{t,v} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if assignment $(t,v)$ differs from the original plan

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; w_1 \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T}\sum_{v \in V} c_v \, x_{t,v}}_{\text{Operating cost}} \;+\; w_2 \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T} r_t}_{\text{Passenger shortage}} \;+\; w_3 \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T}\sum_{v \in V} \Delta_{t,v}}_{\text{Plan deviation}} \;+\; w_4 \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T} d_t}_{\text{Induced delays}}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Composition Constraints

**(C1) Trip coverage.** Every trip must be operated by at least one unit:
$$
\sum_{v \in V} x_{t,v} \;\geq\; 1 \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C2) Capacity with allowed shortage.** The composition must (approximately) satisfy demand:
$$
\sum_{v \in V} \text{cap}_v \, x_{t,v} \;+\; r_t \;\geq\; q_t \qquad \forall t \in T
$$
$$
r_t \;\geq\; 0 \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C3) Coupling requires both units assigned.** If two units are coupled on a trip, both must be present:
$$
x_{t,v} + x_{t,v'} \;\geq\; 2\,w_{(t,t'),v,v'} \qquad \forall (t,t') \in \mathcal{C},\; \forall v \neq v' \in V
$$

**(C4) Coupling implies both units continue.** A coupling activity only makes sense if both units also operate the next trip:
$$
w_{(t,t'),v,v'} \;\leq\; y_{(t,t'),v} \qquad \forall (t,t') \in \mathcal{C},\; \forall v \neq v' \in V
$$
$$
w_{(t,t'),v,v'} \;\leq\; y_{(t,t'),v'} \qquad \forall (t,t') \in \mathcal{C},\; \forall v \neq v' \in V
$$

**(C5) Decoupling requires both units on the trip.** Decoupling can only occur between two units that share a trip:
$$
z_{t,v,v'} \;\leq\; x_{t,v}, \quad z_{t,v,v'} \;\leq\; x_{t,v'} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; \forall v \neq v' \in V
$$

**(C6) Symmetry of coupling/decoupling:**
$$
w_{(t,t'),v,v'} = w_{(t,t'),v',v}, \qquad z_{t,v,v'} = z_{t,v',v}
$$

### 5.2 Rolling Stock Flow Conservation

**(C7) Connection requires assignment on both trips:**
$$
y_{(t,t'),v} \;\leq\; x_{t,v}, \qquad y_{(t,t'),v} \;\leq\; x_{t',v} \qquad \forall (t,t') \in \mathcal{C},\; \forall v \in V
$$

**(C8) At most one outgoing connection per unit arrival:**
$$
\sum_{t' : (t,t') \in \mathcal{C}} y_{(t,t'),v} \;\leq\; x_{t,v} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; \forall v \in V
$$

**(C9) At most one incoming connection per unit departure:**
$$
\sum_{t : (t,t') \in \mathcal{C}} y_{(t,t'),v} \;\leq\; x_{t',v} \qquad \forall t' \in T,\; \forall v \in V
$$

**(C10) Units of canceled trips must start from depots or other connections.** For each $t \in T^D$, the inflow equals the outflow (no unit can "teleport"):
$$
\sum_{t' : (t,t') \in \mathcal{C}} y_{(t,t'),v} \;=\; \sum_{t : (t,t') \in \mathcal{C}} y_{(t,t'),v} \qquad \forall t \in T^D,\; \forall v \in V
$$

### 5.3 Shunting Activity Linking

**(C11) Each coupling induces a coupling activity:**
$$
\sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}^{c}_{tt'}} f_{a,p} \;\geq\; w_{(t,t'),v,v'} \qquad \forall (t,t') \in \mathcal{C},\; \forall v \neq v' \in V
$$
where the activity must be located at $p \in P_{d_t}$ (the destination station of $t$).

**(C12) Each decoupling induces a decoupling activity:**
$$
\sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}^{d}_{t}} f_{a,p} \;\geq\; z_{t,v,v'} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; \forall v \neq v' \in V
$$

**(C13) Parking activities for idle units.** If a unit arrives but does not continue, a parking activity is required:
$$
x_{t,v} - \sum_{t' : (t,t') \in \mathcal{C}} y_{(t,t'),v} \;\leq\; \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}^{p}_{t,v}} f_{a,p} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; \forall v \in V
$$

### 5.4 Shunting Activity Timing

**(C14) Duration of shunting activities:**
$$
\varepsilon_a - \sigma_a \;\geq\; \tau^a - M(1 - f_{a,p}) \qquad \forall a \in \mathcal{A},\; \forall p \in P
$$
$$
\varepsilon_a - \sigma_a \;\leq\; \tau^a + M(1 - f_{a,p}) \qquad \forall a \in \mathcal{A},\; \forall p \in P
$$
where $\tau^a$ equals $\tau^c$, $\tau^d$, or $\tau^p$ depending on the activity type.

**(C15) Coupling/decoupling occurs after train arrival and before next departure:**
$$
\sigma_a \;\geq\; e_t + \tau^{\min}_t - M(1 - f_{a,p}) \qquad \forall a \in \mathcal{A}^{c}_{tt'},\; \forall p \in P_{d_t}
$$
$$
\varepsilon_a \;\leq\; s_{t'} + d_{t'} - M(1 - f_{a,p}) \qquad \forall a \in \mathcal{A}^{c}_{tt'},\; \forall p \in P_{o_{t'}}
$$

### 5.5 Infrastructure (Track) Constraints

**(C16) Track-occupancy definition.** A track is occupied by activity $a$ during every period between its start and end:
$$
o_{a,p,\tau} \;\geq\; f_{a,p} + \mathbf{1}\{\sigma_a \leq \tau \leq \varepsilon_a\} - 1 \qquad \forall a \in \mathcal{A},\; \forall p \in P,\; \forall \tau \in \mathcal{T}
$$
$$
o_{a,p,\tau} \;\leq\; f_{a,p}, \qquad o_{a,p,\tau} \;\leq\; \mathbf{1}\{\sigma_a \leq \tau \leq \varepsilon_a\} \qquad \forall a,p,\tau
$$

**(C17) Track capacity.** At most one shunting activity may occupy a track at any time:
$$
\sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} o_{a,p,\tau} \;\leq\; 1 \qquad \forall p \in P,\; \forall \tau \in \mathcal{T}
$$

**(C18) Track length.** The sum of unit lengths involved in an activity must fit on the chosen track:
$$
\sum_{v \in V_a} \text{len}_v \;\leq\; \text{len}_p + M(1 - f_{a,p}) \qquad \forall a \in \mathcal{A},\; \forall p \in P
$$
where $V_a$ is the set of units involved in activity $a$.

**(C19) Track-type compatibility.** A coupling/decoupling requires a through or siding track; parking requires a siding or bay track:
$$
f_{a,p} \;\leq\; \mathbf{1}\{\text{type}_p \in \text{AllowedTypes}(a)\} \qquad \forall a \in \mathcal{A},\; \forall p \in P
$$

**(C20) No conflict with passenger-train track occupancy.** Shunting activities cannot overlap with the dwell of passenger trains on the same track. For each trip $t$ occupying track $p_t$ from $e_t$ to $s_t + d_t$:
$$
o_{a,p_t,\tau} + \mathbf{1}\{e_t \leq \tau \leq s_t + d_t\} \;\leq\; 1 \qquad \forall a \in \mathcal{A},\; \forall \tau \in \mathcal{T}
$$

### 5.6 Delay Constraints

**(C21) Maximum delay for non-disrupted trains:**
$$
d_t \;\leq\; \delta^{\max} \qquad \forall t \in T \setminus T^D
$$

**(C22) Non-negativity of delays:**
$$
d_t \;\geq\; 0 \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

### 5.7 Plan-Deviation Constraints

**(C23) Linearization of absolute deviation:**
$$
\Delta_{t,v} \;\geq\; x_{t,v} - \text{orig}_{t,v} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; \forall v \in V
$$
$$
\Delta_{t,v} \;\geq\; \text{orig}_{t,v} - x_{t,v} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; \forall v \in V
$$

### 5.8 Variable Domains
$$
x_{t,v},\, y_{(t,t'),v},\, w_{(t,t'),v,v'},\, z_{t,v,v'},\, f_{a,p},\, o_{a,p,\tau},\, \Delta_{t,v} \;\in\; \{0,1\}
$$
$$
\sigma_a,\, \varepsilon_a \;\in\; \mathcal{T}; \qquad d_t \in [0,\delta^{\max}]; \qquad r_t \geq 0
$$

---

## 6. Key Assumptions

1. **Time discretization.** The planning horizon is discretized into uniform periods $\mathcal{T}$; all activity times and train times are integer multiples of this granularity.
2. **Single-track occupancy.** A track can host at most one shunting activity (or one train dwell) at any time. This is a simplification; in practice, parallel non-overlapping movements may be possible on long tracks — this can be relaxed by replacing (C17) with a more detailed conflict graph.
3. **Coupling/decoupling set membership.** The sets $\mathcal{A}^{c}_{tt'}$, $\mathcal{A}^{d}_{t}$, and $\mathcal{A}^{p}_{t,v}$ are pre-generated based on the timetable and station topology; only activities in these sets can be selected.
4. **Shortage definition.** $r_t$ measures the gap between demand and supplied seated capacity; standing passengers are implicitly allowed up to a limit defined by maximum train length.
5. **Delay absorption.** Short delays $d_t \leq \delta^{\max}$ are assumed to be absorbed by timetable buffers on the remainder of the train's line (consistent with the paper's assumption).
6. **Static disruption.** The set of disrupted/canceled trips $T^D$ is given exogenously; the model reschedules rolling stock around this fixed disruption.
7. **Track-type compatibility.** Predefined rules determine which shunting activity types are allowed on each track type (through/siding/bay).
8. **Unit homogeneity within type.** Coupling is only allowed between units of compatible types; this is enforced implicitly through the set $\mathcal{C}$ and the activity sets.

---

## 7. Notes on the Solution Approach

The integrated MILP above can be solved directly for small instances. For larger, practical instances, the paper's **Combinatorial Benders' decomposition** is obtained by:

- **Master problem:** Constraints (C1)–(C13), (C21)–(C23), and the objective — i.e., the *composition model*.
- **Subproblem:** Constraints (C14)–(C20) — i.e., the *infrastructure model*, which, given a fixed set of shunting activities, checks feasibility and returns **no-good cuts** of the form
$$
\sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}^{\text{conflict}}} f_{a,p} \;\leq\; |\mathcal{A}^{\text{conflict}}| - 1
$$
that are added back to the master problem.

The **iterative heuristic** processes shunting activities one at a time (mimicking the dispatcher interaction), feeding each suggested activity to the infrastructure model and accepting/rejecting it based on feasibility, which corresponds to relaxing the integrality of $f_{a,p}$ in the subproblem and processing activities sequentially.

---

This formulation captures the full integrated problem: assigning rolling stock to trips, deciding on couplings and decouplings, scheduling shunting activities in time and space, ensuring track-level feasibility at stations (including Utrecht Centraal and Rotterdam Centraal), and optimizing the weighted combination of operating cost, passenger service, plan adherence, and induced delays.

Text:
# MILP Formulation for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Sets
- $T$ — set of trains, indexed by $t \in T$
- $S$ — set of stations, indexed by $s \in S$
- $B$ — set of block sections, indexed by $b \in B$
- $D \subseteq B$ — set of disrupted (blocked) block sections
- $K$ — set of discretized time intervals, indexed by $k \in K$
- $P$ — set of candidate speed profiles for each train and block, indexed by $p \in P$
- $R = \{+1, -1\}$ — set of travel directions (forward, backward)

**Assumption:** The railway is double-track; each direction has its own normal track, but during disruptions bidirectional trains may share one track.

---

## 2. Parameters
- $\bar{a}_{t,s}$, $\bar{d}_{t,s}$ — scheduled arrival/departure time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $L_b$ — length of block section $b$
- $v_{\max}$, $v_{\min}$ — maximum/minimum allowed speeds
- $\Delta t$ — duration of one time interval
- $E_{t,b,p}$ — energy consumption of profile $p$ for train $t$ on block $b$
- $\tau_p$ — travel time of profile $p$ on block $b$
- $\delta$ — minimum safety headway time
- $M$ — sufficiently large constant (Big-M)
- $C^{\text{cancel}}$ — cancellation penalty
- $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ — weights for delay, energy, and cancellation
- $\mathcal{W} = [w^{\text{start}}, w^{\text{end}}]$ — disruption time window
- $\text{dw}^{\min}_s, \text{dw}^{\max}_s$ — minimum/maximum dwell times at station $s$

---

## 3. Decision Variables
| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{t,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{t,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual departure time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $x_{t,s,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ occupies station $s$ at time interval $k$ |
| $y_{t,b,k,r}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ traverses block $b$ during interval $k$ in direction $r$ |
| $z_{t,b,p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ adopts speed profile $p$ on block $b$ |
| $e_t$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled |
| $o_{t,t',b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ precedes train $t'$ on block $b$ |
| $u_{t,b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is rerouted on block $b$ |
| $\text{delay}_{t,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Arrival delay of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $\text{pos}_{t,b,k}$ | $\geq 0$ | Position of train $t$ on block $b$ at the end of interval $k$ |
| $v_{t,b,k}$ | $\geq 0$ | Speed of train $t$ on block $b$ during interval $k$ |
| $\rho_{t,b}$ | $\geq 0$ | Running time of train $t$ on block $b$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function
$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \alpha \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{s \in S}\text{delay}_{t,s} \;+\; \beta \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{b \in B}\sum_{p \in P} E_{t,b,p}\, z_{t,b,p} \;+\; \gamma \sum_{t \in T} C^{\text{cancel}}\, e_t
$$

The first term penalizes total delay (rescheduling quality), the second penalizes energy consumption (driving strategy), and the third penalizes service cancellations.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Activation / Cancellation
$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{t,s,k} = 1 - e_t \quad \forall t \in T,\; s = s_{\text{origin}}(t)
$$
$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{t,s,k} = 1 - e_t \quad \forall t \in T,\; s = s_{\text{dest}}(t)
$$

If $e_t = 1$, train $t$ is cancelled at all stations.

### 5.2 Station Flow Conservation
$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{t,s+1,k} - \sum_{k \in K} x_{t,s,k} \leq 1 - e_t \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
x_{t,s,k} \geq x_{t,s,k-1} - x_{t,s,k-2} \quad \text{(non-backtracking assumption)}
$$

### 5.3 Dwell Time at Stations
$$
d_{t,s} = a_{t,s} + \text{dw}_t \quad \text{with} \quad \text{dw}^{\min}_s \leq d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \leq \text{dw}^{\max}_s
$$

### 5.4 Arrival–Departure Linkage to Running Time (TRP–TSMP Coupling)
$$
a_{t,s+1} - d_{t,s} = \sum_{b \in B_s} \rho_{t,b} \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\rho_{t,b} = \sum_{p \in P} \tau_{t,b,p}\, z_{t,b,p} \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B
$$
$$
\sum_{p \in P} z_{t,b,p} = 1 - e_t \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B
$$

### 5.5 Speed-Profile Feasibility (Kinematic Constraints)
$$
\text{pos}_{t,b,k+1} - \text{pos}_{t,b,k} = v_{t,b,k}\, \Delta t \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$
$$
v_{\min}\, \bar{y}_{t,b,k} \leq v_{t,b,k} \leq v_{\max}\, \bar{y}_{t,b,k} \quad \text{where } \bar{y}_{t,b,k} = \sum_{r \in R} y_{t,b,k,r}
$$
$$
\text{pos}_{t,b,k} \leq L_b\, \bar{y}_{t,b,k} \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$
$$
\text{pos}_{t,b,0} = 0, \quad \text{pos}_{t,b,|K_b|} = L_b \quad \text{if } \sum_k \bar{y}_{t,b,k} \geq 1
$$

### 5.6 Linking Block Occupation to Speed Profiles
$$
\bar{y}_{t,b,k} \leq \sum_{p \in P} z_{t,b,p} \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$
$$
\sum_{k \in K} \bar{y}_{t,b,k} \geq 1 - e_t \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B
$$

### 5.7 Block Capacity (Unidirectional Sharing)
$$
\sum_{r \in R} \sum_{t \in T} y_{t,b,k,r} \leq 1 \quad \forall b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

**Assumption:** A single track section can be occupied by at most one train (regardless of direction) per time interval — modelling the bidirectional conflict on the shared opposite track.

### 5.8 Train Ordering and Headway on Blocks
$$
o_{t,t',b} + o_{t',t,b} = 1 \quad \forall t \neq t' \in T,\; b \in B
$$
$$
\sum_{k' \leq k} y_{t,b,k',r} \geq o_{t,t',b} - M(1 - \bar{y}_{t,b,k,r}) \quad \text{(ordering enforcement)}
$$

### 5.9 Station Headway
$$
a_{t',s} - a_{t,s} \geq \delta - M(1 - o_{t,t',s}) \quad \forall t \neq t',\; s
$$
$$
d_{t',s} - d_{t,s} \geq \delta - M(1 - o_{t,t',s})
$$

### 5.10 Partial Blockage / Disruption Window Constraints
For $b \in D$ and $k \in \mathcal{W}$, normal-direction traffic is prohibited:
$$
y_{t,b,k,r^{\text{norm}}_b} = 0 \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in D,\; k \in \mathcal{W}
$$

A train may pass a disrupted block $b \in D$ during $\mathcal{W}$ **only** via the opposite track (rerouting):
$$
y_{t,b,k,r^{\text{opp}}_b} \leq u_{t,b} \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in D,\; k \in \mathcal{W}
$$
$$
u_{t,b} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{W}} y_{t,b,k,r^{\text{opp}}_b} \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in D
$$

### 5.11 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution Under Rerouting
For two opposing trains $t, t'$ rerouted through the same block $b \in D$:
$$
y_{t,b,k,r^{\text{opp}}_b} + y_{t',b,k,r^{\text{norm}}_b} \leq 1 \quad \forall t,t' \in T,\; b \in D,\; k \in \mathcal{W}
$$
$$
\sum_{k} y_{t,b,k,r^{\text{opp}}_b} - \sum_{k} y_{t',b,k,r^{\text{norm}}_b} \leq M \cdot o_{t,t',b} \quad \forall t,t' \in T,\; b \in D
$$

### 5.12 Delay Definition
$$
\text{delay}_{t,s} \geq a_{t,s} - \bar{a}_{t,s} \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\text{delay}_{t,s} \geq d_{t,s} - \bar{d}_{t,s} \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\text{delay}_{t,s} \geq 0
$$

### 5.13 Rerouting Exclusivity
$$
u_{t,b} + (1 - u_{t,b})\cdot (1 - e_t) \geq \sum_{k \in \mathcal{W}} y_{t,b,k,r^{\text{norm}}_b} \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in D
$$

(Trains traversing a disrupted block in the disruption window must use rerouting.)

### 5.14 Variable Domains and Bounds
$$
0 \leq a_{t,s}, d_{t,s} \leq T_{\max}, \quad 0 \leq \text{pos}_{t,b,k} \leq L_b, \quad 0 \leq v_{t,b,k} \leq v_{\max}
$$
$$
x_{t,s,k}, y_{t,b,k,r}, z_{t,b,p}, e_t, o_{t,t',b}, u_{t,b} \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Summary of Key Assumptions

1. **Discretization** — Time, space, and speed are discretized into intervals $\Delta t$ for tractability.
2. **Double-track with single-track rerouting** — Normally two tracks (one per direction); during disruptions, both directions may share one track.
3. **Speed profile library** — Each train has a pre-computed finite set $P$ of energy-efficient speed profiles per block, characterized by $(\tau_{t,b,p}, E_{t,b,p})$.
4. **At most one train per block per interval** — Models bidirectional conflict via capacity constraint (5.7).
5. **Cancellation is final** — Once $e_t = 1$, no rescheduling decisions apply for $t$.
6. **Non-backtracking rerouting** — Rerouted trains stay on the opposite track only through the disruption window.
7. **Big-M linearization** — Used for ordering and conditional constraints.

This MILP jointly optimizes the **train timetable** (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) and the **speed profiles** (acceleration/deceleration driving strategies), explicitly handling bidirectional conflict resolution on shared track resources during partial segment blockages, in line with the integrated TRSMP framework described in the introduction.
