# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t, t' \in T$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s \in S$ |
| $B$ | Set of track segments, indexed by $b \in B$ |
| $K$ | Set of discrete time steps, indexed by $k \in K = \{1, \dots, n_K\}$ |
| $V$ | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed by $v \in V$ |
| $D = \{+1, -1\}$ | Set of travel directions (up/down) |
| $M_t$ | Set of driving modes for train $t$: $\{0$ (traction), $1$ (coasting), $2$ (braking)$\}$ |

**Assumptions (marked):**
- **(A1)** Time is discretized into steps of length $\Delta t$ (e.g., 10 s).
- **(A2)** Speed is discretized into a finite set $V$ of admissible levels.
- **(A3)** Each train has a fixed consist (mass, length, traction/braking characteristics).
- **(A4)** Dwell times at stations are bounded: $d^{\min} \le d_{t,s} \le d^{\max}$.
- **(A5)** Minimum headway $h^{\min}$ between consecutive trains on the same track.
- **(A6)** Energy consumption depends on speed level and driving mode.
- **(A7)** Cancellation is allowed as a last resort with a high penalty.
- **(A8)** A single partial blockage affects segment $b^*$ on one track during $[\tau^{\text{start}}, \tau^{\text{end}}]$.
- **(A9)** Rerouting diverts affected trains to the opposite (unblocked) track during the disruption window.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_b$ | Length of segment $b$ (m) |
| $v^{\min}, v^{\max}$ | Minimum/maximum operating speed (m/s) |
| $a^{\max}, b^{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration/deceleration (m/s²) |
| $\Delta t$ | Length of a time step (s) |
| $\tau^{\text{start}}, \tau^{\text{end}}$ | Start/end of disruption window on segment $b^*$ |
| $b^*$ | Index of the disrupted segment |
| $\text{AT}_{t,s}, \text{DT}_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival/departure time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $o(t), d(t)$ | Origin and destination stations of train $t$ |
| $\text{dir}(t) \in D$ | Direction of train $t$ |
| $d^{\min}, d^{\max}$ | Min/max dwell time at stations (s) |
| $h^{\min}$ | Minimum headway time (s) |
| $e^{\text{tr}}(v), e^{\text{co}}(v), e^{\text{br}}(v)$ | Energy rate at speed $v$ in traction/coasting/braking (kW) |
| $P^{\text{delay}}$ | Penalty per time unit of delay |
| $P^{\text{energy}}$ | Penalty per unit of energy |
| $P^{\text{cancel}}$ | Penalty for cancelling a train |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) |
| $\varepsilon$ | A small positive constant |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Rescheduling Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $a_{t,s} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{t,s} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Actual departure time of train $t$ from station $s$ |
| $\delta_{t,s} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Arrival delay of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $c_t \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled |
| $r_{t,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ is rerouted on segment $b$ |
| $o_{t,t',b} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ precedes train $t'$ on segment $b$ |
| $x_{t,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ is at station $s$ at time $k$ |
| $y_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ occupies segment $b$ at time $k$ on its normal track |
| $z_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ occupies segment $b$ at time $k$ on the opposite (rerouted) track |

### 3.2 Speed Management Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $v_{t,b,k} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Speed of train $t$ on segment $b$ at time $k$ (m/s) |
| $p_{t,b,k} \ge 0$ | Continuous | Position of train $t$ on segment $b$ at time $k$ (m) |
| $w_{t,b,k,v} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ on segment $b$ at time $k$ uses speed level $v$ |
| $m_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1,2\}$ | Discrete | Driving mode of train $t$ on segment $b$ at time $k$ |
| $e_t \ge 0$ | Continuous | Total energy consumption of train $t$ (kWh) |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = P^{\text{delay}} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \delta_{t,s} \;+\; P^{\text{energy}} \sum_{t \in T} e_t \;+\; P^{\text{cancel}} \sum_{t \in T} c_t \tag{1}
$$

The objective minimizes a weighted sum of (i) total passenger delay, (ii) total energy consumption, and (iii) the number of cancelled trains.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Flow Conservation at Stations

For each train $t$ and station $s \in [o(t)+1, d(t)]$:

$$
a_{t,s} = d_{t,s-1} + \sum_{b \in B_{t,s-1}} \text{RT}_{t,b} \tag{2}
$$

where $B_{t,s-1}$ is the set of segments between stations $s-1$ and $s$, and $\text{RT}_{t,b}$ is the running time of train $t$ on segment $b$ (linked to the speed profile via Eq. 14).

$$
d_{t,s} = a_{t,s} + \text{dwell}_{t,s} \tag{3}
$$

$$
d^{\min} (1 - c_t) \le \text{dwell}_{t,s} \le d^{\max} (1 - c_t) \tag{4}
$$

### 5.2 Delay Definition

$$
\delta_{t,s} \ge a_{t,s} - \text{AT}_{t,s} - M \cdot c_t, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{5}
$$

$$
\delta_{t,s} \ge 0, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{6}
$$

### 5.3 Cancellation Logic

If a train is cancelled, all its operational variables are zeroed:

$$
a_{t,s} \le M (1 - c_t), \quad d_{t,s} \le M (1 - c_t), \quad \forall t, s \tag{7}
$$

$$
y_{t,b,k} \le 1 - c_t, \quad z_{t,b,k} \le 1 - c_t, \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{8}
$$

### 5.4 Segment Occupancy and Rerouting

Each train occupies exactly one track (normal or rerouted) on each segment at each time:

$$
y_{t,b,k} + z_{t,b,k} \le 1, \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{9}
$$

$$
\sum_{k \in K} (y_{t,b,k} + z_{t,b,k}) \cdot \Delta t \ge \frac{L_b}{v^{\max}} (1 - c_t), \quad \forall t, b \tag{10}
$$

$$
\sum_{k \in K} (y_{t,b,k} + z_{t,b,k}) \cdot \Delta t \le \frac{L_b}{v^{\min}} (1 - c_t) + M \cdot c_t, \quad \forall t, b \tag{11}
$$

Linking rerouting indicator to occupancy:

$$
z_{t,b,k} \le r_{t,b}, \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{12}
$$

$$
r_{t,b} \le \sum_{k \in K} z_{t,b,k}, \quad \forall t, b \tag{13}
$$

### 5.5 Running Time from Speed Profile

The running time of train $t$ on segment $b$ is determined by the speed profile:

$$
\text{RT}_{t,b} = \sum_{k \in K} (y_{t,b,k} + z_{t,b,k}) \cdot \Delta t, \quad \forall t, b \tag{14}
$$

### 5.6 Position Dynamics

The position evolves according to the speed profile (linearized):

$$
p_{t,b,k+1} = p_{t,b,k} + v_{t,b,k} \cdot \Delta t, \quad \forall t, b, k \in K \setminus \{n_K\} \tag{15}
$$

$$
p_{t,b,1} = 0, \quad \forall t, b \tag{16}
$$

$$
p_{t,b,n_K} \ge L_b - M (1 - \sum_{k} (y_{t,b,k} + z_{t,b,k})), \quad \forall t, b \tag{17}
$$

### 5.7 Speed Dynamics

Acceleration limit:

$$
v_{t,b,k+1} - v_{t,b,k} \le a^{\max} \cdot \Delta t + M (1 - y_{t,b,k} - z_{t,b,k}), \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{18}
$$

Deceleration limit:

$$
v_{t,b,k} - v_{t,b,k+1} \le b^{\max} \cdot \Delta t + M (1 - y_{t,b,k} - z_{t,b,k}), \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{19}
$$

Speed bounds:

$$
v^{\min} \cdot (y_{t,b,k} + z_{t,b,k}) \le v_{t,b,k} \le v^{\max} \cdot (y_{t,b,k} + z_{t,b,k}), \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{20}
$$

### 5.8 Speed Level Selection (Discretization)

Exactly one speed level is selected when the train occupies the segment:

$$
\sum_{v \in V} w_{t,b,k,v} = y_{t,b,k} + z_{t,b,k}, \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{21}
$$

$$
v_{t,b,k} = \sum_{v \in V} v \cdot w_{t,b,k,v}, \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{22}
$$

### 5.9 Disruption Avoidance

During the disruption window on segment $b^*$, the normal track is unavailable:

$$
y_{t,b^*,k} = 0, \quad \forall t, k \in [\tau^{\text{start}}, \tau^{\text{end}}] \tag{23}
$$

Trains that would otherwise traverse $b^*$ during the disruption must reroute:

$$
\sum_{k \in [\tau^{\text{start}}, \tau^{\text{end}}]} y_{t,b^*,k} \le M \cdot (1 - r_{t,b^*}) + M \cdot c_t, \quad \forall t \tag{24}
$$

### 5.10 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution on Shared Track

When two trains of opposite directions share the rerouted track on segment $b$, they must be temporally separated by at least $h^{\min}$:

$$
a_{t',b}^{\text{exit}} - a_{t,b}^{\text{exit}} \ge h^{\min} - M (1 - o_{t,t',b}) - M (1 - r_{t,b}) - M (1 - r_{t',b}), \quad \forall t \ne t',\; b \tag{25}
$$

$$
o_{t,t',b} + o_{t',t,b} = 1, \quad \forall t \ne t',\; b \text{ with } \text{dir}(t) \ne \text{dir}(t') \tag{26}
$$

No two trains (any direction) may occupy the same physical location on the rerouted track at the same time:

$$
z_{t,b,k} + z_{t',b,k} \le 1 + M (1 - o_{t,t',b}) + M (1 - o_{t',t,b}), \quad \forall t \ne t',\; b, k \tag{27}
$$

### 5.11 Headway Constraint on Normal Track

For consecutive trains on the same segment in the same direction:

$$
a_{t',b}^{\text{entry}} - a_{t,b}^{\text{exit}} \ge h^{\min} - M (1 - o_{t,t',b}), \quad \forall t \ne t',\; b \text{ with } \text{dir}(t) = \text{dir}(t') \tag{28}
$$

### 5.12 Ordering Transitivity

$$
o_{t,t',b} + o_{t',t'',b} - 1 \le o_{t,t'',b}, \quad \forall t, t', t'' \in T,\; b \tag{29}
$$

### 5.13 Driving Mode and Energy Calculation

Exactly one driving mode is active when the train is on a segment:

$$
\sum_{m \in M_t} m_{t,b,k,m} = y_{t,b,k} + z_{t,b,k}, \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{30}
$$

Energy consumption per time step:

$$
e_t = \sum_{b \in B} \sum_{k \in K} \Delta t \cdot \left[ e^{\text{tr}}(v_{t,b,k}) \cdot m_{t,b,k,0} + e^{\text{co}}(v_{t,b,k}) \cdot m_{t,b,k,1} + e^{\text{br}}(v_{t,b,k}) \cdot m_{t,b,k,2} \right], \quad \forall t \tag{31}
$$

### 5.14 Coupling Between Rescheduling and Speed Management

The arrival time at the next station equals the departure time from the previous station plus the running time derived from the speed profile (Eq. 14). This is the **key coupling constraint** linking the operational layer (TRP) with the control layer (TSMP):

$$
a_{t,s} = d_{t,s-1} + \sum_{b \in B_{t,s-1}} \sum_{k \in K} (y_{t,b,k} + z_{t,b,k}) \cdot \Delta t, \quad \forall t, s \tag{32}
$$

### 5.15 Time Window Constraints

$$
a_{t,s} \ge \text{AT}_{t,s} - M \cdot c_t, \quad d_{t,s} \ge \text{DT}_{t,s} - M \cdot c_t, \quad \forall t, s \tag{33}
$$

$$
a_{t,s} \le \text{AT}_{t,s} + \Delta^{\max}, \quad d_{t,s} \le \text{DT}_{t,s} + \Delta^{\max}, \quad \forall t, s \tag{34}
$$

where $\Delta^{\max}$ is the maximum allowable deviation from the schedule.

---

## 6. Summary of the Model

The proposed MILP integrates:

- **Train Rescheduling (TRP):** arrival/departure times ($a_{t,s}, d_{t,s}$), train ordering ($o_{t,t',b}$), rerouting decisions ($r_{t,b}$), and cancellations ($c_t$) — Eqs. (2)–(13), (23)–(29), (33)–(34).
- **Speed Management (TSMP):** speed profiles ($v_{t,b,k}$), positions ($p_{t,b,k}$), driving modes ($m_{t,b,k}$), and energy consumption ($e_t$) — Eqs. (15)–(22), (30)–(31).
- **Coupling:** Eq. (32) explicitly links rescheduling times with speed-profile-derived running times, ensuring that every rescheduled timetable is executable at the control level.
- **Disruption Handling:** Eqs. (23)–(24) forbid use of the blocked track during the disruption window; Eqs. (25)–(27) resolve bidirectional conflicts on the shared rerouted track.

### Key Modeling Assumptions Recap
- **(A1)** Discrete time steps of length $\Delta t$.
- **(A2)** Discrete speed levels.
- **(A3)** Fixed train consist.
- **(A4)** Bounded dwell times.
- **(A5)** Minimum headway.
- **(A6)** Energy depends on speed and mode.
- **(A7)** Cancellation allowed with penalty.
- **(A8)** Single partial blockage on segment $b^*$ during $[\tau^{\text{start}}, \tau^{\text{end}}]$.
- **(A9)** Rerouting to the opposite track is the only disruption-mitigation strategy besides retiming and cancellation.

This MILP yields a **conflict-free rescheduled timetable together with executable energy-efficient speed profiles**, addressing the dual challenges of bidirectional conflict resolution and the coupling between rescheduling and speed management in a unified framework.

Text:
# CDR-DTG-MILP: A Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance-to-Go Signalling

## 1. Model Overview

This model extends the state-of-the-art RECIFE-MILP formulation (Pellegrini et al., 2015) to handle DTG signalling by introducing:

- **Discrete speed profile options** per train-run, enabling the modelling of speed-dependent braking distances.
- **Speed-dependent headways** based on braking distances rather than fixed block lengths.
- **Explicit brake indication points** that can lie anywhere along the track.
- **Distinction between switches and regular track**, with route-conflict logic at switches.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Set | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, $i, j \in \mathcal{T}$ |
| $\mathcal{E}_i$ | Ordered set of events for train $i$ (arrivals, departures, transits), $e \in \mathcal{E}_i$ |
| $\mathcal{E}_i^{arr}, \mathcal{E}_i^{dep}$ | Arrival / departure events of train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{B}$ | Set of trackside train detection sections (blocks), $b \in \mathcal{B}$ |
| $\mathcal{B}^{reg} = \mathcal{B} \setminus \mathcal{S}$ | Regular (open-line) blocks |
| $\mathcal{S} \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ | Set of switches (special blocks requiring route locking) |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of discrete speed profiles, $k \in \mathcal{K}$ |
| $\mathcal{R}_i$ | Runs of train $i$ (consecutive event pairs), $r \in \mathcal{R}_i$ |
| $\mathcal{R}_i^b \subseteq \mathcal{R}_i$ | Runs of train $i$ traversing block $b$ |
| $\mathcal{C}_b \subseteq \mathcal{T} \times \mathcal{T}$ | Train pairs that may conflict on block $b$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_s$ | Set of routes through switch $s$, $p \in \mathcal{P}_s$ |
| $\mathcal{CF}_s \subseteq \mathcal{P}_s \times \mathcal{P}_s$ | Conflicting route pairs at switch $s$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

### Time parameters
- $d_{i,e}$: scheduled time of event $e$ for train $i$
- $\tau_{i,e}^{\min}, \tau_{i,e}^{\max}$: time-window bounds for event $e$ of train $i$
- $\delta_{i,e}^{0}$: initial (given) delay of event $e$ for train $i$
- $t_{i,e}^{dwell}$: minimum dwell time at station event $e$

### Speed and braking parameters
- $v_{i,k}$: cruising speed of train $i$ under profile $k$
- $a_i^{br}$: (constant) braking deceleration of train $i$
- $\beta_{i,k} = \dfrac{v_{i,k}^{2}}{2\,a_i^{br}}$: braking distance of train $i$ under profile $k$
- $\rho_{i,r,k}$: running time of train $i$ on run $r$ under profile $k$

### Infrastructure parameters
- $L_b$: length of block $b$
- $L_i$: length of train $i$
- $t^{clear}$: clearance (safety) time after a train vacates a block
- $h_s^{sw}$: minimum route headway at switch $s$

### Objective parameters
- $c_{i,e}$: cost per time unit of delay for event $e$ of train $i$

### Big-M
- $M$: sufficiently large positive constant

---

## 4. Variables

### Continuous variables
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $t_{i,e} \geq 0$ | Actual time of event $e$ for train $i$ |
| $\Delta_{i,e} \geq 0$ | Delay of event $e$ for train $i$ w.r.t. scheduled time |
| $b_{i,b}^{in} \geq 0$ | Time train $i$ enters block $b$ |
| $b_{i,b}^{out} \geq 0$ | Time train $i$ exits block $b$ |
| $\tau^{IP}_{i,b} \geq 0$ | Time at which train $i$ reaches its brake indication point before block $b$ |

### Binary variables
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $x_{i,r,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $k$ on run $r$ |
| $y_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on block $b$ |
| $z_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if trains $i$ and $j$ are in conflict on block $b$ |
| $u_{i,s,p} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses route $p$ through switch $s$ |

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimise the total weighted delay over all trains and events:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_i} c_{i,e} \cdot \Delta_{i,e}
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Delay definition
$$
\Delta_{i,e} \;\geq\; t_{i,e} - d_{i,e} \qquad \forall\, i \in \mathcal{T},\; e \in \mathcal{E}_i \tag{1}
$$

### 6.2 Time-window bounds
$$
d_{i,e} + \tau_{i,e}^{\min} \;\leq\; t_{i,e} \;\leq\; d_{i,e} + \tau_{i,e}^{\max} \qquad \forall\, i, e \tag{2}
$$

### 6.3 Initial-condition delays
$$
t_{i,e_0} \;\geq\; d_{i,e_0} + \delta_{i,e_0}^{0} \qquad \forall\, i \in \mathcal{T} \tag{3}
$$

### 6.4 Speed-profile selection (exactly one profile per run)
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} x_{i,r,k} \;=\; 1 \qquad \forall\, i \in \mathcal{T},\; r \in \mathcal{R}_i \tag{4}
$$

### 6.5 Speed-dependent running time
$$
t_{i,e'} - t_{i,e} \;\geq\; \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \rho_{i,r,k} \cdot x_{i,r,k} \qquad \forall\, i,\; r=(e,e') \in \mathcal{R}_i \tag{5}
$$

### 6.6 Minimum dwell time at stations
$$
t_{i,e}^{dep} - t_{i,e}^{arr} \;\geq\; t_{i,e}^{dwell} \qquad \forall\, i,\; e \in \mathcal{E}_i^{station} \tag{6}
$$

### 6.7 Speed-dependent block traversal time
For every train $i$ and block $b$ traversed during run $r$:
$$
b_{i,b}^{out} - b_{i,b}^{in} \;\geq\; \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \frac{L_b}{v_{i,k}} \cdot x_{i,r,k} \qquad \forall\, i,\; b,\; r \in \mathcal{R}_i^{b} \tag{7}
$$

### 6.8 Linking block times to events
Let $e^{in}_{i,b}$ and $e^{out}_{i,b}$ denote the events immediately before entering and after exiting block $b$ for train $i$:
$$
b_{i,b}^{in} \;\geq\; t_{i,e^{in}_{i,b}} \qquad \forall\, i,\, b \tag{8a}
$$
$$
b_{i,b}^{out} \;\leq\; t_{i,e^{out}_{i,b}} \qquad \forall\, i,\, b \tag{8b}
$$

### 6.9 Block-ordering (mutual exclusion)
$$
y_{i,j,b} + y_{j,i,b} \;=\; 1 \qquad \forall\, (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_b,\; b \in \mathcal{B} \tag{9}
$$

### 6.10 Conflict-activation linking
$$
z_{i,j,b} \;\geq\; y_{i,j,b}, \qquad z_{i,j,b} \;\geq\; y_{j,i,b} \qquad \forall\, (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_b,\; b \tag{10a,b}
$$
$$
z_{i,j,b} \;\leq\; y_{i,j,b} + y_{j,i,b} \qquad \forall\, (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_b,\; b \tag{10c}
$$

### 6.11 DTG headway — speed-dependent separation (regular blocks)
For each pair $(i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_b$ and regular block $b \in \mathcal{B}^{reg}$, with $r_j^{b}$ the run of train $j$ that traverses $b$:

$$
b_{j,b}^{in} - b_{i,b}^{out} \;\geq\; t^{clear} \;+\; \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \frac{\beta_{j,k}}{v_{j,k}} \cdot x_{j,r_j^{b},k} \;-\; M\bigl(1 - y_{i,j,b}\bigr) \tag{11}
$$

**Interpretation.** Train $j$ may enter block $b$ only after train $i$ has exited, plus a clearance time, plus the time for train $j$ to cover its braking distance $\beta_{j,k}/v_{j,k}$ — which depends on the chosen speed profile $k$. This is the core DTG principle: the brake indication point can lie anywhere on the track, and the separation is governed by the *braking distance*, not by a fixed block length.

### 6.12 Brake indication point (explicit)
The brake indication point for train $j$ approaching block $b$ is reached at:

$$
\tau^{IP}_{j,b} \;=\; b_{j,b}^{in} \;-\; \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \frac{\beta_{j,k}}{v_{j,k}} \cdot x_{j,r_j^{b},k} \qquad \forall\, (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_b,\; b \tag{12}
$$

Constraint (11) is equivalent to $\tau^{IP}_{j,b} \geq b_{i,b}^{out}$, i.e. train $j$ must not pass its brake indication point before train $i$ has cleared block $b$.

### 6.13 Switch route selection
$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_s} u_{i,s,p} \;=\; 1 \qquad \forall\, i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}_i \tag{13}
$$

### 6.14 Switch route-conflict (route locking)
For each switch $s \in \mathcal{S}$, conflicting route pair $(p_i, p_j) \in \mathcal{CF}_s$, and train pair $(i,j)$:

$$
b_{j,s}^{in} \;\geq\; b_{i,s}^{out} + h_s^{sw} \;-\; M\bigl(2 - u_{i,s,p_i} - u_{j,s,p_j}\bigr) \qquad \forall\, (i,j),\; s,\; (p_i,p_j) \in \mathcal{CF}_s \tag{14}
$$

This enforces that two trains using *conflicting* routes through the same switch are separated by at least $h_s^{sw}$; trains using *non-conflicting* routes are unconstrained by this constraint.

### 6.15 No-overtaking within a block (transitivity, optional tightening)
$$
y_{i,j,b} + y_{j,k,b} - 1 \;\leq\; y_{i,k,b} \qquad \forall\, i,j,k \in \mathcal{T},\; b \in \mathcal{B} \tag{15}
$$

### 6.16 Symmetry-breaking across consecutive blocks (optional)
For each pair of trains $(i,j)$ traversing blocks $b$ and $b'$ in the same direction with $b$ upstream of $b'$:
$$
y_{i,j,b} \;\leq\; y_{i,j,b'} \tag{16}
$$

---

## 7. Modelling Assumptions

1. **Continuous time.** All times are continuous variables.
2. **Discrete speed profiles.** Each train has a finite, predefined set $\mathcal{K}$ of admissible speed profiles (e.g., nominal, slightly reduced, significantly reduced).
3. **Constant braking deceleration.** Braking distance is $\beta_{i,k} = v_{i,k}^{2}/(2 a_i^{br})$; this is a standard quadratic-in-speed approximation linearised through the discrete profile set.
4. **Point-mass trains with length.** Trains are treated as point masses; physical length is absorbed into the blocking time via $L_b/v_{i,k}$.
5. **Fixed block structure.** Track is partitioned into trackside train detection sections (TDSs); the end of authority (EoA) is always at a TDS boundary, consistent with ETCS L2 with TTD.
6. **Switches as special blocks.** Switches belong to $\mathcal{S} \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ and carry route-conflict logic in addition to ordinary headway logic.
7. **Fixed minimum dwell times.** Dwell times at stations are lower-bounded by $t_{i,e}^{dwell}$.
8. **No overtaking within a block.** Enforced through the ordering variables $y_{i,j,b}$ and constraint (15).
9. **Bidirectional traffic.** Trains travelling in opposite directions on the same block are subject to the same headway constraints (11)–(14).
10. **Initial delays exogenous.** Initial delays $\delta_{i,e}^{0}$ are given as input parameters (the disturbances to be resolved).
11. **Big-M formulation.** Disjunctive headway and switch constraints are linearised with a sufficiently large constant $M$; tightening of $M$ is left as a computational concern.

---

## 8. Key DTG-Specific Features of the Model

| Feature | Fixed-block RECIFE-MILP | CDR-DTG-MILP (this model) |
|---------|------------------------|---------------------------|
| Speed profile | Single, fixed | Discrete set $\mathcal{K}$, chosen per run via $x_{i,r,k}$ |
| Running time | Parameter $\rho_{i,r}$ | Speed-dependent via (5) |
| Block headway | Function of block length | Function of braking distance $\beta_{j,k}/v_{j,k}$ via (11) |
| Brake indication point | At block boundary | Anywhere on track via (12) |
| Switches | Generic blocks | Route-conflict logic via (13)–(14) |
| Speed profile impact on rescheduling | Not modelled | Endogenous via $x_{i,r,k}$ |

The model therefore captures the central operational insight of DTG: **rescheduling decisions can exploit the continuous, speed-dependent nature of brake indication points**, allowing closer train spacing and lower total delay than fixed-block CDR can represent.

Text:
# Best MILP Model for TRSMP under Partial Segment Blockage

After evaluating the three generated models, I select **Model 2** as the best because it offers the cleanest linearization strategy (using auxiliary energy variables bounded by mode indicators rather than bilinear products), the most comprehensive constraint set (21 constraints), and the strongest coupling between the trajectory layer and the block-usage layer through explicit position–block relationships.

---

# MILP Formulation for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Model Overview

This MILP jointly optimizes **train rescheduling** (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) and **speed management** (speed profiles and energy consumption) on a bidirectional double-track high-speed railway under partial segment blockage. The model uses time–space discretization to linearize dynamics and capture the interaction between discrete decisions (routing, ordering, speed-level selection) and continuous decisions (timing, speed, energy).

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Set | Description |
|---|---|
| $I$ | Set of trains, $i \in I$ |
| $J$ | Set of stations, $j \in J$ (with $j=0$ origin, $j=|J|$ destination) |
| $L$ | Set of track segments between consecutive stations, $l \in L$ |
| $K$ | Set of discrete time steps, $k \in K$ (planning horizon) |
| $D=\{1,2\}$ | Directions: 1 = original, 2 = opposite (rerouting) |
| $V$ | Set of discretized speed levels, $v \in V$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| $a_{ij}^0,\ d_{ij}^0$ | Scheduled arrival/departure time of train $i$ at station $j$ |
| $T_{il}^{\min},\ T_{il}^{\max}$ | Min/max running time of train $i$ on segment $l$ |
| $\tau_{\text{dwell}}^{\min},\ \tau_{\text{dwell}}^{\max}$ | Min/max dwell time at stations |
| $h^{\min}$ | Minimum headway time between trains |
| $C_l$ | Capacity of segment $l$ (max simultaneous trains) |
| $t_l^{\text{dis,start}},\ t_l^{\text{dis,end}}$ | Disruption time window on segment $l$ |
| $\Delta t,\ \Delta x$ | Time and distance discretization steps |
| $L_l$ | Length of segment $l$ |
| $v^{\min},\ v^{\max}$ | Min/max operating speeds |
| $E_{\text{acc}}(v),\ E_{\text{dec}}(v),\ E_{\text{cru}}(v)$ | Energy rate per distance at speed $v$ (accel/decel/cruise) |
| $a^{\text{acc}},\ a^{\text{dec}}$ | Max acceleration/deceleration |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (Big-M) |
| $w_1,w_2,w_3,w_4$ | Weights for delay, energy, cancellation, rerouting |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

**Rescheduling variables**
- $x_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ stops at station $j$
- $r_{il} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ reroutes to opposite track on segment $l$
- $y_{ii'l} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ departs before train $i'$ on segment $l$
- $c_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled
- $A_{ij} \ge 0$: actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $j$
- $D_{ij} \ge 0$: actual departure time of train $i$ at station $j$
- $\tau_{ijl} \ge 0$: running time of train $i$ on segment $l$ after station $j$
- $\tau_{ij}^{\text{dwell}} \ge 0$: dwell time of train $i$ at station $j$
- $\text{delay}_{ij} \ge 0$: delay of train $i$ at station $j$

**Speed-management variables**
- $v_{ilk} \ge 0$: speed of train $i$ on segment $l$ at time $k$
- $s_{ilk} \in [0,L_l]$: position of train $i$ on segment $l$ at time $k$
- $e_{ilk} \ge 0$: energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $l$ at time $k$
- $z_{ilv} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses speed level $v$ on segment $l$
- $\text{acc}_{ilk},\ \text{dec}_{ilk},\ \text{cru}_{ilk} \in \{0,1\}$: mode indicators (accelerating/decelerating/cruising)

**Block-usage variables**
- $b_{ilk} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if segment $l$ is occupied by train $i$ at time $k$ in original direction
- $b'_{ilk} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if segment $l$ is occupied by train $i$ at time $k$ in opposite direction

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \quad w_1 \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{j \in J}\text{delay}_{ij} \;+\; w_2 \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{l \in L}\sum_{k \in K} e_{ilk} \;+\; w_3 \sum_{i \in I} c_i \;+\; w_4 \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{l \in L} r_{il}
$$

The four weighted terms represent, respectively: (i) total delay across all trains and stations, (ii) total energy consumption, (iii) cancellation penalty, and (iv) rerouting penalty.

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Flow Conservation at Stations
$$
D_{ij} = A_{ij} + \tau_{ij}^{\text{dwell}} \quad \forall i \in I,\ j \in J
$$

### 6.2 Running Time Linkage
$$
A_{i,j+1} = D_{ij} + \tau_{ijl} \quad \forall i \in I,\ j \in J,\ l \in L \text{ corresponding to } (j,j{+}1)
$$

### 6.3 Dwell-Time Bounds
$$
\tau_{\text{dwell}}^{\min}\, x_{ij} \le \tau_{ij}^{\text{dwell}} \le \tau_{\text{dwell}}^{\max}\, x_{ij} \quad \forall i \in I,\ j \in J
$$

### 6.4 Running-Time Bounds
$$
T_{il}^{\min} \le \tau_{ijl} \le T_{il}^{\max} \quad \forall i \in I,\ j \in J,\ l \in L
$$

### 6.5 Segment Capacity
$$
\sum_{i \in I} b_{ilk} \le C_l \quad \forall l \in L,\ k \in K
$$
$$
\sum_{i \in I} b'_{ilk} \le C_l \quad \forall l \in L,\ k \in K
$$

### 6.6 Bidirectional Conflict
$$
b_{ilk} + b'_{ilk} \le 1 \quad \forall i \in I,\ l \in L,\ k \in K
$$

### 6.7 Disruption (Blocked Segment)
$$
b_{ilk} = 0 \quad \forall i \in I,\ l \in L,\ k \in K:\ t_l^{\text{dis,start}} \le k\Delta t \le t_l^{\text{dis,end}}
$$
$$
b'_{ilk} = 0 \quad \forall i \in I,\ l \in L,\ k \in K:\ t_l^{\text{dis,start}} \le k\Delta t \le t_l^{\text{dis,end}}
$$

### 6.8 Train Ordering (No Overtaking)
$$
y_{ii'l} + y_{i'il} = 1 \quad \forall i,i' \in I,\ i \ne i',\ l \in L
$$

### 6.9 Headway Constraint
$$
A_{i,j+1} - A_{i',j+1} \ge h^{\min} - M(1 - y_{ii'l}) - M(1 - x_{ij}) - M(1 - x_{i'j}) \quad \forall i,i' \in I,\ j \in J,\ l \in L
$$

### 6.10 Speed Profile Feasibility
$$
v^{\min} \le v_{ilk} \le v^{\max} \quad \forall i \in I,\ l \in L,\ k \in K
$$
$$
v_{il,k+1} - v_{ilk} \le a^{\text{acc}} \Delta t \quad \forall i \in I,\ l \in L,\ k \in K
$$
$$
v_{ilk} - v_{il,k+1} \le a^{\text{dec}} \Delta t \quad \forall i \in I,\ l \in L,\ k \in K
$$

### 6.11 Mode Selection (Exactly One)
$$
\text{acc}_{ilk} + \text{dec}_{ilk} + \text{cru}_{ilk} = 1 \quad \forall i \in I,\ l \in L,\ k \in K
$$

### 6.12 Mode–Speed Coupling
$$
v_{il,k+1} - v_{ilk} \le M \cdot \text{acc}_{ilk} \quad \forall i \in I,\ l \in L,\ k \in K
$$
$$
v_{ilk} - v_{il,k+1} \le M \cdot \text{dec}_{ilk} \quad \forall i \in I,\ l \in L,\ k \in K
$$

### 6.13 Position Dynamics
$$
s_{il,k+1} = s_{ilk} + v_{ilk} \Delta t \quad \forall i \in I,\ l \in L,\ k \in K
$$

### 6.14 Position Bounds
$$
0 \le s_{ilk} \le L_l \quad \forall i \in I,\ l \in L,\ k \in K
$$

### 6.15 Speed-Level Selection (Exactly One)
$$
\sum_{v \in V} z_{ilv} = 1 \quad \forall i \in I,\ l \in L
$$
$$
v_{ilk} = \sum_{v \in V} v \cdot z_{ilv} \quad \forall i \in I,\ l \in L,\ k \in K
$$

### 6.16 Energy Consumption (Linearized)
Define auxiliary energy variables $e^{\text{acc}}_{ilk}, e^{\text{dec}}_{ilk}, e^{\text{cru}}_{ilk} \ge 0$:

$$
e_{ilk} = e^{\text{acc}}_{ilk} + e^{\text{dec}}_{ilk} + e^{\text{cru}}_{ilk} \quad \forall i \in I,\ l \in L,\ k \in K
$$
$$
e^{\text{acc}}_{ilk} \le M \cdot \text{acc}_{ilk}, \quad e^{\text{dec}}_{ilk} \le M \cdot \text{dec}_{ilk}, \quad e^{\text{cru}}_{ilk} \le M \cdot \text{cru}_{ilk}
$$
$$
e^{\text{acc}}_{ilk} = \sum_{v \in V} z_{ilv}\, E_{\text{acc}}(v)\, \Delta x
$$
$$
e^{\text{dec}}_{ilk} = \sum_{v \in V} z_{ilv}\, E_{\text{dec}}(v)\, \Delta x
$$
$$
e^{\text{cru}}_{ilk} = \sum_{v \in V} z_{ilv}\, E_{\text{cru}}(v)\, \Delta x
$$

### 6.17 Rerouting Coupling
$$
b'_{ilk} \ge r_{il} + b_{ilk} - 1 \quad \forall i \in I,\ l \in L,\ k \in K
$$
$$
b'_{ilk} \le r_{il}, \quad b'_{ilk} \le b_{ilk} \quad \forall i \in I,\ l \in L,\ k \in K
$$

### 6.18 Cancellation Handling
$$
A_{ij} \le M(1 - c_i), \quad D_{ij} \le M(1 - c_i) \quad \forall i \in I,\ j \in J
$$
$$
x_{ij} \le 1 - c_i, \quad b_{ilk} \le 1 - c_i, \quad b'_{ilk} \le 1 - c_i \quad \forall i \in I,\ j \in J,\ l \in L,\ k \in K
$$
$$
v_{ilk} \le v^{\max}(1 - c_i), \quad s_{ilk} \le L_l(1 - c_i) \quad \forall i \in I,\ l \in L,\ k \in K
$$

### 6.19 Delay Definition
$$
\text{delay}_{ij} \ge A_{ij} - a_{ij}^0 \quad \forall i \in I,\ j \in J
$$
$$
\text{delay}_{ij} \ge 0
$$

### 6.20 Arrival/Departure–Position Coupling
For each train $i$ entering segment $l$ after station $j$:
$$
s_{il,\lfloor D_{ij}/\Delta t \rfloor} = 0 \quad \text{(position at departure)}
$$
$$
s_{il,\lfloor A_{i,j+1}/\Delta t \rfloor} = L_l \quad \text{(position at arrival)}
$$

(Implemented via auxiliary binary indicators and Big-M constraints to handle the discrete time mapping.)

### 6.21 Block-Usage–Trajectory Coupling
$$
b_{ilk} \ge \frac{s_{ilk}}{L_l} - \epsilon, \quad b_{ilk} \le \frac{s_{ilk}}{L_l} + \epsilon \quad \forall i \in I,\ l \in L,\ k \in K
$$

(Ensures $b_{ilk}=1$ iff the train's position on segment $l$ is strictly between 0 and $L_l$ at time $k$.)

---

## 7. Explanation of Model Elements

### 7.1 Rescheduling Layer
- **Retiming** is captured by continuous variables $A_{ij}, D_{ij}$ deviating from scheduled times $a_{ij}^0, d_{ij}^0$.
- **Reordering** uses binary $y_{ii'l}$ with the no-overtaking constraint (6.8) and headway (6.9).
- **Rerouting** uses $r_{il}$ coupled with bidirectional block-usage $b'_{ilk}$ via (6.17), allowing trains to use the opposite track when their original track is blocked.
- **Cancellation** is handled by $c_i$ forcing all related variables to zero through (6.18).

### 7.2 Speed-Management Layer
- **Speed profiles** are discretized in time and space; $v_{ilk}$ evolves according to acceleration/deceleration bounds (6.10) and mode indicators (6.11)–(6.12).
- **Position dynamics** (6.13) integrate speed over time to obtain $s_{ilk}$.
- **Speed-level selection** (6.15) restricts the continuous speed to one of the discrete levels in $V$, enabling linear energy modeling.
- **Energy consumption** (6.16) is decomposed into acceleration, deceleration, and cruise components, each linked to the chosen speed level via $z_{ilv}$ — this keeps the formulation linear.

### 7.3 Disruption and Capacity Layer
- **Disruption constraints** (6.7) forbid any block usage during the blockage window, forcing either rerouting, retiming, or cancellation.
- **Segment capacity** (6.5) and **bidirectional conflict** (6.6) ensure physical feasibility of simultaneous train movements.
- **Block-usage–trajectory coupling** (6.21) ties the abstract block-occupation variables to the actual train positions computed from the speed profile.

### 7.4 Objective Trade-offs
The weighted sum allows the dispatcher to balance:
- **Punctuality** (delay minimization),
- **Energy efficiency** (cruise at low-energy speed levels),
- **Service preservation** (avoid cancellation),
- **Infrastructure usage** (avoid rerouting when possible).

By tuning $w_1, w_2, w_3, w_4$, the operator can emphasize different priorities (e.g., peak-hour punctuality vs. off-peak energy savings).

### 7.5 Linearity
All constraints are linear: products of binaries ($z_{ilv} \cdot \text{acc}_{ilk}$) are avoided by using auxiliary energy variables bounded by mode indicators. Big-M is used only where logical implications require it (cancellation, headway, mode–speed coupling).

---

## 8. Assumptions Made

The following assumptions were introduced to make the model complete (marked as such per instructions):

1. **Time discretization**: The planning horizon is discretized into uniform steps $\Delta t$; all events (arrivals, departures, blockages) are aligned to this grid.
2. **Distance discretization**: Energy is computed per distance step $\Delta x$, consistent with the time discretization.
3. **Speed levels**: Speeds are restricted to a finite set $V$ to enable linear energy modeling (otherwise the energy function $E(v)$ would be nonlinear).
4. **Bidirectional double-track**: The infrastructure consists of two parallel tracks, one per nominal direction; rerouting allows trains to use the opposite track.
5. **Single disruption window per segment**: Each affected segment has one contiguous blockage window $[t_l^{\text{dis,start}}, t_l^{\text{dis,end}}]$.
6. **No overtaking**: Trains cannot pass each other on the same segment (consistent with high-speed railway safety rules).
7. **Uniform headway**: A single minimum headway $h^{\min}$ applies to all train pairs.
8. **Cancellation is total**: A cancelled train is removed entirely from the system (no partial service).
9. **Energy model**: Energy consumption is a function of speed level and driving mode (accel/decel/cruise), independent of gradient and curvature (flat-track assumption).
10. **Acceleration/deceleration bounds**: Symmetric bounds $a^{\text{acc}}, a^{\text{dec}}$ apply uniformly to all trains and segments.

---

This MILP provides a unified framework for **real-time dispatch decisions** during partial blockages, jointly producing a feasible timetable, routing plan, and energy-efficient speed profile for all trains in the affected corridor.

# MILP Formulation: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t$ (and $i$) |
| $S$ | Set of block sections along the line, indexed by $s$; $|S|$ sections |
| $K = \{0,1,\ldots,K_s-1\}$ | Discrete time intervals for each section, length $\Delta_t$ |
| $N$ | Set of stations (subset of section boundaries) |
| $R = \{0,1\}$ | Tracks: $r=0$ = original track of train's direction, $r=1$ = opposite track |
| $B \subseteq S$ | Sections whose **original** track is blocked during the disruption window |
| $\text{dir}_t \in \{\text{UP},\text{DOWN}\}$ | Direction of train $t$ |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $\Delta_t$ | s | Time-step duration (e.g. 10 s) |
| $L_s$ | m | Length of section $s$ |
| $V_{\max}$ | m/s | Maximum operational speed |
| $a_{\max}$ | m/s² | Maximum acceleration |
| $a_{\min}<0$ | m/s² | Maximum braking magnitude |
| $\eta_0,\eta_1,\eta_2$ | kWh/interval, kWh/(m/s·interval), kWh/(m/s²·interval) | Linear energy-surrogate coefficients (assumption A1) |
| $\text{arr}^s_{t,n},\text{dep}^s_{t,n}$ | s | Scheduled arrival / departure of train $t$ at station $n$ |
| $D^{\min}_n,D^{\max}_n$ | s | Min / max dwell time at station $n$ |
| $H_{\min}$ | s | Same-direction minimum headway |
| $H_{\text{bi}}$ | s | Bidirectional (opposing-direction) minimum headway, $H_{\text{bi}} \ge H_{\min}$ |
| $T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{start}},T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{end}}$ | s | Disruption time window |
| $\text{turn}_t$ | s | Turnaround time at terminals |
| $w_{\text{delay}},w_{\text{energy}}$ | – | Objective weights |
| $M_{\text{cancel}}$ | – | Cancellation penalty |
| $M_{\text{time}}$ | s | Big-M for time, set to horizon length |
| $M_{\text{pos}}$ | m | Big-M for position, set to $L_s$ |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous**

- $\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,n}, \tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,n}$: actual arrival / departure time (s) of train $t$ at station $n$.
- $v_{t,s,k} \ge 0$: speed (m/s) of train $t$ in section $s$ at interval $k$.
- $p_{t,s,k} \ge 0$: position (m) of train $t$ in section $s$ at interval $k$ (measured from section entry).
- $a_{t,s,k}$: acceleration (m/s²) of train $t$ in section $s$ at interval $k$.
- $u_{t,s,k} \ge 0$: auxiliary ≥ $\max(a_{t,s,k},0)$ (used to linearise positive acceleration in the energy surrogate).
- $E_{t,s,k} \ge 0$: energy consumption (kWh) of train $t$ in section $s$ at interval $k$.
- $d^{\text{arr}}_{t,n}, d^{\text{dep}}_{t,n} \ge 0$: arrival / departure delay (s) of train $t$ at station $n$.

**Binary**

- $y_t \in \{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $t$ is cancelled.
- $x_{t,s,r} \in \{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $t$ uses track $r$ on section $s$.
- $q_{t,s,k,r} \in \{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $t$ occupies $(s,r)$ during interval $k$.
- $z_{t,i,s,r} \in \{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $t$ precedes train $i$ on $(s,r)$.
- $w_{t,s,r} \in \{0,1\}$: $1$ if at least one interval of train $t$ on section $s$ uses track $r$ (auxiliary for rerouting).

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; w_{\text{delay}}\sum_{t \in T}\sum_{n \in N}\!\left(d^{\text{arr}}_{t,n}+d^{\text{dep}}_{t,n}\right) \;+\; w_{\text{energy}}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{k\in K} E_{t,s,k} \;+\; M_{\text{cancel}}\sum_{t\in T} y_t
$$

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Dynamics (linear, time-discretised)

For every $t\in T$, $s\in S$, $k \in K\setminus\{K_s-1\}$:

$$
v_{t,s,k+1} = v_{t,s,k} + a_{t,s,k}\,\Delta_t \qquad\text{(discretised Euler integration)}
$$

$$
p_{t,s,k+1} = p_{t,s,k} + v_{t,s,k}\,\Delta_t
$$

$$
0 \le v_{t,s,k} \le V_{\max}
$$

$$
a_{\min} \le a_{t,s,k} \le a_{\max}
$$

Boundary conditions on each section:

$$
p_{t,s,0} = 0, \qquad p_{t,s,K_s-1} = L_s
$$

### 5.2 Energy Surrogate (assumption A1: linear surrogate of mechanical power)

For every $t,s,k$:

$$
u_{t,s,k} \ge a_{t,s,k},\qquad u_{t,s,k} \ge 0
$$

$$
E_{t,s,k} = \eta_0 + \eta_1\,v_{t,s,k} + \eta_2\,u_{t,s,k}
$$

($\eta_2\ge 0$ so only tractive energy is counted; regenerative-braking losses can be folded into $\eta_1$.)

### 5.3 Station Dwell and Time Linking

For every $t\in T$ and station $n\in N$:

$$
D^{\min}_n \le \tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,n} - \tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,n} \le D^{\max}_n
$$

For every $t$, station $n$ at boundary between sections $s$ and $s+1$:

$$
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,n} \le \Delta_t \sum_{k\in K} k\,q_{t,s,k,\cdot} + M_{\text{time}}(1-q^{\text{arr}}_{t,n})
$$

$$
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,n} \ge \Delta_t \sum_{k\in K} k\,q_{t,s,k,\cdot} - M_{\text{time}}(1-q^{\text{arr}}_{t,n})
$$

where $q^{\text{arr}}_{t,n} \in \{0,1\}$ is $1$ if train $t$ actually visits station $n$. Turnaround at terminals:

$$
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,n_{\text{term}}} - \tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,n_{\text{term}}} \ge \text{turn}_t - M_{\text{time}}\,y_t
$$

### 5.4 Delay Definition

For every $t,n$:

$$
d^{\text{arr}}_{t,n} \ge \tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,n} - \text{arr}^s_{t,n}, \qquad d^{\text{arr}}_{t,n} \ge 0
$$

$$
d^{\text{dep}}_{t,n} \ge \tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,n} - \text{dep}^s_{t,n}, \qquad d^{\text{dep}}_{t,n} \ge 0
$$

### 5.5 Cancellation

If $y_t=1$, all operational variables are forced to zero:

$$
v_{t,s,k},\, p_{t,s,k},\, |a_{t,s,k}|,\, E_{t,s,k} \le M_{\text{cancel}}\,(1-y_t)
$$

$$
x_{t,s,r},\, q_{t,s,k,r},\, w_{t,s,r} \le 1 - y_t
$$

$$
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,n},\, \tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,n} \le M_{\text{time}}\,(1-y_t)
$$

### 5.6 Track Assignment and Rerouting

For every $t,s$:

$$
\sum_{r\in R} x_{t,s,r} = 1 - y_t
$$

Forced rerouting on blocked sections during the disruption window (assumption A2: each affected train's planned traversal falls inside $[T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{start}},T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{end}}]$):

$$
x_{t,s,0} = 0 \quad \forall\, s\in B,\; t:\; \tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,n(s)}\in[T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{start}},T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{end}}]
$$

(The disruption window may also be enforced directly on occupancy — see (5.8).)

Link $x$ and the auxiliary $w$:

$$
w_{t,s,r} \le \sum_k q_{t,s,k,r}, \qquad w_{t,s,r} \ge q_{t,s,k,r} \quad \forall\,k \quad\text{(i.e.\ }w=\max_k q\text{)}
$$

Rerouting cost (optional): introduce a small parameter $\rho^{\text{reroute}}_t$ and add $\sum_{t,s,r\ne\text{dir}_t}\rho^{\text{reroute}}_t\,x_{t,s,r}$ to the objective.

### 5.7 Occupancy Definition

For every $t,s,k,r$:

$$
q_{t,s,k,r} \le x_{t,s,r}
$$

Linear "position lies inside the section" indicator (big-M):

$$
p_{t,s,k} \le L_s + M_{\text{pos}}(1 - q_{t,s,k,r})
$$

$$
p_{t,s,k} \ge 0 - M_{\text{pos}}(1 - q_{t,s,k,r})
$$

$$
q_{t,s,k,r} \ge x_{t,s,r} - M_{\text{pos}}\bigl(\tfrac{L_s}{V_{\max}\Delta_t}\bigr)\bigl(1-\mathbf{1}\{0\le p_{t,s,k}\le L_s\}\bigr)
$$

The third inequality is implemented by:

$$
q_{t,s,k,r} \ge x_{t,s,r} - M_{\text{pos}}\bigl(\tfrac{L_s}{V_{\max}\Delta_t}\bigr)(1-q_{t,s,k,r})
$$

equivalently $q_{t,s,k,r}\ge x_{t,s,r}/(1+M)$, which simplifies to the two inequalities above together with $q\le x$.

### 5.8 Disruption Window Enforcement

No train may occupy the **blocked track** during the disruption window:

$$
q_{t,s,k,0} = 0 \quad \forall\, s\in B,\; k:\, [k\Delta_t,(k+1)\Delta_t]\cap[T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{start}},T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{end}}]\ne\emptyset
$$

(Implemented as: $q_{t,s,k,0}\le \mathbf{1}\{k\Delta_t<T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{start}} \;\text{or}\; (k+1)\Delta_t>T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{end}}\}$.)

### 5.9 Headway — Same Direction

For every pair $t\neq i$ with $\text{dir}_t=\text{dir}_i$, every $s,r$ and every $k,k'$:

$$
q_{t,s,k,r} + q_{i,s,k',r} - 1 \le z_{t,i,s,r} + z_{i,t,s,r}
$$

$$
(k'-k)\Delta_t \ge H_{\min} - M_{\text{time}}\,z_{i,t,s,r}
$$

$$
(k-k')\Delta_t \ge H_{\min} - M_{\text{time}}\,z_{t,i,s,r}
$$

$$
z_{t,i,s,r} + z_{i,t,s,r} \le 1 \quad\text{(or = 1 with a tie-breaker)}
$$

(Standard disjunctive headway linearisation.)

### 5.10 Headway — Bidirectional on Shared Track

For every pair $t\neq i$ with $\text{dir}_t \ne \text{dir}_i$, every $s,r$:

Replace $H_{\min}$ by $H_{\text{bi}}$ in (5.9). This guarantees opposing-direction trains sharing the rerouted track keep safe separation.

### 5.11 Non-negativity and Domains

$$
v_{t,s,k}, p_{t,s,k}, u_{t,s,k}, E_{t,s,k}, d^{\text{arr}}_{t,n}, d^{\text{dep}}_{t,n} \ge 0
$$

$$
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,n}, \tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,n} \in [0, T_{\text{hor}}]
$$

$$
a_{t,s,k} \in [a_{\min},a_{\max}],\quad y_t, x_{t,s,r}, q_{t,s,k,r}, z_{t,i,s,r}, w_{t,s,r}\in\{0,1\}
$$

## 6. Linearisation Notes

1. **Train dynamics** are discretised with explicit Euler integration; this is linear because $v_{t,s,k}$ enters $p_{t,s,k+1}$ linearly (the resulting error $O(\Delta_t^2)$ is controlled by choosing $\Delta_t$ small enough — assumption A3).
2. **Energy surrogate** uses a linear function $E=\eta_0+\eta_1 v+\eta_2 u$ with auxiliary $u\ge a,\,u\ge 0$ to obtain $\max(a,0)$ linearly (assumption A1).
3. **Occupancy / position** uses the standard big-M indicator pair $(p\le L_s + M(1-q),\; p\ge 0 - M(1-q))$ which yields $q=0$ when $p$ is outside $[0,L_s]$ and $q=1$ inside, provided $M\ge L_s$.
4. **Headway** is enforced via the disjunctive formulation with ordering binaries $z$ and big-M $M_{\text{time}}$ (classical headway linearisation; equivalent to $z_{t,i}+z_{i,t}=1$).
5. **Cancellation** is enforced with big-M multipliers on every operational variable so that $y_t=1$ zeros out all physical activity but keeps the objective penalty.
6. **Disruption window** is enforced as a hard occupancy ban on the blocked track during $[T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{start}},T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{end}}]$, linear because the time grid is fixed.
7. **Bidirectional conflicts** are handled by re-using the same headway disjunctive with the larger $H_{\text{bi}}$ whenever the two trains have opposite directions and are assigned to the same $(s,r)$.

## 7. Stated Assumptions

- **A1 (Energy surrogate).** Real tractive energy $P_{\text{mech}}(v,a) = (c_0+c_1v+c_2v^2)+m\,a^+ v$ is approximated by a linear surrogate $\eta_0+\eta_1 v+\eta_2 a^+$, which keeps the MILP strictly linear at the cost of some modelling error (can be tightened via piecewise-linear segments if needed).
- **A2 (Disruption window).** The disruption window $[T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{start}},T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{end}}]$ is known in advance and is applied to a known set of blocked sections $B$; each affected train's planned traversal falls inside the window.
- **A3 (Discretisation).** $\Delta_t$ is chosen small enough for Euler accuracy; $V_{\max}\Delta_t$ is the maximum displacement per interval and is used in the position big-M.
- **A4 (Bidirectional separation).** $H_{\text{bi}}\ge H_{\min}$ accounts for additional safety on the shared track.
- **A5 (Cancellation).** Cancelled trains pay the penalty $M_{\text{cancel}}$ but generate zero delays and zero energy.
- **A6 (Big-M values).** $M_{\text{time}}=T_{\text{hor}}$, $M_{\text{pos}}=L_s$, $M_{\text{cancel}}$ chosen sufficiently large to dominate any feasible value of the bounded variables.

This MILP is self-contained and integrates timetable rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with continuous speed-profile generation and energy accounting in a single linear model, explicitly handling bidirectional conflicts on the rerouted track and the disruption-window constraint.

Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.

Text:
# Complete MILP Formulation: Passenger-Oriented Real-Time Train Rescheduling with Flexible Train Composition and Rolling Stock Circulation

Below is a complete Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for the real-time train rescheduling problem described in the input. The model extends Liu et al. (2023a) to include **time-varying sectional passenger demands**, **flexible train composition**, and **rolling stock circulation**. It is designed to be solved within a Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework at each control step.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of trains indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations indexed by $i$ (ordered along the line) |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of discrete time steps in the prediction horizon, indexed by $t$ |
| $\mathcal{H}$ | Set of time intervals (for piecewise-constant demand), indexed by $h$ |
| $\mathcal{N}$ | Set of allowable train compositions (number of cars), indexed by $n$ |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Set of rolling stock units (cars), indexed by $r$ |
| $\mathcal{L}$ | Set of lines in the network, indexed by $\ell$ |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Set of station sections (origin–destination pairs), indexed by $e = (o,d)$ |
| $i^+$ | Successor station of $i$ |
| $i^-$ | Predecessor station of $i$ |

**Assumption:** The line is bidirectional; trains are indexed by ordered pair $(k,\ell)$ where $\ell \in \mathcal{L}$ denotes the line/direction. For clarity, the formulation below is presented for one line; the network extension uses additional indices.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Length of the prediction horizon (minutes) |
| $\Delta$ | Length of one discrete time step (minutes) |
| $\Delta_h$ | Length of one demand interval (minutes), $\Delta_h = m\Delta$ for integer $m$ |
| $N^{\min}, N^{\max}$ | Minimum/maximum number of cars per train |
| $C^{\text{car}}$ | Passenger capacity per car |
| $d_{i,h}$ | Average passenger arrival rate at station $i$ during interval $h$ (pax/min) |
| $\lambda_{i,h}^{\text{od}}$ | Fraction of demand at $i$ in $h$ destined for station $d$ |
| $\tau^{\text{run}}_{i}$ | Minimum running time from station $i$ to $i^+$ (minutes) |
| $\tau^{\text{dwl}}_{i}$ | Minimum dwell time at station $i$ (minutes) |
| $h^{\min}, h^{\max}$ | Minimum/maximum headway between consecutive trains (minutes) |
| $\bar{t}^{\text{arr}}_{k,i}, \bar{t}^{\text{dep}}_{k,i}$ | Nominal arrival/departure times of train $k$ at station $i$ |
| $\alpha^{\text{wait}}, \alpha^{\text{trav}}, \alpha^{\text{op}}, \alpha^{\text{dev}}$ | Weights for waiting time, travel time, operational cost, and timetable deviation |
| $c^{\text{op}}_n$ | Operational cost of operating a train with $n$ cars per departure |
| $c^{\text{wait}}$ | Cost per passenger-minute of waiting |
| $c^{\text{trav}}$ | Cost per passenger-minute of in-vehicle travel |
| $c^{\text{dev}}$ | Cost per minute of timetable deviation |
| $E_n$ | Energy consumption of a train with $n$ cars per km |
| $L_i$ | Distance between station $i$ and $i^+$ (km) |
| $R$ | Set of available rolling stock units at the start of horizon |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Timetable variables (continuous)
- $t^{\text{arr}}_{k,i} \ge 0$: actual arrival time of train $k$ at station $i$
- $t^{\text{dep}}_{k,i} \ge 0$: actual departure time of train $k$ from station $i$
- $\delta^{\text{arr}}_{k,i} \ge 0$, $\delta^{\text{dep}}_{k,i} \ge 0$: absolute deviations from nominal times

### 3.2 Train composition (integer)
- $n_k \in \{N^{\min}, \dots, N^{\max}\}$: number of cars in train $k$
- $u_{k,r} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if rolling stock unit $r$ is assigned to train $k$

### 3.3 Stopping plan (binary)
- $x_{k,i} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $k$ stops at station $i$

### 3.4 Passenger flow variables (continuous)
- $b_{k,i,h} \ge 0$: number of passengers boarding train $k$ at station $i$ during interval $h$
- $a_{k,i,h} \ge 0$: number of passengers alighting from train $k$ at station $i$ during interval $h$
- $p_{k,i,h} \ge 0$: number of passengers on board train $k$ on section $(i, i^+)$ during interval $h$
- $w_{i,h} \ge 0$: number of passengers waiting at station $i$ at the end of interval $h$
- $W^{\text{tot}}_{i,h} \ge 0$: cumulative passenger waiting time at station $i$ during interval $h$

### 3.5 Rolling stock circulation (binary)
- $z_{k,k',i} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if rolling stock of train $k$ is transferred to train $k'$ at station $i$
- $v_{k,i} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $k$ terminates its trip at station $i$

### 3.6 Auxiliary variables (continuous)
- $\text{load}_{k,i,h} \ge 0$: passenger load of train $k$ when departing $i$ in interval $h$
- $\text{occ}_{k,i,h} \in [0,1]$: occupancy ratio of train $k$ at section $i$ in interval $h$

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of passenger waiting time, in-vehicle travel time, operational cost, and timetable deviation:

$$
\min \; Z = \alpha^{\text{wait}} \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{h \in \mathcal{H}} W^{\text{tot}}_{i,h}}_{\text{passenger waiting time}}
+ \alpha^{\text{trav}} \underbrace{\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{h \in \mathcal{H}} p_{k,i,h} \cdot \tau^{\text{run}}_i}_{\text{passenger travel time}}
$$
$$
+ \alpha^{\text{op}} \underbrace{\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} c^{\text{op}}_{n_k}}_{\text{operational cost}}
+ \alpha^{\text{dev}} \underbrace{\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{S}} \left( \delta^{\text{arr}}_{k,i} + \delta^{\text{dep}}_{k,i} \right)}_{\text{timetable deviation}}
$$

**Assumption:** Energy consumption is omitted from the primary objective to keep the model linear; it can be added as $\sum_{k,i} E_{n_k} L_i$ if desired.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable Structure

**Arrival–departure relationship with dwell time:**
$$
t^{\text{dep}}_{k,i} \ge t^{\text{arr}}_{k,i} + \tau^{\text{dwl}}_{i} \cdot x_{k,i} \qquad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}, \; i \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**Running time between consecutive stations:**
$$
t^{\text{arr}}_{k,i^+} \ge t^{\text{dep}}_{k,i} + \tau^{\text{run}}_{i} \qquad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}, \; i \in \mathcal{S} \setminus \{i_{\text{last}}\}
$$

**Deviation from nominal timetable:**
$$
\delta^{\text{arr}}_{k,i} \ge t^{\text{arr}}_{k,i} - \bar{t}^{\text{arr}}_{k,i}, \quad
\delta^{\text{arr}}_{k,i} \ge \bar{t}^{\text{arr}}_{k,i} - t^{\text{arr}}_{k,i}
$$
$$
\delta^{\text{dep}}_{k,i} \ge t^{\text{dep}}_{k,i} - \bar{t}^{\text{dep}}_{k,i}, \quad
\delta^{\text{dep}}_{k,i} \ge \bar{t}^{\text{dep}}_{k,i} - t^{\text{dep}}_{k,i}
$$

### 5.2 Headway and Safety Constraints

**Minimum headway between consecutive trains at the same station:**
$$
t^{\text{dep}}_{k^+, i} \ge t^{\text{dep}}_{k, i} + h^{\min} - M(2 - x_{k,i} - x_{k^+, i}) \qquad \forall k, \; i
$$

**Maximum headway (to limit passenger waiting):**
$$
t^{\text{dep}}_{k^+, i} \le t^{\text{dep}}_{k, i} + h^{\max} + M(2 - x_{k,i} - x_{k^+, i}) \qquad \forall k, \; i
$$

where $k^+$ denotes the train immediately following $k$ in the timetable.

### 5.3 Stopping Plan Constraints

**Origin and terminal stations must be served:**
$$
x_{k,i_{\text{first}}} = 1, \quad x_{k,i_{\text{last}}} = 1 \qquad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

**If a train skips a station, no boarding/alighting occurs:**
$$
b_{k,i,h} \le M \cdot x_{k,i}, \quad a_{k,i,h} \le M \cdot x_{k,i} \qquad \forall k, i, h
$$

### 5.4 Train Composition and Capacity

**Train capacity (linearized via $n_k$):**
$$
p_{k,i,h} \le C^{\text{car}} \cdot n_k \qquad \forall k, i, h
$$

**Composition bounds:**
$$
N^{\min} \le n_k \le N^{\max}, \quad n_k \in \mathbb{Z}^+ \qquad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

**Rolling stock assignment (linking $n_k$ and $u_{k,r}$):**
$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} u_{k,r} = n_k \qquad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}
$$
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} u_{k,r} \le 1 \qquad \forall r \in \mathcal{R}
$$
$$
u_{k,r} \in \{0,1\} \qquad \forall k, r
$$

### 5.5 Passenger Flow Conservation

**Boarding equals demand minus residual waiting:**
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} b_{k,i,h} + w_{i,h} = w_{i,h-1} + d_{i,h} \cdot \Delta_h \qquad \forall i, h
$$
with $w_{i,0} = 0$ (or carried over from the previous MPC step).

**Alighting equals passengers destined for $i$:**
$$
a_{k,i,h} = \sum_{o < i} b_{k,o,h'} \cdot \lambda_{o,h'}^{\text{od}} \quad \text{(linearized via OD-flow variables } f_{k,o,i,h} \text{):}
$$
$$
a_{k,i,h} = \sum_{o \in \mathcal{S}, o < i} f_{k,o,i,h} \qquad \forall k, i, h
$$
$$
b_{k,i,h} = \sum_{d \in \mathcal{S}, d > i} f_{k,i,d,h} \qquad \forall k, i, h
$$
$$
f_{k,o,d,h} \ge 0 \qquad \forall k, o, d, h
$$

**Load conservation between sections:**
$$
p_{k,i^+,h} = p_{k,i,h} + b_{k,i^+,h} - a_{k,i^+,h} \qquad \forall k, i, h
$$
with $p_{k,i_{\text{first}}^- , h} = 0$ (empty at origin).

### 5.6 Passenger Waiting Time

$$
W^{\text{tot}}_{i,h} \ge w_{i,h-1} \cdot \Delta_h + \tfrac{1}{2} d_{i,h} \Delta_h^2 - \sum_{k} b_{k,i,h} \cdot \tfrac{\Delta_h}{2}
$$

**Assumption:** This linear approximation assumes passengers arrive uniformly within interval $h$ and board the first available train; a more accurate trapezoidal approximation can be used.

### 5.7 Rolling Stock Circulation

**Each rolling stock unit serves exactly one train sequence:**
$$
\sum_{k' \in \mathcal{K}} z_{k,k',i} = v_{k,i} \qquad \forall k, i
$$
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} z_{k,k',i} = v_{k',i} \qquad \forall k', i
$$

**Transfer feasibility (time and location):**
$$
t^{\text{dep}}_{k',i} \ge t^{\text{arr}}_{k,i} + \tau^{\text{turn}}_{i} - M(1 - z_{k,k',i}) \qquad \forall k, k', i
$$

**Rolling stock unit consistency (unit $r$ on train $k$ continues on $k'$):**
$$
u_{k,r} + u_{k',r} \le 1 + z_{k,k',i} \qquad \forall k, k', i, r
$$

**Train termination:**
$$
v_{k,i_{\text{last}}} = 1 \quad \text{(each train terminates at the end of the line)}
$$

### 5.8 Coupling between Composition and Circulation

**Number of cars preserved through transfers:**
$$
n_{k'} \ge n_k - M(1 - z_{k,k',i}) \qquad \forall k, k', i
$$

**Assumption:** Coupling/decoupling is not modeled at the unit level; composition is preserved along a rolling stock circulation path.

### 5.9 Non-Negativity and Binary Domains

$$
t^{\text{arr}}_{k,i}, t^{\text{dep}}_{k,i}, \delta^{\text{arr}}_{k,i}, \delta^{\text{dep}}_{k,i} \ge 0
$$
$$
b_{k,i,h}, a_{k,i,h}, p_{k,i,h}, w_{i,h}, W^{\text{tot}}_{i,h}, f_{k,o,d,h} \ge 0
$$
$$
x_{k,i}, z_{k,k',i}, v_{k,i}, u_{k,r} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
n_k \in \{N^{\min}, \dots, N^{\max}\}
$$

---

## 6. Linearization Notes

The following nonlinear terms have been linearized:

| Original nonlinear term | Linearization |
|---|---|
| $c^{\text{op}}_{n_k}$ (piecewise-linear in $n_k$) | Reformulated as $\sum_{n \in \mathcal{N}} c^{\text{op}}_n \cdot y_{k,n}$ with $\sum_n y_{k,n} = 1$, $y_{k,n} \in \{0,1\}$, and $n_k = \sum_n n \cdot y_{k,n}$ |
| $p_{k,i,h} \cdot \tau^{\text{run}}_i$ in objective | Treated as a constant coefficient since $\tau^{\text{run}}_i$ is a parameter |
| $C^{\text{car}} \cdot n_k$ in capacity constraint | Becomes $p_{k,i,h} \le \sum_n C^{\text{car}} \cdot n \cdot y_{k,n}$ |
| Big-M terms | Validated by choosing $M = T$ (the prediction horizon length) |

---

## 7. Key Assumptions

1. **Single-line focus:** The formulation is presented for one line; the network extension adds line index $\ell$ and inter-line transfer constraints.
2. **Piecewise-constant demand:** Passenger arrival rates $d_{i,h}$ are constant within each interval $h$, as stated in the input.
3. **Uniform boarding distribution:** Passengers arriving in interval $h$ are assumed to board uniformly; this yields a linear waiting-time approximation.
4. **Composition preservation:** Rolling stock units retain their composition through circulation (no mid-day coupling/decoupling).
5. **No energy in objective:** Energy consumption is excluded to preserve linearity; it can be appended as a linear term.
6. **Fixed turnaround time:** $\tau^{\text{turn}}_i$ is a parameter at terminal/intermediate stations.
7. **OD matrix known:** The OD fraction $\lambda_{i,h}^{\text{od}}$ is an input parameter (estimated from historical data).
8. **Discrete time grid:** All times are multiples of $\Delta$; this enables the use of interval-indexed passenger variables.

---

## 8. MPC Integration

At each MPC step $s$:

1. **State measurement:** Obtain current train positions, compositions, and passenger queue lengths $w_{i,h-1}$.
2. **Demand forecast:** Predict $d_{i,h}$ for $h = 1, \dots, H$ over horizon $[t_s, t_s + T]$.
3. **Solve the MILP** above to obtain $\{t^{\text{arr}}, t^{\text{dep}}, n_k, x_{k,i}, z_{k,k',i}\}$.
4. **Apply first control action** (departure times and compositions for the next interval).
5. **Roll the horizon** forward and repeat.

In the **learning-based variant** described in the input, the integer variables $(n_k, x_{k,i}, z_{k,k',i}, u_{k,r})$ are first predicted by an LSTM network after presolve pruning, and the remaining continuous variables are obtained by solving the LP relaxation with the integers fixed.

---

## 9. Summary of Variable Counts (per MPC step)

| Variable type | Symbol | Count (approx.) |
|---|---|---|
| Continuous timetable | $t^{\text{arr}}, t^{\text{dep}}, \delta$ | $O(|\mathcal{K}| \cdot |\mathcal{S}|)$ |
| Integer composition | $n_k$ | $|\mathcal{K}|$ |
| Binary stopping | $x_{k,i}$ | $|\mathcal{K}| \cdot |\mathcal{S}|$ |
| Binary circulation | $z_{k,k',i}$ | $O(|\mathcal{K}|^2 \cdot |\mathcal{S}|)$ |
| Binary rolling stock | $u_{k,r}$ | $|\mathcal{K}| \cdot |\mathcal{R}|$ |
| Continuous passenger | $b, a, p, w, W, f$ | $O(|\mathcal{K}| \cdot |\mathcal{S}| \cdot |\mathcal{H}| \cdot |\mathcal{S}|)$ |

This completes the MILP formulation. The model is ready to be implemented in standard solvers (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX) or to be paired with the LSTM-based integer prediction module described in the input.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

Below is a complete mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation that integrates train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with speed management (speed profiles and energy consumption) for high-speed railway operations under partial segment blockages.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $I$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $B$ | Set of track blocks, indexed by $b$ |
| $K$ | Set of discrete time intervals, $K = \{0, 1, \dots, |K|-1\}$, indexed by $k$ |
| $B^{\text{in}}_b \subset B$ | Set of blocks immediately preceding block $b$ |
| $B^{\text{out}}_b \subset B$ | Set of blocks immediately following block $b$ |
| $B^s \subset B$ | Set of blocks containing station $s$ |
| $B^{\text{up}}, B^{\text{down}} \subset B$ | Blocks in the up and down directions |
| $\text{opp}(b)$ | The opposite-direction block corresponding to block $b$ |
| $P$ | Set of breakpoints for piecewise-linear energy approximation, $p \in P$ |
| $V_p$ | Speed value at breakpoint $p$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $\tau$ | Duration of each time interval | h |
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ | km |
| $v^{\max}$ | Maximum allowed speed | km/h |
| $v^{\min}$ | Minimum allowed speed | km/h |
| $a_i^s$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ | interval |
| $d_i^s$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ | interval |
| $h^{\min}, h^{\max}$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time at stations | interval |
| $\theta$ | Minimum safety headway between consecutive trains | interval |
| $\Delta_{b,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if block $b$ is disrupted during interval $k$ | — |
| $\alpha_e$ | Linear energy coefficient (resistive + traction losses) | kWh/(km·h) |
| $\beta_e$ | Quadratic energy coefficient (aerodynamic drag) | kWh/(km·h²) |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) | — |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3$ | Weights for delay, energy, and cancellation objectives | — |
| $N_i$ | Number of blocks on the original route of train $i$ | — |
| $T^{\max}$ | Length of planning horizon | interval |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_{i,b,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ occupies block $b$ during interval $k$ |
| $y_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ (intervals) |
| $z_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ (intervals) |
| $v_{i,b,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Speed of train $i$ on block $b$ during interval $k$ (km/h) |
| $\hat{v}_{i,b,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Piecewise-linear approximation of $v_{i,b,k}^2$ |
| $e_{i,b,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on block $b$ during interval $k$ (kWh) |
| $\delta_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Arrival delay of train $i$ at station $s$ (intervals) |
| $c_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $w_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ (intervals) |
| $o_{i,j,b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ exits block $b$ before train $j$ enters it (ordering) |
| $r_{i,b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if block $b$ belongs to the (possibly rerouted) route of train $i$ |
| $u_{i,b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted through block $b$ (using the opposite track) |
| $\lambda_{i,b,k,p}$ | $[0,1]$ | Convex combination weight for breakpoint $p$ (SOS2) |

---

## 4. Objective Function

The objective minimizes a weighted sum of total passenger delay, total energy consumption, and the number of cancelled trains:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; w_1 \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{s \in S} \delta_{i,s} \;+\; w_2 \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{b \in B}\sum_{k \in K} e_{i,b,k} \;+\; w_3 \sum_{i \in I} c_i
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Block Occupation and Bidirectional Conflict Resolution

**(C1) Unidirectional block capacity** — at most one train per block per interval:
$$
\sum_{i \in I} x_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; 1 \qquad \forall\, b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

**(C2) Bidirectional conflict resolution on shared (rerouted) track** — for any pair of trains traveling in opposite directions on the same physical track during rerouting:
$$
x_{i,b,k} + x_{j,\text{opp}(b),k} \;\leq\; 1 + o_{i,j,b} \qquad \forall\, i \in I^{\text{up}},\; j \in I^{\text{down}},\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

**(C3) Ordering consistency on shared blocks:**
$$
\sum_{k \in K} k \cdot x_{i,b,k} \;+\; \theta \;\leq\; \sum_{k \in K} k \cdot x_{j,\text{opp}(b),k} + M(1 - o_{i,j,b}) \qquad \forall\, i \in I^{\text{up}},\; j \in I^{\text{down}},\; b \in B
$$

### 5.2 Disruption and Rerouting Constraints

**(C4) Block unavailability during disruption** — a disrupted block cannot be used unless the train is rerouted via the opposite track:
$$
x_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; 1 - \Delta_{b,k} + u_{i,b} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

**(C5) Rerouting activation** — if a train uses the opposite-direction block, it must be flagged as rerouted:
$$
x_{i,\text{opp}(b),k} \;\leq\; u_{i,b} + (1 - \Delta_{b,k}) \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

**(C6) Rerouting consistency** — a train cannot be rerouted through a block unless its original route included the corresponding disrupted block:
$$
u_{i,b} \;\leq\; \sum_{k \in K} \Delta_{b,k} + r_{i,b}^{\text{orig}} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B
$$

where $r_{i,b}^{\text{orig}} \in \{0,1\}$ is a known parameter indicating whether block $b$ is on train $i$'s original route.

### 5.3 Movement (Space–Time Continuity) Constraints

**(C7) Entry continuity** — a train can enter block $b$ at time $k$ only if it was in $b$ or a predecessor block at time $k-1$:
$$
x_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; x_{i,b,k-1} + \sum_{b' \in B^{\text{in}}_b} x_{i,b',k-1} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B,\; k \in K \setminus \{0\}
$$

**(C8) Exit continuity** — a train in block $b$ at time $k$ must remain in $b$ or move to a successor block at time $k+1$:
$$
x_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; x_{i,b,k+1} + \sum_{b' \in B^{\text{out}}_b} x_{i,b',k+1} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B,\; k \in K \setminus \{|K|-1\}
$$

**(C9) Single passage per block** — each train traverses each block on its route at most once:
$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; |K| \cdot r_{i,b} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B
$$

### 5.4 Speed and Traversal-Time Constraints

**(C10) Speed limits:**
$$
v^{\min} \cdot x_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; v_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; v^{\max} \cdot x_{i,b,k} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

**(C11) Minimum traversal time** — the number of intervals spent in block $b$ must suffice to traverse its length:
$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{i,b,k} \;\geq\; \left\lceil \frac{L_b}{v^{\max} \cdot \tau} \right\rceil \cdot r_{i,b} - M(1 - r_{i,b}) \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B
$$

**(C12) Maximum traversal time** — prevents excessive dwelling inside a block:
$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; \left\lceil \frac{L_b}{v^{\min} \cdot \tau} \right\rceil \cdot r_{i,b} + M(1 - r_{i,b}) \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B
$$

### 5.5 Timing and Dwell Constraints

**(C13) Arrival time at station** — let $b_s^{\text{last}}$ denote the last block before station $s$ on train $i$'s route:
$$
y_{i,s} \;\geq\; k - M(1 - x_{i,b_s^{\text{last}},k}) \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S,\; k \in K
$$
$$
y_{i,s} \;\leq\; k + M(1 - x_{i,b_s^{\text{last}},k}) \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S,\; k \in K
$$

**(C14) Departure time at station:**
$$
z_{i,s} \;=\; y_{i,s} + w_{i,s} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S
$$

**(C15) Dwell-time bounds** (only for non-cancelled trains):
$$
h^{\min}(1 - c_i) \;\leq\; w_{i,s} \;\leq\; h^{\max}(1 - c_i) \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S
$$

### 5.6 Delay Definition

**(C16) Arrival delay:**
$$
\delta_{i,s} \;\geq\; y_{i,s} - a_i^s \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\delta_{i,s} \;\geq\; 0
$$

### 5.7 Headway and Safety Constraints

**(C17) Station headway** — minimum time between consecutive trains at the same station:
$$
y_{i,s} - y_{j,s} \;\geq\; \theta - M(1 - o_{i,j,s}) \qquad \forall\, i,j \in I,\; s \in S
$$
$$
y_{j,s} - y_{i,s} \;\geq\; \theta - M \cdot o_{i,j,s} \qquad \forall\, i,j \in I,\; s \in S
$$

**(C18) Block headway** — minimum time between consecutive trains on the same block:
$$
\sum_{k \in K} k \cdot x_{i,b,k} - \sum_{k \in K} k \cdot x_{j,b,k} \;\geq\; \theta - M(1 - o_{i,j,b}) \qquad \forall\, i,j \in I,\; b \in B
$$

### 5.8 Route Definition

**(C19) Route cardinality** — the total number of blocks traversed equals the route length (unless cancelled):
$$
\sum_{b \in B} r_{i,b} \;=\; N_i (1 - c_i) \qquad \forall\, i \in I
$$

**(C20) Block–route consistency:**
$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{i,b,k} \;\geq\; r_{i,b} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B
$$
$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; M \cdot r_{i,b} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B
$$

### 5.9 Energy Consumption (Piecewise-Linear Approximation)

**(C21) Speed-squared approximation via SOS2 weights:**
$$
\sum_{p \in P} \lambda_{i,b,k,p} \;=\; 1 \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$
$$
v_{i,b,k} \;=\; \sum_{p \in P} V_p \cdot \lambda_{i,b,k,p} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$
$$
\hat{v}_{i,b,k} \;=\; \sum_{p \in P} V_p^2 \cdot \lambda_{i,b,k,p} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

with the SOS2 constraint: at most two consecutive $\lambda_{i,b,k,p}$ are nonzero.

**(C22) Energy consumption:**
$$
e_{i,b,k} \;=\; \tau \cdot L_b \cdot \left( \alpha_e \cdot \frac{v_{i,b,k}}{L_b} + \beta_e \cdot \frac{\hat{v}_{i,b,k}}{L_b} \right) \cdot x_{i,b,k} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

which simplifies to:
$$
e_{i,b,k} \;=\; \tau \left( \alpha_e \cdot v_{i,b,k} + \beta_e \cdot \hat{v}_{i,b,k} \right) \cdot x_{i,b,k} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

### 5.10 Cancellation Constraints

**(C23) Cancellation effect on movement:**
$$
\sum_{b \in B}\sum_{k \in K} x_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; M(1 - c_i) \qquad \forall\, i \in I
$$

**(C24) Cancellation effect on delay:**
$$
\delta_{i,s} \;\leq\; M(1 - c_i) \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S
$$

### 5.11 Initial and Terminal Conditions

**(C25) Origin departure** — train $i$ starts at its origin block at the scheduled (or earliest feasible) time:
$$
\sum_{k \in K} k \cdot x_{i,b_i^{\text{orig}},k} \;\leq\; d_i^{\text{orig}} + M \cdot c_i \qquad \forall\, i \in I
$$

**(C26) Destination arrival** — train $i$ must reach its destination block within the planning horizon:
$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{i,b_i^{\text{dest}},k} \;=\; 1 - c_i \qquad \forall\, i \in I
$$

**(C27) Planning horizon:**
$$
y_{i,s},\; z_{i,s},\; \sum_{k \in K} k \cdot x_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; T^{\max} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S,\; b \in B
$$

### 5.12 Variable Domains

$$
x_{i,b,k},\; c_i,\; o_{i,j,b},\; r_{i,b},\; u_{i,b} \;\in\; \{0,1\}
$$
$$
y_{i,s},\; z_{i,s},\; v_{i,b,k},\; \hat{v}_{i,b,k},\; e_{i,b,k},\; \delta_{i,s},\; w_{i,s},\; \lambda_{i,b,k,p} \;\geq\; 0
$$

---

## 6. Modeling Assumptions

1. **Time discretization.** The planning horizon is partitioned into equal intervals of duration $\tau$ (e.g., 1 min). All timing variables are integer multiples of $\tau$.
2. **Block structure.** The track is divided into fixed blocks; each block can be occupied by at most one train at a time, except during bidirectional rerouting where ordering variables $o_{i,j,b}$ enforce safe passage.
3. **Disruption model.** A disruption is represented by a binary matrix $\Delta_{b,k}$ indicating which blocks are unavailable during which intervals; partial blockages affect a contiguous set of blocks over a contiguous time window.
4. **Rerouting.** When a block is disrupted, an affected train may be rerouted to the opposite-direction track ($\text{opp}(b)$); this introduces bidirectional traffic that must be sequenced using the ordering variables.
5. **Speed limits.** Trains operate within $[v^{\min}, v^{\max}]$, assumed identical for all trains for clarity (can be train-specific if needed).
6. **Energy model.** Energy consumption is approximated by a piecewise-linear function of speed, $e = \tau(\alpha_e v + \beta_e v^2)$, capturing both mechanical resistance and aerodynamic drag.
7. **Dwell-time flexibility.** Dwell times at intermediate stations are decision variables bounded by $[h^{\min}, h^{\max}]$.
8. **Cancellation.** Trains are either fully operated or fully cancelled; partial cancellation is not permitted.
9. **Single-track segments per direction.** Each direction has its own dedicated track under normal operations; bidirectional use is permitted only during rerouting through disrupted sections.
10. **Deterministic demand.** Passenger demand is not explicitly modeled; the objective weights $w_1, w_2, w_3$ are exogenously set to balance delay, energy, and cancellation priorities.
11. **No train overtaking within a block.** The spatial continuity constraints (C7)–(C8) and the single-passage constraint (C9) jointly prevent a train from re-entering a block it has already traversed.
12. **Homogeneous trains.** All trains share the same kinematic and energy parameters; train-specific parameters can be introduced by indexing $\alpha_e, \beta_e, v^{\min}, v^{\max}$ with $i$ if required.

---

## 7. Summary of Decision Coverage

| Rescheduling Action | Modeling Element |
|---------------------|------------------|
| **Retiming** | $y_{i,s}, z_{i,s}, w_{i,s}, \delta_{i,s}$ |
| **Reordering** | $o_{i,j,b}$ (block-level), $o_{i,j,s}$ (station-level) |
| **Rerouting** | $u_{i,b}, r_{i,b}$ |
| **Cancellation** | $c_i$ |
| **Speed profile** | $v_{i,b,k}, \hat{v}_{i,b,k}$ |
| **Energy consumption** | $e_{i,b,k}$ |

This MILP jointly produces a **conflict-free rescheduled timetable** (arrival/departure times, train ordering, routes, cancellations) and the corresponding **executable speed profiles** that minimize a weighted combination of passenger delay, energy consumption, and service cancellations, while respecting all operational, safety, and disruption constraints.

messages.content: You convert the text of an optimization model into a structured record. Report only what the text states as mathematics, that is, objective functions, equations and inequalities written with symbols. Do not complete, repair, improve or invent anything.

Read the text below and fill in the predefined form.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
