# Final MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

Below is the complete, refined MILP formulation after three iterations of improvement. The model integrates train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with train speed management (energy-efficient speed profiles) under partial segment blockage disruptions with bidirectional conflict resolution.

---

## 1. Sets and Parameters

### Sets

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{I}$ | Set of trains, $i \in \mathcal{I}$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Stations along the route, $s \in \mathcal{S} = \{0, 1, \dots, |\mathcal{S}|-1\}$ |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Track segments, $p \in \mathcal{P} = \{1, \dots, |\mathcal{S}|-1\}$; segment $p$ connects station $p-1$ to $p$ |
| $\mathcal{D}$ | Disruption events, $d \in \mathcal{D}$ |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Rerouting alternatives, $r \in \mathcal{R}$ |
| $\mathcal{V}$ | Discretized speed grid for SOS-2 approximation |

### Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $m_i$ | Mass of train $i$ [t] |
| $L_p$ | Length of segment $p$ [m] |
| $v^{\max}$ | Maximum allowed speed [m/s] |
| $a^{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration [m/s²] |
| $d^{\max}$ | Maximum deceleration magnitude [m/s²] |
| $f_i^{\text{res}}$ | Specific running resistance of train $i$ [N/t] |
| $\tau^{\text{dw}}_{i,s}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ [s] |
| $\tau^{\text{start}}_i$ | Earliest departure time of train $i$ |
| $\tau^{\text{target}}_i$ | Target arrival time of train $i$ at destination |
| $\tau^{\text{hor}}$ | Planning horizon [s] |
| $\tau^{\text{dis}}_{d,\text{start}}, \tau^{\text{dis}}_{d,\text{end}}$ | Start/end of disruption $d$ |
| $\text{seg}(d)$ | Segment blocked by disruption $d$ |
| $h^{\min}$ | Minimum headway between trains on the same track [s] |
| $h^{\text{cross}}$ | Minimum headway for opposite-direction trains |
| $\rho^{\text{tr}}, \rho^{\text{br}}$ | Energy cost per unit traction / braking power |
| $\eta^{\text{regen}}$ | Regenerative braking efficiency |
| $C^{\text{cancel}}, C^{\text{delay}}, C^{\text{energy}}, C^{\text{reroute}}$ | Penalty weights |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) |

---

## 2. Decision Variables

| Symbol | Type | Domain | Description |
|--------|------|--------|-------------|
| $x_i$ | Binary | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $y_{i,r}$ | Binary | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses reroute $r$ |
| $t_{i,s}$ | Continuous | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $v_{i,s}$ | Continuous | $[0, v^{\max}]$ | Speed of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $a_{i,p}$ | Continuous | $[-d^{\max}, a^{\max}]$ | Average acceleration on segment $p$ |
| $\delta_{i,j,p}$ | Binary | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $p$ before train $j$ |
| $u_{i,d}$ | Binary | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is affected by disruption $d$ |
| $\alpha_{i,d}$ | Binary | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if entry time of train $i$ on $\text{seg}(d)$ is before $\tau^{\text{dis}}_{d,\text{end}}$ |
| $\beta_{i,d}$ | Binary | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if exit time of train $i$ on $\text{seg}(d)$ is after $\tau^{\text{dis}}_{d,\text{start}}$ |
| $w^{\text{tr}}_{i,p}$ | Continuous | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Traction energy on segment $p$ for train $i$ |
| $w^{\text{br}}_{i,p}$ | Continuous | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Braking energy on segment $p$ for train $i$ |
| $E_i$ | Continuous | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Total net energy of train $i$ |
| $\eta_i$ | Continuous | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Linearized positive delay of train $i$ |
| $\sigma_{i,p}$ | Binary | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if segment $p$ is in traction mode for train $i$ |
| $F^{\text{tr}+}_{i,p}, F^{\text{tr}-}_{i,p}$ | Continuous | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Positive/negative tractive force decomposition |
| $\lambda_{i,p,v}$ | Continuous | $[0,1]$ | SOS-2 weights for speed discretization |

---

## 3. Objective Function

$$
\min \; \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \Big[ C^{\text{cancel}} x_i \;+\; C^{\text{delay}} \eta_i \;+\; C^{\text{energy}} E_i \;+\; \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} C^{\text{reroute}}_{i,r} y_{i,r} \Big]
$$

subject to the linearization of the positive delay:

$$
\eta_i \geq t_{i,|\mathcal{S}|-1} - \tau^{\text{target}}_i, \qquad \eta_i \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}
$$

---

## 4. Constraints

### 4.1 Rerouting and Cancellation Logic

Each train selects **at most one** reroute (or none):

$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} y_{i,r} \leq 1 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I}
$$

Cancellation forces all times and speeds to zero:

$$
x_i + \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} y_{i,r} \leq 1 \quad \forall i
$$

$$
t_{i,s} \leq T^{\text{cancel}} x_i + \tau^{\text{hor}}(1 - x_i) \quad \forall i, s
$$

$$
v_{i,s} \leq v^{\max}(1 - x_i) \quad \forall i, s
$$

If rerouted, the segment set used by train $i$ becomes $\mathcal{P}^{r}_i$:

$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P} \setminus \mathcal{P}^{r}_i} \mathbf{1}[a_{i,p} \text{ used}] \leq M(1 - y_{i,r}) \quad \forall i, r
$$

### 4.2 Time Progression along Segments (Kinematic Relation)

For each train $i$ and segment $p$, using the constant-acceleration kinematic equation:

$$
L_p = \frac{v_{i,p-1} + v_{i,p}}{2} \cdot \Delta t_{i,p}
$$

where $\Delta t_{i,p} = t_{i,p} - t_{i,p-1} - \tau^{\text{dw}}_{i,p-1}$. Linearized with auxiliary variable $\theta_{i,p} = v_{i,p-1} + v_{i,p}$:

$$
\theta_{i,p} = v_{i,p-1} + v_{i,p}
$$

$$
2 L_p = \theta_{i,p} \cdot (t_{i,p} - t_{i,p-1} - \tau^{\text{dw}}_{i,p-1})
$$

**Practical linearization (discretized speeds via SOS-2):**

$$
v_{i,p} = \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} v \, \lambda_{i,p,v}, \qquad \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} \lambda_{i,p,v} = 1, \quad \lambda_{i,p,\cdot} \in \text{SOS-2}
$$

$$
\Delta t_{i,p} \cdot \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} v \, \lambda_{i,p,v} = 2 L_p
$$

with each product $\Delta t_{i,p} \cdot \lambda_{i,p,v}$ linearized using McCormick relaxations.

### 4.3 Acceleration Bounds

$$
a_{i,p} = \frac{v_{i,p}^2 - v_{i,p-1}^2}{2 L_p}
$$

Linearize by introducing $z_{i,p} = v_{i,p}^2$ with SOS-2 / piecewise-linear underestimator:

$$
a_{i,p} = \frac{z_{i,p} - z_{i,p-1}}{2 L_p}, \qquad -d^{\max} \leq a_{i,p} \leq a^{\max}
$$

### 4.4 Speed Boundary Conditions

**At origin station ($s = 0$):**

$$
v_{i,0} = v^{\text{init}}_i \quad \forall i
$$

**At destination station ($s = |\mathcal{S}|-1$):**

$$
0 \leq v_{i,|\mathcal{S}|-1} \leq v^{\text{term}}_i \quad \forall i
$$

(typically $v^{\text{term}}_i = 0$).

**Speed continuity at intermediate stations:**

$$
|v_{i,p} - v_{i,p-1}| \leq a^{\max} \cdot \tau^{\text{dw}}_{i,p-1} \quad \forall i, p \in \{1,\dots,|\mathcal{S}|-2\}
$$

### 4.5 Disruption Detection

For disruption $d$ blocking segment $\text{seg}(d) = p_d$, train $i$ enters at $t^{\text{in}}_{i,p_d} = t_{i,p_d - 1}$ and exits at $t^{\text{out}}_{i,p_d} = t_{i,p_d}$. Define auxiliary binaries:

$$
\alpha_{i,d} = \mathbf{1}\!\left[t_{i,p_d - 1} < \tau^{\text{dis}}_{d,\text{end}}\right], \qquad
\beta_{i,d} = \mathbf{1}\!\left[t_{i,p_d} > \tau^{\text{dis}}_{d,\text{start}}\right]
$$

**Linearization:**

$$
\alpha_{i,d} \geq \frac{\tau^{\text{dis}}_{d,\text{end}} - t_{i,p_d - 1}}{M} \quad \forall i, d
$$

$$
\alpha_{i,d} \leq 1 + \frac{\tau^{\text{dis}}_{d,\text{end}} - t_{i,p_d - 1}}{M} \quad \forall i, d
$$

$$
\beta_{i,d} \geq \frac{t_{i,p_d} - \tau^{\text{dis}}_{d,\text{start}}}{M} \quad \forall i, d
$$

$$
\beta_{i,d} \leq 1 + \frac{t_{i,p_d} - \tau^{\text{dis}}_{d,\text{start}}}{M} \quad \forall i, d
$$

**Overlap indicator:**

$$
u_{i,d} \leq \alpha_{i,d}, \qquad u_{i,d} \leq \beta_{i,d}, \qquad u_{i,d} \geq \alpha_{i,d} + \beta_{i,d} - 1
$$

**Hard constraint** — a non-cancelled, non-rerouted train cannot traverse a closed segment during the disruption:

$$
u_{i,d} \leq x_i + \sum_{r \,:\, p_d \notin \mathcal{P}^{r}_i} y_{i,r} \quad \forall i, d
$$

### 4.6 Bidirectional Conflict (Headway) Constraints

**Ordering constraint:**

$$
\delta_{i,j,p} + \delta_{j,i,p} = 1 \quad \forall i \neq j, p
$$

**Case A — Same-direction conflicts** (both trains on forward track, or both on reverse track):

$$
t_{j,p-1} \geq t_{i,p} + h^{\min} - M(1 - \delta_{i,j,p}) \quad \forall i \neq j, p
$$

$$
t_{i,p-1} \geq t_{j,p} + h^{\min} - M \, \delta_{i,j,p} \quad \forall i \neq j, p
$$

**Case B — Cross-direction conflicts** (one train on forward, other on reverse via reroute $r$):

$$
t_{j,p-1} - t_{i,p} \geq h^{\text{cross}} - M(1 - \delta_{i,j,p}) - M(1 - y_{j,r}) \quad \forall i \neq j, p, r
$$

$$
t_{i,p-1} - t_{j,p} \geq h^{\text{cross}} - M \, \delta_{i,j,p} - M(1 - y_{j,r}) \quad \forall i \neq j, p, r
$$

### 4.7 Energy Model

**Tractive force decomposition:**

$$
F^{\text{tr}}_{i,p} = F^{\text{tr}+}_{i,p} - F^{\text{tr}-}_{i,p}
$$

$$
F^{\text{tr}+}_{i,p} \leq M \, \sigma_{i,p}, \qquad F^{\text{tr}-}_{i,p} \leq M (1 - \sigma_{i,p})
$$

**Traction energy (positive force × distance):**

$$
w^{\text{tr}}_{i,p} \geq F^{\text{tr}+}_{i,p} \cdot L_p - M(1 - \sigma_{i,p}), \qquad w^{\text{tr}}_{i,p} \geq 0
$$

**Braking energy (negative force magnitude × distance):**

$$
w^{\text{br}}_{i,p} \geq F^{\text{tr}-}_{i,p} \cdot L_p - M \, \sigma_{i,p}, \qquad w^{\text{br}}_{i,p} \geq 0
$$

**Net energy with regenerative recovery:**

$$
E_i = \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}} \big(w^{\text{tr}}_{i,p} - \eta^{\text{regen}} \, w^{\text{br}}_{i,p}\big)
$$

### 4.8 Time-Window and Horizon Constraints

$$
\tau^{\text{start}}_i \leq t_{i,0} \leq \tau^{\text{hor}} \quad \forall i
$$

$$
0 \leq t_{i,s} \leq \tau^{\text{hor}} \quad \forall i, s
$$

---

## 5. Valid Inequalities (Tightening)

### 5.1 Minimum Segment Traversal Time Cut

$$
t_{i,p} - t_{i,p-1} \geq \frac{L_p}{v^{\max}} + \tau^{\text{dw}}_{i,p-1} \quad \forall i, p
$$

### 5.2 Symmetry Breaking on Train Indices

$$
t_{i,0} \leq t_{i+1,0} \quad \forall i \in \{1, \dots, |\mathcal{I}|-1\}
$$

### 5.3 Discretization of Time for Conflict Checking

Introduce a fine time grid $\mathcal{T} = \{0, \Delta, 2\Delta, \dots, \tau^{\text{hor}}\}$ and binary $\zeta_{i,p,t} = 1$ iff train $i$ occupies segment $p$ at time $t$:

$$
\zeta_{i,p,t} \geq \mathbf{1}[t_{i,p-1} \leq t] + \mathbf{1}[t \leq t_{i,p}] - 1
$$

Linearized analogously to disruption detection. Then for same-track conflict:

$$
\zeta_{i,p,t} + \zeta_{j,p,t} \leq 1 + x_i + x_j \quad \forall i \neq j, p, t
$$

### 5.4 Reroute Mutual Exclusivity

$$
y_{i,r} + y_{j,r'} \leq 1 \quad \text{if reroutes } r, r' \text{ are physically incompatible on segment } p
$$

---

## 6. Complete Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & \sum_i \big[ C^{\text{cancel}} x_i + C^{\text{delay}} \eta_i + C^{\text{energy}} E_i + \sum_r C^{\text{reroute}}_{i,r} y_{i,r} \big] \\[4pt]
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(4.1) Rerouting/cancellation logic} \\
& \text{(4.2)–(4.4) Kinematics, speed, dwell} \\
& \text{(4.5) Disruption overlap detection} \\
& \text{(4.6) Bidirectional headway conflicts} \\
& \text{(4.7) Energy balance} \\
& \text{(4.8) Time windows} \\
& \text{(5) Valid inequalities} \\
& \text{all variables in domains of Section 2.}
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7. Key Modeling Assumptions

1. **Constant acceleration per segment**: Each segment uses a single average acceleration value, providing a good trade-off between accuracy and tractability.
2. **Discretized speed grid (SOS-2)**: Speeds are approximated via a finite grid with SOS-2 structure, enabling linearization of bilinear terms.
3. **Bidirectional single-track working**: When rerouted, a train uses the opposite track; conflicts arise with trains traveling in the opposite direction.
4. **Disruption as segment blockage**: A disruption blocks a specific segment during a time window; trains must reroute, be rescheduled outside the window, or be cancelled.
5. **Regenerative braking**: Braking energy is partially recovered with efficiency $\eta^{\text{regen}}$.
6. **Headway constraints**: Both same-direction ($h^{\min}$) and cross-direction ($h^{\text{cross}}$) minimum time separations are enforced.
7. **Cancellation as last resort**: Trains are cancelled only if rerouting and rescheduling are infeasible.

---

## 8. Notes on Solvability

| Aspect | Treatment |
|--------|-----------|
| Bilinear terms ($\Delta t \cdot v$, $F \cdot v$) | McCormick envelopes + SOS-2 discretization |
| Big-M values | Tightened using time/speed bounds per segment |
| Symmetry | Index-based ordering + reroute exclusivity |
| Scalability | Time-grid discretization (5.3) is the strongest tightening; recommended for $|\mathcal{I}| > 20$ |
| Solver | Gurobi / CPLEX with callbacks for lazy conflict constraints |

This formulation provides a **physically consistent, disruption-aware, energy-minimizing** MILP suitable for operational train rescheduling under bidirectional single-track working during partial segment blockages.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

Below is a complete mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation that integrates train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with train speed management (speed profiles, energy-efficient driving) for a high-speed railway line subject to a partial segment blockage.

---

## 1. Modeling Assumptions

The following assumptions are made (clearly marked as such where the source text leaves them implicit):

- **A1.** The railway line is a double-track corridor with one track per direction; each block *b* has two directional sub-tracks (up/down).
- **A2.** Time is discretized into uniform steps *k* of length Δt (e.g., 10–30 s).
- **A3.** A single partial blockage event affects one track of one block *b\** during a known time window [T^s, T^e].
- **A4.** Trains may be rerouted to the opposite (still-open) track within the disruption window, but this creates bidirectional conflicts that must be resolved.
- **A5.** Train dynamics are described by a point-mass model with constant mass (resistances neglected or absorbed into coefficients).
- **A6.** Energy consumption follows a Davis-type equation, piecewise-linearized for MILP tractability.
- **A7.** Cancellation, delay, and energy costs are aggregated into a single objective via weighting coefficients.
- **A8.** Dwell times at stations have a fixed minimum; platform capacity is one train at a time.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| 𝕀 | Set of trains, indexed by *i, j* |
| 𝔹 | Set of track blocks (segments between two consecutive signals), indexed by *b* |
| 𝕊 | Set of stations, indexed by *s* |
| 𝕂 | Set of discrete time steps, *k* = 1, 2, …, *K* |
| 𝔻 = {+1, −1} | Set of running directions (+1: up, −1: down) |
| 𝓡_i | Set of feasible routes for train *i* (original and rerouted), indexed by *r* |
| 𝓑_dis ⊂ 𝔹 | Set of disrupted blocks (here, a singleton) |
| 𝕋_i^s | Set of scheduled arrival/departure times for train *i* at station *s* |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| Δt | Time-step length | s |
| L_b | Length of block *b* | m |
| V^max, V^min | Maximum / minimum allowable speed | m/s |
| A^max, A^min | Maximum acceleration / deceleration | m/s² |
| M_i | Mass of train *i* | t |
| ρ, C_d, A_f | Air density, drag coefficient, frontal area | – , – , m² |
| μ, g | Rolling-resistance coefficient, gravity | – , m/s² |
| η | Mechanical / regenerative efficiency | – |
| h_d | Minimum headway time | s |
| τ_s^min | Minimum dwell time at station *s* | s |
| T^s, T^e | Disruption start and end times | s |
| T_i^0 | Scheduled arrival time of train *i* at destination | s |
| C_E, C_D, C_C | Cost weights for energy, delay, cancellation | €/kWh, €/min, € |
| e_0, e_1, e_2, e_3 | Coefficients of the (piecewise-linearized) energy function | kWh/(m·s), etc. |
| 𝓜 | A sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) | – |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Operational / Rescheduling Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| x_{i,b,k} ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 if train *i* occupies block *b* at time *k* |
| y_{i,r} ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 if train *i* is assigned route *r* |
| z_{i,j,b,k} ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 if train *i* exits block *b* before train *j* enters |
| w_i ∈ {0,1} | binary | 1 if train *i* is cancelled |
| t_{i,s}^{arr}, t_{i,s}^{dep} ≥ 0 | continuous | Arrival / departure time of train *i* at station *s* |

### 4.2 Speed-Management Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| p_{i,b,k} ≥ 0 | continuous | Position of train *i* inside block *b* at time *k* (m) |
| v_{i,b,k} ≥ 0 | continuous | Speed of train *i* in block *b* at time *k* (m/s) |
| a_{i,b,k} ∈ ℝ | continuous | Acceleration of train *i* in block *b* at time *k* (m/s²) |
| e_{i,b,k} ≥ 0 | continuous | Energy consumed by train *i* in block *b* at time *k* (kWh) |

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize the total weighted cost of energy consumption, total delay, and cancellations:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; C_E \sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}}\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} e_{i,b,k}
\;+\; C_D \sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}} \Bigl(t_{i,s_{\text{dest}}}^{\text{arr}} - T_i^0\Bigr)_+
\;+\; C_C \sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}} w_i
$$

where $(\cdot)_+ = \max\{\cdot, 0\}$ (linearized via auxiliary variable).

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Train Dynamics (Speed Profile)

**(C1) Position update (trapezoidal rule):**
$$
p_{i,b,k+1} = p_{i,b,k} + v_{i,b,k}\,\Delta t + \tfrac{1}{2}\,a_{i,b,k}\,\Delta t^2
\quad \forall i\in\mathcal{I},\; b\in\mathcal{B},\; k\in\mathcal{K}\setminus\{K\}
$$

**(C2) Speed update:**
$$
v_{i,b,k+1} = v_{i,b,k} + a_{i,b,k}\,\Delta t
\quad \forall i,b,k
$$

**(C3) Speed limits (Big-M activation):**
$$
V^{\min}\,x_{i,b,k} \;\le\; v_{i,b,k} \;\le\; V^{\max}\,x_{i,b,k}
\quad \forall i,b,k
$$

**(C4) Acceleration limits:**
$$
A^{\min}\,x_{i,b,k} \;\le\; a_{i,b,k} \;\le\; A^{\max}\,x_{i,b,k}
\quad \forall i,b,k
$$

**(C5) Block-length feasibility:**
$$
p_{i,b,k} \;\le\; L_b\,x_{i,b,k}
\quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### 6.2 Block-Occupancy and Routing

**(C6) Single-block occupation per train per time step:**
$$
\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}} x_{i,b,k} \;\le\; 1 - w_i
\quad \forall i,k
$$

**(C7) Route selection (each non-cancelled train picks exactly one route):**
$$
\sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}_i} y_{i,r} = 1 - w_i
\quad \forall i
$$

**(C8) Block-route consistency:**
$$
x_{i,b,k} \;\le\; \sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}_i:\,b\in r} y_{i,r}
\quad \forall i,b,k
$$

**(C9) Disrupted-block prohibition on the affected track:**
For each disrupted block *b\* ∈ 𝓑_dis and each time *k* with k·Δt ∈ [T^s, T^e], trains may use only the opposite-direction sub-track:
$$
x_{i,b^*,k} \;\le\; \sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}_i:\,b^*\in r^{\text{opposite}}} y_{i,r}
\quad \forall i,\; k\cdot\Delta t \in [T^s, T^e]
$$

### 6.3 Conflict Resolution (Bidirectional and Headway)

**(C10) Bidirectional conflict on shared (rerouted) track:**
For any two trains *i, j* with opposite directions that share a block *b*:
$$
x_{i,b,k} + x_{j,b,k} \;\le\; 1
\quad \forall i,j\in\mathcal{I},\; b\in\mathcal{B},\; k\in\mathcal{K},\; d_i \neq d_j
$$

**(C11) Same-direction headway (safety distance):**
$$
x_{i,b,k} + x_{j,b,k} \;\le\; 1
\quad \forall i\neq j,\; b,\; k,\; d_i = d_j
$$
(Relaxable to a time-separation constraint using *z* variables if finer headway is required.)

**(C12) Ordering at shared blocks (precedence):**
$$
z_{i,j,b,k} + z_{j,i,b,k} = 1
\quad \forall i\neq j,\; b,\; k
$$
$$
x_{i,b,k} - x_{j,b,k} \;\le\; z_{i,j,b,k}
\quad \forall i\neq j,\; b,\; k
$$

### 6.4 Station and Dwell Constraints

**(C13) Minimum dwell time:**
$$
t_{i,s}^{\text{dep}} - t_{i,s}^{\text{arr}} \;\ge\; \tau_s^{\min}\,(1 - w_i)
\quad \forall i,s
$$

**(C14) Platform capacity (one train at a time):**
$$
\sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}} \mathbb{1}\{t_{i,s}^{\text{arr}} \le k\Delta t \le t_{i,s}^{\text{dep}}\} \;\le\; 1
\quad \forall s,\; k
$$
(Linearized via additional binary station-occupation variables.)

**(C15) Arrival/departure time windows:**
$$
T_{i,s}^{\text{arr},\min} \;\le\; t_{i,s}^{\text{arr}} \;\le\; T_{i,s}^{\text{arr},\max}
$$
$$
T_{i,s}^{\text{dep},\min} \;\le\; t_{i,s}^{\text{dep}} \;\le\; T_{i,s}^{\text{dep},\max}
$$

**(C16) Initial and terminal conditions:**
$$
t_{i,s_{\text{orig}}}^{\text{dep}} = T_i^{\text{start}},\qquad
t_{i,s_{\text{dest}}}^{\text{arr}} \;\text{free (minimized)}
$$

### 6.5 Coupling between Timetable and Speed Profile

**(C17) Arrival time equals time at which the train reaches the end of the last block before station *s*:**
$$
t_{i,s}^{\text{arr}} \;\ge\; k\Delta t - \mathcal{M}\bigl(1 - x_{i,b_s^{\text{last}},k}\bigr)
\quad \forall i,s,k
$$
$$
t_{i,s}^{\text{arr}} \;\le\; k\Delta t + \mathcal{M}\bigl(1 - x_{i,b_s^{\text{last}},k}\bigr)
\quad \forall i,s,k
$$

**(C18) Departure time equals time at which the train leaves station *s* (enters the next block):**
$$
t_{i,s}^{\text{dep}} \;\ge\; k\Delta t - \mathcal{M}\bigl(1 - x_{i,b_s^{\text{next}},k}\bigr)
\quad \forall i,s,k
$$

### 6.6 Energy Consumption (Linearized Davis Equation)

The continuous Davis equation:
$$
P_{i}(v,a) = \frac{v}{\eta}\Bigl(M_i g \mu + 0.5\,\rho\,C_d\,A_f\,v^2 + M_i a\Bigr)
$$

is approximated by a piecewise-linear function of *v* and *a*:

**(C19) Piecewise-linear energy definition:**
$$
e_{i,b,k} \;\ge\; \bigl(e_0 + e_1 v_{i,b,k} + e_2 \hat v_{i,b,k} + e_3 \hat a_{i,b,k}\bigr) - \mathcal{M}(1 - x_{i,b,k})
$$
$$
e_{i,b,k} \;\ge\; 0
$$
where $\hat v_{i,b,k}$ and $\hat a_{i,b,k}$ are auxiliary continuous variables linked to *v* and *a* through piecewise-linear envelopes (SOS-2 or convex-combination formulation; see Assumption A6).

### 6.7 Cancellation Logic

**(C20) Cancelled trains occupy no resources:**
$$
x_{i,b,k} \le 1 - w_i,\quad y_{i,r} \le 1 - w_i,\quad t_{i,s}^{\text{arr}} \le \mathcal{M}(1-w_i)
\quad \forall i,b,k,r,s
$$

---

## 7. Linearization Notes

- **Nonlinearities** in (C1)–(C2) are avoided because *v* and *a* are continuous and the equations are linear.
- The **quadratic terms** $v^2$ and $a^2$ in the energy equation (C19) are replaced by piecewise-linear envelopes (SOS-2 variables), standard in railway-energy MILPs.
- The **Big-M** constant 𝓜 is set to a tight value, e.g., $\mathcal{M} = K\Delta t$, to keep the LP relaxation strong.
- **Indicator constraints** (e.g., C3, C4) can equivalently be modeled with SOS-1 structures for tighter relaxation.

---

## 8. Summary

The proposed MILP simultaneously decides, for every train *i*, every block *b*, and every time step *k*:

1. **Whether** the train occupies the block (x_{i,b,k}),
2. **Which route** (original or rerouted) the train follows (y_{i,r}),
3. **At what speed and acceleration** it traverses the block (v_{i,b,k}, a_{i,b,k}),
4. **When** it arrives at and departs from each station (t_{i,s}^{arr}, t_{i,s}^{dep}),
5. **Whether** the train is cancelled (w_i),

subject to kinematic, safety, capacity, disruption, and energy constraints. The objective balances **energy efficiency**, **delay minimization**, and **service preservation**, yielding a conflict-free, executable rescheduling timetable with consistent speed profiles under partial segment blockages.

Text:
# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $I$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i \in I$ |
| $J$ | Set of stations, indexed by $j \in J$ |
| $B$ | Set of track blocks (segments between stations), indexed by $b \in B$ |
| $K$ | Set of discretized time steps, indexed by $k \in K$, $K = \{1, 2, \ldots, |K|\}$ |
| $R_i$ | Set of feasible routes for train $i$ (original + rerouting alternatives), indexed by $r$ |
| $D$ | Set of directions, $D = \{+1, -1\}$ (up/down) |
| $I_b^{\text{aff}}$ | Subset of trains affected by the disruption in block $b$ |

**Assumption (A1):** The time horizon is discretized into equal intervals of duration $\Delta t$. The track is divided into homogeneous blocks of length $L_b$. The disruption affects a single block $b^*$ during a known time window $[k^{\text{dis}}_s, k^{\text{dis}}_e]$.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ (m) |
| $\Delta t$ | Duration of each time step (s) |
| $v^{\max}, v^{\min}$ | Maximum and minimum allowed speeds (m/s) |
| $a^{\max}, a^{\min}$ | Maximum traction and braking accelerations (m/s²) |
| $d^{\min}_{bb'}$ | Minimum headway time between consecutive blocks (s) |
| $\tau^{\min}_j, \tau^{\max}_j$ | Minimum and maximum dwell times at station $j$ (s) |
| $H^{\min}$ | Minimum safe time headway between trains (s) |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (Big-M) |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Energy consumption coefficients: $\alpha$ (resistance), $\beta$ (traction), $\gamma$ (auxiliary) |
| $c^{\text{delay}}$ | Penalty per second of delay (€/s) |
| $c^{\text{cancel}}$ | Penalty for cancelling a train (€/train) |
| $c^{\text{energy}}$ | Cost per kWh of energy (€/kWh) |
| $T^{\text{sch}}_{i,j}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $j$ |
| $r^{\text{dis}}_b$ | Binary parameter: 1 if block $b$ is in the disruption area |
| $[k^{\text{dis}}_s, k^{\text{dis}}_e]$ | Disruption time window (time steps) |
| $M_i$ | Mass of train $i$ (tons) |
| $\eta$ | Regenerative braking efficiency factor |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Speed Profile Variables (TSMP)

| Variable | Description | Domain |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| $v_{i,k}$ | Speed of train $i$ at time step $k$ | $\mathbb{R}^+$, $[v^{\min}, v^{\max}]$ |
| $a_{i,k}$ | Acceleration of train $i$ at time step $k$ | $\mathbb{R}$, $[a^{\min}, a^{\max}]$ |
| $x_{i,k}$ | Position of train $i$ at time step $k$ | $\mathbb{R}^+$ |
| $e_{i,k}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ at time step $k$ | $\mathbb{R}^+$ |
| $e^{\text{reg}}_{i,k}$ | Regenerative energy of train $i$ at time step $k$ | $\mathbb{R}^+$ |
| $p^{\text{tract}}_{i,k}$ | Binary: 1 if train $i$ is in traction mode at $k$ | $\{0,1\}$ |
| $p^{\text{brake}}_{i,k}$ | Binary: 1 if train $i$ is in braking mode at $k$ | $\{0,1\}$ |
| $p^{\text{coast}}_{i,k}$ | Binary: 1 if train $i$ is in coasting mode at $k$ | $\{0,1\}$ |

### 3.2 Timetable and Rescheduling Variables (TRP)

| Variable | Description | Domain |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| $\text{arr}_{i,j}$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $j$ | $\mathbb{R}^+$ |
| $\text{dep}_{i,j}$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ at station $j$ | $\mathbb{R}^+$ |
| $\delta_{i,j}$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $j$ | $\mathbb{R}^+$ |
| $w_{i,r}$ | Binary: 1 if train $i$ uses route $r$ | $\{0,1\}$ |
| $c_i$ | Binary: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled | $\{0,1\}$ |
| $z_{i,b}$ | Binary: 1 if train $i$ traverses block $b$ | $\{0,1\}$ |
| $y_{i,i',b,k}$ | Binary: 1 if train $i$ occupies block $b$ before train $i'$ at time $k$ | $\{0,1\}$ |
| $o_{i,i',b}$ | Binary: 1 if train $i$ departs block $b$ before train $i'$ | $\{0,1\}$ |

### 3.3 Linking Variables

| Variable | Description | Domain |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| $\phi_{i,b,k}$ | Binary: 1 if train $i$ is in block $b$ at time $k$ | $\{0,1\}$ |
| $\theta_{i,b,k}$ | Continuous: time train $i$ enters block $b$ | $\mathbb{R}^+$ |
| $\psi_{i,b,k}$ | Continuous: time train $i$ exits block $b$ | $\mathbb{R}^+$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

The objective minimizes a weighted sum of (i) total delay, (ii) cancellation penalties, (iii) total energy consumption, and (iv) deviation from scheduled times:

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{c^{\text{delay}} \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{j \in J} \delta_{i,j}}_{\text{Total delay}} + \underbrace{c^{\text{cancel}} \sum_{i \in I} c_i}_{\text{Cancellations}} + \underbrace{c^{\text{energy}} \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{k \in K} e_{i,k}}_{\text{Energy consumption}} + \underbrace{c^{\text{dev}} \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{j \in J} \left| \text{arr}_{i,j} - T^{\text{sch}}_{i,j} \right|}_{\text{Schedule deviation}}
$$

**Assumption (A2):** Cancellation is allowed only for non-essential trains; we assume at most a fraction $\rho$ of trains can be cancelled: $\sum_i c_i \leq \rho |I|$.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Dynamics (TSMP)

**(C1) Position update (kinematic equation):**
$$
x_{i,k+1} = x_{i,k} + v_{i,k} \Delta t + \tfrac{1}{2} a_{i,k} \Delta t^2 \quad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K
$$

**(C2) Speed update:**
$$
v_{i,k+1} = v_{i,k} + a_{i,k} \Delta t \quad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K
$$

**(C3) Speed bounds:**
$$
v^{\min} \leq v_{i,k} \leq v^{\max} \quad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K
$$

**(C4) Acceleration bounds:**
$$
a^{\min} \leq a_{i,k} \leq a^{\max} \quad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K
$$

**(C5) Operating mode selection (one mode at a time):**
$$
p^{\text{tract}}_{i,k} + p^{\text{brake}}_{i,k} + p^{\text{coast}}_{i,k} = 1 \quad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K
$$

**(C6) Acceleration sign linked to operating mode:**
$$
a_{i,k} \leq a^{\max} \cdot p^{\text{tract}}_{i,k} \quad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K
$$
$$
a_{i,k} \geq a^{\min} \cdot p^{\text{brake}}_{i,k} \quad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K
$$
$$
-M \cdot p^{\text{coast}}_{i,k} \leq a_{i,k} \leq M \cdot p^{\text{coast}}_{i,k} \quad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K
$$

### 5.2 Energy Consumption (TSMP)

**(C7) Instantaneous power (piecewise-linearized traction force):**
$$
e_{i,k} = \alpha \cdot M_i \cdot v_{i,k} + \beta \cdot M_i \cdot a_{i,k}^{+} \cdot v_{i,k} + \gamma \quad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K
$$
where $a_{i,k}^{+} = \max(a_{i,k}, 0)$ is linearized via SOS-2 or additional variables.

**(C8) Regenerative braking energy:**
$$
e^{\text{reg}}_{i,k} = \eta \cdot M_i \cdot |a_{i,k}| \cdot v_{i,k} \cdot p^{\text{brake}}_{i,k} \quad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K
$$

**(C9) Net energy consumption:**
$$
e^{\text{net}}_{i,k} = e_{i,k} - e^{\text{reg}}_{i,k} \quad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K
$$

### 5.3 Block Occupancy and Routing (TRP–TSMP Linking)

**(C10) Block selection via route choice:**
$$
\sum_{r \in R_i} w_{i,r} = 1 - c_i \quad \forall i \in I
$$

**(C11) Block traversal indicator:**
$$
z_{i,b} = \sum_{r \in R_i} w_{i,r} \cdot \mathbb{1}_{(b \in r)} \quad \forall i \in I,\; b \in B
$$

**(C12) Position within block:**
$$
\sum_{b \in B} L_b \cdot z_{i,b} \geq x_{i,k} \quad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K
$$

**(C13) Block occupancy indicator (linking position to binary):**
$$
L_b \cdot \phi_{i,b,k} \leq x_{i,k} - \sum_{b' < b} L_{b'} \cdot z_{i,b'} + M(1 - \phi_{i,b,k}) \quad \forall i,\; b,\; k
$$
$$
x_{i,k} - \sum_{b' < b} L_{b'} \cdot z_{i,b'} \leq L_b \cdot \phi_{i,b,k} + M(1 - \phi_{i,b,k}) \quad \forall i,\; b,\; k
$$

**(C14) Block entry/exit times:**
$$
\theta_{i,b,k} \leq k \cdot \Delta t + M(1 - \phi_{i,b,k}) \quad \forall i,\; b,\; k
$$
$$
\theta_{i,b,k} \geq k \cdot \Delta t - M(1 - \phi_{i,b,k}) \quad \forall i,\; b,\; k
$$

### 5.4 Disruption Constraints

**(C15) No entry into disrupted block during disruption window:**
$$
\phi_{i,b^*,k} = 0 \quad \forall i \in I,\; k \in [k^{\text{dis}}_s, k^{\text{dis}}_e]
$$

**(C16) Rerouting to opposite track (alternative route activation):**
$$
w_{i,r^{\text{alt}}} = 1 \quad \text{if } \sum_{k=k^{\text{dis}}_s}^{k^{\text{dis}}_e} \phi_{i,b^*,k} > 0 \text{ and rerouting is feasible}
$$

**Assumption (A3):** Rerouting uses the opposite-direction track in the same block $b^*$, which is feasible only if no opposing train occupies it.

### 5.5 Conflict Resolution (Bidirectional Trains)

**(C17) Same-block mutual exclusion:**
$$
\phi_{i,b,k} + \phi_{i',b,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall i \neq i' \in I,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

**(C18) Headway constraint (same direction):**
$$
\psi_{i,b,k} + H^{\min} \leq \theta_{i',b,k} + M(1 - y_{i,i',b,k}) \quad \forall i \neq i',\; b,\; k
$$

**(C19) Ordering consistency:**
$$
y_{i,i',b,k} + y_{i',i,b,k} = 1 \quad \forall i \neq i',\; b,\; k
$$

**(C20) Bidirectional conflict on shared rerouting track:**
$$
\phi_{i,b^*,k} + \phi_{i',b^*,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall i \in I^{+},\; i' \in I^{-},\; k \in [k^{\text{dis}}_s, k^{\text{dis}}_e]
$$
where $I^{+}$ and $I^{-}$ are trains in opposite directions.

### 5.6 Timetable Constraints

**(C21) Arrival/departure time definitions:**
$$
\text{arr}_{i,j} = \min\{k : x_{i,k} \geq X_j\} \quad \forall i \in I,\; j \in J
$$
linearized as:
$$
\text{arr}_{i,j} \geq k \cdot \Delta t - M(1 - \lambda_{i,j,k}) \quad \forall i,\; j,\; k
$$
$$
\text{arr}_{i,j} \leq k \cdot \Delta t + M(1 - \lambda_{i,j,k}) \quad \forall i,\; j,\; k
$$
$$
\sum_{k \in K} \lambda_{i,j,k} = 1 \quad \forall i,\; j
$$

**(C22) Dwell time bounds:**
$$
\tau^{\min}_j \leq \text{dep}_{i,j} - \text{arr}_{i,j} \leq \tau^{\max}_j \quad \forall i \in I,\; j \in J
$$

**(C23) Delay definition:**
$$
\delta_{i,j} = \text{arr}_{i,j} - T^{\text{sch}}_{i,j} \quad \forall i \in I,\; j \in J
$$

**(C24) Cancellation handling:**
$$
\text{arr}_{i,j} = 0,\; \text{dep}_{i,j} = 0 \quad \text{if } c_i = 1 \quad \forall i \in I,\; j \in J
$$
linearized:
$$
\text{arr}_{i,j} \leq M(1 - c_i) \quad \forall i,\; j
$$

### 5.7 Coupling Constraints (TRP ↔ TSMP)

**(C25) Speed at arrival must allow stopping:**
$$
v_{i,k} \cdot \mathbb{1}_{x_{i,k} = X_j} = 0 \quad \forall i \in I,\; j \in J
$$

**(C26) Departure speed:**
$$
v_{i,k} \cdot \mathbb{1}_{x_{i,k} = X_j,\; k = \text{dep}_{i,j}} \geq v^{\min} \quad \forall i \in I,\; j \in J
$$

**(C27) Running time consistency:**
$$
\sum_{k \in K} \Delta t \cdot \mathbb{1}_{x_{i,k} \in [X_j, X_{j+1}]} = \text{dep}_{i,j+1} - \text{dep}_{i,j} \quad \forall i \in I,\; j \in J
$$

**(C28) Speed profile feasibility under retiming:**
$$
v_{i,k} \geq \frac{X_{j+1} - X_j}{\text{dep}_{i,j+1} - \text{dep}_{i,j}} \cdot \mathbb{1}_{\text{interval } k \in [\text{dep}_{i,j}, \text{dep}_{i,j+1}]} \quad \forall i,\; j
$$

### 5.8 Initial and Boundary Conditions

**(C29) Initial conditions:**
$$
x_{i,1} = X^{\text{start}}_i,\quad v_{i,1} = v^{\text{start}}_i,\quad a_{i,1} = 0 \quad \forall i \in I
$$

**(C30) Terminal conditions:**
$$
x_{i,|K|} = X^{\text{end}}_i,\quad v_{i,|K|} = 0 \quad \forall i \in I
$$

**(C31) Terminal time alignment:**
$$
\text{arr}_{i,J^{\text{end}}} = |K| \cdot \Delta t \quad \forall i \in I
$$

---

Several nonlinear terms in the above formulation are linearized as follows:

| Nonlinear Term | Linearization |
|----------------|---------------|
| $a_{i,k} \cdot v_{i,k}$ (in C7) | SOS-2 piecewise-linear approximation over discretized speed range |
| $\max(a_{i,k}, 0)$ | Introduce $a^+_{i,k} \geq a_{i,k}$, $a^+_{i,k} \geq 0$, $a^+_{i,k} \leq a_{i,k} + M(1 - p^{\text{tract}}_{i,k})$ |
| $|a_{i,k}| \cdot v_{i,k}$ | Auxiliary variables with McCormick envelopes |
| $\mathbb{1}$ (indicator) functions | Replaced by binary variables with Big-M constraints |

---

## 7. Model Summary

The complete MILP is:

$$
\min \; Z = c^{\text{delay}} \sum_{i,j} \delta_{i,j} + c^{\text{cancel}} \sum_i c_i + c^{\text{energy}} \sum_{i,k} e^{\text{net}}_{i,k} + c^{\text{dev}} \sum_{i,j} |\text{arr}_{i,j} - T^{\text{sch}}_{i,j}|
$$

subject to constraints **(C1)–(C31)**.

**Key Modeling Features:**
- **Bidirectional conflict resolution** is enforced via (C17) and (C20), ensuring that trains in opposite directions cannot simultaneously occupy the rerouting track.
- **Disruption handling** is captured by (C15)–(C16), which forces trains to either reroute or wait outside the affected block.
- **TRP–TSMP coupling** is realized through (C25)–(C28), which guarantee that any retimed arrival/departure is achievable by a feasible speed profile.
- **Energy awareness** is embedded via (C7)–(C9), linking traction effort to instantaneous power and regenerative braking recovery.

**Assumption (A4):** The disruption time window and affected block are known deterministically (stochastic extensions would require scenario-based reformulation).

**Assumption (A5):** All trains share the same kinematic parameters (mass, max acceleration/deceleration); heterogeneous parameters can be introduced by indexing these constants by $i$.

This MILP provides a unified framework that simultaneously yields (i) a conflict-free rescheduled timetable (with retiming, reordering, rerouting, and cancellation decisions) and (ii) executable energy-efficient speed profiles, ensuring feasibility at both the operational and control levels under partial segment blockage disruptions.

Text:
# MILP Model: Passenger‑Oriented Real‑Time Train Rescheduling with Flexible Train Composition and Rolling‑Stock Circulation

This model extends the passenger‑oriented rescheduling model of Liu et al. (2023a) with flexible train composition and a (simplified) rolling‑stock circulation constraint, suitable for use inside an MPC loop over a prediction horizon.

---

## 1. Assumptions (explicitly marked)

- **(A1)** A single urban rail line with one service direction and stations s = 1,…,S is considered; the extension to both directions is obtained by index duplication.
- **(A2)** Running times between consecutive stations are fixed (no speed-level optimization); dwell times are decision variables bounded between a minimum and maximum.
- **(A3)** Time‑varying passenger demand is approximated as piecewise constant: the prediction horizon is divided into K intervals of equal length Δt, with demand D_{s,k} (passengers arriving at station s during interval k).
- **(A4)** Stop‑skipping is allowed; a binary variable indicates whether train j stops at station s.
- **(A5)** Rolling‑stock circulation is simplified to a fleet‑size constraint: the total number of coupled carriages in simultaneous service must not exceed the available fleet (carriage units are assumed freely reusable between services, i.e., no maintenance/turnaround coupling is modeled).
- **(A6)** Passengers are fully rational (board the first train with sufficient residual capacity) and no alighting is modeled within the horizon (alighting fractions can be added linearly if desired).
- **(A7)** All times are continuous variables (minutes); the model is a genuine MILP (no nonlinear terms appear).

---

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| J = {1,…,N} | trains operated within the prediction horizon |
| S = {1,…,S} | stations |
| K = {1,…,K} | demand time intervals, length Δt |
| U = {1,…,U_max} | admissible train compositions (number of carriages) |
| t^run_{s} | running time from station s to s+1 |
| τ^dw_min, τ^dw_max | minimum/maximum dwell time |
| h_min | minimum headway between successive train departures |
| C | passenger capacity per carriage |
| F | total number of available carriages (fleet) |
| D_{s,k} | passengers arriving at station s in interval k |
| d̄_{j,s}, ā_{j,s} | nominal departure/arrival times (from the nominal timetable) |
| M | sufficiently large constant |
| α, β, γ | weights: waiting time, operation cost, timetable deviation |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous:**
- a_{j,s} ∈ ℝ₊ : arrival time of train j at station s
- d_{j,s} ∈ ℝ₊ : departure time of train j from station s
- b_{j,s} ∈ ℝ₊ : number of passengers boarding train j at station s
- w_{s,k} ∈ ℝ₊ : passengers waiting at station s at the end of interval k

**Binary / Integer:**
- x_{j,s} ∈ {0,1} : 1 if train j stops at station s
- z_{j,u} ∈ {0,1} : 1 if train j is operated with u carriages (flexible composition)
- g_{j,s,k} ∈ {0,1} : 1 if train j departs from station s during interval k

Composition: u_j = Σ_{u∈U} u · z_{j,u} (defined by equality; substituted where needed).

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize total waiting time, operational cost, and deviation from the nominal timetable:

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{s}\sum_{k} \Delta t \, w_{s,k}}_{\text{passenger waiting time}}
+ \underbrace{\beta \sum_{j}\sum_{s} x_{j,s}\, u_j}_{\text{carriage–stop operating cost}}
+ \underbrace{\gamma \sum_{j}\sum_{s}\left[(d_{j,s}-\bar d_{j,s}) + (a_{j,s}-\bar a_{j,s})\right]}_{\text{timetable deviation}}
$$

*Note:* u_j = Σ_u u z_{j,u} keeps the cost term linear.

---

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Timetable structure — running times:**
$$
a_{j,s+1} - d_{j,s} \;=\; t^{\text{run}}_{s}, \qquad \forall j,\; s=1,\dots,S-1
$$

**(C2) Dwell times with stop skipping:**
$$
d_{j,s} - a_{j,s} \;\ge\; \tau^{\text{dw}}_{\min}\, x_{j,s}, \qquad \forall j,s
$$
$$
d_{j,s} - a_{j,s} \;\le\; \tau^{\text{dw}}_{\max}\, x_{j,s}, \qquad \forall j,s
$$
(if x_{j,s}=0, then d_{j,s}=a_{j,s}: no stop).

**(C3) Minimum headway:**
$$
d_{j+1,s} - d_{j,s} \;\ge\; h_{\min}, \qquad \forall j=1,\dots,N-1,\; \forall s
$$

**(C4) Departure–interval assignment (big‑M):**
$$
\sum_{k} g_{j,s,k} = 1, \qquad \forall j,s
$$
$$
d_{j,s} \ge \sum_{k} (k-1)\,\Delta t\, g_{j,s,k} - M(1-g_{j,s,k}), \qquad \forall j,s,k
$$
$$
d_{j,s} \le \sum_{k} k\,\Delta t\, g_{j,s,k} + M(1-g_{j,s,k}), \qquad \forall j,s,k
$$

**(C5) Passenger load dynamics (waiting‑time recursion):**
$$
w_{s,1} = D_{s,1} - \sum_{j} b_{j,s} \cdot \mathbb{1}[d_{j,s}\in \{1\}] \;\Longrightarrow\;
w_{s,k} = w_{s,k-1} + D_{s,k} - \sum_{j} b_{j,s}\, g_{j,s,k}, \quad \forall s, k=2,\dots,K
$$
with w_{s,0}=0 and w_{s,k} ≥ 0.

**(C6) Boarding limited by train capacity and stop decision:**
$$
b_{j,s} \;\le\; C \sum_{u} u\, z_{j,u}, \qquad \forall j,s
$$
$$
b_{j,s} \;\le\; M\, x_{j,s}, \qquad \forall j,s
$$

**(C7) Boarding limited by available waiting passengers (linearized):**
$$
b_{j,s} \;\le\; w_{s,k-1} + D_{s,k} + M(1-g_{j,s,k}), \qquad \forall j,s,k
$$

**(C8) Flexible train composition (exactly one composition per train):**
$$
\sum_{u\in U} z_{j,u} = 1, \qquad \forall j
$$

**(C9) Rolling‑stock circulation (fleet constraint, assumption A5):**
$$
\sum_{j:\, t \in [\,a_{j,1},\, d_{j,S}\,]} \sum_{u} u\, z_{j,u} \;\le\; F \quad \forall t
$$
In linear form, using interval indicators: for each demand interval k,
$$
\sum_{j}\sum_{u} u\, z_{j,u}\, \theta_{j,k} \le F,\qquad
\theta_{j,k}\ge g_{j,1,k},\quad \theta_{j,k}\ge 1-g_{j,S,k},\quad \theta_{j,k}\le g_{j,1,k}+1-g_{j,S,k},\quad \theta_{j,k}\in\{0,1\}
$$
i.e., train j occupies the fleet in interval k if it has departed from station 1 but not yet departed from station S.

**(C10) Horizon boundary conditions:** first train arrival fixed to the current MPC state:
$$
a_{j,1} = a^{\text{meas}}_{j}, \qquad \forall j \text{ already en route}
$$

**(C11) Variable domains:**
$$
a_{j,s}, d_{j,s}, b_{j,s}, w_{s,k} \ge 0; \quad x_{j,s}, z_{j,u}, g_{j,s,k}, \theta_{j,k} \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Use within MPC

At each MPC step, measured train positions and current passenger loads initialize the state (C10, w_{s,0}); the MILP above is solved over the prediction horizon; only the first‑step decisions are applied, and the procedure repeats with updated demand forecasts. In the learning‑based variant, the binaries {x_{j,s}, z_{j,u}} (after presolve pruning) are predicted by an LSTM network, and the remaining continuous variables are obtained by solving the resulting linear program with the binaries fixed — guaranteeing constraint satisfaction while reducing online computation.

Read the text below and fill in the predefined form.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

After evaluating the five generated models, **Model 4** is selected as the best. It is the most complete, mathematically rigorous, and properly linearized formulation. It uses SOS2 piecewise-linear approximation correctly, handles all four rescheduling actions (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation), properly enforces bidirectional conflict on shared tracks, and includes acceleration/braking coupling between consecutive segments.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $I$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i \in I$ |
| $J$ | Set of track segments, indexed by $j \in J$ |
| $K$ | Set of stations, indexed by $k \in K$ |
| $D = \{\text{up}, \text{down}\}$ | Set of travel directions, indexed by $d \in D$ |
| $P$ | Set of piecewise-linear breakpoints for speed, indexed by $p \in P$ |

For each segment $j$, let $k_j^s \in K$ and $k_j^e \in K$ denote its start and end stations.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_j$ | Length of segment $j$ (km) |
| $V_{\min}, V_{\max}$ | Minimum and maximum operating speeds (km/h) |
| $A_{\max}, B_{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration and deceleration rates (km/h²) |
| $t_s, t_e$ | Disruption start and end times (h) |
| $j_b \in J$ | Index of the blocked segment |
| $\tau_{\min}, \tau_{\max}$ | Minimum and maximum dwell times at stations (h) |
| $h$ | Minimum headway time between trains (h) |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Energy consumption coefficients (power $\approx \alpha v^2 + \beta v + \gamma$) |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (big-$M$) |
| $\text{sched}_{i,k}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $k$ (h) |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3$ | Non-negative weights for delay, energy, and cancellation |
| $d_i^{\text{orig}} \in D$ | Original (planned) direction of train $i$ |
| $v_p$ | Speed at breakpoint $p$, with $V_{\min} = v_1 < v_2 < \dots < v_{|P|} = V_{\max}$ |
| $T_{j,p} = L_j / v_p$ | Running time on segment $j$ at speed $v_p$ |
| $E_{j,p} = (\alpha v_p^2 + \beta v_p + \gamma) \cdot T_{j,p}$ | Energy consumption on segment $j$ at speed $v_p$ |
| $\Delta_{\max}$ | Upper bound on acceptable terminal delay |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $x_{i,j,d}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $j$ in direction $d$ |
| $y_i$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $a_{i,k}$ | continuous $\geq 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $k$ |
| $d_{i,k}$ | continuous $\geq 0$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ at station $k$ |
| $v_{i,j}$ | continuous $\geq 0$ | Average speed of train $i$ on segment $j$ |
| $t_{i,j}$ | continuous $\geq 0$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $j$ |
| $e_i$ | continuous $\geq 0$ | Total energy consumption of train $i$ |
| $\delta_{i,k}$ | continuous $\geq 0$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $k$ |
| $z_{i,i',j}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ completes segment $j$ before train $i'$ enters it |
| $z_{i,i',k}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ arrives at station $k$ before train $i'$ |
| $c_{i,i'}$ | binary | 1 if trains $i$ and $i'$ have a scheduling conflict |
| $\lambda_{i,j,p}$ | continuous $\geq 0$ | Convex-combination weight of breakpoint $p$ |
| $\sigma_{i,j,p}$ | binary | 1 if breakpoint $p$ is the upper active breakpoint for SOS2 |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; w_1 \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{k \in K} \delta_{i,k} \;+\; w_2 \sum_{i \in I} e_i \;+\; w_3 \sum_{i \in I} y_i
$$

This is a weighted sum of (i) total passenger/operational delay, (ii) total energy consumption, and (iii) number of cancelled trains.

---

## 5. Constraints

### (1) Segment Coverage — each non-cancelled train must traverse every segment

$$
\sum_{d \in D} x_{i,j,d} \;=\; 1 - y_i, \quad \forall i \in I,\; \forall j \in J
$$

If train $i$ is not cancelled ($y_i = 0$), it must use exactly one direction on every segment; if cancelled, all $x_{i,j,d} = 0$.

### (2) Blocked-Segment Timing — the blocked segment cannot be traversed during $[t_s, t_e]$

For each $i \in I$ and $d \in D$:

$$
a_{i,k_{j_b}^s} + t_{i,j_b} \;\leq\; t_s + M(1 - x_{i,j_b,d})
$$

$$
a_{i,k_{j_b}^s} \;\geq\; t_e - M(1 - x_{i,j_b,d})
$$

If the train uses the blocked segment, its traversal must finish before $t_s$ or start after $t_e$.

### (3) Rerouting Flexibility — trains may use the opposite track

No additional hard constraint is required: the binary $x_{i,j,d}$ is allowed to take either value, so trains can be rerouted onto the opposite (unblocked) track during the disruption. An optional rerouting penalty can be added:

$$
\sum_{i,j} \mathbb{1}[x_{i,j,d} = 1,\; d \neq d_i^{\text{orig}}] \quad \text{(optional rerouting penalty)}
$$

### (4) Bidirectional Conflict on the Shared (Unblocked) Track

For each pair $(i,i')$ with $d_i^{\text{orig}} \neq d_{i'}^{\text{orig}}$, each $j \in J$, and each pair $(d,d')$ with $d \neq d'$:

$$
a_{i,k_j^s} + t_{i,j} \;\leq\; a_{i',k_j^s} + M(1 - z_{i,i',j}) + M(1 - x_{i,j,d}) + M(1 - x_{i',j,d'})
$$

$$
a_{i',k_j^s} + t_{i',j} \;\leq\; a_{i,k_j^s} + M z_{i,i',j} + M(1 - x_{i,j,d}) + M(1 - x_{i',j,d'})
$$

This ensures that if two trains in opposite directions share a segment, one must fully clear it before the other enters.

### (5) Speed Dynamics (Piecewise-Linear Approximation)

The nonlinear relations $t_{i,j} = L_j / v_{i,j}$ are linearized via breakpoints $v_p$:

$$
v_{i,j} = \sum_{p \in P} \lambda_{i,j,p}\, v_p, \quad \forall i \in I,\; j \in J
$$

$$
t_{i,j} = \sum_{p \in P} \lambda_{i,j,p}\, T_{j,p}, \quad \forall i \in I,\; j \in J
$$

$$
\sum_{p \in P} \lambda_{i,j,p} = \sum_{d \in D} x_{i,j,d}, \quad \forall i \in I,\; j \in J
$$

$$
V_{\min} \sum_{d} x_{i,j,d} \;\leq\; v_{i,j} \;\leq\; V_{\max} \sum_{d} x_{i,j,d}, \quad \forall i \in I,\; j \in J
$$

**SOS2 constraint** on $\{\lambda_{i,j,p}\}_{p \in P}$: at most two consecutive $\lambda_{i,j,p}$ may be strictly positive. Enforced via auxiliary binaries $\sigma_{i,j,p}$:

$$
\sum_{p \in P} \sigma_{i,j,p} = \sum_{d \in D} x_{i,j,d}, \quad
\lambda_{i,j,p} \leq \sigma_{i,j,p} + \sigma_{i,j,p-1} \;\; (p \geq 2), \quad
\lambda_{i,j,1} \leq \sigma_{i,j,1}
$$

### (6) Dwell Time Bounds

For each $i \in I$ and each intermediate station $k$:

$$
\tau_{\min} \;\leq\; a_{i,k+1} - d_{i,k} \;\leq\; \tau_{\max}
$$

### (7) Headway at Stations

For each pair $(i,i')$ and each station $k$:

$$
a_{i,k} - a_{i',k} \;\geq\; h - M(1 - z_{i,i',k})
$$

$$
a_{i',k} - a_{i,k} \;\geq\; h - M z_{i,i',k}
$$

$$
z_{i,i',k} + z_{i',i,k} = 1
$$

This guarantees a minimum separation $h$ between any two trains at the same station.

### (8) Running-Time Consistency

For each $i \in I$ and each segment $j$ connecting station $k$ to $k+1$:

$$
d_{i,k} + t_{i,j} \;=\; a_{i,k+1}
$$

### (9) Energy Consumption (Linearized)

$$
e_i \;=\; \sum_{j \in J} \sum_{p \in P} \lambda_{i,j,p}\, E_{j,p}, \quad \forall i \in I
$$

Because $\lambda_{i,j,p}$ and $E_{j,p}$ are both linear, this is a linear expression.

### (10) Delay Calculation (Linearized max)

$$
\delta_{i,k} \;\geq\; a_{i,k} - \text{sched}_{i,k}, \quad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K
$$

$$
\delta_{i,k} \;\geq\; 0, \quad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K
$$

Since the objective minimizes $\sum \delta_{i,k}$, the optimizer will set $\delta_{i,k} = \max(0, a_{i,k} - \text{sched}_{i,k})$ at optimality.

### (11) Conflict Indicator (Auxiliary)

$$
c_{i,i'} \;\geq\; z_{i,i',j} + z_{i',i,j} - 1, \quad \forall i,i' \in I,\; j \in J
$$

Used for post-processing or for adding a conflict penalty to the objective if desired.

### (12) Boundary Conditions

$$
d_{i,k_0} \;=\; \text{sched}_{i,k_0}^{\text{dep}}, \quad \forall i \in I
$$

$$
a_{i,k_{|K|}} \;\leq\; \text{sched}_{i,k_{|K|}} + \Delta_{\max}, \quad \forall i \in I
$$

### (13) Acceleration / Braking Coupling Between Segments

$$
v_{i,j+1} - v_{i,j} \;\leq\; A_{\max} \cdot t_{i,j}, \quad \forall i \in I
$$

$$
v_{i,j} - v_{i,j+1} \;\leq\; B_{\max} \cdot t_{i,j+1}, \quad \forall i \in I
$$

These couple consecutive segments and ensure that speed transitions are physically feasible.

---

## 6. Assumptions

1. **Track topology**: The railway is a double-track line with one track per direction. Segments are defined between consecutive stations.
2. **Disruption scope**: A single segment $j_b$ is blocked during $[t_s, t_e]$. Trains cannot traverse this segment during the window but may reroute via the opposite track.
3. **Train homogeneity**: All trains share the same performance parameters ($V_{\min}, V_{\max}, A_{\max}, B_{\max}$).
4. **Average-speed approximation**: Each segment uses a single average speed $v_{i,j}$ rather than a continuous speed profile; this is a standard simplification for tractability.
5. **Energy model**: Mechanical power is approximated by the convex quadratic $f(v) = \alpha v^2 + \beta v + \gamma$, integrated over running time.
6. **Deterministic disruption**: The disruption time window is known and fixed.
7. **No train overtaking on the same track**: Reordering is allowed at stations and via rerouting, but not within a single segment in the same direction.
8. **Headway is uniform**: The minimum headway $h$ is the same for all pairs of trains and stations.
9. **Cancellation is all-or-nothing**: A cancelled train is fully removed from the schedule.
10. **Boundary conditions**: Trains depart at their originally scheduled departure times from the origin station, and terminal delay is bounded by $\Delta_{\max}$.

---

## 7. Summary of Linearization Techniques

| Element | Linearization Technique |
|---------|-------------------------|
| $t_{i,j} = L_j / v_{i,j}$ (hyperbolic) | Piecewise-linear approximation via breakpoints $v_p$ and SOS2 weights $\lambda_{i,j,p}$ |
| $e_i = \sum (\alpha v^2 + \beta v + \gamma) t$ (bilinear) | Same SOS2 weights $\lambda_{i,j,p}$ — energy becomes linear in $\lambda$ |
| $\delta_{i,k} = \max(0, a_{i,k} - \text{sched}_{i,k})$ | Auxiliary variable with one-sided inequality and non-negativity |
| $\|a_{i,k} - a_{i',k}\| \geq h$ | Disjunctive big-$M$ with binary $z_{i,i',k}$ |
| Opposite-direction track sharing | Big-$M$ with binary $z_{i,i',j}$ enforcing temporal separation |
| Blocked-segment timing | Big-$M$ disjunction (before $t_s$ OR after $t_e$) |

The resulting model is a **mixed-integer linear program** that can be solved by standard solvers (CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, HiGHS). The piecewise-linear approximation accuracy is controlled by the number of breakpoints $|P|$. For large-scale instances, the decomposition framework described in the introduction (IP model + train plans + adaptive iterative algorithm) can be applied to accelerate the solution process.

Text:
# Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $B$ | Set of track blocks, indexed by $b$ |
| $K$ | Set of discretized time intervals, indexed by $k$ |
| $D$ | Set of directions $\{up, down\}$ |
| $V$ | Set of discretized speed levels for piecewise-linear energy, indexed by $v$ |
| $B^{\text{dis}}$ | Subset of disrupted blocks |
| $K^{\text{dis}}$ | Subset of time intervals within the disruption window |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ (km) |
| $V^{\max}, V^{\min}$ | Maximum / minimum allowed speed (km/h) |
| $a^{\max}, d^{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration (km/h²) |
| $\Delta t$ | Duration of each time interval (s) |
| $t^{\text{dis}}_s, t^{\text{dis}}_e$ | Disruption start / end time |
| $\bar{t}^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}, \bar{t}^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure times |
| $\tau^{\min}_s, \tau^{\max}_s$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time at station $s$ |
| $h$ | Minimum headway time between trains |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) |
| $w_d, w_e$ | Weights for delay and energy in objective |
| $E_v$ | Energy consumption coefficient at speed level $v$ (kWh/km) |
| $o_t, d_t$ | Origin / destination station of train $t$ |
| $\text{dir}(t)$ | Direction of train $t$ |
| $b^{\text{opp}}(b)$ | Opposite-direction block paired with $b$ |
| $C^{\text{opp}}$ | Capacity of opposite track during disruption |

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $t^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $t^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Actual departure time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $x_{t,b,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ occupies block $b$ during interval $k$ |
| $v_{t,b,k}$ | $[V^{\min}, V^{\max}]$ | Speed of train $t$ in block $b$ during interval $k$ (km/h) |
| $y_{t,b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ traverses block $b$ |
| $r_{t,b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is rerouted onto opposite track on block $b$ |
| $z_{t,t',b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ enters block $b$ before train $t'$ |
| $\delta_{t,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Delay of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $E^{\text{tot}}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Total energy consumption |
| $\lambda_{t,b,k,v}$ | $[0,1]$ | Convex-combination weight for speed level $v$ (SOS2) |

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; w_d \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \delta_{t,s} \; + \; w_e \cdot E^{\text{tot}}
$$

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Dynamics (Acceleration / Deceleration Limits)

For all $t \in T$, $b \in B$, $k \in K \setminus \{k_1\}$:

$$
v_{t,b,k} - v_{t,b,k-1} \;\leq\; a^{\max} \cdot \Delta t / 3600
$$

$$
v_{t,b,k} - v_{t,b,k-1} \;\geq\; -d^{\max} \cdot \Delta t / 3600
$$

### 5.2 Block Traversal Time (Entry Consistency)

For all $t \in T$, $b \in B$, $k \in K \setminus \{k_1\}$, with $s_2$ the downstream station of block $b$:

$$
t^{\text{arr}}_{t,s_2} \;\geq\; (k+1)\Delta t / 60 \;+\; \frac{L_b}{v_{t,b,k}} \;-\; M\bigl(3 - x_{t,b,k} + x_{t,b,k-1} - y_{t,b}\bigr)
$$

### 5.3 Link Between Occupation and Traversal

For all $t \in T$, $b \in B$:

$$
y_{t,b} \;=\; \sum_{k \in K} x_{t,b,k}
$$

### 5.4 Block Occupation (Same Direction)

For all $b \in B$, $k \in K$:

$$
\sum_{t \in T} x_{t,b,k} \;\leq\; 1
$$

### 5.5 Bidirectional Conflict

For all $t, t' \in T$ with $t < t'$, $b \in B^{\text{dis}}$, $k \in K$:

$$
x_{t,\,b^{\text{opp}}(b),\,k} \;+\; x_{t',\,b,\,k} \;\leq\; 1
$$

### 5.6 Disruption Window Restriction

For all $t \in T$, $b \in B^{\text{dis}}$, $k \in K^{\text{dis}}$:

$$
x_{t,b,k} \;\leq\; r_{t,b}
$$

### 5.7 Rerouting — Mutual Exclusivity

For all $t \in T$, $b \in B^{\text{dis}}$, $k \in K$:

$$
x_{t,b,k} \;+\; x_{t,\,b^{\text{opp}}(b),\,k} \;\leq\; 1
$$

### 5.8 Rerouting — Use of Opposite Track

For all $t \in T$, $b \in B^{\text{dis}}$:

$$
r_{t,b} \;\leq\; y_{t,\,b^{\text{opp}}(b)}
$$

### 5.9 Opposite-Track Capacity During Disruption

For all $k \in K^{\text{dis}}$:

$$
\sum_{t \in T} \sum_{b \in B^{\text{dis}}} r_{t,b} \;\leq\; C^{\text{opp}}
$$

### 5.10 Dwell Time Bounds

For all $t \in T$, $s \in S$:

$$
\tau^{\min}_s \;\leq\; t^{\text{dep}}_{t,s} - t^{\text{arr}}_{t,s} \;\leq\; \tau^{\max}_s
$$

### 5.11 Minimum Running Time Between Stations

For all $t \in T$, $s \in S$ with successor $s'$:

$$
t^{\text{arr}}_{t,s'} - t^{\text{dep}}_{t,s} \;\geq\; \sum_{b \in B(s,s')} \frac{L_b}{V^{\max}}
$$

### 5.12 Headway Between Consecutive Trains

For all $t, t' \in T$ with $t < t'$, $b \in B$:

$$
t^{\text{dep}}_{t',\,s_1(b)} - t^{\text{dep}}_{t,\,s_1(b)} \;\geq\; h \;-\; M\bigl(2 - z_{t,t',b} - y_{t,b}\bigr)
$$

### 5.13 Order Preservation on Blocks

For all $t, t' \in T$ with $t < t'$, $b \in B$:

$$
z_{t,t',b} \;+\; z_{t',t,b} \;=\; 1
$$

### 5.14 No Overtaking Within a Block

For all $t, t' \in T$ with $t < t'$, $b \in B$, $k \in K$:

$$
x_{t,b,k} \;+\; x_{t',b,k} \;\leq\; z_{t,t',b} \;+\; z_{t',t,b}
$$

### 5.15 Speed Limit Linkage

For all $t \in T$, $b \in B$, $k \in K$:

$$
v_{t,b,k} \;\leq\; V^{\max} \cdot x_{t,b,k} \;+\; V^{\min} \cdot (1 - x_{t,b,k})
$$

### 5.16 Piecewise-Linear Speed Representation

For all $t \in T$, $b \in B$, $k \in K$:

$$
v_{t,b,k} \;=\; \sum_{v \in V} v \cdot \lambda_{t,b,k,v}
$$

$$
\sum_{v \in V} \lambda_{t,b,k,v} \;=\; x_{t,b,k}
$$

(with $\lambda$ forming an SOS2 set to ensure convexity)

### 5.17 Energy Consumption

$$
E^{\text{tot}} \;=\; \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{b \in B} \sum_{k \in K} \sum_{v \in V} E_v \cdot L_b \cdot \lambda_{t,b,k,v}
$$

### 5.18 Boundary Conditions

For all $t \in T$:

$$
t^{\text{dep}}_{t,\,o_t} \;=\; \bar{t}^{\text{dep}}_{t,\,o_t}
$$

$$
t^{\text{arr}}_{t,\,d_t} \;=\; \bar{t}^{\text{arr}}_{t,\,d_t} \;+\; \delta_{t,\,d_t}
$$

### 5.19 Delay Definition

For all $t \in T$, $s \in S$:

$$
\delta_{t,s} \;\geq\; t^{\text{arr}}_{t,s} - \bar{t}^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}
$$

### 5.20 Block Sequence (Time Linkage)

For all $t \in T$, $b \in B$ with upstream station $s_1$ and downstream station $s_2$:

$$
t^{\text{arr}}_{t,s_2} \;\geq\; t^{\text{dep}}_{t,s_1} \;-\; M(1 - y_{t,b})
$$

### 5.21 Route Enforcement

For all $t \in T$, $b \in B$:

$$
y_{t,b} \;=\; \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if block } b \text{ lies on the route of train } t \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$

## 6. Assumptions

1. **Time–space discretization**: The planning horizon is discretized into intervals of length $\Delta t$; each block can be occupied by at most one train per interval.
2. **Bidirectional single-track segments**: Each physical block has a paired opposite-direction block $b^{\text{opp}}(b)$; rerouting uses this paired block.
3. **Disruption window**: A partial blockage affects a known set of blocks $B^{\text{dis}}$ during a known time window $[t^{\text{dis}}_s, t^{\text{dis}}_e]$.
4. **Rerouting capacity**: The opposite track has a finite capacity $C^{\text{opp}}$ during the disruption window, reflecting safety headways.
5. **Energy model**: Energy consumption per km is a piecewise-linear function of speed, approximated via SOS2 convex combinations over discretized speed levels $V$.
6. **No overtaking within a block**: Once a train enters a block, it must exit before another train enters (enforced by $z$ and $x$ variables).
7. **Fixed train routes (except rerouting)**: Each train's nominal route is fixed; rerouting only swaps a disrupted block for its opposite-direction counterpart.
8. **Dwell-time flexibility**: Dwell times at stations may vary within $[\tau^{\min}_s, \tau^{\max}_s]$ to absorb delays.
9. **Acceleration/deceleration limits**: Speed transitions between consecutive intervals respect $a^{\max}$ and $d^{\max}$.
10. **Delay accounting**: Delay is measured at each station as the deviation from the scheduled arrival time; total delay is summed across all stations and trains.

Text:
# TRSMP MILP Model Formulation

## Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $B$ | Set of block sections (segments), indexed by $b$ |
| $K$ | Set of discretized speed-profile intervals, indexed by $k$ |
| $D$ | Set of directions, $D = \{+1, -1\}$ |

**Auxiliary functions:**
- $s^{\text{dep}}(b)$: departure station of segment $b$
- $s^{\text{arr}}(b)$: arrival station of segment $b$ (i.e., $b+1$)

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $\bar{d}_i^s$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ | h |
| $\bar{d}_i^{s,\text{dep}}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ | h |
| $L_b$ | Length of block section $b$ | km |
| $v_{\max}, v_{\min}$ | Maximum / minimum allowed speed | km/h |
| $a_{\max}, a_{\text{brake}}$ | Maximum traction / braking acceleration | km/h² |
| $t^{\text{dis}}_s, t^{\text{dis}}_e$ | Disruption start / end time | h |
| $b^*$ | Blocked segment | – |
| $w_{\text{delay}}, w_{\text{energy}}, w_{\text{cancel}}$ | Objective weights | – |
| $\tau_{\min}, \tau_{\max}$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time | h |
| $\Delta t$ | Time discretization step | h |
| $M$ | Big-M constant | – |
| $\beta_1, \beta_2, \beta_3$ | Linearized energy coefficients | – |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum headway time | h |
| $T_{\text{hor}}$ | Planning horizon | h |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Rescheduling Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $x_i^s$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $y_i^s$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $z_{i,j}^s$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ departs station $s$ before train $j$ |
| $r_i^b$ | $\{0,1,2\}$ | Route choice of train $i$ on segment $b$ (0=not used, 1=normal, 2=rerouted) |
| $r^N_i^b$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses the normal track on segment $b$ |
| $r^R_i^b$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted (uses opposite track) on segment $b$ |
| $c_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $\delta_i^s$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |

### 3.2 Speed-Profile Variables (per train $i$, segment $b$, interval $k$)

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $v_i^b{}_k$ | $[v_{\min}, v_{\max}]$ | Speed of train $i$ in segment $b$ at interval $k$ |
| $a_i^b{}_k$ | $[a_{\text{brake}}, a_{\max}]$ | Acceleration of train $i$ in segment $b$ at interval $k$ |
| $p_i^b{}_k$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Traction power of train $i$ in segment $b$ at interval $k$ |
| $e_i^b{}_k$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ in segment $b$ at interval $k$ |
| $\xi_i^b{}_k$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Position of train $i$ in segment $b$ at interval $k$ |
| $\text{occ}_i^b{}_k$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ occupies segment $b$ at interval $k$ |
| $w_{i,k}^{v,a}$ | $\mathbb{R}$ | Auxiliary variable for bilinear term $v \cdot a$ (McCormick envelope) |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min Z \;=\; w_{\text{delay}} \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \delta_i^s \;+\; w_{\text{energy}} \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{b \in B} \sum_{k \in K} e_i^b{}_k \;+\; w_{\text{cancel}} \sum_{i \in T} c_i
$$

The objective is a weighted sum of (i) total passenger delay, (ii) total traction energy consumption, and (iii) cancellation penalties.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Delay Definition
$$
\delta_i^s \;\geq\; x_i^s - \bar{d}_i^s \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### 5.2 Dwell-Time Constraints
$$
x_i^s + \tau_{\min} \;\leq\; y_i^s \;\leq\; x_i^s + \tau_{\max} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### 5.3 Running Time – Speed-Profile Coupling
For each train $i$ and segment $b$, the total traversal time equals the number of intervals times $\Delta t$:
$$
y_i^{s^{\text{dep}}(b)} + |K| \Delta t - x_i^{s^{\text{arr}}(b)} \;\leq\; M \cdot c_i \qquad \forall i \in T,\; b \in B
$$
$$
y_i^{s^{\text{dep}}(b)} + |K| \Delta t - x_i^{s^{\text{arr}}(b)} \;\geq\; -M \cdot c_i \qquad \forall i \in T,\; b \in B
$$

### 5.4 Train Dynamics (Kinematic Equations)
**Speed update:**
$$
v_i^b{}_{k+1} \;=\; v_i^b{}_k + a_i^b{}_k \cdot \Delta t \qquad \forall i \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K \setminus \{|K|-1\}
$$

**Position update:**
$$
\xi_i^b{}_{k+1} \;=\; \xi_i^b{}_k + v_i^b{}_k \cdot \Delta t + \tfrac{1}{2} a_i^b{}_k \cdot (\Delta t)^2 \qquad \forall i \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K \setminus \{|K|-1\}
$$

### 5.5 Speed and Acceleration Limits
Enforced via variable bounds:
$$
v_{\min} \leq v_i^b{}_k \leq v_{\max}, \qquad a_{\text{brake}} \leq a_i^b{}_k \leq a_{\max} \qquad \forall i, b, k
$$

### 5.6 Segment Traversal (Boundary Conditions)
$$
\xi_i^b{}_0 \;=\; 0 \qquad \forall i \in T,\; b \in B
$$
$$
\xi_i^b{}_{|K|-1} \;=\; L_b \qquad \forall i \in T,\; b \in B
$$

### 5.7 Energy Consumption Model (Linearized Davis Equation)
The Davis equation $e = (A v^2 + B v + C + m a) v$ is linearized using McCormick envelopes for the bilinear term $v \cdot a$:

**McCormick envelope (four inequalities):**
$$
w_{i,k}^{v,a} \;\geq\; v_{\min} \cdot a_i^b{}_k + a_{\text{brake}} \cdot v_i^b{}_k - v_{\min} \cdot a_{\text{brake}}
$$
$$
w_{i,k}^{v,a} \;\geq\; v_{\max} \cdot a_i^b{}_k + a_{\max} \cdot v_i^b{}_k - v_{\max} \cdot a_{\max}
$$
$$
w_{i,k}^{v,a} \;\leq\; v_{\min} \cdot a_i^b{}_k + a_{\max} \cdot v_i^b{}_k - v_{\min} \cdot a_{\max}
$$
$$
w_{i,k}^{v,a} \;\leq\; v_{\max} \cdot a_i^b{}_k + a_{\text{brake}} \cdot v_i^b{}_k - v_{\max} \cdot a_{\text{brake}}
$$

**Energy definition:**
$$
e_i^b{}_k \;\geq\; \beta_1 \, v_i^b{}_k + \beta_2 \, a_i^b{}_k + \beta_3 \, w_{i,k}^{v,a} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

### 5.8 Block-Section Occupation (Conflict-Free)
At most one train may occupy a given segment at a given interval:
$$
\sum_{i \in T} \text{occ}_i^b{}_k \;\leq\; 1 \qquad \forall b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

### 5.9 Bidirectional Conflict on Shared Track
For trains in opposite directions sharing a track (one normal, one rerouted):
$$
\text{occ}_i^b{}_k + \text{occ}_j^b{}_k \;\leq\; 1 \qquad \forall b \in B,\; k \in K,\; \forall (i,j): \text{dir}(i) \neq \text{dir}(j)
$$

### 5.10 Disruption Constraints
During the disruption window, the normal track of segment $b^*$ is forbidden:
$$
r^N_i^{b^*} = 0 \qquad \forall i \in T \quad \text{when } t \in [t^{\text{dis}}_s, t^{\text{dis}}_e]
$$

Equivalently, the route variable enforces:
$$
r^N_i^{b^*} \cdot \mathbb{1}[t \in [t^{\text{dis}}_s, t^{\text{dis}}_e]] = 0
$$

### 5.11 Rerouting Consistency
The route choice is decomposed into two binary variables:
$$
r_i^b = r^N_i^b + 2 \cdot r^R_i^b \qquad \forall i \in T,\; b \in B
$$
$$
r^N_i^b + r^R_i^b \leq 1 \qquad \forall i \in T,\; b \in B
$$

If a train is rerouted, the opposite track must be free of conflicting opposite-direction traffic during the traversal window (enforced via 5.9).

### 5.12 Train Ordering at Stations
For every pair of trains sharing a station:
$$
z_{i,j}^s + z_{j,i}^s = 1 \qquad \forall i, j \in T,\; i \neq j,\; s \in S
$$

If $z_{i,j}^s = 1$ (train $i$ before train $j$):
$$
y_i^s + \varepsilon \;\leq\; x_j^s + M(1 - z_{i,j}^s) \qquad \forall i, j \in T,\; i \neq j,\; s \in S
$$

### 5.13 Minimum Headway Constraints
For consecutive trains in the same direction on the same segment:
$$
x_j^{s^{\text{arr}}(b)} \;\geq\; x_i^{s^{\text{arr}}(b)} + h_{\min} - M(1 - z_{i,j}^{s^{\text{dep}}(b)}) \qquad \forall i, j \in T,\; b \in B
$$

### 5.14 Cancellation
If $c_i = 1$, all rescheduling variables for train $i$ are deactivated (via Big-M relaxation in 5.3 and elsewhere).

### 5.15 Initial and Boundary Conditions
$$
x_i^{s_0} = \bar{d}_i^{s_0} \qquad \forall i \in T
$$
$$
y_i^{s_{\text{last}}} \leq T_{\text{hor}} \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

### 5.16 Linking Speed Profile to Rescheduling
The position profile determines occupation:
$$
\text{occ}_i^b{}_k = 1 \iff \xi_i^b{}_k \in [0, L_b] \quad \text{(linearized via Big-M)}
$$
$$
\xi_i^b{}_k \leq L_b \cdot \text{occ}_i^b{}_k + M(1 - \text{occ}_i^b{}_k) \qquad \forall i, b, k
$$
$$
\xi_i^b{}_k \geq 0 \cdot \text{occ}_i^b{}_k - M(1 - \text{occ}_i^b{}_k) \qquad \forall i, b, k
$$

### 5.17 Non-Negativity and Variable Domains
$$
x_i^s, y_i^s, \delta_i^s, v_i^b{}_k, a_i^b{}_k, p_i^b{}_k, e_i^b{}_k, \xi_i^b{}_k \geq 0
$$
$$
z_{i,j}^s, r^N_i^b, r^R_i^b, c_i, \text{occ}_i^b{}_k \in \{0, 1\}
$$
$$
r_i^b \in \{0, 1, 2\}
$$

---

## 6. Modeling Assumptions

1. **Single-line bidirectional corridor** with passing sidings at stations; each direction normally uses its own track.
2. **Identical train performance** characteristics (same $v_{\max}, a_{\max}, a_{\text{brake}}$ for all trains).
3. **Single disruption event** affecting exactly one segment $b^*$ during $[t^{\text{dis}}_s, t^{\text{dis}}_e]$.
4. **Rerouting permitted only within the disruption window** and only on the blocked segment.
5. **Time and space discretization** with uniform step $\Delta t$ to linearize the kinematic equations.
6. **Linearized Davis equation** for energy, using McCormick envelopes for the bilinear term $v \cdot a$.
7. **No partial cancellation** — a train is either fully cancelled ($c_i = 1$) or fully operated.
8. **Headway measured at station exits** to enforce safe separation.
9. **Conflict-free operation** guaranteed by occupation variables and pairwise Big-M ordering constraints.
10. **Deterministic parameters** — no stochasticity in disruption timing or train performance.

---

## Summary

This MILP jointly optimizes:
- **Rescheduling decisions**: arrival/departure times, train ordering, route choice (normal vs. rerouted), and cancellation.
- **Speed-profile decisions**: speed, acceleration, traction power, and energy per discretized interval.
- **Disruption handling**: forbids normal-track usage on the blocked segment during the disruption window while permitting rerouting to the opposite track.
- **Bidirectional safety**: prevents simultaneous occupation of shared track by trains in opposite directions.

The objective balances **delay minimization**, **energy efficiency**, and **service cancellation penalties**, producing a conflict-free, executable timetable with corresponding feasible speed profiles.
