Text:
# MILP Formulation for the Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

Below is a complete mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation that captures the **rerouting, reordering, and rescheduling** sub-problems described in the source paper. The model follows the *pair-wise delay interpretation* of Pellegrini et al. (2014, 2015, 2019) and is presented in two variants: (i) a **sub-optimal model** that ignores delay propagation, and (ii) a **global-optimum model** that explicitly accounts for propagation. Both variants share the same variables and most constraints; the differences are highlighted.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j \in \mathcal{T}$ |
| $\mathcal{B}$ | Set of track blocks (resources), indexed by $b \in \mathcal{B}$ |
| $\mathcal{R}_i$ | Set of feasible routes for train $i$, indexed by $r \in \mathcal{R}_i$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of scheduled stops / stations, indexed by $s \in \mathcal{S}$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of conflict points (block / station pairs), indexed by $k \in \mathcal{K}$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_i$ | Ordered sequence of blocks traversed by train $i$ on route $r$ |
| $\mathcal{T}_b \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Subset of trains that may potentially use block $b$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $t_i^{sch}$ | Scheduled time of train $i$ at its entry point | [min] |
| $\delta_i^{prim}$ | Primary (exogenous) delay of train $i$ | [min] |
| $\pi_i$ | Priority weight of train $i$ (e.g., passenger vs. freight) | – |
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ | [m] |
| $v_i$ | Nominal cruising speed of train $i$ | [m/min] |
| $h_b$ | Minimum headway time on block $b$ | [min] |
| $\tau_s^{min}$ | Minimum dwell time at stop $s$ | [min] |
| $d_{i,r,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if route $r$ of train $i$ traverses block $b$ | – |
| $o_{i,r,s} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if route $r$ of train $i$ stops at station $s$ | – |
| $c_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if trains $i$ and $j$ may both use block $b$ (potential conflict) | – |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) | – |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Routing**
- $x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is assigned route $r$.

**Reordering (pair-wise)**
- $y_{i,j} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is ordered before train $j$ at their common conflict point.
- $z_{i,j} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trains $i$ and $j$ actually share at least one block (conflict activation).

**Pair-wise waiting times**
- $w_{i,j} \geq 0$: additional waiting time imposed on train $j$ because of train $i$ [min].

**Timing**
- $T_{i,b}^{in} \geq 0$: time train $i$ enters block $b$.
- $T_{i,b}^{out} \geq 0$: time train $i$ exits block $b$.
- $T_{i,s}^{arr} \geq 0$: actual arrival time of train $i$ at stop $s$.
- $T_{i,s}^{dep} \geq 0$: actual departure time of train $i$ at stop $s$.

**Aggregate delay**
- $\Delta_i \geq 0$: total secondary delay of train $i$ [min].

---

## 4. Objective Function

The objective minimizes the priority-weighted sum of secondary delays, expressed equivalently through the pair-wise delays:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \pi_i \, \Delta_i 
\;=\; \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \pi_i \sum_{j \in \mathcal{T}} w_{j,i}
$$

*(Assumption: equal weighting between arrival and departure delays; alternative weightings can be introduced by splitting $\Delta_i$ into $\Delta_i^{arr}$ and $\Delta_i^{dep}$.)*

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Routing Constraints

**(R1) Single route per train**
$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_i} x_{i,r} \;=\; 1, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$

**(R2) Block usage activation**
$$
u_{i,b} \;=\; \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_i} d_{i,r,b}\, x_{i,r}, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; b \in \mathcal{B}
$$
where $u_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$ is an auxiliary variable indicating that train $i$ uses block $b$.

**(R3) Stop activation**
$$
\sigma_{i,s} \;=\; \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_i} o_{i,r,s}\, x_{i,r}, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

### 5.2 Train Dynamics (Timing Constraints)

**(T1) Block traversal time** (running time on a block)
$$
T_{i,b}^{out} - T_{i,b}^{in} \;\geq\; \frac{L_b}{v_i} - M(1 - u_{i,b}), \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; b \in \mathcal{B}
$$

**(T2) Block sequence** (continuity along the route)
$$
T_{i,b_{k+1}}^{in} - T_{i,b_k}^{out} \;\geq\; 0 - M(1 - u_{i,b_k}) - M(1 - u_{i,b_{k+1}}), \quad \forall i,\; (b_k, b_{k+1}) \in \mathcal{P}_i
$$

**(T3) Initial entry time** (incorporating primary delay)
$$
T_{i,b_0}^{in} \;=\; t_i^{sch} + \delta_i^{prim}, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$

**(T4) Minimum dwell time at stations**
$$
T_{i,s}^{dep} - T_{i,s}^{arr} \;\geq\; \tau_s^{min} - M(1 - \sigma_{i,s}), \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(T5) Stop ↔ block coupling** (arrival at stop equals entry to first block of stop; departure equals exit from last block)
$$
T_{i,s}^{arr} \;\leq\; T_{i,b_s^{in}}^{in} + M(1 - \sigma_{i,s}), \qquad
T_{i,s}^{dep} \;\geq\; T_{i,b_s^{out}}^{out} - M(1 - \sigma_{i,s})
$$

### 5.3 Conflict Detection and Reordering

**(C1) Conflict activation**
$$
z_{i,j} \;\leq\; \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} c_{i,j,b}\, u_{i,b}\, u_{j,b}, \qquad \forall (i,j),\; i \neq j
$$

*(Linearised with standard McCormick envelopes or auxiliary binaries; assumption: pre-computed potential conflicts.)*

**(C2) Pair-wise ordering** (exactly one direction at every active conflict)
$$
y_{i,j} + y_{j,i} \;=\; z_{i,j}, \qquad \forall (i,j),\; i \neq j
$$

**(C3) Symmetry of conflict activation**
$$
z_{i,j} = z_{j,i}, \qquad \forall (i,j),\; i \neq j
$$

### 5.4 Safety / Headway Constraints

**(H1) Block headway** — if $i$ precedes $j$ on block $b$, $j$ cannot enter before $i$ has cleared it plus the headway margin:
$$
T_{j,b}^{in} \;\geq\; T_{i,b}^{out} + h_b - M(1 - y_{i,j}) - M(2 - z_{i,j}), \quad \forall (i,j),\; b \in \mathcal{B}
$$

**(H2) Safety-relevant overlap** (Lindenmaier et al., 2022): the overlap block $b'$ behind a stop signal at block $b$ must be clear for a time margin $h_b^{ovl}$:
$$
T_{i,b'}^{out} + h_b^{ovl} \;\leq\; T_{j,b}^{in} + M(1 - y_{i,j}) + M(2 - z_{i,j}), \quad \forall (i,j),\; (b,b') \in \mathcal{O}
$$
where $\mathcal{O}$ is the set of (signal-block, overlap-block) pairs.

### 5.5 Pair-wise Waiting Time Definition

**(W1) Waiting time lower bound** — if $i$ precedes $j$, the additional waiting of $j$ over its scheduled time is at least the headway-induced delay:
$$
w_{i,j} \;\geq\; T_{j,b}^{in} - (t_j^{sch} + \delta_j^{prim}) - M(1 - y_{i,j}) - M(2 - z_{i,j}), \quad \forall (i,j),\; b \in \mathcal{B}
$$

**(W2) Waiting time irrelevance when no conflict**
$$
w_{i,j} \;\leq\; M\, z_{i,j}, \qquad \forall (i,j),\; i \neq j
$$

### 5.6 Delay Aggregation

**(D1) Total secondary delay equals sum of incoming pair-wise delays**
$$
\Delta_i \;=\; \sum_{j \in \mathcal{T}} w_{j,i}, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$

---

## 6. Delay-Propagation Extension (Global-Optimum Model)

The **sub-optimal model** terminates here. The **global-optimum model** adds the following constraints to capture how a delay imposed on train $j$ by train $i$ propagates to any train $m$ ordered behind $j$ at a downstream conflict:

**(P1) Propagation through ordering chains** — if $j$ is delayed by $i$ and $m$ is ordered after $j$, then $m$ inherits at least the waiting time of $j$ plus the headway:
$$
w_{i,m} \;\geq\; w_{i,j} + h_b - M(1 - y_{j,m}) - M(2 - z_{j,m}), \quad \forall i, j, m \in \mathcal{T},\; b \in \mathcal{B}
$$

**(P2) Transitive closure of pair-wise delays** (optional strengthening)
$$
w_{i,m} \;\geq\; w_{i,j} + w_{j,m} - M(1 - y_{i,j}) - M(1 - y_{j,m}), \quad \forall i, j, m
$$

**(P3) Redefinition of total delay to include propagated delays**
$$
\Delta_i^{opt} \;=\; \sum_{j \in \mathcal{T}} w_{j,i}^{prop}, \qquad 
\text{where } w_{j,i}^{prop} = w_{j,i} + \sum_{k \neq i,j} w_{j,k}\, y_{k,i}
$$

The objective of the global-optimum model becomes:
$$
\min \; Z^{opt} \;=\; \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \pi_i \, \Delta_i^{opt}
$$

---

## 7. Summary of Model Variants

| Aspect | Sub-Optimal Model (§3.1) | Global-Optimum Model (§3.3) |
|---|---|---|
| Rerouting | ✓ (R1)–(R3) | ✓ (R1)–(R3) |
| Reordering | ✓ (C1)–(C3) | ✓ (C1)–(C3) |
| Rescheduling | ✓ (T1)–(T5), (H1)–(H2) | ✓ (T1)–(T5), (H1)–(H2) |
| Pair-wise delays | ✓ (W1)–(W2), (D1) | ✓ (W1)–(W2), (D1) |
| Delay propagation | ✗ | ✓ (P1)–(P3) |
| Objective | $\sum \pi_i \Delta_i$ | $\sum \pi_i \Delta_i^{opt}$ |

---

## 8. Assumptions

1. **Time discretization** is continuous (events occur at real-valued times); for a discrete-time version, all time variables become integer.
2. **Primary delays** $\delta_i^{prim}$ are known parameters at the time of optimisation (perfect information on disturbances).
3. **Conflict pre-computation**: potential conflicts $c_{i,j,b}$ are derived offline from the route topology.
4. **Single-track / double-track** behaviour is captured by the headway parameters $h_b$ and overlap sets $\mathcal{O}$; no explicit distinction is encoded in the variables.
5. **Train speeds** are constant within each block (no coasting / regenerative-braking profile), which is consistent with the macroscopic representation described in the paper.
6. **No train cancellation or short-turning** is considered — every train must be routed and scheduled.
7. **Symmetric pair-wise ordering**: $y_{i,j}$ and $y_{j,i}$ are mutually exclusive, which is enforced by (C2) together with (C3).
8. **Big-M values** are chosen tight enough to preserve LP relaxation strength but large enough to never be active in any feasible solution (problem-specific tuning required).
9. **Linearisation** of products $u_{i,b}\, u_{j,b}$ in (C1) is performed via standard auxiliary-binary McCormick relaxations (omitted here for brevity but assumed available).
10. **Objective weights** $\pi_i$ are exogenous; in practice they reflect train categories (e.g., long-distance passenger > regional > freight).

---

This formulation is a faithful, self-contained linearisation of the rtRTMP described in the source paper, suitable for direct implementation in any MILP solver (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX, HiGHS). The sub-optimal variant offers a fast first-stage solution that can be warm-started into the global-optimum variant, mirroring the multi-stage framework proposed by the authors.

Text:
# TRSMP — Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (MILP Formulation)

## 1. Sets and indices
- $T$: set of trains, $t \in T$
- $S$: ordered set of stations, $i, j \in S$
- $E \subseteq S \times S$: set of track segments between consecutive stations, $e=(i,j) \in E$
- $\mathrm{TR} = \{\text{nom},\text{opp}\}$: nominal and opposite tracks per segment
- $P_{t,e}$: set of pre-computed discrete speed profiles for train $t$ on segment $e$, $p \in P_{t,e}$
- $D \subseteq E$: set of disrupted segments (nominal track blocked during window $W$)
- $W = [a,b]$: disruption time window
- Each $t \in T$ has direction $\mathrm{dir}_t \in \{\text{up}, \text{down}\}$

## 2. Parameters
- $\mathrm{arr}^0_{t,i}$, $\mathrm{dep}^0_{t,i}$: scheduled arrival/departure of train $t$ at station $i$
- $r_{t,e,p} \ge 0$, $e_{t,e,p} \ge 0$: running time and energy of profile $p$
- $h_{\min}$: minimum headway time between consecutive trains on the same track
- $h_{\text{dwell}}$: minimum dwell time at intermediate stations
- $\delta_{\max}$: maximum tolerated arrival delay (planning horizon)
- $w_{\text{delay}}, w_{\text{energy}}, c_{\text{cancel}}$: objective weights
- $M_1, M_2$: sufficiently large constants (big-$M$)
- $\mathrm{origin}_t$, $\mathrm{dest}_t$: first and last station of train $t$

## 3. Decision variables
- $A_{t,i} \ge 0$: actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $i$
- $D_{t,i} \ge 0$: actual departure time of train $t$ at station $i$
- $\mathrm{delay}_{t,i} \ge 0$: arrival delay of train $t$ at station $i$
- $x_{t,e,p} \in \{0,1\}$: train $t$ uses speed profile $p$ on segment $e$
- $y_{t,e} \in \{0,1\}$: train $t$ reroutes to the opposite track on segment $e$ (only if $e\in D$)
- $z_t \in \{0,1\}$: train $t$ is cancelled
- $o_{t_1,t_2,e,\mathrm{tr}} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering on track $\mathrm{tr}\in\mathrm{TR}$ of segment $e$ (1 if $t_1$ departs $e$ before $t_2$ enters, 0 otherwise)
- $v_{t,e} \in \{0,1\}$: train $t$ actually occupies the opposite track on segment $e$ (joint indicator of rerouting and profile choice)

## 4. Objective function
$$
\min \quad \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{i \in S} w_{\text{delay}}\,\mathrm{delay}_{t,i}
\;+\;\sum_{t \in T} c_{\text{cancel}}\,z_t
\;+\;\sum_{t \in T}\sum_{e \in E}\sum_{p \in P_{t,e}} w_{\text{energy}}\,e_{t,e,p}\,x_{t,e,p}
$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Speed-profile selection (exactly one profile per segment, unless cancelled):**
$$
\sum_{p \in P_{t,e}} x_{t,e,p} + z_t = 1 \quad \forall\, t\in T,\; e\in E
$$

**(C2) Running-time coupling (arrival–departure via chosen profile):**
$$
D_{t,j} - A_{t,i} \;\ge\; \sum_{p \in P_{t,e}} r_{t,e,p}\,x_{t,e,p} \quad \forall\, t\in T,\; e=(i,j)\in E
$$

**(C3) Rerouting allowed only on disrupted segments for up-direction trains:**
$$
y_{t,e} \le \sum_{p\in P_{t,e}} x_{t,e,p},\qquad y_{t,e} \le \mathbf{1}_{\{\mathrm{dir}_t=\text{up}\}} \quad \forall\, t,\; e\in D
$$
$$
y_{t,e} = 0 \quad \forall\, t,\; e \notin D
$$

**(C4) Joint opposite-track-use indicator (linearization of $v_{t,e} = y_{t,e}\cdot\sum_p x_{t,e,p}$):**
$$
v_{t,e} \le y_{t,e},\quad v_{t,e} \le \sum_{p\in P_{t,e}} x_{t,e,p},\quad v_{t,e} \ge y_{t,e} + \sum_{p\in P_{t,e}} x_{t,e,p} - 1 \quad \forall\, t,\; e
$$

**(C5) Minimum dwell time at intermediate stations:**
$$
A_{t,i} + h_{\text{dwell}} \;\le\; D_{t,i} \quad \forall\, t,\; i \notin \{\mathrm{origin}_t,\mathrm{dest}_t\}
$$

**(C6) Delay definition and bound (relaxed when cancelled):**
$$
A_{t,i} - \mathrm{arr}^0_{t,i} \;\le\; \mathrm{delay}_{t,i} \quad \forall\, t,\; i \neq \mathrm{origin}_t
$$
$$
\mathrm{delay}_{t,i} \;\le\; \delta_{\max}\,(1-z_t) \quad \forall\, t,\; i
$$

**(C7) Endpoints anchoring (relaxed when cancelled):**
$$
D_{t,\mathrm{origin}_t} \;\ge\; \mathrm{dep}^0_{t,\mathrm{origin}_t} - M_1\,z_t \quad \forall\, t
$$
$$
A_{t,\mathrm{dest}_t} \;\ge\; \mathrm{arr}^0_{t,\mathrm{dest}_t} - M_1\,z_t \quad \forall\, t
$$

**(C8) Headway / conflict-free ordering on each track of each segment:**
For every $e=(i,j)\in E$, $\mathrm{tr}\in\mathrm{TR}$ and every pair $t_1\neq t_2$ that may share this track:
$$
D_{t_1,j} + h_{\min} - M_1\bigl(1-o_{t_1,t_2,e,\mathrm{tr}}\bigr) \;\le\; D_{t_2,i} + M_1(1 - \alpha_{t_1,t_2,e,\mathrm{tr}})
$$
$$
D_{t_2,i} + h_{\min} - M_1\,o_{t_1,t_2,e,\mathrm{tr}} \;\le\; D_{t_1,j} + M_1(1 - \alpha_{t_1,t_2,e,\mathrm{tr}})
$$
where the activation binary $\alpha_{t_1,t_2,e,\mathrm{tr}}$ is 1 iff both trains use that track, defined as:
- nominal track ($\mathrm{tr}=\text{nom}$): $\alpha_{t_1,t_2,e,\text{nom}} = \min\!\bigl(\sum_p x_{t_1,e,p},\;\sum_p x_{t_2,e,p}\bigr)$ (linearized via auxiliary binaries as in (C4));
- opposite track ($\mathrm{tr}=\text{opp}$): $\alpha_{t_1,t_2,e,\text{opp}} = \min(v_{t_1,e},\,v_{t_2,e})$ (linearized analogously).

**(C9) Disruption blockage — nominal track of $e\in D$ cannot be used during $W$:**
Using auxiliary $w_{t,e}\in\{0,1\}$ (1 = enter before $a$, 0 = enter after $b$):
$$
A_{t,i} \;\le\; a + M_1\bigl(1 - \sum_p x_{t,e,p} + v_{t,e}\bigr) \quad \forall\, t,\; e=(i,j)\in D
$$
$$
A_{t,i} \;\ge\; b - M_1\bigl(1 - \sum_p x_{t,e,p} + v_{t,e}\bigr) \quad \forall\, t,\; e=(i,j)\in D
$$
(constraint is binding only when the nominal track is used and the train has not rerouted.)

**(C10) Rerouting window — opposite track may be used only when entry occurs during $W$:**
$$
A_{t,i} \;\le\; b + M_1(1-v_{t,e}) \quad \forall\, t,\; e=(i,j)\in D
$$
$$
A_{t,i} \;\ge\; a - M_1(1-v_{t,e}) \quad \forall\, t,\; e=(i,j)\in D
$$

**(C11) Station platform capacity — one train per station per headway:**
For each station $i\in S$ and pair $t_1\neq t_2$:
$$
\bigl|D_{t_1,i} - A_{t_2,i}\bigr| \;\ge\; h_{\min}
$$
enforced via an ordering binary and big-$M$ analogous to (C8), activated only if both trains stop at $i$ (auxiliary binary $\beta_{t,i}\in\{0,1\}$).

**(C12) Variable domains:**
$$
A_{t,i}, D_{t,i}, \mathrm{delay}_{t,i} \ge 0;\qquad
x_{t,e,p},\,y_{t,e},\,z_t,\,o_{t_1,t_2,e,\mathrm{tr}},\,v_{t,e},\,w_{t,e},\,\alpha,\,\beta \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 6. Modeling assumptions
- The railway corridor has two directional tracks per segment; trains travel on their nominal track unless rerouted.
- The disruption blocks the up-direction nominal track on a fixed subset of segments $D$ during $[a,b]$; down-direction nominal tracks are unaffected.
- Rerouting diverts up-trains onto the opposite track through $D$ (unidirectional bi-directional traffic conflicts handled by (C8) on the opposite track).
- Speed profiles are precomputed offline from train dynamics; discretization yields a linear coupling between running time, energy and the rescheduling variables.
- The horizon of optimization is bounded by $\delta_{\max}$ for arrivals; departures/arrivals of cancelled trains are relaxed via $M_1\,z_t$.
- All binary products are linearized with big-$M$ / auxiliary variables, keeping the formulation a MILP.

Text:
# MILP Model for Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

## Sets and Indices
- **T**: set of trains, indexed by *t* ∈ T
- **S**: set of stations, indexed by *s* ∈ S, ordered along the line
- **R**: set of track segments between consecutive stations, indexed by *r* ∈ R
- **K**: set of discretized time intervals, indexed by *k* ∈ K, each of duration Δ
- **Dir**: set of train directions, Dir = {up, down}

## Parameters
- $a_{t,s}^{0}$: scheduled arrival time of train *t* at station *s*
- $d_{t,s}^{0}$: scheduled departure time of train *t* at station *s*
- $\tau_{t,r}^{\min}, \tau_{t,r}^{\max}$: minimum/maximum running time of train *t* on segment *r*
- $L_r$: length of segment *r*
- $v^{\max}, v^{\min}$: maximum/minimum allowed speed
- $a^{\max}$: maximum acceleration
- $b^{\max}$: maximum deceleration
- $h^{\min}$: minimum headway time between consecutive trains
- $c^{\text{dwell}}$: minimum dwell time at stations
- $r_d^{\text{start}}, r_d^{\text{end}}$: endpoints of disrupted segment
- $[t_d^{\text{start}}, t_d^{\text{end}}]$: disruption time window
- $w_{\text{delay}}, w_{\text{energy}}$: weights for delay and energy in the objective
- $M$: large constant (big-M)
- $\alpha_i, \beta_i$: coefficients of piecewise-linear energy approximation at breakpoint *i*
- $T^{\text{horizon}}$: planning horizon

## Decision Variables

**Timetable and Rescheduling Variables:**
- $A_{t,s} \geq 0$: actual arrival time of train *t* at station *s*
- $D_{t,s} \geq 0$: actual departure time of train *t* at station *s*
- $\delta_{t,s} \geq 0$: arrival delay of train *t* at station *s*
- $\rho_{t,s} \geq 0$: departure delay of train *t* at station *s*
- $o_{t_1,t_2,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t_1$ departs before $t_2$ at station *s*
- $\text{cancel}_t \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train *t* is cancelled

**Routing Variables:**
- $x_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train *t* traverses segment *r*
- $y_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train *t* is rerouted to the opposite track on segment *r*
- $z_{t,r,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train *t* occupies segment *r* at time interval *k*

**Speed Profile Variables:**
- $v_{t,r,k} \geq 0$: speed of train *t* on segment *r* during interval *k*
- $v_{t,r}^{\text{enter}}, v_{t,r}^{\text{exit}} \geq 0$: entry/exit speed of train *t* into/from segment *r*
- $\tau_{t,r} \geq 0$: actual running time of train *t* on segment *r*

**Energy Variables:**
- $e_{t,r,k} \geq 0$: energy consumption of train *t* on segment *r* during interval *k*

## Objective Function

$$
\min Z = w_{\text{delay}} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \delta_{t,s} + w_{\text{delay}} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \rho_{t,s} + w_{\text{energy}} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{r \in R} \sum_{k \in K} e_{t,r,k} + M \sum_{t \in T} \text{cancel}_t
$$

## Constraints

### 1. Delay Definitions
$$
\delta_{t,s} = A_{t,s} - a_{t,s}^{0}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S
$$
$$
\rho_{t,s} = D_{t,s} - d_{t,s}^{0}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S
$$
$$
\delta_{t,s} \geq 0, \quad \rho_{t,s} \geq 0
$$

### 2. Running Time and Dwell Time Coupling
$$
\tau_{t,r} = \Delta \sum_{k \in K} z_{t,r,k}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; r \in R
$$
$$
D_{t,s} - A_{t,s} \geq c^{\text{dwell}}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S
$$
$$
A_{t,s+1} - D_{t,s} = \sum_{r \in R} \tau_{t,r}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S \setminus \{S_{\text{last}}\}
$$

### 3. Route Feasibility
$$
\sum_{r \in R} x_{t,r} = |S| - 1 - (|S|-1) \cdot \text{cancel}_t, \quad \forall t \in T
$$
$$
y_{t,r} = 0, \quad \forall t \in T, \; r \notin [r_d^{\text{start}}, r_d^{\text{end}}]
$$

### 4. Disruption Constraints
For all *t* ∈ T, *r* ∈ [r_d^{\text{start}}, r_d^{\text{end}}], and *k* corresponding to the disruption window:
$$
z_{t,r,k} \leq y_{t,r}, \quad \text{(trains must reroute to enter disrupted segments)}
$$
$$
z_{t,r,k} = 0, \quad \text{if } y_{t,r} = 0 \text{ and } k \cdot \Delta \in [t_d^{\text{start}}, t_d^{\text{end}}]
$$

### 5. Bidirectional Conflict Resolution (Shared-Track Headway)
For any two trains $t_1, t_2$ of opposite directions on shared track *r*:
$$
z_{t_1,r,k} + z_{t_2,r,k} \leq 1, \quad \forall k \in K
$$

For same-direction trains on segment *r*, if $o_{t_1,t_2,r} = 1$ (t_1 precedes t_2):
$$
\sum_{k' < k} z_{t_1,r,k'} \geq \left\lceil \frac{h^{\min}}{\Delta} \right\rceil \cdot z_{t_2,r,k}, \quad \forall k \in K
$$

### 6. Speed Profile Dynamics (Discrete Motion Equations)
$$
v_{t,r,k+1} - v_{t,r,k} \leq a^{\max} \Delta, \quad \forall t \in T, \; r \in R, \; k \in K \setminus \{K_{\text{last}}\}
$$
$$
v_{t,r,k+1} - v_{t,r,k} \geq -b^{\max} \Delta, \quad \forall t \in T, \; r \in R, \; k \in K \setminus \{K_{\text{last}}\}
$$
$$
v^{\min} \cdot z_{t,r,k} \leq v_{t,r,k} \leq v^{\max} \cdot z_{t,r,k}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; r \in R, \; k \in K
$$

### 7. Distance/Speed Consistency
$$
\Delta \sum_{k \in K} v_{t,r,k} = L_r \cdot x_{t,r}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; r \in R
$$

### 8. Entry/Exit Speed Continuity
$$
v_{t,r}^{\text{enter}} = v_{t,r,1}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; r \in R
$$
$$
v_{t,r}^{\text{exit}} = v_{t,r,|K|}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; r \in R
$$
$$
v_{t,r}^{\text{exit}} = v_{t,r+1}^{\text{enter}}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; r \in R \setminus \{R_{\text{last}}\}
$$

### 9. Station Ordering Constraints
$$
o_{t_1,t_2,s} + o_{t_2,t_1,s} = 1 - \text{cancel}_{t_1} - \text{cancel}_{t_2}, \quad \forall t_1 \neq t_2 \in T, \; s \in S
$$

If $o_{t_1,t_2,s} = 1$:
$$
D_{t_1,s} + h^{\min} \leq D_{t_2,s} + M(1 - o_{t_1,t_2,s}), \quad \forall t_1, t_2, s
$$

### 10. Cancellation Logic
$$
A_{t,s} \leq T^{\text{horizon}} (1 - \text{cancel}_t), \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S
$$
$$
D_{t,s} \leq T^{\text{horizon}} (1 - \text{cancel}_t), \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S
$$

### 11. Energy Consumption (Piecewise-Linear Approximation)
For each breakpoint *i* of the convex energy function:
$$
e_{t,r,k} \geq \alpha_i \cdot v_{t,r,k} + \beta_i \cdot z_{t,r,k}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; r \in R, \; k \in K, \; i \in I
$$

### 12. Time Horizon Bounds
$$
0 \leq A_{t,s} \leq T^{\text{horizon}}, \quad 0 \leq D_{t,s} \leq T^{\text{horizon}}
$$
$$
\tau_{t,r}^{\min} \leq \tau_{t,r} \leq \tau_{t,r}^{\max}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; r \in R
$$

### 13. Linking Occupancy and Routing
$$
z_{t,r,k} \leq x_{t,r}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; r \in R, \; k \in K
$$
$$
\sum_{k \in K} z_{t,r,k} \geq x_{t,r}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; r \in R
$$

## Assumptions Made

1. **Double-track line** with unidirectional traffic on each track under normal conditions; opposite track may be used only via rerouting during the disruption.
2. **Discretized time** with uniform interval length Δ for both timetable coupling and speed profile discretization.
3. **Uniform train characteristics** within a train type (max acceleration, braking, speed limits applied identically).
4. **Energy consumption** is approximated as a piecewise-linear function of speed (since $v^2$ is convex but nonlinear).
5. **No train overtaking within a segment**; ordering decisions are enforced at stations and through headway on segments.
6. **Cancellation** is permitted only at the origin station; partial route cancellation is not modeled.
7. **Disruption is stationary in space** but **bounded in time** $[t_d^{\text{start}}, t_d^{\text{end}}]$.
8. **Symmetric disruption**: only one track of segment *r* in $[r_d^{\text{start}}, r_d^{\text{end}}]$ is blocked, requiring rerouting to the opposite (still operational) track.
9. **Dwell times** are flexible above $c^{\text{dwell}}$ to allow conflict resolution (extended dwell as a retiming tool).
10. **No track gradients or curves** affecting energy/speed (or these are absorbed into $\alpha_i, \beta_i$).
11. **Trains cannot pass each other within a segment**; reordering occurs only at stations.

This MILP jointly optimizes retiming, reordering, rerouting, optional cancellation, and continuous energy-efficient speed profiles, producing a conflict-free timetable that is executable at the train control level under partial segment blockage disruptions.

# MILP Model for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance-to-Go Signalling

Below is a complete mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation that extends the RECIFE-MILP framework with DTG-specific enhancements: (i) discrete speed profile options, (ii) train- and speed-dependent braking distances, (iii) brake indication points (IPs) and end-of-authority (EoA) locations, and (iv) explicit handling of switches.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $I$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j \in I$ |
| $E$ | Set of signalling events (arrivals/departures at stations, block/TDS boundaries), indexed by $e, e' \in E$ |
| $E_i \subseteq E$ | Subset of events belonging to train $i$ |
| $K$ | Set of track sections (blocks/TDS), indexed by $k \in K$ |
| $K^{SW} \subset K$ | Subset of switches, indexed by $sw \in K^{SW}$ |
| $K^{OL} = K \setminus K^{SW}$ | Open-line (non-switch) sections |
| $V$ | Set of discrete speed profiles, indexed by $v \in V$ |
| $R_i$ | Set of feasible routes for train $i$, indexed by $r \in R_i$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s \in S$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $s_e$ | Scheduled time of event $e$ | s |
| $\tau^{dwell}_{i,s}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ | s |
| $\tau^{run}_{i,v,e,e'}$ | Minimum running time from $e$ to $e'$ for train $i$ under profile $v$ | s |
| $L_k$ | Length of section $k$ | m |
| $\ell_i$ | Length of train $i$ | m |
| $v_{i,v}$ | Cruising speed of train $i$ under profile $v$ | m/s |
| $b_{i,v}$ | Braking distance of train $i$ from speed $v_{i,v}$ to standstill | m |
| $h^{min}_k$ | Minimum technological headway on section $k$ | s |
| $h^{min}_{sw}$ | Minimum headway through switch $sw$ | s |
| $c_{k,k'}$ | $=1$ if sections $k$ and $k'$ share a conflicting switch movement, else $0$ | – |
| $w_e$ | Weight of delay at event $e$ in the objective | – |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) | – |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Symbol | Description | Domain |
|--------|-------------|--------|
| $t_e$ | Actual time of event $e$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |
| $\delta_e$ | Delay of event $e$ w.r.t. schedule | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |
| $z_{i,v}$ | $=1$ if train $i$ uses speed profile $v$ | $\{0,1\}$ |
| $w_{i,r}$ | $=1$ if train $i$ uses route $r$ | $\{0,1\}$ |
| $x_{i,k}$ | $=1$ if section $k$ lies on the path of train $i$ | $\{0,1\}$ |
| $y_{i,j,k}$ | $=1$ if train $i$ traverses section $k$ before train $j$ | $\{0,1\}$ |
| $a_{i,k}$ | Time train $i$ enters section $k$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |
| $d_{i,k}$ | Time train $i$ exits section $k$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |
| $\beta^{s}_{i,k}$ | Start of blocking time of train $i$ on section $k$ (brake IP) | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |
| $\beta^{e}_{i,k}$ | End of blocking time of train $i$ on section $k$ (EoA release) | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimise the total weighted delay of all events:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \sum_{e \in E} w_e \, \delta_e
\tag{Obj}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Delay definition
$$
\delta_e \;\geq\; t_e - s_e \qquad \forall e \in E
\tag{1}
$$

### 5.2 Speed-profile and route selection
$$
\sum_{v \in V} z_{i,v} \;=\; 1 \qquad \forall i \in I
\tag{2a}
$$
$$
\sum_{r \in R_i} w_{i,r} \;=\; 1 \qquad \forall i \in I
\tag{2b}
$$

### 5.3 Section usage from route choice
$$
x_{i,k} \;=\; \sum_{r \in R_i \,:\, k \in r} w_{i,r} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K
\tag{3}
$$

### 5.4 Event ordering (running + dwell, speed-dependent)
$$
t_{e'} - t_e \;\geq\; \sum_{v \in V} z_{i(e),v} \, \tau^{run}_{i(e),v,e,e'} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; e, e' \in E_i \text{ consecutive}
\tag{4a}
$$
$$
t_{e^{dep}} - t_{e^{arr}} \;\geq\; \tau^{dwell}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; \text{arrival/departure pair at } s \in S
\tag{4b}
$$

### 5.5 Section entry/exit linking
$$
a_{i,k} \;\leq\; t_e + M(1 - x_{i,k}) \qquad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K,\; e = \text{entry event of } k
\tag{5a}
$$
$$
a_{i,k} \;\geq\; t_e - M(1 - x_{i,k}) \qquad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K,\; e = \text{entry event of } k
\tag{5b}
$$

### 5.6 Section traversal time (speed-dependent, linearised)
$$
d_{i,k} - a_{i,k} \;\geq\; \frac{L_k}{v_{i,v}} - M(1 - z_{i,v}) \qquad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K,\; v \in V
\tag{6a}
$$
$$
d_{i,k} - a_{i,k} \;\leq\; \frac{L_k}{v_{i,v}} + M(1 - z_{i,v}) \qquad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K,\; v \in V
\tag{6b}
$$

### 5.7 DTG blocking-time start — brake indication point (speed-dependent)
The brake IP lies at distance $b_{i,v}$ before the EoA (entry of section $k$). Hence:

$$
\beta^{s}_{i,k} \;\leq\; a_{i,k} - \sum_{v \in V} z_{i,v} \, b_{i,v} + M(1 - x_{i,k}) \qquad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K
\tag{7a}
$$
$$
\beta^{s}_{i,k} \;\geq\; a_{i,k} - \sum_{v \in V} z_{i,v} \, b_{i,v} - M(1 - x_{i,k}) \qquad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K
\tag{7b}
$$

### 5.8 DTG blocking-time end — EoA release (train clears section)
$$
\beta^{e}_{i,k} \;\geq\; d_{i,k} + \sum_{v \in V} z_{i,v} \frac{\ell_i}{v_{i,v}} - M(1 - x_{i,k}) \qquad \forall i \in I,\; k \in K
\tag{8}
$$

### 5.9 Section conflict resolution (open-line blocks)
For every pair of trains sharing a section:

$$
y_{i,j,k} + y_{j,i,k} \;=\; x_{i,k} \, x_{j,k} \quad \text{(linearised via standard McCormick)} \qquad \forall i < j,\; k \in K^{OL}
\tag{9a}
$$
$$
\beta^{s}_{j,k} - \beta^{e}_{i,k} \;\geq\; -M(1 - y_{i,j,k}) \qquad \forall i \neq j,\; k \in K^{OL}
\tag{9b}
$$
$$
\beta^{s}_{i,k} - \beta^{e}_{j,k} \;\geq\; -M(1 - y_{j,i,k}) \qquad \forall i \neq j,\; k \in K^{OL}
\tag{9c}
$$

### 5.10 Switch conflict resolution
Switches require additional mutual-exclusion constraints because two routes through the same switch may be physically incompatible:

$$
y_{i,j,sw} + y_{j,i,sw} \;\geq\; c_{k,sw} \, x_{i,k} \, x_{j,sw} \quad \text{(linearised)} \qquad \forall i < j,\; sw \in K^{SW},\; k \in K
\tag{10a}
$$
$$
\beta^{s}_{j,sw} - \beta^{e}_{i,sw} \;\geq\; h^{min}_{sw} - M(1 - y_{i,j,sw}) \qquad \forall i \neq j,\; sw \in K^{SW}
\tag{10b}
$$
$$
\beta^{s}_{i,sw} - \beta^{e}_{j,sw} \;\geq\; h^{min}_{sw} - M(1 - y_{j,i,sw}) \qquad \forall i \neq j,\; sw \in K^{SW}
\tag{10c}
$$

### 5.11 Minimum technological headway on open-line sections
$$
\beta^{s}_{j,k} - \beta^{s}_{i,k} \;\geq\; h^{min}_k - M(1 - y_{i,j,k}) \qquad \forall i \neq j,\; k \in K^{OL}
\tag{11}
$$

### 5.12 Variable domains
$$
t_e \geq 0,\; \delta_e \geq 0,\; a_{i,k} \geq 0,\; d_{i,k} \geq 0,\; \beta^{s}_{i,k} \geq 0,\; \beta^{e}_{i,k} \geq 0
$$
$$
z_{i,v},\, w_{i,r},\, x_{i,k},\, y_{i,j,k} \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

The resulting MILP — hereafter **RECIFE-DTG-MILP** — is:

$$
\boxed{\;\min_{(t,\delta,z,w,x,y,a,d,\beta)} \; \sum_{e \in E} w_e \, \delta_e \quad \text{s.t. (1)–(12)}\;}
$$

---

## 7. Key Modelling Assumptions

1. **Discrete speed profiles.** Continuous speed is approximated by a finite set $V$ of cruising speeds $\{v_{i,1}, \dots, v_{i,|V|}\}$, each associated with a corresponding braking distance $b_{i,v}$ (assumed precomputed from a braking curve model).
2. **Braking distance independence.** $b_{i,v}$ depends only on train $i$ and speed profile $v$, not on track gradient (assumed negligible or pre-averaged).
3. **Block granularity.** The track is discretised into TDS sections $K$; the EoA is always located at a TDS boundary, consistent with ETCS L2 with TTD.
4. **No virtual/moving block.** The model targets ETCS L2 with TTD (fixed-block DTG); ETCS L3 moving block is out of scope.
5. **Deterministic dwell and running times.** Stochastic variations are not modelled; the input timetable already contains the realised (delayed) events.
6. **Single-route per train.** Each train selects exactly one route $r \in R_i$ and one speed profile $v \in V$ for its entire journey (extension to per-section profiles is straightforward via additional binary variables).
7. **Linearised products.** All bilinear terms $x_{i,k} x_{j,k}$ and $z_{i,v} b_{i,v}$ are linearised using big-M or McCormick envelopes; $M$ is chosen as the planning horizon length.
8. **Switch conflicts.** Two trains using the same switch in conflicting directions cannot have overlapping blocking times; this is captured by (10a)–(10c) using a conflict matrix $c_{k,sw}$.
9. **No re-routing beyond predefined routes.** Re-routing is limited to the discrete set $R_i$; new routes are not generated by the solver.
10. **Brake IP is the start of the blocking time.** Following ETCS L2, the blocking time of a section starts when the preceding train's brake IP is reached, and ends when the train fully clears the section plus its length.

---

## 8. Remarks on the DTG Enhancement

Compared to the original RECIFE-MILP for fixed-block signalling, the model introduces three principal enhancements:

| Enhancement | Variable/Constraint | Effect |
|-------------|---------------------|--------|
| Speed-profile choice | $z_{i,v}$ + (2a), (4a), (6a–b) | Captures speed-dependent running times |
| Speed-dependent braking distance | $b_{i,v}$ inside (7a–b) | Models DTG brake IP anywhere on the track |
| Switch vs. open-line distinction | $K^{SW}$ vs. $K^{OL}$ in (9)–(10) | Captures additional switch-move conflicts |

These enhancements enable the model to reproduce the shorter, speed-dependent headways of DTG signalling and to propose different rescheduling decisions (retiming, reordering, rerouting) than the fixed-block baseline.

Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## Complete MILP Model

---

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

**Setting.** A double-track high-speed railway corridor consists of stations connected by segments. Each segment normally carries unidirectional traffic (one track per direction). Due to a disruption (e.g., equipment failure), one track of a segment is blocked during a time window. Affected trains may either wait or **reroute onto the opposite track**, provided bidirectional conflicts on that shared track are resolved.

**Assumptions (marked where they fill gaps in the input):**

- (A1) The corridor is a linear double-track line with stations $S=\{1,\dots,n\}$ and segments $L=\{1,\dots,n-1\}$. *(Reasonable assumption; the literature referenced uses corridors.)*
- (A2) The disruption blocks track $d$ (direction $d\in\{1,2\}$) of segment $\ell^\ast$ during $[T^s, T^e]$; one train occupies the segment at a time; no entrance–exit conflict at stations is modeled beyond headway times. *(Standard simplification.)*
- (A3) Each train has a finite set of pre-computed **speed profiles** per segment (macroscopic integration of the TSMP), each characterized by an unimpeded running time and energy consumption; a lower speed bound applies if the profile must respect disruption-specific speed restrictions.
- (A4) A train route through a segment is either its nominal track or the opposite track (rerouting only in the disruption area). Cancellation is permitted with a penalty. *(Input mentions cancellations.)*
- (A5) Time is discretized or continuous; all constraints below are linear.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, index $i$ |
| $S$ | set of stations, index $s$ |
| $L$ | set of segments, index $\ell$ |
| $P_{i\ell}$ | set of speed profiles of train $i$ on segment $\ell$ (from the TSMP), index $p$ |
| $R_{i\ell}=\{0,1\}$ | track choice: 0 = nominal track, 1 = opposite track |
| $K$ | set of (macroscopic) time slots (discretization of the horizon), index $k$ |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $a_i^s, d_i^s$ | originally scheduled arrival/departure of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\tau^{arr}_{i}, \tau^{dep}_{i}$ | minimum arrival headway / departure headway at station $s$ (direction-aware) |
| $h_{\ell}$ | minimum headway between trains on segment $\ell$ (same track) |
| $t^p_{i\ell}$ | running time of train $i$ on segment $\ell$ with speed profile $p$ |
| $e^p_{i\ell}$ | energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $\ell$ with profile $p$ |
| $w_i$ | lateness weight of train $i$; $\gamma_i$ | cancellation penalty |
| $\delta^{pen}_\ell$ | penalty for using the opposite (rerouted) track on segment $\ell$ |
| $U^s$ | capacity (number of parallel platform tracks) at station $s$ |
| $M$ | sufficiently large constant |

## 4. Decision Variables

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $a_{is}, d_{is}\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}$ | actual arrival / departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $x^p_{i\ell}\in\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ runs segment $\ell$ with speed profile $p$ |
| $r_{i\ell}\in\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses the opposite track on segment $\ell$ (reroute) |
| $y_{ij\ell}\in\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $\ell$ (same track usage order) |
| $z_{ij s}\in\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ arrives at/leaves station $s$ before train $j$ (station order) |
| $c_i\in\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $q_{i\ell}\in\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ occupies segment $\ell$ (non-cancelled) |
| $\Delta^{arr}_{is}, \Delta^{dep}_{is}\ge0$ | arrival / departure delay |

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize total weighted delay, energy consumption, rerouting penalty, and cancellation cost:

$$
\min \; \underbrace{\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\bigl(w_i\,\Delta^{arr}_{is}+w_i\,\Delta^{dep}_{is}\bigr)}_{\text{delays}}
+\underbrace{\rho\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{\ell\in L}\sum_{p\in P_{i\ell}} e^p_{i\ell}\,x^p_{i\ell}}_{\text{energy (TSMP)}}
+\underbrace{\sum_{i\in T}\sum_{\ell\in L}\delta^{pen}_\ell\, r_{i\ell}}_{\text{rerouting penalty}}
+\underbrace{\sum_{i\in T}\gamma_i\, c_i}_{\text{cancellations}}
$$

with $\rho$ a monetary conversion factor from kWh to cost-equivalent delay units.

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Timetable consistency (TRP)

**(C1) Running time coupled to speed profile (core TRP–TSMP coupling):**
$$
d_{i,\ell} - a_{i,\ell+1} = \sum_{p\in P_{i\ell}} t^p_{i\ell}\, x^p_{i\ell}
\qquad \forall i\in T,\ \ell\in L
$$
Here station $\ell+1$ denotes the downstream station of segment $\ell$.

**(C2) Dwell time:**
$$
d_{is} - a_{is} \ge \tau^{dwell}_{is} \qquad \forall i\in T,\ s\in S\setminus\{1,n\}
$$

**(C3) Profile selection uniqueness:**
$$
\sum_{p\in P_{i\ell}} x^p_{i\ell} = q_{i\ell} \qquad \forall i\in T,\ \ell\in L
$$

**(C4) Delay definition (linearization):**
$$
\Delta^{arr}_{is} \ge a_{is} - a^s_i, \qquad \Delta^{dep}_{is} \ge d_{is} - d^s_i
\qquad \forall i\in T,\ s\in S
$$

### 6.2 Rerouting and disruption constraints

**(C5) Reroute only in the disruption segment, only during the window:**
$$
r_{i\ell} = 0 \qquad \forall i\in T,\ \ell\in L\setminus\{\ell^\ast\}
$$
$$
a_{i\ell} \ge T^s \ \wedge\ d_{i\ell}\le T^e \ \Longrightarrow\ \text{(feasible via Big-}M\text{ below)}
$$
A train that is fully inside the disruption window on the blocked track is infeasible, hence it must either reroute or shift out of the window. Linearized as: if train $i$ is scheduled to pass $\ell^\ast$ inside $[T^s,T^e]$ on its nominal (blocked) track, then
$$
a_{i\ell^\ast} \le T^s + M(1-r_{i\ell^\ast}) + M\beta_i, \qquad
d_{i\ell^\ast} \ge T^e - M(1-r_{i\ell^\ast}) - M\beta_i
$$
where $\beta_i\in\{0,1\}=1$ allows the train to wait until after $T^e$ on the nominal track.

**(C6) Cancellation propagation:** if $c_i=1$, all movement variables are free and the train does not occupy resources:
$$
q_{i\ell} \le 1-c_i \qquad \forall i\in T,\ \ell\in L
$$

### 6.3 Conflict-free operations (bidirectional headways)

**(C7) Segment headway, same track (both directions may share via rerouting):**
For all ordered pairs $i,j$ and $\ell$:
$$
d_{j\ell} \ge a_{i\ell} + h_{\ell} - M\bigl(1 - y_{ij\ell}\bigr) - M\,r_{j\ell} - M(1-r_{i\ell})
$$
$$
d_{i\ell} \ge a_{j\ell} + h_{\ell} - M\, y_{ij\ell} - M\,r_{i\ell} - M(1-r_{i\ell})
$$
i.e., headway is enforced only when **both** trains use the same track ($r_{i\ell}=r_{j\ell}$); $y_{ij\ell}$ selects the ordering (this handles bidirectional conflicts on the shared track).

**(C8) Pairwise ordering consistency (substitution to strengthen):**
$$
y_{ij\ell} + y_{ji\ell} = r_{i\ell}\cdot r_{j\ell}\ \text{(linearized via } g_{ij\ell}\ge r_{i\ell}+r_{j\ell}-1,\ y_{ij\ell}+y_{ji\ell}\ge g_{ij\ell})
$$

**(C9) Station arrival/departure headways and platform capacity:** for ordered pairs at station $s$:
$$
a_{js} \ge a_{is} + \tau^{arr}_s - M(1-z_{ijs}), \qquad
a_{is} \ge a_{js} + \tau^{arr}_s - M z_{ijs}
$$
Platform occupancy: at most $U^s$ trains dwell simultaneously (enforced via standard pairwise or time-indexed occupancy constraints; omitted for brevity — standard).

**(C10) Overtaking consistency (first-order / no overtake within segment):** guaranteed by (C7) with $y$ fixed per segment; overtaking is possible only at stations, since segment headways are enforced between consecutive occupancies.

### 6.4 Variable domains
$$
a_{is}, d_{is}, \Delta^{arr}_{is}, \Delta^{dep}_{is} \ge 0;\quad
x^p_{i\ell}, r_{i\ell}, y_{ij\ell}, z_{ijs}, c_i, \beta_i, q_{i\ell}\in\{0,1\}
$$

---

## 7. Remarks on Validity and Solution (as in the source paper)

- **Equivalence of timetable and speed profiles:** Constraint (C1)+(C3) ensures that the selected arrival/departure times are *exactly* consistent with an executable speed profile from the underlying TSMP, i.e., every solution of the MILP corresponds to a feasible driving strategy, and vice versa (discretized profiles).
- **Conflict-free guarantee:** Constraints (C7)–(C9) ensure no two trains occupy the same track resource within the headway time, covering bidirectional conflicts arising from rerouting on the opposite track.
- **Decomposition:** For solution, the MILP decomposes into (i) a reformulated IP over train interactions ($y,z,r,c$) and (ii) per-train plan selection problems ($x^p_{i\ell}$, timing), solved by an adaptive iterative refinement of plan granularity with local branching, which converges to the MILP optimum with sufficiently fine plan intervals.

# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Below is the complete mathematical formulation of the integrated MILP model for the TRSMP under partial segment blockages.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $B$ | Set of blocks (track segments), indexed by $b$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $K$ | Set of discretized time intervals, indexed by $k$ |
| $D = \{1,2\}$ | Direction set: 1 = nominal, 2 = opposite (diverted) |
| $R \subseteq B$ | Set of disrupted blocks |
| $K^{dis} = [k^{dis}_s, k^{dis}_e]$ | Disruption time interval indices |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ (m) |
| $V^{max}, V^{min}$ | Maximum / minimum speed (m/s) |
| $a^{+}, a^{-}$ | Maximum traction / braking acceleration (m/s²) |
| $\tau^{dwell}$ | Minimum dwell time at stations (s) |
| $\tau^{hd}$ | Minimum headway time between trains (s) |
| $\Delta t$ | Length of time interval (s) |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (Big-M) |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3$ | Weights for delay, energy, and cancellation |
| $\rho$ | Aerodynamic resistance coefficient |
| $m_i$ | Mass of train $i$ (kg) |
| $\eta$ | Regenerative braking efficiency |
| $d_i^s, a_i^s$ | Scheduled departure / arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\theta^{cancel}$ | Delay threshold for cancellation eligibility (s) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Binary variables:**
- $x_{i,b,d} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ traverses block $b$ in direction $d$
- $y_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on block $b$
- $z_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is rerouted on block $b$ (uses opposite track)
- $c_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled
- $u_{i,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ occupies block $b$ at interval $k$
- $\sigma_{i,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ enters block $b$ at interval $k$

**Continuous variables:**
- $t^{arr}_{i,s}, t^{dep}_{i,s} \geq 0$: actual arrival/departure time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $v_{i,b,k} \in [V^{min}, V^{max}]$: speed of train $i$ on block $b$ at interval $k$
- $p_{i,b,k} \in [0, L_b]$: position of train $i$ on block $b$ at interval $k$
- $a_{i,b,k} \in [-a^{-}, a^{+}]$: acceleration of train $i$ on block $b$ at interval $k$
- $e_{i,b,k} \geq 0$: energy consumption of train $i$ on block $b$ at interval $k$
- $\delta^{arr}_{i,s}, \delta^{dep}_{i,s} \geq 0$: arrival/departure delay of train $i$ at station $s$
- $t^{ent}_{i,b}, t^{ext}_{i,b} \geq 0$: entry/exit time of train $i$ to/from block $b$
- $w_{i,b,k} \geq 0$: auxiliary variable equal to $v_{i,b,k}^2$ (for linearization)

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the total weighted cost combining delay, energy consumption, and cancellations:

$$\min Z = w_1 \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \left( \delta^{arr}_{i,s} + \delta^{dep}_{i,s} \right) + w_2 \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{b \in B} \sum_{k \in K} e_{i,b,k} + w_3 \sum_{i \in T} c_i$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Flow and Timetable Constraints

**Dwell time at intermediate stations** (for all $i \in T$, $s \in S \setminus \{s^{last}\}$):
$$t^{dep}_{i,s} = t^{arr}_{i,s} + \tau^{dwell}$$

**Running time between consecutive stations** (for all $i \in T$, $s \in S \setminus \{s^{last}\}$, with $b$ being the block connecting $s$ and $s+1$):
$$t^{arr}_{i,s+1} = t^{dep}_{i,s} + \sum_{k \in K} \Delta t \cdot u_{i,b,k}$$

**Delay definition:**
$$\delta^{arr}_{i,s} \geq t^{arr}_{i,s} - a_i^s, \quad \delta^{dep}_{i,s} \geq t^{dep}_{i,s} - d_i^s$$
$$\delta^{arr}_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad \delta^{dep}_{i,s} \geq 0$$

**Initial and terminal conditions:**
$$t^{dep}_{i,s^{first}} \geq d_i^{s^{first}}, \quad t^{arr}_{i,s^{last}} \geq a_i^{s^{last}}$$

---

### 5.2 Block Traversal and Rerouting Constraints

**Each train traverses each block exactly once** (or is cancelled):
$$\sum_{d \in D} x_{i,b,d} + c_i = 1, \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B$$

**Rerouting constraint on disrupted blocks** (for all $i \in T$, $b \in R$):
$$\sum_{d \in D} d \cdot x_{i,b,d} = 1 + z_{i,b}$$

**No rerouting on non-disrupted blocks** (for all $i \in T$, $b \in B \setminus R$):
$$z_{i,b} = 0, \quad x_{i,b,2} = 0$$

**Linking rerouting to occupancy:**
$$z_{i,b} \leq \sum_{k \in K^{dis}} u_{i,b,k} + M \cdot c_i, \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in R$$

---

### 5.3 Block Capacity and Conflict Resolution

**Single train per block per time interval:**
$$\sum_{i \in T} u_{i,b,k} \leq 1, \quad \forall b \in B, \; k \in K$$

**Train ordering on blocks** (for all $i,j \in T$, $i < j$, $b \in B$):
$$y_{i,j,b} + y_{j,i,b} = 1$$

**Headway constraint based on ordering:**
$$t^{ext}_{i,b} + \tau^{hd} \leq t^{ent}_{j,b} + M(1 - y_{i,j,b})$$
$$t^{ext}_{j,b} + \tau^{hd} \leq t^{ent}_{i,b} + M \cdot y_{i,j,b}$$

**Bidirectional conflict on shared (rerouted) track** (for all $i,j \in T$, $b \in R$):
$$u_{i,b,k} + u_{j,b,k} \leq 1 + M(2 - z_{i,b} - z_{j,b}), \quad \forall k \in K$$

---

### 5.4 Entry/Exit Time Linking Constraints

**Entry time definition:**
$$t^{ent}_{i,b} = \sum_{k \in K} k \cdot \Delta t \cdot \sigma_{i,b,k}$$

**Exit time definition:**
$$t^{ext}_{i,b} = \sum_{k \in K} k \cdot \Delta t \cdot (u_{i,b,k} - u_{i,b,k-1} + u_{i,b,k^{last}})$$

**Entry-occupancy linking:**
$$\sigma_{i,b,k} \geq u_{i,b,k} - u_{i,b,k-1}, \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$
$$\sum_{k \in K} \sigma_{i,b,k} = x_{i,b,1} + x_{i,b,2}$$

---

### 5.5 Disruption Time Window Constraints

**Trains cannot occupy disrupted blocks during disruption** (unless rerouted):
$$u_{i,r,k} \leq z_{i,r}, \quad \forall i \in T, \; r \in R, \; k \in K^{dis}$$

**Disrupted block capacity during disruption:**
$$\sum_{i \in T} u_{i,r,k} \leq |D|, \quad \forall r \in R, \; k \in K^{dis}$$

---

### 5.6 Speed Profile Dynamics

**Speed evolution (kinematic equation):**
$$v_{i,b,k+1} = v_{i,b,k} + a_{i,b,k} \cdot \Delta t, \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K \setminus \{k^{last}\}$$

**Position evolution:**
$$p_{i,b,k+1} = p_{i,b,k} + v_{i,b,k} \cdot \Delta t + \tfrac{1}{2} a_{i,b,k} \cdot \Delta t^2$$

**Speed bounds:**
$$V^{min} \leq v_{i,b,k} \leq V^{max}$$

**Acceleration bounds:**
$$-a^{-} \leq a_{i,b,k} \leq a^{+}$$

**Block length completion:**
$$\sum_{k \in K} v_{i,b,k} \cdot \Delta t = L_b \cdot \left( \sum_{d \in D} x_{i,b,d} \right)$$

**Auxiliary variable linearization** (McCormick envelopes):
$$w_{i,b,k} \geq 2 V^{min} \cdot v_{i,b,k} - (V^{min})^2$$
$$w_{i,b,k} \geq 2 V^{max} \cdot v_{i,b,k} - (V^{max})^2$$
$$w_{i,b,k} \leq V^{min} \cdot v_{i,b,k} + V^{max} \cdot v_{i,b,k} - V^{min} \cdot V^{max}$$

---

### 5.7 Energy Consumption Constraints

**Traction energy (Davis equation linearization):**
$$e_{i,b,k} = m_i \cdot \left( \rho \cdot w_{i,b,k} + a_{i,b,k} \cdot v_{i,b,k} \right) \cdot \Delta t$$

**Regenerative braking recovery:**
$$e_{i,b,k} \geq m_i \cdot \left( \rho \cdot w_{i,b,k} + a_{i,b,k} \cdot v_{i,b,k} \right) \cdot \Delta t - \eta \cdot \tfrac{1}{2} m_i \cdot |w_{i,b,k+1} - w_{i,b,k}|$$

**Non-negativity of net energy:**
$$e_{i,b,k} \geq 0$$

---

### 5.8 Cancellation Constraints

**Cancellation only when delay exceeds threshold:**
$$c_i \leq \frac{1}{\theta^{cancel}} \sum_{s \in S} \delta^{arr}_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in T$$

**If cancelled, all related variables are zero:**
$$u_{i,b,k} \leq 1 - c_i, \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$
$$x_{i,b,d} \leq 1 - c_i, \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B, \; d \in D$$

---

### 5.9 Station Headway Constraints

**Departure headway at stations** (for all $i,j \in T$, $i \neq j$, $s \in S$):
$$t^{dep}_{i,s} - t^{dep}_{j,s} \geq \tau^{hd} - M \cdot \alpha_{i,j,s}$$
$$t^{dep}_{j,s} - t^{dep}_{i,s} \geq \tau^{hd} - M \cdot (1 - \alpha_{i,j,s})$$
where $\alpha_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}$ is an auxiliary binary variable.

**Arrival headway at stations:**
$$t^{arr}_{i,s} - t^{arr}_{j,s} \geq \tau^{hd} - M \cdot \beta_{i,j,s}$$
$$t^{arr}_{j,s} - t^{arr}_{i,s} \geq \tau^{hd} - M \cdot (1 - \beta_{i,j,s})$$

---

### 5.10 Linking Speed Profile with Timetable

**Speed profile only active when train is on block:**
$$v_{i,b,k} \leq V^{max} \cdot u_{i,b,k}, \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$
$$p_{i,b,k} \leq L_b \cdot u_{i,b,k}$$

**Position continuity at block boundaries:**
$$p_{i,b,k^{last}} = L_b \cdot \sum_{d \in D} x_{i,b,d}, \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B$$

**Initial position at block entry:**
$$p_{i,b,k^{first}} = 0$$

---

## 6. Assumptions

1. **Discretization**: Time is discretized into uniform intervals of length $\Delta t$, and space (blocks) is discretized into segments.
2. **Two-track line**: The railway has two tracks (one per direction). During disruption, trains can use the opposite track.
3. **Single-track blockage**: A partial blockage disables one track in a specific segment for a defined time window.
4. **Bidirectional conflicts**: When rerouted, trains in opposite directions may conflict on the shared track, requiring precise coordination.
5. **Train homogeneity**: All trains have identical mass $m$ and aerodynamic coefficient $\rho$ (assumption for simplicity; can be indexed by $i$ if heterogeneous).
6. **Regenerative braking**: A fraction $\eta$ of kinetic energy during braking is recovered.
7. **Cancellation threshold**: Trains are only eligible for cancellation if total delay exceeds $\theta^{cancel}$.
8. **No overtaking within blocks**: Train ordering on each block is fixed once established.
9. **Speed profile feasibility**: All generated speed profiles satisfy kinematic and dynamic constraints.
10. **Disruption parameters**: The disruption time window $[t^{dis}_s, t^{dis}_e]$ and affected blocks $R$ are known in advance.

---

## 7. Model Summary

This MILP simultaneously optimizes:
- **Train times** (retiming via $t^{arr}, t^{dep}$)
- **Train orders** (reordering via $y_{i,j,b}$)
- **Train routes** (rerouting via $z_{i,b}$ and $x_{i,b,d}$)
- **Train cancellations** (via $c_i$)
- **Speed profiles** (via $v_{i,b,k}, a_{i,b,k}$)

while ensuring:
- Conflict-free bidirectional operations on shared tracks
- Feasible kinematic speed profiles
- Energy-efficient driving strategies
- Compliance with disruption time windows and operational headways

- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

Text:
# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Overview and Modeling Approach

The proposed MILP integrates the **Train Rescheduling Problem (TRP)** and the **Train Speed Management Problem (TSMP)** into a unified space-time-speed network. The model simultaneously decides:
- **Retiming**: actual arrival/departure times at stations
- **Reordering**: sequence of trains in shared track sections
- **Rerouting**: use of opposite track during disruption
- **Cancellation**: whether to cancel a train service
- **Speed profiles**: continuous speed and acceleration trajectories
- **Energy consumption**: tractive energy usage

The formulation uses a **time-indexed (discrete-time)** representation where the railway is divided into blocks (track sections) and time is discretized into intervals of duration $\Delta$.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t, t'$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^U, \mathcal{T}^D$ | Subsets of up-direction and down-direction trains |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{B}$ | Set of track blocks (sections between stations), indexed by $b$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of discrete time steps, indexed by $k$ (with $k=0$ as start) |
| $\mathcal{D} = \{U, D\}$ | Set of track directions: Up-track and Down-track |
| $\mathcal{K}^{disr} = [k^{disr}_s, k^{disr}_e]$ | Disruption time window |
| $b^{disr}$ | Disrupted block (one track blocked) |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ | m |
| $\Delta$ | Duration of a time step | s |
| $v^{\max}, v^{\min}$ | Maximum and minimum operating speeds | m/s |
| $a^{\max}, a^{\min}$ | Maximum acceleration and deceleration ($a^{\min}<0$) | m/s² |
| $T^{sch}_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ | s |
| $\tau^{\min}$ | Minimum dwell time at stations | s |
| $h^{hd}$ | Minimum headway time between consecutive trains | s |
| $\alpha_0, \alpha_1, \alpha_2$ | Energy coefficients (resistance, motoring, regenerative braking) | kWh/(m/s), kWh/(m/s²), kWh/(m/s²) |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3$ | Weights for delay, energy, and cancellation in objective | – |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (Big-M) | – |
| $v^{in}_t, v^{out}_t$ | Initial and final speed of train $t$ | m/s |
| $\ell_t$ | Length of train $t$ | m |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Discrete (Binary) Variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $x_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ occupies block $b$ at time $k$ |
| $x^{U}_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses the **up-track** of block $b$ at time $k$ |
| $x^{D}_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses the **down-track** of block $b$ at time $k$ |
| $r_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ **reroutes** (uses opposite track) in block $b$ at time $k$ |
| $y_{t,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is dwelling at station $s$ at time $k$ |
| $o_{t,t',b,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ departs block $b$ no later than train $t'$ at time $k$ (ordering) |
| $c_t \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled |

### 4.2 Continuous Variables

| Variable | Description | Unit |
|----------|-------------|------|
| $v_{t,b,k} \geq 0$ | Speed of train $t$ in block $b$ at time $k$ | m/s |
| $a_{t,b,k}$ | Acceleration of train $t$ in block $b$ at time $k$ | m/s² |
| $a^{+}_{t,b,k} \geq 0$ | Motoring (positive) acceleration component | m/s² |
| $a^{-}_{t,b,k} \geq 0$ | Braking (negative) acceleration component | m/s² |
| $p_{t,b,k} \geq 0$ | Position of train $t$ within block $b$ at time $k$ | m |
| $e_{t,b,k} \geq 0$ | Energy consumption of train $t$ in block $b$ at time $k$ | kWh |
| $A_{t,s} \geq 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ | s |
| $D_{t,s} \geq 0$ | Actual departure time of train $t$ at station $s$ | s |
| $\delta_{t,s} \geq 0$ | Delay of train $t$ at station $s$ | s |

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total passenger delay, total energy consumption, and number of cancellations:

$$
\min \; Z = w_1 \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \delta_{t,s} \;+\; w_2 \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} e_{t,b,k} \;+\; w_3 \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} c_t
$$

**Assumption**: $w_1, w_2, w_3 > 0$ are calibrated weights reflecting operational priorities (e.g., $w_1 \gg w_2 \gg w_3$ to prioritize punctuality).

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Flow Conservation (Train Location Uniqueness)

Each active train must occupy exactly one location (block or station) at each time step:

$$
\sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} x_{t,b,k} + \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} y_{t,s,k} = 1 - c_t \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K} \tag{1}
$$

### 6.2 Track Assignment Consistency

The total block occupancy equals the sum of track-specific occupancies:

$$
x^{U}_{t,b,k} + x^{D}_{t,b,k} = x_{t,b,k} \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{2}
$$

### 6.3 Rerouting Logic

For **up-direction trains** ($t \in \mathcal{T}^U$): no rerouting → up-track; rerouting → down-track.

$$
x^{U}_{t,b,k} \leq 1 - r_{t,b,k} \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}^U,\; b, k \tag{3a}
$$
$$
x^{D}_{t,b,k} \leq r_{t,b,k} \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}^U,\; b, k \tag{3b}
$$

For **down-direction trains** ($t \in \mathcal{T}^D$): no rerouting → down-track; rerouting → up-track.

$$
x^{D}_{t,b,k} \leq 1 - r_{t,b,k} \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}^D,\; b, k \tag{3c}
$$
$$
x^{U}_{t,b,k} \leq r_{t,b,k} \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}^D,\; b, k \tag{3d}
$$

### 6.4 Bidirectional Track Capacity (Conflict Resolution)

Each track of each block can be used by at most one train at any time:

$$
\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} x^{U}_{t,b,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall b \in \mathcal{B},\; k \in \mathcal{K} \tag{4a}
$$
$$
\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} x^{D}_{t,b,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall b \in \mathcal{B},\; k \in \mathcal{K} \tag{4b}
$$

### 6.5 Disruption Constraints

Assume the **up-track** of block $b^{disr}$ is blocked during $[k^{disr}_s, k^{disr}_e]$. No train may use the up-track during this window:

$$
x^{U}_{t,b^{disr},k} = 0 \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}^{disr} \tag{5}
$$

Consequently, any up-direction train traversing $b^{disr}$ during the disruption window is forced to reroute (via constraints 3a–3b).

### 6.6 Kinematic Equations (Train Dynamics)

**Position update** (assuming constant acceleration within interval):

$$
p_{t,b,k+1} = p_{t,b,k} + v_{t,b,k} \cdot \Delta + \tfrac{1}{2} a_{t,b,k} \cdot \Delta^2 \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{6}
$$

**Speed update**:

$$
v_{t,b,k+1} = v_{t,b,k} + a_{t,b,k} \cdot \Delta \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{7}
$$

### 6.7 Speed and Acceleration Limits

$$
v^{\min} \cdot x_{t,b,k} \leq v_{t,b,k} \leq v^{\max} \cdot x_{t,b,k} \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{8}
$$

**Acceleration decomposition**:

$$
a_{t,b,k} = a^{+}_{t,b,k} - a^{-}_{t,b,k} \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{9a}
$$
$$
a^{+}_{t,b,k} \leq a^{\max} \cdot x_{t,b,k} \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{9b}
$$
$$
a^{-}_{t,b,k} \leq -a^{\min} \cdot x_{t,b,k} \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{9c}
$$

### 6.8 Block Entry/Exit and Position Bounds

A train's position within a block is bounded by the block length, and is zero when the train is not in the block:

$$
0 \leq p_{t,b,k} \leq L_b \cdot x_{t,b,k} \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{10}
$$

**Block transition** (train must traverse the full block length to exit):

$$
p_{t,b,k} \geq L_b - M(1 - x_{t,b,k+1}) - M(1 - x_{t,b,k}) \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{11}
$$

### 6.9 Station Dwell Time

$$
D_{t,s} - A_{t,s} \geq \tau^{\min} \cdot y_{t,s,k} \quad \forall t, s, k \tag{12}
$$

### 6.10 Delay Definition

$$
\delta_{t,s} \geq A_{t,s} - T^{sch}_{t,s} \quad \forall t, s \tag{13a}
$$
$$
\delta_{t,s} \geq 0 \quad \forall t, s \tag{13b}
$$

### 6.11 Headway Constraints (Safety Separation)

For any two trains $t, t'$ sharing the same track of block $b$, their departures must be separated by at least $h^{hd}$:

$$
A_{t,s} + h^{hd} \leq A_{t',s} + M(1 - o_{t,t',s}) \quad \forall t \neq t', s \tag{14a}
$$
$$
o_{t,t',s} + o_{t',t,s} = 1 \quad \forall t \neq t', s \tag{14b}
$$

### 6.12 Energy Consumption Model

A linearized energy model assuming tractive energy is proportional to motoring effort and regenerative braking recovers energy:

$$
e_{t,b,k} = \alpha_0 \cdot v_{t,b,k} \cdot \Delta + \alpha_1 \cdot a^{+}_{t,b,k} \cdot \Delta - \alpha_2 \cdot a^{-}_{t,b,k} \cdot \Delta \quad \forall t, b, k \tag{15}
$$

**Assumption**: $\alpha_2 < \alpha_1$ (regenerative braking is less efficient than motoring).

### 6.13 Initial and Terminal Conditions

$$
v_{t,b,0} = v^{in}_t \cdot x_{t,b,0} \quad \forall t, b \tag{16a}
$$
$$
p_{t,b,0} = 0 \quad \forall t, b \tag{16b}
$$
$$
v_{t,b,|\mathcal{K}|} = v^{out}_t \cdot x_{t,b,|\mathcal{K}|} \quad \forall t, b \tag{16c}
$$

### 6.14 Cancellation Logic

If a train is cancelled, all its operational variables are zero:

$$
x_{t,b,k} \leq 1 - c_t, \quad y_{t,s,k} \leq 1 - c_t \quad \forall t, b, s, k \tag{17}
$$

### 6.15 Train Length and Block Occupancy (Safety)

To prevent two trains from occupying overlapping sections of the same block (assuming block length exceeds train length):

$$
x_{t,b,k} + x_{t',b,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall t \neq t', b, k \text{ (same track)} \tag{18}
$$

This is already implied by constraints (4a)–(4b) when trains use the same track.

---

## 7. Model Summary

The complete MILP is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & w_1 \sum_{t,s} \delta_{t,s} + w_2 \sum_{t,b,k} e_{t,b,k} + w_3 \sum_t c_t \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{Constraints (1)–(18)} \\
& x_{t,b,k}, x^{U}_{t,b,k}, x^{D}_{t,b,k}, r_{t,b,k}, y_{t,s,k}, o_{t,t',b,k}, c_t \in \{0,1\} \\
& v_{t,b,k}, p_{t,b,k}, e_{t,b,k}, A_{t,s}, D_{t,s}, \delta_{t,s}, a^{+}_{t,b,k}, a^{-}_{t,b,k} \geq 0 \\
& a_{t,b,k} \text{ free}
\end{aligned}
$$

---

## 8. Key Assumptions

1. **Double-track line**: The railway has two parallel tracks (up and down). Normal operation segregates directions.
2. **Single-side disruption**: Only one track of the disrupted block is blocked; the other remains operational but must be shared bidirectionally.
3. **Discrete time**: Time is discretized into intervals of length $\Delta$. The granularity must be sufficiently fine to capture speed profile dynamics (typically $\Delta = 10$–$30$ s).
4. **Block structure**: The line is partitioned into blocks between stations (or signaling points). Trains are assumed to fit within one block at a time.
5. **Constant acceleration within intervals**: The kinematic equations use a piecewise-constant acceleration approximation.
6. **Linear energy model**: Energy consumption is linearized as a function of speed and acceleration components, suitable for MILP solvability.
7. **No train overtaking within a block**: Reordering is permitted at stations and block boundaries, not within blocks.
8. **Homogeneous trains**: All trains have similar kinematic parameters ($v^{\max}, a^{\max}, a^{\min}$) unless differentiated by additional parameters.
9. **Deterministic disruption**: The disruption time window and location are known with certainty.
10. **Fixed train routes (except for rerouting)**: The sequence of blocks each train traverses is predetermined; only the track choice (original vs. opposite) is a decision variable.

---

## 9. Remarks on Computational Tractability

The full MILP contains $O(|\mathcal{T}|^2 \cdot |\mathcal{B}| \cdot |\mathcal{K}|)$ binary variables and is NP-hard in general. For practical large-scale instances, the authors' companion **decomposition method** (reformulating as an Integer Programming model with interval plans, solved via an adaptive iterative algorithm with local branching) is recommended. The MILP above serves as the **exact reference formulation** whose optimal value provides a benchmark for evaluating the heuristic solution quality.

Text:
# MILP Formulation for Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $tr \in \{1,\dots,T\}$ |
| $\mathcal{I}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $i \in \{1,\dots,N\}$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of segments, indexed by $s \in \{1,\dots,N-1\}$; segment $s$ connects station $i$ to $i+1$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of discretized time steps, indexed by $k \in \{1,\dots,K\}$ |
| $\mathcal{B}$ | Set of spatial blocks, indexed by $b \in \{1,\dots,B_s\}$ |
| $\mathcal{W}$ | Disruption window $\{k_w^{start},\dots,k_w^{end}\}$ on segment $d$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^+,\mathcal{T}^-$ | Trains traveling in forward / reverse direction |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $v_{\max}$ | Maximum allowed speed | m/s |
| $a_{\max}, b_{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration | m/s² |
| $M_{tr}$ | Mass of train $tr$ | kg |
| $\Delta t, \Delta x$ | Time step duration / spatial block length | s, m |
| $\tau_{dwell}$ | Minimum dwell time at stations | s |
| $\tau_{headway}$ | Minimum headway time | s |
| $L_s$ | Length of segment $s$ | m |
| $t^{a}_{tr,i}, t^{d}_{tr,i}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure time of train $tr$ at station $i$ | s |
| $\delta_{tr}$ | Direction of train $tr$ ($+1$ forward, $-1$ reverse) | – |
| $\alpha$ | Traction energy coefficient | J/(N·m) |
| $\beta$ | Regenerative braking recovery factor | – |
| $\gamma_d, \gamma_e$ | Weights for delay / energy in objective | – |
| $C$ | Station platform capacity | trains |
| $M_{big}$ | Large positive constant (big-M) | – |
| $\eta$ | Drivetrain efficiency | – |

## 3. Decision Variables

### Binary Variables
$$
\begin{aligned}
x_{tr,i,k} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } tr \text{ arrives at station } i \text{ at time } k \\
y_{tr,i,k} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } tr \text{ departs station } i \text{ at time } k \\
z_{tr,s,b,k} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } tr \text{ is in block } b \text{ of segment } s \text{ at time } k \\
r_{tr,s,k} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } tr \text{ uses rerouted (opposite) track on segment } s \text{ at time } k \\
o_{tr_1,tr_2,i} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } tr_1 \text{ departs station } i \text{ before train } tr_2 \\
u^{acc}_{tr,s,b,k} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } tr \text{ accelerates (} a \geq 0\text{) in block } b \text{ at time } k \\
u^{brk}_{tr,s,b,k} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } tr \text{ brakes (} a \leq 0\text{) in block } b \text{ at time } k \\
\phi_{tr,s,b,k} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } tr \text{ occupies block } b \text{ of segment } s \text{ at time } k \text{ (conflict variable)} \\
\end{aligned}
$$

### Continuous Variables
$$
\begin{aligned}
v_{tr,s,b,k} &\geq 0 && \text{Speed of train } tr \text{ in block } b \text{ of segment } s \text{ at time } k \quad [\text{m/s}] \\
a_{tr,s,b,k} &&& \text{Acceleration of train } tr \text{ in block } b \text{ of segment } s \text{ at time } k \quad [\text{m/s}^2] \\
a^{+}_{tr,s,b,k}, a^{-}_{tr,s,b,k} &\geq 0 && \text{Positive / negative parts of acceleration} \\
p_{tr,s,b,k} &\geq 0 && \text{Position within block } b \text{ of segment } s \text{ at time } k \quad [\text{m}] \\
w^{acc}_{tr,s,b,k}, w^{brk}_{tr,s,b,k} &\geq 0 && \text{Auxiliary products } a^{+} \cdot v,\; a^{-} \cdot v \\
e^{trac}_{tr,s,b,k} &\geq 0 && \text{Traction energy} \quad [\text{J}] \\
e^{brk}_{tr,s,b,k} &\geq 0 && \text{Regenerative braking energy} \quad [\text{J}] \\
\tau^{a}_{tr,i}, \tau^{d}_{tr,i} &\geq 0 && \text{Actual arrival / departure time of train } tr \text{ at station } i \quad [\text{s}] \\
\Delta^{a}_{tr,i}, \Delta^{d}_{tr,i} &\geq 0 && \text{Arrival / departure delay} \quad [\text{s}] \\
E_{total} &\geq 0 && \text{Total net energy consumption} \quad [\text{J}]
\end{aligned}
$$

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \gamma_d \sum_{tr \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \Delta^{a}_{tr,i} \;+\; \gamma_d \sum_{tr \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \Delta^{d}_{tr,i} \;+\; \gamma_e \cdot E_{total}
$$

where
$$
E_{total} \;=\; \sum_{tr \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \left( e^{trac}_{tr,s,b,k} \;-\; \beta \cdot e^{brk}_{tr,s,b,k} \right)
$$

The objective balances **minimizing passenger delays** (arrival + departure) against **minimizing net energy consumption** (traction minus recovered braking).

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Dynamics (Linear Motion Equations)

For all $tr \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S},\; b \in \mathcal{B},\; k \in \mathcal{K} \setminus \{K\}$:

$$
p_{tr,s,b,k+1} \;=\; p_{tr,s,b,k} \;+\; v_{tr,s,b,k} \cdot \Delta t \;+\; \tfrac{1}{2} \, a_{tr,s,b,k} \cdot \Delta t^{2}
\tag{D1}
$$

$$
v_{tr,s,b,k+1} \;=\; v_{tr,s,b,k} \;+\; a_{tr,s,b,k} \cdot \Delta t
\tag{D2}
$$

These are **linear** in $v$ and $a$ (no products), so they remain MILP-compatible.

### 5.2 Speed and Acceleration Bounds

$$
0 \;\leq\; v_{tr,s,b,k} \;\leq\; v_{\max}
\tag{B1}
$$

$$
-b_{\max} \;\leq\; a_{tr,s,b,k} \;\leq\; a_{\max}
\tag{B2}
$$

Decomposition of acceleration:
$$
a_{tr,s,b,k} \;=\; a^{+}_{tr,s,b,k} \;-\; a^{-}_{tr,s,b,k}
\tag{B3}
$$

$$
0 \;\leq\; a^{+}_{tr,s,b,k} \;\leq\; a_{\max} \cdot u^{acc}_{tr,s,b,k}
\tag{B4}
$$

$$
0 \;\leq\; a^{-}_{tr,s,b,k} \;\leq\; b_{\max} \cdot u^{brk}_{tr,s,b,k}
\tag{B5}
$$

$$
u^{acc}_{tr,s,b,k} \;+\; u^{brk}_{tr,s,b,k} \;=\; 1
\tag{B6}
$$

### 5.3 Block Occupancy (Each Train in Exactly One Location)

For all $tr \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S},\; k \in \mathcal{K}$:
$$
\sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} z_{tr,s,b,k} \;\leq\; 1
\tag{O1}
$$

For all $tr \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}$:
$$
\sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} z_{tr,s,b,k} \;+\; \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \left( x_{tr,i,k} + y_{tr,i,k} \right) \;=\; 1
\tag{O2}
$$

> **Interpretation:** At every time step, each train is either at a station (arriving or departing) or in exactly one block of one segment.

### 5.4 Position Within Block

For all $tr, s, b, k$:
$$
0 \;\leq\; p_{tr,s,b,k} \;\leq\; \Delta x \cdot z_{tr,s,b,k}
\tag{P1}
$$

**Block transition** (train moves forward in its direction):
$$
p_{tr,s,b,k} \;\geq\; \Delta x - M_{big}\left(1 - z_{tr,s,b,k} + z_{tr,s,b+\delta_{tr},k+1}\right)
\tag{P2}
$$

$$
z_{tr,s,b+\delta_{tr},k+1} \;\geq\; z_{tr,s,b,k} - M_{big}\left(1 - \mathbb{1}[p_{tr,s,b,k} \geq \Delta x]\right)
$$

(Implemented via big-M with auxiliary binary $\psi_{tr,s,b,k}$ indicating block exit.)

### 5.5 Station Arrival and Departure

For all $tr \in \mathcal{T},\; i \in \mathcal{I}$:
$$
\tau^{a}_{tr,i} \;=\; \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} k \cdot \Delta t \cdot x_{tr,i,k}
\tag{S1}
$$

$$
\tau^{d}_{tr,i} \;=\; \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} k \cdot \Delta t \cdot y_{tr,i,k}
\tag{S2}
$$

**Departure after arrival:**
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} y_{tr,i,k} \;\leq\; \sum_{k' \geq k} x_{tr,i,k'} \quad \forall k
\tag{S3}
$$

**Minimum dwell time:**
$$
\tau^{d}_{tr,i} \;-\; \tau^{a}_{tr,i} \;\geq\; \tau_{dwell}
\tag{S4}
$$

**Flow conservation at stations** (each train arrives and departs each station once):
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} x_{tr,i,k} \;=\; \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} y_{tr,i,k} \;=\; 1
\tag{S5}
$$

### 5.6 Delay Calculation

For all $tr \in \mathcal{T},\; i \in \mathcal{I}$:
$$
\Delta^{a}_{tr,i} \;\geq\; \tau^{a}_{tr,i} \;-\; t^{a}_{tr,i}, \qquad \Delta^{a}_{tr,i} \;\geq\; 0
\tag{DL1}
$$

$$
\Delta^{d}_{tr,i} \;\geq\; \tau^{d}_{tr,i} \;-\; t^{d}_{tr,i}, \qquad \Delta^{d}_{tr,i} \;\geq\; 0
\tag{DL2}
$$

### 5.7 Disruption Constraints (Segment $d$, Window $\mathcal{W}$)

**No train on original track during disruption:**
$$
z_{tr,d,b,k} \;+\; r_{tr,d,k} \;\leq\; 1 \qquad \forall tr,\; b,\; k \in \mathcal{W}
\tag{DS1}
$$

**No rerouting outside disruption window:**
$$
r_{tr,d,k} \;=\; 0 \qquad \forall tr,\; k \notin \mathcal{W}
\tag{DS2}
$$

**Rerouting only at allowed segments:**
$$
r_{tr,s,k} \;=\; 0 \qquad \forall tr,\; s \neq d,\; k
\tag{DS3}
$$

### 5.8 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution on Rerouted Track

For any two trains $tr_1, tr_2$ with $\delta_{tr_1} \neq \delta_{tr_2}$ on segment $d$ during $k \in \mathcal{W}$:
$$
z_{tr_1,d,b,k} \;+\; z_{tr_2,d,b,k} \;+\; r_{tr_1,d,k} \;+\; r_{tr_2,d,k} \;\leq\; 2
\tag{CR1}
$$

**Same-block conflict (no two trains in same block at same time):**
$$
\phi_{tr_1,s,b,k} \;+\; \phi_{tr_2,s,b,k} \;\leq\; 1 \qquad \forall tr_1 \neq tr_2,\; s,b,k
\tag{CR2}
$$

where $\phi_{tr,s,b,k} \geq z_{tr,s,b,k} - M_{big}(1 - z_{tr,s,b,k})$ (active iff train is in block).

### 5.9 Headway Constraints (Same Direction, Same Track)

For consecutive trains $tr_1, tr_2$ on segment $s$ with $\delta_{tr_1} = \delta_{tr_2}$:
$$
\tau^{a}_{tr_2, i+1} \;-\; \tau^{d}_{tr_1, i+1} \;\geq\; \tau_{headway} \;-\; M_{big}\left(1 - o_{tr_1,tr_2,i+1}\right)
\tag{HW1}
$$

$$
o_{tr_1,tr_2,i} \;+\; o_{tr_2,tr_1,i} \;=\; 1 \qquad \forall tr_1 \neq tr_2,\; i
\tag{HW2}
$$

### 5.10 Station Capacity

For all $i \in \mathcal{I},\; k \in \mathcal{K}$:
$$
\sum_{tr \in \mathcal{T}} \left( x_{tr,i,k} + y_{tr,i,k} \right) \;\leq\; C
\tag{SC1}
$$

### 5.11 Energy Consumption (McCormick Linearization)

**Auxiliary product** $w^{acc}_{tr,s,b,k} = a^{+}_{tr,s,b,k} \cdot v_{tr,s,b,k}$:

$$
w^{acc}_{tr,s,b,k} \;\geq\; a^{+}_{tr,s,b,k} \cdot v_{\min} \;+\; v_{tr,s,b,k} \cdot 0 \;-\; v_{\min} \cdot 0
\tag{E1}
$$

$$
w^{acc}_{tr,s,b,k} \;\geq\; a^{+}_{tr,s,b,k} \cdot v_{\max} \;+\; v_{tr,s,b,k} \cdot a_{\max} \;-\; v_{\max} \cdot a_{\max}
\tag{E2}
$$

$$
w^{acc}_{tr,s,b,k} \;\leq\; a^{+}_{tr,s,b,k} \cdot v_{\max} \;+\; v_{tr,s,b,k} \cdot 0 \;-\; v_{\max} \cdot 0
\tag{E3}
$$

$$
w^{acc}_{tr,s,b,k} \;\leq\; a^{+}_{tr,s,b,k} \cdot 0 \;+\; v_{tr,s,b,k} \cdot a_{\max} \;-\; 0 \cdot a_{\max}
\tag{E4}
$$

Analogous constraints for $w^{brk}_{tr,s,b,k} = a^{-}_{tr,s,b,k} \cdot v_{tr,s,b,k}$.

**Traction energy:**
$$
e^{trac}_{tr,s,b,k} \;=\; \frac{M_{tr}}{\eta} \cdot w^{acc}_{tr,s,b,k} \cdot \Delta t
\tag{E5}
$$

**Braking (regenerative) energy:**
$$
e^{brk}_{tr,s,b,k} \;=\; \frac{M_{tr}}{\eta} \cdot w^{brk}_{tr,s,b,k} \cdot \Delta t
\tag{E6}
$$

### 5.12 Initial and Final Conditions

**Initial position** (each train at origin station at $k=1$):
$$
x_{tr, i^{orig}_{tr}, 1} \;=\; 1, \qquad y_{tr, i^{orig}_{tr}, 1} \;=\; 0
\tag{IC1}
$$

**Final position** (each train reaches destination by $k=K$):
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} x_{tr, i^{dest}_{tr}, k} \;=\; 1
\tag{IC2}
$$

**Initial speed = 0:**
$$
v_{tr,s,b,1} \;=\; 0 \qquad \forall tr,s,b
\tag{IC3}
$$

### 5.13 Rerouting Transition

Rerouting flag can only change at station boundaries:
$$
r_{tr,d,k} \;-\; r_{tr,d,k-1} \;\leq\; \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \left( x_{tr,i,k} + y_{tr,i,k} \right) \;+\; M_{big}\left(1 - r_{tr,d,k}\right)
\tag{RT1}
$$

$$
r_{tr,d,k-1} \;-\; r_{tr,d,k} \;\leq\; \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \left( x_{tr,i,k} + y_{tr,i,k} \right) \;+\; M_{big} \cdot r_{tr,d,k}
\tag{RT2}
$$

> **Interpretation:** A train can only enter or exit the rerouted section while stopped at a station.

### 5.14 Segment Connectivity (Flow Between Segments)

For all $tr \in \mathcal{T},\; i \in \mathcal{I}$:
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} y_{tr,i,k} \cdot \delta_{tr} \;=\; \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} x_{tr,i+1,k} \cdot \delta_{tr} \qquad \text{(forward)}
\tag{FC1}
$$

$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} y_{tr,i,k} \cdot \delta_{tr} \;=\; \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} x_{tr,i-1,k} \cdot \delta_{tr} \qquad \text{(reverse)}
\tag{FC2}
$$
