| Component | Type | Linear? | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| Objective | Linear | ✅ | Weighted sum of delays and net energy |
| Dynamics (D1, D2) | Linear | ✅ | Position/speed updates |
| Bounds (B1–B6) | Linear | ✅ | Speed/acceleration limits |
| Occupancy (O1, O2) | Linear | ✅ | One location per train per time |
| Position (P1, P2) | Big-M | ✅ | Block transitions |
| Station (S1–S5) | Linear | ✅ | Arrival/departure/dwell |
| Delay (DL1, DL2) | Linear | ✅ | Delay definitions |
| Disruption (DS1–DS3) | Linear | ✅ | Blocked segment logic |
| Conflict (CR1, CR2) | Linear | ✅ | Bidirectional safety |
| Headway (HW1, HW2) | Big-M | ✅ | Minimum time gap |
| Capacity (SC1) | Linear | ✅ | Platform limits |
| Energy (E1–E6) | McCormick | ✅ | Bilinear product relaxation |
| Initial/Final (IC1–IC3) | Linear | ✅ | Boundary conditions |
| Rerouting (RT1, RT2) | Big-M | ✅ | Transition at stations |

## 7. Explanation of Key Modeling Choices

1. **Time–space discretization** ($\Delta t, \Delta x$) converts the continuous train dynamics into a discrete MILP. The motion equations (D1, D2) are linear because they contain no $v \cdot a$ products — only $v$ and $a$ separately.

2. **Binary occupancy variables** $z_{tr,s,b,k}$ enforce that each train occupies exactly one spatial block at each time step. This is essential for **conflict detection** between trains.

3. **McCormick envelopes** (E1–E4) linearize the bilinear term $a^{+} \cdot v$ that appears in the energy model. This is the standard MILP relaxation; tighter bounds can be obtained by partitioning $v$ into intervals (piecewise McCormick).

4. **Big-M constraints** are used wherever a logical condition must be enforced (e.g., "departure only after arrival", "block transition only when position reaches $\Delta x$", "rerouting changes only at stations"). The value of $M_{big}$ should be chosen as small as possible for solver performance.

5. **Ordering variables** $o_{tr_1,tr_2,i}$ resolve conflicts when multiple trains compete for the same station at overlapping times, ensuring a well-defined departure sequence.

6. **Disruption handling** uses a separate binary $r_{tr,s,k}$ that activates only during window $\mathcal{W}$ on segment $d$, forcing trains onto the opposite track. Transition constraints (RT1, RT2) ensure trains can only switch tracks at stations, respecting signaling reality.

7. **The objective** is a Pareto-style weighted combination. By varying $\gamma_d$ and $\gamma_e$, the dispatcher can trade off punctuality against energy efficiency.

## 8. Assumptions Made

The following assumptions were introduced due to missing details in the original problem description:

- **Single double-track line** with $N$ stations indexed $i=1,\dots,N$.
- **Segments** indexed $s=1,\dots,N-1$ between consecutive stations.
- **Time horizon discretized** into $K$ time steps of duration $\Delta t$.
- **Space discretized** into blocks of length $\Delta x$.
- **Uniform train characteristics**: max speed $v_{\max}$, max acceleration $a_{\max}$, max deceleration $b_{\max}$, mass $M_{tr}$.
- **Minimum dwell time** $\tau_{dwell}$ at each station.
- **Minimum headway time** $\tau_{headway}$ between consecutive trains on the same track.
- **Energy model**: traction energy proportional to force × distance, regenerative braking recovers a fraction $\beta$ of braking energy.
- **Disruption affects only one segment** $d$ during a single time window $\mathcal{W}$.
- **Rerouting only at station boundaries** (no mid-segment track switches).
- **Station capacity** $C$ (maximum simultaneous trains at a station).
- **Drivetrain efficiency** $\eta$ for energy conversion.

This MILP yields, upon solution, a **conflict-free rescheduled timetable** (via $x, y, \tau^a, \tau^d$), **feasible speed profiles** (via $v, a$), and **energy consumption** (via $e^{trac}, e^{brk}$) that jointly minimize weighted delay and energy.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

Based on the described framework (decomposition into rerouting, reordering, rescheduling; pair-wise delay interpretation; optional delay propagation), the following complete MILP is formulated. It follows the style of Pellegrini et al. (2014, 2019) with pair-wise delay variables as in Section 3.1 of the paper, extended with a propagation term (Section 3.3 variant).

---

## 1. Assumptions (explicitly marked)

- **(A1)** Macroscopic infrastructure model: the network is a set of blocks/circuits; signals, gradients and speed profiles are neglected except for minimum running times.
- **(A2)** Each train has a set of feasible routes through each station; each route occupies a fixed set of blocks for a fixed duration.
- **(A3)** Trains cannot overtake or stop outside scheduled stops unless reordering is enabled (reordering binary variables then allow sequence changes only at overtaking-capable locations).
- **(A4)** Primary delays are known at the time of optimization (deterministic, rolling-horizon dispatching).
- **(A5)** If delay propagation is neglected, a train's secondary delay is attributed to the single train it waits for (pair-wise interpretation).
- **(A6)** Safety margins (overlap behind stop signals) are treated as extended block occupancy time (Lindenmaier et al., 2022).
- **(A7)** All data are deterministic; the horizon is finite.

---

## 2. Sets and indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, index $t$ |
| $R_t$ | set of feasible routes for train $t$ |
| $B$ | set of blocks (resources), index $b$ |
| $S_t$ | ordered set of blocks visited by train $t$ on a given route |
| $P$ | set of ordered train pairs $(t_1,t_2)$ that may conflict |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $d_t^{prim}$ | primary delay of train $t$ [s] |
| $r_{t,b}^{min}$ | minimum running time of train $t$ on block $b$ |
| $h_{b}$ | headway / minimum separation time on block $b$ (incl. safety margin, A6) |
| $w_{t,b}$ | scheduled dwell/stop time of train $t$ at block $b$ |
| $a_{t,b}^{\rho}, d_{t,b}^{\rho}$ | nominal arrival/departure time of $t$ at $b$ on route $\rho \in R_t$ |
| $M$ | sufficiently large constant |
| $H$ | time horizon |

## 4. Variables

**Continuous:**
- $a_{t,b}, d_{t,b} \ge 0$ : actual arrival / departure time of train $t$ at block $b$
- $\delta_{t} \ge 0$ : total secondary delay of train $t$

**Binary:**
- $x_{t,\rho} \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $t$ uses route $\rho \in R_t$
- $y_{t_1 t_2} \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $t_1$ runs **before** train $t_2$ on a potentially conflicting resource (ordering variable)
- $z_{t_1 t_2} \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $t_1$ is **waiting for** train $t_2$ (pair-wise delay attribution, A5)

---

## 5. Objective function

Minimize total delay (sum of primary and secondary delays):

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{t \in T} \left( \delta_t + d_t^{prim} \right)
$$

With delay propagation (global-optimum variant, Section 3.3), the secondary delay is decomposed pair-wise:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{t \in T} d_t^{prim} + \sum_{(t_1,t_2) \in P} \Delta_{t_1 t_2}
$$

where $\Delta_{t_1 t_2} \ge 0$ is the delay train $t_1$ incurs by waiting for train $t_2$.

---

## 6. Constraints

**(C1) Route selection — each train uses exactly one route:**
$$
\sum_{\rho \in R_t} x_{t,\rho} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C2) Running-time / schedule consistency:**
$$
d_{t,b} \ge a_{t,b} + r_{t,b}^{min} + w_{t,b} - M(1 - x_{t,\rho}) \qquad \forall t,\, b \in S_t,\, \rho \in R_t
$$

**(C3) Delay definition (pair-wise, A5):** a train's secondary delay equals the wait caused by at most one other train:
$$
\delta_t \ge \left( d_{t_2,b} + h_b \right) - a_{t,b} - M(1 - z_{t t_2}) \qquad \forall t,\; \forall t_2 \neq t,\; \forall b
$$
$$
z_{t t_2} \le y_{t_2 t} \qquad \forall (t,t_2) \in P
$$
i.e., $t$ waits for $t_2$ only if $t_2$ goes first.

**(C3′) Delay propagation variant (Section 3.3):** replace (C3) by pair-wise delay variables allowing accumulation:
$$
\Delta_{t_1 t_2} \ge \left( d_{t_2,b} + h_b \right) - a_{t_1,b} - M(1 - y_{t_2 t_1}) \qquad \forall (t_1,t_2) \in P,\; \forall b
$$
$$
\delta_t \ge \sum_{t_2:\,(t,t_2)\in P} \Delta_{t t_2} \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C4) Ordering on shared resources:** for every pair of trains and common block $b$:
$$
a_{t_2,b} \ge d_{t_1,b} + h_b - M(1 - y_{t_1 t_2}) \qquad \forall (t_1,t_2) \in P,\; \forall b \in S_{t_1} \cap S_{t_2}
$$
$$
a_{t_1,b} \ge d_{t_2,b} + h_b - M\, y_{t_1 t_2} \qquad \forall (t_1,t_2) \in P,\; \forall b \in S_{t_1} \cap S_{t_2}
$$

**(C5) Anti-symmetry of ordering:**
$$
y_{t_1 t_2} + y_{t_2 t_1} = 1 \qquad \forall (t_1,t_2) \in P
$$

**(C6) Reordering restriction (A3):** overtaking only where infrastructure allows:
$$
y_{t_1 t_2} = y_{t_1 t_2}^{nom} \qquad \forall (t_1,t_2) \notin P^{overtake}
$$
where $y^{nom}$ is the nominal (timetable) order and $P^{overtake}$ are pairs meeting at overtaking-capable locations.

**(C7) Route-dependent nominal times:** actual times must match the chosen route's nominal schedule plus delay:
$$
a_{t,b} \ge a_{t,b}^{\rho} - M(1 - x_{t,\rho}) \qquad \forall t,\, b,\, \rho
$$

**(C8) Horizon bounds:**
$$
0 \le a_{t,b}, d_{t,b} \le H \qquad \forall t, b
$$

**(C9) Variable domains:**
$$
x_{t,\rho} \in \{0,1\},\quad y_{t_1 t_2} \in \{0,1\},\quad z_{t_1 t_2} \in \{0,1\},\quad \delta_t \ge 0,\quad \Delta_{t_1 t_2} \ge 0
$$

---

## 7. Two-stage decomposition (as in the paper)

- **Stage 1 (rerouting + reordering):** Solve the MILP with (C1)–(C6), (C9), fixing $a_{t,b}$ implicitly via pair-wise constraints only, **without** propagation (C3 instead of C3′). Fast, sub-optimal; yields $\hat{x}_{t,\rho}$, $\hat{y}_{t_1t_2}$.
- **Stage 2 (rescheduling):** Fix $x_{t,\rho} = \hat{x}_{t,\rho}$ (and optionally $y_{t_1t_2} = \hat{y}_{t_1t_2}$), solve the full timing MILP (C2)–(C4), (C7)–(C9) with propagation (C3′) to obtain exact train times.
- **Optimality condition (Section 3.2):** the two-stage solution is globally optimal iff no delay propagation chain exists, i.e., no train waits for a train that is itself delayed by a third train; otherwise the extended model with (C3′) guarantees the global optimum of the original rtRTMP.

The model is a standard MILP solvable by branch-and-bound; the decomposition reduces integer variables in each stage, lowering runtime as reported in the paper.

# MILP Formulation: Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Infrastructure Constraints

## 1. Model Overview

The model captures the rolling stock rescheduling problem during railway disruptions, integrating two components:
- **Composition Model** (master): assigns rolling stock units to trips and selects shunting movements.
- **Infrastructure Model** (subproblem): verifies feasibility of shunting movements given track availability and generates Combinatorial Benders' cuts.

The integrated MILP below combines both components. The iterative heuristic corresponds to solving the master problem, feeding shunting decisions one-by-one to the subproblem, and adding cuts.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Set | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| $T$ | Train trips in the (possibly disrupted) timetable, indexed by $t$ |
| $S$ | Stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $R$ | Rolling stock units, indexed by $r$ |
| $U$ | Unit types (e.g., ICM, VIRM, DDM), indexed by $u$ |
| $C$ | Feasible compositions (multi-sets of unit types), indexed by $c$ |
| $L_s$ | Tracks/platforms at station $s$; $L = \bigcup_s L_s$, indexed by $\ell$ |
| $M$ | Candidate shunting movements, indexed by $m$ |
| $K$ | Discrete time periods (e.g., minutes), indexed by $k$ |
| $P$ | Passenger demand segments, indexed by $p$ |

Derived sets:
- $T^{arr}_s = \{t \in T : \text{trip } t \text{ arrives at } s\}$
- $T^{dep}_s = \{t \in T : \text{trip } t \text{ departs from } s\}$
- $M_t \subseteq M$: shunting movements associated with trip $t$
- $E = T \cup M$: all events (trips + shunting movements)

---

## 3. Parameters

**Composition & demand**
- $n_{c,u}$: number of units of type $u$ in composition $c$
- $cap_u$: seat capacity of unit type $u$
- $max_u$: maximum (seated + standing) capacity of unit type $u$
- $dem_t$: passenger demand for trip $t$
- $\tau_s$: minimum turnaround time at station $s$
- $a_t, d_t$: scheduled arrival/departure time of trip $t$ (using $a_t^{arr}, a_t^{dep}$ for clarity)
- $orig_{r,t} \in \{0,1\}$: original-plan assignment (1 if unit $r$ was on trip $t$ originally)

**Costs**
- $c^{op}_{t,c}$: operating cost of trip $t$ with composition $c$
- $c^{stand}$: cost per standing passenger per trip
- $c^{cancel}$: cost per cancelled passenger
- $c^{dev}$: cost per unit of deviation from original plan
- $c^{sh}_m$: cost of performing shunting movement $m$
- $c^{delay}$: cost per minute of delay imposed on non-disrupted trains

**Shunting**
- $\sigma_m$: duration of shunting movement $m$ (periods)
- $o_m, d_m$: origin/destination track of shunting movement $m$
- $[e_m^{\min}, e_m^{\max}]$: time window of shunting movement $m$

**Infrastructure**
- $\delta_{m,\ell} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if shunting movement $m$ can use track $\ell$
- $avail_{\ell,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if track $\ell$ is available at time $k$
- $D^{\max}$: maximum allowed delay for non-disrupted trains (minutes)
- $B$: sufficiently large constant (big-M)

---

## 4. Decision Variables

**Composition (master) variables**
- $x_{t,c} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trip $t$ uses composition $c$
- $y_{r,t} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if unit $r$ operates trip $t$
- $z_m \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if shunting movement $m$ is performed
- $can_t \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trip $t$ is cancelled
- $s_t \geq 0$: number of standing passengers on trip $t$
- $f^{r}_{t,t'} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if unit $r$ operates trip $t$ immediately followed by trip $t'$ at the same station
- $\Delta^+_{r,t}, \Delta^-_{r,t} \geq 0$: positive/negative deviation of unit $r$ from original plan on trip $t$

**Infrastructure (subproblem) variables**
- $w_{m,\ell} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if shunting movement $m$ is executed on track $\ell$
- $v_{m,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if shunting movement $m$ starts at time $k$
- $\delta_t \geq 0$: delay (minutes) imposed on trip $t$
- $\theta_{t,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trip $t$ (after delay) occupies a track at time $k$

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; \alpha_1 Z^{op} + \alpha_2 Z^{pax} + \alpha_3 Z^{dev} + \alpha_4 Z^{sh} + \alpha_5 Z^{delay}
$$

with

$$
Z^{op} = \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{c \in C} c^{op}_{t,c}\, x_{t,c}
$$

$$
Z^{pax} = \sum_{t \in T}\left(c^{stand}\, s_t + c^{cancel}\, dem_t\, can_t\right)
$$

$$
Z^{dev} = \sum_{r \in R}\sum_{t \in T} c^{dev}\left(\Delta^+_{r,t} + \Delta^-_{r,t}\right)
$$

$$
Z^{sh} = \sum_{m \in M} c^{sh}_m\, z_m
$$

$$
Z^{delay} = \sum_{t \in T} c^{delay}\, \delta_t
$$

Weights $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_5 \geq 0$ reflect planner priorities (assumption: $\alpha_i = 1$ unless stated otherwise).

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Composition Constraints

**(C1) Single composition per trip (unless cancelled):**
$$
\sum_{c \in C} x_{t,c} + can_t = 1 \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C2) Unit count equals composition size:**
$$
\sum_{r \in R} y_{r,t} = \sum_{c \in C}\left(\sum_{u \in U} n_{c,u}\right) x_{t,c} \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C3) Unit-type composition consistency:**
$$
\sum_{r:\, type(r)=u} y_{r,t} = \sum_{c \in C} n_{c,u}\, x_{t,c} \quad \forall t \in T,\; u \in U
$$

### 6.2 Flow Conservation and Turnaround

**(C4) Unit flow conservation at each station:**
For each unit $r$, station $s$, and time-ordered trip pair $(t,t')$ with $t$ arriving at $s$ before $t'$ departs from $s$:
$$
\sum_{t' \in T^{dep}_s:\, a^{dep}_{t'} \geq a^{arr}_t} f^{r}_{t,t'} = y_{r,t} \quad \forall r \in R,\; t \in T^{arr}_s
$$
$$
\sum_{t \in T^{arr}_s:\, a^{arr}_t \leq a^{dep}_{t'}} f^{r}_{t,t'} = y_{r,t'} \quad \forall r \in R,\; t' \in T^{dep}_s
$$

**(C5) Minimum turnaround time:**
$$
a^{dep}_{t'} - a^{arr}_t \geq \tau_s - B\left(1 - f^{r}_{t,t'}\right) \quad \forall r,\; s,\; (t,t') \text{ at } s
$$

**(C6) Linking shunting to unit succession:**
Each shunting movement $m$ between trips $t$ and $t'$ (at station $s$) requires a unit succession:
$$
z_m \leq \sum_{r \in R} f^{r}_{t,t'} \quad \forall m \in M
$$

### 6.3 Capacity and Passenger Service

**(C7) Seated capacity (with standing allowance):**
$$
\sum_{c \in C}\left(\sum_{u \in U} n_{c,u}\, cap_u\right) x_{t,c} \geq dem_t(1 - can_t) - s_t \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C8) Maximum capacity (seated + standing):**
$$
\sum_{c \in C}\left(\sum_{u \in U} n_{c,u}\, max_u\right) x_{t,c} \geq dem_t(1 - can_t) \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C9) Standing passengers non-negative:**
$$
s_t \leq dem_t(1 - can_t) \quad \forall t \in T
$$

### 6.4 Deviation from Original Plan

**(C10) Linearization of absolute deviation:**
$$
y_{r,t} - orig_{r,t} = \Delta^+_{r,t} - \Delta^-_{r,t} \quad \forall r \in R,\; t \in T
$$
$$
\Delta^+_{r,t}, \Delta^-_{r,t} \geq 0
$$

### 6.5 Infrastructure Constraints (Subproblem)

**(I1) Shunting movement requires a track:**
$$
\sum_{\ell \in L} w_{m,\ell} \geq z_m \quad \forall m \in M
$$

**(I2) Track compatibility:**
$$
w_{m,\ell} \leq \delta_{m,\ell}\, z_m \quad \forall m \in M,\; \ell \in L
$$

**(I3) Shunting start time selection:**
$$
\sum_{k \in K} v_{m,k} = z_m \quad \forall m \in M
$$
$$
v_{m,k} = 0 \quad \forall m,\; k < e^{\min}_m \text{ or } k > e^{\max}_m - \sigma_m
$$

**(I4) Track occupancy by shunting (duration):**
$$
w_{m,\ell} \leq \sum_{k' = k}^{k+\sigma_m - 1} v_{m,k'} + B(1 - \theta^{sh}_{m,\ell,k}) \quad \forall m,\ell,k
$$
(where $\theta^{sh}_{m,\ell,k}$ indicates shunting $m$ occupies track $\ell$ at time $k$; implied by $v_{m,k'}$ for $k' \in [k-\sigma_m+1, k]$).

**(I5) Track conflict — at most one event per track per time:**
$$
\sum_{m \in M} \theta^{sh}_{m,\ell,k} + \sum_{t \in T} \theta_{t,\ell,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall \ell \in L,\; k \in K
$$

**(I6) Track availability:**
$$
\theta^{sh}_{m,\ell,k} \leq avail_{\ell,k} \quad \forall m,\ell,k
$$
$$
\theta_{t,\ell,k} \leq avail_{\ell,k} \quad \forall t,\ell,k
$$

**(I7) Train track occupancy after delay:**
$$
\theta_{t,\ell,k} = 1 \iff a^{arr}_t + \delta_t \leq k < a^{dep}_t + \delta_t + \text{dwell}_t \text{ and trip } t \text{ uses } \ell
$$
(linearized via standard big-M formulations).

### 6.6 Delay Management

**(D1) Maximum delay for non-disrupted trips:**
$$
\delta_t \leq D^{\max}(1 - can_t) \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(D2) Delay propagation along rolling-stock chain:**
For each unit $r$ and successor pair $(t,t')$:
$$
\delta_{t'} \geq \delta_t - B(1 - f^{r}_{t,t'}) \quad \forall r,\; (t,t')
$$

**(D3) Cancellation implies zero delay:**
$$
\delta_t \leq B(1 - can_t) \quad \forall t \in T
$$

### 6.7 Linking Constraints (Master–Subproblem Coupling)

**(L1) Shunting decision implies track assignment exists:**
$$
z_m \leq \sum_{\ell \in L} w_{m,\ell} \quad \forall m \in M
$$

**(L2) No shunting without time slot:**
$$
z_m \leq \sum_{k \in K} v_{m,k} \quad \forall m \in M
$$

---

## 7. Combinatorial Benders' Cuts (Iterative Refinement)

After solving the subproblem for a candidate set $\hat{z}$ of shunting movements, if the subproblem is infeasible, identify a minimal infeasible subset $\hat{M}^{inf} \subseteq \{m : \hat{z}_m = 1\}$ and add:

**(B1) Combinatorial Benders' cut:**
$$
\sum_{m \in \hat{M}^{inf}} z_m \leq |\hat{M}^{inf}| - 1
$$

These cuts are added iteratively to the master problem until feasibility is achieved (exact algorithm) or until a stopping criterion is met (iterative heuristic).

---

## 8. Iterative Heuristic Variant

The iterative heuristic processes shunting movements one at a time:
1. Solve master problem to obtain $z^*$.
2. For each $m$ with $z^*_m = 1$ (in arbitrary order), solve subproblem with that single movement.
3. If infeasible, set $z_m = 0$ in master and re-solve.
4. Repeat until all selected shunting movements are individually feasible.

This corresponds to adding singleton cuts:
$$
z_m \leq 0 \quad \text{(i.e., } z_m = 0 \text{)} \quad \forall m \text{ individually infeasible}
$$

---

## 9. Key Assumptions

1. **Time discretization**: Time is discretized into uniform periods (1 minute assumed).
2. **Deterministic data**: Passenger demand, track availability, and disruption scope are known.
3. **Composition homogeneity**: A composition is fixed for the duration of a trip.
4. **Unit interchangeability**: Units of the same type are interchangeable.
5. **Driver availability**: Shunting drivers are available when needed (per problem description).
6. **Bounded delays**: Non-disrupted trains can be delayed by at most $D^{\max}$ minutes.
7. **Single shunting per gap**: At most one shunting movement occurs between two consecutive trips of a unit.
8. **Linear costs**: All objective components are linear in decision variables.
9. **Track granularity**: Tracks/platforms are modeled as discrete resources.
10. **Disruption scope**: Disruption affects a contiguous time window and a known set of trips/tracks (full blockages in the case study).

---

## 10. Model Size and Complexity

The integrated MILP is a large-scale binary problem. Key variable counts:
- $|T| \cdot |C|$ composition variables
- $|R| \cdot |T|$ unit-trip assignments
- $|M| \cdot |L|$ track-shunting assignments
- $|M| \cdot |K|$ shunting start times
- $|T| \cdot |L| \cdot |K|$ track-time occupancy indicators

The Combinatorial Benders' decomposition dramatically reduces the effective problem size by separating composition logic from infrastructure feasibility, making the model tractable for real-world instances (e.g., disruptions at Utrecht Centraal and Rotterdam Centraal).

The final model is complete and well-formed. Here is the polished MILP for the **Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)** under partial segment blockages:

---

# Complete MILP Model for the TRSMP

## Section 1: Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t \in T$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s \in S$, ordered along the line |
| $B$ | Set of blocks (track segments), indexed by $b \in B$ |
| $I$ | Set of discrete time steps, indexed by $i \in I$ |
| $K$ | Set of piecewise-linear breakpoints, indexed by $k \in K$ |
| $B^{\text{blk}} \subseteq B$ | Blocks affected by the disruption |
| $B^{\text{rer}} \subseteq B$ | Blocks eligible for rerouting |
| $s_b^{\text{in}}, s_b^{\text{out}}$ | Entry/exit stations of block $b$ |
| $T^{\text{pair}}$ | Ordered train pairs $(t,t')$ with $t < t'$ |

## Section 2: Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\Delta t$, $L_b$ | Time step; block length |
| $v_{\min}, v_{\max}$; $a_{\min}, a_{\max}$ | Speed bounds; acceleration bounds ($a_{\min}<0<a_{\max}$) |
| $\text{dwell}_{\min}, \text{dwell}_{\max}$ | Min/max dwell time at stations |
| $\text{run}_{\min}$ | Minimum running time between adjacent stations |
| $\tau^{\text{arr},0}_{t,s}, \tau^{\text{dep},0}_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival/departure times |
| $\tau^{\text{run},0}_{t,b}$ | Scheduled running time on block $b$ |
| $\tau^{\text{start}}, \tau^{\text{end}}$ | Disruption time window |
| $M$, $\varepsilon$ | Big-M constant; small positive constant |
| $\text{cap}_s$ | Platform capacity at station $s$ |
| $w_d, w_e, w_c, w_r$ | Weights: delay, energy, cancellation, reordering |
| $\alpha, \beta$; $P_{\text{aux}}$ | Energy coefficients; auxiliary power rate |
| $v_k$, $f^{\text{inv}}_k = 1/v_k$, $f^{\text{sq}}_k = v_k^2$ | Breakpoint values for SOS2 linearization |
| $o^0_{t,t',b,i}$ | Reference ordering from the nominal timetable |

## Section 3: Decision Variables

**Timing:** $\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}, \tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s} \ge 0$ (actual arrival/departure); $\delta^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}, \delta^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}, \delta^{\text{run}}_{t,b} \ge 0$ (delays).

**Speed:** $v_{t,b,i} \in [v_{\min}, v_{\max}]$ (speed of train $t$ on block $b$ at time $i$).

**Occupancy:** $x_{t,b,i}, y_{t,b,i} \in \{0,1\}$ (entry/exit of block $b$ at time $i$); $z_{t,s,i} \in \{0,1\}$ (dwelling at station $s$ at time $i$).

**Rerouting:** $r_{t,b} \in \{0,1\}$ (train $t$ uses the opposite track on block $b$).

**Ordering:** $o_{t,t',b,i} \in \{0,1\}$ (train $t$ precedes $t'$); $\rho_{t,t',b,i} \in \{0,1\}$ (reordering deviation).

**Cancellation:** $c_t \in \{0,1\}$.

**Energy:** $\text{aux}_{t,s} \ge 0$ (auxiliary energy during dwell).

**SOS2:** $\lambda_{t,b,i,k} \in [0,1]$ (convex-combination weights).

## Section 4: Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; w_d \!\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\!\left(\delta^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}+\delta^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}\right)
\;+\; w_e \!\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{b\in B}\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{k\in K}\lambda_{t,b,i,k}\!\left(\alpha\, f^{\text{sq}}_k + \beta\, f^{\text{inv}}_k\right)L_b
\;+\; w_e \!\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\text{aux}_{t,s}
\;+\; w_c \!\sum_{t\in T} c_t
\;+\; w_r \!\sum_{(t,t')\in T^{\text{pair}}}\sum_{b\in B}\sum_{i\in I}\rho_{t,t',b,i}
$$

Weighted sum of **total delay**, **traction + auxiliary energy**, **cancellations**, and **reordering penalties**.

## Section 5: Constraints

### 5.1 Delay Linking
$$
\delta^{\text{arr}}_{t,s} \geq \tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s} - \tau^{\text{arr},0}_{t,s}, \qquad
\delta^{\text{dep}}_{t,s} \geq \tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s} - \tau^{\text{dep},0}_{t,s} \qquad \forall\, t,s \tag{D1–D2}
$$
$$
\delta^{\text{run}}_{t,b} \geq \bigl(\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s_b^{\text{out}}} - \tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s_b^{\text{in}}}\bigr) - \tau^{\text{run},0}_{t,b} \qquad \forall\, t,b \tag{D3}
$$

### 5.2 Dwell Time
$$
\text{dwell}_{\min}(1-c_t) \leq \tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s} - \tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s} \leq \text{dwell}_{\max}(1-c_t) + M c_t \qquad \forall\, t,s \tag{DW1}
$$

### 5.3 Running Time
$$
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s+1} - \tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s} \geq \text{run}_{\min}(1-c_t) \qquad \forall\, t,s \tag{RT1}
$$
$$
\sum_{i\in I} v_{t,b,i}\,\Delta t \geq L_b(1-c_t), \qquad
\sum_{i\in I} v_{t,b,i}\,\Delta t \leq L_b + M c_t \qquad \forall\, t,b \tag{RT2–RT3}
$$

### 5.4 Disruption Window
$$
x_{t,b,i} = 0 \quad \forall\, t,\, b\in B^{\text{blk}},\, i\Delta t \in [\tau^{\text{start}},\tau^{\text{end}] \tag{DI1}
$$
$$
y_{t,b,i} = 0 \quad \forall\, t,\, b\in B^{\text{blk}},\, i\Delta t \notin [\tau^{\text{start}},\tau^{\text{end}}] \tag{DI2}
$$

### 5.5 Cancellation
$$
\sum_{b,i} x_{t,b,i} \leq M(1-c_t), \qquad \sum_{s}\bigl(\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}+\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}\bigr) \leq M(1-c_t) \qquad \forall\, t \tag{CN1–CN2}
$$

### 5.6 Reordering Penalty (absolute value linearization)
$$
\rho_{t,t',b,i} \geq o_{t,t',b,i} - o^0_{t,t',b,i}, \qquad
\rho_{t,t',b,i} \geq o^0_{t,t',b,i} - o_{t,t',b,i} \qquad \forall\, (t,t'),b,i \tag{RO1–RO2}
$$

### 5.7 Acceleration / Deceleration
$$
a_{\min}\Delta t \leq v_{t,b,i+1} - v_{t,b,i} \leq a_{\max}\Delta t \qquad \forall\, t,b,i \tag{AC1}
$$

### 5.8 Auxiliary Power During Dwell
$$
\text{aux}_{t,s} = P_{\text{aux}}\bigl(\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}-\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}\bigr) \quad \text{(linear, relaxed by } M c_t\text{)} \qquad \forall\, t,s \tag{AP1–AP2}
$$

### 5.9 Big-M Occupancy Linking (4 inequalities per indicator)
**Entry indicator $x_{t,b,i}$** ($x=1 \Rightarrow$ entry time in interval $i$ and traversal time within $[L_b/v_{\max}, L_b/v_{\min}]$):
$$
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s_b^{\text{in}}} \geq i\Delta t - M(1-x_{t,b,i}), \qquad
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s_b^{\text{in}}} \leq (i{+}1)\Delta t + M(1-x_{t,b,i}) \tag{OC1–OC2}
$$
$$
\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s_b^{\text{out}}} \geq \tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s_b^{\text{in}}} + \tfrac{L_b}{v_{\max}} - M(1-x_{t,b,i}), \qquad
\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s_b^{\text{out}}} \leq \tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s_b^{\text{in}}} + \tfrac{L_b}{v_{\min}} + M(1-x_{t,b,i}) \tag{OC3–OC4}
$$
Analogous constraints **(OC5–OC8)** for the exit indicator $y_{t,b,i}$, plus uniqueness:
$$
\sum_{i} x_{t,b,i} \leq 1, \qquad \sum_{i} y_{t,b,i} \leq 1 \qquad \forall\, t,b \tag{OC9–OC10}
$$

### 5.10 Piecewise-Linear Speed Functions (shared SOS2)
$$
v_{t,b,i} = \sum_{k} \lambda_{t,b,i,k}\, v_k, \qquad \sum_{k} \lambda_{t,b,i,k} = 1, \qquad \{\lambda_{t,b,i,k}\}_k \text{ SOS2} \qquad \forall\, t,b,i \tag{PW1–PW4}
$$
The same $\lambda$ variables evaluate $v^2$ (via $f^{\text{sq}}_k$) and $1/v$ (via $f^{\text{inv}}_k$) in the objective.

### 5.11 Rerouting Entry/Exit Only at Stations
$$
r_{t,b} = r_{t,b-1} \quad \text{(no station between } b{-}1 \text{ and } b\text{)}, \qquad r_{t,b} = 0 \;\; \forall\, b \notin B^{\text{rer}} \tag{RR1–RR3}
$$

### 5.12 Bidirectional Conflict Constraints
**Mutual exclusion:**
$$
x_{t,b,i} + x_{t',b,i} \leq 1, \qquad y_{t,b,i} + y_{t',b,i} \leq 1 \qquad \forall\, t\neq t', b, i \tag{BC1–BC2}
$$
**Ordering variant (with headway):**
$$
o_{t,t',b,i} + o_{t',t,b,i} = 1 \qquad \forall\, (t,t'), b, i \tag{BC3}
$$
$$
x_{t,b,i} \leq x_{t,b,i-1} + o_{t,t',b,i-1} + M(1-x_{t',b,i}), \quad \text{symmetrically for } t' \tag{BC4–BC5}
$$

### 5.13 Platform Capacity
$$
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s} \leq i\Delta t + M(1-z_{t,s,i}), \qquad
\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s} \geq (i{+}1)\Delta t - M(1-z_{t,s,i}) \tag{PC1–PC2}
$$
$$
\sum_{t} z_{t,s,i} \leq \text{cap}_s \qquad \forall\, s,i \tag{PC3}
$$

### 5.14 Minimum Speed at Block Exit (no mid-block stops)
$$
v_{t,b,i} \geq v_{\min}\, y_{t,b,i} \qquad \forall\, t,b,i \tag{MS1}
$$

### 5.15 Boundary Conditions
$$
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s_1} = \tau^{\text{arr},0}_{t,s_1}, \qquad
\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s_{|S|}} = \tau^{\text{dep},0}_{t,s_{|S|}}, \qquad
v_{t,b,1} = v^0_{t,b}, \qquad v_{t,b,|I|} = v^0_{t,b} \tag{BC-A1–A4}
$$

## Section 6: Linearization Notes

| Nonlinear element | Technique |
|---|---|
| $\lvert o - o^0\rvert$ | Auxiliary binary $\rho$ with two inequalities (RO1–RO2) |
| $v^2$ and $1/v$ in energy | Shared SOS2 convex combination $\lambda$ (PW1–PW4) |
| Indicator–continuous linking | Big-M with 4 inequalities per indicator (OC1–OC8) |
| Cancellation coupling | Big-M relaxation with $c_t$ |
| Ordering consistency | Linear inequalities (BC3–BC5) |

## Section 7: Assumptions

1. Uniform time discretization $\Delta t$; speed constant within each step.
2. Double-track corridor; rerouting uses the opposite track for $b \in B^{\text{rer}}$.
3. Disruption known in advance: blocks $B^{\text{blk}}$ blocked during $[\tau^{\text{start}}, \tau^{\text{end}}]$.
4. Trains cannot stop mid-block (MS1, OC3–OC4).
5. Rerouting entry/exit only at stations (switch locations).
6. Homogeneous train performance parameters.
7. Constant auxiliary power $P_{\text{aux}}$ during dwell.
8. Reference ordering $o^0$ from the nominal timetable.
9. Big-M chosen tight but valid; weights $w_d, w_e, w_c, w_r$ set by the operator.

---

**Key features of this final model:**
- **Integrated TRP + TSMP**: timing variables ($\tau^{\text{arr}}, \tau^{\text{dep}}$) and speed variables ($v$) are coupled through running-time constraints (RT2–RT3) and occupancy linking (OC1–OC8), ensuring the rescheduled timetable is executable at the train-control level.
- **Partial blockage handling**: DI1–DI2 forbid nominal-track use during the disruption window while permitting rerouting to the opposite track.
- **Bidirectional conflict resolution**: BC1–BC5 coordinate trains sharing track resources, both via mutual exclusion and via ordering variables with headway.
- **Energy-efficient co-optimization**: the objective balances delay against traction energy (piecewise-linear $v^2$ and $1/v$ via shared SOS2 variables) and auxiliary dwell energy.
- **Full decision flexibility**: retiming, reordering, rerouting, and cancellation are all captured, with a complete variable-usage audit confirming every variable appears in the objective or constraints — a valid, complete MILP.

Text:
# MILP Formulation: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

Below is the complete, fully linearized MILP model. It jointly decides train cancellation, departure/arrival times, track (normal vs. opposite), block-by-block sequencing, and per-block speed profiles, while minimizing a weighted combination of delay, energy, and cancellations.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed $i, j \in T$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations (passing loops), indexed $s \in S$ |
| $B$ | Set of block sections, indexed $b \in B$ |
| $K=\{0,\dots,|K|\}$ | Discrete time steps, indexed $k$ |
| $D=[k_d^{\rm start},k_d^{\rm end}]$ | Disruption window on block $b^*$ |
| $B(i)$ | Ordered blocks traversed by train $i$ |
| $S(i)$ | Ordered stations visited by train $i$ |
| $T^{\rm req}$ | Trains that must cross $b^*$ during $D$ |
| $T^{\uparrow}, T^{\downarrow}$ | Trains travelling up- / down-direction |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Value |
|---|---|---|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ | (m) |
| $v_{\min}, v_{\max}$ | Min / max allowed speed | $0$, $83.33$ m/s |
| $a_{\max}, a_{\rm brake}$ | Max acceleration, braking | $1.0$, $1.0$ m/s² |
| $d_{\min}, d_{\max}$ | Min / max dwell time | $60$ s, $300$ s |
| $h$ | Minimum headway | $180$ s |
| $\Delta t$ | Time discretization | $30$ s |
| $P_{\rm aux}$ | Auxiliary power | (kW) |
| $P_{\max}$ | Max tractive power | (kW) |
| $\eta$ | Drivetrain efficiency | (–) |
| $\eta_{\rm rec}$ | Regenerative braking fraction | $0.8$ |
| $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ | Weights (delay / energy / cancel) | tunable |
| $P_{\rm cancel}$ | Cancellation penalty | $10{,}000$ |
| $M$ | Big-M constant | sufficiently large |
| $a_i^0, b_i^0$ | Scheduled departure / arrival | (s) |
| $o_i, d_i$ | Origin, destination of train $i$ | – |
| $T_H$ | Scheduling horizon | (s) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Binary**
- $x_{i,b,k}\in\{0,1\}$ — train $i$ on **normal** track of block $b$ at time $k$
- $y_{i,b,k}\in\{0,1\}$ — train $i$ on **opposite** track of block $b$ at time $k$
- $o_{i,j,b,k}\in\{0,1\}$ — train $i$ precedes $j$ on block $b$ at time $k$
- $o_{i,j,s}\in\{0,1\}$ — station-ordering indicator at $s$
- $z_i\in\{0,1\}$ — train $i$ is cancelled

**Continuous (non-negative)**
- $t_{i,s}^{\rm arr}, t_{i,s}^{\rm dep}\ge 0$ — arrival / departure times at station $s$
- $v_{i,b,k}\ge 0$ — speed (m/s) on block $b$ at time $k$
- $p_{i,b,k}\ge 0$ — position (m) on block $b$ at time $k$
- $e_{i,b,k}\ge 0$ — energy consumed (kWh) on block $b$ at time $k$
- $u_{i,b,k}\ge 0$ — tractive power (kW) on block $b$ at time $k$
- $d_i^+\ge 0$ — positive arrival delay of train $i$

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \alpha \sum_{i \in T} d_i^{+} \;+\; \beta \sum_{i\in T,\,b\in B,\,k\in K} e_{i,b,k} \;+\; \gamma\, P_{\rm cancel}\sum_{i\in T} z_i
$$

with the positive-delay linearization
$$
d_i^{+} \;\geq\; t_{i,d_i}^{\rm arr} - b_i^{0}, \qquad d_i^{+} \geq 0 \quad \forall i\in T.
$$

The three terms capture (i) destination delay, (ii) total traction + auxiliary energy, and (iii) a heavy penalty on cancellations.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Kinematic / Position Update (big-M relaxed)

$$
p_{i,b,k+1} - p_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; v_{i,b,k}\Delta t + M\bigl(2 - x_{i,b,k} - y_{i,b,k} - x_{i,b,k+1} - y_{i,b,k+1}\bigr)
$$

$$
p_{i,b,k+1} - p_{i,b,k} \;\geq\; v_{i,b,k}\Delta t - M\bigl(2 - x_{i,b,k} - y_{i,b,k} - x_{i,b,k+1} - y_{i,b,k+1}\bigr) \qquad \forall i,b,k.
$$

$$
p_{i,b,0} = 0, \qquad p_{i,b,|K|} \geq L_b - M\bigl(1 - x_{i,b,|K|} - y_{i,b,|K|}\bigr) \qquad \forall i, b\in B(i).
$$

### 5.2 Speed Dynamics

$$
v_{i,b,k+1} \;\leq\; v_{i,b,k} + a_{\max}\Delta t + M\bigl(1 - x_{i,b,k} - y_{i,b,k}\bigr) \qquad \forall i,b,k
$$

$$
v_{i,b,k+1} \;\geq\; v_{i,b,k} - a_{\rm brake}\Delta t - M\bigl(1 - x_{i,b,k} - y_{i,b,k}\bigr) \qquad \forall i,b,k
$$

$$
v_{\min}\bigl(x_{i,b,k} + y_{i,b,k}\bigr) \;\leq\; v_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; v_{\max}\bigl(x_{i,b,k} + y_{i,b,k}\bigr) \qquad \forall i,b,k.
$$

### 5.3 Block Traversal (full coverage per uncancelled train)

$$
\sum_{k\in K} v_{i,b,k}\Delta t \;=\; L_b\,(1 - z_i) \qquad \forall i\in T,\; b\in B(i).
$$

### 5.4 Track / Occupancy Consistency

$$
x_{i,b,k} + y_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; 1 \qquad \forall i,b,k.
$$

$$
0 \;\leq\; p_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; L_b\bigl(x_{i,b,k} + y_{i,b,k}\bigr) \qquad \forall i,b,k.
$$

### 5.5 Same-Direction Capacity (reordering)

For every pair $i<j$:
$$
x_{i,b,k} + x_{j,b,k} \;\leq\; 1 + M(1 - o_{i,j,b,k}) \qquad \forall b,k
$$

$$
y_{i,b,k} + y_{j,b,k} \;\leq\; 1 + M(1 - o_{i,j,b,k}) \qquad \forall b,k
$$

$$
o_{i,j,b,k} + o_{j,i,b,k} \;\geq\; 1, \qquad o_{i,j,b,k},\,o_{j,i,b,k}\in\{0,1\}.
$$

### 5.6 Bidirectional Conflict on the Disrupted Block

During the disruption window on the surviving (opposite) track:
$$
x_{i,b^*,k} + y_{j,b^*,k} \;\leq\; 1 \qquad \forall i,j,\; k\in D
$$

$$
y_{i,b^*,k} + x_{j,b^*,k} \;\leq\; 1 \qquad \forall i,j,\; k\in D.
$$

### 5.7 Disruption Rerouting (forced use of opposite track)

$$
x_{i,b^*,k} = 0 \qquad \forall i,\; k\in D
$$

$$
y_{i,b^*,k} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in T^{\rm req},\; k\in D.
$$

### 5.8 Station Dwell

$$
d_{\min}\,\delta_{i,s} \;\leq\; t_{i,s}^{\rm dep} - t_{i,s}^{\rm arr} \;\leq\; d_{\max}\,\delta_{i,s} \qquad \forall i,\; s\in S(i),
$$

with $\delta_{i,s}\in\{0,1\}$ indicating that $i$ stops at $s$ (omitted at terminals).

### 5.9 Time Continuity Between Stations

$$
t_{i,s+1}^{\rm arr} \;=\; t_{i,s}^{\rm dep} \;+\; \!\!\sum_{b\in B(s,s+1)}\!\!\sum_{k\in K}\Delta t\,(x_{i,b,k}+y_{i,b,k}) \qquad \forall i,\; s,s{+}1\in S(i).
$$

### 5.10 Station Headway (linearized disjunction)

$$
t_{i,s}^{\rm arr} - t_{j,s}^{\rm arr} \;\geq\; h - M(1 - o_{i,j,s}) \qquad \forall i\neq j,\; s
$$

$$
t_{j,s}^{\rm arr} - t_{i,s}^{\rm arr} \;\geq\; h - M\cdot o_{i,j,s} \qquad \forall i\neq j,\; s.
$$

### 5.11 Cancellation Logic

$$
x_{i,b,k} + y_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i,b,k
$$

$$
t_{i,o_i}^{\rm dep} \;\leq\; T_H(1 - z_i), \qquad t_{i,d_i}^{\rm arr} \;\leq\; T_H(1 - z_i) \qquad \forall i.
$$

### 5.12 Energy Model (linearized Davis-style)

Tractive power is introduced to avoid the bilinear $F\cdot v$:

$$
e_{i,b,k} \;\geq\; \Bigl(\frac{u_{i,b,k}}{\eta} + P_{\rm aux}\Bigr)\Delta t \qquad \forall i,b,k
$$

$$
0 \;\leq\; u_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; P_{\max}\bigl(x_{i,b,k} + y_{i,b,k}\bigr) \qquad \forall i,b,k.
$$

Regenerative braking credit:
$$
e_{i,b,k} \;\geq\; \frac{u_{i,b,k}}{\eta}\Delta t \;-\; \eta_{\rm rec}\bigl(v_{i,b,k-1} - v_{i,b,k}\bigr) \qquad \forall i,b,k.
$$

### 5.13 Initial / Terminal Conditions

$$
t_{i,o_i}^{\rm dep} \;\geq\; a_i^{0} \qquad \forall i
$$

$$
t_{i,d_i}^{\rm arr} \;\leq\; T_H \qquad \forall i
$$

$$
t_{i,s}^{\rm dep} \;\geq\; t_{i,s}^{\rm arr} \quad\forall i,s, \qquad t_{i,s+1}^{\rm arr} \;\geq\; t_{i,s}^{\rm dep} \quad\forall i,\, s,s{+}1\in S(i).
$$

---

## 6. Linearization Summary

| Nonlinear element | MILP reformulation |
|---|---|
| $(t^{\rm arr} - b^0)^+$ | Auxiliary $d_i^+$ with two linear inequalities |
| Bilinear $F\cdot v$ in energy | Power variable $u_{i,b,k}$ replaces $F\cdot v$ |
| Indicator dynamics $p_{k+1}-p_k = v_k\Delta t$ if occupied | Big-M relaxation (5.1) |
| Disjunction $\|t_i - t_j\|\ge h$ | Ordering binary $o_{i,j,s}$ and two linear constraints (5.10) |
| Bidirectional occupation conflict $x+y\le 1$ on disrupted block | (5.6) and (5.7) |
| Regenerative-braking nonlinear term | Linear envelope in (5.12) |

---

## 7. Explanation of Model Elements

**Track-choice binaries** $x_{i,b,k}$ and $y_{i,b,k}$ encode both *where* and *on which track* each train is moving. Constraint (5.4) forbids a single train from occupying both tracks of the same block at the same instant, while (5.5) prohibits two trains on the same track of the same block simultaneously unless explicitly ordered by $o_{i,j,b,k}$. Together with (5.6), this captures the bidirectional conflict that arises in the rerouting window.

**Disruption handling** is split into (5.7): the *normal* track of $b^*$ during $D$ is closed (any train needing to traverse it must take the opposite track), and (5.6) forbids head-on collisions when both up- and down-direction traffic share the surviving track.

**Speed variables** $v_{i,b,k}$ obey linearized acceleration / braking limits (5.2), producing a discrete trapezoidal speed profile typical of MILP-based train control. Combined with the position update (5.1) and the block-traversal requirement (5.3), they implicitly define each train's trajectory.

**Station timing** $t_{i,s}^{\rm arr}, t_{i,s}^{\rm dep}$ glue blocks together: the arrival at the next station equals departure from the previous one plus cumulative time on each intervening block (5.9). Dwell bounds (5.8) keep station stops inside operating limits, and headway (5.10) keeps minimum inter-train separation at stations.

**Cancellation** $z_i$ zeroes every occupancy (5.11), forcing the solver either to operate each train or absorb the heavy penalty $\gamma P_{\rm cancel}=10{,}000$ — making cancellation a last resort only.

**Energy accounting** uses a tractive-power variable $u_{i,b,k}$ to keep the model fully linear while still distinguishing acceleration (high power) from coasting (low power) and recovering part of the kinetic energy through $\eta_{\rm rec}$ when speeds drop (5.12). This makes the trade-off between fast running and energy consumption explicit.

**Objective weights** $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ encode operational priorities (e.g. $\alpha\gg\beta$ for punctuality-dominant operations, or lexicographic ordering via sequential solves). The objective simultaneously drives (i) on-time arrival, (ii) energy-efficient driving, and (iii) preservation of service.

The resulting MILP yields, in a single solve, the **conflict-free rescheduled timetable** and the **executable speed profiles** that achieve it — exactly the integrated decision required for the TRSMP under partial blockages.

A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j \in T$ |
| $T_{up} \subseteq T$ | Set of trains traveling in the up direction |
| $T_{down} \subseteq T$ | Set of trains traveling in the down direction |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s \in S$ |
| $S_0 \subset S$ | Set of stations excluding origin/destination terminals |
| $K$ | Set of track segments (block sections), indexed by $k \in K$ |
| $K^{dis} \subseteq K$ | Set of disrupted block sections |
| $D = \{up, down\}$ | Set of directions, indexed by $d \in D$ |
| $I$ | Set of discretized time intervals, indexed by $t \in I$ |
| $V$ | Set of discretized speed levels, indexed by $v \in V$ |
| $P_i$ | Set of feasible paths (including rerouting options) for train $i$, indexed by $p \in P_i$ |
| $E$ | Set of energy consumption coefficients for driving regimes |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $L_k$ | Length of block section $k$ | km |
| $L^{max}$ | Maximum block section length | km |
| $a_i^{max}$ | Maximum acceleration of train $i$ | m/s² |
| $b_i^{max}$ | Maximum deceleration (braking) of train $i$ | m/s² |
| $v_i^{max}$ | Maximum operating speed of train $i$ | km/h |
| $v_i^{min}$ | Minimum operating speed of train $i$ | km/h |
| $d_{i,s}^{arr,sch}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ | min |
| $d_{i,s}^{dep,sch}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ | min |
| $\tau_{i,s}^{min}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ | min |
| $\tau_{i,s}^{max}$ | Maximum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ | min |
| $h^{min}$ | Minimum headway time between consecutive trains | min |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (Big-M) | — |
| $\Delta t$ | Length of a time interval | min |
| $\Delta v$ | Increment between consecutive speed levels | km/h |
| $t_k^{dis,start}$ | Start time of disruption on block $k$ | min |
| $t_k^{dis,end}$ | End time of disruption on block $k$ | min |
| $c^{delay}$ | Penalty cost per minute of delay | €/min |
| $c^{cancel}$ | Penalty cost for canceling a train | € |
| $c^{energy}$ | Cost coefficient for energy consumption | €/kWh |
| $\alpha_e$ | Energy consumption rate for driving regime $e$ (traction/coasting/braking) | kWh/km |
| $M_i$ | Mass of train $i$ | tonnes |
| $R_i$ | Resistance coefficient of train $i$ | kN |
| $\rho_{i,k,p}$ | 1 if path $p$ of train $i$ traverses block $k$, 0 otherwise | — |
| $\delta_{i,k,p}^{rer}$ | 1 if path $p$ of train $i$ uses rerouting on block $k$, 0 otherwise | — |
| $o_{i,s}$ | Scheduled origin station of train $i$ | — |
| $dst_{i,s}$ | Scheduled destination station of train $i$ | — |

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Train Rescheduling Variables

| Symbol | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $y_{i,s}$ | $\in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ stops at station $s$, 0 otherwise |
| $z_i$ | $\in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is canceled, 0 otherwise |
| $x_{i,j,k}$ | $\in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on block $k$, 0 otherwise |
| $w_{i,p}$ | $\in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if path $p$ is selected for train $i$, 0 otherwise |
| $r_{i,k}$ | $\in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted on block $k$, 0 otherwise |

### 3.2 Speed Profile Variables

| Symbol | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| $v_{i,k,t}$ | $\geq 0$ | Speed of train $i$ on block $k$ at time interval $t$ |
| $s_{i,k,t}$ | $\geq 0$ | Position of train $i$ on block $k$ at time interval $t$ |
| $e_{i,k,t}$ | $\geq 0$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on block $k$ at time interval $t$ |
| $u_{i,k,t}^{acc}$ | $\in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is accelerating on block $k$ at time $t$ |
| $u_{i,k,t}^{coa}$ | $\in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is coasting on block $k$ at time $t$ |
| $u_{i,k,t}^{brk}$ | $\in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is braking on block $k$ at time $t$ |
| $\phi_{i,k,t}$ | $\in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ occupies block $k$ at time $t$, 0 otherwise |

### 3.3 Auxiliary Variables

| Symbol | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| $\Delta_{i,s}^{arr}$ | $\geq 0$ | Arrival delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\Delta_{i,s}^{dep}$ | $\geq 0$ | Departure delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $E_i$ | $\geq 0$ | Total energy consumption of train $i$ |

## 4. Objective Function

The objective minimizes a weighted sum of total delay, cancellation penalties, and energy consumption:

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{c^{delay} \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \left(\Delta_{i,s}^{arr} + \Delta_{i,s}^{dep}\right)}_{\text{Total delay cost}} + \underbrace{c^{cancel} \sum_{i \in T} z_i}_{\text{Cancellation cost}} + \underbrace{c^{energy} \sum_{i \in T} E_i}_{\text{Energy cost}}
$$

where the total energy consumption is:

$$
E_i = \sum_{k \in K} \sum_{t \in I} e_{i,k,t} \quad \forall i \in T
$$

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Path Selection Constraints

**Single path per train:**
$$
\sum_{p \in P_i} w_{i,p} = 1 - z_i \quad \forall i \in T
$$

**Rerouting indicator:**
$$
r_{i,k} = \sum_{p \in P_i} \delta_{i,k,p}^{rer} \cdot w_{i,p} \quad \forall i \in T, \; k \in K
$$

### 5.2 Train Dynamics Constraints (Speed Profile)

**Speed limits:**
$$
v_i^{min} \cdot \phi_{i,k,t} \leq v_{i,k,t} \leq v_i^{max} \cdot \phi_{i,k,t} \quad \forall i \in T, \; k \in K, \; t \in I
$$

**Driving regime exclusivity:**
$$
u_{i,k,t}^{acc} + u_{i,k,t}^{coa} + u_{i,k,t}^{brk} = \phi_{i,k,t} \quad \forall i \in T, \; k \in K, \; t \in I
$$

**Acceleration constraint:**
$$
v_{i,k,t+1} - v_{i,k,t} \leq a_i^{max} \cdot \Delta t \cdot u_{i,k,t}^{acc} + M \cdot (1 - u_{i,k,t}^{acc}) \quad \forall i, k, t
$$

**Deceleration constraint:**
$$
v_{i,k,t} - v_{i,k,t+1} \leq b_i^{max} \cdot \Delta t \cdot u_{i,k,t}^{brk} + M \cdot (1 - u_{i,k,t}^{brk}) \quad \forall i, k, t
$$

**Position update (kinematic equation):**
$$
s_{i,k,t+1} = s_{i,k,t} + \frac{v_{i,k,t} + v_{i,k,t+1}}{2} \cdot \Delta t \quad \forall i, k, t
$$

**Block boundary:**
$$
0 \leq s_{i,k,t} \leq L_k \cdot \sum_{p \in P_i} \rho_{i,k,p} \cdot w_{i,p} \quad \forall i, k, t
$$

### 5.3 Energy Consumption Constraints

**Energy by driving regime:**
$$
e_{i,k,t} = \alpha_{acc} \cdot u_{i,k,t}^{acc} + \alpha_{coa} \cdot u_{i,k,t}^{coa} + \alpha_{brk} \cdot u_{i,k,t}^{brk} \quad \forall i, k, t
$$

where $\alpha_{acc}, \alpha_{coa}, \alpha_{brk}$ are energy rates (note: $\alpha_{brk} \leq 0$ for regenerative braking).

### 5.4 Disruption Constraints

**No occupation during disruption (non-rerouted trains):**
$$
\phi_{i,k,t} \leq 1 - r_{i,k} \quad \forall i \in T, \; k \in K^{dis}, \; t \in [t_k^{dis,start}, t_k^{dis,end}]
$$

**Rerouted trains must use opposite track:**
$$
\phi_{i,k,t} \leq M \cdot (1 - r_{i,k}) + \sum_{j \in T_{opp}(i)} \phi_{j,k,t}^{opp} \quad \forall i, k \in K^{dis}, t
$$

where $T_{opp}(i)$ denotes trains in the opposite direction.

### 5.5 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution

**Block occupation by at most one train (same direction):**
$$
\sum_{i \in T_d} \phi_{i,k,t} \leq 1 \quad \forall k \in K, \; t \in I, \; d \in D
$$

**Bidirectional conflict on shared (rerouted) track:**
$$
\phi_{i,k,t} + \phi_{j,k,t} \leq 1 + M \cdot (1 - r_{i,k}) + M \cdot (1 - r_{j,k}) \quad \forall i \in T_{up}, j \in T_{down}, k, t
$$

**Train ordering on shared track:**
$$
x_{i,j,k} + x_{j,i,k} = 1 \quad \forall i \neq j, \; k \in K, \; t \in I
$$

**Headway constraint (same direction):**
$$
a_{j,s} - d_{i,s} \geq h^{min} - M \cdot (1 - x_{i,j,k}) \quad \forall i, j \in T_d, \; k, s
$$

### 5.6 Station and Dwell Time Constraints

**Dwell time bounds:**
$$
\tau_{i,s}^{min} \cdot y_{i,s} \leq d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \leq \tau_{i,s}^{max} \cdot y_{i,s} \quad \forall i, s \in S_0
$$

**Arrival-departure consistency:**
$$
a_{i,s} \leq d_{i,s} \quad \forall i, s
$$

**Delay definition:**
$$
\Delta_{i,s}^{arr} \geq a_{i,s} - d_{i,s}^{arr,sch} \quad \forall i, s
$$
$$
\Delta_{i,s}^{dep} \geq d_{i,s} - d_{i,s}^{dep,sch} \quad \forall i, s
$$

### 5.7 Coupling Constraints (Timetable ↔ Speed Profile)

**Arrival time equals position-based arrival:**
$$
a_{i,s} = \sum_{t \in I} t \cdot \phi_{i,k_s,t}^{arr} \quad \forall i, s
$$

where $k_s$ is the block section immediately preceding station $s$.

**Departure time equals position-based departure:**
$$
d_{i,s} = \sum_{t \in I} t \cdot \phi_{i,k_s,t}^{dep} \quad \forall i, s
$$

**Running time consistency:**
$$
\sum_{k \in K} \sum_{t \in I} \phi_{i,k,t} \cdot \Delta t = d_{i,s_{i}^{next}} - a_{i,s_i} \quad \forall i, s_i, s_i^{next}
$$

### 5.8 Cancellation Constraints

**No operations if canceled:**
$$
a_{i,s} \leq M \cdot (1 - z_i) \quad \forall i, s
$$
$$
d_{i,s} \leq M \cdot (1 - z_i) \quad \forall i, s
$$
$$
\phi_{i,k,t} \leq 1 - z_i \quad \forall i, k, t
$$

### 5.9 Origin/Destination Constraints

**Origin departure:**
$$
d_{i,o_i} = d_{i,o_i}^{sch} \quad \forall i \in T
$$

**Destination arrival:**
$$
a_{i,dst_i} \leq d_{i,dst_i}^{sch} + \Delta^{max} \quad \forall i \in T
$$

## 6. Model Summary

The complete MILP formulation is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min \; & c^{delay} \sum_{i,s} (\Delta_{i,s}^{arr} + \Delta_{i,s}^{dep}) + c^{cancel} \sum_i z_i + c^{energy} \sum_i E_i \\
\text{s.t.} \; & \text{Constraints (5.1)–(5.9)} \\
& \text{All variables within their defined domains}
\end{aligned}
$$

## 7. Key Assumptions

1. **Discretization**: Time is discretized into uniform intervals $\Delta t$, and speed into discrete levels, enabling linearization of nonlinear train dynamics.
2. **Single-track segments**: Each physical track consists of two directional tracks; rerouting uses the opposite-direction track.
3. **Homogeneous trains**: Trains of the same class share identical dynamic parameters (relaxable to heterogeneous).
4. **Deterministic disruption**: The disruption time window $[t_k^{dis,start}, t_k^{dis,end}]$ is known and fixed.
5. **No partial cancellations**: A train is either fully operated or fully canceled.
6. **Fixed block sections**: Track topology and block section lengths are predetermined and immutable.
7. **Energy model**: Energy consumption is approximated as a linear function of driving regime and travel distance (neglecting regenerative braking efficiency variations).
8. **First-come-first-served priority**: When two trains conflict on a shared rerouted track, the earlier-arriving train has priority (enforced via $x_{i,j,k}$ variables).
9. **Dwell time flexibility**: Dwell times can be extended within $[\tau^{min}, \tau^{max}]$ to absorb delays.
10. **Path enumeration**: The set of feasible paths $P_i$ (including rerouting options) is pre-generated and finite.
11. **No train overtaking within a block**: Trains maintain their order within a single block section.
12. **Coupling assumption**: The arrival/departure times at stations are exactly synchronized with the position-based arrival/departure derived from the speed profile (enforced by constraints 5.7).

## 8. Notation Summary

| Category | Variables | Count |
|----------|-----------|-------|
| Rescheduling | $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, y_{i,s}, z_i, x_{i,j,k}, w_{i,p}, r_{i,k}$ | $O(|T||S| + |T|^2|K| + \sum_i |P_i|)$ |
| Speed profile | $v_{i,k,t}, s_{i,k,t}, e_{i,k,t}, u_{i,k,t}^{\cdot}, \phi_{i,k,t}$ | $O(|T||K||I|)$ |
| Auxiliary | $\Delta_{i,s}^{arr}, \Delta_{i,s}^{dep}, E_i$ | $O(|T||S|)$ |

This MILP model captures the integrated nature of the TRSMP by simultaneously optimizing train rescheduling decisions (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) and speed profile decisions (acceleration, coasting, braking regimes) under partial segment blockage disruptions, while ensuring conflict-free bidirectional operations on shared track resources.

messages.content: You convert the text of an optimization model into a structured record. Report only what the text states as mathematics, that is, objective functions, equations and inequalities written with symbols. Do not complete, repair, improve or invent anything.

Read the text below and fill in the predefined form.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

The form, as a JSON template: replace every <...> and give each list as many entries as the text requires (possibly none). Write each text field in at most 240 characters (symbols and names in at most 120) and shorten a long expression instead of copying it.

# A Complete MILP Model for Passenger-Oriented Train Rescheduling in Urban Rail Transit with Flexible Train Composition and Rolling Stock Circulation

Below is a complete Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation for the real-time train rescheduling problem described in the input. The model extends Liu et al. (2023a) by incorporating time-varying sectional passenger demands, flexible train composition, and rolling stock circulation, and is intended to be solved within a Model Predictive Control (MPC) rolling-horizon framework.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $S = \{1, 2, \dots, |S|\}$ | Stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $R = \{(s,s+1): s \in S \setminus \{|S|\}\}$ | Sections between consecutive stations |
| $T = \{1, 2, \dots, |T|\}$ | Trains in the planning horizon, indexed by $t$ |
| $K = \{1, 2, \dots, |K|\}$ | Time intervals for the piecewise-constant demand approximation, indexed by $k$ |
| $P = \{1, 2, \dots, |P|\}$ | Discrete time steps in the MPC prediction horizon, indexed by $p$ |
| $C = \{1, 2, \dots, |C|\}$ | Candidate train compositions (number of cars), indexed by $c$ |
| $U = \{1, 2, \dots, |U|\}$ | Rolling-stock units (cars) available in the depot, indexed by $u$ |
| $O = \{1, 2, \dots, |O|\}$ | Origin stations for sectional OD demand, indexed by $o$ |
| $D = \{1, 2, \dots, |D|\}$ | Destination stations for sectional OD demand, indexed by $d$ |

**Assumption (A1):** A single bi-directional metro line is considered. The line is divided into $|S|$ stations and $|S|-1$ sections. Trains run in one direction (the reverse direction is symmetric and omitted for brevity).

**Assumption (A2):** The MPC prediction horizon $[t_0, t_0+H]$ is divided into $|K|$ equal-length intervals of length $\Delta\tau$, so that $H = |K|\cdot \Delta\tau$. Passenger demand is approximated as piecewise constant within each interval.

---

## 2. Parameters

### 2.1 Time and operational parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $t^{run}_{s,s+1}$ | Minimum running time on section $(s,s+1)$ | s |
| $t^{run,max}_{s,s+1}$ | Maximum running time on section $(s,s+1)$ | s |
| $t^{dwl}_{s}$ | Minimum dwell time at station $s$ | s |
| $t^{dwl,max}_{s}$ | Maximum dwell time at station $s$ | s |
| $t^{h,min}$ | Minimum headway between consecutive trains at any station | s |
| $t^{h,max}$ | Maximum headway between consecutive trains at any station | s |
| $t^{turn}$ | Minimum turnaround time at terminal stations | s |
| $\Delta\tau$ | Length of a demand interval | s |
| $H$ | Length of the MPC prediction horizon | s |
| $\Delta t$ | Time step of the discretized MPC horizon | s |

### 2.2 Passenger demand parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $\lambda_{s,k}$ | Arrival rate of passengers at station $s$ during interval $k$ | pax/s |
| $\mu_{o,d,k}$ | Fraction of passengers at station $o$ whose destination is $d$ during interval $k$ | – |
| $\rho_{s,k}$ | Total expected passenger arrivals at station $s$ during interval $k$, $\rho_{s,k} = \lambda_{s,k}\Delta\tau$ | pax |

### 2.3 Train and rolling-stock parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $n_c$ | Number of cars in composition $c$ | cars |
| $cap_c$ | Maximum passenger capacity of composition $c$ | pax |
| $cost^{op}_c$ | Operating cost of running one train with composition $c$ | $/train |
| $cost^{fleet}_u$ | Cost of deploying rolling-stock unit $u$ | $/unit |
| $cost^{coup}_u$ | Cost of coupling/decoupling unit $u$ | $/event |
| $\tilde{a}_{t,s}, \tilde{d}_{t,s}$ | Nominal (planned) arrival/departure times of train $t$ at station $s$ | s |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) | s or pax |

### 2.4 Cost weights

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $w_1$ | Weight on total passenger waiting time |
| $w_2$ | Weight on total in-vehicle passenger travel time |
| $w_3$ | Weight on operating cost (fleet + composition) |
| $w_4$ | Weight on coupling/decoupling cost |
| $w_5$ | Weight on timetable deviation from nominal schedule |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Timetable variables (continuous)

| Symbol | Description | Domain |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{t,s}$ | Arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |
| $d_{t,s}$ | Departure time of train $t$ at station $s$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |
| $r_{t,s}$ | Dwell time of train $t$ at station $s$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |

### 3.2 Stopping plan and composition (binary)

| Symbol | Description | Domain |
|---|---|---|
| $y_{t,s}$ | 1 if train $t$ stops at station $s$, 0 otherwise | $\{0,1\}$ |
| $x_{t,c}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses composition $c$, 0 otherwise | $\{0,1\}$ |

### 3.3 Rolling-stock circulation (binary)

| Symbol | Description | Domain |
|---|---|---|
| $w_{t,u}$ | 1 if rolling-stock unit $u$ is assigned to train $t$, 0 otherwise | $\{0,1\}$ |
| $z_{u,u'}^{t,t'}$ | 1 if unit $u$ from train $t$ is transferred to train $t'$, 0 otherwise | $\{0,1\}$ |
| $\sigma_{t,u}^{cou}$ | 1 if unit $u$ is coupled to train $t$ at its origin, 0 otherwise | $\{0,1\}$ |
| $\sigma_{t,u}^{dec}$ | 1 if unit $u$ is decoupled from train $t$ at its destination, 0 otherwise | $\{0,1\}$ |

### 3.4 Passenger flow variables (continuous)

| Symbol | Description | Domain |
|---|---|---|
| $b_{t,s}$ | Number of passengers boarding train $t$ at station $s$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |
| $e_{t,s}$ | Number of passengers alighting from train $t$ at station $s$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |
| $q_{t,s}$ | Number of passengers waiting at station $s$ just before train $t$ departs | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |
| $q^{rem}_{t,s}$ | Number of passengers remaining at station $s$ after train $t$ departs | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |
| $f_{t,s}$ | Number of passengers on board train $t$ after it departs station $s$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |
| $w^{pax}_{t,s}$ | Passenger waiting time contribution at station $s$ for train $t$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |
| $g_{t,o,d,s}$ | Passengers on train $t$ at station $s$ whose OD is $(o,d)$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |

### 3.5 Deviation variables (continuous, non-negative)

| Symbol | Description | Domain |
|---|---|---|
| $\delta^{+}_{t,s}, \delta^{-}_{t,s}$ | Positive/negative deviation of $d_{t,s}$ from $\tilde{d}_{t,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

The objective minimizes a weighted sum of (i) total passenger waiting time, (ii) in-vehicle passenger travel time, (iii) operating costs (composition and fleet), (iv) coupling/decoupling costs, and (v) timetable deviations from the nominal schedule.

$$
\min \; Z = w_1 \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T}\sum_{s \in S} w^{pax}_{t,s}}_{\text{(i) waiting time}} 
\;+\; w_2 \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T}\sum_{s \in S} f_{t,s} \cdot \Delta t}_{\text{(ii) in-vehicle time}}
\;+\; w_3 \underbrace{\left[\sum_{t \in T}\sum_{c \in C} cost^{op}_c \, x_{t,c} \;+\; \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{u \in U} cost^{fleet}_u \, w_{t,u}\right]}_{\text{(iii) operating cost}}
$$
$$
+\; w_4 \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T}\sum_{u \in U} cost^{coup}_u \left(\sigma^{cou}_{t,u} + \sigma^{dec}_{t,u}\right)}_{\text{(iv) coupling/decoupling cost}}
\;+\; w_5 \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T}\sum_{s \in S} \left(\delta^{+}_{t,s} + \delta^{-}_{t,s}\right)}_{\text{(v) timetable deviation}}
$$

**Assumption (A3):** The in-vehicle travel time is approximated by $\sum_{s} f_{t,s}\Delta t$, which is a standard linearization used in passenger-oriented timetabling (Qi et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2023a).

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train stopping plan

Each train must stop at the terminal stations and may optionally stop at intermediate stations:

$$
y_{t,1} = 1, \quad y_{t,|S|} = 1, \quad \forall t \in T \tag{5.1}
$$

A train cannot depart a station at which it does not stop:

$$
d_{t,s} \leq M \cdot y_{t,s}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{5.2}
$$

### 5.2 Running time constraints

The arrival time at the next station must respect both minimum and maximum running times:

$$
a_{t,s+1} \geq d_{t,s} + t^{run}_{s,s+1} - M(1 - y_{t,s+1}), \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S\setminus\{|S|\} \tag{5.3}
$$

$$
a_{t,s+1} \leq d_{t,s} + t^{run}_{s,s+1} + (t^{run,max}_{s,s+1} - t^{run}_{s,s+1})\,y_{t,s+1}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S\setminus\{|S|\} \tag{5.4}
$$

### 5.3 Dwell time constraints

$$
r_{t,s} \geq t^{dwl}_{s}\,y_{t,s}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{5.5}
$$

$$
r_{t,s} \leq t^{dwl,max}_{s}\,y_{t,s}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{5.6}
$$

$$
d_{t,s} = a_{t,s} + r_{t,s}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{5.7}
$$

### 5.4 Headway constraints

$$
d_{t+1,s} - d_{t,s} \geq t^{h,min}, \quad \forall t \in T\setminus\{|T|\},\; s \in S \tag{5.8}
$$

$$
d_{t+1,s} - d_{t,s} \leq t^{h,max}, \quad \forall t \in T\setminus\{|T|\},\; s \in S \tag{5.9}
$$

### 5.5 Turnaround constraints

$$
a_{t+1,1} \geq d_{t,|S|} + t^{turn}, \quad \forall t \in T\setminus\{|T|\} \tag{5.10}
$$

### 5.6 Composition assignment

Each train uses exactly one composition:

$$
\sum_{c \in C} x_{t,c} = 1, \quad \forall t \in T \tag{5.11}
$$

The number of cars in the assigned composition equals the number of rolling-stock units assigned to the train:

$$
\sum_{u \in U} w_{t,u} = \sum_{c \in C} n_c \, x_{t,c}, \quad \forall t \in T \tag{5.12}
$$

### 5.7 Capacity constraints

The number of passengers on board must not exceed the capacity of the chosen composition:

$$
f_{t,s} \leq \sum_{c \in C} cap_c \, x_{t,c}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{5.13}
$$

### 5.8 Passenger demand and waiting queue

Let $k(t,s)$ denote the demand interval containing $d_{t,s}$, i.e., $k(t,s) = \left\lceil d_{t,s}/\Delta\tau \right\rceil$. The waiting queue evolves as:

$$
q_{t,s} = q^{rem}_{t-1,s} + \rho_{s,k(t,s)}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{5.14}
$$

where $q^{rem}_{0,s}$ is the initial queue known at the start of the MPC horizon.

The remaining queue after train $t$ departs:

$$
q^{rem}_{t,s} = q_{t,s} - b_{t,s}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{5.15}
$$

$$
q^{rem}_{t,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{5.16}
$$

Boarding cannot exceed the number of waiting passengers:

$$
b_{t,s} \leq q_{t,s}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{5.17}
$$

Boarding is zero if the train does not stop:

$$
b_{t,s} \leq M \cdot y_{t,s}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{5.18}
$$

### 5.9 Passenger flow conservation on board

$$
f_{t,s} = f_{t,s-1} + b_{t,s} - e_{t,s}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{5.19}
$$

with $f_{t,0} = 0$ (train starts empty at the origin).

### 5.10 OD-based passenger flow

Passengers with OD $(o,d)$ board at $o$ and alight at $d$:

$$
g_{t,o,d,s} = g_{t,o,d,s-1} + b_{t,s,o,d} - e_{t,s,o,d}, \quad \forall t,o,d,s \tag{5.20}
$$

$$
\sum_{d \in D} b_{t,s,o,d} = b_{t,s}, \quad \forall t,s \tag{5.21}
$$

$$
\sum_{o \in O} e_{t,s,o,d} = e_{t,s}, \quad \forall t,s \tag{5.22}
$$

The demand at station $s$ for destination $d$ during interval $k$ is:

$$
\sum_{t: k(t,s)=k} b_{t,s,o,d} = \lambda_{s,k}\,\mu_{s,d,k}\,\Delta\tau, \quad \forall s,k,o=d \tag{5.23}
$$

**Assumption (A4):** For tractability, OD demand is aggregated by destination within each interval, and passengers are assumed to take the first train on which they can board (first-come-first-served). This is a standard simplification in passenger-oriented timetabling.

### 5.11 Passenger waiting time

The waiting time at station $s$ for passengers boarding train $t$ is approximated by the time elapsed since the previous train departure:

$$
w^{pax}_{t,s} \geq \frac{1}{2}\left(q_{t,s} + q^{rem}_{t-1,s}\right)\left(d_{t,s} - d_{t-1,s}\right), \quad \forall t \in T \setminus \{1\},\; s \in S \tag{5.24}
$$

$$
w^{pax}_{1,s} \geq \frac{1}{2} q_{1,s} \cdot d_{1,s}, \quad \forall s \in S \tag{5.25}
$$

**Assumption (A5):** Equation (5.24) is a linear under-estimate of the trapezoidal area under the queue-length curve, which is a standard MILP-compatible relaxation (see Liu et al., 2023a).

### 5.12 Rolling-stock circulation

Each unit can be assigned to at most one train at any time:

$$
\sum_{t \in T} w_{t,u} \leq 1, \quad \forall u \in U \tag{5.26}
$$

A unit used by train $t$ either enters from the depot, comes from a previous train, or is decoupled at the destination:

$$
\sum_{u' \in U} z_{u',u}^{t-1,t} + \sigma^{cou}_{t,u} = w_{t,u}, \quad \forall t \in T \setminus \{1\},\; u \in U \tag{5.27}
$$

$$
w_{t,u} = \sum_{u' \in U} z_{u,u'}^{t,t+1} + \sigma^{dec}_{t,u}, \quad \forall t \in T \setminus \{|T|\},\; u \in U \tag{5.28}
$$

For the first train in the horizon, units must come from the depot:

$$
w_{1,u} = \sigma^{cou}_{1,u}, \quad \forall u \in U \tag{5.29}
$$

For the last train, units must return to the depot:

$$
w_{|T|,u} = \sigma^{dec}_{|T|,u}, \quad \forall u \in U \tag{5.30}
$$

Coupling/decoupling is only allowed at terminal stations and only between consecutive trains in time:

$$
z_{u,u'}^{t,t'} = 0, \quad \forall |t - t'| > 1,\; u,u' \in U \tag{5.31}
$$

The number of units transferred between two consecutive trains cannot exceed the smaller of the two train sizes:

$$
\sum_{u' \in U} z_{u,u'}^{t,t+1} \leq w_{t,u}, \quad \forall t,\; u \tag{5.32}
$$

$$
\sum_{u \in U} z_{u,u'}^{t,t+1} \leq w_{t+1,u'}, \quad \forall t,\; u' \tag{5.33}
$$

### 5.13 Timetable deviation

$$
d_{t,s} - \tilde{d}_{t,s} = \delta^{+}_{t,s} - \delta^{-}_{t,s}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{5.34}
$$

$$
\delta^{+}_{t,s},\, \delta^{-}_{t,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{5.35}
$$

### 5.14 MPC boundary conditions

The state at the beginning of the horizon (positions of trains, queues, and rolling-stock assignments) is fixed by the previous MPC solution:

$$
a_{1,s} = \hat{a}_{1,s}, \quad f_{1,s} = \hat{f}_{1,s}, \quad q^{rem}_{0,s} = \hat{q}^{rem}_{0,s}, \quad w_{1,u} = \hat{w}_{1,u}, \quad \forall s,u \tag{5.36}
$$

where $\hat{\cdot}$ denotes values carried over from the previous MPC iteration.

**Assumption (A6):** The first train in the horizon has its arrival times fixed (it has already departed when the MPC problem is solved). This is the standard "receding horizon" boundary condition.

---

## 6. MPC Rolling-Horizon Procedure

At each MPC step $n$, with current time $t_n$:

1. **Measure / estimate** the current state: train positions, passenger queues, rolling-stock availability, and realized disturbances.
2. **Predict** future passenger demand $\lambda_{s,k}$ for $k$ such that $[t_n + (k-1)\Delta\tau, t_n + k\Delta\tau]$ lies within the horizon.
3. **Solve** the MILP above over the prediction horizon $[t_n, t_n + H]$.
4. **Implement** the first control action (departure time, composition, and rolling-stock assignment of the next train).
5. **Shift** the horizon forward by one step and repeat.

---

## 7. Linearization Notes and Assumptions

| Item | Treatment | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| $|x|$ in objective | Replaced by $\delta^+ + \delta^-$ | Standard |
| $\min/\max$ of running time | Big-M linearization | Eqs. (5.3)–(5.4) |
| Passenger waiting time (trapezoidal) | Linear under-estimate | Eq. (5.24) |
| OD demand assignment | Aggregated by interval, first-come-first-served | Eq. (5.23) |
| Coupling/decoupling | Binary transfer variables with flow conservation | Eqs. (5.27)–(5.33) |
| Piecewise-constant demand | Approximation via interval index $k(t,s)$ | Section 1 |

**Assumption (A7):** All big-M constants are chosen tight enough to preserve LP relaxation strength. In practice, $M$ can be set to $t^{h,max}$ for time-related constraints and to $\sum_{k} \rho_{s,k}$ for passenger-related constraints.

---

## 8. Summary of the Model

The resulting model is a **mixed-integer linear program (MILP)** with:

- **Continuous variables:** arrival/departure times $a_{t,s}, d_{t,s}$, dwell times $r_{t,s}$, passenger flows $b_{t,s}, e_{t,s}, f_{t,s}, q_{t,s}, q^{rem}_{t,s}, g_{t,o,d,s}$, deviations $\delta^{\pm}_{t,s}$.
- **Binary variables:** stopping plan $y_{t,s}$, composition $x_{t,c}$, rolling-stock assignment $w_{t,u}$, transfer $z_{u,u'}^{t,t'}$, coupling/decoupling $\sigma^{cou}_{t,u}, \sigma^{dec}_{t,u}$.
- **Objective:** weighted sum of passenger waiting time, in-vehicle time, operating cost, coupling/decoupling cost, and timetable deviation.
- **Constraints:** running/dwell time, headway, turnaround, capacity, passenger flow conservation, OD demand satisfaction, rolling-stock circulation, timetable deviation, and MPC boundary conditions.

This MILP can be solved at each MPC step using a commercial solver (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX) for small-to-medium instances, or — as described in the input — accelerated by an LSTM-based learning approach that predicts the integer variables ($x_{t,c}$, $w_{t,u}$, $z_{u,u'}^{t,t'}$, $y_{t,s}$) after presolve pruning, leaving only a continuous LP to be solved online for the timetable variables.
