Text:
# Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

Below is the final, integrated MILP formulation. The model tightly couples timetable decisions (arrival/departure times, train order, routes) with train-control decisions (speed profiles, traction/braking modes) while handling bidirectional rerouting during a partial segment blockage.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t, t'$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $K$ | Set of track segments, indexed by $k$ ($\lvert K\rvert = \lvert S\rvert - 1$) |
| $I$ | Set of discrete time intervals, indexed by $i$ |
| $R = \{N, R\}$ | Routing options: Normal ($N$) or Reverse ($R$, i.e., reroute to opposite track) |
| $D = \{\text{up}, \text{down}\}$ | Physical track directions |
| $J$ | Set of breakpoints for the piecewise-linear energy function |
| $K^{\text{dis}} \subseteq K$ | Subset of disrupted segments |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_k$ | Length of segment $k$ (km) |
| $v^{\min}, v^{\max}$ | Minimum and maximum operating speeds (km/h) |
| $A^{\max}, B^{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration and braking rates (km/h²) |
| $\tau^{\min}_s, \tau^{\max}_s$ | Minimum and maximum dwell times at station $s$ (h) |
| $h^{\min}$ | Minimum safety headway between consecutive trains (h) |
| $T^{\text{dis}}_s, T^{\text{dis}}_e$ | Start and end of the disruption time window (h) |
| $\Delta t$ | Duration of each time interval (h) |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Coefficients of the energy function $e(v) = \alpha + \beta v + \gamma v^{2}$ |
| $v_j, e_j$ | Breakpoint speeds and corresponding energy values, $e_j = \alpha + \beta v_j + \gamma v_j^{2}$ |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (Big-M) |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3, w_4$ | Objective weights for delay, energy, cancellations, and travel time |
| $v^{\text{start}}, v^{\text{end}}$ | Initial and final speeds ($v^{\text{end}} = 0$) |
| $d_t \in D$ | Nominal direction of train $t$ |
| $\text{sch}^{a}_{t,s}, \text{sch}^{d}_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival and departure times of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $p_{k,i} \in \{0,1\}$ | Disruption indicator: $p_{k,i} = 1$ if interval $i$ overlaps $[T^{\text{dis}}_s, T^{\text{dis}}_e]$ for $k \in K^{\text{dis}}$, else $0$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Timetable variables:**
- $a_{t,s} \geq 0$: actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $d_{t,s} \geq 0$: actual departure time of train $t$ from station $s$
- $\delta_{t,s} \geq 0$: delay of train $t$ at station $s$
- $z_{t,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ stops at station $s$, 0 if pass-through
- $c_t \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ is cancelled

**Routing variables:**
- $x_{t,k,r} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses route $r \in \{N, R\}$ on segment $k$
- $y_{t,t',k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ traverses segment $k$ before train $t'$
- $w_{t,k,d} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses physical track $d$ on segment $k$

**Speed and energy variables:**
- $v_{t,k} \geq 0$: representative (average) speed of train $t$ on segment $k$
- $v_{t,k,i} \geq 0$: speed of train $t$ on segment $k$ during interval $i$
- $\text{enter}_{t,k} \geq 0$: time train $t$ enters segment $k$
- $\text{exit}_{t,k} \geq 0$: time train $t$ exits segment $k$
- $b_{t,k,i} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ occupies segment $k$ during interval $i$
- $u_{t,k,i} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses traction on segment $k$ during interval $i$
- $w^{\text{brk}}_{t,k,i} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses braking on segment $k$ during interval $i$
- $E_{t,k,i} \geq 0$: energy consumed by train $t$ on segment $k$ in interval $i$
- $\lambda_{t,k,i,j} \geq 0$: SOS2 weight for breakpoint $j$ (energy model)

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; w_1 \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{s \in S} \delta_{t,s} \;+\; w_2 \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{k \in K}\sum_{i \in I} E_{t,k,i} \;+\; w_3 \sum_{t \in T} c_t \;+\; w_4 \sum_{t \in T}\!\left(a_{t,\text{dest}(t)} - d_{t,\text{orig}(t)}\right)
$$

The four terms capture: (i) total station delays, (ii) total energy consumption, (iii) number of cancelled trains, and (iv) total travel time.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable and Dwell Time (with Pass-Through Logic)

$$
d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \;\geq\; \tau^{\min}_s \, z_{t,s} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \;\leq\; \tau^{\max}_s \, z_{t,s} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

When $z_{t,s} = 0$ (pass-through), both bounds force $d_{t,s} = a_{t,s}$.

### 5.2 Delay Definition

$$
\delta_{t,s} \;\geq\; a_{t,s} - \text{sch}^{a}_{t,s} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\delta_{t,s} \;\geq\; d_{t,s} - \text{sch}^{d}_{t,s} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\delta_{t,s} \;\geq\; 0 \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### 5.3 Initial and Final Conditions

$$
a_{t,\,s_{\text{origin}}(t)} = \text{sch}^{a}_{t,\,s_{\text{origin}}(t)} \qquad \forall t \in T
$$
$$
d_{t,\,s_{\text{dest}}(t)} = a_{t,\,s_{\text{dest}}(t)} \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

### 5.4 Tight Coupling: Timetable ↔ Speed Profile

The entry/exit times of each segment are linked to station times, and the segment traversal time is determined by the representative speed:

$$
\text{enter}_{t,k} \;=\; d_{t,\,s_k} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K
$$
$$
\text{exit}_{t,k} \;=\; a_{t,\,s_{k+1}} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K
$$
$$
L_k \;=\; v_{t,k} \cdot (\text{exit}_{t,k} - \text{enter}_{t,k}) \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K
$$
$$
v^{\min} \;\leq\; v_{t,k} \;\leq\; v^{\max} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K
$$

The product $v_{t,k} \cdot (\text{exit}_{t,k} - \text{enter}_{t,k})$ is linearized via the substitution $u_{t,k} = 1/v_{t,k}$ with a piecewise-linear approximation (SOS2 on breakpoints of $1/v$), or equivalently by fixing $v_{t,k}$ to one of a finite set of candidate speeds and using binary selection variables.

### 5.5 Speed Profile Consistency

The detailed interval speed equals the representative speed whenever the train is on the segment:

$$
v_{t,k,i} \;\leq\; v_{t,k} + M(1 - b_{t,k,i}) \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; i \in I
$$
$$
v_{t,k,i} \;\geq\; v_{t,k} - M(1 - b_{t,k,i}) \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; i \in I
$$
$$
v^{\min}\, b_{t,k,i} \;\leq\; v_{t,k,i} \;\leq\; v^{\max}\, b_{t,k,i} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; i \in I
$$

### 5.6 Segment Occupation (Interval Linking)

$$
\text{enter}_{t,k} \;\leq\; i\,\Delta t + M(1 - b_{t,k,i}) \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; i \in I
$$
$$
\text{exit}_{t,k} \;\geq\; (i+1)\,\Delta t - M(1 - b_{t,k,i}) \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; i \in I
$$
$$
\sum_{i \in I} b_{t,k,i}\,\Delta t \;\geq\; \text{exit}_{t,k} - \text{enter}_{t,k} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K
$$
$$
\sum_{i \in I} b_{t,k,i}\,\Delta t \;\leq\; \text{exit}_{t,k} - \text{enter}_{t,k} + \Delta t \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K
$$

### 5.7 Route Selection

$$
\sum_{r \in R} x_{t,k,r} \;=\; 1 \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K
$$
$$
\sum_{i \in I} b_{t,k,i} \;\geq\; x_{t,k,r} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; r \in R
$$

### 5.8 Time-Indexed Disruption Handling

For disrupted segments during the disruption window, normal-direction travel is forbidden. Let $q_{t,k,i} \in \{0,1\}$ capture whether train $t$ is on disrupted segment $k$ during disruption interval $i$:

$$
q_{t,k,i} \;\geq\; b_{t,k,i} + p_{k,i} - 1 \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K^{\text{dis}},\; i \in I
$$
$$
q_{t,k,i} \;\leq\; b_{t,k,i} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K^{\text{dis}},\; i \in I
$$
$$
q_{t,k,i} \;\leq\; p_{k,i} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K^{\text{dis}},\; i \in I
$$
$$
x_{t,k,N} + q_{t,k,i} \;\leq\; 1 \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K^{\text{dis}},\; i \in I
$$

Outside the disruption window ($p_{k,i} = 0$), the constraint is non-binding, allowing normal-track usage.

### 5.9 Bidirectional Rerouting (Track Capacity)

Each physical track can host at most one train at a time. The mapping from routing decisions to physical tracks is:

$$
w_{t,k,d} \;=\; x_{t,k,N} \cdot \mathbb{1}(d_t = d) + x_{t,k,R} \cdot \mathbb{1}(d_t \neq d) \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; d \in D
$$

This is linearized as:

$$
w_{t,k,d} \;\leq\; x_{t,k,N} + x_{t,k,R} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; d \in D
$$
$$
w_{t,k,d} \;\geq\; x_{t,k,N} \cdot \mathbb{1}(d_t = d) \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; d \in D
$$
$$
w_{t,k,d} \;\geq\; x_{t,k,R} \cdot \mathbb{1}(d_t \neq d) \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; d \in D
$$

The track-capacity constraint is:

$$
\sum_{t \in T} w_{t,k,d}\, b_{t,k,i} \;\leq\; 1 \qquad \forall k \in K,\; d \in D,\; i \in I
$$

### 5.10 Headway Between Same-Direction Trains

For any pair of trains sharing the same physical track on segment $k$:

$$
y_{t,t',k} + y_{t',t,k} \;=\; 1 \qquad \forall k \in K,\; (t,t') \in T^{2}_{\text{same}}(k),\; t \neq t'
$$
$$
\text{exit}_{t,k} + h^{\min} \;\leq\; \text{enter}_{t',k} + M(1 - y_{t,t',k}) \qquad \forall k \in K,\; (t,t') \in T^{2}_{\text{same}}(k)
$$
$$
\text{exit}_{t',k} + h^{\min} \;\leq\; \text{enter}_{t,k} + M\, y_{t,t',k} \qquad \forall k \in K,\; (t,t') \in T^{2}_{\text{same}}(k)
$$

where $T^{2}_{\text{same}}(k)$ is the set of ordered train pairs using the same physical track on segment $k$.

### 5.11 Speed Dynamics (Acceleration/Deceleration)

$$
v_{t,k,i+1} \;\leq\; v_{t,k,i} + A^{\max} \cdot \Delta t \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; i \in I
$$
$$
v_{t,k,i+1} \;\geq\; v_{t,k,i} - B^{\max} \cdot \Delta t \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; i \in I
$$

### 5.12 Traction/Braking Mode Selection

$$
u_{t,k,i} + w^{\text{brk}}_{t,k,i} \;\leq\; 1 \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; i \in I
$$
$$
v_{t,k,i+1} \;=\; v_{t,k,i} + \left(A^{\max} \cdot u_{t,k,i} - B^{\max} \cdot w^{\text{brk}}_{t,k,i}\right) \cdot \Delta t \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; i \in I
$$

### 5.13 Initial and Final Speed Conditions

$$
v_{t,\,k^{\text{first}}(t)} \;=\; v^{\text{start}} \qquad \forall t \in T
$$
$$
v_{t,\,k^{\text{last}}(t)} \;=\; v^{\text{end}} \;=\; 0 \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

### 5.14 Piecewise-Linear Energy Model

For each $(t,k,i)$, the energy function is approximated by a convex combination of breakpoints (SOS2):

$$
\sum_{j \in J} \lambda_{t,k,i,j} \;=\; 1 \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; i \in I
$$
$$
v_{t,k,i} \;=\; \sum_{j \in J} \lambda_{t,k,i,j}\, v_j \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; i \in I
$$
$$
E_{t,k,i} \;=\; \sum_{j \in J} \lambda_{t,k,i,j}\, e_j \cdot b_{t,k,i} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; i \in I
$$
$$
\lambda_{t,k,i,j} \;\geq\; 0 \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; i \in I,\; j \in J
$$
$$
\text{SOS2}\!\left(\{\lambda_{t,k,i,j}\}_{j \in J}\right) \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; i \in I
$$

> **Note**: For a strictly convex $e(v)$, the chord-based (incremental) formulation with binary segment-selection variables $\mu_{t,k,i,j} \in \{0,1\}$ provides a tighter approximation.

### 5.15 Cancellation Modeling

$$
a_{t,s} \;\leq\; M(1 - c_t) + \text{sch}^{a}_{t,s} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \text{ after cancellation point}
$$
$$
b_{t,k,i} \;\leq\; 1 - c_t \qquad \forall t \in T,\; k \text{ after cancellation point},\; i \in I
$$

If a train is cancelled ($c_t = 1$), all downstream arrival times and segment occupations are relaxed.

### 5.16 Variable Domain Constraints

$$
a_{t,s},\, d_{t,s},\, \delta_{t,s},\, v_{t,k},\, v_{t,k,i},\, \text{enter}_{t,k},\, \text{exit}_{t,k},\, E_{t,k,i},\, \lambda_{t,k,i,j} \;\geq\; 0
$$
$$
x_{t,k,r},\, y_{t,t',k},\, z_{t,s},\, b_{t,k,i},\, u_{t,k,i},\, w^{\text{brk}}_{t,k,i},\, w_{t,k,d},\, q_{t,k,i},\, c_t \;\in\; \{0, 1\}
$$

---

## 6. Modeling Notes and Assumptions

### 6.1 Linearization Techniques
- **Reciprocal speed ($L_k/v$)**: Handled via the product form $L_k = v_{t,k} \cdot (\text{exit}_{t,k} - \text{enter}_{t,k})$ with $v_{t,k}$ discretized to candidate values, or via piecewise-linear approximation of $1/v$ using SOS2.
- **Energy function**: The quadratic term $\gamma v^{2}$ is approximated by a piecewise-linear function via SOS2 variables $\lambda_{t,k,i,j}$.
- **Big-M constraints**: All disjunctive constraints use sufficiently large $M$ values; tight $M$ values improve LP relaxation.

### 6.2 Key Assumptions
1. Time is discretized into uniform intervals of length $\Delta t$.
2. Each segment has two physical tracks (one per direction); rerouting means using the opposite track.
3. Trains cannot pass each other on the same physical track segment.
4. The disruption affects only the normal-direction track on segments $k \in K^{\text{dis}}$ during $[T^{\text{dis}}_s, T^{\text{dis}}_e]$.
5. Acceleration and braking rates are constant at $A^{\max}$ and $B^{\max}$.
6. Dwell times are bounded by $\tau^{\min}_s$ and $\tau^{\max}_s$; pass-through stations have zero dwell.
7. Energy consumption follows $e(v) = \alpha + \beta v + \gamma v^{2}$ (tractive effort model).
8. Cancellation is allowed as a last resort, penalized by $w_3$.

### 6.3 Model Strengths
- **Unified framework**: Timetable, routing, and speed-profile decisions are jointly optimized, eliminating infeasibilities between operational and control levels.
- **Bidirectional conflict resolution**: The track-capacity constraint (5.9) and headway constraints (5.10) ensure conflict-free operation when trains share rerouted tracks.
- **Disruption-aware**: The time-indexed disruption indicator $p_{k,i}$ allows normal operations outside the disruption window while enforcing rerouting during the window.
- **Energy-aware**: The piecewise-linear energy model captures the convex relationship between speed and energy consumption, enabling energy-efficient speed profiles.

This MILP formulation provides a rigorous foundation for the TRSMP under partial segment blockages, enabling coordinated rescheduling and energy-efficient speed management in high-speed railway operations.

Text:
# MILP Formulation for Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

Below is a complete mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation inspired by the multi-stage framework described in the input. The model captures **rerouting**, **reordering**, and **rescheduling** of trains in a real-time conflict resolution context. Two variants are presented:

- **Model A (Sub-optimal):** Rerouting + Reordering without delay propagation (fast, low-complexity).
- **Model B (Optimal):** Extends Model A with delay propagation (guarantees global optimum).

---

## 1. Assumptions

1. The rail network is represented at a **macroscopic level** (sections/blocks), neglecting detailed signaling logic except for safety overlaps.
2. Trains are assumed to be **point-mass** entities traveling at a nominal speed on each section.
3. **Primary delays** are exogenous inputs (already known at the moment of rescheduling).
4. **Secondary delays** are decision variables to be minimized.
5. A finite set of **alternative routes** has been pre-generated for each train (e.g., via a TRSP solver).
6. **Conflict points** are locations where two or more routes may share the same track resource.
7. **FIFO** is not enforced; reordering is allowed.
8. The planning horizon is discretized in time (continuous-time relaxation).
9. Energy consumption is approximated as a linear function of running time (optional objective term).
10. Safety overlaps (margins behind stop signals) are modeled as additional headway constraints.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $I$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j, k$ |
| $R_i$ | Set of feasible alternative routes for train $i$, indexed by $r$ |
| $C$ | Set of conflict points (shared resources), indexed by $c$ |
| $S$ | Set of track sections, indexed by $s$ |
| $E$ | Set of directed edges in the network |
| $O_s$ | Set of safety overlap zones behind signals on section $s$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $t_i^{0}$ | Original scheduled (planned) time of train $i$ at reference point | min |
| $d_i^{prim}$ | Primary (exogenous) delay of train $i$ | min |
| $a_{i,r,c}$ | 1 if route $r$ of train $i$ traverses conflict point $c$ | binary |
| $a_{i,r,s}$ | 1 if route $r$ of train $i$ traverses section $s$ | binary |
| $h_c$ | Minimum headway time at conflict point $c$ | min |
| $\tau_s^{run}$ | Minimum running time on section $s$ | min |
| $o_s$ | Safety overlap margin behind stop signal on section $s$ | min |
| $L_s$ | Length of section $s$ | m |
| $v_i$ | Nominal speed of train $i$ | m/min |
| $e_i$ | Specific energy consumption of train $i$ | kWh/min |
| $w_1, w_2$ | Weights for delay and energy in objective | – |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) | min |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### Route & Ordering Variables
- $x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is assigned route $r$.
- $y_{i,j,c} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ at conflict point $c$ (i.e., $i$ passes $c$ before $j$).
- $z_{i,j,c} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trains $i$ and $j$ are both routed through conflict point $c$ (i.e., they actually conflict at $c$).

### Timing Variables
- $\tau_i \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$: Actual (rescheduled) time of train $i$ at the reference conflict point.
- $\tau_{i,s}^{arr}, \tau_{i,s}^{dep} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$: Arrival/departure times of train $i$ at section $s$.
- $\delta_i \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$: Secondary delay of train $i$.

### Pair-wise Waiting Variables (Model B only)
- $w_{i,j} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is delayed because it waits for train $j$.
- $\Delta_{i,j} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$: Additional delay propagated from train $j$ to train $i$.

### Auxiliary Variables
- $\rho_{i,c} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ traverses conflict point $c$ (route-dependent).
- $E_i \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$: Energy consumption of train $i$.

---

## 5. Objective Function

**Primary objective — minimize total secondary delay (Model A):**
$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{i \in I} \delta_i
$$

**Extended objective — minimize weighted sum of secondary delay and energy (Model B):**
$$
\min \; Z = w_1 \sum_{i \in I} \delta_i + w_2 \sum_{i \in I} E_i
$$

where $E_i = e_i \cdot \sum_{s \in S} a_{i,r^*,s} \cdot (\tau_{i,s}^{dep} - \tau_{i,s}^{arr})$ and $r^*$ is the selected route of train $i$.

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Route Selection

**(C1) Each train must be assigned exactly one route:**
$$
\sum_{r \in R_i} x_{i,r} = 1, \quad \forall i \in I
$$

**(C2) Route–conflict linkage:**
$$
\rho_{i,c} = \sum_{r \in R_i} a_{i,r,c} \cdot x_{i,r}, \quad \forall i \in I,\; c \in C
$$

### 6.2 Conflict Detection

**(C3) Two trains conflict at $c$ if and only if both traverse $c$:**
$$
z_{i,j,c} \leq \rho_{i,c}, \quad z_{i,j,c} \leq \rho_{j,c}, \quad \forall i,j \in I,\; c \in C
$$
$$
z_{i,j,c} \geq \rho_{i,c} + \rho_{j,c} - 1, \quad \forall i,j \in I,\; c \in C
$$

### 6.3 Train Ordering at Conflict Points

**(C4) Mutual exclusion of ordering (at most one ordering per pair):**
$$
y_{i,j,c} + y_{j,i,c} \leq 1, \quad \forall i,j \in I,\; c \in C
$$

**(C5) Ordering only applies when both trains are in conflict:**
$$
y_{i,j,c} \leq z_{i,j,c}, \quad y_{j,i,c} \leq z_{i,j,c}, \quad \forall i,j \in I,\; c \in C
$$

**(C6) Transitivity of ordering (consistency across conflict points):**
$$
y_{i,j,c} + y_{j,k,c} - 1 \leq y_{i,k,c}, \quad \forall i,j,k \in I,\; c \in C
$$

### 6.4 Timing Constraints

**(C7) Lower bound on actual time (primary delay):**
$$
\tau_i \geq t_i^{0} + d_i^{prim}, \quad \forall i \in I
$$

**(C8) Section traversal time (running time):**
$$
\tau_{i,s}^{dep} - \tau_{i,s}^{arr} \geq \tau_s^{run} - M(1 - \rho_{i,s}), \quad \forall i \in I,\; s \in S
$$

### 6.5 Headway and Safety Constraints

**(C9) Minimum headway between consecutive trains at conflict point $c$:**
$$
\tau_j - \tau_i \geq h_c - M(1 - y_{i,j,c}) - M(1 - z_{i,j,c}), \quad \forall i,j \in I,\; c \in C
$$

**(C10) Safety overlap behind stop signal on section $s$:**
$$
\tau_{j,s}^{arr} - \tau_{i,s}^{dep} \geq o_s - M(1 - y_{i,j,s}) - M(1 - z_{i,j,s}), \quad \forall i,j \in I,\; s \in S
$$

**(C11) Block-section occupancy (no two trains simultaneously on $s$):**
$$
\tau_{j,s}^{arr} \geq \tau_{i,s}^{dep} + \tau_s^{run} - M(1 - y_{i,j,s}), \quad \forall i,j \in I,\; s \in S
$$

### 6.6 Secondary Delay Definition

**(C12) Secondary delay of train $i$:**
$$
\delta_i \geq \tau_i - t_i^{0}, \quad \forall i \in I
$$
$$
\delta_i \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in I
$$

### 6.7 Delay Propagation (Model B — Optimal)

**(C13) Pair-wise waiting indicator:**
$$
w_{i,j} \leq \sum_{c \in C} y_{j,i,c}, \quad \forall i,j \in I
$$
$$
w_{i,j} \geq y_{j,i,c} - (1 - z_{i,j,c}), \quad \forall i,j \in I,\; c \in C
$$

**(C14) Delay propagation from train $j$ to train $i$:**
$$
\Delta_{i,j} \geq h_c \cdot y_{j,i,c} - M(1 - z_{i,j,c}), \quad \forall i,j \in I,\; c \in C
$$
$$
\Delta_{i,j} \geq 0, \quad \forall i,j \in I
$$

**(C15) Total secondary delay includes propagated delays:**
$$
\delta_i \geq \tau_i - t_i^{0} - \sum_{j \in I} \Delta_{i,j}, \quad \forall i \in I
$$

**(C16) Causality: train $i$ cannot depart before it has arrived:**
$$
\tau_{i,s}^{dep} \geq \tau_{i,s}^{arr}, \quad \forall i \in I,\; s \in S
$$

### 6.8 Linkage Between Sub-problems (Multi-stage Coupling)

**(C17) Fixing routes from Model A as input to Model B:**
$$
x_{i,r}^{A} = x_{i,r}^{B}, \quad \forall i \in I,\; r \in R_i
$$

**(C18) Optional fixing of ordering from Model A:**
$$
y_{i,j,c}^{A} \leq y_{i,j,c}^{B} + (1 - \alpha_{i,j}), \quad \forall i,j \in I,\; c \in C
$$
where $\alpha_{i,j} \in \{0,1\}$ is a parameter indicating whether the ordering from Model A is enforced (1) or relaxed (0).

---

## 7. Model Variants Summary

| Feature | Model A (Sub-optimal) | Model B (Optimal) |
|---|---|---|
| Route selection | ✓ | ✓ (fixed from A) |
| Train reordering | ✓ | ✓ (fixed from A) |
| Rescheduling | ✓ | ✓ |
| Delay propagation | ✗ | ✓ |
| Safety overlaps | ✓ | ✓ |
| Energy in objective | optional | optional |
| Computational complexity | low | medium-high |
| Solution quality | sub-optimal | global optimum |

---

## 8. Notes on Implementation

1. **Big-M values** must be chosen carefully (e.g., $M = \max_i t_i^{0} + \max_i d_i^{prim} + \sum_c h_c$) to avoid weak relaxations.
2. **Symmetry breaking**: Add $y_{i,j,c} = 0$ for $i < j$ if ordering is symmetric, or impose $i < j \Rightarrow y_{i,j,c} \geq y_{j,i,c}$ to halve the search space.
3. **Pre-processing**: The TRSP (Train Route Selection Problem) can be solved first to reduce $|R_i|$ before running the MILP, as suggested in Samà et al. (2016).
4. **Decomposition**: For large networks, Benders decomposition or iterative re-solving (rerouting → reordering → rescheduling) can be applied.
5. **Warm-starting**: Use the solution of Model A as a warm-start for Model B to reduce runtime.

---

This MILP formulation captures the essential structure of the rtRTMP described in the input, including the decomposition into rerouting, reordering, and rescheduling sub-problems, the pair-wise waiting interpretation for the sub-optimal variant, and the delay-propagation extension for the optimal variant.

Text:
# Final MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Below is the complete, refined Mixed-Integer Linear Programming model that integrates the Train Rescheduling Problem (TRP) and Train Speed Management Problem (TSMP) for high-speed railways under partial segment blockages.

---

## 1. Assumptions

> **A1.** The railway line is double-track, with stations $S = \{1, \ldots, N_S\}$ and segments $K = \{1, \ldots, N_K\}$ connecting consecutive stations ($N_K = N_S - 1$).

> **A2.** Time is discretized into intervals $I = \{1, \ldots, N_I\}$ of length $\Delta t$ (minutes).

> **A3.** Each train $i$ has fixed origin $O_i$ and destination $D_i$ stations.

> **A4.** Train dynamics follow a point-mass model with constant mass $M_i$.

> **A5.** Energy consumption is approximated by a piecewise-linear function of speed and acceleration.

> **A6.** A minimum headway time $h_{min}$ is enforced between consecutive trains on the same track.

> **A7.** Dwell time at each station is bounded: $\tau_{min} \leq \sigma_{i,s} - \tau_{i,s} \leq \tau_{max}$.

> **A8.** Disruption affects segment $d \in D$ during time window $W \subset I$; the nominal-direction track of segment $d$ is blocked during $W$.

> **A9.** Trains may be cancelled at penalty $\psi$ per train.

> **A10.** Trains can be rerouted to the opposite (non-blocked) track during the disruption, with single-track bidirectional operation enforced.

> **A11.** Position dynamics are linearized using the trapezoidal rule.

> **A12.** The quadratic speed term $v^2$ in the energy function is approximated via SOS2 piecewise-linear segments.

---

## 2. Sets

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T = \{1, \ldots, N_T\}$ | Set of trains |
| $S = \{1, \ldots, N_S\}$ | Set of stations (ordered along the line) |
| $K = \{1, \ldots, N_K\}$ | Set of segments, $N_K = N_S - 1$ |
| $I = \{1, \ldots, N_I\}$ | Set of discrete time intervals |
| $D \subset K$ | Set of disrupted segments |
| $W \subset I$ | Disruption time window |
| $Dir = \{0, 1\}$ | Track directions: $0$ = nominal, $1$ = opposite |
| $B = \{1, \ldots, N_B\}$ | Breakpoints for piecewise-linear $v^2$ approximation |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $L_k$ | Length of segment $k$ | km |
| $v_{min}, v_{max}$ | Min/max operating speed | km/h |
| $a_{max}, b_{max}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration | km/h per interval |
| $M_i$ | Mass of train $i$ | tons |
| $\Delta t$ | Time interval length | min |
| $\tau_{min}, \tau_{max}$ | Min/max dwell time at stations | min |
| $h_{min}$ | Minimum headway time | min |
| $\rho_1, \rho_2, \rho_3$ | Weights for delay, energy, cancellation | – |
| $\psi$ | Cancellation penalty per train | – |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Energy coefficients | kWh |
| $O_i, D_i$ | Origin/destination station of train $i$ | – |
| $t^{sched}_{arr,i,s}, t^{sched}_{dep,i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival/departure times | min |
| $M$ | Big-M constant | – |
| $v^b_b$ | Speed value at breakpoint $b \in B$ | km/h |
| $\phi^b_b$ | Linearized value $(v^b_b)^2$ | (km/h)² |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

**Continuous variables:**

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $\tau_{i,s}$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ | min |
| $\sigma_{i,s}$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ | min |
| $\delta_{i,s}$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ | min |
| $v_{i,k,t}$ | Speed of train $i$ on segment $k$ in interval $t$ | km/h |
| $p_{i,k,t}$ | Position of train $i$ on segment $k$ at end of interval $t$ | km |
| $e_{i,k,t}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $k$ in interval $t$ | kWh |
| $E_i$ | Total energy consumption of train $i$ | kWh |
| $a^+_{i,k,t}, a^-_{i,k,t}$ | Positive/negative acceleration parts | km/h per interval |
| $\lambda^b_{i,k,t}$ | SOS2 weight for breakpoint $b$ on segment $k$, interval $t$ | – |

**Binary variables:**

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $x_{i,k,t}$ | 1 if train $i$ occupies segment $k$ in interval $t$ |
| $r_{i,k,t}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses the nominal direction on segment $k$ in interval $t$ |
| $z_{i,j,k,t}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $k$ in interval $t$ |
| $w_{i,k,t}$ | 1 if train $i$ enters segment $k$ at interval $t$ |
| $f_{i,k,t}$ | 1 if train $i$ exits segment $k$ at interval $t$ |
| $c_i$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \rho_1 \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \delta_{i,s} \;+\; \rho_2 \sum_{i \in T} E_i \;+\; \rho_3 \sum_{i \in T} c_i
$$

where
$$
E_i \;=\; \sum_{k \in K} \sum_{t \in I} e_{i,k,t}
$$

The objective minimizes a weighted sum of **total delay**, **total energy consumption**, and **number of cancelled trains**.

---

## 6. Constraints

### (1) Delay Definition

$$
\delta_{i,s} \;\geq\; \tau_{i,s} - t^{sched}_{arr,i,s}, \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\delta_{i,s} \;\geq\; 0, \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (2) Dwell Time Constraints

$$
\sigma_{i,s} - \tau_{i,s} \;\geq\; \tau_{min} \cdot (1 - c_i), \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\sigma_{i,s} - \tau_{i,s} \;\leq\; \tau_{max} \cdot (1 - c_i) + M \cdot c_i, \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (3) Running Time Consistency (Timetable ↔ Speed Profile)

For each train $i$ and segment $k$ connecting stations $s$ and $s+1$:

$$
\sum_{t \in I} x_{i,k,t} \cdot \Delta t \;=\; \sigma_{i,s+1} - \tau_{i,s} - \tau_{min} \cdot (1 - c_i), \qquad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K
$$

### (4) Position Dynamics (Trapezoidal Rule)

$$
p_{i,k,t} \;=\; p_{i,k,t-1} + \frac{\Delta t}{2} \left( v_{i,k,t-1} + v_{i,k,t} \right) \cdot x_{i,k,t}, \qquad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K,\; t \in I
$$
$$
0 \;\leq\; p_{i,k,t} \;\leq\; L_k \cdot x_{i,k,t}, \qquad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K,\; t \in I
$$

### (5) Train Flow Conservation at Stations

$$
\sum_{k:\, s \text{ is start of } k} w_{i,k,t} \;=\; \sum_{k:\, s \text{ is end of } k} f_{i,k,t-1}, \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S,\; t \in I
$$

### (6) Segment Entry / Exit Linking

$$
w_{i,k,t} \;\leq\; x_{i,k,t}, \qquad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K,\; t \in I
$$
$$
f_{i,k,t} \;\leq\; x_{i,k,t}, \qquad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K,\; t \in I
$$
$$
\sum_{t \in I} w_{i,k,t} \;=\; 1 - c_i, \qquad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K
$$
$$
\sum_{t \in I} f_{i,k,t} \;=\; 1 - c_i, \qquad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K
$$

### (7) Speed Limits

$$
v_{min} \cdot x_{i,k,t} \;\leq\; v_{i,k,t} \;\leq\; v_{max} \cdot x_{i,k,t}, \qquad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K,\; t \in I
$$

### (8) Acceleration / Deceleration Limits

$$
v_{i,k,t} - v_{i,k,t-1} \;\leq\; a_{max} \cdot \Delta t + M \cdot (1 - x_{i,k,t}) + M \cdot (1 - x_{i,k,t-1}), \quad \forall i,k,t
$$
$$
v_{i,k,t-1} - v_{i,k,t} \;\leq\; b_{max} \cdot \Delta t + M \cdot (1 - x_{i,k,t}) + M \cdot (1 - x_{i,k,t-1}), \quad \forall i,k,t
$$

### (9) Segment Capacity (One Train per Direction per Interval)

$$
\sum_{i \in T} x_{i,k,t} \cdot r_{i,k,t} \;\leq\; 1, \qquad \forall k \in K,\; t \in I
$$
$$
\sum_{i \in T} x_{i,k,t} \cdot (1 - r_{i,k,t}) \;\leq\; 1, \qquad \forall k \in K,\; t \in I
$$

### (10) Disruption Constraints

For each disrupted segment $k \in D$ and interval $t \in W$:

$$
r_{i,k,t} \;=\; 0, \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

### (11) Bidirectional Conflict Resolution (Headway on Shared Track)

For trains $i, j \in T$ ($i < j$), segment $k \in K$, interval $t \in I$:

$$
z_{i,j,k,t} + z_{j,i,k,t} \;\leq\; 1, \qquad \forall i,j \in T,\; k \in K,\; t \in I
$$
$$
x_{i,k,t} + x_{j,k,t} - 1 \;\leq\; z_{i,j,k,t} + z_{j,i,k,t}, \qquad \forall i,j \in T,\; k \in K,\; t \in I
$$

### (12) Headway Constraints (Same Direction)

For trains $i, j \in T$ ($i \neq j$), segment $k \in K$, interval $t \in I$:

$$
\sum_{t' = t}^{t + h_{min}/\Delta t - 1} x_{j,k,t'} \;\geq\; z_{i,j,k,t} \cdot \frac{h_{min}}{\Delta t} - M \cdot (1 - z_{i,j,k,t})
$$

### (13) Train Ordering at Stations

For trains $i, j \in T$ ($i \neq j$) at station $s \in S$:

$$
\sum_{t \in I} t \cdot w_{i,k,t} \;\leq\; \sum_{t \in I} t \cdot w_{j,k,t} + M \cdot (1 - o_{i,j,s}), \qquad \forall i,j \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
o_{i,j,s} + o_{j,i,s} \;=\; 1, \qquad \forall i,j \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (14) Energy Consumption (Linearized)

**Step 1 — Acceleration decomposition:**
$$
a^+_{i,k,t} - a^-_{i,k,t} \;=\; v_{i,k,t} - v_{i,k,t-1}, \qquad \forall i \in T,\; k \in K,\; t \in I
$$
$$
a^+_{i,k,t} \;\geq\; 0, \qquad a^-_{i,k,t} \;\geq\; 0
$$

**Step 2 — Piecewise-linear approximation of $v^2$ via SOS2:**

For each $(i,k,t)$, define weights $\lambda^b_{i,k,t} \in [0,1]$ for $b \in B$:

$$
\sum_{b \in B} \lambda^b_{i,k,t} \;=\; 1, \qquad \lambda^b_{i,k,t} \;\geq\; 0
$$
$$
v_{i,k,t} \;=\; \sum_{b \in B} \lambda^b_{i,k,t} \cdot v^b_b, \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$
$$
v^2_{i,k,t} \;\approx\; \sum_{b \in B} \lambda^b_{i,k,t} \cdot \phi^b_b, \qquad \forall i,k,t
$$

**Step 3 — Energy lower bound:**
$$
e_{i,k,t} \;\geq\; \alpha \cdot v_{i,k,t} + \beta \cdot v^2_{i,k,t} + \gamma \cdot a^+_{i,k,t} + \gamma \cdot a^-_{i,k,t}, \quad \forall i,k,t
$$

### (15) Cancellation Constraints

$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{i,k,t} \;\leq\; M \cdot (1 - c_i), \qquad \forall i \in T,\; t \in I
$$

### (16) Origin / Destination Constraints

For each train $i \in T$:

$$
\tau_{i,O_i} \;=\; \sigma_{i,O_i}, \qquad \text{(train starts at scheduled departure)}
$$
$$
\sigma_{i,D_i} \;=\; \tau_{i,D_i}, \qquad \text{(train ends at arrival)}
$$
$$
\sigma_{i,s} \;\geq\; \tau_{i,s}, \qquad \forall s \in S \setminus \{O_i, D_i\}
$$

### (17) Variable Domain Constraints

$$
x_{i,k,t}, r_{i,k,t}, z_{i,j,k,t}, w_{i,k,t}, f_{i,k,t}, c_i \;\in\; \{0, 1\}, \qquad \forall i,j,k,t
$$
$$
\tau_{i,s}, \sigma_{i,s}, \delta_{i,s}, v_{i,k,t}, p_{i,k,t}, e_{i,k,t}, E_i, a^+_{i,k,t}, a^-_{i,k,t}, \lambda^b_{i,k,t} \;\geq\; 0
$$

---

## 7. Linearization Techniques Summary

| Technique | Applied To | Purpose |
|-----------|------------|---------|
| **Big-M** | Dwell time (2), acceleration limits (8), headway (12), ordering (13), cancellation (15) | Activates/deactivates constraints based on binary state |
| **Piecewise-linear (SOS2)** | $v^2_{i,k,t}$ in energy (14) | Convexifies the quadratic speed term |
| **Absolute-value decomposition** | $\|v_{i,k,t} - v_{i,k,t-1}\|$ in energy (14) | Splits into $a^+ + a^-$ |
| **Indicator-product linearization** | $x_{i,k,t} \cdot r_{i,k,t}$ in capacity (9) | Uses $x_{i,k,t}$ as a multiplier on the binary direction |
| **Trapezoidal rule** | Position dynamics (4) | Linearizes continuous motion |

---

## 8. Integration of TRP and TSMP

The model achieves a **tight coupling** between the Train Rescheduling Problem (TRP) and the Train Speed Management Problem (TSMP) through three key linking mechanisms:

1. **Running-time linkage (Constraint 3):** The sum of occupancy intervals $x_{i,k,t}$ on each segment equals the timetable-derived travel time $\sigma_{i,s+1} - \tau_{i,s}$. This means that any change in the timetable (rescheduling) directly affects the feasible speed profiles, and vice versa.

2. **Position dynamics (Constraint 4):** The trapezoidal rule enforces that the actual distance traveled by the train (via $v_{i,k,t}$) is consistent with the segment length $L_k$ and the occupancy pattern. This ensures that the chosen speed profile is physically realizable within the scheduled time window.

3. **Joint objective:** The objective simultaneously penalizes delay (TRP metric) and energy (TSMP metric). The optimizer naturally trades off faster running (more energy, less delay) against slower running (less energy, more delay), producing a Pareto-optimal joint solution.

**Rescheduling levers** include: adjusting $\tau_{i,s}$ and $\sigma_{i,s}$ (timetable shifts), choosing $r_{i,k,t}$ (rerouting around disruption), setting $c_i$ (cancellation), and reordering trains via $z_{i,j,k,t}$ and $o_{i,j,s}$. **Speed-management levers** include: choosing $v_{i,k,t}$ (speed profile) and $a^+_{i,k,t}, a^-_{i,k,t}$ (acceleration pattern), which determine $e_{i,k,t}$ and hence $E_i$.

The disruption handling is fully integrated: Constraint (10) blocks the nominal direction, forcing affected trains to either use the opposite direction (single-track operation, handled by Constraints 9 and 11) or to wait (handled by adjusting $\tau$ and $\sigma$), with all consequences propagating through the running-time and energy constraints.

---

This completes the MILP formulation. The model is fully linear (after piecewise-linear approximation of $v^2$) and can be solved by standard MILP solvers such as Gurobi, CPLEX, or SCIP.

# Complete MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

After comparing the three generated models, I select **Model 2** as the best — it has the most rigorous constraint structure, explicit occupancy variables, proper handling of bidirectional conflicts (only during disruption), well-explained PWL linearization, and a thorough explanation section. Below I present it with minor refinements for clarity and correctness.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Set | Description |
|---|---|
| $T = \{1,\dots,m\}$ | Set of trains |
| $S = \{1,\dots,n\}$ | Set of stations (ordered along the line) |
| $B = \{1,\dots,n-1\}$ | Set of blocks; block $b$ connects station $b$ and $b+1$ |
| $K = \{1,\dots,T_{\max}\}$ | Discrete time steps, step length $\Delta t$ |
| $I_b = \{1,\dots,N_b\}$ | Speed-control intervals within block $b$ |
| $D = \{k : k_{\text{dis}}^{\text{start}} \le k \le k_{\text{dis}}^{\text{end}}\}$ | Disruption window (in time steps) |
| $b^*$ | Disrupted block |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Set of breakpoints for PWL approximation of $v^2$ and $a^2$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Parameter | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ | m |
| $v_{\max}, v_{\min}$ | Max/min operating speed | m/s |
| $a_{\max}, b_{\max}$ | Max acceleration / braking | m/s² |
| $d_s^{\min}, d_s^{\max}$ | Min/max dwell time at station $s$ | s |
| $\sigma_{t,s}^{\text{dep}}, \sigma_{t,s}^{\text{arr}}$ | Scheduled departure/arrival times | s |
| $o_t, d_t$ | Origin / destination station of train $t$ | – |
| $\text{dir}_t \in \{+1,-1\}$ | Nominal direction of train $t$ | – |
| $h$ | Minimum headway between consecutive trains | s |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (big-M) | – |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Energy coefficients ($E = \alpha v^2 + \beta a^2 + \gamma$) | – |
| $\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \lambda_3, \lambda_4$ | Objective weights | – |
| $\bar{v}_p$ | Breakpoints for PWL of $v^2$ | m/s |
| $\tau_{t,b}^{\min}$ | Min time steps to traverse block $b$ at $v_{\max}$ | – |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Binary (discrete-event) variables**

$$
\begin{aligned}
x_{t,s,k} &\in \{0,1\} &&\text{train } t \text{ departs station } s \text{ at time } k \\
y_{t,b,k} &\in \{0,1\} &&\text{train } t \text{ enters block } b \text{ on its nominal track at time } k \\
z_{t,b,k} &\in \{0,1\} &&\text{train } t \text{ enters block } b \text{ on the opposite track (rerouted) at time } k \\
r_{t,b} &\in \{0,1\} &&\text{train } t \text{ is rerouted on block } b \\
\text{arr}_{t,s,k} &\in \{0,1\} &&\text{train } t \text{ arrives at station } s \text{ at time } k \\
c_t &\in \{0,1\} &&\text{train } t \text{ is cancelled} \\
u_{t,b,k} &\in \{0,1\} &&\text{train } t \text{ occupies block } b \text{ during time step } k
\end{aligned}
$$

**Continuous (speed/energy) variables**

$$
\begin{aligned}
v_{t,b,i} &\in [0, v_{\max}] &&\text{speed of train } t \text{ in interval } i \text{ of block } b \\
a_{t,b,i} &\in [-b_{\max}, a_{\max}] &&\text{acceleration of train } t \text{ in interval } i \text{ of block } b \\
w_{t,b,i} &\ge 0 &&\text{auxiliary for PWL of } v^2 \\
q_{t,b,i} &\ge 0 &&\text{auxiliary for PWL of } a^2 \\
\text{dwell}_{t,s} &\ge 0 &&\text{actual dwell time of train } t \text{ at station } s \\
\delta_{t,s} &\ge 0 &&\text{delay of train } t \text{ at station } s \\
\theta_t &\ge 0 &&\text{total travel-time deviation of train } t \\
e_{t,b} &\ge 0 &&\text{energy consumed by train } t \text{ on block } b
\end{aligned}
$$

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \lambda_1 \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{s \in S} \delta_{t,s} \;+\; \lambda_2 \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{b \in B} e_{t,b} \;+\; \lambda_3 \sum_{t \in T} c_t \;+\; \lambda_4 \sum_{t \in T} \theta_t
\tag{OF}
$$

The four terms balance: (1) passenger delay, (2) energy consumption, (3) service cancellations (high penalty), (4) schedule adherence.

---

## 5. Constraints

### (A) Timetable structure

**(C1) Departure uniqueness** — each train departs each station at most once:
$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{t,s,k} \le 1 - c_t \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
\tag{C1}
$$

**(C2) Arrival uniqueness:**
$$
\sum_{k \in K} \text{arr}_{t,s,k} \le 1 - c_t \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
\tag{C2}
$$

**(C3) Flow conservation at stations** (arrivals + origin start = departures + destination end):
$$
\sum_{k} \text{arr}_{t,s,k} + \mathbb{1}[s = o_t](1-c_t) \;=\; \sum_{k} x_{t,s,k} + \mathbb{1}[s = d_t](1-c_t) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
\tag{C3}
$$

**(C4) Origin departure** — a non-cancelled train departs its origin exactly once:
$$
\sum_{k} x_{t,o_t,k} = 1 - c_t \qquad \forall\, t \in T
\tag{C4}
$$

**(C5) Destination arrival:**
$$
\sum_{k} \text{arr}_{t,d_t,k} = 1 - c_t \qquad \forall\, t \in T
\tag{C5}
$$

**(C6) Time ordering** — arrival precedes departure, departure precedes next arrival:
$$
\sum_{k} k\, \text{arr}_{t,s,k} \;\le\; \sum_{k} k\, x_{t,s,k} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{d_t\}
\tag{C6a}
$$
$$
\sum_{k} k\, x_{t,s,k} \;\le\; \sum_{k} k\, \text{arr}_{t,s+1,k} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{d_t\}
\tag{C6b}
$$

### (B) Block occupancy and travel-time consistency

**(C7) Linking entry to occupancy** — train $t$ occupies block $b$ at time $k$ iff it entered within the last $\tau_{t,b}^{\min}$ steps:
$$
u_{t,b,k} \;\ge\; y_{t,b,k'} + z_{t,b,k'} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k' \le k \le k' + \tau_{t,b}^{\min} - 1
\tag{C7a}
$$
$$
u_{t,b,k} \;\le\; \sum_{k' : k - \tau_{t,b}^{\min} < k' \le k} (y_{t,b,k'} + z_{t,b,k'}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
\tag{C7b}
$$

**(C8) Linking departure → block entry → arrival** (big-M):
$$
\sum_{k} k\, x_{t,s,k} \;\le\; \sum_{k'} k'\,(y_{t,b(s),k'} + z_{t,b(s),k'}) + M\Big(1 - \sum_{k'}(y_{t,b(s),k'}+z_{t,b(s),k'})\Big)
\tag{C8a}
$$
$$
\sum_{k'} k'\,(y_{t,b,k'} + z_{t,b,k'}) \;\le\; \sum_{k} k\, \text{arr}_{t,s(b)+1,k} + M\Big(1 - \sum_{k'}(y_{t,b,k'}+z_{t,b,k'})\Big)
\tag{C8b}
$$

**(C9) Travel-time consistency** — the distance covered by the speed profile equals block length:
$$
\sum_{i \in I_b} v_{t,b,i}\, \Delta t \;=\; L_b \cdot \sum_{k \in K}(y_{t,b,k} + z_{t,b,k}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B
\tag{C9a}
$$

The traversal time grows as average speed drops (linear lower bound):
$$
\sum_{k} k\, \text{arr}_{t,s(b)+1,k} - \sum_{k} k\, x_{t,s(b),k} \;\ge\; N_b \cdot \Delta t \cdot \frac{v_{\max}}{\frac{1}{N_b}\sum_{i} v_{t,b,i} + \epsilon} - M\Big(1 - \sum_k(y_{t,b,k}+z_{t,b,k})\Big)
\tag{C9b}
$$

In practice, (C9b) is replaced by the equivalent linear constraint:
$$
\Big(\sum_{k} k\, \text{arr}_{t,s(b)+1,k} - \sum_{k} k\, x_{t,s(b),k}\Big) \cdot \Big(\sum_{i} v_{t,b,i}\Big) \;\ge\; N_b^2 \cdot v_{\max} \cdot \Delta t - M\Big(1 - \sum_k(y_{t,b,k}+z_{t,b,k})\Big)
\tag{C9b'}
$$

**(C10) Rerouting indicator:**
$$
\sum_{k} z_{t,b,k} \le r_{t,b} \le \sum_{k} (y_{t,b,k} + z_{t,b,k}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B
\tag{C10}
$$

### (C) Speed dynamics and limits

**(C11) Speed propagation** through intervals:
$$
v_{t,b,i+1} = v_{t,b,i} + a_{t,b,i}\, \Delta t \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B,\; i \in I_b \setminus \{N_b\}
\tag{C11}
$$

**(C12) Speed limits** (zero when block is not traversed):
$$
v_{\min}\sum_k (y_{t,b,k}+z_{t,b,k}) \;\le\; v_{t,b,i} \;\le\; v_{\max}\sum_k (y_{t,b,k}+z_{t,b,k}) \qquad \forall\, t,b,i
\tag{C12}
$$

**(C13) Acceleration limits:**
$$
-b_{\max}\sum_k (y_{t,b,k}+z_{t,b,k}) \;\le\; a_{t,b,i} \;\le\; a_{\max}\sum_k (y_{t,b,k}+z_{t,b,k}) \qquad \forall\, t,b,i
\tag{C13}
$$

### (D) Dwell times and delays

**(C14) Dwell definition:**
$$
\text{dwell}_{t,s} = \sum_k k\, x_{t,s,k} - \sum_k k\, \text{arr}_{t,s,k} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{o_t, d_t\}
\tag{C14}
$$

**(C15) Dwell bounds:**
$$
d_s^{\min} \Big(\sum_k x_{t,s,k}\Big) \le \text{dwell}_{t,s} \le d_s^{\max} \Big(\sum_k x_{t,s,k}\Big) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
\tag{C15}
$$

**(C16) Delay definition** (nonnegative lateness):
$$
\delta_{t,s} \;\ge\; \sum_k k\, \text{arr}_{t,s,k} - \sigma_{t,s}^{\text{arr}} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
\tag{C16}
$$

**(C17) Travel-time deviation:**
$$
\theta_t \;\ge\; \sum_k k\, \text{arr}_{t,d_t,k} - \sum_k k\, x_{t,o_t,k} - \big(\sigma_{t,d_t}^{\text{arr}} - \sigma_{t,o_t}^{\text{dep}}\big) \qquad \forall\, t \in T
\tag{C17}
$$

### (E) Capacity, headway, and disruption

**(C18) Same-direction headway on a block** — no two trains enter the same block on the same track within headway $h$:
$$
\sum_{k'=k-h+1}^{k} y_{t,b,k'} + \sum_{k'=k-h+1}^{k} y_{t',b,k'} \le 1 \qquad \forall\, b \in B,\; \forall\, t < t',\; \forall\, k,\; \text{dir}_t = \text{dir}_{t'}
\tag{C18a}
$$
Analogously for $z_{t,b,k}$ on the reverse track:
$$
\sum_{k'=k-h+1}^{k} z_{t,b,k'} + \sum_{k'=k-h+1}^{k} z_{t',b,k'} \le 1 \qquad \forall\, b \in B,\; \forall\, t < t',\; \forall\, k,\; \text{dir}_t = \text{dir}_{t'}
\tag{C18b}
$$

**(C19) Single-track capacity during disruption on $b^*$** — at most one train (either direction) occupies the disrupted block per time step:
$$
\sum_{t \in T} u_{t,b^*,k} \le 1 \qquad \forall\, k \in D
\tag{C19}
$$

**(C20) Blocked-track prohibition** — if the forward track of $b^*$ is blocked during $D$:
$$
y_{t,b^*,k} = 0 \qquad \forall\, t : \text{dir}_t = +1,\; k \in D
\tag{C20a}
$$
$$
z_{t,b^*,k} = 0 \qquad \forall\, t : \text{dir}_t = -1,\; k \in D
\tag{C20b}
$$

**(C21) Rerouting consistency** — a train traversing $b^*$ during the disruption must be flagged as rerouted:
$$
y_{t,b^*,k} + z_{t,b^*,k} \le r_{t,b^*} + \big(1 - \mathbb{1}[k \in D]\big) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; k \in K
\tag{C21}
$$

### (F) Cancellation

**(C22) Cancellation kills all movements:**
$$
x_{t,s,k} \le 1 - c_t,\quad \text{arr}_{t,s,k} \le 1 - c_t,\quad y_{t,b,k} \le 1 - c_t,\quad z_{t,b,k} \le 1 - c_t \qquad \forall\, t,s,b,k
\tag{C22}
$$

### (G) Energy consumption (linearization)

**(C23) PWL approximation of $v^2$** — with breakpoints $0 = \bar{v}_0 < \bar{v}_1 < \dots < \bar{v}_P = v_{\max}$ and slopes $\mu_p = \frac{\bar{v}_{p+1}^2 - \bar{v}_p^2}{\bar{v}_{p+1} - \bar{v}_p}$:
$$
w_{t,b,i} \;\ge\; \bar{v}_p^2 + \mu_p(v_{t,b,i} - \bar{v}_p) \qquad \forall\, t,b,i,\; p \in \mathcal{P}
\tag{C23}
$$

Since $w_{t,b,i}$ carries positive cost in the objective, the PWL is exact at optimality (convex envelope).

**(C24) PWL for $a^2$** — analogously with breakpoints on $[-b_{\max}, a_{\max}]$:
$$
q_{t,b,i} \;\ge\; \bar{a}_p^2 + \nu_p(a_{t,b,i} - \bar{a}_p) \qquad \forall\, t,b,i,\; p \in \mathcal{P}
\tag{C24}
$$

**(C25) Energy definition** (linearized, activated only when block is traversed):
$$
e_{t,b} \;\ge\; \sum_{i \in I_b}\big(\alpha\, w_{t,b,i} + \beta\, q_{t,b,i} + \gamma\big)\Delta t - M\Big(1 - \sum_k(y_{t,b,k}+z_{t,b,k})\Big) \qquad \forall\, t,b
\tag{C25}
$$

Since $e_{t,b} \ge 0$ and appears with positive cost, equality holds at optimality.

### (H) Sequence preservation (fairness)

**(C26) Overtaking prohibition on same track** — for trains $t < t'$ with same direction on common stations:
$$
\sum_k k\, \text{arr}_{t,s+1,k} \;\le\; \sum_k k\, \text{arr}_{t',s+1,k} + M\big(2 - \sum_k \text{arr}_{t,s+1,k} - \sum_k \text{arr}_{t',s+1,k}\big) \qquad \forall\, s \in S
\tag{C26}
$$

### (I) Variable domains

$$
x_{t,s,k},\, y_{t,b,k},\, z_{t,b,k},\, \text{arr}_{t,s,k},\, c_t,\, r_{t,b},\, u_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
v_{t,b,i} \ge 0,\quad a_{t,b,i} \in \mathbb{R},\quad \text{dwell}_{t,s},\, \delta_{t,s},\, \theta_t,\, e_{t,b},\, w_{t,b,i},\, q_{t,b,i} \ge 0
$$

## 6. Linearization Summary

| Nonlinear term | Linearization method |
|---|---|
| $v^2$ | Convex PWL epigraph (C23) — exact since $w$ has positive cost |
| $a^2$ | Convex PWL epigraph (C24) — exact since $q$ has positive cost |
| $L_b / \bar{v}$ (travel time) | Bilinear reformulation (C9b') with big-M relaxation |
| $y_{t,b,k} \Rightarrow$ arrival | Big-M implications (C7, C8, C21, C22) |
| Binary × continuous products | Tied via $\sum_k(y_{t,b,k}+z_{t,b,k})$ indicator (C12, C13, C15, C25) |

## 7. Explanation of Model Elements

**Three coupled decision layers:**

1. **Retiming layer** ($x, \text{arr}$): binary time-indexed variables form a time-space network. Constraints (C1)–(C6) guarantee each non-cancelled train follows a connected path from origin to destination through stations over time — producing the conflict-free rescheduled timetable.

2. **Rerouting layer** ($y, z, r, u$): on the disrupted block $b^*$, trains whose nominal track is closed are forced onto the opposite track by (C20)–(C21). Constraint (C19) makes the single available track mutually exclusive per time step during the disruption window, so opposing directions alternate safely.

3. **Speed layer** ($v, a$): continuous speeds per control interval, linked to the timetable via (C9): the distance covered equals $L_b$ (C9a) and traversal time grows as average speed drops (C9b'). Dynamics (C11) and limits (C12)–(C13) ensure executable speed profiles.

**Disruption handling.** Constraint (C20) forbids use of the blocked track during $D$. Constraint (C21) opens the opposite track as a rerouting channel for affected trains. Constraint (C19) enforces single-direction occupancy per time slot on the rerouting track, preserving safety.

**Cancellation as last resort.** A high weight $\lambda_3$ in the objective discourages $c_t = 1$ unless infeasible; constraint (C22) zeroes out all movement variables when cancelled.

**Headway and conflicts.** Constraints (C18) enforce same-direction headway on every block; (C19) handles bidirectional conflicts specifically during the disruption on $b^*$.

**Energy model.** The quadratic-in-speed tractive effort is captured by convex PWL (C23); acceleration-dependent losses use the same technique (C24). This keeps the formulation MILP rather than MIQP, and the PWL is exact at optimality because the auxiliary variables carry positive cost.

**Feasibility guarantees.** (C3)–(C5) ensure flow conservation so every non-cancelled train completes its journey; (C18)–(C21) guarantee capacity feasibility including the disruption; (C22) ensures cancelled trains vanish from the network. If the disruption makes some train infeasible within the horizon, the model cancels it rather than becoming infeasible.

**Output.** Solving yields: (1) the rescheduled timetable from $x, \text{arr}$; (2) speed profiles from $v, a$; (3) rerouting decisions from $z, r$; (4) retiming from the shifted $x, \text{arr}$ versus scheduled times, with delays $\delta$ reported; (5) total energy consumption from $e$.

---

## 8. Key Assumptions (marked)

1. **Discretization**: Time is discretized uniformly with step $\Delta t$; speed profiles are discretized spatially within each block into $N_b$ intervals of length $\Delta s = L_b / N_b$.
2. **Single disruption**: Exactly one block $b^*$ is affected, with a contiguous disruption window $D$.
3. **Bidirectional traffic**: Both directions share the line; rerouting uses the opposite track only during the disruption window.
4. **Energy model**: Quadratic in speed and acceleration, plus a constant term — a standard tractive-effort approximation.
5. **No overtaking on same track**: Enforced by (C26); can be relaxed if needed.
6. **Cancellation is binary**: Partial cancellations (e.g., skipping stations) are not modeled.
7. **Dwell-time flexibility**: Dwell can be adjusted within $[d_s^{\min}, d_s^{\max}]$ independently at each station.
8. **Headway is uniform**: A single parameter $h$ governs all same-direction separations.

---

## 9. Compact Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & \lambda_1 \sum_{t,s} \delta_{t,s} + \lambda_2 \sum_{t,b} e_{t,b} + \lambda_3 \sum_{t} c_t + \lambda_4 \sum_{t} \theta_t \\[4pt]
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(C1)–(C26)} \\
& \text{Linearizations (C23)–(C25), (C9b')} \\
& \text{Variable domains (Section 5-I)}
\end{aligned}
}
$$

This single MILP simultaneously produces a **conflict-free rescheduled timetable**, **executable speed profiles**, **rerouting decisions**, and **retiming decisions** — all while respecting kinematic, capacity, safety, and disruption constraints — and minimizes a weighted combination of delay, energy, cancellation, and schedule deviation.

Text:
# MILP for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance-to-Go (DTG) Signalling

An enhanced RECIFE-MILP model with speed-profile options and speed-dependent blocking times

---

## 1. Problem Description and Assumptions

Given a railway corridor (open line plus station area with switches), a reference timetable, and actual (delayed) train positions at a start time, we must retime and reorder trains and assign each train a speed-profile option such that:

- no two trains occupy the same track section at the same time (DTG separation),
- braking distances (hence blocking times) depend on the train type and chosen speed profile,
- headway/switching constraints and rolling-stock minimum dwell times are respected,
- total delay is minimised.

**Assumptions (marked where not stated in the source text):**

- **(A1)** ETCS Level 2 with trackside train detection (TDS): the end of authority (EoA) is always at the end of a TDS; brake indication points (IP) may lie anywhere on the track.
- **(A2)** Each train–section pair has a finite set of feasible speed-profile options *p* (e.g., coasting, cruising, maximum speed). Each option *p* induces a running time and a **speed-dependent blocking time** on each section, computed offline from braking-curve supervision (this precomputation keeps the model linear).
- **(A3)** Trains are non-overtaking on a single track section unless a switching/reordering variable explicitly allows it at passing loops or station tracks *(assumption; standard in RECIFE-MILP)*.
- **(A4)** Delay is measured with respect to scheduled arrival/departure times; delays propagate through stops via minimum dwell times.
- **(A5)** Rolling stock circulation and driver constraints are neglected *(assumption)*.
- **(A6)** Route locking/release times are included in the blocking times *(assumption)*.

---

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains |
| $S$ | set of TDS sections; $S^{sw} \subseteq S$ switch sections, $S^{ln} = S \setminus S^{sw}$ line sections |
| $P_t$ | set of speed-profile options of train $t$ |
| $E_t \subset S \times S$ | ordered pairs of consecutive sections in the (fixed) route of train $t$ |
| $r_{tsp}$ | running time of train $t$ on section $s$ under profile $p$ |
| $b_{tsp}$ | blocking time of train $t$ on section $s$ under profile $p$, including speed-dependent approach/braking distance and release time |
| $d_{ts}$ | minimum dwell time of train $t$ at station section $s$ |
| $\tau^{min}_{tuv}$ | minimum headway between trains $t$ and $u$ on the same track resource (used for switch sections) |
| $a^{ref}_{ts}, dep^{ref}_{ts}$ | reference (planned) arrival/departure times |
| $w_t$ | delay weight of train $t$ |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $t_0$ | start of the rescheduling horizon; $h^{arr}_{ts}, h^{dep}_{ts}$ earliest possible arrival/departure given initial delays |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{tsp} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ uses speed profile $p$ |
| $y_{ts} \ge 0$ | continuous | entry (passing) time of train $t$ at section $s$ |
| $z_{ts} \ge 0$ | continuous | exit time of train $t$ from section $s$ |
| $\delta^{arr}_{ts}, \delta^{dep}_{ts} \ge 0$ | continuous | arrival/departure delay of train $t$ at section $s$ |
| $o^{ln}_{tu} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | for line sections: 1 if $t$ passes before $u$ (ordering) |
| $o^{sw}_{tu} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | ordering on switch sections |
| $u_{tsp} \ge 0$ | continuous | start of the blocking interval of train $t$ on $s$ under profile $p$ |
| $v_{tsp} \ge 0$ | continuous | end of the blocking interval of train $t$ on $s$ under profile $p$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimise total weighted delay:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{t \in T} w_t \sum_{s \in S} \big( \delta^{arr}_{ts} + \delta^{dep}_{ts} \big)
$$

*(Alternative: minimise only final-station arrival delays — a modelling choice.)*

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Speed-profile selection

Exactly one profile per train:

$$
\sum_{p \in P_t} x_{tp} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T \tag{1}
$$

### 5.2 Running time and section traversal

Exit time equals entry time plus the running time of the selected profile:

$$
z_{ts} \ge y_{ts} + \sum_{p \in P_t} r_{tsp}\, x_{tp} - M(1 - x_{tp}) \qquad \forall t \in T,\ \forall s \in S,\ \forall p \in P_t \tag{2}
$$

Equivalently, since $\sum_p x_{tp}=1$, one may write $z_{ts} = y_{ts} + \sum_p r_{tsp} x_{tp}$.

### 5.3 Route continuity

Entry time at the next section follows exit time at the previous one (plus dwell if it is a stop):

$$
y_{t,s'} \ge z_{ts} + d_{ts} \qquad \forall t \in T,\ \forall (s,s') \in E_t \tag{3}
$$

### 5.4 Blocking-time intervals (speed- and train-dependent)

The blocking interval on section $s$ starts before entry (approach braking distance depends on profile) and ends after exit:

$$
u_{tsp} \ge y_{ts} - \beta_{tsp}\, x_{tp} \qquad \forall t, s, p \tag{4a}
$$
$$
v_{tsp} \ge z_{ts} + \gamma_{tsp}\, x_{tp} \qquad \forall t, s, p \tag{4b}
$$

where $\beta_{tsp}$ = speed-dependent approach/braking time before the EoA (the DTG-specific term: the IP may lie before the section entry) and $\gamma_{tsp}$ = release/clearance time. *(Both precomputed; assumption A2.)*

### 5.5 Conflict-freedom on line sections (disjunctive, big-M)

For every pair of trains $t \neq u$ whose routes share a line section $s \in S^{ln}$, either $t$'s blocking interval ends before $u$'s starts, or vice versa:

$$
v_{tsp} \le u_{usq} + M(3 - x_{tp} - x_{usq} - o^{ln}_{tu}) \qquad \forall t<u,\ s \in S^{ln},\ p \in P_t,\ q \in P_u \tag{5a}
$$
$$
v_{usq} \le u_{tsp} + M(2 - x_{tp} - x_{usq} + o^{ln}_{tu}) \qquad \forall t<u,\ s \in S^{ln},\ p \in P_t,\ q \in P_u \tag{5b}
$$

*(If $t$ and $u$ do not both use $s$, the constraints are relaxed via the profile binaries; alternatively route-section binaries $\rho_{ts}$ can be introduced.)*

### 5.6 Switch sections: ordering with minimum headway

On switch sections $s \in S^{sw}$, trains may not overlap and must respect a minimum headway $\tau^{min}_{tuv}$ (route locking):

$$
y_{us} \ge z_{ts} + \tau^{min}_{tus} + M(o^{sw}_{tu} - 1) \qquad \forall t \neq u,\ s \in S^{sw} \tag{6a}
$$
$$
y_{ts} \ge z_{us} + \tau^{min}_{ust} - M\, o^{sw}_{tu} \qquad \forall t \neq u,\ s \in S^{sw} \tag{6b}
$$

Consistency of ordering along the route (no overtaking unless allowed):

$$
o^{sw}_{tu} = o^{sw}_{ut} \qquad \forall t<u,\ s \in S^{sw} \tag{6c}
$$

$$
o^{ln}_{tu} + o^{ln}_{ut} \ge 1 \qquad \forall t<u,\ s \in S^{ln} \text{ shared} \tag{6d}
$$

### 5.7 Delay definition

$$
\delta^{arr}_{ts} \ge y_{ts} - a^{ref}_{ts} \qquad \forall t, s \tag{7a}
$$
$$
\delta^{dep}_{ts} \ge z_{ts} - dep^{ref}_{ts} \qquad \forall t, s \tag{7b}
$$

### 5.8 Horizon bounds

$$
t_0 \le y_{ts},\ z_{ts} \le t_0 + H \qquad \forall t, s \tag{8}
$$

Initial conditions: for trains already in the network at $t_0$, $y_{t,s_1} = h^{arr}_{t,s_1}$ (fixed), reflecting measured positions/delays.

---

## 6. Remarks on DTG Enhancements (vs. classic RECIFE-MILP)

1. **Speed-profile options (1)–(3):** classic RECIFE-MILP uses fixed running times; here each train may choose among profiles, trading off running time and blocking time.
2. **Speed-dependent blocking times (4):** $\beta_{tsp}$ captures the DTG principle that the brake indication point lies at the end of the train's absolute braking curve, so the approach distance to an occupied section depends on speed — replacing fixed-block signal-guard distances.
3. **Switch/line distinction (5) vs (6):** line sections use pure blocking-time separation; switch sections additionally require explicit ordering and headway because of interlocking route locking.
4. **Linearity:** all non-linearities (speed-dependence) are pushed into the parameters $\beta_{tsp}, \gamma_{tsp}, r_{tsp}, b_{tsp}$ via the profile-selection binaries, keeping the model a MILP.

The model is a standard MILP solvable by branch-and-bound; the profile binaries $x_{tp}$ and ordering binaries $o$ are the only integer variables.

# Final MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockage Disruptions

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $I = \{1,\dots,N\}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $S = \{1,\dots,M\}$ | Set of stations, ordered along the line, indexed by $s$ |
| $B = \{1,\dots,B_{\max}\}$ | Set of track segments (block sections), indexed by $b$ |
| $K = \{0,1,\dots,K_{\text{end}}\}$ | Set of spatial discretization points, indexed by $k$ |
| $Q = \{1,\dots,Q_{\max}\}$ | Set of breakpoints for piecewise-linear energy function, indexed by $q$ |
| $D \subseteq B$ | Set of disrupted segments |

**Derived indices:**
- $s_b, s_{b+1} \in S$: endpoints of segment $b$ (entry and exit stations)
- $O_i, D_i \in S$: origin and destination stations of train $i$
- $K_{\text{end}} = \lceil L_{\text{total}} / \Delta_k \rceil$: number of spatial intervals

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $t^{\text{arr,sch}}_{i,s}, t^{\text{dep,sch}}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival/departure times | min |
| $t^{\text{ready}}_i$ | Ready (departure) time of train $i$ at origin | min |
| $L_b$ | Length of segment $b$ | m |
| $L_{\text{total}}$ | Total track length | m |
| $\Delta_k$ | Spatial discretization step | m |
| $v^{\max}, v^{\min}$ | Maximum/minimum allowed speed | m/s |
| $a^{\max}, a^{\min}$ | Maximum acceleration/deceleration ($a^{\min}<0$) | m/s² |
| $d^{\min}_{i,s}, d^{\max}_{i,s}$ | Min/max dwell time at station $s$ | min |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum headway time between consecutive trains | min |
| $\tau^{\text{start}}, \tau^{\text{end}}$ | Disruption window start/end times | min |
| $f_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if segment $b$ lies on train $i$'s planned O–D path | — |
| $\text{dir}_i \in \{-1,+1\}$ | Travel direction of train $i$ | — |
| $P_i$ | Power coefficient of train $i$ | kW |
| $\gamma_i$ | Mass × drag coefficient | kg/m |
| $v^q, q=0,\dots,Q$ | Speed breakpoints for energy linearization ($v^0=0, v^Q=v^{\max}$) | m/s |
| $s^q = v^q + v^{q-1}$ | Slope of $q$-th linear piece of $v^2$ | m/s |
| $c^q = -v^{q-1}\cdot v^q$ | Intercept of $q$-th linear piece | m²/s² |
| $T_{\text{horizon}}$ | End of planning horizon | min |
| $M$ | Big-M constant | min |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Objective weights for delay, energy, cancellation | — |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous variables:**

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s} \geq 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\text{dep}_{i,s} \geq 0$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $v_{i,k} \geq 0$ | Speed of train $i$ at position point $k$ |
| $u_{i,k} \in \mathbb{R}$ | Acceleration of train $i$ between points $k$ and $k+1$ |
| $u^{+}_{i,k}, u^{-}_{i,k} \geq 0$ | Positive/negative parts of $u_{i,k}$ |
| $p_{i,k} \geq 0$ | Position of train $i$ at point $k$ (m from origin) |
| $e_{i,k} \geq 0$ | Energy consumption rate of train $i$ at point $k$ |
| $E_i \geq 0$ | Total energy consumption of train $i$ |
| $\delta^{\text{arr}}_{i,s}, \delta^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \geq 0$ | Arrival/departure delays |
| $\lambda^q_{i,k} \geq 0$ | Convex combination weights for piecewise-linear energy |

**Binary variables:**

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $x_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses segment $b$ in normal direction |
| $r_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted on segment $b$ (opposite track) |
| $z_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $b$ |
| $w_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$'s traversal of segment $b$ overlaps disruption window |
| $c_i \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \alpha \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{s \in S}\left(\delta^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} + \delta^{\text{dep}}_{i,s}\right) \;+\; \beta \sum_{i \in I} E_i \;+\; \gamma \sum_{i \in I} c_i
$$

The objective minimizes: **(i)** total schedule delay (arrival + departure), **(ii)** total energy consumption, and **(iii)** number of cancelled trains.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Trajectory Dynamics (Speed Management)

**(C1) Position update — trapezoidal rule** *(exact for constant acceleration)*
$$
p_{i,k+1} - p_{i,k} = \frac{v_{i,k} + v_{i,k+1}}{2}\,\Delta_k \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K \setminus \{K_{\text{end}}\}
$$

**(C2) Speed update — linearized acceleration**
$$
v_{i,k+1} = v_{i,k} + u_{i,k} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K \setminus \{K_{\text{end}}\}
$$

**(C3) Acceleration decomposition** *(linearizes $|u_{i,k}|$)*
$$
u_{i,k} = u^{+}_{i,k} - u^{-}_{i,k}, \qquad u^{+}_{i,k}, u^{-}_{i,k} \geq 0 \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K \setminus \{K_{\text{end}}\}
$$

**(C4) Acceleration bounds**
$$
a^{\min} \leq u_{i,k} \leq a^{\max} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K \setminus \{K_{\text{end}}\}
$$

**(C5) Speed bounds**
$$
0 \leq v_{i,k} \leq v^{\max} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K
$$

**(C6) Position bounds and monotonicity**
$$
0 \leq p_{i,k} \leq L_{\text{total}}, \qquad p_{i,k+1} \geq p_{i,k} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K
$$

**(C7) Boundary conditions**
$$
p_{i,0} = 0, \quad p_{i,K_{\text{end}}} = L_{\text{total}}, \quad v_{i,0} = 0, \quad v_{i,K_{\text{end}}} = 0 \qquad \forall\, i \in I
$$

---

### 5.2 Station Timing

**(C8) Dwell time bounds** *(intermediate stations only)*
$$
d^{\min}_{i,s} \leq \text{dep}_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \leq d^{\max}_{i,s} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S \setminus \{O_i, D_i\}
$$

**(C9) Initial departure — ready time at origin**
$$
\text{dep}_{i,O_i} = t^{\text{ready}}_i \qquad \forall\, i \in I
$$

**(C10) Journey completion**
$$
a_{i,D_i} \leq T_{\text{horizon}} \qquad \forall\, i \in I
$$

---

### 5.3 Segment Traversal and Routing

**(C11) Path feasibility** *(train can only use segments on its O–D path)*
$$
x_{i,b} + r_{i,b} \leq f_{i,b} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B
$$

**(C12) Cancellation coupling**
$$
x_{i,b} \leq 1 - c_i, \qquad r_{i,b} \leq 1 - c_i \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B
$$

**(C13) Rerouting exclusivity** *(cannot use both directions simultaneously)*
$$
x_{i,b} + r_{i,b} \leq 1 \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B
$$

**(C14) Minimum segment traversal time**
$$
a_{i,s_{b+1}} - \text{dep}_{i,s_b} \geq \frac{L_b}{v^{\max}}\,(x_{i,b} + r_{i,b}) \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B
$$

**(C15) Maximum segment traversal time**
$$
a_{i,s_{b+1}} - \text{dep}_{i,s_b} \leq \frac{L_b}{v^{\min}}\,(x_{i,b} + r_{i,b}) + M\,c_i \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in B
$$

---

### 5.4 Disruption Handling

**(C16) Disruption window — finish before disruption starts**
$$
a_{i,s_{b+1}} \leq \tau^{\text{start}} + M\,w_{i,b} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in D
$$

**(C17) Disruption window — start after disruption ends**
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s_b} \geq \tau^{\text{end}} - M\,(1 - w_{i,b}) \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in D
$$

**(C18) Forced rerouting during disruption overlap**
$$
w_{i,b} + x_{i,b} \leq 1, \qquad w_{i,b} \leq r_{i,b} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; b \in D
$$

**Interpretation:** If $w_{i,b}=1$, the train's traversal overlaps the disruption window, so it must finish before $\tau^{\text{start}}$ or start after $\tau^{\text{end}}$, and must be rerouted ($r_{i,b}=1$).

---

### 5.5 Conflict Resolution

**(C19) Ordering variable definition**
$$
z_{i,j,b} + z_{j,i,b} = 1 \qquad \forall\, i,j \in I,\; i < j,\; b \in B
$$

**(C20) Same-direction headway** *(both trains use normal direction on segment $b$)*
$$
\text{dep}_{j,s_b} - \text{dep}_{i,s_b} \geq h_{\min} - M\,(1 - z_{i,j,b}) \qquad \forall\, i,j \in I,\; b \in B
$$

**(C21) Bidirectional conflict on rerouted (single-track) segments**

For trains $i$ (direction $+$) and $j$ (direction $-$) sharing rerouted segment $b$:
$$
\text{dep}_{j,s_{b+1}} \geq a_{i,s_{b+1}} + h_{\min} - M\,(2 - r_{i,b} - r_{j,b}) \qquad \forall\, i,j \in I,\; b \in D
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s_b} \geq a_{j,s_b} + h_{\min} - M\,(2 - r_{i,b} - r_{j,b}) \qquad \forall\, i,j \in I,\; b \in D
$$

These constraints ensure mutual exclusion on the shared single track: one train must fully clear the segment before the other enters.

---

### 5.6 Coupling: Timetable ↔ Speed Profile

**(C22) Station position alignment** *(train must be at station position at arrival/departure)*
$$
p_{i,k^{\text{arr}}_{i,s}} = \sum_{b \leq s-1} L_b \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S
$$
$$
p_{i,k^{\text{dep}}_{i,s}} = \sum_{b \leq s-1} L_b \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S
$$

**(C23) Station stop** *(speed must be zero at stations)*
$$
v_{i,k^{\text{arr}}_{i,s}} = 0, \qquad v_{i,k^{\text{dep}}_{i,s}} = 0 \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S
$$

where $k^{\text{arr}}_{i,s}$ and $k^{\text{dep}}_{i,s}$ are the spatial grid indices corresponding to station $s$.

---

### 5.7 Delay Definition

**(C24) Arrival delay**
$$
\delta^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} - t^{\text{arr,sch}}_{i,s} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S
$$

**(C25) Departure delay**
$$
\delta^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \geq \text{dep}_{i,s} - t^{\text{dep,sch}}_{i,s} \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S
$$

---

### 5.8 Energy Consumption (Piecewise-Linear Approximation)

**(C26) SOS2 convex combination**
$$
\sum_{q=0}^{Q} \lambda^q_{i,k} = 1 \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K
$$

**(C27) Speed via convex combination**
$$
v_{i,k} = \sum_{q=0}^{Q} \lambda^q_{i,k}\cdot v^q \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K
$$

**(C28) Adjacency (SOS2):** at most two consecutive $\lambda^q_{i,k}$ are nonzero.

**(C29) Energy lower bound** *(convex hull of quadratic $v^2$)*
$$
e_{i,k} \geq P_i \sum_{q=1}^{Q} \lambda^q_{i,k}\bigl(s^q\cdot v^q + c^q\bigr) \qquad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K
$$

**(C30) Total energy per train**
$$
E_i = \sum_{k \in K} e_{i,k}\,\Delta_k \qquad \forall\, i \in I
$$

Since energy is minimized with positive weight $\beta$, constraints (C29) are tight at optimality.

---

### 5.9 Variable Domains

$$
a_{i,s}, \text{dep}_{i,s}, v_{i,k}, p_{i,k}, e_{i,k}, E_i, \delta^{\text{arr}}_{i,s}, \delta^{\text{dep}}_{i,s}, \lambda^q_{i,k}, u^{+}_{i,k}, u^{-}_{i,k} \geq 0
$$
$$
u_{i,k} \in \mathbb{R}, \qquad x_{i,b}, r_{i,b}, z_{i,j,b}, w_{i,b}, c_i \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Key Assumptions

1. **Single-line bidirectional track**: The railway line consists of two tracks (one per direction). During disruption, one track is blocked, and trains can be rerouted to the opposite track.

2. **Known disruption**: The disruption segment(s) and time window $[\tau^{\text{start}}, \tau^{\text{end}}]$ are known in advance.

3. **Uniform train characteristics**: All trains have identical performance parameters ($v^{\max}, a^{\max}, a^{\min}$) for simplicity; can be relaxed by indexing parameters per train.

4. **Spatial discretization**: The track is discretized into spatial points with step $\Delta_k$. Stations are assumed to lie on grid points.

5. **Constant acceleration between grid points**: The trapezoidal rule (C1) provides exact kinematics under this assumption.

6. **Energy model**: Energy consumption is modeled as a quadratic function of speed ($E \propto v^2$), linearized via piecewise-linear (SOS2) approximation.

7. **No track gradients or curves**: The track is assumed flat and straight for energy calculations.

8. **Deterministic parameters**: All parameters (travel times, headways, etc.) are deterministic.

9. **Cancellation as last resort**: Cancellation is allowed but heavily penalized in the objective.

10. **Direction consistency**: Each train has a fixed direction $\text{dir}_i$; bidirectional traffic is handled via the rerouting mechanism on disrupted segments.

---

## 7. Model Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & \alpha \sum_{i,s}\left(\delta^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} + \delta^{\text{dep}}_{i,s}\right) + \beta \sum_{i} E_i + \gamma \sum_{i} c_i \\[4pt]
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(C1)–(C30)} \\
& x_{i,b}, r_{i,b}, z_{i,j,b}, w_{i,b}, c_i \in \{0,1\} \\
& \text{all continuous variables} \geq 0 \\
& \lambda^q_{i,k} \text{ SOS2 over } q
\end{aligned}
}
$$

**Variable/constraint complexity:** $O(|I| \cdot |K| + |I| \cdot |B| + |I|^2 \cdot |B|)$ variables and constraints. For large instances, decomposition methods (e.g., Benders decomposition or the iterative plan-selection framework described in the paper) are recommended.

This MILP model integrates train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with speed management (kinematically feasible speed profiles and energy consumption) under partial segment blockage disruptions, yielding a conflict-free timetable with executable speed profiles.

Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
