Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ (ordered along the line) |
| $B$ | Set of block sections between consecutive stations, indexed by $b$ |
| $K$ | Set of discretized time intervals, indexed by $k$, with duration $\Delta t$ |
| $D$ | Disruption data: blocked section $b_d$ and time window $[\tau_d^{start}, \tau_d^{end}]$ |
| $\mathcal{R}_i$ | Set of feasible routes for train $i$, indexed by $r$ (original or rerouted) |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_b$ | Length of block section $b$ [m] |
| $\Delta t$ | Length of discretized time interval [s] |
| $v^{min}, v^{max}$ | Minimum and maximum allowable train speeds [m/s] |
| $a^{max}, d^{max}$ | Maximum acceleration and deceleration [m/s²] |
| $\tau^{orig}_{i,s,a}, \tau^{orig}_{i,s,d}$ | Originally scheduled arrival/departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $dwell^{min}, dwell^{max}$ | Minimum and maximum dwell time at stations [s] |
| $h^{same}$ | Minimum headway on same block section for trains in same direction [s] |
| $h^{bi}$ | Minimum bidirectional headway on shared track [s] |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (Big-M) |
| $c_0, c_1, c_2, \ldots$ | Coefficients of the piecewise-linear energy function |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Weighting coefficients in the objective function |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Binary variables:**
- $x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}$: equals 1 if train $i$ uses route $r$
- $y_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}$: equals 1 if train $i$ occupies block section $b$ before train $j$
- $z_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}$: equals 1 if trains $i$ and $j$ are in opposite directions on block $b$ (bidirectional conflict indicator)
- $w_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: equals 1 if train $i$ stops at station $s$
- $\delta_i \in \{0,1\}$: equals 1 if train $i$ arrives at disrupted block after the disruption ends

**Continuous variables:**
- $t^{a}_{i,s}, t^{d}_{i,s}$: actual arrival/departure time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $t^{enter}_{i,b}, t^{exit}_{i,b}$: entry/exit time of train $i$ at block $b$
- $v_{i,b,k}$: speed of train $i$ on block $b$ during interval $k$ [m/s]
- $a_{i,b,k}$: acceleration of train $i$ on block $b$ during interval $k$ [m/s²]
- $p_{i,b,k}$: position of train $i$ on block $b$ at the end of interval $k$ [m]
- $e_{i,k}$: energy consumed by train $i$ during interval $k$ [kWh]
- $\text{delay}_{i,s} \geq 0$: delay of train $i$ at station $s$ [s]
- $\text{total\_delay}_i$: total end-to-end delay of train $i$ [s]

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total delay, total energy consumption, and total end-to-end delay:

$$\min Z = \alpha \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \text{delay}_{i,s} + \beta \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{k \in K} e_{i,k} + \gamma \sum_{i \in T} |\text{total\_delay}_i|$$

where the absolute value is linearized using auxiliary variables.

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timing Consistency at Stations (Dwell Time)

$$t^{d}_{i,s} \geq t^{a}_{i,s} + dwell^{min} \cdot w_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T, s \in S$$

$$t^{d}_{i,s} \leq t^{a}_{i,s} + dwell^{max} \cdot w_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T, s \in S$$

$$t^{a}_{i,s} \leq t^{d}_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T, s \in S$$

### 5.2 Boundary Conditions at Origin and Destination

$$t^{d}_{i,1} = \tau^{orig}_{i,1,d} \quad \forall i \in T$$

$$t^{a}_{i,|S|} \leq \tau^{orig}_{i,|S|,a} + \Delta^{max} \quad \forall i \in T$$

### 5.3 Train Dynamics on Block Sections (Speed Management)

$$p_{i,b,k+1} = p_{i,b,k} + v_{i,b,k} \cdot \Delta t + \tfrac{1}{2} a_{i,b,k} \cdot \Delta t^2 \quad \forall i, b, k$$

$$v_{i,b,k+1} = v_{i,b,k} + a_{i,b,k} \cdot \Delta t \quad \forall i, b, k$$

### 5.4 Speed and Acceleration Limits

$$v^{min} \leq v_{i,b,k} \leq v^{max} \quad \forall i, b, k$$

$$-d^{max} \leq a_{i,b,k} \leq a^{max} \quad \forall i, b, k$$

### 5.5 Position Bounds and Initial/Final Conditions on Blocks

$$0 \leq p_{i,b,k} \leq L_b \quad \forall i, b, k$$

$$p_{i,b,0} = 0, \quad p_{i,b,K} = L_b \quad \forall i, b$$

### 5.6 Coupling Between Timetable and Speed Profiles

$$t^{enter}_{i,b} = \sum_{k} k \cdot \Delta t \cdot \mathbb{1}_{\{p_{i,b,k-1}=0 \wedge p_{i,b,k}>0\}} \quad \forall i, b$$

$$t^{exit}_{i,b} = \sum_{k} k \cdot \Delta t \cdot \mathbb{1}_{\{p_{i,b,k-1}<L_b \wedge p_{i,b,k}=L_b\}} \quad \forall i, b$$

(linearized using auxiliary binary indicators linked to position transitions)

### 5.7 Same-Direction Headway Constraints (Train Rescheduling – Ordering)

$$t^{enter}_{j,b} - t^{exit}_{i,b} \geq h^{same} - M(1 - y_{i,j,b}) \quad \forall i,j,b, \; i \neq j$$

$$t^{enter}_{i,b} - t^{exit}_{j,b} \geq h^{same} - M \cdot y_{i,j,b} \quad \forall i,j,b, \; i \neq j$$

$$y_{i,j,b} + y_{j,i,b} = 1 \quad \forall i,j,b, \; i \neq j$$

### 5.8 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution on Shared Track (Key Innovation)

For each pair of trains $(i,j)$ traveling in opposite directions on block $b$:

$$t^{exit}_{j,b} - t^{enter}_{i,b} \geq h^{bi} - M(1 - z_{i,j,b})$$

$$t^{exit}_{i,b} - t^{enter}_{j,b} \geq h^{bi} - M \cdot z_{i,j,b}$$

$$z_{i,j,b} + z_{j,i,b} = 1 \quad \forall i,j \in T^{opp}_b$$

where $T^{opp}_b$ denotes pairs of trains moving in opposite directions on block $b$.

### 5.9 Rerouting Constraints (Route Choice)

$$\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_i} x_{i,r} = 1 \quad \forall i \in T$$

### 5.10 Disruption Time Window Avoidance (Original Route)

For train $i$ using the original route through disrupted block $b_d$:

$$t^{enter}_{i,b_d} \leq \tau_d^{start} + M \cdot \delta_i + M(1 - x_{i,orig})$$

$$t^{enter}_{i,b_d} \geq \tau_d^{end} - M(1 - \delta_i) - M(1 - x_{i,orig})$$

### 5.11 Disruption Participation Constraint (Rerouted Route)

For train $i$ using the rerouted (opposite) track during disruption:

$$x_{i,rerouted} = 1 \implies \tau_d^{start} \leq t^{enter}_{i,b_d} \leq \tau_d^{end}$$

$$t^{enter}_{i,b_d} \geq \tau_d^{start} - M(1 - x_{i,rerouted})$$

$$t^{enter}_{i,b_d} \leq \tau_d^{end} + M(1 - x_{i,rerouted})$$

### 5.12 Block Section Continuity (Retiming Coupling)

$$t^{d}_{i,s} = t^{enter}_{i,b_s} \quad \forall i, s \in S \setminus \{|S|\}$$

$$t^{a}_{i,s} = t^{exit}_{i,b_{s-1}} \quad \forall i, s \in S \setminus \{1\}$$

### 5.13 Delay Definitions

$$\text{delay}_{i,s} \geq t^{a}_{i,s} - \tau^{orig}_{i,s,a} \quad \forall i, s$$

$$\text{delay}_{i,s} \geq 0 \quad \forall i, s$$

$$\text{total\_delay}_i = t^{a}_{i,|S|} - \tau^{orig}_{i,|S|,a} \quad \forall i$$

### 5.14 Energy Consumption (Piecewise-Linear Approximation)

Using SOS2 or multiple linear segments to approximate $e(v,a)$:

$$e_{i,k} \geq c_1 \cdot v_{i,b,k} + c_2 \cdot a_{i,b,k} + c_0 - M(1 - \lambda_{i,k,p}) \quad \forall i, k, p \in P$$

$$\sum_{p \in P} \lambda_{i,k,p} = 1, \quad \lambda_{i,k,p} \geq 0 \quad \forall i, k$$

where $\lambda_{i,k,p}$ are convex combination weights for piecewise segment $p$ of the energy function.

### 5.15 Non-Negativity

$$v_{i,b,k} \geq 0, \quad p_{i,b,k} \geq 0, \quad e_{i,k} \geq 0$$

## 6. Assumptions

1. **Double-track line**: Each direction normally uses its own track; during disruption, bidirectional traffic can share one track.
2. **Known disruption window**: The blocked segment $b_d$ and time window $[\tau_d^{start}, \tau_d^{end}]$ are known in advance.
3. **Discrete time–space representation**: Train dynamics are discretized with interval $\Delta t$; positions and speeds are tracked at interval boundaries.
4. **Homogeneous train fleet**: All trains share the same maximum speed, acceleration, and deceleration limits (the model extends naturally to heterogeneous fleets).
5. **No overtaking within blocks**: Reordering occurs only at stations; within a block section trains maintain their order.
6. **Fixed headways**: Headway times $h^{same}$ and $h^{bi}$ are treated as constants, independent of speed.
7. **No track gradients or curvature** are considered in the energy model.
8. **No service cancellations**: All trains must be rescheduled; however, the framework can be extended to include cancellation decisions.
9. **Energy recovery during braking** is captured via the piecewise-linear function coefficients.
10. **Conflict-free condition**: The combined timetable and speed profile must ensure no two trains (same or opposite direction) occupy the same track resource simultaneously.

This MILP model jointly determines retiming, reordering, rerouting decisions at the operational level, and continuous speed profiles at the control level, while explicitly resolving bidirectional conflicts on shared track sections during partial segment blockages and co-optimizing delay and energy consumption.

---

# MILP for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 0. Assumptions

1. Time is discretized into uniform steps Δt; speed and acceleration are **piecewise-constant** per step.
2. Each segment has two tracks r ∈ {1, 2}; each train uses at most one track per segment.
3. Resistance follows the Davis equation: F_r(v) = c₀ + c₁v + c₂v²; tractive power is e = (m·a + F_r)·v, approximated by a 2-D PWL function on an (a, v) grid.
4. Kinematics use first-order Euler updates (fully linear).
5. Disruption affects a single (segment, track) pair over a closed time window [T_d^s, T_d^e].
6. Headway is enforced at segment **entry** times and includes train-length clearance.
7. Cancellations are allowed and penalized; a cancelled train occupies no resources.
8. Overtaking only at stations (no overtaking within a segment).

## 1. Sets

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| T | trains t ∈ T |
| S | segments s ∈ S |
| P | stations p ∈ P |
| K | time steps k ∈ {1,…,\|K\|} |
| D | disruptions d ∈ D |
| R = {1,2} | tracks per segment |
| G_a, G_v | acceleration / velocity grid indices for PWL |

## 2. Parameters

Δt (s); L_s (m); v̄_s, v_min, v_max (m/s); a_min, a_max (m/s²); p_s^start, p_s^end, p_p (m); p_t⁰, p_t^F, v_t⁰, v_t^F; T_d^s, T_d^e (s); s_d, r_d; h, h_bi (s); L_t, m_t; ā_g, v̄_h, ē_{g,h} (PWL grid values, ē precomputed from Davis equation); d_t^p (scheduled times), w_t^p (deviation weights); dwell_p^min (s); TT_t^min, TT_t^max; C_e, C_τ (cost coefficients); M₁, M₂, M₃ (big-M); ε (small constant).

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous:** v_{t,k}, a_{t,k}, p_{t,k} (speed, acceleration, position); e_{t,k} (power); E_t (total energy); τ_t^{s,ent}, τ_t^{s,ext} (segment entry/exit times); τ_t^p, σ_t^p (station arrival/departure); T_t (travel time); dev_t^{p,arr}, dev_t^{p,dep} (schedule deviations); λ_{t,k,g,h} ≥ 0 (PWL weights).

**Binary:** z_{t,k,s} (occupancy); x_{t,s,r} (track selection); y_t (cancellation); α_{t,d}, β_{t,d}, γ_{t,d} (before window / after window / rerouted); o_{t1,t2,s,r} (ordering); σ^{ent}, σ^{ext}, σ^{arr}, σ^{dep} (event indicators).

## 4. Objective Function

$$\min\; C_e \sum_{t} E_t \;+\; C_\tau \sum_{t} T_t \;+\; \sum_{t}\sum_{p} w_t^p\left(dev_t^{p,\text{arr}} + dev_t^{p,\text{dep}}\right) \;+\; C_{\text{cancel}} \sum_{t} y_t$$

## 5. Constraints

**Kinematics (C1–C4):**
- v_{t,k+1} = v_{t,k} + Δt·a_{t,k};  p_{t,k+1} = p_{t,k} + Δt·v_{t,k}  ∀t, k
- p_{t,1} = p_t⁰, v_{t,1} = v_t⁰;  p_{t,|K|} = p_t^F, v_{t,|K|} = v_t^F

**Segment occupancy (C5–C10):**
- Σ_s z_{t,k,s} = 1 ∀t,k
- p_s^start − M(1−z_{t,k,s}) ≤ p_{t,k} ≤ p_s^end + M(1−z_{t,k,s})
- v_{t,k} ≤ Σ_s z_{t,k,s}·v̄_s;  z_{t,k,s} ≤ Σ_r x_{t,s,r}
- Σ_r x_{t,s,r} ≤ 1;  Σ_k z_{t,k,s}·Δt ≥ (L_s/v̄_s)·Σ_r x_{t,s,r}

**Entry/exit time linking (C11–C18):**
- Σ_k σ_{t,k,s}^{ent} = Σ_r x_{t,s,r};  Σ_k σ_{t,k,s}^{ext} = Σ_r x_{t,s,r}
- kΔt − M(1−σ_{t,k,s}^{ent}) ≤ τ_t^{s,ent} ≤ kΔt + M(1−σ_{t,k,s}^{ent}) (analogously for ext)
- Position-based activation: p_{t,k} ≥ p_s^start − M(1−σ_{t,k,s}^{ent}); p_{t,k−1} ≤ p_s^start − ε + M·σ_{t,k,s}^{ent}; analogous constraints for exit at p_s^end.

**Station arrival/departure (C19–C22):**
- Σ_k σ_{t,k,p}^{arr} = Σ_k σ_{t,k,p}^{dep} = 1; big-M linking of τ_t^p, σ_t^p to event steps
- σ_t^p ≥ τ_t^p + dwell_p^min

**Travel time and deviations (C23–C26):**
- T_t = σ_t^{p_final} − τ_t^{p_origin}; TT_t^min ≤ T_t ≤ TT_t^max
- dev_t^{p,arr} ≥ ±(τ_t^p − d_t^p); dev_t^{p,dep} ≥ ±(σ_t^p − d_t^p)

**Energy via 2-D PWL (C27–C33):**
- Σ_{g,h} λ_{t,k,g,h} = 1; Σ_{g,h} λ·ā_g = a_{t,k}; Σ_{g,h} λ·v̄_h = v_{t,k}; Σ_{g,h} λ·ē_{g,h} = e_{t,k}
- SOS2 on {λ : h ∈ G_v} for fixed g, and {λ : g ∈ G_a} for fixed h
- E_t = Σ_k Δt·e_{t,k}

**Disruption and rerouting (C34–C39):** ∀t, d:
- α_{t,d} + β_{t,d} + γ_{t,d} ≥ 1 − y_t  and ≤ 1 + y_t
- τ_t^{s_d,ext} ≤ T_d^s + M₁(1−α_{t,d});  τ_t^{s_d,ent} ≥ T_d^e − M₁(1−β_{t,d})
- x_{t,s_d,3−r_d} ≥ γ_{t,d};  x_{t,s_d,r_d} ≤ α_{t,d} + β_{t,d} + y_t

**Headway and conflicts (C40–C46):**
- Ordering linearization: o_{t1,t2,s,r} + o_{t2,t1,s,r} ≤ x_{t1,s,r}; ≤ x_{t2,s,r}; ≥ x_{t1,s,r} + x_{t2,s,r} − 1
- Same-direction headway: τ_{t2}^{s,ent} ≥ τ_{t1}^{s,ent} + h − M₂(2 − o_{t1,t2,s,r} − x_{t1,s,r} − x_{t2,s,r})
- Bidirectional headway on shared track: analogous with h_bi and o^{bi}
- Block clearing: τ_{t2}^{s,ent} ≥ τ_{t1}^{s,ext} + L_{t1}/v_min − M₂(1 − o_{t1,t2,s,r}) (and symmetric)

**Cancellation (C47–C54):** if y_t = 1: v_{t,k} ≤ M₃(1−y_t); |p_{t,k} − p_t⁰| ≤ M₃(1−y_t); τ_t^{s,ent}, τ_t^{s,ext}, σ_t^p ≤ M₃(1−y_t); |a_{t,k}| ≤ M₃(1−y_t).

**Speed/acceleration bounds (C55–C59):** v_min ≤ v_{t,k} ≤ v_max; a_min ≤ a_{t,k} ≤ a_max; v_{t,k} ≤ Σ_s z_{t,k,s}·v̄_s.

## 6. Model Size

For |T|=20, |S|=10, |K|=60, |P|=11, N_a·N_v=36: roughly 10⁵ continuous variables (dominated by PWL weights), ~5·10⁴ binaries (dominated by z and o), ~3·10⁵ constraints — tractable for Gurobi/CPLEX within minutes.

## 7. Solver Notes

- Declare λ groups as SOS2; use tight big-Ms (M₁ = T_horizon, M₃ = v_max / T_horizon per variable type).
- Warm-start with the nominal timetable and a greedy disruption heuristic (prefer α, then β, then γ, then cancellation).
- Use Δt = 30 s; refine granularity only near the disruption window (this mirrors the adaptive plan-refinement idea of the decomposition framework).

This formulation is fully linear, exactly couples the rescheduled timetable with executable time-indexed speed profiles, handles bidirectional conflicts from rerouting on the shared opposite track, and is directly implementable in standard MILP solvers.

Text:
# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Infrastructure Constraints

## 1. Introduction and Assumptions

This MILP formulation combines the **Composition Model** (based on Fioole et al., 2006) and the **Infrastructure Model** (based on Van Aken et al., 2017) into a unified framework for rolling stock rescheduling during railway disruptions.

**Key Assumptions:**
- Each train trip requires a composition of one or more coupled rolling stock units
- Shunting movements are modeled as events on specific tracks at specific stations
- Other passenger trains may be delayed by at most $\Delta^{max}$ minutes to enable shunting
- The planning horizon covers the disruption period plus buffer time
- Rolling stock units are homogeneous in type but distinguishable
- Coupling and decoupling operations occur at station platforms
- Track conflicts are resolved through sequencing and limited delays

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of train trips in the (adjusted) timetable |
| $T^{dis} \subseteq T$ | Set of trips affected by the disruption |
| $R$ | Set of rolling stock units |
| $S$ | Set of stations |
| $Tr_s$ | Set of tracks at station $s \in S$ |
| $K$ | Set of all possible shunting movements |
| $K_s \subseteq K$ | Set of shunting movements at station $s$ |
| $E = T \cup K$ | Set of all events (train trips and shunting movements) |
| $L$ | Set of train lines |
| $D$ | Set of disruption scenarios |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $o_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if unit $r$ was originally assigned to trip $t$ |
| $cap_r$ | Passenger capacity of unit $r$ |
| $dem_t$ | Passenger demand for trip $t$ |
| $dep_t, arr_t$ | Scheduled departure/arrival time of trip $t$ |
| $s_k, e_k$ | Earliest start / latest end time of shunting movement $k$ |
| $dur_k$ | Duration of shunting movement $k$ |
| $c^{delay}$ | Cost per minute of train delay |
| $c^{cancel}$ | Cost of canceling a trip |
| $c^{dev}$ | Cost per unit deviation from original assignment |
| $c^{shunt}$ | Cost of performing a shunting movement |
| $c^{stand}$ | Cost per standing passenger |
| $c^{cap}$ | Cost per unit of capacity shortage |
| $\Delta^{max}$ | Maximum allowed delay (minutes) |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (Big-M) |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta, \epsilon$ | Objective weights |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

**Composition Variables:**
- $x_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if unit $r$ is assigned to trip $t$
- $y_{t,r,r'} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if units $r$ and $r'$ are coupled on trip $t$ ($r < r'$)
- $z_k \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if shunting movement $k$ is performed
- $c_t \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trip $t$ is canceled
- $d_t \geq 0$: Delay of trip $t$ (minutes)
- $s_t \geq 0$: Number of standing passengers on trip $t$

**Infrastructure Variables:**
- $f_{e,tr,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if event $e$ uses track $tr$ at station $s$
- $u_{e,tr,s} \geq 0$: Start time of event $e$ on track $tr$ at station $s$
- $p_{e,e',tr,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if event $e$ precedes event $e'$ on track $tr$ at station $s$

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of operational, passenger service, and stick-to-the-plan objectives:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad Z = \; & \alpha \sum_{t \in T} c^{delay} \cdot d_t \\
& + \beta \sum_{t \in T} c^{cancel} \cdot c_t \\
& + \gamma \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{r \in R} c^{dev} \cdot |x_{t,r} - o_{t,r}| \\
& + \delta \sum_{k \in K} c^{shunt} \cdot z_k \\
& + \epsilon \sum_{t \in T} \left( c^{stand} \cdot s_t + c^{cap} \cdot \max(0, dem_t - \sum_{r \in R} cap_r \cdot x_{t,r}) \right)
\end{aligned}
$$

*Note: The absolute value and max terms are linearized using auxiliary variables.*

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Composition Model Constraints

**(C1) Trip Coverage:** Each non-canceled trip must be covered by at least one unit.
$$
\sum_{r \in R} x_{t,r} \geq 1 - c_t \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C2) Capacity Constraint:** Total capacity must meet demand (accounting for standing).
$$
\sum_{r \in R} cap_r \cdot x_{t,r} + s_t \geq dem_t \cdot (1 - c_t) \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C3) Flow Conservation:** Units arriving at a station must be available for subsequent trips.
$$
\sum_{t \in T: arr_t \leq dep_{t'}} x_{t,r} = \sum_{t' \in T: dep_{t'} \geq arr_t} x_{t',r} \quad \forall r \in R, \; \text{at each station}
$$

**(C4) Coupling Symmetry:** If two units are coupled, both must be assigned.
$$
y_{t,r,r'} \leq x_{t,r}, \quad y_{t,r,r'} \leq x_{t,r'} \quad \forall t \in T, \; r, r' \in R, \; r < r'
$$

**(C5) Composition Cardinality:** A trip uses at most $U^{max}$ units.
$$
\sum_{r \in R} x_{t,r} \leq U^{max} \cdot (1 - c_t) \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C6) Shunting Activation:** A shunting movement is required when coupling changes between consecutive trips.
$$
z_k \geq x_{t,r} - x_{t',r} \quad \forall k \in K \text{ connecting trips } t \text{ and } t', \; r \in R
$$
$$
z_k \geq x_{t',r} - x_{t,r} \quad \forall k \in K \text{ connecting trips } t \text{ and } t', \; r \in R
$$

**(C7) Disruption Handling:** Trips through blocked sections cannot use original rolling stock.
$$
x_{t,r} \leq 1 - o_{t,r}^{block} \quad \forall t \in T^{dis}, \; r \in R
$$

**(C8) Delay Bound:** Maximum delay for non-canceled trips.
$$
d_t \leq \Delta^{max} \cdot (1 - c_t) \quad \forall t \in T
$$

### 6.2 Infrastructure Model Constraints

**(C9) Track Assignment:** Each event uses exactly one track at each station it visits.
$$
\sum_{tr \in Tr_s} f_{e,tr,s} = 1 \quad \forall e \in E, \; s \in S \text{ where } e \text{ visits } s
$$

**(C10) Shunting Track Feasibility:** Shunting movements require available tracks.
$$
z_k \leq \sum_{tr \in Tr_s} f_{k,tr,s} \quad \forall k \in K_s, \; s \in S
$$

**(C11) Time Window:** Events must start within their time windows.
$$
u_{e,tr,s} \geq s_e \cdot f_{e,tr,s} \quad \forall e \in E, \; tr \in Tr_s, \; s \in S
$$
$$
u_{e,tr,s} \leq e_e \cdot f_{e,tr,s} \quad \forall e \in E, \; tr \in Tr_s, \; s \in S
$$

**(C12) Track Sequencing:** No two events overlap on the same track.
$$
u_{e,tr,s} + dur_e \leq u_{e',tr,s} + M \cdot (1 - p_{e,e',tr,s}) \quad \forall e \neq e', \; tr \in Tr_s, \; s \in S
$$
$$
u_{e',tr,s} + dur_{e'} \leq u_{e,tr,s} + M \cdot p_{e,e',tr,s} \quad \forall e \neq e', \; tr \in Tr_s, \; s \in S
$$

**(C13) Track Capacity:** A track can host at most one event at a time.
$$
f_{e,tr,s} + f_{e',tr,s} \leq 1 + M \cdot (1 - p_{e,e',tr,s}) + M \cdot (1 - p_{e',e,tr,s}) \quad \forall e \neq e', \; tr \in Tr_s, \; s \in S
$$

**(C14) Train Delay Linkage:** Trip start times account for delays.
$$
u_{t,tr,s} \geq dep_t + d_t - M \cdot (1 - f_{t,tr,s}) \quad \forall t \in T, \; tr \in Tr_s, \; s \in S
$$

### 6.3 Linking Constraints (Composition ↔ Infrastructure)

**(C15) Shunting-Train Interaction:** Shunting movements may require delaying nearby trains.
$$
d_{t} \geq u_{k,tr,s} - s_k - M \cdot (1 - f_{k,tr,s}) - M \cdot (1 - f_{t,tr,s}) \quad \forall k \in K, \; t \in T^{near}, \; tr \in Tr_s, \; s \in S
$$

**(C16) Coupling-Decoupling Consistency:** Shunting movements must align with coupling changes.
$$
y_{t,r,r'} - y_{t',r,r'} \leq z_k \quad \forall k \in K \text{ connecting trips } t, t', \; r, r' \in R, \; r < r'
$$

**(C17) Rolling Stock Location Tracking:** Units must be at the correct location for shunting.
$$
\sum_{t \in T: arr_t = s} x_{t,r} = \sum_{k \in K_s: \text{start}} \text{unit}_r(k) \cdot z_k \quad \forall r \in R, \; s \in S
$$

**(C18) Shunting Driver Availability:** (Optional) Limits concurrent shunting movements.
$$
\sum_{k \in K_s: \text{overlapping time}} z_k \leq N^{drivers}_s \quad \forall s \in S
$$

---

## 7. Linearization of Non-Linear Terms

**Absolute Value Linearization:**
$$
|x_{t,r} - o_{t,r}| = \Delta_{t,r}^+ + \Delta_{t,r}^-
$$
$$
x_{t,r} - o_{t,r} = \Delta_{t,r}^+ - \Delta_{t,r}^-, \quad \Delta_{t,r}^+, \Delta_{t,r}^- \geq 0
$$

**Max Linearization (Capacity Shortage):**
$$
\text{short}_t \geq dem_t - \sum_{r \in R} cap_r \cdot x_{t,r}, \quad \text{short}_t \geq 0
$$

---

## 8. Algorithm Integration Notes

This unified MILP can be decomposed for solution via **Combinatorial Benders' Decomposition**:

1. **Master Problem (Composition):** Solves constraints (C1)–(C8), generating candidate shunting movements.

2. **Subproblem (Infrastructure):** Solves constraints (C9)–(C18) for fixed $z_k$ values, generating feasibility cuts.

3. **Iterative Heuristic Variant:** Processes shunting movements sequentially, feeding each to the infrastructure model and accepting/rejecting based on feasibility, mimicking the dispatcher interaction described in the paper.

---

## 9. Model Summary

| Component | Variables | Constraints | Purpose |
|-----------|-----------|-------------|---------|
| Composition | $x, y, z, c, d, s$ | C1–C8 | Rolling stock assignment |
| Infrastructure | $f, u, p$ | C9–C14 | Track feasibility |
| Linking | Combined | C15–C18 | Integration |

This formulation captures the threefold contribution described in the paper: (1) ensuring infrastructure feasibility, (2) optimizing operational and passenger service objectives, and (3) maintaining proximity to the original plan through the deviation penalty.

Text:
# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

Based on the provided text, I propose a unified MILP formulation that integrates the multi-stage framework described in the paper, combining rerouting, reordering, and rescheduling with delay propagation and safety overlaps.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T = \{1, \ldots, n_T\}$ | Set of trains |
| $S = \{1, \ldots, n_S\}$ | Set of stations / signal sections |
| $E_t = \{1, \ldots, n_{E_t}\}$ | Ordered set of events (arrivals/departures) of train $t$ |
| $A \subseteq S \times S$ | Set of track arcs |
| $R = \{1, \ldots, n_R\}$ | Set of feasible routes |
| $C \subseteq T \times T$ | Set of conflicting train pairs, with $t_1 < t_2$ |
| $K_s \subseteq T \times T$ | Set of conflicting train pairs at section $s$ |
| $V_t \subseteq R$ | Subset of routes feasible for train $t$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $a_{t,i}$ | Planned time of event $i$ of train $t$ |
| $\tau_{t,a}$ | Minimum running time of train $t$ on arc $a$ |
| $h$ | Minimum headway time between consecutive trains |
| $o_{t,s}$ | Safety overlap margin for train $t$ at section $s$ |
| $\pi_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if route $r$ is feasible for train $t$, 0 otherwise |
| $c_{t,a}$ | Energy consumption rate of train $t$ on arc $a$ |
| $\alpha, \beta \geq 0$ | Weights balancing delay and energy in the objective |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Symbol | Domain | Description |
|--------|--------|-------------|
| $x_{t,i}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual time of event $i$ of train $t$ |
| $\delta_t$ | $\geq 0$ | Total (primary + secondary) delay of train $t$ |
| $\delta_{t_1,t_2}$ | $\geq 0$ | Pair-wise secondary delay of train $t_1$ caused by waiting for train $t_2$ |
| $z_{t_1,t_2}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t_1$ is scheduled before train $t_2$ at the conflict point, 0 otherwise |
| $w_{t,r}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if route $r$ is assigned to train $t$, 0 otherwise |
| $e_{t,a}$ | $\geq 0$ | Additional energy consumption of train $t$ on arc $a$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total delays and additional energy consumption:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \alpha \sum_{t \in T} \delta_t \;+\; \beta \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{a \in A} c_{t,a} \cdot e_{t,a}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Route Selection (Rerouting)

Each train must be assigned exactly one feasible route:

$$
\sum_{r \in V_t} \pi_{t,r} \, w_{t,r} = 1, \quad \forall t \in T \tag{1}
$$

### 5.2 Event Time Definition

The actual time of each event must be at least the planned time plus the total delay:

$$
x_{t,i} \geq a_{t,i} + \delta_t, \quad \forall t \in T,\; i \in E_t \tag{2}
$$

### 5.3 Travel Time on Arcs (Rescheduling)

The time between consecutive events of the same train must respect the minimum running time:

$$
x_{t,i+1} - x_{t,i} \geq \tau_{t,a}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; a = (s_i, s_{i+1}) \in A \tag{3}
$$

### 5.4 Headway and Ordering (Reordering)

For every pair of conflicting trains at section $s$, exactly one ordering is enforced with the minimum headway:

$$
x_{t_1,s} + h + o_{t_1,s} \leq x_{t_2,s} + M(1 - z_{t_1,t_2}), \quad \forall (t_1,t_2) \in K_s \tag{4a}
$$

$$
x_{t_2,s} + h + o_{t_2,s} \leq x_{t_1,s} + M \cdot z_{t_1,t_2}, \quad \forall (t_1,t_2) \in K_s \tag{4b}
$$

### 5.5 Pair-wise Secondary Delay (Sub-optimal Component)

The pair-wise delay captures the additional waiting time of $t_1$ imposed by $t_2$:

$$
\delta_{t_1,t_2} \geq x_{t_2,s} - x_{t_1,s} - h - o_{t_1,s} - M(1 - z_{t_1,t_2}), \quad \forall (t_1,t_2) \in K_s \tag{5}
$$

### 5.6 Delay Propagation (Optimal Component)

The total delay of a train aggregates the primary delay and all pair-wise secondary delays propagated from preceding trains:

$$
\delta_t \geq \delta_t^{primary} + \sum_{t' \in T \,:\, (t',t) \in C} \delta_{t',t}, \quad \forall t \in T \tag{6}
$$

where $\delta_t^{primary}$ is the exogenous (primary) delay of train $t$ given as input.

### 5.7 Safety Overlap Margins

Following Lindenmaier et al. (2022), the departure event of a train at section $s$ must respect the overlap margin behind the corresponding stop signal:

$$
x_{t,s}^{dep} \geq x_{t,s}^{arr} + o_{t,s}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{7}
$$

### 5.8 Energy Consumption Coupling

Additional energy consumption is proportional to the additional running time beyond the minimum:

$$
e_{t,a} \geq x_{t,a+1} - x_{t,a} - \tau_{t,a}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; a \in A \tag{8}
$$

### 5.9 Symmetry Breaking of Ordering Variables

To avoid redundant symmetric solutions:

$$
z_{t_1,t_2} + z_{t_2,t_1} = 1, \quad \forall (t_1,t_2) \in C \tag{9}
$$

### 5.10 Domain Constraints

$$
x_{t,i} \geq 0,\; \delta_t \geq 0,\; \delta_{t_1,t_2} \geq 0,\; e_{t,a} \geq 0, \quad \forall t, t_1, t_2, i, a \tag{10a}
$$

$$
z_{t_1,t_2} \in \{0,1\},\; w_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall t_1, t_2, r \tag{10b}
$$

---

## 6. Multi-Stage Solution Strategy

The model above is solved in three sequential stages (similar to Keita et al., 2020, but without Benders' iterations):

**Stage 1 — Rerouting & Reordering (Sub-optimal model):**  
Solve the model with constraints (1), (4)–(5), (9)–(10), omitting (6). This provides a fast, low-complexity solution identifying routes and ordering decisions.

**Stage 2 — Rescheduling (Optimal model):**  
Fix $w_{t,r}$ and $z_{t_1,t_2}$ from Stage 1, then solve the full model including (6) and (7). This guarantees the global optimum for the original rtRTMP of Pellegrini et al. (2014).

**Stage 3 — Safety Verification:**  
The obtained schedule is forwarded to the extended model of Lindenmaier et al. (2022) to verify safety-relevant overlaps.

---

## 7. Assumptions

1. **Macroscopic infrastructure representation** — signals and lower-level track elements are abstracted away (consistent with Dollevoet et al., 2015; Kanai et al., 2011).
2. **Deterministic primary delays** — initial delays are known at the time of rescheduling; stochastic disturbances are not modeled.
3. **Constant minimum headway** — $h$ is the same for all train pairs; relaxing this would require train-pair-specific parameters.
4. **Fixed train speeds** — running times $\tau_{t,a}$ are deterministic and independent of the chosen route.
5. **Linear energy model** — energy consumption is proportional to additional running time, neglecting regenerative braking and speed profiles.
6. **No train overtaking on the same route** — implicit in the ordering constraints (4a)–(4b).
7. **Big-M tightness** — $M$ is chosen as the smallest value that does not cut off any feasible integer solution (typically the length of the planning horizon).
8. **Static conflict set** — $K_s$ is determined before optimization from the planned timetable and route alternatives.
9. **Single planning horizon** — all events occur within a fixed time window; cyclic timetables are not considered.
10. **FIFO is not enforced** — the model permits non-FIFO ordering when beneficial, in line with the literature (Corman, 2010; Pellegrini et al., 2014).

---

## 8. Remarks on Optimality

- The **sub-optimal** version (without constraint (6)) corresponds to the pair-wise delay interpretation described in Section 3.1 of the paper. It neglects delay propagation and therefore may yield a sub-optimal global solution.
- The **optimal** version (with constraint (6)) extends the sub-optimal model and guarantees the global optimum of the original rtRTMP, as analyzed in Section 3.2 and formalized in Section 3.3 of the paper.
- The computational advantage over the original formulation of Pellegrini et al. (2014) arises from the pair-wise delay reformulation, which reduces the number of equivalent integer combinations and avoids redundant delay-propagation constraints during the rerouting/reordering stage.

Text:
# Final MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Introduction and Modeling Assumptions

This MILP integrates **train rescheduling** (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with **speed management** (generation of feasible speed profiles) for high-speed railways during a partial segment blockage. The model yields a conflict-free timetable with executable speed profiles that minimize total delay and energy consumption.

**Key Assumptions:**
1. **Time discretization**: Planning horizon is discretized into uniform intervals of duration $\Delta t$.
2. **Homogeneous fleet**: All trains share identical kinematic parameters ($V_{\max}, V_{\min}, A_{\max}, D_{\max}$).
3. **Single disruption**: Only one segment $k_{dis}$ is blocked during window $[\tau_s, \tau_e]$.
4. **Bidirectional rerouting**: Rerouting uses the opposite track within the same segment.
5. **Single-track usage per train**: A train uses exactly one track per segment at any time.
6. **Convex energy function**: Energy consumption is a convex function of speed, linearized via piecewise approximation.
7. **Cancellation allowed**: Trains may be cancelled with penalty.
8. **Fixed minimum dwell**: Dwell times have lower bounds but can extend up to a maximum.
9. **No track switching mid-segment**: A train cannot switch tracks within a segment.
10. **Known directions**: Each train's direction is predefined.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of track segments, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{I} = \{1, 2, \dots, |\mathcal{I}|\}$ | Set of discretized time intervals, indexed by $i$ |
| $\mathcal{D} = \{U, D\}$ | Set of directions (Up / Down) |
| $\mathcal{B}$ | Set of breakpoints for PWL energy curve, indexed by $b$ |
| $\mathcal{K}^{dis} \subseteq \mathcal{K}$ | Set of disrupted segments (here, $\{k_{dis}\}$) |
| $\mathcal{T}^+(k), \mathcal{T}^-(k)$ | Trains in up/down direction on segment $k$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $L_k$ | Length of segment $k$ | km |
| $V_{\max}, V_{\min}$ | Maximum / minimum allowable speed | km/h |
| $A_{\max}, D_{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration | km/h² |
| $\tau_s^{dw,\min}, \tau_s^{dw,\max}$ | Min/max dwell time at station $s$ | h |
| $H_{\min}$ | Minimum headway (same direction) | h |
| $H_{\min}^{opp}$ | Minimum headway (opposite direction) | h |
| $\tau_s^{dis}, \tau_e^{dis}$ | Disruption window start/end | h |
| $k_{dis}$ | Disrupted segment index | – |
| $\Delta t$ | Duration of one time interval | h |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (Big-M) | – |
| $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3, \alpha_4$ | Weights for delay, energy, cancellation, rerouting | – |
| $a_{t,s}^0, d_{t,s}^0$ | Scheduled arrival/departure times | h |
| $P_{\max}$ | Maximum traction power | kW |
| $v_b$ | $b$-th speed breakpoint | km/h |
| $E_b$ | Energy at breakpoint $b$ | kWh/km |
| $d(t) \in \mathcal{D}$ | Predefined direction of train $t$ | – |
| $\text{tr}^0(t, k)$ | Original (default) track of train $t$ on segment $k$ | – |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### Timing Variables
- $a_{t,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$: actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $d_{t,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$: actual departure time of train $t$ from station $s$
- $\delta_{t,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$: arrival delay of train $t$ at station $s$
- $w_{t,s} \in [\tau_s^{dw,\min}, \tau_s^{dw,\max}]$: dwell time of train $t$ at station $s$

### Speed and Position Variables
- $v_{t,k,i} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$: speed of train $t$ on segment $k$ during interval $i$
- $p_{t,k,i} \in [0, L_k]$: position of train $t$ on segment $k$ at end of interval $i$
- $x_{t,k,i} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ occupies segment $k$ during interval $i$
- $y_{t,k,i} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ enters segment $k$ at interval $i$
- $z_{t,k,i} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ exits segment $k$ at interval $i$

### Conflict and Rerouting Variables
- $o_{t,t',k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ precedes train $t'$ on segment $k$
- $r_{t,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses opposite (rerouted) track on segment $k$
- $\text{cancel}_t \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ is cancelled

### Energy Variables
- $e_{t,k,i} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$: energy consumption of train $t$ on segment $k$ during interval $i$
- $\lambda_{t,k,i,b} \in [0,1]$: convex combination weight for breakpoint $b$ (SOS2)

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min Z = \alpha_1 \underbrace{\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \delta_{t,s}}_{\text{total delay}} + \alpha_2 \underbrace{\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} e_{t,k,i}}_{\text{total energy}} + \alpha_3 \underbrace{\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \text{cancel}_t}_{\text{cancellations}} + \alpha_4 \underbrace{\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} r_{t,k}}_{\text{reroutings}}
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### (a) Train Dynamics Constraints

**Speed limits (linked to occupation):**
$$
V_{\min} \, x_{t,k,i} \leq v_{t,k,i} \leq V_{\max} \, x_{t,k,i} \quad \forall t, k, i
$$

**Acceleration limit:**
$$
v_{t,k,i+1} - v_{t,k,i} \leq A_{\max} \Delta t + M(1 - x_{t,k,i+1}) \quad \forall t, k, i
$$

**Deceleration limit:**
$$
v_{t,k,i} - v_{t,k,i+1} \leq D_{\max} \Delta t + M(1 - x_{t,k,i+1}) \quad \forall t, k, i
$$

**Position progression:**
$$
p_{t,k,i+1} = p_{t,k,i} + v_{t,k,i} \Delta t \quad \forall t, k, i
$$

**Segment traversal:**
$$
p_{t,k,|\mathcal{I}|} \geq L_k (1 - \text{cancel}_t) \quad \forall t, k
$$

**Power limit:**
$$
v_{t,k,i} \leq P_{\max} \quad \forall t, k, i
$$

### (b) Timing Constraints

**Dwell time definition:**
$$
d_{t,s} = a_{t,s} + w_{t,s} \quad \forall t, s
$$

**Dwell time bounds:**
$$
\tau_s^{dw,\min} \leq w_{t,s} \leq \tau_s^{dw,\max} \quad \forall t, s
$$

**Arrival-departure linkage across segments** (for segment $k$ from $s$ to $s'$):
$$
a_{t,s'} \geq d_{t,s} + \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} x_{t,k,i} \Delta t - M(1 - \text{use}_{t,k}) \quad \forall t, k
$$

**Delay definition:**
$$
\delta_{t,s} \geq a_{t,s} - a_{t,s}^0 \quad \forall t, s
$$

$$
\delta_{t,s} \leq a_{t,s} - a_{t,s}^0 + M \cdot \text{cancel}_t \quad \forall t, s
$$

**Initial departure time:**
$$
d_{t,s_0(t)} \geq d_{t,s_0(t)}^0 \quad \forall t
$$

### (c) Same-Direction Headway Constraints

For each pair of trains $t, t'$ in the same direction on segment $k$:

$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} i \cdot x_{t',k,i} \Delta t \geq \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} i \cdot x_{t,k,i} \Delta t + H_{\min} - M(1 - o_{t,t',k}) \quad \forall t, t', k
$$

$$
o_{t,t',k} + o_{t',t,k} = 1 \quad \forall t, t', k
$$

### (d) Bidirectional Conflict Resolution

For opposing trains $t \in \mathcal{T}^+(k)$, $t' \in \mathcal{T}^-(k)$ sharing the same track on segment $k$:

$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} i \cdot x_{t,k,i} \Delta t + \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} x_{t,k,i} \Delta t + H_{\min}^{opp} \leq \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} i \cdot x_{t',k,i} \Delta t + M(1 - o_{t,t',k}) \quad \forall k
$$

$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} i \cdot x_{t',k,i} \Delta t + \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} x_{t',k,i} \Delta t + H_{\min}^{opp} \leq \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} i \cdot x_{t,k,i} \Delta t + M \cdot o_{t,t',k} \quad \forall k
$$

**Single-track capacity (opposing directions):**
$$
\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}^+(k)} x_{t,k,i} + \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}^-(k)} x_{t,k,i} \leq 1 \quad \forall k, i
$$

### (e) Disruption Constraints

**Blocked segment during disruption window (default track):**
$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}_d} x_{t,k_{dis},i} \leq M \cdot r_{t,k_{dis}} \quad \forall t
$$

where $\mathcal{I}_d = \{i : \tau_s^{dis} \leq i \Delta t \leq \tau_e^{dis}\}$.

**Traverse before or after disruption:**
$$
a_{t,s'} \leq \tau_s^{dis} + M(1 - \text{before}_t) + M \cdot r_{t,k_{dis}} \quad \forall t
$$

$$
d_{t,s} \geq \tau_e^{dis} - M \cdot \text{before}_t - M \cdot r_{t,k_{dis}} \quad \forall t
$$

$$
\text{before}_t + \text{after}_t + r_{t,k_{dis}} + \text{cancel}_t \geq 1 \quad \forall t
$$

### (f) Rerouting Constraints

**Rerouting only on disrupted segments:**
$$
r_{t,k} \leq \mathbb{1}_{(k = k_{dis})} \quad \forall t, k
$$

**Rerouting implies non-cancellation:**
$$
r_{t,k} \leq 1 - \text{cancel}_t \quad \forall t, k
$$

**Track indicator consistency:**
$$
\text{tr}_{t,k} = \text{tr}^0(t,k) \oplus r_{t,k} \quad \forall t, k
$$

where $\oplus$ denotes XOR (linearized via auxiliary variables).

### (g) Energy Consumption (Piecewise Linear)

**Convex combination of breakpoints:**
$$
\sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} \lambda_{t,k,i,b} = x_{t,k,i} \quad \forall t, k, i
$$

**Speed from breakpoints:**
$$
v_{t,k,i} = \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} v_b \cdot \lambda_{t,k,i,b} \quad \forall t, k, i
$$

**Energy from breakpoints:**
$$
e_{t,k,i} = \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} E_b \cdot \lambda_{t,k,i,b} \quad \forall t, k, i
$$

**SOS2 constraint:**
$$
\{\lambda_{t,k,i,b}\}_{b \in \mathcal{B}} \text{ is SOS2} \quad \forall t, k, i
$$

### (h) Flow Conservation Constraints

**Entry-exit linking:**
$$
y_{t,k,i} - z_{t,k,i} = x_{t,k,i} - x_{t,k,i-1} \quad \forall t, k, i
$$

**At most one entry per segment:**
$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} y_{t,k,i} \leq 1 - \text{cancel}_t \quad \forall t, k
$$

**At most one exit per segment:**
$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} z_{t,k,i} \leq 1 - \text{cancel}_t \quad \forall t, k
$$

**Station flow conservation:**
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}^{in}(s)} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} z_{t,k,i} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}^{out}(s)} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} y_{t,k,i} \quad \forall t, s \notin \{s_0(t), s_f(t)\}
$$

### (i) Logical Constraints

**Cancelled trains have no activity:**
$$
x_{t,k,i} \leq 1 - \text{cancel}_t \quad \forall t, k, i
$$

$$
a_{t,s} \leq M(1 - \text{cancel}_t) \quad \forall t, s
$$

$$
d_{t,s} \leq M(1 - \text{cancel}_t) \quad \forall t, s
$$

$$
\delta_{t,s} \leq M(1 - \text{cancel}_t) \quad \forall t, s
$$

**Active trains traverse at least one segment:**
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} x_{t,k,i} \geq 1 - \text{cancel}_t \quad \forall t
$$

**Ordering symmetry breaking:**
$$
o_{t,t',k} + o_{t',t,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall t < t', k
$$

---

## 7. Model Summary

| Component | Approximate Count |
|-----------|-------------------|
| **Binary variables** | $O(|\mathcal{T}| \cdot |\mathcal{K}| \cdot |\mathcal{I}| + |\mathcal{T}|^2 \cdot |\mathcal{K}|)$ |
| **Continuous variables** | $O(|\mathcal{T}| \cdot |\mathcal{K}| \cdot |\mathcal{I}| + |\mathcal{T}| \cdot |\mathcal{S}|)$ |
| **SOS2 sets** | $|\mathcal{T}| \cdot |\mathcal{K}| \cdot |\mathcal{I}|$ (each of size $|\mathcal{B}|$) |
| **Constraints** | $O(|\mathcal{T}|^2 |\mathcal{K}| + |\mathcal{T}| |\mathcal{K}| |\mathcal{I}| + |\mathcal{T}| |\mathcal{K}| |\mathcal{I}| |\mathcal{B}|)$ |

**Model Classification**: Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) with SOS2 constraints.

**Solution Approach**: The model can be solved directly by branch-and-cut solvers (CPLEX, Gurobi) for small-to-medium instances. For large instances, the proposed decomposition-based method (reformulated IP + train plan selection with adaptive iterative refinement) is recommended.

**Key Strengths**:
- Unified framework coupling rescheduling and speed management
- Explicit handling of bidirectional conflicts on shared tracks
- Flexible rerouting with energy-aware speed profiles
- Comprehensive delay, energy, cancellation, and rerouting objectives

**Key Challenges**:
- Large-scale instances require decomposition due to combinatorial complexity
- Big-M values must be carefully tightened for solver efficiency
- SOS2 constraints require native solver support (available in CPLEX/Gurobi)

Text:
# Final MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

Below is the complete, integrated Mixed-Integer Linear Programming formulation that simultaneously handles **retiming, reordering, rerouting, and speed profile optimization** for bidirectional high-speed rail traffic during a single-track disruption.

---

## 1. Modelling Assumptions

- **A1 (Space–time discretization):** Time is discretized in steps of $\Delta t$; each segment $e$ is discretized in position steps of $\Delta x_e$.
- **A2 (PWL resistance):** Davis resistance $F(v)=c_0+c_1 v+c_2 v^2$ is approximated by an **SOS2 piecewise-linear** function over $K$ breakpoints.
- **A3 (Single disrupted segment):** One segment $e^\star$ has a partial blockage on its mainline track during $[T_d^-,T_d^+]$.
- **A4 (Bidirectional rerouting):** During the disruption, trains normally using $R_{\text{main}}$ of $e^\star$ are rerouted to $R_{\text{opp}}$, where bidirectional conflicts are resolved by temporal separation $h^{\text{opp}}$.
- **A5 (No overtaking in segments):** Reordering occurs at stations only.
- **A6 (Cancellation allowed):** Each train may be cancelled at a penalty.

---

## 2. Sets & Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | trains, $t,t'\in T$ |
| $U$ | stations, $u\in U$ |
| $E$ | segments, $e\in E$ |
| $R=\{R_m,R_o\}$ | track sides (main, opposite) |
| $I=\{1,\dots,N_I\}$ | time steps |
| $J(e)=\{1,\dots,N_J(e)\}$ | position steps of segment $e$ |
| $K=\{1,\dots,|K|\}$ | PWL breakpoints |
| $e^\star$ | disrupted segment |
| $u^-(e),u^+(e)$ | upstream/downstream station of $e$ |

**Parameters:** $L_e, \Delta t, \Delta x_e, v^{\min}, v^{\max}, a^{\max}, b^{\max}, F^{\max}, B^{\max}, M_{\text{big}}, \eta, \tau_u^{\min},\tau_u^{\max}, h^{\min}, h^{\text{opp}}, \phi_E,\phi_D,\phi_C$, scheduled times $A_t^0(u),D_t^0(u)$, Davis coefficients $c_0,c_1,c_2$, PWL breakpoints $(v^k,F^k)$, gradient $g_e$.

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Binary (occupancy / logic):**
$$x_{t,e,r,i,j},\; z_{t,e,r},\; y_{t,t',e},\; o_{t,t',u},\; w_{t,t',e},\; c_t,\; \zeta_{t,i},\; \rho_{t,e^\star},\; \lambda_{k,t,e,r,i,j}\in\{0,1\}$$

**Continuous:**
$$\text{arr}_{t,u},\;\text{dep}_{t,u},\;\text{ent}_{t,e,r},\;\text{exit}_{t,e,r},\; v_{t,e,r,i,j},\; a_{t,e,r,i,j},\; u_{t,e,r,i,j},\; b_{t,e,r,i,j},\; \sigma_{k,t,e,r,i,j}\geq 0$$
$$\delta_t^{\text{arr}}(u),\;\delta_t^{\text{dep}}(u),\;\delta_t^{\text{total}},\;E_t\geq 0$$

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$\boxed{\;\min\;\;\phi_E\sum_{t\in T}E_t \;+\; \phi_D\sum_{t\in T}\delta_t^{\text{total}} \;+\; \phi_C\sum_{t\in T}c_t\;\tag{OBJ}\;}$$

with $E_t=\eta\sum_{e,r,i,j}u_{t,e,r,i,j}\,\Delta x_e$ and $\delta_t^{\text{total}}\geq \sum_u\!\left(\delta_t^{\text{arr}}(u)+\delta_t^{\text{dep}}(u)\right)$.

The objective jointly minimizes **energy**, **total delay**, and **cancellation** cost.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Occupancy & Routing

**(C1) Cell mutual exclusion:**
$$\sum_{t\in T}x_{t,e,r,i,j}\leq 1 \qquad\forall e,r,i,j.$$

**(C2) Single-cell per time step:**
$$\sum_{e,r,j}x_{t,e,r,i,j}\leq 1 \qquad\forall t,i.$$

**(C3) Track–segment assignment (exactly one track, unless cancelled):**
$$\sum_{r\in R}z_{t,e,r}=1-c_t,\qquad \sum_{i,j}x_{t,e,r,i,j}\leq M_{\text{big}}\,z_{t,e,r},\qquad \sum_{i,j}x_{t,e,r,i,j}\geq z_{t,e,r} \qquad\forall t,e,r.$$

### 5.2 Spatial Flow Conservation

**(C4) Progression within a segment:**
$$x_{t,e,r,i,j}\leq x_{t,e,r,i-1,j-1}+x_{t,e,r,i-1,j}\qquad\forall t,e,r,i\geq 2,j\geq 2.$$

**(C5) No backward motion:**
$$x_{t,e,r,i+1,j}+x_{t,e,r,i,j-1}\leq 1\qquad\forall t,e,r,i,j\geq 2.$$

**(C6) Entry/exit uniqueness:**
$$\sum_{j}x_{t,e,r,1,j}=z_{t,e,r},\qquad \sum_{j}x_{t,e,r,N_I,j}=z_{t,e,r}\qquad\forall t,e,r.$$

### 5.3 Speed Dynamics & Kinematics

**(C7) Speed evolution (big-M linearized):**
$$v_{t,e,r,i+1,j+1}-v_{t,e,r,i,j}-a_{t,e,r,i,j}\,\Delta t \leq M_{\text{big}}\!\left(2-x_{t,e,r,i,j}-x_{t,e,r,i+1,j+1}\right),$$
$$v_{t,e,r,i+1,j+1}-v_{t,e,r,i,j}-a_{t,e,r,i,j}\,\Delta t \geq -M_{\text{big}}\!\left(2-x_{t,e,r,i,j}-x_{t,e,r,i+1,j+1}\right).$$

**(C8) Speed & acceleration limits (inactive when $x=0$):**
$$v^{\min}\,x_{t,e,r,i,j}\leq v_{t,e,r,i,j}\leq v^{\max}\,x_{t,e,r,i,j},$$
$$-b^{\max}\,x_{t,e,r,i,j}\leq a_{t,e,r,i,j}\leq a^{\max}\,x_{t,e,r,i,j}.$$

**(C9) Force limits:**
$$0\leq u_{t,e,r,i,j}\leq F^{\max}\,x_{t,e,r,i,j},\qquad 0\leq b_{t,e,r,i,j}\leq B^{\max}\,x_{t,e,r,i,j}.$$

### 5.4 Longitudinal Dynamics (Newton's law with SOS2 resistance)

**(C10) Speed-to-PWL interpolation (SOS2):**
$$v_{t,e,r,i,j}=\sum_{k\in K}\sigma_{k,t,e,r,i,j}\,v^k,\qquad \sum_k\sigma_{k,t,e,r,i,j}=1,\quad \sigma_k\geq 0,$$
$$\sigma_{1}\leq\lambda_1,\quad \sigma_{|K|}\leq\lambda_{|K|-1},$$
$$\sigma_k\leq \lambda_{k-1}+\lambda_k\;\;(k=2,\dots,|K|-1),\qquad \sum_{k=1}^{|K|-1}\lambda_k=1.$$

**(C11) Resistance and Newton's law:**
$$M\,a_{t,e,r,i,j}=u_{t,e,r,i,j}-b_{t,e,r,i,j}-M\,g_e-\sum_k\sigma_{k,t,e,r,i,j}\,F^k.$$

**(C12) Energy definition:**
$$E_t=\eta\sum_{e,r,i,j}u_{t,e,r,i,j}\,\Delta x_e.$$

### 5.5 Segment Entry/Exit Times

**(C13) Linking occupancy to entry/exit times:**
$$\text{ent}_{t,e,r}=\sum_{i,j} i\Delta t\;x_{t,e,r,i,1},\qquad \text{exit}_{t,e,r}=\sum_{i,j}i\Delta t\;x_{t,e,r,i,N_J(e)}.$$

**(C14) Kinematic travel-time lower bound:**
$$\text{exit}_{t,e,r}-\text{ent}_{t,e,r}\;\geq\;\frac{L_e}{v^{\max}}\,z_{t,e,r}.$$

### 5.6 Station Timing & Delay

**(C15) Dwell bounds:**
$$\tau_u^{\min}\leq \text{dep}_{t,u}-\text{arr}_{t,u}\leq \tau_u^{\max}.$$

**(C16) Station–segment linking:**
$$\text{arr}_{t,u^+(e)}=\text{exit}_{t,e,r},\qquad \text{dep}_{t,u^-(e)}=\text{ent}_{t,e,r}.$$

**(C17) Delay definitions:**
$$\delta_t^{\text{arr}}(u)\geq \text{arr}_{t,u}-A_t^0(u),\qquad \delta_t^{\text{dep}}(u)\geq \text{dep}_{t,u}-D_t^0(u),$$
$$\delta_t^{\text{total}}\geq\sum_{u\in U}\!\left(\delta_t^{\text{arr}}(u)+\delta_t^{\text{dep}}(u)\right).$$

### 5.7 Headway, Reordering & Bidirectional Conflicts

**(C18) Same-track, same-direction segment headway:**
$$\text{ent}_{t,e,r}-\text{ent}_{t',e,r}\geq h^{\min}\,z_{t,e,r}z_{t',e,r}-M_{\text{big}}(1-y_{t,t',e})\qquad(\text{dir}_t=\text{dir}_{t'}),$$
with the symmetric counterpart and the requirement $y_{t,t',e}+y_{t',t,e}=1$.

**(C19) Intra-segment safety gap (no co-occupancy at distance $<h^{\min}$):**
$$x_{t,e,r,i,j}+x_{t',e,r,i,j+h}\leq 1+(1-z_{t,e,r})+(1-z_{t',e,r})\;\;(h<\lceil h^{\min}/\Delta t\rceil).$$

**(C20) Bidirectional conflict on opposite track ($e^\star$):**
$$\text{ent}_{t,e^\star,R_o}-\text{exit}_{t',e^\star,R_o}\geq h^{\text{opp}}-M_{\text{big}}(1-w_{t,t',e^\star})\quad(\text{dir}_t\neq\text{dir}_{t'}),$$
with the symmetric counterpart and $w_{t,t',e^\star}+w_{t',t,e^\star}=1$.

**(C21) Departure ordering at stations:**
$$\text{dep}_{t,u}-\text{dep}_{t',u}\geq h^{\min}\,o_{t,t',u}-M_{\text{big}}(1-o_{t,t',u}),$$
with the symmetric counterpart.

**(C22) Platform-track capacity:**
$$\sum_{t}d_{t,u,i}\leq P_u^{\max},\qquad \text{dep}_{t,u}\in[i\Delta t,(i+1)\Delta t)\Leftrightarrow d_{t,u,i}=1.$$

### 5.8 Disruption & Rerouting

**(C23) Mainline blockage:**
$$x_{t,e^\star,R_m,i,j}=0\qquad \forall t,\; i\in[T_d^-,T_d^+],\; j.$$

**(C24) Rerouting indicator via time-overlap binary $\rho_{t,e^\star}$:**
$$\text{ent}_{t,e^\star,r}\leq T_d^++M_{\text{big}}(1-\rho_{t,e^\star}),\qquad \text{exit}_{t,e^\star,r}\geq T_d^--M_{\text{big}}(1-\rho_{t,e^\star}),$$
$$\text{ent}_{t,e^\star,r}\geq T_d^--M_{\text{big}}\rho_{t,e^\star},\qquad \text{exit}_{t,e^\star,r}\leq T_d^++M_{\text{big}}\rho_{t,e^\star},\qquad \rho_{t,e^\star}\leq z_{t,e^\star,r}.$$

**(C25) Forced rerouting during disruption:**
$$z_{t,e^\star,R_m}\leq 1-\rho_{t,e^\star},\qquad z_{t,e^\star,R_o}\geq \rho_{t,e^\star}(1-c_t).$$

### 5.9 Cancellation, Boundary & Symmetry-Breaking

**(C26) Cancellation:**
$$x_{t,e,r,i,j}\leq 1-c_t\qquad\forall t,e,r,i,j.$$

**(C27) Boundary conditions:**
$$\text{arr}_{t,o_t}=D_t^0(o_t),\qquad v_{t,e^{\text{last}}_t,r,N_J}=0,\qquad x_{t,e,r,i,j}=0\;(\forall e\notin\text{route}_t).$$

**(C28) Symmetry-breaking on bidirectional conflicts:**
$$w_{t,t',e}=0\quad\text{for }(t,t')\in B\text{ with }t<t'\text{ (lex).}$$

---

## 6. Integration of the Four Decision Layers

| Decision Layer | Key variables | Binding constraints |
|---------------|---------------|---------------------|
| **Retiming** | $\text{arr}_{t,u},\text{dep}_{t,u},\delta^{\text{arr}},\delta^{\text{dep}}$ | C15–C17 → cost via $\phi_D$ |
| **Reordering** | $y_{t,t',e}, o_{t,t',u}$ | C18, C19, C21, C22 |
| **Rerouting** | $z_{t,e,R_o}$ | C23–C25 (couples with C20) |
| **Speed profile** | $v,a,u,b,\sigma,\lambda$ | C7–C12 → cost via $\phi_E$ |

The objective **OBJ** balances all four; the constraints **couple** them so that, e.g., rerouting forces different $(v,u,b)$ choices which alter energy (C12), and reordering interacts with retiming through platform capacity (C22).

---

## 7. Computational Complexity & Decomposition Rationale

The number of binaries scales as
$$\#\text{bin}\;\approx\;|T|\cdot|E|\cdot|R|\cdot|I|\cdot|J| + |T|\cdot|E| + |T|\cdot|D| + \tfrac{1}{2}|B|\cdot|E|,$$
which for realistic instances ($|T|\!\sim\!50$, $|E|\!\sim\!200$, $|R|=2$, $|I|\!\sim\!20$, $|J|\!\sim\!5$) reaches $>10^6$ binaries. This justifies the **decomposition-based solution framework** referenced in the paper:

1. **Benders decomposition** on edge-coupling variables ($\tau$, $w$, $y$).
2. **SOS2 lazy-callbacks** for the PWL resistance.
3. **Lagrangian relaxation** of safety couplings (C19–C20) yielding per-train dynamic programs.
4. **Symmetry-breaking** (C28) halves the binary search space on bidirectional pairs.

The Big-M constants should be tightened using the time-window horizon rather than chosen conservatively, which is essential for obtaining a tight LP relaxation in the decomposition.

---

## 8. Final Compact Statement

$$\boxed{\;\min\;\;\phi_E\!\sum_t E_t+\phi_D\!\sum_t\delta_t^{\text{total}}+\phi_C\!\sum_t c_t\;\;\text{s.t.}\;\;\text{C1–C28 over variables defined in §3.}\;}$$

This MILP simultaneously optimizes train retiming, reordering, rerouting (with bidirectional conflict resolution), and physics-based speed profiles under a single-track partial blockage, while enforcing safety headways, dwell-time bounds, platform capacity, energy budgets, and cancellation feasibility through explicit linear constraints.

Text:
# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## Assumptions

1. The railway line is a double-track high-speed line; one track per travel direction under normal conditions, with the option to reroute trains onto the opposite track within the disruption time window.
2. Time is discretised into intervals of length Δt, indexed by *i* ∈ *I*, covering the planning horizon [0, *H*].
3. The line is partitioned into |*S*| − 1 sections between stations and further into |*B*| block sections; each block section *b* has a known length *L_b*.
4. A partial segment blockage affects block *B\** during the disruption window [*T*_start, *T*_end]; no train of any direction may occupy *B\** during that window.
5. Each train executes a four-phase speed profile on every section: acceleration → cruising → coasting → braking. Only one phase is active per (train, section) at a time (coasting is treated as a low-power cruising variant).
6. Trains cannot pass each other inside a block section; the block capacity is one train at a time. Trains on the opposite track during rerouting share capacity via an explicit bidirectional-conflict constraint.
7. Dwell times are bounded between *t*_min_dwell and *t*_max_dwell at every intermediate station.
8. A minimum headway *h*_min separates two consecutive trains at any station.
9. Energy consumption is approximated linearly through phase-specific reference speeds *v*_*k*,ref (a standard engineering linearisation that avoids bilinear terms).

---

## Sets

- *T* — trains, indexed by *t*
- *S* — stations, indexed by *s* ∈ {0, 1, …, |*S*|}; section *s* lies between stations *s* and *s* + 1
- *B* — block sections, indexed by *b* (|*B*| ≥ |*S*| − 1)
- *R* = {normal, reroute} — feasible routes
- *K* = {acc, cruise, coast, brake} — speed-profile phases, indexed by *k*
- *I* — discretised time intervals, indexed by *i*
- *D* = {fwd, bwd} — travel directions

---

## Parameters

- *L_b* — length of block *b*
- *v*_max, *v*_min — maximum and minimum operating speeds
- *a*_max, *d*_max — maximum acceleration and deceleration
- *h*_min — minimum safe headway
- *t*_min_dwell, *t*_max_dwell — dwell-time bounds
- *a*_sched^*t,s*, *d*_sched^*t,s* — scheduled arrival/departure times
- Δ*t* — interval length; *H* = |*I*| · Δ*t*
- *M* — sufficiently large positive constant
- cap_*b* — block capacity (here 1)
- ρ — energy-consumption coefficient
- *P*_cancel — penalty per cancelled train
- *w*_delay, *w*_energy, *w*_cancel — objective weights
- *B\** — blocked block; [*T*_start, *T*_end] — disruption window
- *v*_*k*,ref — reference speed for phase *k* (used to linearise energy)
- routeBlocks(*r*, dir) ⊆ *B* — blocks traversed by route *r* in direction dir
- dir(*t*) — direction of train *t*

---

## Decision Variables

- *a*_*t,s* ≥ 0 — actual arrival time of train *t* at station *s*
- *d*_*t,s* ≥ 0 — actual departure time of train *t* at station *s*
- delay_*t* ≥ 0 — total delay of train *t*
- *x*_*t,b,i* ∈ {0, 1} — 1 if train *t* occupies block *b* during interval *i*
- *y*_*t,r* ∈ {0, 1} — 1 if train *t* uses route *r*
- *z*_*t,t′,b* ∈ {0, 1} — 1 if train *t* traverses block *b* before train *t′*
- *w*_*t,s,k* ∈ {0, 1} — 1 if phase *k* is active on section *s* for train *t*
- *v*_*t,s* ∈ [*v*_min, *v*_max] — average speed of train *t* on section *s*
- τ_*t,s,k* ≥ 0 — time spent by train *t* in phase *k* on section *s*
- *d*_acc^*t,s*, *d*_cru^*t,s*, *d*_brk^*t,s* ≥ 0 — distances covered in acceleration, cruising and braking on section *s*
- *e_t* ≥ 0 — energy consumption of train *t*
- *c_t* ∈ {0, 1} — 1 if train *t* is cancelled
- occ_*t,b,i,d* ∈ {0, 1} — direction-tagged block occupation (for bidirectional conflict)

---

## Objective Function

$$\min \; w_{\text{delay}}\!\sum_{t\in T}\!\text{delay}_t \;+\; w_{\text{energy}}\!\sum_{t\in T}\!e_t \;+\; w_{\text{cancel}}\!\sum_{t\in T}\!c_t\,P_{\text{cancel}}$$

---

## Constraints

### 1. Train dynamics / speed-profile feasibility (per section *s*, train *t*)

$$d_{\text{acc}}^{t,s}+d_{\text{cru}}^{t,s}+d_{\text{brk}}^{t,s}=L_s \qquad (1a)$$

$$\sum_{k\in K} w_{t,s,k}=1-c_t \qquad (1b)$$

$$v_{\min}\le v_{t,s}\le v_{\max} \qquad (1c)$$

$$\tau_{t,s,\text{acc}}\ge \tfrac{d_{\text{acc}}^{t,s}}{v_{\text{acc,ref}}}-M(1-w_{t,s,\text{acc}}) \qquad (1d)$$

$$\tau_{t,s,\text{cruise}}\ge \tfrac{d_{\text{cru}}^{t,s}}{v_{\text{cruise,ref}}}-M(1-w_{t,s,\text{cruise}}) \qquad (1e)$$

$$\tau_{t,s,\text{coast}}\ge \tfrac{d_{\text{cru}}^{t,s}}{v_{\text{coast,ref}}}-M(1-w_{t,s,\text{coast}}) \qquad (1f)$$

$$\tau_{t,s,\text{brake}}\ge \tfrac{d_{\text{brk}}^{t,s}}{v_{\text{brake,ref}}}-M(1-w_{t,s,\text{brake}}) \qquad (1g)$$

(Assumption: the cruise phase saturates at *v*_max, *v*_ts is bounded by (1c); more refined kinematics may use piecewise-linear acceleration.)

### 2. Section traversal time

$$\sum_{k\in K}\tau_{t,s,k}=a_{t,s+1}-d_{t,s}+M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,\;s\in S\setminus\{|S|-1\} \qquad (2)$$

### 3. Dwell-time consistency

$$a_{t,0}=d_{t,0},\qquad a_{t,|S|-1}=d_{t,|S|-1} \qquad (3a)$$

$$t_{\min,\text{dwell}}\le d_{t,s}-a_{t,s}\le t_{\max,\text{dwell}} \qquad \forall t,\;s\in\{1,\dots,|S|-2\} \qquad (3b)$$

### 4. Block-occupation consistency

$$\sum_{i\in I}x_{t,b,i}\,\Delta t \;\ge\; \tfrac{L_b}{v_{\max}}-M\,c_t \qquad (4a)$$

$$\sum_{i\in I}x_{t,b,i}\,\Delta t \;\le\; \tfrac{L_b}{v_{\min}}+M\,c_t \qquad (4b)$$

### 5. Block capacity

$$\sum_{t\in T}x_{t,b,i}\le \text{cap}_b \qquad \forall b,i \qquad (5)$$

### 6. Disruption (blocked block impassable during the disruption window)

$$\sum_{t\in T}x_{t,B^{*},i}=0 \qquad \forall i\;\text{with}\; i\Delta t\in[T_{\text{start}},T_{\text{end}}] \qquad (6)$$

### 7. Route–block coupling

$$x_{t,b,i}\le 1-y_{t,r} \qquad \forall t,b,i,\;r \;\text{with}\; b\notin\text{routeBlocks}(r,\text{dir}(t)) \qquad (7)$$

### 8. Ordering at shared blocks (same direction)

$$z_{t,t',b}+z_{t',t,b}=1 \qquad \forall t\neq t',\;b \qquad (8a)$$

$$x_{t,b,i}+x_{t',b,i}\le 1+M\,(1-z_{t,t',b}) \qquad \forall t\neq t',\;b,i \qquad (8b)$$

### 9. Station headway

$$a_{t',s}-a_{t,s}\ge h_{\min}-M\,(1-z_{t,t',s}) \qquad \forall t\neq t',\;s \qquad (9a)$$

$$d_{t',s}-d_{t,s}\ge h_{\min}-M\,(1-z_{t,t',s}) \qquad \forall t\neq t',\;s \qquad (9b)$$

### 10. Delay measurement

$$\text{delay}_t \ge a_{t,|S|-1}-a_{\text{sched}}^{t,|S|-1} \qquad (10a)$$

$$\text{delay}_t \ge d_{t,0}-d_{\text{sched}}^{t,0} \qquad (10b)$$

### 11. Energy (linearised through reference speeds)

$$e_t=\rho\sum_{s\in S\setminus\{|S|-1\}}\sum_{k\in K}\tau_{t,s,k}\,v_{k,\text{ref}} \qquad (11)$$

### 12. Cancellation deactivates occupation

$$x_{t,b,i}\le 1-c_t \qquad \forall t,b,i \qquad (12)$$

### 13. Bidirectional conflict on the rerouted track

$$\text{occ}_{t,b,i,\text{dir}(t)}=x_{t,b,i} \qquad \forall t,b,i \qquad (13a)$$

$$\sum_{t:\text{dir}(t)=\text{fwd}}\text{occ}_{t,b,i,\text{fwd}}+\sum_{t:\text{dir}(t)=\text{bwd}}\text{occ}_{t,b,i,\text{bwd}}\le \text{cap}_b \qquad \forall b,i \qquad (13b)$$

### 14. Monotonicity of arrival/departure times

$$a_{t,s+1}\ge d_{t,s},\qquad d_{t,s}\ge a_{t,s} \qquad \forall t,\;s\in S\setminus\{|S|-1\} \qquad (14)$$

### 15. Section-speed bounds

Already enforced by (1c) on the variable *v*_*t,s*; together with (1a)–(1g) this guarantees that the kinematic relations between acceleration, cruising, coasting and braking are respected, producing an executable speed profile consistent with the timetable.

---

## Closing Remark

The model above jointly decides (i) the timetable — arrival/departure times, ordering, rerouting, and cancellation — and (ii) the speed profile — phase selection, distance allocations, phase durations, and section-average speeds — while enforcing block capacity, station headways, the disruption infeasibility window, and the bidirectional conflict that arises when opposite-direction trains share the rerouted track. The energy term is linear, the dynamics are linearised through reference speeds and big-M, and every operational constraint (C1–C15) is represented as a linear inequality over continuous and binary variables, yielding a fully linear mixed-integer program.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockage

Below is a complete, linearized MILP formulation inspired by the described integrated framework. The model jointly decides (i) **arrival/departure times** (retiming), (ii) **train order** at conflict points (reordering), (iii) **track assignment** including rerouting (rerouting), and (iv) **speed profiles** (speed management) for trains operating on a bidirectional high-speed line during a partial segment blockage.

---

## 1 Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i,j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations along the line, indexed by $s$, in fixed order |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of (inter-station) track segments, $k \in \{1,\dots,|\mathcal{K}|\}$, between stations $s$ and $s+1$ |
| $\mathcal{B}=\{U,D\}$ | Running direction: $U$ = nominal direction, $D$ = opposite (rerouting) direction |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Set of discretized planning time periods, indexed by $p$ |
| $\mathcal{N}_k$ | Set of nodes (track-circuit / conflict-point) within segment $k$ |

---

## 2 Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $L_k$ | Length of segment $k$ (m) |
| $\Delta t$ | Length of a time period (s) |
| $P$ | Length of planning horizon ($|\mathcal{P}| \cdot \Delta t$) |
| $V_{\min}, V_{\max}$ | Minimum and maximum operating speeds (m/s) |
| $A_{\max}, D_{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration and deceleration (m/s²) |
| $\tau_{\min}, \tau_{\max}$ | Minimum and maximum dwell times at stations (s) |
| $h$ | Minimum safe headway time between consecutive trains (s) |
| $L_{\text{train}}$ | Length of a train (m) |
| $A_{i,s}^{\text{sch}}, D_{i,s}^{\text{sch}}$ | Scheduled arrival and departure of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $[W_k^{\text{start}}, W_k^{\text{end}}]$ | Disruption time window on segment $k$ (s) |
| $C_k \in \{0,1\}$ | $1$ if segment $k$ is blocked in direction $U$ during the disruption, $0$ otherwise |
| $e(v)$ | Energy consumption rate (kWh/s) at speed $v$ (piecewise-linearized, see §6) |
| $P_{\text{cancel}}$ | Penalty for cancelling a train |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Weights for delay, energy, and cancellation in the objective |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (Big-M) |

---

## 3 Decision Variables

### 3.1 Discrete (routing, ordering, cancellation)

- $x_{i,k}^b \in \{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $i$ traverses segment $k$ in direction $b \in \mathcal{B}$.
- $r_{i,k} \in \{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $i$ uses local rerouting on segment $k$.
- $y_{i,j,k} \in \{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $i$ departs segment $k$ before train $j$ enters it.
- $z_i \in \{0,1\}$: $1$ if train $i$ is cancelled.

### 3.2 Continuous (timing, speed, energy)

- $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \ge 0$: actual arrival and departure times of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $\delta_{i,s} \ge 0$: additional dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $v_{i,p} \ge 0$: speed of train $i$ at the end of period $p$.
- $\pi_{i,p} \ge 0$: position (distance from origin) of train $i$ at the end of period $p$.
- $e_i \ge 0$: total energy consumption of train $i$.
- $t_{i,k}^{\text{in}}, t_{i,k}^{\text{out}} \ge 0$: entry and exit times of train $i$ at segment $k$.
- $\Delta_{i,s} \ge 0$: arrival delay of train $i$ at station $s$.

---

## 4 Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \alpha \underbrace{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} \sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} \Delta_{i,s}}_{\text{total delay}}
\;+\; \beta \underbrace{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} e_i}_{\text{total energy}}
\;+\; \gamma \underbrace{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} P_{\text{cancel}}\, z_i}_{\text{cancellation penalty}}
$$

Linearization of the delay definition is given in (C1).

---

## 5 Constraints

### 5.1 Delay definition
$$
\Delta_{i,s} \;\ge\; a_{i,s} - A_{i,s}^{\text{sch}}, \qquad \Delta_{i,s} \ge 0 \quad \forall\, i\in\mathcal{T},\, s\in\mathcal{S} \tag{C1}
$$

### 5.2 Dwell time and departure
$$
d_{i,s} \;=\; a_{i,s} + \tau_{\min} + \delta_{i,s}, \qquad
0 \le \delta_{i,s} \le \tau_{\max} - \tau_{\min} \quad \forall\, i,s \tag{C2}
$$

### 5.3 Routing consistency
$$
\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}} x_{i,k}^b \;=\; 1 - z_i \quad \forall\, i\in\mathcal{T},\, k\in\mathcal{K} \tag{C3}
$$
$$
r_{i,k} \;\le\; x_{i,k}^{D}, \qquad
r_{i,k} \;\ge\; x_{i,k}^{D} - x_{i,k}^{U} \quad \forall\, i,k \tag{C4}
$$
A train may reroute only by switching from nominal direction $U$ to opposite direction $D$.

### 5.4 Disruption avoidance
For any segment $k$ partially blocked during $[W_k^{\text{start}}, W_k^{\text{end}}]$:
$$
\text{if } C_k = 1:\qquad t_{i,k}^{\text{out}} \le W_k^{\text{start}} \;+\; M(1 - x_{i,k}^{U}) \quad \forall\, i \tag{C5a}
$$
$$
\text{or } \qquad t_{i,k}^{\text{in}} \;\ge\; W_k^{\text{end}} \;-\; M(1 - x_{i,k}^{U}) \quad \forall\, i \tag{C5b}
$$
$$
\text{if } C_k = 0:\qquad t_{i,k}^{\text{out}} \le W_k^{\text{start}} \;+\; M(1 - x_{i,k}^{D}) \quad \forall\, i \tag{C5c}
$$
A train using the blocked track in the affected direction must exit before the disruption begins or enter after it ends.

### 5.5 Inter-station timing consistency
$$
t_{i,k}^{\text{in}} \;=\; d_{i,s(k)} \quad\forall\, i,k \tag{C6a}
$$
$$
t_{i,k}^{\text{out}} \;=\; t_{i,k}^{\text{in}} \;+\; \rho_{i,k} \quad \forall\, i,k \tag{C6b}
$$
where $\rho_{i,k}$ is the running time on segment $k$, computed via (C11)–(C12) using the speed profile.

### 5.6 Segment traversal with conflict resolution (headway)
For every pair $(i,j)$ and segment $k$:
$$
t_{i,k}^{\text{out}} + h \;\le\; t_{j,k}^{\text{in}} \;+\; M(1 - y_{i,j,k}) \tag{C7a}
$$
$$
t_{j,k}^{\text{out}} + h \;\le\; t_{i,k}^{\text{in}} \;+\; M(1 - y_{j,i,k}) \tag{C7b}
$$
$$
y_{i,j,k} + y_{j,i,k} \;\le\; 1, \qquad y_{i,j,k} \in \{0,1\} \tag{C7c}
$$

### 5.7 Bidirectional conflict on rerouted track
If trains $i$ and $j$ use opposite directions on the same segment, an additional separation is required:
$$
\bigl| t_{i,k}^{\text{out}} - t_{j,k}^{\text{out}} \bigr| \;\ge\; h \quad \text{when } x_{i,k}^{U} = x_{j,k}^{D} = 1 \tag{C8}
$$
Linearized as:
$$
t_{i,k}^{\text{out}} - t_{j,k}^{\text{out}} \;\ge\; h - M\bigl(2 - x_{i,k}^{U} - x_{j,k}^{D}\bigr) \tag{C8a}
$$
$$
t_{j,k}^{\text{out}} - t_{i,k}^{\text{out}} \;\ge\; h - M\bigl(2 - x_{i,k}^{U} - x_{j,k}^{D}\bigr) \tag{C8b}
$$

### 5.8 Speed profile dynamics (linearized via time discretization)
$$
\pi_{i,p} \;=\; \pi_{i,p-1} + v_{i,p}\,\Delta t \quad \forall\, i, p\ge 2 \tag{C9}
$$
with $\pi_{i,1} = 0$. (Acceleration is represented implicitly by changes in $v_{i,p}$; a tighter formulation with $\tfrac{1}{2}\Delta v \Delta t$ can be added if desired.)

### 5.9 Speed and acceleration bounds
$$
V_{\min} \;\le\; v_{i,p} \;\le\; V_{\max} \quad \forall\, i,p \tag{C10a}
$$
$$
-D_{\max}\,\Delta t \;\le\; v_{i,p} - v_{i,p-1} \;\le\; A_{\max}\,\Delta t \quad \forall\, i,p\ge 2 \tag{C10b}
$$

### 5.10 Coupling of speed profile with segment running time
$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_k} v_{i,p}\,\Delta t \;=\; L_k \quad \forall\, i,k \tag{C11}
$$
$$
\rho_{i,k} \;=\; t_{i,k}^{\text{out}} - t_{i,k}^{\text{in}} \;=\; |\mathcal{P}_k|\,\Delta t \tag{C12}
$$
where $\mathcal{P}_k \subseteq \mathcal{P}$ is the set of periods during which train $i$ is physically located on segment $k$ (enforced via the position variable $\pi_{i,p}$).

### 5.11 Energy consumption
Using a piecewise-linear approximation of $e(\cdot)$ with breakpoints $(v^{(\ell)}, \eta^{(\ell)})$:
$$
e_i \;=\; \sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}} \sum_{\ell} \eta^{(\ell)} \,\lambda_{i,p}^{(\ell)} \,\Delta t \tag{C13a}
$$
$$
v_{i,p} = \sum_{\ell} v^{(\ell)} \lambda_{i,p}^{(\ell)}, \quad
\sum_{\ell} \lambda_{i,p}^{(\ell)} = 1, \quad \lambda_{i,p}^{(\ell)} \ge 0 \tag{C13b}
$$

### 5.12 Terminal and initial conditions
$$
\pi_{i,1} = 0, \qquad a_{i,s_0} = D_{i,s_0}^{\text{sch}}, \qquad d_{i,s_{\text{end}}} \le P \tag{C14}
$$

### 5.13 Cancellation logic
$$
z_i = 1 \Rightarrow a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, \pi_{i,p}, v_{i,p}, t_{i,k}^{\text{in}}, t_{i,k}^{\text{out}} = 0 \;\; \forall s,k,p \tag{C15}
$$
(implemented by multiplying each affected variable by $(1-z_i)$ or with Big-M.)

---

## 6 Linearization Notes and Modeling Assumptions

1. **Time discretization.** The planning horizon is divided into periods of equal length $\Delta t$, following the standard "discretized time–space network" approach (D’Ariano et al. 2008; Xu et al. 2017). Finer $\Delta t$ improves accuracy at the cost of larger model size.
2. **Continuous space within segments.** Train positions are continuous, but arrival/departure times at stations are tied to discrete time periods. This enables integration with the continuous-time speed profile (C9)–(C10) without loss of generality.
3. **Piecewise-linear energy function.** $e(v)$ is convex in $v$ for typical HSR traction curves and is approximated with $K$ segments (typically $K = 3\text{–}5$), preserving linearity.
4. **Rerouting on a single segment.** It is assumed rerouting re-routes trains to the opposite track for the *blocked segment only* (a standard modeling choice for partial blockages, cf. Louwerse & Huisman 2014; Zhan et al. 2016).
5. **Single-track bidirectional conflict.** Constraint (C8) captures the headway required when two trains use the same physical track in opposite directions; an additional safety margin $h$ is enforced.
6. **Disturbance ≠ disruption.** The model focuses on disruptions: $W_k^{\text{start}} < W_k^{\text{end}}$, i.e., the blockage lasts longer than a normal dwell buffer.
7. **No train overtaking within a segment.** Overtaking is allowed only at stations, encoded implicitly via the ordering variables $y_{i,j,k}$.
8. **Cancellation as a recourse.** $z_i$ allows complete cancellation as a last resort, consistent with Veelenturf et al. (2016) and Borraz-Sánchez et al. (2020).
9. **Coupling TRP ↔ TSMP.** Constraints (C9)–(C12) ensure that the rescheduled timetable ($a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, t_{i,k}^{\text{in/out}}$) is *physically realizable* through the speed profile ($v_{i,p}, \pi_{i,p}$). This is the central novelty of the integrated MILP relative to a separate TRP or TSMP formulation.
10. **Uniform train characteristics.** All trains share $V_{\min}, V_{\max}, A_{\max}, D_{\max}$. Heterogeneity can be added by indexing these parameters with $i$ at the cost of additional notation.

---

## 7 Summary

The above MILP produces, for every train $i$:

- **arrival/departure times** $(a_{i,s}, d_{i,s})$,
- **track/direction assignment** $(x_{i,k}^{U}, x_{i,k}^{D}, r_{i,k})$,
- **ordering decisions** at shared segments $(y_{i,j,k})$,
- **speed profile** $(v_{i,p}, \pi_{i,p})$,

jointly minimizing weighted delay, energy consumption, and cancellations, while satisfying disruption windows, headway safety, and acceleration/deceleration limits. It is the integrated core of the TRSMP-MILP referenced in §4 of the source manuscript and serves as the mathematical foundation on which the decomposition into a reformulated IP and train plans (described in §5 of the source) can be developed.
