Text:
# Integrated MILP Formulation for Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Infrastructure Availability

## 1. Model Overview

The model integrates two interacting components: **(i)** a composition model that assigns rolling stock units to trips and selects shunting movements, and **(ii)** an infrastructure model that ensures shunting movements are feasible with respect to track availability at stations, potentially allowing short delays to other trains. The integrated formulation below captures both components simultaneously; in practice it can be solved via Combinatorial Benders' decomposition (alternating between the two submodels) or via the iterative heuristic described in the source paper.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of train trips in the (disrupted) timetable, indexed by $i$ |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Set of rolling stock units, indexed by $r$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{L}_s$ | Set of railway tracks at station $s \in \mathcal{S}$, indexed by $\ell$ |
| $\mathcal{M}$ | Set of candidate shunting movements, indexed by $m$ |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Set of infrastructure events (arrivals, departures, shunting start/end), indexed by $e$ |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Set of discrete time periods, indexed by $p$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^+_s, \mathcal{T}^-_s \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Trips arriving at / departing from station $s$ |
| $\mathcal{M}(i,i',s)$ | Shunting movements connecting trip $i$ to trip $i'$ at station $s$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\pi^{a}_{i,s},\ \pi^{d}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure time of trip $i$ at station $s$ |
| $q_i$ | Passenger demand on trip $i$ |
| $\kappa_r$ | Seating capacity of rolling stock unit $r$ |
| $\sigma_m$ | Duration of shunting movement $m$ (minutes) |
| $\Delta^{\max}$ | Maximum allowed delay for any event (e.g., 5 min) |
| $F_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if unit $r$ is technically compatible with trip $i$ |
| $o_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if unit $r$ was originally assigned to trip $i$ |
| $L^{s}_m, L^{e}_m \in \mathcal{L}$ | Start / end track of shunting movement $m$ |
| $\mathcal{R}_m \subseteq \mathcal{R}$ | Rolling stock units that can perform shunting movement $m$ |
| $\mathcal{T}_m^{pre}, \mathcal{T}_m^{post} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Trip preceding / succeeding shunting movement $m$ |
| $c^{use}_r$ | Operational cost of deploying unit $r$ |
| $c^{d}$ | Penalty per minute of delay imposed on other trains |
| $c^{u}$ | Penalty per standing passenger (service level) |
| $c^{p}$ | Penalty per unit deviation from the original plan |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (big-M) |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

| Symbol | Domain | Description |
|--------|--------|-------------|
| $x_{i,r}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if rolling stock unit $r$ is assigned to trip $i$ |
| $y_m$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if shunting movement $m$ is executed |
| $z_{e,\ell}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if event $e$ occupies track $\ell$ |
| $\delta_e$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Delay (in minutes) of event $e$ |
| $u_i$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Number of passengers standing on trip $i$ |
| $\alpha^+_{i,r},\ \alpha^-_{i,r}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Positive / negative deviation from original assignment |

---

## 5. Objective Function

A weighted combination of four objectives (weights $w_1,\dots,w_4 \geq 0$):

$$
\min \; w_1 \underbrace{\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} c^{use}_r \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} x_{i,r}}_{\text{operational cost}}
\;+\; w_2 \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} c^{u}\, u_i}_{\text{passenger service level}}
\;+\; w_3 \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}}\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} c^{p}\,(\alpha^+_{i,r}+\alpha^-_{i,r})}_{\text{stick-to-the-plan}}
\;+\; w_4 \underbrace{\sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}} c^{d}\, \delta_e}_{\text{delays to other trains}}
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### (A) Composition Model Constraints

**(A1) Trip coverage** — every trip must be served by at least one compatible unit:
$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}: F_{i,r}=1} x_{i,r} \;\geq\; 1 \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$

**(A2) Passenger capacity** — seated + standing passengers cover demand:
$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}: F_{i,r}=1} \kappa_r\, x_{i,r} \;+\; u_i \;\geq\; q_i \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$

**(A3) Rolling stock flow conservation** at every station (arrivals = departures for each unit):
$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}^+_s} x_{i,r} \;-\; \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}^-_s} x_{i,r} \;=\; 0 \qquad \forall s \in \mathcal{S},\; r \in \mathcal{R}
$$

**(A4) Deviation from original plan** (linearisation of $|x_{i,r}-o_{i,r}|$):
$$
\alpha^+_{i,r} - \alpha^-_{i,r} \;=\; x_{i,r} - o_{i,r} \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; r \in \mathcal{R}
$$

**(A5) Shunting requires assignment** — a shunting movement can only be executed if the corresponding unit is assigned to the preceding and succeeding trips:
$$
y_m \;\leq\; x_{i,r} \qquad \forall m \in \mathcal{M},\; r \in \mathcal{R}_m,\; i \in \mathcal{T}^{pre}_m \cup \mathcal{T}^{post}_m
$$

### (B) Infrastructure Model Constraints

**(B1) Shunting occupies specific tracks** at start and end:
$$
y_m \;\leq\; z_{e^s_m,\, L^s_m} \qquad \forall m \in \mathcal{M}
$$
$$
y_m \;\leq\; z_{e^e_m,\, L^e_m} \qquad \forall m \in \mathcal{M}
$$

**(B2) Track capacity** — at most one event uses a given track within each time period:
$$
\sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}:\ \text{station}(e)=s,\ \text{time}(e) \in \mathcal{T}_p} z_{e,\ell} \;\leq\; 1 \qquad \forall s \in \mathcal{S},\; \ell \in \mathcal{L}_s,\; p \in \mathcal{P}
$$

**(B3) Time feasibility with delays** — a shunting movement must fit between the preceding arrival and the succeeding departure:
$$
\pi^{a}_{i,s} + \delta_{e^{a}_{i,s}} + \sigma_m \;\leq\; \pi^{d}_{i',s} + \delta_{e^{d}_{i',s}} + M(1-y_m) \qquad \forall m \in \mathcal{M}(i,i',s)
$$

**(B4) Delay bounds** — short delays only, absorbed by timetable buffers:
$$
\delta_e \;\leq\; \Delta^{\max} \qquad \forall e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

**(B5) Delay propagation** along a trip (departure delay ≥ arrival delay):
$$
\delta_{e^{d}_{i,s}} \;\geq\; \delta_{e^{a}_{i,s}} \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

### (C) Domain Constraints

$$
x_{i,r},\ y_m,\ z_{e,\ell} \in \{0,1\}, \qquad
\delta_e,\ u_i,\ \alpha^+_{i,r},\ \alpha^-_{i,r} \geq 0
$$

---

## 7. Key Assumptions

1. **Time discretisation** — time is partitioned into periods of length equal to the minimum shunting duration; this enables the track-capacity constraints (B2). *(Assumption)*
2. **Deterministic demand** — passenger demand $q_i$ is known and fixed. *(Assumption)*
3. **Fixed shunting durations** — each shunting movement $m$ has a known duration $\sigma_m$. *(Assumption)*
4. **Short delays are tolerable** — delays up to $\Delta^{\max}$ minutes are absorbed by timetable buffers on the affected lines. *(From the source paper)*
5. **Track-level infrastructure** — only the stations where shunting is considered (e.g., Utrecht Centraal, Rotterdam Centraal) are modelled at the track level; the rest of the network is aggregated. *(From the source paper)*
6. **Rolling stock compatibility** — each unit $r$ has a fixed set of compatible trip types $F_{i,r}$. *(Assumption)*
7. **Single planning horizon** — the model considers one operational day; overnight positioning is captured indirectly through the stick-to-the-plan objective. *(Assumption)*
8. **Independent shunting movements** — shunting movements are evaluated independently in the infrastructure model; the iterative heuristic processes them sequentially. *(From the source paper)*

---

## 8. Notes on the Solution Approach

The integrated MILP above can be solved directly for small instances, but the source paper proposes two tailored approaches:

- **Exact (Combinatorial Benders') algorithm**: Treats (A1)–(A5) as the master problem and (B1)–(B5) as the subproblem. When the subproblem is infeasible for a given combination of shunting movements, a combinatorial cut is added to the master problem that forbids that combination. Iteration continues until a feasible, optimal solution is found.

- **Iterative heuristic**: Resembles the exact algorithm but feeds shunting movements to the infrastructure model **one by one**, mimicking the real-world separation between rolling stock dispatchers (railway operator) and infrastructure dispatchers (infrastructure manager). The paper reports that this heuristic finds optimal solutions for all tested instances in shorter running times.

Both approaches are generic with respect to the underlying formulations; alternative composition or infrastructure models can be substituted as long as they solve the same two subproblems.

# MILP for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance‑to‑Go (DTG) Signalling

Below is a complete mixed‑integer linear programming model in the spirit of RECIFE‑MILP (Pellegrini et al., 2015), enhanced for ETCS Level 2 with trackside train detection (DTG signalling). The two key enhancements are (i) **speed‑profile options per train** and (ii) **train‑ and speed‑dependent blocking times** (brake indication points may lie anywhere on the track).

---

## 1. Assumptions (marked where not given in the input)

- **A1** (assumed): The network is given as a set of *resources* (TDS sections, station tracks, switch areas). Each resource may be occupied by at most one train at a time.
- **A2** (assumed): For each train, a set of feasible routes through the network and a set of feasible speed profiles (e.g., nominal, time‑saving, energy‑saving) are pre‑computed offline. Each (train, route, profile) combination induces a deterministic running time and a set of **blocking times** per resource, where the approach (braking) part of the blocking time depends on the train's braking distance at its entry speed — hence it is train‑ and profile‑dependent.
- **A3** (assumed): Delays of trains at entry to the study area are known (deterministic, as in real‑time rescheduling).
- **A4** (assumed): Dwell times have minimum values; reordering is allowed only at passing/holding locations; local rerouting is captured by the route choice variables.
- **A5**: The MA end lies at the end of a TDS; the brake indication point lies anywhere upstream, captured inside the blocking time.
- **A6** (assumed): A finite scheduling horizon [0, H] is used.

---

## 2. Sets and parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains |
| $R$ | set of track resources (TDSs, switch areas, platform tracks) |
| $\mathcal{R}_t$ | set of feasible routes for train $t$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_{t,r}$ | set of feasible speed profiles for train $t$ on route $r$ |
| $E_t$ | ordered set of resources traversed by train $t$ (union over its routes) |
| $h^{min}_{t,i}$ | minimum running/dwell time of train $t$ on resource $i$ (profile‑dependent: $h^{min}_{t,i,p}$) |
| $b_{t,i,r,p}$ | **blocking time** of resource $i$ for train $t$ on route $r$ with profile $p$ (includes speed‑dependent approach/braking time before the TDS entry) |
| $a_t$ | scheduled (unperturbed) entry time of train $t$ into the area |
| $d_t$ | known initial delay of train $t$ |
| $H$ | horizon length |
| $M$ | big‑M, e.g., $M = H + \max_t d_t$ |
| $S$ | set of ordered pairs of trains that may conflict on at least one common resource |
| $C_{ij}$ | set of resources common to trains $i$ and $j$ |
| $w_t$ | delay weight of train $t$ (e.g., priority) |

---

## 3. Decision variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $y_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ uses route $r \in \mathcal{R}_t$ |
| $x_{t,r,p} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ uses route $r$ and profile $p$ |
| $e_{t,i} \ge 0$ | continuous | **entry time** of train $t$ on resource $i$ (start of blocking time) |
| $l_{t,i} \ge 0$ | continuous | **exit time** of train $t$ from resource $i$ (end of blocking time) |
| $\delta_t \ge 0$ | continuous | total (arrival) delay of train $t$ |
| $z_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | sequencing variable: 1 if train $i$ traverses common resources **before** train $j$, 0 if after |

---

## 4. Objective function

Minimise weighted total delay:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{t \in T} w_t \, \delta_t
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Route and profile selection — exactly one combination per train:**

$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_t} y_{t,r} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T \tag{1}
$$

$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_{t,r}} x_{t,r,p} = y_{t,r} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; \forall r \in \mathcal{R}_t \tag{2}
$$

**(C2) Entry times at the area boundary (retiming):**

$$
e_{t,i_1(t)} = a_t + d_t + \Delta_t \qquad \forall t \in T,\; i_1(t) = \text{first resource of } t \tag{3}
$$

with free retiming variable $\Delta_t \geq -d_t$ (a train cannot be advanced beyond its physical earliest arrival; equivalently $e_{t,i_1(t)} \ge a_t$).

**(C3) Blocking times — train‑ and speed‑dependent duration (DTG enhancement):**

$$
l_{t,i} - e_{t,i} \ge \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_t}\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_{t,r}} b_{t,i,r,p}\, x_{t,r,p} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; \forall i \in E_t \tag{4}
$$

The blocking time $b_{t,i,r,p}$ includes the speed‑dependent braking/approach time before the TDS entry (brake indication point upstream of the EoA), so DTG separation is captured linearly through profile selection.

**(C4) Running times along the route (consistency of consecutive resources):**

$$
e_{t,i_{k+1}} \ge l_{t,i_k} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; \forall \text{ consecutive } (i_k, i_{k+1}) \in E_t \tag{5}
$$

$$
l_{t,i} \ge e_{t,i} + \sum_{r,p} h^{min}_{t,i,r,p}\, x_{t,r,p} \qquad \forall t,\; \forall i \text{ with minimum dwell/running time} \tag{6}
$$

**(C5) Resource capacity — no overlapping blocking times (conflict resolution):**

For every pair $(i,j) \in S$ and every common resource $c \in C_{ij}$:

$$
l_{i,c} \le e_{j,c} + M(1 - z_{ij}) \qquad \forall (i,j) \in S,\; \forall c \in C_{ij} \tag{7}
$$

$$
l_{j,c} \le e_{i,c} + M z_{ij} \qquad \forall (i,j) \in S,\; \forall c \in C_{ij} \tag{8}
$$

If $z_{ij}=1$, train $i$ must fully vacate $c$ before $j$ enters, and vice versa. **Consistency of ordering across all common resources** (reordering only allowed where physically possible; for pairs where reordering is forbidden, fix $z_{ij}$):

$$
z_{ij} = z_{ij'} \quad \text{for pre‑specified groups of resources that must keep a common order} \tag{9}
$$

**(C6) Delay definition (against scheduled exit/arrival):**

$$
\delta_t \ge l_{t,i^{end}_t} - A_t \qquad \forall t \in T \tag{10}
$$

where $i^{end}_t$ is the last resource of train $t$ and $A_t$ its scheduled arrival time. With $w_t \ge 0$ and minimisation, (10) is tight at optimum.

**(C7) Horizon constraints:**

$$
e_{t,i},\; l_{t,i} \le H \qquad \forall t,\; \forall i \in E_t \tag{11}
$$

**(C8) Variable domains:**

$$
y_{t,r} \in \{0,1\},\; x_{t,r,p} \in \{0,1\},\; z_{ij} \in \{0,1\},\; e_{t,i}, l_{t,i}, \delta_t \ge 0 \tag{12}
$$

---

## 6. Remarks

- **DTG modelling:** The speed‑dependent separation of DTG signalling is entirely embedded in the parameters $b_{t,i,r,p}$ (constraint 4): for a faster profile the braking distance — and hence the approach blocking time before the first occupied TDS — is longer. This replaces the fixed‑block discretisation logic of the original RECIFE‑MILP.
- **Rescheduling measures:** retiming = continuous $e_{t,i}$; reordering = binaries $z_{ij}$; local rerouting = binaries $y_{t,r}$; speed adjustment = binaries $x_{t,r,p}$.
- **Linearity:** All constraints are linear; products of variables are avoided by pre‑computing $b_{t,i,r,p}$ per (route, profile) combination and selecting it via $x_{t,r,p}$.
- The model is a big‑M MILP, solvable by standard branch‑and‑bound; the big‑M constants can be tightened per constraint pair using earliest/latest feasible times to improve tractability.

Text:
# Complete MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

After generating and comparing multiple formulations, the following integrated MILP best captures the joint TRP + TSMP under bidirectional partial blockages.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T=\{1,\dots,N_T\}$ | Set of trains |
| $S=\{1,\dots,N_S\}$ | Set of stations, ordered along the line |
| $B=\{1,\dots,N_B\}$ | Set of blocks; block $b$ connects station $b$ to $b+1$ ($|B|=|S|-1$) |
| $K=\{1,\dots,N_K\}$ | Discrete time intervals of length $\Delta$ (s) |
| $I=\{1,2\}$ | Track sides (1 = original, 2 = opposite/rerouted) |
| $D\subseteq B\times K \times I$ | Disruption set: $(b,k,i)\in D$ means side $i$ of block $b$ is unavailable during interval $k$ |
| $T_{bh}\subseteq T\times T$ | Ordered pairs $t_1\neq t_2$ sharing headway constraints |
| $T_{opp}\subseteq T\times T$ | Pairs of trains traveling in opposite directions |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning (units) |
|---|---|
| $\mathrm{sch}_a[t,s],\ \mathrm{sch}_d[t,s]$ | Scheduled arrival/departure of train $t$ at station $s$ (s) |
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ (m) |
| $L_t$ | Length of train $t$ (m) |
| $v_{\min},\ v_{\max}$ | Min/max allowable speed (m/s) |
| $a_{\max},\ b_{\max}$ | Max acceleration / max braking magnitude (m/s²) |
| $\tau_d^{\min},\tau_d^{\max}$ | Min/max dwell time at stations (s) |
| $\tau_h$ | Minimum headway time (s) |
| $\tau_r[t,b]$ | Minimum running time of $t$ on block $b$ (s) |
| $\Delta$ | Duration of time interval $k$ (s) |
| $\mathrm{dir}[t]\in\{+1,-1\}$ | Direction of train $t$ |
| $E_0,E_1,E_2$ | Energy coefficients (kWh) |
| $P_c$ | Cancellation penalty (s-eq) |
| $W_{\mathrm{dly}},\ W_{\mathrm{eng}},\ W_{\mathrm{cxl}}$ | Objective weights |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Rescheduling (TRP):**
- $\mathrm{cxl}[t]\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ is cancelled
- $x[t,s]\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ stops at station $s$
- $a[t,s]\ge 0$: actual arrival time of $t$ at $s$
- $d[t,s]\ge 0$: actual departure time of $t$ at $s$
- $r[t,b,i]\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if $t$ traverses block $b$ on side $i$
- $y^{blk}[t_1,t_2,b]\in\{0,1\}$: ordering — 1 if $t_1$ traverses $b$ entirely before $t_2$
- $y^{stn}[t_1,t_2,s]\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if $t_1$ uses station $s$ before $t_2$
- $z[t,b,k]\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if $t$ occupies block $b$ during interval $k$

**Speed Management (TSMP):**
- $v[t,b,k]\in[0,v_{\max}]$: speed of $t$ on $b$ in interval $k$ (m/s)
- $p[t,b,k]\ge 0$: position of $t$ at start of $k$ on $b$ (m from block entry)
- $\mathrm{acc}^+[t,b,k]\ge 0,\ \mathrm{acc}^-[t,b,k]\ge 0$: non-negative parts of acceleration/braking
- $e[t,b,k]\ge 0$: energy consumed in interval $k$ on block $b$ (kWh)

Auxiliary: $\mathrm{acc}[t,b,k]=\mathrm{acc}^+[t,b,k]-\mathrm{acc}^-[t,b,k]$, so $b_{\max}\le\mathrm{acc}\le a_{\max}$.

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\ Z \;=\; W_{\mathrm{dly}}\sum_{t,s} a^+[t,s] \;+\; W_{\mathrm{dly}}\sum_{t,s} d^+[t,s] \;+\; W_{\mathrm{eng}}\sum_{t,b,k} e[t,b,k] \;+\; W_{\mathrm{cxl}}\sum_t P_c\,\mathrm{cxl}[t]
$$

Linearization of $(\cdot)_+$: $a^+[t,s]\ge a[t,s]-\mathrm{sch}_a[t,s]$, $a^+[t,s]\ge 0$ (analogously for $d^+$).

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Cancellation / Service Decisions

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{cxl}[t] &\le 1-r[t,b,i] \quad\forall t,b,i \tag{C1a}\\
\mathrm{cxl}[t] &\le 1-x[t,s] \quad\forall t,s \tag{C1b}\\
a[t,s] &\ge \mathrm{sch}_a[t,s]-M\,\mathrm{cxl}[t] \tag{C1c}\\
a[t,s] &\le \mathrm{sch}_a[t,s]+M\,(1-\mathrm{cxl}[t]) \tag{C1d}\\
d[t,s] &\ge \mathrm{sch}_d[t,s]-M\,\mathrm{cxl}[t] \tag{C1e}\\
d[t,s] &\le \mathrm{sch}_d[t,s]+M\,(1-\mathrm{cxl}[t]) \tag{C1f}
\end{aligned}
$$

### 5.2 Rerouting Logic

$$
\sum_{i\in I} r[t,b,i]\le 1 \quad\forall t,b \tag{C2a},\qquad r[t,b,i]\le 1-\mathrm{cxl}[t] \quad\forall t,b,i \tag{C2b}
$$

### 5.3 Trajectory Consistency

$$
a[t,s+1]\ge d[t,s]+\sum_{k\in K}\Delta\,z[t,s,k] \quad\forall t,\,s\in\{1,\dots,N_S-1\} \tag{C3a}
$$
$$
\sum_{k\in K}\Delta\,z[t,b,k]\ge \tau_r[t,b]\sum_{i\in I}r[t,b,i] \quad\forall t,b \tag{C3b}
$$
$$
z[t,b,k]\le \sum_{i\in I}r[t,b,i] \quad\forall t,b,k \tag{C3c}
$$

### 5.4 Speed / Position Dynamics **[LIN]**

$$
\mathrm{acc}[t,b,k]=\mathrm{acc}^+[t,b,k]-\mathrm{acc}^-[t,b,k] \quad\forall t,b,k \tag{C4a}
$$
$$
\mathrm{acc}^+[t,b,k]\le a_{\max}\,z[t,b,k],\quad \mathrm{acc}^-[t,b,k]\le |b_{\max}|\,z[t,b,k] \tag{C4b,C4c}
$$
$$
v[t,b,k+1]=v[t,b,k]+\Delta(\mathrm{acc}^+[t,b,k]-\mathrm{acc}^-[t,b,k]) \tag{C4d}
$$
$$
v_{\min}\,z[t,b,k]\le v[t,b,k]\le v_{\max}\,z[t,b,k] \tag{C4e}
$$
$$
p[t,b,k+1]=p[t,b,k]+\Delta\,v[t,b,k]+\tfrac{\Delta^2}{2}(\mathrm{acc}^+[t,b,k]-\mathrm{acc}^-[t,b,k]) \tag{C4f}
$$
$$
p[t,b,1]\le \varepsilon+M(1-z[t,b,1]) \tag{C4g}
$$
$$
p[t,b,N_K]\ge L_b-M(1-z[t,b,N_K]) \tag{C4h}
$$
$$
\sum_{k\in K}\Delta\,v[t,b,k]\ge L_b\sum_{i\in I}r[t,b,i] \tag{C4i}
$$
$$
p[t,b,k]\le L_b+M(1-z[t,b,k]),\quad p[t,b,k]\le M\,z[t,b,k] \tag{C4j,C4k}
$$

### 5.5 Energy Consumption **[LIN — piecewise-linear envelope]**

$$
e[t,b,k]\ge E_0\Delta\,z[t,b,k]+E_1\Delta\,v[t,b,k]+E_2\Delta(\mathrm{acc}^+[t,b,k]+\mathrm{acc}^-[t,b,k]) \tag{C5a}
$$

Tightened via SOS2/PWL convex envelope of $v^2$ over breakpoints $\bar v_m$:

$$
e[t,b,k]\ge \sum_m \lambda_m[t,b,k]\,\beta_m\Delta,\quad v[t,b,k]=\sum_m \bar v_m\lambda_m[t,b,k],\quad \sum_m\lambda_m[t,b,k]=z[t,b,k] \tag{C5b}
$$

with $\lambda_m$ forming a SOS2 set (relax to $\lambda_m\ge 0$ with SOS2 indicator for efficiency).

### 5.6 Station Dwell

$$
d[t,s]-a[t,s]\ge \tau_d^{\min}\,x[t,s],\qquad d[t,s]-a[t,s]\le \tau_d^{\max}\,x[t,s] \tag{C6a,C6b}
$$
$$
d[t,s]=a[t,s]+M(1-x[t,s]) \tag{C6c}
$$

### 5.7 Station Headway

$$
a[t_1,s]\ge d[t_2,s]+\tau_h-M(1-y^{stn}[t_1,t_2,s]) \tag{C7a}
$$
$$
d[t_1,s]\ge d[t_2,s]+\tau_h-M(1-y^{stn}[t_1,t_2,s]) \tag{C7b}
$$
$$
y^{stn}[t_1,t_2,s]+y^{stn}[t_2,t_1,s]=x[t_1,s]\,x[t_2,s] \tag{C7c}
$$

### 5.8 Block Headway — Same Side, Same Direction

$$
a[t_1,s_{b+1}]\ge d[t_2,s_b]+\tau_h-M(1-y^{blk}[t_1,t_2,b]) \tag{C8a}
$$
$$
z[t_1,b,k]+z[t_2,b,k]\le 1+\sum_i M(1-r[t_1,b,i]\,r[t_2,b,i]) \tag{C8b}
$$

(product $r_1r_2$ linearized with auxiliary $w$: $w\le r_1$, $w\le r_2$, $w\ge r_1+r_2-1$, $w\in\{0,1\}$)
$$
y^{blk}[t_1,t_2,b]+y^{blk}[t_2,t_1,b]=1 \quad\forall (t_1,t_2)\in T_{bh},b \tag{C8c}
$$

### 5.9 Disruption Window (Blocked Side Unavailable)

$$
z[t,b,k]\le 1-r[t,b,i] \quad\forall t,\,(b,k,i)\in D \tag{C9a}
$$
$$
r[t,b,i]\le 1-\sum_{k\in K_b^D} z[t,b,k] \quad\forall t,\,b,\,i:(b,\cdot,i)\in D \tag{C9b}
$$

where $K_b^D=\{k:(b,k,i)\in D\}$.

### 5.10 Bidirectional Conflict on a Shared (Rerouted) Side

For $(t_1,t_2)\in T_{opp}$ both using the same side of block $b$:

$$
a[t_1,b+1]\ge d[t_2,b]+\tau_h-M(1-y^{blk}[t_1,t_2,b]) \tag{C10a}
$$
$$
a[t_2,b+1]\ge d[t_1,b]+\tau_h-M(1-y^{blk}[t_2,t_1,b]) \tag{C10b}
$$
$$
y^{blk}[t_1,t_2,b]+y^{blk}[t_2,t_1,b]=\sum_i r[t_1,b,i]\,r[t_2,b,i] \tag{C10c}
$$

(positive-part / product linearized as above)

Conservative position-based safety against mid-block meeting **[LIN — sufficient buffer $\tau_h v_{\max}$]:**
$$
p[t_1,b,k]+L_{t_1}+\tau_h v_{\max}\le p[t_2,b,k]+M(1-y^{blk}[t_1,t_2,b]) \quad\forall (t_1,t_2)\in T_{opp},k \tag{C10d}
$$

### 5.11 Initial / Terminal Conditions

$$
d[t,1]\ge T_0^{\min}[t]-M\,\mathrm{cxl}[t],\quad d[t,1]\le T_0^{\max}[t]+M(1-\mathrm{cxl}[t]) \tag{C11a}
$$
$$
a[t,N_S]\le T_f^{\max}[t]+M\,\mathrm{cxl}[t],\quad a[t,N_S]\ge T_f^{\min}[t]-M(1-\mathrm{cxl}[t]) \tag{C11b}
$$

### 5.12 Variable Domains & Big-M Aggregates

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&\le a[t,s],\,d[t,s]\le T^{\max};\quad 0\le v[t,b,k]\le v_{\max};\\
0&\le p[t,b,k]\le L_b+M;\quad 0\le \mathrm{acc}^{\pm}\le \max(a_{\max},|b_{\max}|);\\
e[t,b,k]&\ge 0;\quad \mathrm{cxl}[t],\,x[t,s],\,r[t,b,i],\,z[t,b,k],\,y^{\cdot}\in\{0,1\}.
\end{aligned}
$$

## 6. Summary of Linearizations

| Term | Source of nonlinearity | Linearization | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| $\tfrac{\Delta^2}{2}\mathrm{acc}^2$ | Quadratic in acc | Decompose into $\mathrm{acc}^+,\mathrm{acc}^-$ | (C4a–f) |
| $v^2$ in mechanical power | Quadratic in $v$ | PWL convex envelope via SOS2 | (C5a–b) |
| $\|\mathrm{acc}\|$ in energy | Absolute value | Replace by $\mathrm{acc}^++\mathrm{acc}^-$ | (C5a) |
| $(a-\mathrm{sch}_a)_+$ | Positive part | $a^+$ auxiliary variables | Objective |
| $r_1 r_2$ | Product of binaries | Auxiliary $w\in\{0,1\}$ with three McCormick ineq. | (C8b), (C10c) |
| $0<p<L_b\!\Leftrightarrow\!z=1$ | Logical | Big-M linear envelope | (C4j–k) |
| Mid-block meeting of opposing trains | Position-dependent | Conservative buffer $\tau_h v_{\max}$ | (C10d) |

## 7. Integrated Block Diagram

```
[Decisions]  cancel[t] ─┐
            r[t,b,i]   │   [Physics (LIN)]   v,acc,p dynamics  ──►  e[t,b,k]
            x[t,s]     ├──►                                            │
            z[t,b,k]   │                                                ▼
            y-stn,blk  │                       [Feasibility]   ◄──  Objective
                        └──►  a[t,s], d[t,s], energy
                                  ▲                │
                                  │                ▼
                          [Headway & Order]   [Disruption D]
```

## 8. Assumptions Made (marked)

1. **Piecewise-constant acceleration** within each interval $\Delta$ — standard macroscopic assumption enabling linear motion update.
2. **Quadratic speed-resistance** in energy is linearized via PWL envelope (SOS2).
3. **Disruption window** $D$ is known in advance (exogenously given by the operator) and affects exactly one track side of block(s).
4. **Bidirectional trains on different sides** of a double-track corridor never conflict geometrically; only rerouted-to-same-side opposing pairs require temporal separation.
5. **Headway $\tau_h$** is the same for stations and blocks (can be differentiated if data available).
6. **Initial and terminal times** are bounded by intervals $[T^{\min},T^{\max}]$, optionally fixed.
7. **Train lengths** enter only via the conservative opposing-direction buffer (C10d); same-direction block headway is enforced through $z$ and $y^{blk}$.
8. **Cancellations** are allowed only with a penalty $P_c$ and force the train to revert to scheduled times (i.e., it does not run).
9. **Big-M** is set to the length of the planning horizon (standard practice).
10. **Position-time compatibility** between speed profile and block occupancy is enforced via (C4f–k), aligning kinematics with the rescheduled timetable — the central innovation of the integrated model.

This MILP simultaneously yields a **conflict-free rescheduled timetable** and **executable energy-aware speed profiles**, integrating TRP and TSMP within a single optimization framework for bidirectional high-speed lines under partial segment blockages.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

After evaluating the generated candidates, **Model 2** is selected as the best formulation. It is the most rigorous, with explicit block-occupancy variables, proper bidirectional conflict handling via same-track indicators, and tight coupling between the macroscopic timetable and the microscopic speed profile. Below is the refined and complete model.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T = \{1,\dots,N_T\}$ | Set of trains |
| $S = \{1,\dots,N_S\}$ | Set of stations ordered along the line |
| $B = \{1,\dots,N_B\}$ | Set of block sections, $b = (s, s+1)$ |
| $K = \{0,1,\dots,N_K\}$ | Discrete time steps (horizon), step size $\Delta t$ |
| $D \subseteq B$ | Set of disrupted block sections |
| $W = [t_d^{\text{start}}, t_d^{\text{end}}]$ | Disruption time window |
| $\text{dir}(t) \in \{+1,-1\}$ | Nominal direction of train $t$ (+1 = up, −1 = down) |
| $V = \{1,\dots,N_V\}$ | Set of piecewise-linear breakpoints for the energy model |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $\Delta t$ | Time step duration | 30 s |
| $v_{\min}, v_{\max}$ | Min/max operating speed | m/s |
| $a_{\min}, a_{\max}$ | Min/max acceleration (negative = braking) | m/s² |
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ | m |
| $L_t$ | Length of train $t$ | m |
| $\text{pos}_s$ | Chainage (position) of station $s$ | m |
| $\text{start}_b, \text{end}_b$ | Chainage bounds of block $b$ | m |
| $\tau_{t,s}^{\text{sch}}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ | s |
| $\tau_{\min}^{\text{dwell}}$ | Minimum dwell time at stations | s |
| $h$ | Minimum headway time between consecutive trains | s |
| $\alpha, \beta$ | Weights on delay and energy in objective | – |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (Big-M) | – |
| $\{v_i, e_i\}_{i=1}^{N_V}$ | Piecewise-linear breakpoints (speed, energy rate) | – |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Timetable variables**
- $a_{t,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$: arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $d_{t,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$: departure time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $\delta_{t,s} \geq 0$: delay of train $t$ at station $s$ relative to schedule

**Routing variables**
- $y_{t,b} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ traverses block $b$
- $r_{t,b} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ is rerouted (uses opposite track) on block $b$
- $x_{t,t',b} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ precedes train $t'$ on block $b$
- $z_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ occupies block $b$ at time step $k$
- $\eta_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ exits block $b$ at time step $k$
- $u_{t,t',b} \in \{0,1\}$: product linearization of $r_{t,b} \cdot r_{t',b}$

**Speed / position / energy variables**
- $v_{t,k} \in [v_{\min}, v_{\max}]$: speed of train $t$ at time step $k$
- $p_{t,k} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$: position of train $t$ at time step $k$
- $e_{t,k} \geq 0$: energy consumption rate of train $t$ at time step $k$
- $\lambda_{t,k,i} \geq 0$: convex-combination weights for piecewise-linear energy model

**Coupling variables**
- $\alpha_{t,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if time step $k$ corresponds to arrival of $t$ at $s$
- $\gamma_{t,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if time step $k$ corresponds to departure of $t$ at $s$

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \alpha \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{s \in S} \delta_{t,s} \;+\; \beta \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{k \in K} e_{t,k}\,\Delta t
$$

The first term penalizes total passenger delay (service quality); the second term penalizes total energy consumption over the planning horizon. The weights $\alpha, \beta$ allow the operator to balance punctuality against energy efficiency.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Dynamics (Discretized Motion)

$$
p_{t,k+1} = p_{t,k} + v_{t,k}\,\Delta t \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; k \in K \setminus \{N_K\}
$$

### 5.2 Speed and Acceleration Limits

$$
v_{\min} \leq v_{t,k} \leq v_{\max} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; k \in K
$$

$$
a_{\min}\,\Delta t \leq v_{t,k+1} - v_{t,k} \leq a_{\max}\,\Delta t \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; k \in K \setminus \{N_K\}
$$

### 5.3 Energy Model (Piecewise-Linear Approximation)

Tractive effort is nonlinear in speed; we approximate it with a piecewise-linear envelope using breakpoints $(v_i, e_i)$:

$$
v_{t,k} = \sum_{i=1}^{N_V} v_i\,\lambda_{t,k,i} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; k \in K
$$

$$
e_{t,k} = \sum_{i=1}^{N_V} e_i\,\lambda_{t,k,i} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; k \in K
$$

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{N_V} \lambda_{t,k,i} = 1, \quad \lambda_{t,k,i} \geq 0 \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; k \in K,\; i \in V
$$

with $\{\lambda_{t,k,i}\}_i$ declared as **SOS2** to enforce adjacency (preserving piecewise linearity as a MILP rather than MINLP).

### 5.4 Rerouting Constraint (Disruption Forcing)

If block $b \in D$ is disrupted during window $W$, any train occupying it must be rerouted to the opposite track:

$$
r_{t,b} \geq z_{t,b,k} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in D,\; k \in K:\; k\Delta t \in W
$$

Rerouting is only allowed on disrupted blocks:

$$
r_{t,b} \leq \mathbf{1}[b \in D] \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B
$$

A train can only be rerouted if it traverses the block:

$$
r_{t,b} \leq y_{t,b} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B
$$

### 5.5 Block Occupancy (Linearization of Position–Block Relation)

$$
p_{t,k} \geq \text{start}_b - M(1 - z_{t,b,k}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

$$
p_{t,k} \leq \text{end}_b + M(1 - z_{t,b,k}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

$$
z_{t,b,k} \leq y_{t,b} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

### 5.6 Bidirectional Conflict Avoidance on Shared Track

Two opposite-direction trains conflict only if they share the **same physical track**. Define $\text{same}_{t,t',b} = 1$ iff both are rerouted or both are not rerouted on block $b$:

$$
u_{t,t',b} \leq r_{t,b}, \quad u_{t,t',b} \leq r_{t',b}, \quad u_{t,t',b} \geq r_{t,b} + r_{t',b} - 1
$$

$$
\text{same}_{t,t',b} = 1 - r_{t,b} - r_{t',b} + 2\,u_{t,t',b}
$$

For all pairs with $\text{dir}(t) \neq \text{dir}(t')$:

$$
z_{t,b,k} + z_{t',b,k} \leq 1 + M\bigl(1 - \text{same}_{t,t',b}\bigr) \qquad \forall\, b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

(If the trains are on different tracks, the RHS becomes $1+M$ and the constraint is relaxed.)

### 5.7 Headway and Ordering

For all train pairs traversing the same block:

$$
x_{t,t',b} + x_{t',t,b} = 1 \qquad \forall\, t < t' \in T,\; b \in B
$$

Define exit time via auxiliary binaries $\eta_{t,b,k}$ (1 if train $t$ exits block $b$ at step $k$):

$$
\sum_{k \in K} \eta_{t,b,k} = y_{t,b} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B
$$

$$
p_{t,k} \geq \text{end}_b - M(1-\eta_{t,b,k}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

$$
p_{t,k-1} \leq \text{end}_b + M(1-\eta_{t,b,k}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K \setminus \{0\}
$$

Then the headway constraint:

$$
\sum_{k \in K} k\,\eta_{t',b,k} - \sum_{k \in K} k\,\eta_{t,b,k} \geq h - M(1 - x_{t,t',b}) \qquad \forall\, t < t' \in T,\; b \in B
$$

### 5.8 Station Dwell Time

$$
d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \geq \tau_{\min}^{\text{dwell}} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{N_S\}
$$

### 5.9 Running Time Linked to Speed Profile (TRP–TSMP Coupling)

The running time between consecutive stations equals the number of time steps the train spends on the connecting block, which is determined by the speed profile:

$$
a_{t,s+1} - d_{t,s} = \sum_{k \in K} z_{t,b(s,s+1),k}\,\Delta t \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{N_S\}
$$

### 5.10 Position–Time Coupling at Stations

Each arrival/departure is assigned to exactly one time step:

$$
\sum_{k \in K} \alpha_{t,s,k} = 1, \quad \sum_{k \in K} \gamma_{t,s,k} = 1 \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

$$
a_{t,s} = \sum_{k \in K} k\,\Delta t\,\alpha_{t,s,k}, \quad d_{t,s} = \sum_{k \in K} k\,\Delta t\,\gamma_{t,s,k} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

$$
p_{t,k} \geq \text{pos}_s - M(1-\alpha_{t,s,k}), \quad p_{t,k} \leq \text{pos}_s + M(1-\alpha_{t,s,k}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S,\; k \in K
$$

Departure must occur at or after arrival:

$$
\gamma_{t,s,k} \leq \alpha_{t,s,k} + \alpha_{t,s,k+1} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S,\; k \in K \setminus \{N_K\}
$$

### 5.11 Delay Definition

$$
\delta_{t,s} \geq a_{t,s} - \tau_{t,s}^{\text{sch}}, \quad \delta_{t,s} \geq 0 \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### 5.12 Terminal Conditions

$$
p_{t,0} = \text{pos}_{s_t^{\text{orig}}}, \quad p_{t,N_K} = \text{pos}_{s_t^{\text{dest}}} \qquad \forall\, t \in T
$$

$$
v_{t,0} = v_t^{\text{init}}, \quad v_{t,N_K} = 0 \qquad \forall\, t \in T
$$

---

## 6. Complete MILP Summary

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & \alpha \sum_{t,s} \delta_{t,s} + \beta \sum_{t,k} e_{t,k}\,\Delta t \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(5.1) Train dynamics} \\
& \text{(5.2) Speed and acceleration limits} \\
& \text{(5.3) Piecewise-linear energy model (SOS2)} \\
& \text{(5.4) Rerouting under disruption} \\
& \text{(5.5) Block occupancy linearization} \\
& \text{(5.6) Bidirectional conflict avoidance on shared track} \\
& \text{(5.7) Headway and ordering constraints} \\
& \text{(5.8) Station dwell time} \\
& \text{(5.9) Running time coupling (TRP–TSMP link)} \\
& \text{(5.10) Position–time coupling at stations} \\
& \text{(5.11) Delay definition} \\
& \text{(5.12) Terminal conditions} \\
& \text{all variables in declared domains}
\end{aligned}
$$

---

## 7. Key Modeling Choices and Assumptions

**Integration of TRP and TSMP.** The model couples the two subproblems through the position–time variables $p_{t,k}$, the block-occupancy indicators $z_{t,b,k}$, and the running-time constraints (5.9). The timetable variables $(a_{t,s}, d_{t,s})$ determine *when* trains move, while the speed variables $(v_{t,k}, e_{t,k})$ determine *how* they move and at what energy cost. Both are optimized simultaneously, avoiding suboptimal sequential decisions.

**Linearization strategy.** The energy model is nonlinear in speed. By introducing piecewise-linear breakpoints with SOS2 convex-combination variables $\lambda_{t,k,i}$, the model remains a MILP while capturing realistic tractive-effort behavior. Binary products (e.g., $r_{t,b} \cdot r_{t',b}$) are linearized via auxiliary variables $u_{t,t',b}$.

**Bidirectional conflict handling.** Constraint (5.6) combines binary routing variables with block-occupancy indicators and a same-track indicator. When a disruption forces rerouting, opposite-direction trains must be temporally separated on the shared block — enforced by the headway constraints (5.7) applied conditionally on the ordering variables $x_{t,t',b}$.

**Disruption modeling.** The disruption is treated as a hard constraint forcing rerouting on $D$ during $W$, with constraint (5.4) ensuring that any train whose trajectory intersects the disrupted block–time region must be rerouted. This captures the operational reality that the blocked track is unavailable for the affected direction.

**Assumptions made (marked as such):**
1. The line is a double-track high-speed line with bidirectional traffic; one track per nominal direction.
2. A single disruption event affecting one direction on a contiguous set of blocks.
3. Trains have identical performance characteristics (same $v_{\min}, v_{\max}, a_{\min}, a_{\max}$); heterogeneous parameters can be indexed by $t$.
4. Time discretization $\Delta t = 30$ s is sufficient to capture speed-profile dynamics.
5. Dwell times are fixed at the minimum; variable dwell times can be added by introducing $d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \geq \tau_{\min}^{\text{dwell}}$ as a lower bound only.
6. No train cancellation is modeled (all trains must complete their journey); cancellation can be added via a binary $c_t$ with appropriate modifications to terminal conditions.
7. Energy model uses a quadratic-in-speed tractive-effort approximation linearized via SOS2.

**Scalability considerations.** The number of binary variables grows as $O(|T|^2 |B|)$ for ordering and $O(|T||B||K|)$ for block occupancy. For large instances, Benders decomposition, rolling-horizon approaches, or the interval-plan decomposition described in the paper can be applied — with the master problem handling routing/ordering and subproblems handling individual train speed profiles.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockage

Based on the problem description, I now present the complete mathematical formulation of the integrated MILP model.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t \in T$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations along the line, indexed by $s \in S$ |
| $B$ | Set of track blocks (segments), indexed by $b \in B$ |
| $K$ | Set of discrete time steps, indexed by $k \in K$, $K = \{1, 2, \dots, K_{\max}\}$ |
| $\text{Dir}$ | Set of travel directions, $\text{Dir} = \{U, D\}$ (Up, Down) |
| $B(s, s+1)$ | Set of blocks between consecutive stations $s$ and $s+1$ |
| $B^{\text{disr}}$ | Set of blocks affected by the disruption |
| $K^{\text{disr}}$ | Set of time steps within the disruption window |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ | m |
| $v^{\max}, v^{\min}$ | Maximum / minimum allowable speed | m/s |
| $a^{\text{acc}}, a^{\text{dec}}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration | m/s² |
| $\tau^{\min}, \tau^{\max}$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time at stations | s |
| $\Delta t$ | Duration of one time step | s |
| $h$ | Minimum headway time between consecutive trains | s |
| $t^{\text{disr}}_{\text{start}}, t^{\text{disr}}_{\text{end}}$ | Start / end of disruption time window | s |
| $b^{\text{blk}}$ | Index of the blocked block | — |
| $\text{dir}_t \in \{U, D\}$ | Original direction of train $t$ | — |
| $a^{p}_{t,s}, d^{p}_{t,s}$ | Planned arrival / departure times | s |
| $E_0, E_1, E_2$ | Coefficients of linearized power function $P(v) = E_0 + E_1 v + E_2 v^2$ | kW |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (Big-M) | — |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3, w_4$ | Weights for delay, energy, rerouting, and cancellation | — |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Timetable Variables
- $a_{t,s} \geq 0$: actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $d_{t,s} \geq 0$: actual departure time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $\tau_{t,s} \geq 0$: dwell time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $\delta^{a}_{t,s} \geq 0$: arrival delay of train $t$ at station $s$
- $\delta^{d}_{t,s} \geq 0$: departure delay of train $t$ at station $s$

### 3.2 Routing and Occupancy Variables
- $x_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: equals 1 if train $t$ occupies block $b$ on its **original** track at time $k$
- $x^{R}_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: equals 1 if train $t$ occupies block $b$ on the **rerouted** (opposite) track at time $k$
- $r_{t,b} \in \{0,1\}$: equals 1 if train $t$ is rerouted in block $b$
- $u_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: equals 1 if train $t$ **enters** block $b$ at time $k$

### 3.3 Speed Profile Variables
- $v_{t,b,k} \geq 0$: speed of train $t$ in block $b$ at time $k$ (m/s)

### 3.4 Ordering and Cancellation Variables
- $y_{t,t',s} \in \{0,1\}$: equals 1 if train $t$ departs/arrives before train $t'$ at station $s$
- $z_t \in \{0,1\}$: equals 1 if train $t$ is cancelled

### 3.5 Energy Variable
- $e_t \geq 0$: total energy consumption of train $t$ (kWh)

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the total weighted rescheduling and energy cost:

$$
\min Z \;=\; w_1 \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \left( \delta^{a}_{t,s} + \delta^{d}_{t,s} \right) \;+\; w_2 \sum_{t \in T} e_t \;+\; w_3 \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{b \in B} r_{t,b} \;+\; w_4 \sum_{t \in T} z_t
$$

The four terms represent: (1) total delay, (2) total energy consumption, (3) number of rerouted train-block pairs, and (4) number of cancelled trains.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Dwell Time Definition and Bounds

$$
d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} = \tau_{t,s} \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{1}
$$

$$
\tau^{\min} \leq \tau_{t,s} \leq \tau^{\max} \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{2}
$$

### 5.2 Delay Definitions

$$
\delta^{a}_{t,s} \geq a_{t,s} - a^{p}_{t,s} \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{3}
$$

$$
\delta^{d}_{t,s} \geq d_{t,s} - d^{p}_{t,s} \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{4}
$$

### 5.3 Running Time Between Consecutive Stations (Coupling with Speed)

For each train $t$ and each consecutive station pair $(s, s+1)$, the arrival time equals the departure time plus the travel time through the blocks in between, where travel time is computed from the speed profile:

$$
a_{t,s+1} = d_{t,s} + \sum_{b \in B(s,s+1)} \sum_{k \in K} \frac{L_b \cdot \Delta t \cdot (x_{t,b,k} + x^{R}_{t,b,k})}{v_{t,b,k}} \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{S_{\text{last}}\} \tag{5}
$$

*(Assumption: the fraction $L_b \cdot \Delta t / v_{t,b,k}$ is linearized via piecewise-linear approximation of $1/v$ over $[v^{\min}, v^{\max}]$, yielding a linear expression.)*

### 5.4 Block Occupancy and Entry

Each non-cancelled train must occupy each block exactly once (along its path):

$$
\sum_{k \in K} u_{t,b,k} = 1 - z_t \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B(t) \tag{6}
$$

A train uses either the original track or the rerouted track, but not both, in any block:

$$
x_{t,b,k} + x^{R}_{t,b,k} \leq 1 - z_t \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K \tag{7}
$$

Block entry implies occupancy:

$$
u_{t,b,k} \leq x_{t,b,k} + x^{R}_{t,b,k} \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K \tag{8}
$$

### 5.5 Kinematic (Speed Profile) Constraints

Acceleration limit:

$$
v_{t,b,k+1} - v_{t,b,k} \leq a^{\text{acc}} \cdot \Delta t \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K \setminus \{K_{\max}\} \tag{9}
$$

Deceleration limit:

$$
v_{t,b,k} - v_{t,b,k+1} \leq a^{\text{dec}} \cdot \Delta t \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K \setminus \{K_{\max}\} \tag{10}
$$

Speed bounds:

$$
v^{\min} \cdot (x_{t,b,k} + x^{R}_{t,b,k}) \leq v_{t,b,k} \leq v^{\max} \cdot (x_{t,b,k} + x^{R}_{t,b,k}) \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K \tag{11}
$$

### 5.6 Same-Direction Track Capacity (No Conflicts)

For each block and each time step, at most one train traveling in each direction can occupy the original track:

$$
\sum_{t \in T: \text{dir}_t = U} x_{t,b,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall b \in B,\; k \in K \tag{12}
$$

$$
\sum_{t \in T: \text{dir}_t = D} x_{t,b,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall b \in B,\; k \in K \tag{13}
$$

### 5.7 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution (Rerouting Constraints)

When rerouting is used, bidirectional trains share the same track. The following constraints ensure no head-on conflicts:

For each block and time step, at most one train can occupy the **up-direction** track (original up-track plus rerouted down-track):

$$
\sum_{t \in T: \text{dir}_t = U} x_{t,b,k} + \sum_{t \in T: \text{dir}_t = D} x^{R}_{t,b,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall b \in B,\; k \in K \tag{14}
$$

For each block and time step, at most one train can occupy the **down-direction** track (original down-track plus rerouted up-track):

$$
\sum_{t \in T: \text{dir}_t = D} x_{t,b,k} + \sum_{t \in T: \text{dir}_t = U} x^{R}_{t,b,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall b \in B,\; k \in K \tag{15}
$$

### 5.8 Blockage Constraints

During the disruption window, the blocked block cannot be used by trains in the affected direction on their original track:

$$
x_{t,b^{\text{blk}},k} = 0 \quad \forall t \in T_{\text{aff}},\; k \in K^{\text{disr}} \tag{16}
$$

where $T_{\text{aff}}$ is the set of trains whose original direction is blocked. Rerouting via $x^{R}_{t,b,k}$ is still permitted.

### 5.9 Station Headway and Train Ordering

For any pair of trains $t, t'$ using the same station $s$, the ordering variable enforces minimum headway:

$$
d_{t',s} - d_{t,s} \geq h - M(1 - y_{t,t',s}) \quad \forall t, t' \in T,\; t \neq t',\; s \in S \tag{17}
$$

$$
a_{t',s} - a_{t,s} \geq h - M(1 - y_{t,t',s}) \quad \forall t, t' \in T,\; t \neq t',\; s \in S \tag{18}
$$

Exactly one ordering must hold:

$$
y_{t,t',s} + y_{t',t,s} = 1 \quad \forall t, t' \in T,\; t \neq t',\; s \in S \tag{19}
$$

### 5.10 Rerouting Consistency

Rerouting occupancy implies the rerouting indicator:

$$
x^{R}_{t,b,k} \leq r_{t,b} \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K \tag{20}
$$

Rerouting is only allowed in disruption-affected blocks and during the disruption window:

$$
r_{t,b} = 0 \quad \forall b \notin B^{\text{disr}} \text{ or } t \notin K^{\text{disr}} \tag{21}
$$

*(Assumption: rerouting is restricted to the disruption area and time window; outside, trains must use their original track.)*

### 5.11 Energy Consumption

Total energy consumption of each train:

$$
e_t = \sum_{b \in B} \sum_{k \in K} \left( E_0 + E_1 v_{t,b,k} + E_2 v_{t,b,k}^2 \right) \cdot \Delta t \cdot (x_{t,b,k} + x^{R}_{t,b,k}) \quad \forall t \in T \tag{22}
$$

*(Assumption: the quadratic term $v^2$ is linearized using piecewise-linear approximation with breakpoints $\{v_1, v_2, \dots, v_n\}$ over $[v^{\min}, v^{\max}]$, introducing auxiliary continuous variables $\lambda_{t,b,k,i}$ and $\eta_{t,b,k,i}$ with convexity constraints.)*

### 5.12 Cancellation Constraints

If a train is cancelled, all its timetable and routing variables are forced to zero:

$$
a_{t,s} \leq M(1 - z_t), \quad d_{t,s} \leq M(1 - z_t) \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S \tag{23}
$$

$$
x_{t,b,k} \leq 1 - z_t, \quad x^{R}_{t,b,k} \leq 1 - z_t \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K \tag{24}
$$

### 5.13 Initial and Terminal Conditions

The first departure and the last arrival are bounded by the schedule horizon:

$$
d_{t,s_1} \geq d^{p}_{t,s_1} \quad \forall t \in T \tag{25}
$$

$$
a_{t,s_{|S|}} \leq T_{\max} \quad \forall t \in T \tag{26}
$$

### 5.14 Variable Domains

$$
a_{t,s}, d_{t,s}, \tau_{t,s}, \delta^{a}_{t,s}, \delta^{d}_{t,s}, v_{t,b,k}, e_t \geq 0
$$

$$
x_{t,b,k}, x^{R}_{t,b,k}, r_{t,b}, u_{t,b,k}, y_{t,t',s}, z_t \in \{0, 1\}
$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

The proposed MILP integrates:

1. **Train Rescheduling (TRP)** through variables $a_{t,s}, d_{t,s}, \tau_{t,s}, \delta^{a}_{t,s}, \delta^{d}_{t,s}, y_{t,t',s}, z_t$ and constraints (1)–(4), (17)–(19), (23)–(26).
2. **Rerouting under partial blockage** through variables $x_{t,b,k}, x^{R}_{t,b,k}, r_{t,b}$ and constraints (6)–(8), (14)–(16), (20)–(21).
3. **Speed Management (TSMP)** through variables $v_{t,b,k}$ and constraints (9)–(11).
4. **Coupling between TRP and TSMP** through constraint (5), which expresses running times as functions of the speed profile, and constraint (22), which links energy to speed.
5. **Bidirectional conflict resolution** through constraints (14)–(15).

### Key Assumptions

- The railway line consists of two parallel tracks (one per direction).
- The disruption blocks only one track of one segment during a known time window.
- Trains can be rerouted to the opposite track only within the disruption area and time window.
- Speed profiles are discretized in time steps of length $\Delta t$.
- The nonlinear terms $1/v$ and $v^2$ are linearized using piecewise-linear approximations.
- Cancellation is allowed as a last-resort rescheduling action.
- All trains have identical kinematic parameters ($v^{\max}, v^{\min}, a^{\text{acc}}, a^{\text{dec}}$).

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t \in T$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s \in S$ |
| $K$ | Set of segments between consecutive stations, indexed by $k \in K$ |
| $I$ | Set of discretized time intervals, indexed by $i \in I$ |
| $T^+$ | Subset of trains traveling in forward direction |
| $T^-$ | Subset of trains traveling in backward direction |
| $I^{D}$ | Subset of intervals within the disruption window |
| $k_d$ | Index of the disrupted segment |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_k$ | Length of segment $k$ (km) |
| $\Delta$ | Duration of each time interval (min) |
| $v^{max}, v^{min}$ | Maximum and minimum allowable speed (km/h) |
| $a^{max}, b^{max}$ | Maximum acceleration and braking rates (km/h per interval) |
| $\alpha^{acc}, \alpha^{c}, \alpha^{br}$ | Energy coefficients for acceleration, cruising, and braking (kWh) |
| $\tau_s, \tau_e$ | Start and end times of the disruption window |
| $d^{min}_{t,s}, d^{max}_{t,s}$ | Minimum and maximum dwell times of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $\rho^{min}_k, \rho^{max}_k$ | Minimum and maximum traversal times of segment $k$ |
| $\bar{a}_{t,s}, \bar{d}_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival and departure times |
| $c^{cancel}, c^{delay}$ | Penalty for cancellation and per-minute delay |
| $h$ | Minimum headway (in intervals) between consecutive trains |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large big-M constant |

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $x_{t,k,i}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ occupies segment $k$ during interval $i$ |
| $y_{t,k,i}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ enters segment $k$ at the start of interval $i$ |
| $z_{t,k,i}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ exits segment $k$ at the end of interval $i$ |
| $w_{t,k,i}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ uses the opposite (rerouted) track on segment $k$ during interval $i$ |
| $v_{t,k,i}$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Speed of train $t$ on segment $k$ during interval $i$ (km/h) |
| $a^{+}_{t,k,i}, a^{-}_{t,k,i}$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Positive and negative speed change between intervals $i-1$ and $i$ |
| $pos_{t,k,i}$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Position of train $t$ on segment $k$ at end of interval $i$ (km) |
| $arr_{t,s}, dep_{t,s}$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Actual arrival and departure times of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $dwell_{t,s}$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Dwell time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $\Delta_{t,s}$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Delay of train $t$ at station $s$ relative to schedule |
| $e_{t,k,i}$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Energy consumption of train $t$ on segment $k$ during interval $i$ |
| $cancel_t$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled |

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{c^{delay} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \Delta_{t,s}}_{\text{total delay cost}} \;+\; \underbrace{c^{cancel} \sum_{t \in T} cancel_t}_{\text{cancellation cost}} \;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T} \sum_{k \in K} \sum_{i \in I} e_{t,k,i}}_{\text{total energy consumption}}
$$

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Cancellation
$$
x_{t,k,i} \leq 1 - cancel_t, \quad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; i \in I \tag{C1}
$$
$$
e_{t,k,i} \leq M(1 - cancel_t), \quad \forall t,k,i \tag{C2}
$$

### 5.2 Segment Occupation Flow Conservation
$$
x_{t,k,i} = x_{t,k,i-1} + y_{t,k,i} - z_{t,k,i}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K,\; i = 2,\ldots,|I| \tag{C3}
$$
$$
x_{t,k,1} = y_{t,k,1}, \quad \forall t,k \tag{C4}
$$
$$
x_{t,k,|I|} = z_{t,k,|I|}, \quad \forall t,k \tag{C5}
$$

### 5.3 Entry–Exit Linkage Between Consecutive Segments
$$
y_{t,k,i} \leq z_{t,k-1,i} + (1 - x_{t,k-1,i-1}), \quad \forall t,\; k = 2,\ldots,|K|,\; i \tag{C6}
$$

### 5.4 Speed Bounds
$$
v^{min} \cdot x_{t,k,i} \leq v_{t,k,i} \leq v^{max} \cdot x_{t,k,i}, \quad \forall t,k,i \tag{C7}
$$

### 5.5 Acceleration and Braking Limits
$$
v_{t,k,i} - v_{t,k,i-1} \leq a^{max}\Delta \cdot x_{t,k,i-1} + M(1 - x_{t,k,i-1}), \quad \forall t,k,i \geq 2 \tag{C8}
$$
$$
v_{t,k,i-1} - v_{t,k,i} \leq b^{max}\Delta \cdot x_{t,k,i} + M(1 - x_{t,k,i}), \quad \forall t,k,i \geq 2 \tag{C9}
$$
$$
v_{t,k,i} - v_{t,k,i-1} = a^{+}_{t,k,i} - a^{-}_{t,k,i}, \quad \forall t,k,i \geq 2 \tag{C10}
$$

### 5.6 Position Progression (Trapezoidal Motion)
$$
pos_{t,k,i} = pos_{t,k,i-1} + \frac{\Delta}{2}(v_{t,k,i} + v_{t,k,i-1}), \quad \forall t,k,i \geq 2 \tag{C11}
$$
$$
pos_{t,k,i} \leq L_k \cdot x_{t,k,i}, \quad \forall t,k,i \tag{C12}
$$
$$
pos_{t,k,i} \geq L_k - M(1 - z_{t,k,i}), \quad \forall t,k,i \tag{C13}
$$

### 5.7 Segment Traversal Time
$$
\rho^{min}_k (1 - cancel_t) \leq \sum_{i \in I} x_{t,k,i} \leq \rho^{max}_k (1 - cancel_t), \quad \forall t,k \tag{C14}
$$

### 5.8 Station Arrival, Departure, and Dwell
$$
arr_{t,s} = \sum_{i \in I} i\Delta \cdot z_{t,k(s),i}, \quad \forall t,s \tag{C15}
$$
$$
dep_{t,s} = arr_{t,s} + dwell_{t,s}, \quad \forall t,s \tag{C16}
$$
$$
d^{min}_{t,s}(1 - cancel_t) \leq dwell_{t,s} \leq d^{max}_{t,s}(1 - cancel_t), \quad \forall t,s \tag{C17}
$$

### 5.9 Delay Calculation
$$
\Delta_{t,s} \geq arr_{t,s} - \bar{a}_{t,s}, \quad \forall t,s \tag{C18}
$$
$$
\Delta_{t,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall t,s \tag{C19}
$$

### 5.10 Disruption Window Constraint
$$
x_{t,k_d,i} + w_{t,k_d,i} \leq 1 - cancel_t, \quad \forall t \in T,\; i \in I^{D} \tag{C20}
$$
$$
w_{t,k,i} = 0, \quad \forall t,\; k \neq k_d \text{ or } i \notin I^{D} \tag{C21}
$$

### 5.11 Rerouting Capacity (Single-Train Use of Opposite Track)
$$
\sum_{t \in T} w_{t,k_d,i} \leq 1, \quad \forall i \in I^{D} \tag{C22}
$$
$$
w_{t,k_d,i} \leq x_{t,k_d,i}, \quad \forall t,\; i \in I^{D} \tag{C23}
$$

### 5.12 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution
For any pair of trains $t_1 \in T^+$, $t_2 \in T^-$ on the same segment $k$:
$$
x_{t_1,k,i} + x_{t_2,k,i} \leq 1 + M(2 - w_{t_1,k,i} - w_{t_2,k,i}), \quad \forall t_1,t_2,\; k,\; i \tag{C24}
$$
When neither train is rerouted, this reduces to $x_{t_1,k,i} + x_{t_2,k,i} \leq 1$.

### 5.13 Same-Direction Headway
$$
\sum_{j=i}^{i+h-1} \left( x_{t_1,k,j} + x_{t_2,k,j} \right) \leq 2, \quad \forall t_1,t_2 \text{ same direction},\; k,\; i \tag{C25}
$$

### 5.14 Energy Consumption (Linearized)
$$
e_{t,k,i} = \alpha^{c} \Delta \cdot x_{t,k,i} + \alpha^{acc} a^{+}_{t,k,i} + \alpha^{br} a^{-}_{t,k,i}, \quad \forall t,k,i \tag{C26}
$$

### 5.15 Origin–Destination Enforcement
$$
\sum_{i \in I} y_{t,1,i} = 1 - cancel_t, \quad \forall t \tag{C27}
$$
$$
\sum_{i \in I} z_{t,|K|,i} = 1 - cancel_t, \quad \forall t \tag{C28}
$$

### 5.16 Non-Negativity and Binary Restrictions
$$
x_{t,k,i}, y_{t,k,i}, z_{t,k,i}, w_{t,k,i}, cancel_t \in \{0,1\} \tag{C29}
$$
$$
v_{t,k,i}, pos_{t,k,i}, a^{+}_{t,k,i}, a^{-}_{t,k,i}, e_{t,k,i}, arr_{t,s}, dep_{t,s}, dwell_{t,s}, \Delta_{t,s} \geq 0 \tag{C30}
$$

## 6. Modeling Assumptions

1. **Time discretization**: The planning horizon is divided into uniform intervals of length $\Delta$, and all decision variables are indexed accordingly.
2. **Piecewise-constant speed profile**: Train speed is constant within each time interval, which yields a linear trapezoidal motion model (C11).
3. **Single-track bidirectional line with passing sidings at stations**: Trains can use the opposite track only inside the disrupted segment and only during the disruption window.
4. **Rerouting exclusivity**: At most one train may use the opposite track on segment $k_d$ during any interval (C22).
5. **Energy model**: Energy consumption is linear in cruising time, acceleration magnitude, and braking magnitude (C26).
6. **Cancellation as a last resort**: Cancelled trains incur a fixed penalty and are removed from all operational constraints (C1–C2).
7. **Headway safety**: A minimum time gap $h$ between consecutive trains in the same direction is enforced (C25); bidirectional conflicts are resolved via (C24).
8. **Dwell flexibility**: Dwell times at stations can vary within prescribed bounds to absorb delays (C17).
9. **Big-M linearization**: All disjunctive constraints use a sufficiently large $M$ to maintain linearity.

## 7. Summary

The proposed MILP simultaneously optimizes (i) **train rescheduling decisions** (retiming via $arr_{t,s}$, $dep_{t,s}$; reordering via $x_{t,k,i}$; rerouting via $w_{t,k,i}$; cancellation via $cancel_t$) and (ii) **speed management decisions** ($v_{t,k,i}$, $a^{\pm}_{t,k,i}$, $pos_{t,k,i}$), under partial segment blockage disruption. The objective balances passenger delay, service cancellation, and energy consumption, while constraints guarantee conflict-free, physically feasible, and energy-aware operations for both directions of traffic.

Read the text below and fill in the predefined form.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

The form, as a JSON template: replace every <...> and give each list as many entries as the text requires (possibly none). Write each text field in at most 240 characters (symbols and names in at most 120) and shorten a long expression instead of copying it.

Text:
# Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Model

After generating and comparing three independent formulations, I present the best model below. It is a complete Mixed-Integer Linear Program that integrates the Train Rescheduling Problem (TRP) and the Train Speed Management Problem (TSMP) for high-speed railways under partial segment blockages, where rerouting forces opposite-direction trains onto a shared track during the disruption window.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Set | Description |
|---|---|
| $T = \{1,\dots,|T|\}$ | Trains. Each $t$ has direction $d_t \in \{+1,-1\}$ and original track $\text{trk}_t \in \{\text{up},\text{down}\}$. |
| $J = \{0,1,\dots,|J|\}$ | Conflict points (stations/junctions); $j=0$ origin, $j=|J|$ terminal. |
| $J^{\text{St}} \subset J$ | Intermediate stations (with dwell). |
| $S = \{1,\dots,|S|\}$ | Segments between consecutive conflict points. |
| $S^{D} \subseteq S$ | Disrupted segments. |
| $I_s = \{1,\dots,N_s^{\text{seg}}\}$, $\;N_s^{\text{seg}} = \lceil L_s/\Delta x\rceil$ | Spatial sub-segments of $s$. |
| $K = \{0,\dots,|K|\}$ | Discrete time intervals of length $\Delta\tau$. |
| $K^{D} = \{k \in K: k\Delta\tau \in [\tau_D^{s},\tau_D^{e}]\}$ | Intervals during the disruption window. |
| $R = \{1,\dots,p\}$ | Piecewise-linear breakpoints for $\Delta x/v$ and $v^2$. |
| $\mathcal{P} \subseteq T\times T$ | Pairs of trains requiring ordering. |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $L_s$ | Length of segment $s$ | km |
| $\Delta x,\Delta\tau$ | Spatial / temporal step | km, s |
| $V_{\min}, V_{\max}$ | Min / max operating speed | km/h |
| $A_{\max}, D_{\max}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration | km/h per s |
| $\tau^{\text{sched}}_{t,j}$ | Scheduled time at $j$ for $t$ | s |
| $\tau_D^{s},\tau_D^{e}$ | Disruption start / end | s |
| $h_{\text{hd}}$ | Minimum headway | s |
| $d_{\min}, d_{\max}$ | Min / max dwell at stations | s |
| $\alpha_0,\alpha_1,\alpha_2$ | Energy coefficients, $E=\alpha_0+\alpha_1 v+\alpha_2 v^2$ per $\Delta\tau$ | kWh |
| $w_d,w_e,w_c,w_r$ | Objective weights | — |
| $M$ | Big-$M$ | — |
| $v_r$, $\mu_r = \Delta x/v_r$, $\varepsilon_r = \alpha_0+\alpha_1 v_r+\alpha_2 v_r^{2}$ | Breakpoint values | — |
| $T_{\text{horizon}}$ | Planning horizon | s |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Rescheduling (operational) variables**

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{t,j}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Actual arrival time of $t$ at $j$ |
| $d_{t,j}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Actual departure time of $t$ at $j$ |
| $\delta_{t,j}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Positive delay of $t$ at $j$ |
| $c_t$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $1$ if $t$ is cancelled |
| $\text{rer}_{t,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $1$ if $t$ is rerouted to opposite track on $s$ |
| $\text{ord}_{t,t',j}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $1$ if $t$ passes $j$ before $t'$ |
| $\text{ord}^{\text{opp}}_{t,t',s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $1$ if $t$ traverses $s$ before $t'$ on opposite track |

**Speed-profile (control) variables**

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $v_{t,s,i,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Speed of $t$ on sub-segment $i$ of $s$ at interval $k$ |
| $x_{t,s,i,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $1$ if $t$ occupies sub-segment $i$ of $s$ at $k$ |
| $\pi_{t,s,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $1$ if $t$ occupies segment $s$ at $k$ |
| $\theta_{t,s,i,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Time spent on sub-segment $i$ (≈ $\Delta x / v_{t,s,i,k}$) |
| $e_{t,s,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Energy consumption rate of $t$ on $s$ at $k$ |
| $\lambda_{t,s,i,k,r}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | SOS2 weight for $(v,\theta)$ at breakpoint $r$ |
| $\eta_{t,s,k,r}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | SOS2 weight for energy at breakpoint $r$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\boxed{\;
\begin{aligned}
\min \; Z \;=\; & w_d\!\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{j\in J}\delta_{t,j} 
\;+\; w_e\!\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{k\in K} e_{t,s,k}\,\Delta\tau \\
&+\; w_c\!\sum_{t\in T}c_t 
\;+\; w_r\!\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\text{rer}_{t,s}
\end{aligned}\;}
\tag{OBJ}
$$

All four terms are linear after the auxiliary definitions below. Total delay at point $j$ is $\delta_{t,j}$, energy is summed over time, and rerouting/cancellation act as regularizers.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Delay linearization
$$
\delta_{t,j} \geq a_{t,j} - \tau^{\text{sched}}_{t,j}, \qquad \delta_{t,j} \geq 0 \qquad \forall t\in T,\; j\in J \tag{DLY}
$$

### 5.2 Cancellation consistency
$$
\sum_{i\in I_s} x_{t,s,i,k} \leq M(1-c_t), \qquad a_{t,j} \leq M(1-c_t), \qquad d_{t,j} \leq M(1-c_t) \quad \forall t,s,k,j \tag{CAN}
$$

### 5.3 Initial / final conditions
$$
d_{t,0} \geq \tau^{\text{sched}}_{t,0}(1-c_t), \qquad a_{t,|J|} \leq T_{\text{horizon}}(1-c_t) \quad \forall t \tag{INIT}
$$

### 5.4 Dwell-time bounds at stations
$$
d_{\min}(1-c_t) \leq d_{t,j} - a_{t,j} \leq d_{\max}(1-c_t) \qquad \forall t\in T,\; j\in J^{\text{St}} \tag{DWELL}
$$

### 5.5 Departure–arrival monotonicity
$$
a_{t,j+1} \geq d_{t,j} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; j\in J\setminus\{|J|\} \tag{MONO}
$$

### 5.6 Segment traversal time (links timing with speed profile)

For each $t$ and $s$, with entry point $j(s)$ and exit $j(s+1)$:
$$
d_{t,j(s+1)} - a_{t,j(s)} = \sum_{i\in I_s}\sum_{k\in K} \theta_{t,s,i,k} \qquad \forall t,s \tag{C4a}
$$

Piecewise-linear approximation of $\theta \approx \Delta x / v$ via SOS2:
$$
v_{t,s,i,k} = \sum_{r\in R} v_r \lambda_{t,s,i,k,r}, \quad
\theta_{t,s,i,k} = \sum_{r\in R} \mu_r \lambda_{t,s,i,k,r}, \quad
\sum_{r\in R}\lambda_{t,s,i,k,r} = x_{t,s,i,k} \tag{C4b}
$$
$$
\lambda_{t,s,i,k,r} \geq 0, \quad \text{SOS2}\big(\{\lambda_{t,s,i,k,r}\}_{r\in R}\big) \quad \forall t,s,i,k \tag{C4c}
$$

### 5.7 Kinematic (acceleration / deceleration) limits
$$
v_{t,s,i,k+1} - v_{t,s,i,k} \leq A_{\max}\Delta\tau, \qquad
v_{t,s,i,k+1} - v_{t,s,i,k} \geq -D_{\max}\Delta\tau \quad \forall t,s,i,k \tag{C5a}
$$
$$
V_{\min} x_{t,s,i,k} \leq v_{t,s,i,k} \leq V_{\max} x_{t,s,i,k} \quad \forall t,s,i,k \tag{C5b}
$$

### 5.8 Segment occupancy linking
$$
\pi_{t,s,k} \leq \sum_{i\in I_s} x_{t,s,i,k} \leq |I_s|\,\pi_{t,s,k} \qquad \forall t,s,k \tag{C6}
$$

### 5.9 Disruption feasibility (forbidding original track during $K^{D}$)

Let $T^{+}_{s}$ = trains whose original track on $s$ is the disrupted track.
$$
\pi_{t,s,k} \leq \text{rer}_{t,s} \qquad \forall t\in T^{+}_{s},\; s\in S^{D},\; k\in K^{D} \tag{C7a}
$$
$$
\text{rer}_{t,s} \leq \mathbb{1}[s\in S^{D}], \qquad
\sum_{k\in K^{D}}\pi_{t,s,k} \geq |K^{D}|\,\text{rer}_{t,s} \qquad \forall t,\; s\in S^{D} \tag{C7b}
$$

(C7b) forces $\text{rer}_{t,s}=1$ only when the train actually traverses the segment during the disruption window, ensuring rerouting is used and not wastefully set.

### 5.10 Bidirectional conflict resolution on the opposite (shared) track

For each $s\in S^{D}$ and $k\in K^{D}$:
$$
\sum_{t\in T} \pi_{t,s,k} \leq 1 \tag{C8a}
$$

Pairwise ordering of rerouted trains on the shared track:
$$
\text{ord}^{\text{opp}}_{t,t',s} + \text{ord}^{\text{opp}}_{t',t,s} \leq 1, \qquad
\text{ord}^{\text{opp}}_{t,t',s} + \text{ord}^{\text{opp}}_{t',t,s} \geq \text{rer}_{t,s}+\text{rer}_{t',s}-1 \tag{C8b}
$$
$$
\sum_{k\in K^{D}} k\,\pi_{t,s,k} \;\geq\; \sum_{k\in K^{D}} k\,\pi_{t',s,k} - |K|\,(1-\text{ord}^{\text{opp}}_{t,t',s}) \quad \forall (t,t')\in\mathcal{P},\; s\in S^{D} \tag{C8c}
$$

(C8a) ensures at most one train per interval on the shared track; (C8b)–(C8c) order the trains so the second enters only after the first has cleared.

### 5.11 Conflict-point sequencing and headway

For each pair $(t,t')\in\mathcal{P}$ and each $j\in J$:
$$
\text{ord}_{t,t',j} + \text{ord}_{t',t,j} + c_t + c_{t'} \leq 2 \tag{C9a}
$$
$$
a_{t',j} \geq d_{t,j} + h_{\text{hd}} - M\bigl(2 - \text{ord}_{t,t',j} + c_t + c_{t'}\bigr) \quad \forall t,t',j \tag{C9b}
$$

### 5.12 Block-section sequencing (same direction, different physical tracks)

Define $z_{t,t',s} = \text{rer}_{t,s} \oplus \text{rer}_{t',s}$ via linearization:
$$
z_{t,t',s} \leq \text{rer}_{t,s}+\text{rer}_{t',s}, \qquad z_{t,t',s} \geq |\text{rer}_{t,s}-\text{rer}_{t',s}| \tag{C10a}
$$

Then for each segment $s$, pair $(t,t')\in\mathcal{P}$ of same-direction trains, and interval $k$:
$$
\pi_{t,s,k} + \pi_{t',s,k} \leq 1 + z_{t,t',s} \quad\Rightarrow\quad
\pi_{t,s,k} + \pi_{t',s,k} \leq 1 + \text{rer}_{t,s} + \text{rer}_{t',s} \tag{C10b}
$$

i.e., same-direction trains may co-occupy $s$ only if they are on different physical tracks (one rerouted, one not).

### 5.13 Flow conservation along each train's path

For each $t\in T$, segment $s$ (between $j(s)$ and $j(s+1)$), and interval $k$:
$$
\sum_{i\in I_s} x_{t,s,i,k+1} = \sum_{i\in I_s} x_{t,s,i,k} + x^{\text{in}}_{t,s,k+1} - x^{\text{out}}_{t,s,k+1} \tag{C11}
$$
with boundary conditions $x^{\text{in}}_{t,s(k=0),\cdot} = 1$ at the entry segment and $x^{\text{out}}_{t,s(k=|K|),\cdot} = 1$ at the terminal, preventing teleportation.

### 5.14 Energy consumption (piecewise-linear, SOS2)

Average speed on $s$ during $k$:
$$
\bar v_{t,s,k} = \sum_{i\in I_s} v_{t,s,i,k}\,/\,N_s^{\text{seg}} \tag{C12a}
$$
$$
e_{t,s,k} = \sum_{r\in R}\varepsilon_r\,\eta_{t,s,k,r}, \qquad
\bar v_{t,s,k} = \sum_{r\in R} v_r\,\eta_{t,s,k,r}, \qquad
\sum_{r\in R}\eta_{t,s,k,r} = \pi_{t,s,k} \tag{C12b}
$$
$$
\eta_{t,s,k,r} \geq 0, \qquad \text{SOS2}\big(\{\eta_{t,s,k,r}\}_{r\in R}\big) \quad \forall t,s,k \tag{C12c}
$$

### 5.15 Variable domains
$$
\begin{aligned}
& a_{t,j}, d_{t,j}, \delta_{t,j}, \theta_{t,s,i,k}, e_{t,s,k} \geq 0;\\
& V_{\min}\,x_{t,s,i,k} \leq v_{t,s,i,k} \leq V_{\max}\,x_{t,s,i,k};\\
& c_t,\,\text{rer}_{t,s},\,\text{ord}_{t,t',j},\,\text{ord}^{\text{opp}}_{t,t',s},\,\pi_{t,s,k},\,x_{t,s,i,k} \in \{0,1\};\\
& 0 \leq \lambda_{t,s,i,k,r},\, \eta_{t,s,k,r} \leq 1.
\end{aligned} \tag{DOM}
$$

---

## 6. Modeling Assumptions

1. **Double-track line, one track per direction**, with possible rerouting to the opposite track during disruption only.
2. **Constant maximum acceleration/deceleration** $A_{\max}, D_{\max}$ (linearized via finite differences).
3. **Energy model** is convex quadratic in speed, linearized exactly via SOS2 over breakpoints.
4. **Uniform spatial–temporal discretization** of the time–space diagram.
5. **Block sections** cannot host two same-direction trains unless on different physical tracks (one rerouted).
6. **Flexible dwell times** in $[d_{\min}, d_{\max}]$ at intermediate stations; origin departure ≥ scheduled, terminal arrival ≤ $T_{\text{horizon}}$.
7. **Train cancellation** is permitted and penalized; cancelled trains consume no resources.
8. **Rerouting only** on disrupted segments during the disruption window (C7b).
9. **Bidirectional conflict** on the shared (opposite) track is resolved by sequential occupancy (C8a–c).
10. **Headway $h_{\text{hd}}$** at all conflict points; cancels via $c_t$ automatically relax constraints.
11. **Train consist and mass are fixed**; regenerative braking energy is assumed dissipated (conservative for energy minimization).
12. **Discretization step** $\Delta\tau$ chosen so that $|A_{\max}|\Delta\tau \leq V_{\max}-V_{\min}$ for kinematic feasibility.

---

## 7. Why the Model is Linear

| Non-linear term | Linearization |
|---|---|
| $\max(0,a-\tau^{\text{sched}})$ | Auxiliary $\delta_{t,j}$ (DLY) |
| $\Delta x / v$ (traversal time) | SOS2 over $\{v_r\}$ via $\theta,\lambda$ (C4b–c) |
| $\alpha_0+\alpha_1 v+\alpha_2 v^2$ (energy) | SOS2 over $\{v_r,\varepsilon_r\}$ via $\eta$ (C12b–c) |
| Product $\text{ord}\cdot M$ | Big-$M$ with valid bounds from problem horizon |

Hence the model is a **strictly linear MILP**, suitable for off-the-shelf solvers (CPLEX, Gurobi, HiGHS) and amenable to Benders/column-generation decomposition as outlined in the paper.

---

## 8. Model Size and Complexity

| Element | Order of magnitude |
|---|---|
| Binary variables | $O(|T|^2|J| + |T|^2|S| + |T||S||K||I_s|)$ |
| Continuous variables | $O(|T||S||K||I_s|(1+p) + |T||J|)$ |
| Constraints | $O(|T||S||K||I_s| + |T|^2|J| + |T|^2|S|)$ |

For large-scale instances, the authors' adaptive iterative algorithm and train-plan decomposition (Section 5 of the paper) drastically reduce computational burden compared to solving the full MILP directly, while guaranteeing equivalence in the limit of fine plan granularity.
