# MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed $t$ |
| $N=\{0,1,\dots,M\}$ | Stations (nodes) |
| $E=\{1,\dots,M\}$ | Blocks (segments); block $e$ connects nodes $e-1$ and $e$ |
| $K=\{0,1,\dots,K_{\max}\}$ | Discrete time intervals of length $\Delta$ (s) |
| $P=\{1,\dots,|P|\}$ | Speed breakpoints for piecewise-linear approximation |
| $B_d\subseteq E$ | Disrupted (partially blocked) blocks |
| $R(t)\subseteq E$ | Ordered blocks on the route of train $t$ |
| $S(t)\subseteq N$ | Ordered stations on the route of train $t$ |
| $K^D=\{k\in K: k\Delta\in[T^D_{\text{start}},T^D_{\text{end}}]\}$ | Intervals overlapping the disruption window |
| $\text{dir}(t)\in\{+1,-1\}$ | Direction of train $t$ |
| $o(t),\,d(t)$ | Origin / destination of $t$ |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $L_e>0$ | Length of block $e$ (m) |
| $\Delta>0$ | Time-interval length (s) |
| $T^D_{\text{start}},T^D_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption window start/end (s) |
| $\tau_{\min},\tau_{\max}$ | Min/max dwell time at stations (s) |
| $M_t$ | Mass of train $t$ (t) |
| $P_{\max},F_{\max},B_{\max}$ | Max power (W), max tractive / brake force (kN) |
| $c_0,c_1,c_2$ | Davis resistance coefficients |
| $V_{\max}$ | Max operating speed (m/s) |
| $A_{\max}$ | Max $|\text{acceleration}|$ (m/s²) |
| $a^{\text{sched}}_{t,n},\,d^{\text{sched}}_{t,n}$ | Scheduled arrival/departure of $t$ at $n$ (s) |
| $w_t$ | Passenger weight of train $t$ |
| $C$ | Cancellation penalty |
| $v^p$ | $p$-th speed breakpoint, $0<v^1<\dots<v^{|P|}=V_{\max}$ |
| $\eta^p_e=L_e/v^p$ | Traversal time of $e$ at $v^p$ (s) |
| $w_D,w_E,w_C$ | Objective weights (delay, energy, cancellation) |
| $M_\tau,M_v$ | Sufficiently large constants (Big-M) |
| $\eta_{\text{regen}}\in[0,1]$ | Regenerative brake recovery efficiency |

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{t,e,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ occupies block $e$ in interval $k$ |
| $\tau_{t,n}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Actual arrival time of $t$ at node $n$ |
| $\theta_{t,n}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Actual departure time of $t$ from node $n$ |
| $\delta_{t,n}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Delay of $t$ at node $n$ |
| $z_t$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled |
| $r_{t,e}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses opposite (rerouted) track on $e$ |
| $v_{t,e}$ | $[0,V_{\max}]$ | Average speed of $t$ on $e$ (m/s) |
| $v^{\text{in}}_{t,e},v^{\text{out}}_{t,e}$ | $[0,V_{\max}]$ | Entry/exit speeds of $t$ on $e$ (m/s) |
| $a_{t,e}$ | $[-A_{\max},A_{\max}]$ | Average acceleration of $t$ on $e$ |
| $E_{t,e}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Mechanical traction energy of $t$ on $e$ (kWh) |
| $\lambda^p_{t,e}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | SOS2 weights for speed breakpoint $p$ on $e$ for $t$ |
| $\mu^p_{t,e}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | SOS2 weights for entry-speed breakpoint $p$ on $e$ |
| $\nu^p_{t,e}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | SOS2 weights for exit-speed breakpoint $p$ on $e$ |
| $s_{t,e,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if interval $k$ starts occupancy of $e$ by $t$ |

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\;\; w_{D}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{n\in S(t)} w_t\,\delta_{t,n}
\;+\;w_{E}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{e\in R(t)} E_{t,e}
\;+\;w_{C}\;C\sum_{t\in T} z_t
$$

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Piecewise-Linear Speed (SOS2)

For every $t\in T,\,e\in R(t)$:

$$
v_{t,e}=\sum_{p\in P}\lambda^{p}_{t,e}\,v^{p},\qquad
\sum_{p\in P}\lambda^{p}_{t,e}=1,\qquad
\{\lambda^{p}_{t,e}\}_{p\in P}\in\mathrm{SOS2}
$$

Entry/exit speeds (linked across blocks via SOS2):

$$
v^{\text{in}}_{t,e}=\sum_{p\in P}\mu^{p}_{t,e}\,v^{p},\quad
\sum_{p}\mu^{p}_{t,e}=1,\quad
\{\mu^{p}_{t,e}\}\in\mathrm{SOS2}
$$

$$
v^{\text{out}}_{t,e}=\sum_{p\in P}\nu^{p}_{t,e}\,v^{p},\quad
\sum_{p}\nu^{p}_{t,e}=1,\quad
\{\nu^{p}_{t,e}\}\in\mathrm{SOS2}
$$

Boundary between consecutive blocks:

$$
v^{\text{in}}_{t,e}=v^{\text{out}}_{t,e-1}\;\;\text{for all }e\in R(t)\setminus\{e_1\}
$$

### 5.2 Block Traversal Time

$$
\eta_{t,e}:=\sum_{p\in P}\lambda^{p}_{t,e}\,\frac{L_e}{v^{p}}
$$

### 5.3 Block Occupancy and Contiguity

For every $t\in T,\,e\in R(t)$:

$$
\sum_{k\in K} x_{t,e,k}\,\Delta\;\ge\;\eta_{t,e},\qquad
\sum_{k\in K} x_{t,e,k}\,\Delta\;\le\;\eta_{t,e}+\Delta
$$

Contiguity of occupancy (single connected run):

$$
\sum_{k\in K} s_{t,e,k}=1,\qquad
x_{t,e,k}\le s_{t,e,k}+\sum_{k'<k} x_{t,e,k'}\;\;\forall k
$$

$$
s_{t,e,k}\ge x_{t,e,k}-x_{t,e,k-1},\;\;
s_{t,e,k}\le x_{t,e,k},\;\;
s_{t,e,k}\le 1-x_{t,e,k-1}
$$

### 5.4 Station Time Linkage (Coupling of Rescheduling & Speed Profile)

For every $t\in T$ and consecutive stations $n,\,n'=n+1\in S(t)$:

$$
\tau_{t,n'}=\theta_{t,n}+\sum_{e\text{ between }n,n'}\eta_{t,e}
$$

For origin and destination:

$$
\tau_{t,o(t)}=\theta_{t,o(t)},\qquad
\theta_{t,o(t)}\ge d^{\text{sched}}_{t,o(t)}-M_{\tau}\,z_t
$$

$$
\tau_{t,d(t)}\le T_{\max}+M_{\tau}\,z_t
$$

### 5.5 Dwell Time

For every $t\in T,\,n\in S(t)\setminus\{d(t)\}$:

$$
\theta_{t,n}\ge \tau_{t,n}+\tau_{\min}-M_{\tau}\,z_t,\qquad
\theta_{t,n}\le \tau_{t,n}+\tau_{\max}+M_{\tau}\,z_t
$$

### 5.6 Delay Definition

For every $t\in T,\,n\in S(t)$:

$$
\delta_{t,n}\ge \tau_{t,n}-a^{\text{sched}}_{t,n}-M_{\tau}\,z_t,\qquad
\delta_{t,n}\le M_{\tau}(1-z_t),\qquad \delta_{t,n}\ge 0
$$

### 5.7 Cancellation Consistency

For every $t\in T$:

$$
\sum_{e\in R(t)}\sum_{k\in K} x_{t,e,k}\le M_{\tau}(1-z_t),\qquad
\sum_{e\in R(t)}\sum_{k\in K} x_{t,e,k}\ge 1-M_{\tau}\,z_t
$$

### 5.8 Same-Direction Block Conflict

For every $e\in E$, $k\in K$, and pair $t\neq t'\in T$ with $\text{dir}(t)=\text{dir}(t')$ and $e\in R(t)\cap R(t')$:

$$
x_{t,e,k}+x_{t',e,k}\le 1
$$

### 5.9 Bidirectional Conflict on Rerouted Blocks

For every $e\in B_d$, $k\in K$, and pair $t\neq t'\in T$ with $\text{dir}(t)\neq\text{dir}(t')$ and $e\in R(t)\cap R(t')$:

$$
x_{t,e,k}+x_{t',e,k}\le 1+(1-r_{t,e})+(1-r_{t',e})
$$

### 5.10 Reroute Feasibility

For every $t\in T,\,e\in E\setminus B_d$:

$$
r_{t,e}=0
$$

For every $t\in T,\,e\in B_d$:

$$
r_{t,e}\ge x_{t,e,k}\;\;\forall k\in K^D,\qquad
r_{t,e}\le \sum_{k\in K^D} x_{t,e,k}
$$

### 5.11 Speed and Acceleration Bounds

For every $t\in T,\,e\in R(t)$:

$$
0\le v_{t,e}\le V_{\max},\qquad -A_{\max}\le a_{t,e}\le A_{\max}
$$

Kinematic coupling (linearized via SOS2 weights):

$$
a_{t,e}\,L_e=\tfrac{1}{2}\!\left(\sum_{p\in P}\nu^{p}_{t,e}(v^{p})^{2}-\sum_{p\in P}\mu^{p}_{t,e}(v^{p})^{2}\right)
$$

### 5.12 Energy (Linearized)

Resistance force on $e$ (linear in SOS2 weights):

$$
R_{t,e}=c_0+c_1\,v_{t,e}+c_2\sum_{p\in P}\lambda^{p}_{t,e}(v^{p})^{2}
$$

Mechanical traction energy (with regenerative brake recovery):

$$
E_{t,e}\;\ge\; R_{t,e}\,L_e+\tfrac{M_t}{2}\!\left(\sum_{p}\nu^{p}_{t,e}(v^{p})^{2}-\sum_{p}\mu^{p}_{t,e}(v^{p})^{2}\right)
$$

$$
E_{t,e}\;\ge\; R_{t,e}\,L_e+\eta_{\text{regen}}\cdot\tfrac{M_t}{2}\!\left(\sum_{p}\mu^{p}_{t,e}(v^{p})^{2}-\sum_{p}\nu^{p}_{t,e}(v^{p})^{2}\right)
$$

(Max of accelerating vs. regenerative-braking expressions; with positive $a$ the first dominates, with negative $a$ the second; the max is linearized by writing both as $\ge$ lower bounds on $E_{t,e}$.)

### 5.13 Force / Power Limits

For every $t\in T,\,e\in R(t)$:

$$
M_t\,a_{t,e}+R_{t,e}\le F_{\max},\qquad
-M_t\,a_{t,e}\le B_{\max}+R_{t,e}
$$

Traction-power bound:

$$
F_{\max}\,v_{t,e}\;\ge\; M_t\,a_{t,e}\,v_{t,e}+R_{t,e}\,v_{t,e}\;\;\Rightarrow\;\;P_{\max}\ge (M_t\,a_{t,e}+R_{t,e})\,v_{t,e}
$$

(Linearized via $R_{t,e}$ and SOS2 weights.)

### 5.14 Initial and Final Boundary Conditions

For every $t\in T$:

$$
\theta_{t,o(t)}\ge a^{\text{dep}}_t-M_{\tau}\,z_t,\qquad
\tau_{t,d(t)}\le T_{\max}+M_{\tau}\,z_t
$$

$$
v^{\text{in}}_{t,\text{first}(t)}\le V_{\max},\qquad
v^{\text{out}}_{t,\text{last}(t)}\ge 0
$$

### 5.15 Coupling of Rescheduling and Speed Profile

The block traversal time $\eta_{t,e}$ (function of speed profile) feeds directly into station times $\tau_{t,n},\theta_{t,n}$ via (5.4), which in turn drive dwell times (5.5), delays (5.6), and downstream conflicts (5.8–5.9). This bi-directional coupling is realized by (5.1)–(5.4) without further constraints.

## 6. Linearization Assumptions

| # | Item | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | Reciprocal $1/v$ in traversal time | SOS2 over breakpoints $\{v^p\}$; $1/v^p$ precomputed |
| A2 | Quadratic $v^2$ in energy/acceleration | SOS2 weights $\mu,\nu$ for entry/exit speeds; product with $(v^p)^2$ remains linear |
| A3 | Discretization of block occupancy | $x_{t,e,k}$ integral; $\eta_{t,e}$ bounded within one $\Delta$ interval |
| A4 | Contiguity of occupancy | Single start-indicator $s_{t,e,k}$; equals 1 exactly once |
| A5 | Bidirectional conflict | Big-M on $r_{t,e},r_{t',e}$; ordering $y_{t,t',e}$ optional auxiliary |
| A6 | Cancellation | All physical variables decoupled via $M_\tau$; $\delta_{t,n}=0$ if cancelled |
| A7 | Disruption coupling | $r_{t,e}$ active iff block traversed during $K^D$ |
| A8 | Acceleration link | Derived from discrete entry/exit speed differences (trapezoidal motion over $L_e$) |
| A9 | Force/power bounds | Linear in SOS2 weights since $R_{t,e}$ uses precomputed $(v^p)^2$ |
| A10 | Energy with regen brake | Max of accelerating and decelerating expressions enforced via dual $\ge$ |
| A11 | Objective weights | $w_D,w_E,w_C$ are scalar trade-off parameters |
| A12 | Dwell time | Free variable within $[\tau_{\min},\tau_{\max}]$; could be fixed to scheduled value if required |
| A13 | Headway beyond blocks | Station departure-arrival conflicts can be added analogously to (5.8)–(5.9) if station-track resources modeled |

The resulting formulation is a **fully linear Mixed-Integer Program** with:
- **Binary variables**: $x_{t,e,k}, z_t, r_{t,e}, s_{t,e,k}$
- **Continuous variables**: $\tau_{t,n},\theta_{t,n},\delta_{t,n},v_{t,e},v^{\text{in}}_{t,e},v^{\text{out}}_{t,e},a_{t,e},E_{t,e},\lambda^p_{t,e},\mu^p_{t,e},\nu^p_{t,e}$

Solvable by Gurobi, CPLEX, or SCIP with SOS2 support.

Now write the filled-in form for the text above as one JSON object, without code fences and without repeating the template.

Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.

Text:
# Final MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

The or_operator returned empty responses, so I am providing the complete, refined MILP directly with all feedback improvements incorporated.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, $t \in T$ |
| $S$ | set of stations, $s \in S$, ordered along the line |
| $B$ | set of block sections, $b \in B$ |
| $B_t \subseteq B$ | ordered blocks traversed by train $t$ |
| $S_t \subseteq S$ | candidate stops of train $t$ |
| $K = \{0,1,\dots,K_{\max}\}$ | global discrete time intervals, $k \in K$ |
| $R = \{N, R\}$ | route choices: $N$ = normal track, $R$ = rerouted (opposite track) |
| $b_d \in B$ | disrupted block |
| $K_d = \{k : T_d^{\text{start}} \le k\Delta t \le T_d^{\text{end}}\}$ | disrupted time intervals |
| $I$ | breakpoints for piecewise-linear $v^2$ approximation |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $L_b$ | length of block $b$ (m) |
| $V_{\max}, V_{\min}$ | maximum / minimum speed (m/s) |
| $A_{\text{acc}}, A_{\text{dec}}$ | maximum acceleration / deceleration (m/s²) |
| $\Delta t$ | duration of a time interval (s) |
| $H_{\min}$ | minimum headway between trains (s) |
| $T_{\text{dwell}}^{\min}, T_{\text{dwell}}^{\max}$ | min / max dwell time at a station (s) |
| $\text{arr}^{\text{sch}}_{t,s},\; \text{dep}^{\text{sch}}_{t,s}$ | scheduled arrival / departure (s) |
| $T_d^{\text{start}}, T_d^{\text{end}}$ | disruption time window on $b_d$ (s) |
| $M$ | sufficiently large big-M constant |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma \ge 0$ | weights for delay, energy, cancellation |
| $\eta_1, \eta_2, \kappa$ | energy coefficients (propulsion, regen, drag) |
| $v_i, i \in I$ | breakpoint speed values for piecewise-linear $v^2$ |
| $v^{0}_{t}, v^{f}_{t}$ | initial / final speed of train $t$ (m/s) |
| $L_{\text{train}}$ | train length (m) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Timing (continuous)**
- $\text{arr}_{t,s} \ge 0$ — actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $\text{dep}_{t,s} \ge 0$ — actual departure time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $\text{delay}_{t,s} \ge 0$ — arrival delay at $s$
- $\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,b}, \tau^{\text{out}}_{t,b} \ge 0$ — entry / exit time of train $t$ on block $b$

**Driving dynamics (continuous)**
- $v_{t,b,k} \in [0, V_{\max}]$ — speed of train $t$ on block $b$ at interval $k$
- $p_{t,b,k} \in [0, L_b]$ — position of train $t$ on block $b$ at interval $k$
- $a_{t,b,k} \in [-A_{\text{dec}}, A_{\text{acc}}]$ — acceleration
- $a^{+}_{t,b,k} \ge 0$ — positive part of acceleration

**Discrete choices (binary)**
- $x_{t,b,r} \in \{0,1\}$ — train $t$ uses route $r$ on block $b$
- $y_{t,s} \in \{0,1\}$ — train $t$ stops at station $s$
- $z_{t,t',b} \in \{0,1\}$ — train $t$ precedes train $t'$ on block $b$
- $w_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$ — block $b$ occupied by train $t$ at interval $k$
- $c_t \in \{0,1\}$ — train $t$ is cancelled
- $\text{opp}_{t,t',b} \in \{0,1\}$ — trains $t, t'$ use opposite directions on rerouted block $b$

**Energy linearization (continuous)**
- $u_{t,b,k}$ — McCormick envelope for product $a \cdot v$
- $q_{t,b,k}$ — piecewise-linear approximation of $v^2$
- $e_{t,b,k} \ge 0$ — energy consumed on block $b$ in interval $k$
- $\lambda_{t,b,k,i} \ge 0$ — convex combination weights for $v^2$ breakpoints

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; \alpha \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{s \in S_t} \text{delay}_{t,s}
\;+\; \beta \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{b \in B_t}\sum_{k \in K} e_{t,b,k}
\;+\; \gamma \sum_{t \in T} c_t
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Dynamics — Euler Discretization

$$
v_{t,b,k+1} = v_{t,b,k} + a_{t,b,k}\,\Delta t \qquad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B_t,\; k \in K \setminus \{K_{\max}\}
$$

$$
p_{t,b,k+1} = p_{t,b,k} + v_{t,b,k}\,\Delta t + \tfrac{1}{2} a_{t,b,k}\,\Delta t^{2} \qquad \forall t, b \in B_t,\; k \in K \setminus \{K_{\max}\}
$$

### 5.2 Speed and Acceleration Bounds

$$
V_{\min}(1-c_t) \le v_{t,b,k} \le V_{\max}(1-c_t) \qquad \forall t, b, k
$$

$$
-A_{\text{dec}}(1-c_t) \le a_{t,b,k} \le A_{\text{acc}}(1-c_t) \qquad \forall t, b, k
$$

$$
a^{+}_{t,b,k} \ge a_{t,b,k}, \qquad a^{+}_{t,b,k} \ge 0 \qquad \forall t, b, k
$$

### 5.3 Block Traversal Time

$$
\tau^{\text{out}}_{t,b} - \tau^{\text{in}}_{t,b} \;\ge\; \frac{L_b}{V_{\max}}(1-c_t) \qquad \forall t, b \in B_t
$$

$$
\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,b} \le M(1-c_t), \qquad \tau^{\text{out}}_{t,b} \le M(1-c_t) \qquad \forall t, b
$$

### 5.4 Boundary Conditions (per block)

$$
p_{t,b,0} = 0, \qquad p_{t,b,K_{\max}} = L_b(1-c_t) \qquad \forall t, b \in B_t
$$

$$
v_{t,b,0} = v^{0}_{t}(1-c_t), \qquad v_{t,b,K_{\max}} = v^{f}_{t}(1-c_t) \qquad \forall t, b \in B_t
$$

### 5.5 Dwell Times (strengthened: exact zero when no stop)

$$
T_{\text{dwell}}^{\min}\,y_{t,s} \;\le\; \text{dep}_{t,s} - \text{arr}_{t,s} \;\le\; T_{\text{dwell}}^{\max}\,y_{t,s} \qquad \forall t, s \in S_t
$$

### 5.6 Linking Arrival / Departure to Block Entry / Exit

For each station $s$ between blocks $b^{\text{in}}(s)$ (incoming) and $b^{\text{out}}(s)$ (outgoing):

$$
\text{arr}_{t,s} = \tau^{\text{out}}_{t,b^{\text{in}}(s)} \qquad \forall t, s \in S_t
$$

$$
\text{dep}_{t,s} = \tau^{\text{in}}_{t,b^{\text{out}}(s)} \qquad \forall t, s \in S_t
$$

### 5.7 Consecutive Block Linking

For each train $t$ and each consecutive pair $(b, b')$ on its path with station $s$ between them:

$$
\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,b'} = \tau^{\text{out}}_{t,b} + (\text{dep}_{t,s} - \text{arr}_{t,s}) \qquad \forall t,\; (b,b') \text{ consecutive in } B_t
$$

### 5.8 Stop Decisions

$$
\text{arr}_{t,s} \le M\,y_{t,s}, \qquad \text{dep}_{t,s} \le M\,y_{t,s} \qquad \forall t, s
$$

### 5.9 Route Choice and Rerouting (cancellation-aware)

$$
\sum_{r \in R} x_{t,b,r} = 1 - c_t \qquad \forall t, b \in B_t
$$

$$
x_{t,b_d,N} = 0 \qquad \forall t \in T \quad \text{(normal route blocked during disruption)}
$$

### 5.10 Disruption Window — Corrected (rerouted trains may use block during $K_d$)

A normal-route train cannot occupy block $b_d$ during the disruption window; a rerouted train may:

$$
w_{t,b_d,k} \le 1 - x_{t,b_d,N} \qquad \forall t,\; k \in K_d
$$

$$
w_{t,b_d,k} \le x_{t,b_d,R} \qquad \forall t,\; k \in K_d
$$

Equivalently, a normal-route train must schedule its traversal outside $K_d$:

$$
\tau^{\text{out}}_{t,b_d} \le T_d^{\text{start}} + M\,x_{t,b_d,R} + M\,c_t \qquad \forall t
$$

$$
\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,b_d} \ge T_d^{\text{end}} - M\,x_{t,b_d,R} - M\,c_t \qquad \forall t
$$

### 5.11 Block Occupation — Corrected (big-M linking)

Train $t$ occupies block $b$ in interval $k$ if its position is strictly within $(0, L_b)$:

$$
w_{t,b,k} \ge \frac{p_{t,b,k}}{L_b} \qquad \forall t, b, k
$$

$$
w_{t,b,k} \le \frac{p_{t,b,k}}{L_b} + (1 - \text{on}_{t,b,k}) \cdot M \qquad \forall t, b, k
$$

$$
w_{t,b,k} \ge \text{on}_{t,b,k} \qquad \forall t, b, k
$$

where $\text{on}_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$ indicates the train is actively traversing block $b$ in interval $k$. Single occupancy:

$$
\sum_{t \in T} w_{t,b,k} \le 1 \qquad \forall b, k
$$

### 5.12 Headway Constraints (at stations)

$$
\text{arr}_{t,s} + H_{\min} \le \text{arr}_{t',s} + M(1-z_{t,t',s}) + M(1-y_{t,s}) + M(1-y_{t',s}) \qquad \forall t \ne t', s
$$

$$
\text{arr}_{t',s} + H_{\min} \le \text{arr}_{t,s} + M\,z_{t,t',s} + M(1-y_{t,s}) + M(1-y_{t',s}) \qquad \forall t \ne t', s
$$

### 5.13 Ordering Constraints (on shared blocks)

$$
z_{t,t',b} + z_{t',t,b} = 1 \qquad \forall t \ne t', b
$$

$$
\tau^{\text{out}}_{t,b} + H_{\min} \le \tau^{\text{in}}_{t',b} + M(1-z_{t,t',b}) + M(1-\text{on}_{t,b}) + M(1-\text{on}_{t',b}) \qquad \forall t \ne t', b
$$

### 5.14 Bidirectional Conflicts on Rerouted Track

Define $\text{opp}_{t,t',b}$ when both trains use the rerouted route on block $b$:

$$
\text{opp}_{t,t',b} \ge x_{t,b,R} + x_{t',b,R} - 1 \qquad \forall t \ne t', b
$$

$$
\text{opp}_{t,t',b} \le x_{t,b,R}, \qquad \text{opp}_{t,t',b} \le x_{t',b,R} \qquad \forall t \ne t', b
$$

Enforce headway in both directions when opposite-direction trains share the rerouted block:

$$
\tau^{\text{out}}_{t,b} + H_{\min} \le \tau^{\text{in}}_{t',b} + M(1-z_{t,t',b}) + M(1-\text{opp}_{t,t',b}) \qquad \forall t \ne t', b
$$

$$
\tau^{\text{out}}_{t',b} + H_{\min} \le \tau^{\text{in}}_{t,b} + M\,z_{t,t',b} + M(1-\text{opp}_{t,t',b}) \qquad \forall t \ne t', b
$$

### 5.15 Cancellation

$$
v_{t,b,k} \le V_{\max}(1-c_t), \quad p_{t,b,k} \le L_b(1-c_t), \quad a_{t,b,k} \le A_{\text{acc}}(1-c_t) \qquad \forall t, b, k
$$

$$
\text{arr}_{t,s} \le M(1-c_t), \quad \text{dep}_{t,s} \le M(1-c_t) \qquad \forall t, s
$$

$$
x_{t,b,r} \le 1 - c_t \qquad \forall t, b, r
$$

### 5.16 Linearized Energy

**McCormick envelopes** for $u_{t,b,k} \approx a_{t,b,k} \cdot v_{t,b,k}$ with $a \in [-A_{\text{dec}}, A_{\text{acc}}]$, $v \in [V_{\min}, V_{\max}]$:

$$
u_{t,b,k} \ge -A_{\text{dec}}\,v_{t,b,k} + V_{\min}\,a_{t,b,k} + A_{\text{dec}}V_{\min}
$$

$$
u_{t,b,k} \ge A_{\text{acc}}\,v_{t,b,k} + V_{\max}\,a_{t,b,k} - A_{\text{acc}}V_{\max}
$$

$$
u_{t,b,k} \le -A_{\text{dec}}\,v_{t,b,k} + V_{\max}\,a_{t,b,k} + A_{\text{dec}}V_{\max}
$$

$$
u_{t,b,k} \le A_{\text{acc}}\,v_{t,b,k} + V_{\min}\,a_{t,b,k} - A_{\text{acc}}V_{\min}
$$

**Piecewise-linear** approximation of $v^2$ using breakpoints $\{v_i\}$:

$$
\sum_{i \in I} \lambda_{t,b,k,i} = 1, \qquad \sum_{i \in I} \lambda_{t,b,k,i}\,v_i = v_{t,b,k}, \qquad \lambda_{t,b,k,i} \ge 0
$$

$$
q_{t,b,k} = \sum_{i \in I} \lambda_{t,b,k,i}\,v_i^{2} \quad \text{(SOS2 / convex-combination formulation)}
$$

**Energy aggregation:**

$$
e_{t,b,k} \;\ge\; \eta_1\,a^{+}_{t,b,k}\,v_{t,b,k} + \eta_2\,u_{t,b,k} + \kappa\,q_{t,b,k}
$$

(If $\eta_2 < 0$ for regenerative braking, replace $u$ by an additional McCormick pair on $a^{+}_{t,b,k} \cdot v_{t,b,k}$.)

### 5.17 Delay Linearization

$$
\text{delay}_{t,s} \ge \text{arr}_{t,s} - \text{arr}^{\text{sch}}_{t,s}, \qquad \text{delay}_{t,s} \ge 0 \qquad \forall t, s
$$

---

## 6. Linearization Summary

| Nonlinear term | Method |
|---|---|
| $v_{t,b,k+1} = v_{t,b,k} + a_{t,b,k}\,\Delta t$ | Linear (Euler) |
| $p_{t,b,k+1} = p_{t,b,k} + v_{t,b,k}\,\Delta t + 0.5\,a_{t,b,k}\,\Delta t^2$ | Linear (Euler) |
| $a \cdot v$ in energy | McCormick envelopes (4 linear inequalities) |
| $v^2$ in energy | Piecewise-linear via SOS2 / convex combination |
| $\max(0, a)$ | Auxiliary $a^+ \ge a$, $a^+ \ge 0$ |
| $\max(0, \text{arr} - \text{arr}^{\text{sch}})$ | Auxiliary $\text{delay} \ge \text{arr} - \text{arr}^{\text{sch}}$, $\text{delay} \ge 0$ |
| Disjunctive (if-then) constraints | Big-M |

---

## 7. Assumptions

1. **Discretization**: $\Delta t$ is small enough that the Euler update is a valid approximation of continuous motion (typical $\Delta t = 10$–$30$ s).
2. **Block structure**: Each block $b$ is single-track in normal operation; rerouted blocks are shared bidirectionally.
3. **Rerouting feasibility**: A valid rerouted path exists for every train affected by the disruption on $b_d$.
4. **Direction encoding**: Direction on a block is fully determined by the chosen route $r$ (normal vs. rerouted).
5. **Headway**: $H_{\min}$ is enforced at every station and at the entry/exit of every shared block.
6. **Cancellation**: A cancelled train releases all blocks, dwells, and timing constraints; all its route choices are forced to 0.
7. **Energy model**: Mechanical energy is linear in $a \cdot v$; aerodynamic losses are quadratic in $v$ and approximated by piecewise-linear segments.
8. **Big-M validity**: $M$ is chosen large enough to never bind feasible solutions but small enough to relax infeasible ones (typically $M \ge K_{\max}\Delta t$).
9. **Single occupancy**: At most one train occupies a block at any interval (no train-following within a block).
10. **Station topology**: Each station has one incoming block $b^{\text{in}}(s)$ and one outgoing block $b^{\text{out}}(s)$ per train.
11. **Initial / final speeds** $v^{0}_t, v^{f}_t$ are parameters (not variables).
12. **Symmetry**: $z_{t,t,b} = 0$ for all $t, b$ (a train does not precede itself).
13. **Objective weights** $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are exogenous and reflect operator preferences (delay vs. energy vs. service cancellation).
14. **Disruption scope**: Only one block $b_d$ is disrupted at a time; the disruption window $[T_d^{\text{start}}, T_d^{\text{end}}]$ is known in advance.
15. **No partial rerouting**: A train either uses the normal route or the rerouted route on each block; mixed routing on the same block is not allowed.

---

## 8. Model Size (Indicative)

For $|T|$ trains, $|B|$ blocks, $|K|$ intervals, $|I|$ breakpoints:
- Continuous variables: $O(|T| \cdot |B| \cdot |K| \cdot (|I|+5))$
- Binary variables: $O(|T|^2 \cdot |B| + |T| \cdot |B| \cdot |K| + |T| \cdot |S|)$
- Constraints: $O(|T| \cdot |B| \cdot |K| + |T|^2 \cdot |B|)$

This MILP is computationally intensive for large instances, motivating the decomposition-based solution method described in the paper (reformulated IP + train-plan selection + adaptive iterative refinement).

Text:
# MILP Model for Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

## 1. Model Overview

The proposed formulation is a **Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP)** model that jointly addresses the **rerouting, reordering, and rescheduling** of trains in a disturbed railway network. The model extends the reference formulation of Pellegrini et al. (2014) by introducing a **pair-wise delay interpretation** that captures which train each delayed train is waiting for, and by explicitly modelling **delay propagation** along the chosen routes. A sub-optimal variant (without delay propagation) is also defined for fast initialisation.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Set | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t, t' \in T$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations / signal blocks / conflict points, indexed by $s, s' \in S$ |
| $R_t$ | Set of feasible alternative routes for train $t$, indexed by $r \in R_t$ |
| $A$ | Set of directed arcs (track sections) connecting consecutive stations, indexed by $(s, s') \in A$ |
| $C$ | Set of potential pairwise conflicts, indexed by $(t, t', s)$ |
| $E_t$ | Set of scheduled events of train $t$ (arrivals and departures), indexed by $e \in E_t$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| $a_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{t,s}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $\tau_{t,s,s'}$ | Minimum running time of train $t$ on arc $(s,s')$ |
| $h_{t,s}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $H_{t,t',s}$ | Minimum headway time required between trains $t$ and $t'$ at conflict point $s$ |
| $\pi_{t,r,s} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if route $r$ of train $t$ passes through station $s$ |
| $\pi_{t,r,s,s'} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if route $r$ of train $t$ uses arc $(s,s')$ |
| $\gamma_t$ | Weighting coefficient for the delay of train $t$ (e.g., passenger load) |
| $\gamma_d$ | Weighting coefficient for departure delays |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (Big-M) |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### Routing variables
$$
x_{t,r} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; r \in R_t
$$
1 if train $t$ is assigned to route $r$.

### Ordering variables
$$
y_{t,t',s} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall\, (t,t',s) \in C
$$
1 if train $t$ is scheduled to pass conflict point $s$ before train $t'$.

$$
p_{t,t',s} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall\, (t,t',s) \in C
$$
1 if trains $t$ and $t'$ actually share conflict point $s$ (i.e., both routes traverse $s$).

### Pair-wise waiting variables
$$
w_{t,t'} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall\, t, t' \in T,\; t \neq t'
$$
1 if train $t'$ is delayed because it waits for train $t$ (i.e., $t'$ is the follower).

### Timing variables
$$
\alpha_{t,s} \geq 0 \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
$$
Actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$.

$$
\beta_{t,s} \geq 0 \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
$$
Actual departure time of train $t$ at station $s$.

### Delay variables
$$
\delta_{t,s} \geq 0 \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
$$
Arrival delay of train $t$ at station $s$.

$$
\delta^d_{t,s} \geq 0 \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
$$
Departure delay of train $t$ at station $s$.

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimise the total weighted delay of all trains, including both arrival and departure delays:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \left( \gamma_t \, \delta_{t,s} \;+\; \gamma_d \, \delta^d_{t,s} \right)
$$

**Assumption:** Equal weighting ($\gamma_t = \gamma_d = 1$) is used by default; these coefficients can be tuned to reflect passenger importance, train priority, or service type.

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Route Selection Constraints

**(R1) Exactly one route per train:**
$$
\sum_{r \in R_t} x_{t,r} = 1 \quad \forall\, t \in T
$$

**(R2) Conflict activation (both trains must traverse the point):**
$$
p_{t,t',s} \leq \sum_{r \in R_t} \pi_{t,r,s}\, x_{t,r} \quad \forall\, (t,t',s) \in C
$$
$$
p_{t,t',s} \leq \sum_{r \in R_{t'}} \pi_{t',r,s}\, x_{t',r} \quad \forall\, (t,t',s) \in C
$$
$$
p_{t,t',s} \geq \sum_{r \in R_t} \pi_{t,r,s}\, x_{t,r} + \sum_{r \in R_{t'}} \pi_{t',r,s}\, x_{t',r} - 1 \quad \forall\, (t,t',s) \in C
$$

### 6.2 Ordering Constraints

**(O1) Mutual exclusivity of ordering:**
$$
y_{t,t',s} + y_{t',t,s} = p_{t,t',s} \quad \forall\, (t,t',s) \in C
$$

**(O2) Transitivity of ordering (acyclicity):**
$$
y_{t,t'',s} \geq y_{t,t',s} + y_{t',t'',s} - 1 \quad \forall\, t,t',t'' \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### 6.3 Pair-wise Waiting Constraints (Sub-Optimal Model)

**(W1) At most one follower direction per pair:**
$$
w_{t,t'} + w_{t',t} \leq 1 \quad \forall\, t, t' \in T,\; t \neq t'
$$

**(W2) Waiting only if conflict exists:**
$$
w_{t,t'} \leq \sum_{s \in S} p_{t,t',s} \quad \forall\, t, t' \in T,\; t \neq t'
$$

**(W3) Pair-wise delay interpretation — if $t'$ waits for $t$, then $t'$ inherits at least the delay of $t$:**
$$
\delta_{t',s} \geq \delta_{t,s} - M(1 - w_{t,t'}) - M(1 - p_{t,t',s}) \quad \forall\, (t,t',s) \in C
$$

### 6.4 Headway Constraints

**(H1) Minimum headway enforced by ordering:**
$$
\alpha_{t',s} \geq \alpha_{t,s} + H_{t,t',s} - M(1 - y_{t,t',s}) - M(1 - p_{t,t',s}) \quad \forall\, (t,t',s) \in C
$$

**(H2) Equivalent headway on departures:**
$$
\beta_{t',s} \geq \beta_{t,s} + H_{t,t',s} - M(1 - y_{t,t',s}) - M(1 - p_{t,t',s}) \quad \forall\, (t,t',s) \in C
$$

### 6.5 Running Time and Dwell Time Constraints

**(T1) Minimum running time on each arc (route-dependent):**
$$
\alpha_{t,s'} \geq \beta_{t,s} + \tau_{t,s,s'} - M\left(1 - \sum_{r \in R_t} \pi_{t,r,s,s'}\, x_{t,r}\right) \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; (s,s') \in A
$$

**(T2) Minimum dwell time at stations:**
$$
\beta_{t,s} \geq \alpha_{t,s} + h_{t,s} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### 6.6 Delay Definition and Propagation (Extended / Optimal Model)

**(D1) Arrival delay definition:**
$$
\delta_{t,s} \geq \alpha_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

**(D2) Departure delay definition:**
$$
\delta^d_{t,s} \geq \beta_{t,s} - d_{t,s} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

**(D3) Delay propagation along the chosen route (key extension for global optimality):**
$$
\delta_{t,s'} \geq \delta_{t,s} - M\left(1 - \sum_{r \in R_t} \pi_{t,r,s,s'}\, x_{t,r}\right) \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; (s,s') \in A
$$

**(D4) Departure delay lower-bounded by arrival delay plus dwell deviation:**
$$
\delta^d_{t,s} \geq \delta_{t,s} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### 6.7 Initial Delay Constraints (Disturbance Modelling)

**(I1) Trains enter the network with their primary (initial) delay:**
$$
\delta_{t,s_0} \geq \Delta^0_t \quad \forall\, t \in T
$$
where $s_0$ is the entry station and $\Delta^0_t$ is the known primary delay of train $t$.

---

## 7. Model Variants

### Variant A — Sub-Optimal Model (Section 3.1 of the paper)
Includes constraints: (R1)–(R2), (O1)–(O2), (W1)–(W3), (H1)–(H2), (T1)–(T2), (D1)–(D2), (D4), (I1).  
**Excludes** delay propagation constraint (D3).  
Provides a fast, sub-optimal solution that neglects delay propagation.

### Variant B — Globally Optimal Model (Section 3.3 of the paper)
Includes **all** constraints listed above, in particular adding **(D3)**.  
Guarantees the global optimum of the original rtRTMP of Pellegrini et al. (2014) at lower computational cost due to the pair-wise reformulation.

---

## 8. Key Assumptions

1. **Discrete time representation:** All times are expressed in a common discrete time unit (e.g., seconds).
2. **Deterministic disturbances:** Primary delays $\Delta^0_t$ are known at the time of optimisation.
3. **Conflict points are station-based:** Conflicts are evaluated at a finite set of stations/signal blocks; microscopic track details are abstracted (macroscopic modelling).
4. **Single-track and double-track compatibility:** The headway matrix $H_{t,t',s}$ encodes both block-section and platform conflicts.
5. **Route pre-generation:** The set of feasible routes $R_t$ is generated a priori (e.g., by the TRSP of Samà et al., 2016) and provided as input.
6. **No train cancellation or short-turning:** All trains must complete their full journey; only rerouting, reordering, and rescheduling are allowed.
7. **FIFO relaxation:** The ordering variables allow non-FIFO resolutions, consistent with dispatcher practice.
8. **Big-M validity:** $M$ is chosen large enough (e.g., the planning horizon length) so that deactivated constraints do not bind.
9. **Linearisation:** All products of binary and continuous variables are linearised using standard Big-M techniques.
10. **Objective scope:** Energy consumption is not explicitly modelled; it can be added as a secondary term weighted by tractive-effort coefficients if desired (cf. Naldini et al., 2022).

---

## 9. Summary of Model Size

| Element | Count |
|---------|-------|
| Binary variables | $\sum_t |R_t| + 3|C| + |T|(|T|-1)$ |
| Continuous variables | $2|T||S| + 2|T||S| = 4|T||S|$ |
| Constraints | $\approx |T| + 9|C| + 4|T||A| + 2|T||S|$ |

This compact formulation, especially through the pair-wise waiting variables and the propagation constraint (D3), provides a tighter LP relaxation than the original Pellegrini et al. (2014) model and is amenable to efficient MILP solvers (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX) for real-time applications.

# MILP Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

We consider a double-track high-speed railway corridor with a set of stations and segments. A partial blockage disrupts one track of a segment during a known time window, so affected trains may either wait or **reroute to the opposite track** (unidirectional single-track operation during the disruption).

**Assumptions (stated explicitly, as some details are not given in the input):**
- (A1) The disruption window $[\underline{t}_d, \bar{t}_d]$ on segment $s \in D$ (blocked track) is known in advance (deterministic disruption).
- (A2) Train dynamics are linearized: each train $f$ has a fixed set of **speed profiles** (regimes) per segment, each characterized by running time $r_{fsk}$ and energy consumption $e_{fsk}$; this keeps the model linear (discretization assumption).
- (A3) Time is discretized into periods $t \in T$ (or handled with big-M continuous time — we use the latter).
- (A4) Minimum headway between consecutive trains on a segment is constant $h$.
- (A5) Each train occupies a track exclusively; dwell times have minimum and maximum bounds at stations.
- (A6) Cancellation is allowed with a penalty; no short-turning is considered.
- (A7) Each train has a scheduled timetable $\{\sigma^{arr}_{fs}, \sigma^{dep}_{fs}\}$; deviations are penalized linearly.

**Sets:**
- $F$: trains; $S$: segments; $K_{fs}$: speed profiles of train $f$ on segment $s$; $D \subset S$: disrupted segments; $P$: ordered sequence of segments/stations along the line for train $f$, with indices $p$ (position of train $f$ in its route).

**Parameters:**
- $r_{fsk}, e_{fsk}$: running time / energy of profile $k$ of train $f$ on segment $s$; $M$: big-M; $h$: headway; $\underline{d}_{fs}, \bar{d}_{fs}$: min/max dwell at station after segment position $p$; $\underline{t}_d, \bar{t}_d$: disruption window; $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$: weights on delay, energy, cancellation.

## 2. Variables

- $a_{fp}, d_{fp} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$: arrival / departure time of train $f$ at position $p$ of its route.
- $x_{fpk} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ uses speed profile $k$ on the segment at route position $p$.
- $y_{fp} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ uses the **opposite track** (reroute) on the segment at position $p$.
- $o_{fp} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ occupies the affected track direction on segment $s(p)$ (its original track).
- $z_f \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ is **cancelled**.
- $\delta^{dep}_{fp}, \delta^{arr}_{fp} \ge 0$: departure/arrival delay at position $p$.

## 3. Objective Function

Minimize total weighted delay, energy consumption, and cancellation cost:

$$\min \; \sum_{f \in F}\sum_{p} \big(\delta^{arr}_{fp} + \delta^{dep}_{fp}\big) \;+\; \alpha \sum_{f \in F}\sum_{p}\sum_{k \in K_{fs(p)}} e_{fs(p)k}\, x_{fpk} \;+\; \gamma \sum_{f \in F} z_f$$

## 4. Constraints

**(C1) Linking arrival/departure to schedule and delay:**
$$a_{fp} = \sigma^{arr}_{fs(p)} + \delta^{arr}_{fp} + W\, z_f, \quad d_{fp} = \sigma^{dep}_{fs(p)} + \delta^{dep}_{fp} + W\, z_f \qquad \forall f, p$$
($W$ = large constant so that cancelled trains' times become irrelevant.)

**(C2) Running time consistency (timetable ↔ speed profile coupling):**
$$a_{f,p+1} \ge d_{fp} + \sum_{k \in K_{fs(p)}} r_{fs(p)k}\, x_{fpk} - M\, z_f \qquad \forall f, \forall p$$
$$\sum_{k \in K_{fs(p)}} x_{fpk} = 1 - z_f \qquad \forall f, \forall p$$

**(C3) Minimum/maximum dwell time:**
$$\underline{d}_{fp} \le d_{fp} - a_{fp} \le \bar{d}_{fp} + M z_f \qquad \forall f, p \text{ at stations}$$

**(C4) Rerouting logic:** a train either keeps its track or reroutes to the opposite track:
$$y_{fp} \le 1 - z_f \qquad \forall f, p$$
$$y_{fp} \le \mathbb{1}\{s(p) \in D\} \qquad \forall f, p \quad \text{(rerouting only on disrupted segments)}$$

**(C5) Disruption closure — original track unusable during the window:**
If train $f$ traverses disrupted segment $s(p)$ on its **original track** ($y_{fp}=0$) it may not enter during $[\underline{t}_d, \bar{t}_d]$:
$$a_{f,p+1} - \underline{t}_d \le M(3 - y_{fp}^{\text{orig}} - u^{in}_{fp} - \mathbb{1}\{s(p)\in D\})$$
$$\bar{t}_d - a_{f,p+1} \le M(3 - y_{fp}^{\text{orig}} - u^{out}_{fp} - \mathbb{1}\{s(p)\in D\})$$
where $y^{\text{orig}}_{fp} = 1 - y_{fp}$ (implicit substitution), and $u^{in}_{fp}, u^{out}_{fp}$ are auxiliary binaries indicating entry before $\underline{t}_d$ and exit after $\bar{t}_d$ respectively, linked by:
$$a_{f,p+1} \le \underline{t}_d + M u^{in}_{fp}, \qquad a_{f,p+1} \ge \bar{t}_d - M u^{out}_{fp} \qquad \forall f, p \in D$$

**(C6) Headway / conflict-freedom on shared track (both directions, original and opposite track):**
For each pair of trains $(f,g)$, $f \ne g$, and each route position $p$, trains sharing the same track ($y_{fp} = y_{gp}$ and same physical segment in opposing or same direction) must be separated by at least $h$:
$$a_{g,p'} \ge d_{fp} + h - M(1 - \eta_{fgp}) - M z_f - M z_g$$
$$d_{fp} \ge a_{g,p'} + h - M\,\eta_{fgp} - M z_f - M z_g$$
where $\eta_{fgp} \in \{0,1\}$ is the sequencing variable and $p'$ denotes the corresponding position of train $g$ on the same physical resource. Applied to both tracks (original and opposite), including bidirectional trains rerouted onto the same single track.

**(C7) Departure-order consistency (reordering) on a station/segment resource:**
$$d_{fp} \ge d_{gp} + h - M(1 - \eta_{fgp}) \qquad \text{(complemented with the symmetric constraint above)}$$

**(C8) Cancellation inactivity:**
$$z_f = 1 \Rightarrow x_{fpk} = 0, \; y_{fp} = 0 \;\; \forall p, k \quad \text{(enforced via C2 and } y_{fp} \le 1-z_f\text{)}$$

**(C9) Variable domains:**
$$a_{fp}, d_{fp}, \delta^{arr}_{fp}, \delta^{dep}_{fp} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}; \quad x_{fpk}, y_{fp}, \eta_{fgp}, z_f \in \{0,1\}$$

## 5. Remarks

- Constraints (C2) are the core **integration mechanism**: the timetable feasibility depends directly on the selected speed profile's running time, while the objective rewards energy-efficient (typically slower) profiles — capturing the trade-off between accelerating to reduce delay and coasting to save energy.
- (C5)–(C6) jointly guarantee conflict-free bidirectional operation on the single open track during the disruption window, including rerouted trains.
- The model is a valid MILP: all constraints are linear; nonlinear train dynamics are captured via the discrete profile set $K_{fs}$ (Assumption A2). With sufficiently fine profile discretization, this MILP approximates the continuous optimal-control version arbitrarily well.
- Note on the solution method mentioned in the input: the MILP decomposes naturally — for fixed $(x, y, z)$ selections per train ("train plans"), timing variables are determined by linear propagation; the IP over plan selections can be solved by an adaptive iterative scheme with plan refinement near the incumbent and local branching, as described in the paper's framework.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{B}$ | Set of block sections, indexed by $b$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of time intervals, indexed by $k$ (duration $\Delta t$ seconds each) |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{V}$ | Set of discretized speed levels, indexed by $v$, with values $\bar v_v$ [m/s] |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Set of discrete acceleration levels, indexed by $p$, with values $\bar a_p$ [m/s²], $\bar a_p \in [-a_{\max}^{\text{brk}}, +a_{\max}^{\text{trc}}]$ |
| $[t^{ds}, t^{de}]$ | Disruption time window (interval indices) |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $L_b$ | Length of block section $b$ [m] |
| $L_i$ | Length of train $i$ [m] |
| $h$ | Minimum station headway [intervals] |
| $\bar v_b^{\max}$ | Maximum permitted speed on block $b$ [m/s] |
| $\bar e_v$ | Traction power at speed level $v$ [kW] |
| $e^{\text{reg}}$ | Regenerative braking recovery factor |
| $M_i$ | Mass of train $i$ [tons] |
| $\tau_{i,s}^{\text{sch}}$ | Scheduled arrival interval of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\text{dwell}_{\min}(s), \text{dwell}_{\max}(s)$ | Min/max dwell time at station $s$ |
| $\beta_b \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if block $b$ is in the disrupted segment |
| $b^\text{opp}(b)$ | Opposite-direction counterpart of block $b$ |
| $\alpha, \gamma, \delta$ | Weights on energy, cancellation, and rerouting |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (Big-M) |
| $\Delta t$ | Time interval length [s] |

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{i,b,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ occupies block $b$ in interval $k$ |
| $y_{i,b,k,b',k+1}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ moves from $(b,k)$ to $(b',k+1)$ |
| $w_{i,v,b,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses speed level $v$ on block $b$ in interval $k$ |
| $a_{i,p,b,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses acceleration level $p$ on block $b$ in interval $k$ |
| $o_{i,j,b,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on block $b$ at interval $k$ |
| $z_{i,j,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is processed before train $j$ at station $s$ |
| $r_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses the detour (opposite-track) route |
| $c_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $\text{arr}_{i,s}, \text{dep}_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ | Actual arrival/departure interval of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $D_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ [intervals] |
| $E_i^{\text{trc}}, E_i^{\text{reg}}, E_i$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Traction, regenerative, and net energy of train $i$ [kJ] |

## 4. Objective Function

$$\min \; \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} E_i}_{\text{energy}} \;+\; \underbrace{\beta \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} D_{i,s}}_{\text{delay}} \;+\; \underbrace{\gamma \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} c_i}_{\text{cancellations}} \;+\; \underbrace{\delta \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} r_i}_{\text{rerouting cost}}$$

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Flow Conservation
For all $i \in \mathcal{T},\, b \in \mathcal{B},\, k \in \mathcal{K}$:
$$x_{i,b,k} - x_{i,b,k-1} = \sum_{b'} y_{i,b',k-1,b,k} - \sum_{b'} y_{i,b,k,b',k+1}$$

### 5.2 Forward Movement (one block per interval, except during dwell)
$$\sum_{b'} y_{i,b,k,b',k+1} = x_{i,b,k}, \quad \forall i,b,k \text{ where } b' \neq b^{\text{next}}_i$$
$$y_{i,b,k,b,k+1} \leq x_{i,b,k} \quad \text{(dwell transition)}$$

### 5.3 Speed Level Uniqueness
$$\sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} w_{i,v,b,k} = x_{i,b,k}, \quad \forall i,b,k$$

### 5.4 Acceleration Level Uniqueness
$$\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}} a_{i,p,b,k} = x_{i,b,k}, \quad \forall i,b,k$$

### 5.5 Kinematic Link Between Speed and Acceleration (linearized via Big-M)
$$-M(1-a_{i,p,b,k}) \leq \bar v_{v(k+1)} - \bar v_{v(k)} - \bar a_p \, \Delta t \leq M(1-a_{i,p,b,k})$$
where $\bar v_{v(k)} = \sum_{v} \bar v_v \, w_{i,v,b,k}$.

### 5.6 Speed Limit Enforcement
$$\sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} \bar v_v \, w_{i,v,b,k} \leq \bar v_b^{\max}, \quad \forall i,b,k$$

### 5.7 Transition Coherence
$$y_{i,b,k,b',k+1} \leq x_{i,b,k}, \qquad y_{i,b,k,b',k+1} \leq x_{i,b',k+1}, \quad \forall i,b,b',k$$

### 5.8 Disrupted Block Forbidance (original route)
$$x_{i,b,k} \leq 1 - \beta_b, \quad \forall i, b: \beta_b=1, k \in [t^{ds}, t^{de}] \text{ with } r_i = 0$$

### 5.9 Detour Permits Use of Opposite Track
$$x_{i,b^{\text{opp}}(b),k} \leq r_i + (1-\beta_b), \quad \forall i, b: \beta_b=1, k \in [t^{ds}, t^{de}]$$

### 5.10 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution on Shared (Rerouted) Track
For all $i,j \in \mathcal{T}$ with $\text{dir}_i \neq \text{dir}_j$, and all $b,k$:
$$x_{i,b,k} + x_{j,b,k} \leq 1$$
$$x_{i,b,k} \leq o_{i,j,b,k} + M(1-x_{j,b,k})$$
$$x_{j,b,k} \leq o_{j,i,b,k} + M(1-x_{i,b,k})$$
$$o_{i,j,b,k} + o_{j,i,b,k} \leq 1$$

### 5.11 Ordering Consistency Along Block (same-direction trains)
For all $i \neq j$ with $\text{dir}_i = \text{dir}_j$, $b,k$:
$$x_{i,b,k} + x_{j,b,k} - 1 \leq o_{i,j,b,k} + o_{j,i,b,k}$$

### 5.12 Block Length Compatibility
$$L_i \leq L_b + M(1-x_{i,b,k}), \quad \forall i,b,k$$

### 5.13 Station Headway Constraints
For all $i \neq j$, $s \in \mathcal{S}$:
$$\text{dep}_{i,s} + h \leq \text{arr}_{j,s} + M(1 - z_{i,j,s})$$
$$\text{dep}_{j,s} + h \leq \text{arr}_{i,s} + M \cdot z_{i,j,s}$$

### 5.14 Dwell Time Bounds
$$\text{dwell}_{\min}(s) \leq \text{dep}_{i,s} - \text{arr}_{i,s} \leq \text{dwell}_{\max}(s), \quad \forall i,s$$

### 5.15 Arrival/Departure Link to Block Occupation
$$\text{arr}_{i,s} \leq k + M(1-x_{i,b_s^{\text{arr}},k}), \quad \text{arr}_{i,s} \geq k - M(1-x_{i,b_s^{\text{arr}},k})$$
$$\text{dep}_{i,s} \geq k + x_{i,b_s^{\text{dep}},k} - M(1-x_{i,b_s^{\text{dep}},k})$$

### 5.16 Delay Definition
$$D_{i,s} \geq \text{arr}_{i,s} - \tau_{i,s}^{\text{sch}}, \qquad D_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall i,s$$

### 5.17 Cancellation Logic
$$x_{i,b,k} \leq 1 - c_i, \quad \forall i,b,k$$
$$\text{arr}_{i,s} \leq M(1-c_i), \qquad \text{dep}_{i,s} \leq M(1-c_i)$$

### 5.18 Traction Energy
$$E_i^{\text{trc}} = \Delta t \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}} \bar e_v \, w_{i,v,b,k}, \quad \forall i$$

### 5.19 Regenerative Braking Energy
$$E_i^{\text{reg}} = e^{\text{reg}} \, \Delta t \sum_{b,k} \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}: \bar a_p < 0} |\bar a_p| \, M_i \, a_{i,p,b,k}, \quad \forall i$$

### 5.20 Net Energy
$$E_i = E_i^{\text{trc}} - E_i^{\text{reg}}, \qquad E_i \geq 0, \quad \forall i$$

### 5.21 Origin/Destination Boundary Conditions
$$\sum_k x_{i,b_{O_i},k} = 1, \qquad \sum_k x_{i,b_{D_i},k} = 1, \quad \forall i$$

### 5.22 Route Topology (original vs. detour)
If $r_i = 1$, the block sequence of train $i$ follows $\{b^{\text{opp}}(b)\}$ within the disrupted segment; implemented through the $y$-transition variables using a route index parameter.

## 6. Assumptions Made

1. **Discretization is sufficiently fine** so that the linearization of kinematic and energy relationships is tight in practice.
2. **Single contiguous disrupted segment** on one side of the double-track line.
3. **Bidirectional rerouting** is permitted only through the opposite track on the disrupted segment.
4. **Piecewise-linear energy model** in speed and acceleration is used (with $\bar e_v$ and regenerative factor $e^{\text{reg}}$).
5. **Cancellation** is a binary decision; if cancelled, the train is entirely removed from the network.
6. **Trains share a common discretization** for time, space, speed, and acceleration.
7. **Weights** $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ are exogenous parameters reflecting operational priorities.
8. **Regenerative energy recovery** is assumed available only during deceleration phases ($a_p < 0$).

Text:
# MILP Formulation for Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Model Overview

This MILP integrates **train rescheduling** (which trains run, when, on which route) with **train speed management** (energy-efficient speed profiles) under partial segment blockages. Nonlinear terms (squared speed/acceleration in the energy model) are linearized using **piecewise linear approximation with SOS2 variables**.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Set | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| $I$ | Set of trains, $i \in I$ |
| $J$ | Set of stations (ordered along the line), $j \in J$ |
| $B$ | Set of track blocks/segments, $b \in B$ |
| $K$ | Set of discretized time steps, $k \in K$ |
| $R$ | Set of possible routes (original + rerouting), $r \in R$ |
| $P^v$ | Set of piecewise-linear breakpoints for $v^2$, $p \in P^v$ |
| $P^a$ | Set of piecewise-linear breakpoints for $a^2$, $p \in P^a$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Parameter | Description | Unit |
|-----------|-------------|------|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ | km |
| $V_{\max}, V_{\min}$ | Maximum / minimum allowed speed | km/h |
| $a_{\max}, d_{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration | m/s² |
| $\Delta t$ | Time step duration | s |
| $t^{ds}, t^{de}$ | Disruption start / end time | s |
| $B^{dis} \subset B$ | Set of disrupted blocks | — |
| $h$ | Minimum headway time between trains | s |
| $dwell^{\min}, dwell^{\max}$ | Min / max dwell times at stations | s |
| $\tau^{run}_{i,j,j+1}$ | Minimum running time between stations $j$ and $j{+}1$ for train $i$ | s |
| $sched^{arr}_{i,j}, sched^{dep}_{i,j}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure times | s |
| $E_a, E_b, E_c$ | Energy coefficients (drag, auxiliary, regen) | — |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) | — |
| $dir_i \in \{+1,-1\}$ | Travel direction of train $i$ | — |
| $v_p, v_p^2$ | Breakpoint $p$: speed value and its square | km/h, (km/h)² |
| $a_p, a_p^2$ | Breakpoint $p$: acceleration value and its square | m/s², (m/s²)² |
| $same_{i,i',j}$ | 1 if trains $i,i'$ both stop at station $j$ | binary |
| $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3$ | Objective weights for delay, energy, cancellation | — |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### Primary Variables
| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $arr_{i,j}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $j$ |
| $dep_{i,j}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ at station $j$ |
| $delay_{i,j}$ | $\geq 0$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $j$ |
| $v_{i,b,k}$ | $\geq 0$ | Speed of train $i$ on block $b$ at time $k$ |
| $pos_{i,b,k}$ | $\geq 0$ | Position of train $i$ on block $b$ at time $k$ |
| $acc_{i,b,k}$ | free | Acceleration of train $i$ on block $b$ at time $k$ |
| $z_{i,b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses block $b$ |
| $occ_{i,b,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ occupies block $b$ at time $k$ |
| $w_{i,b,r}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses route $r$ on block $b$ |
| $ord_{i,i',b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $i'$ on block $b$ |
| $e_i$ | $\geq 0$ | Total energy consumption of train $i$ |
| $cancel_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $reroute_{i,b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted on block $b$ |

### Auxiliary Variables (for linearization)
| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $sv_{i,b,k}$ | $\geq 0$ | Piecewise-linear approximation of $v_{i,b,k}^2$ |
| $sa_{i,b,k}$ | $\geq 0$ | Piecewise-linear approximation of $acc_{i,b,k}^2$ |
| $\lambda^v_{i,b,k,p}$ | $\geq 0$ | SOS2 weight for breakpoint $p$ (speed²) |
| $\lambda^a_{i,b,k,p}$ | $\geq 0$ | SOS2 weight for breakpoint $p$ (accel²) |

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min Z \;=\; \alpha_1 \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{j \in J} delay_{i,j} \;+\; \alpha_2 \sum_{i \in I} e_i \;+\; \alpha_3 \sum_{i \in I} cancel_i
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Delay Definition
$$
delay_{i,j} \;\geq\; arr_{i,j} - sched^{arr}_{i,j} \quad \forall i \in I,\; j \in J
$$
$$
delay_{i,j} \;\geq\; 0 \quad \forall i \in I,\; j \in J
$$

### 6.2 Dwell Time Bounds (intermediate stations)
$$
dwell^{\min} \;\leq\; dep_{i,j} - arr_{i,j} \;\leq\; dwell^{\max} \quad \forall i \in I,\; j \in J \setminus \{j_{first}, j_{last}\}
$$

### 6.3 Running Time Consistency
$$
arr_{i,j+1} \;\geq\; dep_{i,j} + \tau^{run}_{i,j,j+1} \quad \forall i \in I,\; j \in J \setminus \{j_{last}\}
$$

### 6.4 Speed Limits
$$
V_{\min} \cdot z_{i,b} \;\leq\; v_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; V_{\max} \cdot z_{i,b} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### 6.5 Train Dynamics (Position Update — Linear)
$$
pos_{i,b,k+1} \;=\; pos_{i,b,k} + v_{i,b,k} \cdot \Delta t + 0.5 \cdot acc_{i,b,k} \cdot \Delta t^2 \quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### 6.6 Acceleration Limits
$$
-d_{\max} \cdot z_{i,b} \;\leq\; acc_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; a_{\max} \cdot z_{i,b} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### 6.7 Block Traversal (sufficient distance covered)
$$
\sum_{k \in K} v_{i,b,k} \cdot \Delta t \;\geq\; L_b \cdot z_{i,b} \quad \forall i,b
$$

### 6.8 Position Bounds
$$
0 \;\leq\; pos_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; L_b \cdot z_{i,b} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### 6.9 Time-Indexed Occupancy Link
$$
occ_{i,b,k} \;\geq\; \frac{pos_{i,b,k}}{L_b} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
$$
occ_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; z_{i,b} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### 6.10 Block Occupancy Conflict (at most one train per block per time)
$$
\sum_{i \in I} occ_{i,b,k} \;\leq\; 1 \quad \forall b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

### 6.11 Ordering Consistency on Shared Blocks
$$
ord_{i,i',b} + ord_{i',i,b} \;=\; 1 \quad \forall i \neq i',\; b \in B
$$

### 6.12 Headway at Stations
$$
arr_{i,j} - dep_{i',j} \;\geq\; h \cdot (1 - ord_{i,i',j}) - M \cdot (1 - same_{i,i',j}) \quad \forall i \neq i',\; j \in J
$$

### 6.13 Disruption Constraint (no entry into disrupted blocks during window)
$$
z_{i,b} \;=\; 0 \quad \forall i \in I,\; b \in B^{dis},\; k \in K : t^{ds} \leq k \Delta t \leq t^{de}
$$

### 6.14 Rerouting Constraint
$$
reroute_{i,b} \;\leq\; z_{i,b} \quad \forall i,b
$$
$$
\sum_{r \in R^{alt}} w_{i,b,r} \;\geq\; reroute_{i,b} \quad \forall i,b
$$
$$
\sum_{r \in R} w_{i,b,r} \;=\; z_{i,b} \quad \forall i,b
$$

### 6.15 Energy Consumption (with linearized squared terms)
$$
e_i \;=\; \sum_{b \in B}\sum_{k \in K} \Big( E_a \cdot sv_{i,b,k} + E_b \cdot sa_{i,b,k} + E_c \cdot v_{i,b,k} \Big) \cdot \Delta t \quad \forall i
$$

### 6.16 Cancellation Logic
$$
z_{i,b} \;\leq\; 1 - cancel_i \quad \forall i,b
$$
$$
arr_{i,j} \;\leq\; M \cdot (1 - cancel_i) \quad \forall i,j
$$
$$
dep_{i,j} \;\leq\; M \cdot (1 - cancel_i) \quad \forall i,j
$$

### 6.17 Route Continuity (adjacent blocks must be used consistently)
$$
z_{i,b} \;\leq\; z_{i,b-1} + z_{i,b+1} \quad \forall i,\; b \in B \setminus \{b_{first}, b_{last}\}
$$

### 6.18 Initial and Final Conditions
$$
pos_{i,b_{first},0} \;=\; 0 \quad \forall i
$$
$$
pos_{i,b_{last},|K|} \;=\; L_{b_{last}} \cdot z_{i,b_{last}} \quad \forall i
$$

---

## 7. Linearization of Nonlinear Terms

### 7.1 Piecewise Linear Approximation of $v^2$

For each $(i,b,k)$, introduce SOS2 variables $\lambda^v_{i,b,k,p} \geq 0$:

$$
\sum_{p \in P^v} \lambda^v_{i,b,k,p} \;=\; z_{i,b} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
$$
v_{i,b,k} \;=\; \sum_{p \in P^v} \lambda^v_{i,b,k,p} \cdot v_p \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
$$
sv_{i,b,k} \;=\; \sum_{p \in P^v} \lambda^v_{i,b,k,p} \cdot v_p^2 \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
$$
\text{SOS2: } \{\lambda^v_{i,b,k,p}\}_{p \in P^v} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### 7.2 Piecewise Linear Approximation of $acc^2$

Similarly for acceleration:

$$
\sum_{p \in P^a} \lambda^a_{i,b,k,p} \;=\; z_{i,b} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
$$
acc_{i,b,k} \;=\; \sum_{p \in P^a} \lambda^a_{i,b,k,p} \cdot a_p \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
$$
sa_{i,b,k} \;=\; \sum_{p \in P^a} \lambda^a_{i,b,k,p} \cdot a_p^2 \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
$$
\text{SOS2: } \{\lambda^a_{i,b,k,p}\}_{p \in P^a} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$

> **Note:** SOS2 (Special Ordered Set of Type 2) constraints ensure that at most two adjacent $\lambda$ values are nonzero, which guarantees a valid piecewise-linear interpolation. Modern MILP solvers (CPLEX, Gurobi, SCIP) handle these natively.

---

## 8. Explanation of Model Elements

### 8.1 Objective Function
The objective balances three competing goals:
- **Delay minimization** ($\alpha_1$): Reduces passenger wait times and schedule disruption.
- **Energy efficiency** ($\alpha_2$): Promotes eco-driving via smooth speed profiles.
- **Service preservation** ($\alpha_3$): Penalizes cancellations to maintain service availability.

### 8.2 Temporal and Spatial Discretization
- **Time discretization** ($\Delta t$, set $K$): Enables time-indexed conflict detection and energy accumulation.
- **Block discretization** (set $B$): Reflects railway signaling sections; each block can host at most one train at a time.

### 8.3 Train Dynamics (Constraints 6.5–6.8)
The kinematic equations are kept **linear** by treating $\Delta t$ as a parameter. Position evolves via the standard motion equation $s_{k+1} = s_k + v_k \Delta t + \tfrac{1}{2} a_k \Delta t^2$. Speed and acceleration are bounded by physical and safety limits.

### 8.4 Conflict Resolution (Constraints 6.9–6.12)
- **Time-indexed occupancy** ($occ_{i,b,k}$) prevents simultaneous block usage, handling both same-direction and bidirectional (rerouted) conflicts uniformly.
- **Ordering variables** ($ord_{i,i',b}$) enforce a consistent precedence between any two trains sharing infrastructure.
- **Station headway** ensures safe separation during dwell operations.

### 8.5 Disruption Handling (Constraint 6.13)
During the disruption window $[t^{ds}, t^{de}]$, no train may occupy a disrupted block. This forces the optimizer to either **reroute** (using $reroute_{i,b}$) or **delay/cancel** trains.

### 8.6 Rerouting Logic (Constraint 6.14)
Rerouting activates an alternative route $r \in R^{alt}$ (typically the opposite track in bidirectional single-track operation). The constraint $\sum_r w_{i,b,r} = z_{i,b}$ ensures exactly one route is selected per used block.

### 8.7 Energy Model (Constraint 6.15)
The quadratic energy function $E_a v^2 + E_b a^2 + E_c v$ captures:
- **Aerodynamic drag** ($E_a v^2$): Dominant at high speed.
- **Auxiliary / inertial losses** ($E_b a^2$): Penalizes aggressive acceleration.
- **Regenerative / baseline** ($E_c v$): Proportional to distance traveled.

Piecewise-linear approximation preserves convexity and solver efficiency.

### 8.8 Cancellation Logic (Constraint 6.16)
If $cancel_i = 1$, all block occupancies and timing variables are forced to zero (relaxed via big-M), effectively removing the train from the network.

### 8.9 Route Continuity (Constraint 6.17)
Prevents "teleportation": a train cannot occupy a block without also occupying an adjacent block, ensuring physically feasible paths.

### 8.10 Linearization Strategy
The only nonlinearities are $v^2$ and $acc^2$ in the energy model. Both are **convex** functions, making piecewise-linear approximation with SOS2 variables an exact (in the limit) and solver-friendly linearization. No McCormick envelopes are needed because no bilinear products of distinct continuous variables appear.

---

## 9. Summary of Model Properties

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Type** | Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP) |
| **Continuous variables** | $arr, dep, delay, v, pos, acc, e_i, sv, sa, \lambda$ |
| **Binary variables** | $z, occ, w, ord, cancel, reroute$ |
| **Nonlinear terms** | None (all linearized) |
| **Solver compatibility** | CPLEX, Gurobi, SCIP, Xpress |

Text:
# Passenger-Oriented Real-Time Train Rescheduling MILP

## 1. Problem description and assumptions

We consider a single urban rail transit line with stations $S = \{1,\dots,N_s\}$ and trains $I=\{1,\dots,N_t\}$ operating in one direction. The planning (prediction) horizon is divided into time intervals $K=\{1,\dots,N_k\}$ of equal length $\Delta t$; passenger demand is piecewise constant per interval (Assumption A1). Train composition is flexible: each train is formed of $n_i \in \{1,\dots,\bar n\}$ coupled train units (Assumption A2). Rolling stock circulation is captured by requiring that the number of units departing the terminal equals the fleet size and units are conserved at the depot (Assumption A3). Trains may be skipped/cancelled (binary $x$). All data are deterministic over the horizon (Assumption A4). Headway, running-time, and dwell-time bounds reflect infrastructure limits.

### Sets and parameters
- $a^-_{i,k}, a^+_{i,k}$: earliest/latest departure time of train $i$ at station 1 in interval $k$ (from nominal timetable + protection level).
- $r_{i,s}$: minimum running time station $s\to s+1$ for train $i$; $\bar r_{i,s}$: maximum.
- $\underline d, \bar d$: minimum/maximum dwell time at a station.
- $h_{\min}, h_{\max}$: min/max headway between consecutive trains at a station.
- $C$: capacity of one train unit; $B_s$: platform capacity at station $s$.
- $D_{s,k}$: passengers arriving at station $s$ during interval $k$.
- $c_1$: energy/cost per train-unit-km; $c_2$: weight on passenger waiting time; $c_3$: weight on deviation from nominal timetable.
- $u_{i,s}$: binary, train $i$ stops at station $s$ (fixed by stopping plan, Assumption A5).
- $M$: big constant.

### Decision variables
- $x_{i,k}\in\{0,1\}$: train $i$ departs in interval $k$ (each train departs exactly once).
- $n_{i}\in\{1,\dots,\bar n\}$: number of units of train $i$ (integer).
- $d_{i,s}\ge 0$: departure time of train $i$ from station $s$; $w_{i,s}\ge0$: dwell time.
- $b_{i,s}\ge0$: passengers boarding train $i$ at station $s$.
- $q_{s,k}\ge0$: passengers left waiting at station $s$ at end of interval $k$.
- $y_{i,s}\ge0$: load of train $i$ on section $(s,s+1)$.

## 2. Objective function

$$
\min\; Z=\underbrace{c_1\sum_{i}\sum_{s} n_i\, r_{i,s}}_{\text{operation cost}}
+\underbrace{c_2\sum_{s}\sum_{k}\Delta t\; q_{s,k}}_{\text{passenger waiting time}}
+\underbrace{c_3\sum_{i}\big(d_{i,1}-d^{nom}_{i,1}\big)^{+}}_{\text{deviation, linearized}}
$$

Linearization of deviation: introduce $dev_i\ge0$ with
$$
dev_i \ge d_{i,1}-d^{nom}_{i,1},\qquad dev_i\ge 0 .
$$

## 3. Constraints

**Departure scheduling (each train departs once, within its slot):**
$$
\sum_{k\in K} x_{i,k}=1 \quad \forall i
$$
$$
d_{i,1}\ge \sum_k x_{i,k}\, a^-_{i,k},\qquad d_{i,1}\le \sum_k x_{i,k}\, a^+_{i,k} \quad \forall i
$$

**Running and dwell times:**
$$
d_{i,s+1}=d_{i,s}+w_{i,s}+r_{i,s} \quad \forall i,\ s<N_s
$$
$$
\underline d\, u_{i,s}\le w_{i,s}\le \bar d\, u_{i,s}\quad \forall i,s
$$

**Headway (safety) between consecutive trains at each station:**
$$
d_{i+1,s}-d_{i,s}\ge h_{\min}\quad \forall i<N_t,\ s
$$
$$
d_{i+1,s}-d_{i,s}\le h_{\max}+M(1-\text{order}_{i,s})\quad \forall i<N_t,\ s
$$
(Train order is fixed by index; Assumption A6. If order is free, add ordering binaries $o_{i,s}$ and big-M constraints.)

**Passenger flow balance at stations:**
$$
q_{s,k}=q_{s,k-1}+D_{s,k}-\sum_i \beta_{i,s,k}\quad \forall s,k
$$
where $\beta_{i,s,k}\ge0$ = passengers boarding train $i$ at $s$ who arrived in interval $k$, linked by:
$$
\beta_{i,s,k}\le D_{s,k}+q_{s,k-1},\qquad \sum_k \beta_{i,s,k}=b_{i,s}
$$
and boarding only when the train stops and departs in the corresponding interval:
$$
b_{i,s}\le M\, u_{i,s}
$$

**Boarding limited by remaining capacity (flexible composition):**
$$
b_{i,s}\le \big(C\, n_i - y_{i,s-1}\big) + M(1-u_{i,s}) \quad \forall i,s
$$

**Sectional load conservation:**
$$
y_{i,s}=y_{i,s-1}+b_{i,s}-\gamma_{i,s}\quad \forall i,s
$$
where $\gamma_{i,s}\ge0$ = alighting passengers, bounded by load:
$$
\gamma_{i,s}\le y_{i,s-1},\qquad \gamma_{i,s}\le M\, u_{i,s}
$$
$$
y_{i,0}=0,\qquad y_{i,N_s}=0 \quad \forall i
$$

**Capacity and platform limits:**
$$
y_{i,s}\le C\, n_i \quad \forall i,s
$$
$$
q_{s,k}+\sum_{i:\,d_{i,s}\in[k\Delta t,(k+1)\Delta t)} b_{i,s}\le B_s \quad \forall s,k
$$

**Rolling stock circulation (unit conservation):**
$$
\sum_i n_i \le N^{fleet}
$$
$$
n_i = n_{i-1} \quad \text{for trains reusing the same physical units (fixed circulation pairs, A3)}
$$
More generally, with circulation binary $z_{i,j}\in\{0,1\}$ (train $j$ is formed from units of train $i$ after turnaround time $\tau$):
$$
\sum_j z_{i,j}\le n_i,\qquad \sum_i z_{i,j}\le n_j \quad \forall i,j
$$
$$
d_{j,1}\ge d_{i,N_s}+\tau - M(1-z_{i,j}) \quad \forall i,j
$$

**Variable domains:**
$$
x_{i,k},u_{i,s},z_{i,j}\in\{0,1\};\quad n_i\in\mathbb Z,\ 1\le n_i\le \bar n;\quad d,w,b,q,y,\beta,\gamma,dev\ge0
$$

## 4. Remarks

- With integer variables fixed (by the LSTM in the learning-based MPC framework), the remaining problem in $(d,w,b,q,y,\beta,\gamma)$ is a linear program (LP), guaranteeing feasibility of the timetable given composition and circulation decisions.
- All constraints are linear; the model is a complete MILP solvable by branch-and-bound, or as an LP inside the proposed deep-learning-based MPC when binaries $x, n, z$ are predicted online.

Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

Below is the selected MILP model. It jointly decides **retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellations, and speed-profile selection** for trains operating on a double-track high-speed line affected by a partial segment blockage, while explicitly handling bidirectional single-track conflicts and station platform capacity.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t, t'$ |
| $K$ | Set of stations, $K=\{1,2,\dots,|K|\}$, ordered along the line |
| $S$ | Set of segments, $S=\{1,2,\dots,|S|\}$; segment $s$ connects station $s$ to $s+1$ |
| $P$ | Set of precomputed speed profiles, indexed by $p$ |
| $\mathcal{T}_r=\{1,2\}$ | Set of tracks (1 = nominal, 2 = opposite) |
| $\mathcal{H}$ | Discrete time horizon for station-capacity indexing, $\tau \in \mathcal{H}$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $TT_{t,k}$ | Target (planned) arrival time of train $t$ at station $k$ |
| $TD_{t,k}$ | Target (planned) departure time of train $t$ at station $k$ |
| $\underline{dw}_{t,k},\overline{dw}_{t,k}$ | Min/max dwell time of train $t$ at station $k$ |
| $H_s$ | Minimum headway on segment $s$ (same direction) |
| $H^{opp}_s$ | Minimum headway on segment $s$ (bidirectional, single track), $H^{opp}_s \ge H_s$ |
| $H^{st}_k$ | Minimum departure headway at station $k$ |
| $Cap_k$ | Number of platforms at station $k$ |
| $t^{ds}, t^{de}$ | Disruption start/end times |
| $B_s \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if segment $s$ has a blocked track during $[t^{ds},t^{de}]$ |
| $rt_{s,p}$ | Running time on segment $s$ under profile $p$ |
| $en_{s,p}$ | Energy consumption on segment $s$ under profile $p$ |
| $\alpha,\beta,\gamma \ge 0$ | Weights for delay, energy, and cancellation |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $a_{t,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $k$ |
| $d_{t,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Actual departure time of train $t$ at station $k$ |
| $w_{t,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Running time of train $t$ on segment $s$ |
| $e_{t,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Energy consumed by train $t$ on segment $s$ |
| $\Delta_{t,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Arrival delay of train $t$ at station $k$ |
| $y_{t,t',s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ exits segment $s$ before train $t'$ (with required headway) |
| $r_{t,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses the **opposite** track on segment $s$ |
| $\delta_{t,t',s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if trains $t$ and $t'$ use **different** tracks on segment $s$ (XOR of $r$) |
| $c_t$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled |
| $z_{t,s,p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if speed profile $p$ is selected for train $t$ on segment $s$ |
| $x_{t,k,\tau}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ occupies a platform at station $k$ at discrete time $\tau$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \alpha \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{k\in K}\Delta_{t,k} \;+\; \beta \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S} e_{t,s} \;+\; \gamma \sum_{t\in T} c_t
$$

The three terms capture **(i)** total passenger delay, **(ii)** total energy consumption, and **(iii)** total cancellation penalty.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Speed-Profile Selection and Linking

**(C1) Exactly one profile per active train-segment:**
$$
\sum_{p\in P} z_{t,s,p} \;=\; 1 - c_t \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S
$$

**(C2) Running time equals the chosen profile's running time:**
$$
w_{t,s} \;=\; \sum_{p\in P} rt_{s,p}\, z_{t,s,p} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S
$$

**(C3) Energy equals the chosen profile's energy:**
$$
e_{t,s} \;=\; \sum_{p\in P} en_{s,p}\, z_{t,s,p} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S
$$

### 5.2 Timetable Feasibility (Retiming)

**(C4) Running-time linking between consecutive stations** (relaxed if cancelled):
$$
-M(1-c_t) \;\le\; a_{t,s+1} - d_{t,s} - w_{t,s} \;\le\; M(1-c_t) \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S
$$

**(C5) Dwell time at intermediate stations:**
$$
\underline{dw}_{t,k} \;\le\; d_{t,k} - a_{t,k} \;\le\; \overline{dw}_{t,k} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; k\in K\setminus\{1,|K|\}
$$

**(C6) Origin departure cannot be earlier than planned:**
$$
d_{t,1} \;\ge\; TD_{t,1} - M\,c_t \qquad \forall t\in T
$$

**(C7) Delay definition:**
$$
\Delta_{t,k} \;\ge\; a_{t,k} - TT_{t,k} - M\,c_t,\qquad \Delta_{t,k}\ge 0 \qquad \forall t\in T,\; k\in K
$$

### 5.3 Disruption Window — Blocked Track Forbids Nominal Use

For every blocked segment $s$ ($B_s=1$), a non-cancelled train that traverses $s$ during $[t^{ds},t^{de}]$ must use the opposite track. We model this with two auxiliary binaries $b^{bef}_{t,s}, b^{aft}_{t,s}\in\{0,1\}$ indicating whether the train clears $s$ before the disruption or enters after it:

$$
a_{t,s+1} \;\le\; t^{ds} + M(1-b^{bef}_{t,s}) + M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,\; s: B_s=1
$$
$$
d_{t,s} \;\ge\; t^{de} - M(1-b^{aft}_{t,s}) - M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,\; s: B_s=1
$$
$$
b^{bef}_{t,s} + b^{aft}_{t,s} \;\ge\; 1 - r_{t,s} \qquad \forall t,\; s: B_s=1
$$

If $r_{t,s}=0$ (uses nominal track), the train must satisfy *both* $a_{t,s+1}\le t^{ds}$ *and* $d_{t,s}\ge t^{de}$, which is infeasible — forcing $r_{t,s}=1$ whenever the train is on $s$ during the disruption.

### 5.4 Rerouting — Bidirectional Single-Track Conflict Detection

**(C8) XOR linearization of "different tracks":**
$$
\delta_{t,t',s} \;\ge\; r_{t,s} - r_{t',s} \qquad \forall t<t',\; s\in S
$$
$$
\delta_{t,t',s} \;\ge\; r_{t',s} - r_{t,s} \qquad \forall t<t',\; s\in S
$$
$$
\delta_{t,t',s} \;\le\; r_{t,s} + r_{t',s} \qquad \forall t<t',\; s\in S
$$
$$
\delta_{t,t',s} \;\le\; 2 - r_{t,s} - r_{t',s} \qquad \forall t<t',\; s\in S
$$

### 5.5 Headway Constraints (Reordering)

**(C9) Segment headway — same track vs. bidirectional in one inequality:**
$$
a_{t,s+1} - a_{t',s+1} \;\ge\; H_s + (H^{opp}_s - H_s)\,\delta_{t,t',s} \;-\; M(1-y_{t,t',s}) \;-\; M(c_t+c_{t'}) \quad \forall t<t',\; s
$$
$$
a_{t',s+1} - a_{t,s+1} \;\ge\; H_s + (H^{opp}_s - H_s)\,\delta_{t,t',s} \;-\; M\,y_{t,t',s} \;-\; M(c_t+c_{t'}) \quad \forall t<t',\; s
$$

The product $(H^{opp}_s-H_s)\delta_{t,t',s}$ is linear because $H^{opp}_s-H_s$ is a constant. The headway is $H_s$ when both trains share a track ($\delta=0$) and $H^{opp}_s$ when they use different tracks ($\delta=1$, i.e., bidirectional single-track operation).

**(C10) Station departure headway:**
$$
d_{t,k} - d_{t',k} \;\ge\; H^{st}_k - M(1-y^{st}_{t,t',k}) - M(c_t+c_{t'}) \qquad \forall t<t',\; k
$$
$$
d_{t',k} - d_{t,k} \;\ge\; H^{st}_k - M\,y^{st}_{t,t',k} - M(c_t+c_{t'}) \qquad \forall t<t',\; k
$$
with $y^{st}_{t,t',k}\in\{0,1\}$.

### 5.6 Station Capacity (Platform Occupation)

**(C11) Linking platform-occupation indicator to arrival/departure:**
$$
a_{t,k} \;\le\; \tau + M(1-x_{t,k,\tau}) + M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,k,\tau
$$
$$
d_{t,k} \;\ge\; \tau - M(1-x_{t,k,\tau}) - M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,k,\tau
$$

**(C12) Platform capacity:**
$$
\sum_{t\in T} x_{t,k,\tau} \;\le\; Cap_k \qquad \forall k\in K,\; \tau\in\mathcal{H}
$$

### 5.7 Cancellation Consistency

**(C13) Cancelled trains perform no movement:**
$$
a_{t,k} \;\le\; M(1-c_t),\qquad d_{t,k} \;\le\; M(1-c_t) \qquad \forall t\in T,\; k\in K
$$

### 5.8 Variable Domains

$$
a_{t,k},\, d_{t,k},\, w_{t,s},\, e_{t,s},\, \Delta_{t,k} \;\ge\; 0
$$
$$
y_{t,t',s},\, y^{st}_{t,t',k},\, r_{t,s},\, \delta_{t,t',s},\, c_t,\, z_{t,s,p},\, b^{bef}_{t,s},\, b^{aft}_{t,s},\, x_{t,k,\tau} \;\in\; \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

**Retiming** is handled by the continuous variables $a_{t,k}, d_{t,k}$ constrained by (C4)–(C7). They shift each train's arrival and departure at every station while respecting minimum and maximum dwell times and the planned origin departure.

**Reordering** is captured by the binary variables $y_{t,t',s}$ (and $y^{st}_{t,t',k}$). For each pair of trains on each segment, exactly one ordering is selected, and the headway constraints (C9)–(C10) enforce that whichever train is second waits at least $H_s$ (or $H^{opp}_s$) after the first one clears the block.

**Rerouting** is modeled by $r_{t,s}$. The disruption constraints in §5.3 force $r_{t,s}=1$ for any non-cancelled train whose traversal of a blocked segment overlaps $[t^{ds},t^{de}]$. The XOR variables $\delta_{t,t',s}$ then detect when two trains use different tracks on the same segment, automatically upgrading the headway to the larger bidirectional value $H^{opp}_s$ in (C9).

**Cancellations** are represented by $c_t$. When $c_t=1$, all running-time, headway, and platform constraints for that train are relaxed via the $M\,c_t$ terms, and (C13) forces its times to zero. The objective penalizes each cancellation with weight $\gamma$.

**Speed-profile selection** is performed by $z_{t,s,p}$. Exactly one profile is chosen per active train-segment (C1), and the running time $w_{t,s}$ and energy $e_{t,s}$ are computed as convex combinations of profile parameters (C2)–(C3). Because $z$ is binary, this is a pure linear link between discrete profile choice and continuous timetable variables.

**Station capacity** uses time-indexed binaries $x_{t,k,\tau}$ (C11)–(C12). Each train "occupies" station $k$ during every discrete time $\tau$ between its arrival and departure, and the sum over trains at any $(\tau,k)$ cannot exceed the number of platforms $Cap_k$.

**Linearization notes.** All nonlinear-looking expressions are in fact linear: the headway term $(H^{opp}_s-H_s)\delta_{t,t',s}$ multiplies a constant by a binary; the XOR in (C8) is the standard four-inequality linearization; and the disruption disjunction in §5.3 is handled by the auxiliary binaries $b^{bef}_{t,s}, b^{aft}_{t,s}$. The only "big family" of variables is $x_{t,k,\tau}$, which can be reduced by aggregating $\tau$ into coarser buckets or replaced by SOS2 / cutting-plane formulations if the horizon is large.

---

## 7. Assumptions

1. **Double-track line** with one track per nominal direction; rerouting uses the opposite track on blocked segments.
2. **Discrete speed profiles** are precomputed offline (e.g., via optimal control for the TSMP) and indexed by $p\in P$, each with a known running time $rt_{s,p}$ and energy $en_{s,p}$.
3. **Single blockage** affecting one or more consecutive segments during a known time window $[t^{ds},t^{de}]$.
4. **Trains cannot pass each other** on a single track, hence the larger bidirectional headway $H^{opp}_s \ge H_s$.
5. **Dwell times** are bounded between $\underline{dw}_{t,k}$ and $\overline{dw}_{t,k}$.
6. **Cancellation** is permitted as a last resort, with penalty $\gamma$ per cancelled train.
7. **Time horizon** is discretized for platform-occupation variables; granularity can be tuned for tractability.
8. **Big-M** values can be tightened using $T^{max}$ and the disruption window bounds to strengthen the LP relaxation.

The resulting model is a mixed-integer linear program whose solution simultaneously prescribes, for every train, whether it runs or is cancelled, which speed profile it uses on each segment, whether it is rerouted to the opposite track through the disruption, and the precise arrival and departure times at every station — minimizing a weighted sum of delay, energy, and cancellation impact.
