Text:
# MILP Model for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockage

Below is a complete mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation. Since the source text does not specify every numerical detail, I introduce explicit modeling assumptions (clearly labeled) to make the model complete and linear.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $I$ | Set of trains scheduled during the planning horizon |
| $i,j \in I$ | Train indices |
| $S$ | Set of stations |
| $s \in S$ | Station index |
| $E$ | Set of segments (blocks) between consecutive stations |
| $e \in E$ | Segment index |
| $P$ | Set of precomputed discrete speed profiles for an inter-station run |
| $p \in P$ | Speed-profile index |
| $D \in \{up, down\}$ | Directions; $d_i$ is the (fixed) direction of train $i$ |
| $T$ | Planning horizon with continuous time (minutes) |

The blocked segment is $e^* \in E$, with disruption window $[t_0, t_1] \subset T$.

For each train $i$, let:
- $\text{orig}(i), \text{dest}(i) \in S$: origin and destination.
- $S_i \subseteq S$: stations served by train $i$ in order; $E_i \subseteq E$: consecutive inter-station segments traversed.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Parameter | Description (units) |
|---|---|
| $R^{p}_{i,e}$ | Running time (minutes) on segment $e$ for train $i$ under profile $p$ |
| $E^{p}_{i,e}$ | Energy consumption (kWh) on segment $e$ for train $i$ under profile $p$ |
| $\tau^{\min}_{i,s}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ (minutes) |
| $\tau^{\max}_{i,s}$ | Maximum dwell time (minutes) |
| $a^0_{i,s}, d^0_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival/departure times (input timetable) |
| $\alpha^{arr}_{i,s}, \alpha^{dep}_{i,s}$ | Per-minute delay penalty weights at station $s$ |
| $\beta^{arr}_{i,s}, \beta^{dep}_{i,s}$ | Per-minute earliness penalty weights |
| $\Pi_i$ | Cancellation penalty for train $i$ |
| $\lambda$ | Weight on energy consumption in objective |
| $h^{\text{seg}}_e$ | Minimum safe headway on a single-direction track of segment $e$ |
| $h^{\text{opp}}_e$ | Minimum safe headway between two trains moving in opposite directions on the same (opposite) track during rerouting |
| $h^{\text{sta}}_s$ | Minimum headway at station $s$ (departures / arrivals to the same platform or track) |
| $N^{\text{sta}}_s$ | Maximum number of trains simultaneously occupying station $s$ |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large constant (big-M) |
| $\delta^{d}_i$ | Direction of train $i$: $\delta^{d}_i = +1$ (up) or $-1$ (down) |
| $\text{dirBlocked} = -1$ | Direction of the blocked track on $e^*$ (assumed: down) |
| $y^{\max}$ | Maximum number of trains that may reroute on $e^*$ during $[t_0,t_1]$ (assumed: capacity of the shared opposite track, equal to 1 in the tightest case) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{i,s}$ | $\ge 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | $\ge 0$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $x^{p}_{i,e}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ on segment $e$ uses speed profile $p$ |
| $y_{i}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ reroutes onto the opposite track of $e^*$ (only meaningful if $i$ travels in the blocked direction on $e^*$) |
| $z_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $\sigma^{e}_{i,j}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ departs segment $e$ before train $j$ departs it (ordering on segment $e$, including the rerouted shared track) |
| $\theta^{e}_{i}$ | $\ge 0$ | Departure time of train $i$ from the start of segment $e$ |
| $\phi^{e}_{i}$ | $\ge 0$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at the end of segment $e$ |
| $w^{arr+}_{i,s}, w^{arr-}_{i,s}, w^{dep+}_{i,s}, w^{dep-}_{i,s}$ | $\ge 0$ | Positive/negative deviations from scheduled arrival/departure (used to linearize absolute values in the objective) |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{s \in S_i}
\Bigl(\alpha^{arr}_{i,s}\, w^{arr+}_{i,s} + \beta^{arr}_{i,s}\, w^{arr-}_{i,s}
     + \alpha^{dep}_{i,s}\, w^{dep+}_{i,s} + \beta^{dep}_{i,s}\, w^{dep-}_{i,s}\Bigr)
\;+\; \lambda \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{e \in E_i}\sum_{p \in P} E^{p}_{i,e}\, x^{p}_{i,e}
\;+\; \sum_{i \in I}\Pi_i\, z_i .
$$

The first term penalizes delays and earliness versus the planned timetable; the second minimizes energy; the third penalizes cancellations.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Deviation linearization

$$
a_{i,s} - a^0_{i,s} = w^{arr+}_{i,s} - w^{arr-}_{i,s},\qquad
d_{i,s} - d^0_{i,s} = w^{dep+}_{i,s} - w^{dep-}_{i,s},\quad \forall i,s.
\tag{1}
$$

### 5.2 Station dwell

$$
\tau^{\min}_{i,s}\, (1 - z_i) \le d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le \tau^{\max}_{i,s}\, (1 - z_i),\quad \forall i,s.
\tag{2}
$$

For cancelled trains, all station times are set identically later by (3).

### 5.3 Cancellation handling

$$
a_{i,s} = d_{i,s} = 0,\quad \forall s \in S_i,\;\forall i,\;\text{if } z_i = 1.
$$

Linearized:
$$
a_{i,s} \le M(1-z_i),\qquad d_{i,s} \le M(1-z_i),\quad \forall i,s.
\tag{3}
$$

### 5.4 Single speed-profile per train-segment

If train $i$ is not cancelled, exactly one speed profile is chosen on each segment it traverses; otherwise none.

$$
\sum_{p \in P} x^{p}_{i,e} = 1 - z_i,\quad \forall i,\;\forall e \in E_i.
\tag{4}
$$

### 5.5 Running-time coupling (timetable ↔ speed profile)

The departure time at the end of segment $e$ equals the departure time at its start plus the running time implied by the chosen profile:

$$
\phi^{e}_{i} = \theta^{e}_{i} + \sum_{p \in P} R^{p}_{i,e}\, x^{p}_{i,e},\quad \forall i,\;\forall e \in E_i.
\tag{5}
$$

Linkage with station times (departure from station $s$ equals departure time at start of next segment; arrival at station $s$ equals arrival at end of previous segment):

$$
\theta^{e_k}_i = d_{i,s_k},\qquad \phi^{e_k}_i = a_{i,s_{k+1}},\quad \forall i,\; e_k=(s_k,s_{k+1})\in E_i,
\tag{6}
$$
with consistency: $d_{i,\text{orig}(i)} = \theta^{e_1}_i$, $a_{i,\text{dest}(i)} = \phi^{e_{|E_i|}}_i$.

If cancelled: $\theta^{e}_i,\phi^{e}_i \le M(1-z_i)$.

### 5.6 Rerouting logic on the blocked segment $e^*$

Only trains whose direction $\delta^d_i$ equals the blocked direction $\text{dirBlocked}$ on $e^*$ may reroute; rerouting is permitted only if the train crosses $e^*$ during $[t_0,t_1]$; otherwise it must wait or use the normal (now blocked) track outside the window.

$$
y_i \le \mathbf{1}\{\delta^d_i = \text{dirBlocked}\},\quad \forall i.
\tag{7}
$$

If $y_i = 1$, the train must be on segment $e^*$ within $[t_0,t_1]$:

$$
\theta^{e^*}_i \ge t_0\, y_i - M(1-y_i),\qquad
\phi^{e^*}_i \le t_1\, y_i + M(1-y_i),\quad \forall i.
\tag{8}
$$

If $y_i = 0$ and the train must still cross $e^*$ in the blocked direction, it must do so outside $[t_0,t_1]$ (delay to recover):

$$
(\theta^{e^*}_i \ge t_1) \;\lor\; (\phi^{e^*}_i \le t_0),
$$
linearized as
$$
\theta^{e^*}_i \ge t_1 - M\, y_i,\qquad \phi^{e^*}_i \le t_0 + M\, y_i,\quad \forall i.
\tag{9}
$$

### 5.7 Conflict-free headway on every (directional) track resource

For any two non-cancelled trains $i,j$ that both traverse segment $e$ on the same physical track, exactly one ordering must hold, with the appropriate headway. Let $\text{trk}(i,e)\in\{\text{norm},\text{opp}\}$ denote the physical track used by $i$ on $e$. For rerouted trains on $e^*$, $\text{trk}(i,e^*)=\text{opp}$ if $y_i=1$, else norm. Trains in the non-blocked direction on $e^*$ use their normal track (no rerouting needed).

Define auxiliary binary $\gamma^{e}_{i,j} = 1$ if $i$ and $j$ share the same physical track on $e$. The constraints are:

$$
\sigma^{e}_{i,j} + \sigma^{e}_{j,i} = 1,\quad \forall i\neq j \text{ with both on }e.
\tag{10}
$$

Same-direction same-track headway:
$$
\theta^{e}_j \ge \theta^{e}_i + \sum_{p} R^{p}_{i,e} x^{p}_{i,e} + h^{\text{seg}}_e - M(1-\sigma^{e}_{i,j}) - M(1-\gamma^{e}_{i,j}),\quad \forall i,j.
\tag{11}
$$

Opposite-direction headway on a shared track during rerouting (only relevant on $e^*$ when one train is rerouted):

$$
\theta^{e^*}_j \ge \theta^{e^*}_i - h^{\text{opp}}_{e^*} + M(1-\sigma^{e^*}_{i,j}),\quad \forall i,j \text{ with } y_i y_j = 1,
\tag{12}
$$
and the symmetric version for the reverse ordering (linearized through $\sigma$).

### 5.8 Shared-track rerouting capacity on $e^*$

At most $y^{\max}$ rerouted trains may share the opposite track during any instant of $[t_0,t_1]$. Using time-indexed occupancy (assume discretized time $t\in\mathcal{T}$ with binary $\rho_{i,t}\in\{0,1\}$ indicating whether rerouted train $i$ occupies $e^*$ at time $t$):

$$
\sum_{i:\, \delta^d_i = \text{dirBlocked}} \rho_{i,t} \le y^{\max},\quad \forall t\in\mathcal{T}.
\tag{13}
$$

The $\rho_{i,t}$ are linked to the running times through (5); in a fully linear MILP they are produced via big-M discretization:

$$
\rho_{i,t} \ge \frac{(\theta^{e^*}_i - t) + (t - \theta^{e^*}_i)}{2M} \text{ (replaced by standard big-M disjunctions)}.
$$

(Equivalent, cleaner linearization: introduce auxiliary variables $u_i \ge \theta^{e^*}_i$, $v_i \ge \theta^{e^*}_i + \sum_p R^p_{i,e^*}x^p_{i,e^*}$, and add $\sum_i y_i \le y^{\max}$ as a conservative aggregate surrogate when running-time overlaps are preverified.)

### 5.9 Station capacity

Number of trains at station $s$ at any time bounded by $N^{\text{sta}}_s$ (enforced via pairwise headway $h^{\text{sta}}_s$ or time-indexed occupancy as in (13)):

$$
d_{i,s} \ge d_{j,s} + h^{\text{sta}}_s - M(1-\sigma^{s}_{i,j}),\quad \forall i\neq j, s.
\tag{14}
$$

### 5.10 Variable domains

$$
x^{p}_{i,e},\; y_i,\; z_i,\; \sigma^{e}_{i,j},\;\gamma^{e}_{i,j},\;\rho_{i,t} \in \{0,1\};
\quad a_{i,s},\, d_{i,s},\, \theta^{e}_i,\, \phi^{e}_i,\, w^{\cdot^{\pm}}_{i,s} \ge 0.
\tag{15}
$$

### 5.11 Horizon

$$
0 \le a_{i,s},\, d_{i,s} \le T^{\max},\quad \forall i,s.
\tag{16}
$$

---

## 6. Modeling Assumptions Made Explicit (since unspecified in the input)

1. **Discrete precomputed speed profiles.** Energy and running time depend only on the chosen profile $p$, so the product (running time) × $x$ and (energy) × $x$ remain linear.
2. **Single-track partial blockage.** The disruption renders only one track (one direction) of segment $e^*$ unavailable during $[t_0,t_1]$; rerouting uses the opposite track in a shared (bidirectional) manner.
3. **Cancellation is allowed**, with a fixed penalty; cancelled trains consume no resources and are removed from all sequencing constraints by $z_i$.
4. **Headways are constant** per resource type (segment same-direction, segment opposite-direction during rerouting, station).
5. **Rerouting capacity** $y^{\max}$ during $[t_0,t_1]$ is a fixed input; aggregated as $\sum_i y_i \le y^{\max}$ as a tractable surrogate for finer time-indexed constraints.
6. **Deviation penalties** $\alpha,\beta$ are separable and linear; absolute values are linearized via auxiliary $w^{\pm}$.
7. **No partial rerouting** of a single train (whole segment $e^*$ decision $y_i$).
8. **Train directions are fixed**; no reversal or coupling of trains.
9. **Big-M constants** $M$ are chosen large enough (e.g., $T^{\max}$) so that disjunctions are non-binding when the corresponding binary is 0.

---

This MILP jointly decides retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and the choice of energy-efficient speed profiles for each inter-station run, under the safety headways required when bidirectional trains share the rerouted track during the partial segment blockage.

Text:
# MILP Formulation for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Overview and Modeling Approach

The integrated TRSMP is formulated as a Mixed-Integer Linear Program on a **time–space network** in which space is discretized into track segments (blocks) and time is discretized into uniform intervals. The model jointly decides (i) retiming, reordering, rerouting, and cancellation decisions at the operational level, and (ii) speed profiles at the control level, while enforcing safety, blockage, and energy constraints.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$, ordered along the line |
| $K$ | Set of track segments, $k = 1, \dots, |K|$; segment $k$ connects station $k$ to $k+1$ |
| $B = \{N, R\}$ | Track types: $N$ = normal (original) track, $R$ = reverse (opposite) track |
| $I$ | Set of discrete time intervals, $i = 1, \dots, |I|$, each of length $\Delta t$ |
| $D \subseteq K$ | Index of the blocked segment |
| $\mathcal{W} = [\tau^{s}, \tau^{e}]$ | Disruption time window |
| $\mathcal{L}$ | Set of breakpoints for piecewise-linear energy approximation, $\ell = 1, \dots, |\mathcal{L}|$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $L_k$ | Length of segment $k$ | km |
| $v^{\max}, v^{\min}$ | Maximum / minimum operating speed | km/h |
| $a^{+}, a^{-}$ | Maximum traction / braking acceleration | km/h² |
| $\tau^{\min}_s, \tau^{\max}_s$ | Min / max dwell time at station $s$ | h |
| $h$ | Minimum safety headway time | h |
| $\bar{T}^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}, \bar{T}^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure time of train $t$ at $s$ | h |
| $c^{\text{d}}, c^{\text{e}}, c^{\text{c}}$ | Cost per hour of delay, per kWh of energy, per cancellation | – |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Davis-equation coefficients ($e = \alpha + \beta v + \gamma v^2$) | – |
| $v_\ell, e_\ell$ | Speed and energy breakpoints of piece $\ell$ | km/h, kWh |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large positive constant (big-$M$) | – |
| $\Delta t$ | Length of a time interval | h |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Train-Rescheduling Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Actual departure time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $x_{t,k,b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses track type $b$ on segment $k$ |
| $z_{t,t',k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ exits segment $k$ before train $t'$ |
| $\delta_t$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled |

### 4.2 Speed-Management Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $v_{t,k,i}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Speed of train $t$ on segment $k$ during interval $i$ (km/h) |
| $p_{t,k,i}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Position of train $t$ on segment $k$ at the end of interval $i$ (km) |
| $e_{t,k,i}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Energy consumed by train $t$ on segment $k$ during interval $i$ (kWh) |
| $y_{t,k,i}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ occupies segment $k$ during interval $i$ |

### 4.3 Auxiliary Variables (Piecewise-Linear Energy)

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $\lambda_{t,k,i,\ell}$ | $[0,1]$ | Convex weight of breakpoint $\ell$ for the energy function |

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total delay, energy consumption, and cancellations:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; c^{\text{d}} \!\!\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\!\!\Big[\big(\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s} - \bar{T}^{\text{arr}}_{t,s}\big)^{+} + \big(\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s} - \bar{T}^{\text{dep}}_{t,s}\big)^{+}\Big]
\;+\; c^{\text{e}} \!\!\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{i\in I} e_{t,k,i}
\;+\; c^{\text{c}} \sum_{t\in T} \delta_t
$$

where $(x)^{+} = \max\{0,x\}$. The first term penalizes arrival and departure delays beyond the schedule; the second term penalizes energy use; the third term penalizes cancellations.

---

## 6. Constraints

### A. Train-Rescheduling Constraints

**A1. Segment assignment (each non-cancelled train traverses each segment exactly once):**
$$
\sum_{b\in B} x_{t,k,b} \;=\; 1 - \delta_t \qquad \forall t\in T,\; k\in K
$$

**A2. Dwell-time window at stations:**
$$
\tau^{\min}_s (1-\delta_t) \;\leq\; \tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s} - \tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s} \;\leq\; \tau^{\max}_s (1-\delta_t) \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S
$$

**A3. Cancellation logic** (if cancelled, no arrival/departure is recorded):
$$
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s} \leq M(1-\delta_t), \quad \tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s} \leq M(1-\delta_t) \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S
$$

**A4. Ordering consistency on each segment:**
$$
z_{t,t',k} + z_{t',t,k} \;=\; \sum_{b\in B} x_{t,k,b}\, x_{t',k,b} \qquad \forall t,t'\in T,\; k\in K,\; t\neq t'
$$
(The right-hand side is linearized using auxiliary binaries $u_{t,t',k,b} \leq x_{t,k,b}$, $u_{t,t',k,b} \leq x_{t',k,b}$, $u_{t,t',k,b} \geq x_{t,k,b}+x_{t',k,b}-1$.)

---

### B. Train-Dynamics (Speed-Management) Constraints

**B1. Position update (Euler-discretized kinematics):**
$$
p_{t,k,i} \;=\; p_{t,k,i-1} + v_{t,k,i}\,\Delta t \qquad \forall t\in T,\; k\in K,\; i\in I
$$

**B2. Position bounds and segment occupation:**
$$
0 \;\leq\; p_{t,k,i} \;\leq\; L_k\, y_{t,k,i} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; k\in K,\; i\in I
$$

**B3. Link between segment occupation and assignment:**
$$
y_{t,k,i} \;\leq\; \sum_{b\in B} x_{t,k,b} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; k\in K,\; i\in I
$$

**B4. Speed limits:**
$$
v^{\min}\, y_{t,k,i} \;\leq\; v_{t,k,i} \;\leq\; v^{\max}\, y_{t,k,i} \qquad \forall t\in T,\; k\in K,\; i\in I
$$

**B5. Acceleration limits (linearized with big-$M$):**
$$
v_{t,k,i} - v_{t,k,i-1} \;\leq\; a^{+}\Delta t + M\big(2 - y_{t,k,i} - y_{t,k,i-1}\big) \qquad \forall t,k,i
$$
$$
v_{t,k,i-1} - v_{t,k,i} \;\leq\; a^{-}\Delta t + M\big(2 - y_{t,k,i} - y_{t,k,i-1}\big) \qquad \forall t,k,i
$$

**B6. Boundary conditions:**
$$
p_{t,1,0} = 0, \qquad p_{t,|K|,|I|} = L_{|K|} \qquad \forall t\in T
$$

---

### C. Linking Rescheduling and Speed Management

**C1. Arrival time at station $s$ from segment $k = s-1$:**
$$
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s} \;\geq\; i\,\Delta t - M\big(1 - y_{t,s-1,i}\big) \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S\setminus\{1\},\; i\in I
$$
$$
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,s} \;\leq\; i\,\Delta t + M\big(1 - y_{t,s-1,i}\big) \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S\setminus\{1\},\; i\in I
$$

**C2. Departure time at station $s$ to segment $k = s$:**
$$
\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s} \;\geq\; i\,\Delta t - M\big(1 - y_{t,s,i}\big) \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S\setminus\{|S|\},\; i\in I
$$
$$
\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,s} \;\leq\; i\,\Delta t + M\big(1 - y_{t,s,i}\big) \qquad \forall t\in T,\; s\in S\setminus\{|S|\},\; i\in I
$$

---

### D. Blockage and Rerouting Constraints

**D1. Blocked segment is unavailable on the normal track during the disruption window:**
$$
y_{t,d,i} = 0 \qquad \forall t\in T,\; d\in D,\; i\in I \text{ with } i\Delta t \in \mathcal{W}
$$

**D2. Rerouting to opposite track is mandatory for trains that would otherwise use the blocked track during $\mathcal{W}$:**
$$
x_{t,d,R} \;\geq\; 1 - \delta_t - M\!\sum_{i:\,i\Delta t\in\mathcal{W}}\!\!\big(1 - y_{t,d,i}\big) \qquad \forall t\in T,\; d\in D
$$

**D3. Rerouting is only permitted during the disruption window:**
$$
x_{t,d,R} \;\leq\; \sum_{i:\,i\Delta t\in\mathcal{W}} y_{t,d,i} + M\,\delta_t \qquad \forall t\in T,\; d\in D
$$

---

### E. Conflict-Resolution Constraints

**E1. Same-direction headway on segment $k$:**
$$
\tau^{\text{exit}}_{t',k} - \tau^{\text{exit}}_{t,k} \;\geq\; h - M\big(1 - z_{t,t',k}\big) - M\big(1 - x_{t,k,b}\big) - M\big(1 - x_{t',k,b}\big)
$$
for all $t,t'\in T$, $k\in K$, $b\in B$, where $\tau^{\text{exit}}_{t,k}$ is the time train $t$ leaves segment $k$ (linearized analogously to C1).

**E2. Bidirectional conflict on the opposite track (segment $d$, trains in opposite directions):**
$$
\tau^{\text{exit}}_{t',d} - \tau^{\text{exit}}_{t,d} \;\geq\; h - M\big(1 - z_{t,t',d}\big) - M\big(1 - x_{t,d,R}\big) - M\big(1 - x_{t',d,N}\big)
$$
for all $t,t'\in T$ with opposite nominal directions.

**E3. Track-capacity (single-track per direction):**
$$
\sum_{t\in T} y_{t,k,i} \;\leq\; 1 \qquad \forall k\in K,\; i\in I
$$

**E4. Mutual exclusion on the opposite track (no simultaneous occupation by trains in opposite directions):**
$$
y_{t,d,i} + y_{t',d,i} \;\leq\; 1 \qquad \forall t,t'\in T \text{ with opposite nominal directions},\; d\in D,\; i\in I
$$

---

### F. Energy Consumption (Piecewise-Linear Approximation)

The Davis equation $e(v) = \alpha + \beta v + \gamma v^{2}$ is approximated by a piecewise-linear function through breakpoints $(v_\ell, e_\ell)$:

**F1. Convex combination of breakpoints:**
$$
v_{t,k,i} = \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}} \lambda_{t,k,i,\ell}\, v_\ell, \qquad
e_{t,k,i} = \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}} \lambda_{t,k,i,\ell}\, e_\ell, \qquad
\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}} \lambda_{t,k,i,\ell} = 1 \qquad \forall t,k,i
$$

**F2. Adjacent-binary (SOS2) formulation:**
Introduce binaries $\mu_{t,k,i,\ell}\in\{0,1\}$ with $\sum_\ell \mu_{t,k,i,\ell}=1$ and at most two consecutive $\mu$'s may be 1, enforced via standard SOS2 constraints on $(\lambda_{t,k,i,\ell},\mu_{t,k,i,\ell})$.

---

### G. Initial / Final and Logical Constraints

**G1. Scheduled first departure (lower bound):**
$$
\tau^{\text{dep}}_{t,1} \;\geq\; \bar{T}^{\text{dep}}_{t,1} - M\delta_t \qquad \forall t\in T
$$

**G2. Scheduled last arrival (upper bound):**
$$
\tau^{\text{arr}}_{t,|S|} \;\leq\; \bar{T}^{\text{arr}}_{t,|S|} + M\delta_t + \text{max delay allowance} \qquad \forall t\in T
$$

**G3. Cancellation is the last resort** (optional, encourages rescheduling over cancellation):
$$
\delta_t \;\leq\; \delta_{t-1} + \delta_{t+1} \qquad \forall t\in T \text{ (interior trains)}
$$

---

## 7. Key Assumptions

1. **Bidirectional single-track line** with stations acting as passing loops; segments are uni-directional between stations.
2. **Partial blockage**: exactly one segment $d\in D$ is unavailable on its normal track during $\mathcal{W}$; the opposite track remains usable.
3. **Homogeneous rolling stock**: identical traction/braking characteristics and length for all trains (extension to heterogeneous fleets is straightforward by indexing parameters with $t$).
4. **Discretized time horizon**: $|I|$ intervals of length $\Delta t$ cover the planning window; finer $\Delta t$ improves accuracy at the cost of computational effort.
5. **Euler-discretized kinematics** with constant speed within each interval; this is exact for piecewise-constant speed profiles and a standard approximation otherwise.
6. **Davis-equation energy model**, convex in speed, approximated by a piecewise-linear function (assumption of regenerative braking disabled; otherwise add a regenerative term).
7. **No train-following conflicts within a single track-type block** beyond the headway $h$; this is enforced by E1 and E3.
8. **Cancellation is permitted** as a last-resort measure, but the model can be run with $\delta_t \equiv 0$ to forbid it.
9. **Deterministic disruption**: the blocked segment and time window are known in advance (real-time rolling-horizon extensions are possible).
10. **Dwell times are flexible** within $[\tau^{\min}_s, \tau^{\max}_s]$; fixed dwell times are obtained by setting $\tau^{\min}_s = \tau^{\max}_s$.

---

## 8. Notes on Linearization

- All products of binary variables (e.g., $x_{t,k,b}\,x_{t',k,b}$ in A4) are linearized with auxiliary binaries and big-$M$ constraints.
- The quadratic energy function $\gamma v^{2}$ is replaced by a piecewise-linear approximation (F1–F2), which is exact at the breakpoints and conservative in between.
- The indicator constraints (B5, D2, E1–E2) all use the standard big-$M$ technique; tightening $M$ via valid inequalities (e.g., $M = |I|\Delta t$) accelerates solution.
- The model is a **MILP** because the binaries $x_{t,k,b}$, $z_{t,t',k}$, $\delta_t$, $y_{t,k,i}$, $\mu_{t,k,i,\ell}$ are discrete while the remaining variables are continuous.

---

## 9. Summary

The MILP above produces, in a single optimization:

- a **conflict-free rescheduled timetable** ($\tau^{\text{arr}}, \tau^{\text{dep}}, x, z, \delta$),
- **executable speed profiles** ($v, p$) consistent with that timetable,
- **rerouting decisions** ($x_{t,d,R}=1$) for trains affected by the partial blockage,
- and the **minimum combined delay + energy + cancellation cost**.

The model explicitly captures the bidirectional conflicts that arise when rerouting to the opposite track (E2, E4), and tightly couples rescheduling with speed management through the position–time linking constraints (B1–B3, C1–C2), thereby guaranteeing that every operational decision is feasible at the control level.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

Below is a complete MILP formulation inspired by the described framework: a **global-optimum model** that handles **rerouting, reordering, and rescheduling simultaneously**, using **pair-wise delay variables** extended with **delay propagation**, in the style of Pellegrini et al. (2014, 2019).

---

## 1. Assumptions (explicitly stated)

- **A1 (Macroscopic infrastructure):** The network is a set of stations/cells connected by tracks; signals and block sections are aggregated.
- **A2 (Routes):** Each train has a finite set of feasible routes through each station; each route occupies a set of resources (track segments).
- **A3 (Safety):** Two trains may not occupy the same resource at the same time; a minimum headway time applies between consecutive occupancies (including safety-relevant overlaps behind stop signals, modeled as extra resource occupancy time).
- **A4 (Schedule):** Each train has a nominal timetable with minimum running times per route and minimum dwell times; scheduled stops are fixed.
- **A5 (Delays):** Secondary delays arise only from waiting for other trains (pair-wise interpretation) or from route-dependent running times; no stochastic disturbances during the optimization horizon.
- **A6 (Horizon):** A finite discrete horizon \([0, T]\) is considered; all decisions are made at the beginning (rolling horizon possible).
- **A7 (Objective):** Minimize total (weighted) arrival delay; weights allow prioritization.

---

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| \(T\!\!r\) | set of trains \(i\) |
| \(R_i\) | set of feasible routes for train \(i\) (concatenated through its path) |
| \(B\) | set of resources (track segments) \(b\) |
| \(B_{ir} \subseteq B\) | resources occupied by train \(i\) on route \(r\) |
| \(P_i\) | ordered set of stations on train \(i\)'s path |
| \(d^{sch}_i\) | scheduled arrival time of train \(i\) at its final destination |
| \(r^{min}_{ir}\) | minimum running time of train \(i\) using route \(r\) |
| \(w^{min}_i\) | minimum dwell time of train \(i\) |
| \(h_{bb'}\) | minimum headway between releases of resources \(b, b'\) (incl. overlap margins) |
| \(M\) | sufficiently large constant |
| \(W_i\) | delay weight of train \(i\) |

---

## 3. Variables

**Continuous:**
- \(a_i \ge 0\) — actual arrival time of train \(i\) at destination.
- \(\delta_i \ge 0\) — final delay of train \(i\): \(\delta_i = a_i - d^{sch}_i\).
- \(t^{rel}_{ib} \ge 0\) — release (exit) time of train \(i\) from resource \(b\).

**Binary:**
- \(x_{ir} \in \{0,1\}\) — 1 if train \(i\) uses route \(r \in R_i\).
- \(y_{ij} \in \{0,1\}\) — **pair-wise ordering variable**: 1 if train \(i\) passes resource \(b\) before train \(j\) (defined per conflicting resource pair \((i,j,b)\)).
- \(z_{ij} \in \{0,1\}\) — **pair-wise delay propagation variable**: 1 if train \(j\) waits for train \(i\) (i.e., \(j\)'s delay is caused by \(i\)).

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize total weighted final delay:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{i \in T\!\!r} W_i \, \delta_i
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Route selection — exactly one route per train:**

$$
\sum_{r \in R_i} x_{ir} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in T\!\!r
$$

**(C2) Arrival time definition (delay propagation along own path):**

$$
a_i \;\ge\; d^{sch}_i \qquad \forall i \in T\!\!r
$$

$$
a_i \;\ge\; \sum_{r \in R_i} x_{ir}\big(d^{sch}_i + r^{min}_{ir}\big) \;+\; \sum_{j \in T\!\!r, j \ne i} M \, z_{ji} \qquad \forall i \in T\!\!r
$$

i.e., train \(i\)'s arrival is at least its earliest possible arrival, plus \(M\) for every train it must wait for (pair-wise delay propagation).

**(C3) Delay definition:**

$$
\delta_i \;\ge\; a_i - d^{sch}_i \qquad \forall i \in T\!\!r
$$

**(C4) Link waiting variables to ordering variables** (a train can only wait for a train it follows on a shared resource):

$$
z_{ij} \;\le\; \sum_{b \in B_i \cap B_j} (1 - y_{ijb}) \qquad \forall i \ne j \in T\!\!r
$$

where \(y_{ijb} = 1\) means \(i\) exits \(b\) before \(j\); if \(j\) follows \(i\) somewhere, \(j\) may wait for \(i\).

**(C5) Resource occupancy — no overlap, with headway:**

For each resource \(b\) and each pair \(i \ne j\) with \(b \in B_{ir} \cap B_{jr}\) for some routes:

$$
t^{rel}_{jb} \;\ge\; t^{rel}_{ib} + h_{bb} - M(1 - y_{ijb}) - M(2 - x_{ir} - x_{jr}) \qquad \forall (i,r),(j,r'), b \in B_{ir}\cap B_{jr'}
$$

$$
t^{rel}_{ib} \;\ge\; t^{rel}_{jb} + h_{bb} - M\, y_{ijb} - M(2 - x_{ir} - x_{jr}) \qquad \forall (i,r),(j,r'), b \in B_{ir}\cap B_{jr'}
$$

(Headways for adjacent resources \(b, b'\) are enforced analogously with \(h_{bb'}\) on consecutive occupancy relations.)

**(C6) Route-dependent release times (running time consistency):**

$$
t^{rel}_{ib} \;\ge\; \sum_{r \in R_i:\, b \in B_{ir}} x_{ir} \cdot \tau^{entry}_{ir,b} \qquad \forall i, b
$$

where \(\tau^{entry}_{ir,b}\) is the earliest entry time of \(i\) into \(b\) on route \(r\) derived from the timetable (scheduled departure + minimum running/dwell times upstream).

**(C7) Consistency of ordering along a train's path (no overtaking unless a station allows it):**

$$
y_{ijb} \;\ge\; y_{ijb'} - 1 \qquad \forall i \ne j,\; \text{consecutive non-overtaking resources } b \to b'
$$

**(C8) Waiting implies delay propagation (logical link):**

$$
z_{ij} \;\ge\; y_{jib} + x_{ir} + x_{jr} - 2 - M(1 - w_{ijb}) \quad\text{(linearized big-M form)}
$$

or equivalently, with auxiliary \(w_{ijb} \in \{0,1\}\) ("\(j\) waits for \(i\) at \(b\)"):

$$
w_{ijb} \ge y_{jib} - 1 + x_{ir} + x_{jr} - 2, \qquad z_{ij} \ge w_{ijb} \quad \forall i \ne j, b
$$

**(C9) Variable domain:**

$$
a_i, \delta_i, t^{rel}_{ib} \ge 0; \qquad x_{ir}, y_{ijb}, z_{ij}, w_{ijb} \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Remarks

- **Sub-optimal variant (Stage 1):** Dropping constraints (C4), (C7), (C8) and fixing \(z_{ij}\) via only direct pair-wise waiting (no propagation) yields the fast, low-complexity model for rerouting + reordering described in the paper; its solution feeds the full model as a warm start or route-fixing (\(x_{ir}\) fixed) for Stage 2 rescheduling.
- **Safety overlaps** (Lindenmaier et al., 2022) are captured by inflating \(h_{bb}\) or adding overlap resources to \(B_{ir}\).
- **Complexity reduction:** The number of binaries is \(O(|T\!\!r|^2 |B|)\) rather than time-indexed, which — as claimed in the paper — gives favorable computational cost versus the reference model of Pellegrini et al. (2014), especially in complex scenarios.

Text:
# MILP Formulation for Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

## 1. Overview and Modeling Assumptions

The model below formalizes the **real-time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)** as a Mixed-Integer Linear Program that jointly handles **rerouting**, **reordering**, and **rescheduling** of trains in a disturbed traffic situation. The formulation extends the reference model of Pellegrini et al. (2014) with (i) pair-wise delay variables, (ii) explicit delay propagation, and (iii) safety-relevant overlap clearances.

**Modeling Assumptions** (clearly stated as such where the original paper leaves room):

1. Time is discretized on a continuous scale (seconds or minutes).
2. The railway network is represented at a **macroscopic level**: stations are nodes, inter-station track sections are blocks; signals are abstracted by block exits.
3. Each train has a predefined set of feasible alternative routes (route catalogue).
4. Trains have scheduled (timetabled) arrival/departure times at every station they stop at.
5. Conflicts occur only at stations (merging/diverging points) and at block entries/exits.
6. Minimum headway times between consecutive trains at each conflict point are known and constant.
7. Dwell times at stations are bounded below by a minimum value.
8. Running times on blocks are fixed (no energy-optimal driving inside the MILP).
9. The safety overlap is a fixed time margin that must elapse after a train vacates a block before another train may enter the block that depends on it.
10. Primary delays (external disturbances) are input parameters; secondary delays are decision-dependent.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j \in \mathcal{T}$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations (conflict / stop points), indexed by $s \in \mathcal{S}$ |
| $\mathcal{B}$ | Set of track blocks (sections), indexed by $b \in \mathcal{B}$ |
| $\mathcal{R}_i$ | Set of feasible alternative routes for train $i$, indexed by $r \in \mathcal{R}_i$ |
| $\mathcal{C}$ | Set of conflict points (subset of $\mathcal{S} \cup \mathcal{B}$), indexed by $c \in \mathcal{C}$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_i$ | Ordered sequence of stations served by train $i$ on its chosen route |
| $\mathcal{B}(s, s')$ | Set of blocks connecting station $s$ to station $s'$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $a_i^s$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ | min |
| $d_i^s$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ | min |
| $\tau_i^b$ | Nominal running time of train $i$ on block $b$ | min |
| $\theta_i^s$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ | min |
| $h_{ij}^c$ | Minimum headway time between trains $i$ and $j$ at conflict point $c$ (when $i$ precedes $j$) | min |
| $o^b$ | Safety overlap (clearance margin) behind block $b$ | min |
| $\pi_i^{b}$ | 1 if block $b$ is on train $i$'s nominal route, 0 otherwise | – |
| $\varphi_{i,r}^b$ | 1 if route $r$ of train $i$ traverses block $b$, 0 otherwise | – |
| $\psi_{i,r}^s$ | 1 if route $r$ of train $i$ stops at station $s$, 0 otherwise | – |
| $\Delta_i^{s,\text{prim}}$ | Primary (external) delay of train $i$ already known at station $s$ | min |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (Big-M) | min |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3$ | Weights for total delay, energy, and number of changed routes | – |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Routing variables
$$
x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; r \in \mathcal{R}_i
$$
1 if train $i$ is assigned route $r$, 0 otherwise.

$$
u_i^b \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; b \in \mathcal{B}
$$
1 if train $i$ uses block $b$ (auxiliary, defined by routing).

$$
v_i^s \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$
1 if train $i$ stops at station $s$ (auxiliary, defined by routing).

### 4.2 Ordering variables
$$
y_{ij}^c \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{T}^2,\; c \in \mathcal{C},\; i \neq j
$$
1 if train $i$ is ordered before train $j$ at conflict point $c$, 0 otherwise.

### 4.3 Timing variables
$$
A_i^s \ge 0, \quad D_i^s \ge 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$
Actual arrival and departure times of train $i$ at station $s$.

$$
T_i^b \ge 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; b \in \mathcal{B}
$$
Time at which train $i$ enters block $b$.

### 4.4 Delay variables
$$
\delta_i^s \ge 0, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$
Total (primary + secondary) delay of train $i$ at station $s$.

$$
\delta_{ij}^c \ge 0, \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{T}^2,\; c \in \mathcal{C},\; i \neq j
$$
Pair-wise delay: delay incurred by train $i$ because it waits for train $j$ at conflict point $c$.

---

## 5. Objective Function

The objective is to **minimize a weighted sum of total secondary delay, primary-delay propagation, rerouting cost, and energy consumption**:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; w_1 \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \delta_i^s}_{\text{total delay}} \;+\; w_2 \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} \tau_i^b \, u_i^b}_{\text{running time / energy proxy}} \;+\; w_3 \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_i \setminus \{r_i^{\text{nom}}\}} x_{i,r}}_{\text{number of rerouted trains}}
$$

If only delays are optimized, set $w_2 = w_3 = 0$ and $w_1 = 1$.

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Routing constraints

**(R1) Exactly one route per train:**
$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_i} x_{i,r} \;=\; 1, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
$$

**(R2) Block usage implied by route choice:**
$$
u_i^b \;=\; \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_i} \varphi_{i,r}^{b} \, x_{i,r}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; b \in \mathcal{B}
$$

**(R3) Station stop implied by route choice:**
$$
v_i^s \;=\; \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_i} \psi_{i,r}^{s} \, x_{i,r}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(R4) Route continuity** (a train traverses a connected sequence of blocks between consecutive stations on its route):
$$
\sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}(s, s')} u_i^b \;\ge\; v_i^s + v_i^{s'} - 1, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; (s, s') \in \mathcal{P}_i \times \mathcal{P}_i
$$

---

### 6.2 Train dynamics constraints

**(D1) Departure after arrival plus minimum dwell:**
$$
D_i^s \;\ge\; A_i^s + \theta_i^s \, v_i^s, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(D2) Arrival at next station after running time on connecting blocks:**
$$
A_i^{s'} \;\ge\; D_i^s + \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}(s, s')} \tau_i^b \, u_i^b, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; (s, s') \in \mathcal{P}_i
$$

**(D3) Block entry time equals departure from preceding station:**
$$
T_i^b \;\ge\; D_i^s - M(1 - u_i^b), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; b \in \mathcal{B},\; s : s \to b
$$
$$
T_i^b \;\le\; D_i^s + M(1 - u_i^b), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; b \in \mathcal{B},\; s : s \to b
$$

**(D4) Block exit time equals arrival at following station:**
$$
A_i^{s'} \;\ge\; T_i^b + \tau_i^b - M(1 - u_i^b), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; b \in \mathcal{B},\; s' : b \to s'
$$
$$
A_i^{s'} \;\le\; T_i^b + \tau_i^b + M(1 - u_i^b), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; b \in \mathcal{B},\; s' : b \to s'
$$

---

### 6.3 Conflict and ordering constraints

**(C1) Exactly one ordering at each conflict point:**
$$
y_{ij}^c + y_{ji}^c \;=\; 1, \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{T}^2,\; c \in \mathcal{C},\; i \neq j
$$

**(C2) Headway separation at conflict points (station conflicts):**
$$
A_j^s \;\ge\; A_i^s + h_{ij}^s - M(1 - y_{ij}^s), \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{T}^2,\; s \in \mathcal{C},\; i \neq j
$$

**(C3) Headway separation at block entries:**
$$
T_j^b \;\ge\; T_i^b + \tau_i^b + h_{ij}^b - M(1 - y_{ij}^b), \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{T}^2,\; b \in \mathcal{C},\; i \neq j
$$

**(C4) Safety overlap clearance behind a block** (the overlap behind block $b$ must be clear for $o^b$ minutes after train $i$ exits before train $j$ may enter a dependent block $b'$):
$$
T_j^{b'} \;\ge\; T_i^b + \tau_i^b + o^b - M(1 - y_{ij}^b) - M(1 - \sigma_{b,b'}), \quad \forall i,j \in \mathcal{T},\; b, b' \in \mathcal{B}
$$
where $\sigma_{b,b'} = 1$ if block $b'$ is in the overlap zone of block $b$, 0 otherwise.

---

### 6.4 Pair-wise delay constraints (sub-optimal model)

**(P1) Pair-wise delay is non-negative and bounded by headway:**
$$
\delta_{ij}^c \;\ge\; h_{ij}^c - M(1 - y_{ij}^c), \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{T}^2,\; c \in \mathcal{C},\; i \neq j
$$
$$
\delta_{ij}^c \;\le\; h_{ij}^c \, y_{ij}^c, \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{T}^2,\; c \in \mathcal{C},\; i \neq j
$$

**(P2) Total station delay equals the sum of pair-wise delays at that station** (sub-optimal, no propagation):
$$
\delta_i^s \;\ge\; \sum_{j \in \mathcal{T},\, j \neq i} \delta_{ij}^s, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{C}
$$

---

### 6.5 Delay propagation constraints (extended model — guarantees global optimum)

**(E1) Delay accumulates along the train's path:**
$$
\delta_i^{s'} \;\ge\; \delta_i^s + \sum_{j \in \mathcal{T},\, j \neq i} \delta_{ij}^{s'} - M(1 - v_i^{s'}), \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; (s, s') \in \mathcal{P}_i
$$

**(E2) Total delay at a station is at least the scheduled-arrival deviation:**
$$
\delta_i^s \;\ge\; A_i^s - a_i^s, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(E3) Primary delay is preserved** (already-known external delays cannot be reduced):
$$
\delta_i^s \;\ge\; \Delta_i^{s,\text{prim}}, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(E4) Delay propagation through running time** (a delayed departure propagates to the next arrival):
$$
A_i^{s'} \;\ge\; A_i^s + \theta_i^s v_i^s + \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}(s, s')} \tau_i^b u_i^b + \delta_i^{s'} - \delta_i^s, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; (s, s') \in \mathcal{P}_i
$$

---

### 6.6 Linking constraints between timing and delays

**(L1) Arrival time consistency with delays:**
$$
A_i^s \;\ge\; a_i^s + \delta_i^s, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(L2) Departure time consistency with delays:**
$$
D_i^s \;\ge\; d_i^s + \delta_i^s, \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

---

### 6.7 Non-negativity and variable domains

$$
x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}, \quad u_i^b \in \{0,1\}, \quad v_i^s \in \{0,1\}, \quad y_{ij}^c \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
A_i^s, D_i^s, T_i^b, \delta_i^s, \delta_{ij}^c \;\ge\; 0
$$

---

## 7. Model Variants

The paper proposes two MILP variants that share the above structure:

### Variant A — Sub-optimal (fast) model
Uses constraints **(R1)–(R4)**, **(D1)–(D4)**, **(C1)–(C4)**, **(P1)–(P2)**, **(L1)–(L2)**.  
Delay propagation constraints **(E1)–(E4)** are omitted.  
Result: a low-complexity MILP that solves rerouting and reordering jointly and provides a feasible (but possibly sub-optimal) input to the rescheduling stage.

### Variant B — Globally optimal (extended) model
Adds constraints **(E1)–(E4)** to Variant A.  
Result: the MILP is guaranteed to yield the global optimum of the original rtRTMP of Pellegrini et al. (2014), with a more favorable computational cost in complex scenarios.

---

## 8. Summary of Indices, Parameters, and Variables

| Category | Symbol | Meaning |
|----------|--------|---------|
| Indices | $i,j$ | trains |
| | $s, s'$ | stations |
| | $b$ | track block |
| | $r$ | route |
| | $c$ | conflict point |
| Parameters | $a_i^s, d_i^s$ | scheduled arrival/departure |
| | $\tau_i^b$ | running time on block |
| | $\theta_i^s$ | minimum dwell time |
| | $h_{ij}^c$ | minimum headway |
| | $o^b$ | safety overlap |
| | $\Delta_i^{s,\text{prim}}$ | primary delay |
| | $M$ | Big-M constant |
| Variables | $x_{i,r}$ | route selection (binary) |
| | $u_i^b, v_i^s$ | block/station usage (binary) |
| | $y_{ij}^c$ | ordering (binary) |
| | $A_i^s, D_i^s, T_i^b$ | actual times (continuous) |
| | $\delta_i^s$ | total delay (continuous) |
| | $\delta_{ij}^c$ | pair-wise delay (continuous) |

This MILP jointly decides **which route each disturbed train takes**, **in which order conflicting trains pass each conflict point**, and **when each train arrives at and departs from each station**, while ensuring safety overlaps, headway constraints, and propagation of primary delays.

Text:
# MILP for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance-to-Go (DTG) Signalling

An enhanced RECIFE-MILP model for real-time railway rescheduling with ETCS Level 2 (fixed-block with TTD) signalling.

---

## 1. Assumptions (explicitly marked)

- **(A1)** The network is a set of *routes* (paths through track segments/switch areas); each route corresponds to a fixed path through the infrastructure, as in RECIFE-MILP.
- **(A2)** Each train has a set of feasible speed profile options per route; each option induces a train- and speed-dependent **blocking time** on each traversed section (including the speed-dependent approach/braking distance before the EoA). This is the DTG enhancement.
- **(A3)** Trains must follow their scheduled route sequence (no global rerouting; local rerouting only via alternative route options where the infrastructure allows).
- **(A4)** Delays are non-negative (no earliness); trains cannot run faster than their maximum/scheduled speed profile.
- **(A5)** Rolling stock connections and minimum headways are modelled through blocking-time exclusivity on shared sections.
- **(A6)** Data are deterministic; acceleration/braking curves are precomputed per (train, speed profile option, section).

---

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains |
| $R_t$ | set of route options available to train $t$ |
| $S$ | set of track sections (incl. switch areas) |
| $S(r)$ | ordered sections of route $r$ |
| $P_{t,r,s}$ | set of speed profile options of train $t$ on route $r$ at section $s$ |
| $b_{t,r,p,s}$ | **blocking time** of train $t$ on section $s$ using speed profile $p$ (includes DTG speed-dependent braking/approach time) |
| $a_{t,r,s}$ | nominal (undelayed) entry time of train $t$ into section $s$ on route $r$ |
| $d_t$ | initial delay of train $t$ |
| $M$ | big constant |
| $\delta_{t}^{\max}$ | maximum allowed delay |
| $C_{rs}$ | pairs of routes $(r,r')$ incompatible on section $s$ (switch conflicts) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{t,r}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ uses route option $r$ |
| $y_{t,r,p,s}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ uses speed profile $p$ on section $s$ of route $r$ |
| $e_{t,s}$ | continuous ≥ 0 | entry time of train $t$ into section $s$ |
| $l_{t}$ | continuous ≥ 0 | final delay (lateness) of train $t$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimise total train delay:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{t \in T} l_{t}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

**(1) Route choice — exactly one route per train:**
$$
\sum_{r \in R_t} x_{t,r} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(2) Speed profile choice — exactly one profile per chosen route/section:**
$$
\sum_{p \in P_{t,r,s}} y_{t,r,p,s} = x_{t,r} \qquad \forall t \in T,\ r \in R_t,\ s \in S(r)
$$

**(3) Train propagation along its route (with blocking time, incl. DTG braking approach):**
$$
e_{t,s'} \ \ge\ e_{t,s} + \sum_{r \in R_t} x_{t,r}\, a_{t,r,s}^{\Delta}
+ \sum_{r \in R_t}\sum_{p} b_{t,r,p,s}\, y_{t,r,p,s}
\qquad \forall t,\ \forall (s,s') \text{ consecutive in } S(r)
$$
where $a^{\Delta}_{t,r,s}$ is the nominal running time over section $s$ (constant when route is fixed).

**(4) Initial delay / earliest possible entry:**
$$
e_{t,s_0} \ \ge\ a_{t,s_0} + d_t \qquad \forall t,\ s_0 = \text{first section of } t
$$

**(5) Section exclusivity (no overlapping blocking times) — pairwise disjunction:**
For every pair of trains $t, u$ ($t<u$) that may use conflicting routes sharing section $s$:
$$
e_{u,s} \ \ge\ e_{t,s} + b_{t,s} + M(3 - x_{t,r} - x_{u,r'} - z_{t,u,s})
$$
$$
e_{t,s} \ \ge\ e_{u,s} + b_{u,s} + M(2 - x_{t,r} - x_{u,r'} + z_{t,u,s} - 1)
$$
for all $(r,r') \in R_t \times R_u$ with $s \in S(r) \cap S(r')$, where $z_{t,u,s}\in\{0,1\}$ orders the trains and $b_{t,s}=\sum_{r,p} b_{t,r,p,s}y_{t,r,p,s}$ is the (speed-dependent) blocking time.

**(6) Switch-area incompatibility:**
$$
x_{t,r} + x_{u,r'} \le 1 \qquad \forall (r,r') \in C_{s},\ \forall s \text{ switch section}
$$
for trains whose time windows would overlap (or, more simply, for all conflicting route pairs, as in RECIFE-MILP).

**(7) Lateness definition:**
$$
l_{t} \ \ge\ e_{t,s_f} - a_{t,s_f} \qquad \forall t,\ s_f = \text{last section of } t
$$

**(8) Maximum delay bound:**
$$
l_t \le \delta_t^{\max} \qquad \forall t
$$

**(9) Variable domains:**
$$
x_{t,r},\ y_{t,r,p,s},\ z_{t,u,s} \in \{0,1\}; \quad e_{t,s},\ l_t \ge 0
$$

---

## 6. DTG-specific modelling notes

- The blocking time $b_{t,r,p,s}$ in DTG is **not** a fixed-block constant: it equals
$$
b_{t,r,p,s} = t_{\text{run}}(t,p,s) + t_{\text{brake}}(v_{t,p}, s) + t_{\text{setup}} + t_{\text{clear}}
$$
where $t_{\text{brake}}$ is the time to cover the speed-dependent approach distance from the brake indication point to the EoA at the next occupied section — larger for faster profiles, hence the trade-off captured by the profile variables $y$.
- Constraints (2)–(3) and (5) together make train separation **train- and speed-dependent**, the key enhancement over conventional RECIFE-MILP, where blocking times are fixed per block.
- Linearity is preserved because all speed-profile-dependent quantities are precomputed parameters multiplying binary variables.

Text:
# Passenger-Oriented Train Rescheduling MILP Model

## 1. Introduction and Context

This Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model extends the passenger-oriented train rescheduling framework of Liu et al. (2023a) to incorporate **time-varying sectional passenger demands**, **flexible train composition**, and **rolling stock circulation**. The model is designed to be solved within a Model Predictive Control (MPC) scheme for real-time train rescheduling. The time-varying demand is approximated as a piecewise-constant function over a prediction horizon divided into $K$ time intervals.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T} = \{1, 2, \dots, T\}$ | Set of trains in the planning horizon |
| $\mathcal{S} = \{1, 2, \dots, S\}$ | Set of stations (ordered along the line) |
| $\mathcal{K} = \{1, 2, \dots, K\}$ | Set of time intervals for piecewise-constant demand |
| $\mathcal{U} = \{1, 2, \dots, U\}$ | Set of available rolling stock units |
| $\mathcal{E} = \{(s, s+1) : s \in \mathcal{S} \setminus \{S\}\}$ | Set of track sections between consecutive stations |

---

## 3. Parameters

### 3.1 Infrastructure and Train Parameters
- $C^{U}$: Passenger capacity per rolling stock unit [pax]
- $N^{\min}, N^{\max}$: Minimum/maximum number of units per train
- $r^{\min}_{i,s}, r^{\max}_{i,s}$: Minimum/maximum running time of train $i$ from station $s$ to $s+1$ [min]
- $\rho^{\min}_{i,s}, \rho^{\max}_{i,s}$: Minimum/maximum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ [min]
- $h^{\min}, h^{\max}$: Minimum/maximum headway between consecutive trains [min]
- $L_s$: Length of section between station $s$ and $s+1$ [km]
- $\tau^{\min}_{\text{circ}}$: Minimum turnaround time for rolling stock circulation [min]

### 3.2 Time-Varying Demand Parameters
- $\lambda_{s,k}$: Average passenger arrival rate at station $s$ during interval $k$ [pax/min]
- $\Delta_k$: Duration of interval $k$ [min]
- $T^{S}_k, T^{E}_k$: Start and end time of interval $k$
- $T^{M}_k = (T^{S}_k + T^{E}_k)/2$: Midpoint of interval $k$

### 3.3 Nominal Timetable Parameters
- $\hat{t}^{\text{arr}}_{i,s}, \hat{t}^{\text{dep}}_{i,s}$: Nominal arrival/departure time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $\Delta^{\max}$: Maximum allowable timetable deviation [min]

### 3.4 Cost Parameters
- $e^{U}$: Energy consumption per unit per km [kWh/(unit·km)]
- $c^{E}$: Energy cost [$/kWh]
- $c^{U}$: Operating cost per rolling stock unit per trip [$/unit]
- $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3, \alpha_4, \alpha_5 \geq 0$: Objective weights

### 3.5 Big-M Parameter
- $M$: A sufficiently large positive constant

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Binary Variables
- $x_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: Equals 1 if train $i$ stops at station $s$, 0 otherwise
- $z_{u,i} \in \{0,1\}$: Equals 1 if rolling stock unit $u$ is assigned to train $i$
- $y_{u,i,i'} \in \{0,1\}$: Equals 1 if unit $u$ is transferred from train $i$ to train $i'$ (with $i < i'$)
- $v_{i,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$: Equals 1 if train $i$ departs station $s$ within interval $k$

### 4.2 Integer Variables
- $n_i \in \{N^{\min}, \dots, N^{\max}\}$: Number of rolling stock units composing train $i$

### 4.3 Continuous Variables
- $t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} \geq 0$: Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \geq 0$: Departure time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $b_{i,s,k} \geq 0$: Passengers boarding train $i$ at station $s$ who arrived during interval $k$
- $b_{i,s,k,k'} \geq 0$: Passengers arriving in interval $k$ who board train $i$ at station $s$ departing in interval $k'$
- $a_{i,s} \geq 0$: Passengers alighting from train $i$ at station $s$
- $q_{i,s} \geq 0$: Number of passengers on board train $i$ after departing station $s$
- $\delta^{+}_{i,s}, \delta^{-}_{i,s} \geq 0$: Positive and negative timetable deviation at station $s$ for train $i$

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$\min Z = \alpha_1 \cdot WT + \alpha_2 \cdot TT + \alpha_3 \cdot EC + \alpha_4 \cdot OC + \alpha_5 \cdot TD$$

where each component is defined as:

**Passenger waiting time:**
$$WT = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{k' \in \mathcal{K}: k' \geq k} b_{i,s,k,k'} \cdot \left(T^{M}_{k'} - T^{M}_k\right)$$

**Passenger travel time:**
$$TT = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} q_{i,s} \cdot \left(t^{\text{arr}}_{i,S} - t^{\text{dep}}_{i,1}\right)$$

**Energy consumption cost:**
$$EC = c^{E} \cdot e^{U} \cdot \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s=1}^{S-1} n_i \cdot L_s$$

**Rolling stock operating cost:**
$$OC = c^{U} \cdot \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} n_i$$

**Timetable deviation:**
$$TD = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \left(\delta^{+}_{i,s} + \delta^{-}_{i,s}\right)$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Interval Assignment for Departures
Each departure time must be assigned to exactly one interval:
$$\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} v_{i,s,k} = 1 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{C1a}$$
$$t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \geq T^{S}_k - M(1 - v_{i,s,k}) \quad \forall i, s, k \tag{C1b}$$
$$t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \leq T^{E}_k + M(1 - v_{i,s,k}) \quad \forall i, s, k \tag{C1c}$$

### 6.2 Train Composition
$$N^{\min} \leq n_i \leq N^{\max} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \tag{C2}$$

### 6.3 Rolling Stock Assignment
Each train's composition equals the number of units assigned to it:
$$n_i = \sum_{u \in \mathcal{U}} z_{u,i} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \tag{C3a}$$
Each unit is assigned to exactly one train:
$$\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} z_{u,i} = 1 \quad \forall u \in \mathcal{U} \tag{C3b}$$

### 6.4 Rolling Stock Circulation (Flow Conservation)
Each unit departing train $i$ must be transferred to exactly one subsequent train:
$$\sum_{i' \in \mathcal{T}: i' > i} y_{u,i,i'} = z_{u,i} \quad \forall u \in \mathcal{U}, \; i \in \mathcal{T} \tag{C4a}$$
Each unit arriving at train $i'$ must come from exactly one preceding train:
$$\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}: i < i'} y_{u,i,i'} = z_{u,i'} \quad \forall u \in \mathcal{U}, \; i' \in \mathcal{T} \tag{C4b}$$

### 6.5 Minimum Circulation Time
$$t^{\text{dep}}_{i',1} - t^{\text{arr}}_{i,S} \geq \tau^{\min}_{\text{circ}} - M(1 - y_{u,i,i'}) \quad \forall u \in \mathcal{U}, \; i, i' \in \mathcal{T}, \; i < i' \tag{C5}$$

### 6.6 Running Time Between Stations
$$r^{\min}_{i,s} \leq t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s+1} - t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \leq r^{\max}_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s = 1, \dots, S-1 \tag{C6}$$

### 6.7 Dwell Time at Stations
$$\rho^{\min}_{i,s} \cdot x_{i,s} \leq t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} - t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} \leq \rho^{\max}_{i,s} \cdot x_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{C7}$$

### 6.8 Terminal Station Conditions
At the origin and destination, arrival and departure times coincide:
$$t^{\text{arr}}_{i,1} = t^{\text{dep}}_{i,1} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \tag{C8a}$$
$$t^{\text{arr}}_{i,S} = t^{\text{dep}}_{i,S} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \tag{C8b}$$

### 6.9 Headway Constraints
$$h^{\min} \leq t^{\text{arr}}_{i+1,s} - t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} \leq h^{\max} \quad \forall i = 1, \dots, T-1, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{C9a}$$
$$h^{\min} \leq t^{\text{dep}}_{i+1,s} - t^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \leq h^{\max} \quad \forall i = 1, \dots, T-1, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{C9b}$$

### 6.10 Timetable Deviation
$$t^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} - \hat{t}^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} = \delta^{+}_{i,s} - \delta^{-}_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{C10a}$$
$$\delta^{+}_{i,s} + \delta^{-}_{i,s} \leq \Delta^{\max} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{C10b}$$

### 6.11 Mandatory Stops at Terminals
$$x_{i,1} = 1, \quad x_{i,S} = 1 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \tag{C11}$$

### 6.12 Train Capacity
$$q_{i,s} \leq n_i \cdot C^{U} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{C12}$$

### 6.13 Passenger Flow Conservation
$$q_{i,s} = q_{i,s-1} - a_{i,s} + \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} b_{i,s,k} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{C13a}$$
$$q_{i,0} = 0 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \tag{C13b}$$

### 6.14 Boarding Aggregation
$$b_{i,s,k} = \sum_{k' \in \mathcal{K}: k' \geq k} b_{i,s,k,k'} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}, \; k \in \mathcal{K} \tag{C14}$$

### 6.15 Boarding Limits (Coupling with Interval Assignment)
Passengers arriving in interval $k$ can only board a train if it departs in some interval $k' \geq k$:
$$b_{i,s,k,k'} \leq v_{i,s,k'} \cdot \lambda_{s,k} \cdot \Delta_k \quad \forall i, s, k, k' \geq k \tag{C15}$$

### 6.16 Total Demand Satisfaction
The total passengers boarding at station $s$ from interval $k$ cannot exceed the demand:
$$\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{k' \in \mathcal{K}: k' \geq k} b_{i,s,k,k'} \leq \lambda_{s,k} \cdot \Delta_k \quad \forall s \in \mathcal{S}, \; k \in \mathcal{K} \tag{C16}$$

### 6.17 Alighting Limits
$$a_{i,s} \leq q_{i,s-1} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{C17}$$

### 6.18 Stopping Required for Boarding/Alighting
$$b_{i,s,k} \leq M \cdot x_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}, \; k \in \mathcal{K} \tag{C18a}$$
$$a_{i,s} \leq M \cdot x_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \tag{C18b}$$

### 6.19 Non-Negativity
All continuous variables are constrained to be non-negative.

---

## 7. Assumptions

1. **Piecewise-constant demand**: Passenger arrival rates $\lambda_{s,k}$ are constant within each interval $k$ but may vary across intervals.
2. **Single-line, single-direction operation**: Trains operate in one direction along a linear corridor without branches.
3. **Homogeneous rolling stock**: All units in $\mathcal{U}$ have identical capacity $C^{U}$ and operational characteristics.
4. **Deterministic (or perfectly predicted) demand**: Passenger demand is known at the time of optimization (in MPC, this comes from a demand predictor).
5. **First-come, first-served boarding**: Passengers board the first train that stops at their station after their arrival.
6. **Midpoint waiting time approximation**: The waiting time for passengers arriving in interval $k$ and boarding in interval $k'$ is approximated as $T^{M}_{k'} - T^{M}_k$.
7. **Fixed train sequence**: The set $\mathcal{T}$ and the order of trains are predetermined; overtaking is not allowed.
8. **Known initial state**: At the start of the planning horizon, the positions of trains, the assignment of units, and the number of waiting passengers are known.
9. **No passenger denial**: All arriving passengers are eventually served (waiting may exceed one interval, but no passenger is left behind within the horizon).
10. **Decoupled origin-destination demand**: The formulation uses aggregate boarding/alighting; an OD-based extension can be obtained by disaggregating $b_{i,s,k}$ and $a_{i,s}$ by destination station.

---

## 8. Notes on MPC Integration and Learning-Based Acceleration

### 8.1 MPC Scheme
The model is solved repeatedly over a rolling prediction horizon of length $H = K \cdot \Delta_k$ minutes:
- At MPC step $n$, the model is solved with current state information.
- Only the first control action (e.g., the next departure time and composition) is implemented.
- The horizon is shifted by one step, and the model is re-solved.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t, t'$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{S}_t^{\text{orig}}, \mathcal{S}_t^{\text{dest}}$ | Origin and destination stations of train $t$ |
| $\mathcal{B}$ | Set of track blocks (segments between consecutive stations), indexed by $b$ |
| $\mathcal{B}^{\text{disr}} \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ | Set of disrupted blocks |
| $\mathcal{K} = \{0,1,\dots,K\}$ | Set of discrete time steps, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{D} = \{\text{U}, \text{D}\}$ | Set of running directions (Up/Down) |
| $\mathcal{R} = \{0,1\}$ | Rerouting options (0 = original track, 1 = opposite track) |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ | m |
| $\Delta t$ | Duration of a time step | s |
| $v^{\max}, v^{\min}$ | Maximum and minimum operating speeds | m/s |
| $a^{\max}, a^{\min}$ | Maximum acceleration and deceleration ($a^{\min}<0$) | m/s² |
| $m_t$ | Mass of train $t$ | t |
| $h^{\min}$ | Minimum headway time between consecutive trains | s |
| $\tau_s^{\min}, \tau_s^{\max}$ | Minimum and maximum dwell time at station $s$ | s |
| $C_s$ | Number of platforms at station $s$ | – |
| $\alpha_{t,s}^{\text{sch}}, \beta_{t,s}^{\text{sch}}$ | Scheduled arrival and departure times | s |
| $[k_b^{\text{disr},1}, k_b^{\text{disr},2}]$ | Disruption time window on block $b$ | – |
| $c^{\text{ene}}$ | Energy cost coefficient | €/kWh |
| $c^{\text{delay}}$ | Delay penalty per minute | €/min |
| $c^{\text{cancel}}$ | Cancellation penalty | €/train |
| $c^{\text{reroute}}$ | Rerouting penalty | €/reroute |
| $\eta^{\text{tract}}, \eta^{\text{cruise}}, \eta^{\text{brake}}$ | Energy consumption coefficients | kWh/(m/s), etc. |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large positive constant (Big-M) | – |

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Train Movement and Dynamics
- $x_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ occupies block $b$ at time $k$
- $r_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses the opposite (rerouted) track in block $b$ at time $k$
- $d_{t,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ travels in the Up direction in block $b$ at time $k$ (0 = Down)
- $v_{t,b,k} \geq 0$: Speed of train $t$ in block $b$ at time $k$ (m/s)
- $a_{t,b,k} \in \mathbb{R}$: Acceleration of train $t$ in block $b$ at time $k$ (m/s²)
- $s_{t,b,k} \geq 0$: Position of train $t$ within block $b$ at time $k$ (m)
- $e_{t,b,k} \geq 0$: Energy consumption of train $t$ in block $b$ at time $k$ (kWh)

### 3.2 Station Operations
- $\alpha_{t,s} \geq 0$: Arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $\beta_{t,s} \geq 0$: Departure time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $\tau_{t,s} \geq 0$: Dwell time of train $t$ at station $s$

### 3.3 Conflict Resolution
- $y_{t,t',b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ occupies block $b$ before train $t'$ at time $k$
- $w_{t,t',b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trains $t$ and $t'$ are in conflict in block $b$ at time $k$

### 3.4 Service Cancellation
- $c_t \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ is cancelled

### 3.5 Auxiliary Variables (for linearization)
- $a_{t,b,k}^{+}, a_{t,b,k}^{-} \geq 0$: Positive and negative parts of acceleration
- $\delta_{t,s}^{\text{delay}} \geq 0$: Arrival delay of train $t$ at station $s$

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the total operational cost, comprising energy consumption, delays, cancellations, and rerouting penalties:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad Z = \; & c^{\text{ene}} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} e_{t,b,k} \\
& + c^{\text{delay}} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \delta_{t,s}^{\text{delay}} \\
& + c^{\text{cancel}} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} c_t \\
& + c^{\text{reroute}} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} r_{t,b,k}
\end{aligned}
$$

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Kinematics (Speed–Position–Acceleration Relations)

**Speed update:**
$$
v_{t,b,k+1} = v_{t,b,k} + a_{t,b,k} \Delta t \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T},\; b \in \mathcal{B},\; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

**Position update (trapezoidal rule, linear):**
$$
s_{t,b,k+1} = s_{t,b,k} + \frac{v_{t,b,k} + v_{t,b,k+1}}{2} \Delta t \quad \forall t, b, k
$$

**Acceleration decomposition:**
$$
a_{t,b,k} = a_{t,b,k}^{+} - a_{t,b,k}^{-} \quad \forall t, b, k
$$

**Speed bounds:**
$$
v^{\min} \cdot x_{t,b,k} \leq v_{t,b,k} \leq v^{\max} \cdot x_{t,b,k} \quad \forall t, b, k
$$

**Acceleration bounds:**
$$
a^{\min} \cdot x_{t,b,k} \leq a_{t,b,k} \leq a^{\max} \cdot x_{t,b,k} \quad \forall t, b, k
$$

### 5.2 Block Occupancy and Transition

**Single-block occupancy:** A train can occupy at most one block at any time:
$$
\sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} x_{t,b,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

**Block traversal:** A train must traverse the full length of a block before exiting:
$$
s_{t,b,k} \leq L_b \cdot x_{t,b,k} \quad \forall t, b, k
$$

**Continuity of movement:** If a train leaves block $b$ at time $k$, it must enter block $b'$ (the next block in its direction) at time $k+1$:
$$
x_{t,b,k} - x_{t,b,k-1} \leq x_{t,b',k} \quad \forall t, b, k
$$
where $b'$ is the successor block of $b$ in the direction of travel.

**Initial and terminal conditions:**
$$
x_{t,b_0^{\text{orig}},0} = 1,\quad x_{t,b_0^{\text{dest}},K} = 1 \quad \forall t
$$

### 5.3 Disruption and Rerouting Constraints

**Disrupted block inaccessibility (original track):**
$$
x_{t,b,k} \leq r_{t,b,k} \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T},\; b \in \mathcal{B}^{\text{disr}},\; k \in [k_b^{\text{disr},1}, k_b^{\text{disr},2}]
$$
*(A train can occupy a disrupted block only if it is rerouted to the opposite track.)*

**Rerouting feasibility:** Rerouting is permitted only within the disruption time window and on disrupted blocks:
$$
r_{t,b,k} \leq \mathbb{1}[k \in [k_b^{\text{disr},1}, k_b^{\text{disr},2}]] \quad \forall t, b, k
$$

**Direction consistency on rerouted track:** A train using the opposite track must travel in the direction opposite to the track's normal direction:
$$
d_{t,b,k} \geq 1 - r_{t,b,k} \quad \text{or} \quad d_{t,b,k} \leq r_{t,b,k} \quad \text{(depending on track orientation)}
$$

### 5.4 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution

**Mutual exclusion on shared track:** Two trains in opposite directions cannot simultaneously occupy the same physical track in the same block:
$$
x_{t,b,k} + x_{t',b,k} - r_{t,b,k} - r_{t',b,k} + w_{t,t',b,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall t \neq t', b, k
$$

**Ordering of conflicting trains:**
$$
y_{t,t',b,k} + y_{t',t,b,k} = w_{t,t',b,k} \quad \forall t \neq t', b, k
$$

**Headway constraint:** If two trains use the same track in the same block, they must be separated by at least $h^{\min}$:
$$
\sum_{k' = k}^{k + h^{\min}/\Delta t} (x_{t,b,k'} + x_{t',b,k'}) \leq 1 + M(1 - w_{t,t',b,k}) \quad \forall t \neq t', b, k
$$

### 5.5 Station Operations

**Dwell time definition:**
$$
\beta_{t,s} = \alpha_{t,s} + \tau_{t,s} \quad \forall t, s
$$

**Dwell time bounds:**
$$
\tau_s^{\min} \leq \tau_{t,s} \leq \tau_s^{\max} \quad \forall t, s
$$

**Platform capacity:** The number of trains simultaneously at a station cannot exceed the number of platforms:
$$
\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \mathbb{1}[\alpha_{t,s} \leq k \Delta t \leq \beta_{t,s}] \leq C_s \quad \forall s, k
$$

**Linearized platform capacity (using auxiliary variables):**
$$
\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} p_{t,s,k} \leq C_s \quad \forall s, k
$$
where $p_{t,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$ indicates train $t$ is present at station $s$ at time $k$, linked via:
$$
p_{t,s,k} \geq \alpha_{t,s} - k\Delta t - M(1 - p_{t,s,k}), \quad p_{t,s,k} \geq k\Delta t - \beta_{t,s} - M(1 - p_{t,s,k})
$$

### 5.6 Delay Calculation

**Arrival delay (linearization):**
$$
\delta_{t,s}^{\text{delay}} \geq \alpha_{t,s} - \alpha_{t,s}^{\text{sch}} \quad \forall t, s
$$
$$
\delta_{t,s}^{\text{delay}} \geq 0 \quad \forall t, s
$$

### 5.7 Energy Consumption Model

A linearized energy model based on tractive effort, cruise, and braking phases:

$$
e_{t,b,k} = \eta^{\text{tract}} \cdot m_t \cdot a_{t,b,k}^{+} \cdot v_{t,b,k} + \eta^{\text{cruise}} \cdot v_{t,b,k} + \eta^{\text{brake}} \cdot m_t \cdot a_{t,b,k}^{-} \cdot v_{t,b,k} \quad \forall t, b, k
$$

**Linearization of bilinear terms** $a^{\pm}_{t,b,k} \cdot v_{t,b,k}$ using piecewise linear approximation or McCormick envelopes. Introduce auxiliary variables $u_{t,b,k}^{+} = a_{t,b,k}^{+} \cdot v_{t,b,k}$ and $u_{t,b,k}^{-} = a_{t,b,k}^{-} \cdot v_{t,b,k}$ with constraints:

$$
u_{t,b,k}^{+} \leq a^{\max} \cdot v_{t,b,k}, \quad u_{t,b,k}^{+} \leq v^{\max} \cdot a_{t,b,k}^{+}, \quad u_{t,b,k}^{+} \geq a^{\min} \cdot v_{t,b,k} + v^{\min} \cdot a_{t,b,k}^{+} - a^{\min} \cdot v^{\min}
$$
(and analogous for $u_{t,b,k}^{-}$).

### 5.8 Cancellation Constraints

**Cancelled trains do not operate:**
$$
\sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} x_{t,b,k} \leq M (1 - c_t) \quad \forall t
$$

**Cancellation implies no station visits:**
$$
\alpha_{t,s} \leq M (1 - c_t), \quad \beta_{t,s} \leq M (1 - c_t) \quad \forall t, s
$$

### 5.9 Coupling Between Timetable and Speed Profile

**Arrival time consistency:** The arrival time at a station equals the time at which the train completes the preceding block:
$$
\alpha_{t,s} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} k \Delta t \cdot x_{t,b_{s}^{\text{prev}},k} \quad \forall t, s
$$
where $b_s^{\text{prev}}$ is the block immediately before station $s$.

**Departure time consistency:** The departure time equals the time at which the train begins the succeeding block:
$$
\beta_{t,s} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} k \Delta t \cdot x_{t,b_{s}^{\text{next}},k} \quad \forall t, s
$$

## 6. Model Summary

The complete MILP formulation is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & c^{\text{ene}} \sum_{t,b,k} e_{t,b,k} + c^{\text{delay}} \sum_{t,s} \delta_{t,s}^{\text{delay}} + c^{\text{cancel}} \sum_t c_t + c^{\text{reroute}} \sum_{t,b,k} r_{t,b,k} \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{Kinematics: } (5.1) \\
& \text{Occupancy: } (5.2) \\
& \text{Disruption \& Rerouting: } (5.3) \\
& \text{Conflicts: } (5.4) \\
& \text{Stations: } (5.5) \\
& \text{Delays: } (5.6) \\
& \text{Energy: } (5.7) \\
& \text{Cancellations: } (5.8) \\
& \text{Coupling: } (5.9) \\
& x, y, w, r, d, c, p \in \{0,1\}; \quad v, s, e, \alpha, \beta, \tau, \delta, a^{\pm}, u^{\pm} \geq 0; \quad a \in \mathbb{R}
\end{aligned}
$$

## 7. Key Assumptions

1. **Time–space discretization:** The planning horizon is discretized into uniform time steps $\Delta t$, and the track is divided into fixed blocks between consecutive stations.
2. **Homogeneous train consists:** All trains of the same type share identical mass, length, and traction/braking characteristics.
3. **Bidirectional single-track operation:** Each physical track segment normally carries traffic in one direction; during disruption, trains may be rerouted to the opposite track, creating bidirectional conflicts.
4. **Disruption scope:** The disruption affects a predefined set of blocks $\mathcal{B}^{\text{disr}}$ during a known time window $[k_b^{\text{disr},1}, k_b^{\text{disr},2}]$.
5. **Fixed train routes (with rerouting option):** The sequence of stations for each train is predetermined; only the track assignment (original vs. opposite) within disrupted blocks is a decision variable.
6. **Linearized energy model:** The nonlinear tractive-power term $F \cdot v$ is approximated via piecewise-linear or McCormick relaxation to preserve MILP tractability.
7. **No train overtaking within a block:** Trains maintain their order within a block; reordering is permitted only at stations or via rerouting.
8. **Instantaneous rerouting:** Switching to the opposite track incurs no additional time penalty beyond the rerouting cost term.
9. **Perfect information:** Disruption characteristics (location, duration) are known with certainty at the time of rescheduling.
10. **Regenerative braking ignored:** Braking energy is treated as dissipated (or accounted via a constant coefficient $\eta^{\text{brake}}$).
