Text:
# MILP Formulation for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Below is the best of the generated models — a complete, linear MILP that integrates train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with train speed management (speed profiles, energy consumption) under partial segment blockages on a bidirectional single-track line.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Set | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| $\mathcal{I}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$; $s=1$ origin, $s=\lvert\mathcal{S}\rvert$ terminal |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of track segments, indexed by $k$; segment $k$ connects station $k$ and $k+1$ |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of discrete time blocks, indexed by $t = 0,1,\dots,\lvert\mathcal{T}\rvert$ |
| $\mathcal{D}\subseteq\mathcal{K}$ | Set of disrupted segments |
| $\mathcal{W}\subseteq\mathcal{T}$ | Disruption time window |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| $L_k$ | Length of segment $k$ (km) |
| $V^{\max}, V^{\min}$ | Maximum / minimum allowed speed (km/h) |
| $A^{\max}, D^{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration (km/h²) |
| $E_c$ | Energy consumption coefficient |
| $h$ | Minimum headway time (time blocks) |
| $\delta^{\min}_s, \delta^{\max}_s$ | Min / max dwell time at station $s$ |
| $\bar{a}_{i,s}, \bar{d}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure time of train $i$ at $s$ |
| $\tau_{i,k}$ | Nominal running time of train $i$ on segment $k$ |
| $\Delta t$ | Duration of one time block (h) |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3$ | Objective weights (delay, energy, cancellation) |
| $P^{\text{cncl}}$ | Cancellation penalty |
| $F^{\min}, F^{\max}$ | Bounds on tractive effort |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Binary variables**

- $x_{i,s,t}\in\{0,1\}$ — train $i$ occupies station $s$ during time block $t$
- $y_{i,k,t}\in\{0,1\}$ — train $i$ occupies segment $k$ during time block $t$
- $y^{N}_{i,k,t}, y^{R}_{i,k,t}\in\{0,1\}$ — train $i$ on **normal** or **reverse** (rerouting) track of segment $k$ at $t$
- $r_{i,k}\in\{0,1\}$ — train $i$ uses rerouting on segment $k$
- $\sigma_{i,j,k}\in\{0,1\}$ — train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $k$
- $c_i\in\{0,1\}$ — train $i$ is cancelled

**Continuous variables**

- $\alpha_{i,s}, \beta_{i,s}\geq 0$ — actual arrival / departure time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $v_{i,k,t}\geq 0$ — speed of train $i$ on segment $k$ at time $t$
- $p_{i,k,t}\geq 0$ — position of train $i$ on segment $k$ at time $t$
- $a_{i,k,t}$ — acceleration of train $i$ on segment $k$ at time $t$
- $F_{i,k,t}\geq 0$ — tractive effort
- $\Pi_{i,k,t}\geq 0$ — power (linearized product $F\cdot v$)
- $e_{i,k,t}\geq 0$ — energy consumption
- $d_{i,s}\geq 0$ — delay of train $i$ at station $s$
- $\rho_{i,k}\geq 0$ — actual running time on segment $k$

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; w_1 \!\!\sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} d_{i,s} \;+\; w_2 \!\!\sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}} e_{i,k,t} \;+\; w_3 \!\!\sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}} c_i\, P^{\text{cncl}}
$$

The objective balances **passenger delay**, **energy consumption**, and **cancellation penalties**.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Flow Conservation at Stations

$$
\alpha_{i,s+1} = \beta_{i,s} + \rho_{i,s} \quad \forall i,\; s=1,\dots,\lvert\mathcal{S}\rvert-1 \tag{C1}
$$

$$
\delta^{\min}_s (1-c_i) \;\leq\; \beta_{i,s}-\alpha_{i,s} \;\leq\; \delta^{\max}_s (1-c_i) \quad \forall i,s \tag{C2}
$$

$$
\beta_{i,1} \geq \bar{d}_{i,1}(1-c_i), \qquad \alpha_{i,\lvert\mathcal{S}\rvert} \leq T(1-c_i) \quad \forall i \tag{C3}
$$

### 5.2 Delay Definition

$$
d_{i,s} \geq \alpha_{i,s}-\bar{a}_{i,s}, \qquad d_{i,s} \leq M(1-c_i) \quad \forall i,s \tag{C4}
$$

### 5.3 Segment Occupancy and Timing

$$
\rho_{i,k} = \alpha_{i,k+1}-\beta_{i,k} \quad \forall i,k \tag{C5}
$$

$$
\rho_{i,k} \geq \tau_{i,k}(1-c_i) \quad \forall i,k \tag{C6}
$$

$$
y_{i,k,t} \leq \frac{t\Delta t-\beta_{i,k}}{M}+1 \quad \forall i,k,t \tag{C7}
$$

$$
y_{i,k,t} \leq \frac{\alpha_{i,k+1}-t\Delta t}{M}+1 \quad \forall i,k,t \tag{C8}
$$

$$
\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}} y_{i,k,t} = \frac{\rho_{i,k}}{\Delta t} \quad \forall i,k \tag{C9}
$$

### 5.4 Train Dynamics (Linearized)

$$
p_{i,k,t+1} = p_{i,k,t} + v_{i,k,t}\Delta t + \tfrac{1}{2}a_{i,k,t}\Delta t^{2} \quad \forall i,k,t \tag{C10}
$$

$$
v_{i,k,t+1} = v_{i,k,t} + a_{i,k,t}\Delta t \quad \forall i,k,t \tag{C11}
$$

$$
-D^{\max} \leq a_{i,k,t} \leq A^{\max} \quad \forall i,k,t \tag{C12}
$$

$$
V^{\min}\, y_{i,k,t} \leq v_{i,k,t} \leq V^{\max}\, y_{i,k,t} \quad \forall i,k,t \tag{C13}
$$

$$
0 \leq p_{i,k,t} \leq L_k\, y_{i,k,t} \quad \forall i,k,t \tag{C14}
$$

$$
p_{i,k,0} = 0, \qquad p_{i,k,\lvert\mathcal{T}\rvert} = L_k(1-c_i) \quad \forall i,k \tag{C15}
$$

### 5.5 Headway / Safety Constraints

$$
\sigma_{i,j,k}+\sigma_{j,i,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall i\neq j,\; k \tag{C16}
$$

$$
\beta_{j,k} \geq \beta_{i,k}+\rho_{i,k}+h - M(1-\sigma_{i,j,k}) - M(c_i+c_j) \quad \forall i\neq j,\; k \tag{C17}
$$

$$
y^{N}_{i,k,t}+y^{N}_{j,k,t} \leq 1 \quad \forall i\neq j,\; k, t \tag{C18}
$$

$$
y^{R}_{i,k,t}+y^{R}_{j,k,t} \leq 1 \quad \forall i\neq j,\; k, t \tag{C19}
$$

### 5.6 Rerouting Constraints

$$
y_{i,k,t} = y^{N}_{i,k,t}+y^{R}_{i,k,t} \quad \forall i,k,t \tag{C20}
$$

$$
r_{i,k} \geq y^{R}_{i,k,t} \quad \forall i,k,t \tag{C21}
$$

$$
r_{i,k} \leq \sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}} y^{R}_{i,k,t} \quad \forall i,k \tag{C22}
$$

$$
r_{i,k} \leq 1-c_i \quad \forall i,k \tag{C23}
$$

### 5.7 Disruption Constraints

$$
y^{N}_{i,k,t} = 0 \quad \forall i,\; k\in\mathcal{D},\; t\in\mathcal{W} \tag{C24}
$$

$$
y^{R}_{i,k,t} \leq 1 \quad \forall i,\; k\in\mathcal{D},\; t\in\mathcal{W} \tag{C25}
$$

### 5.8 Cancellation Logic

$$
\alpha_{i,s}\leq M(1-c_i),\;\; \beta_{i,s}\leq M(1-c_i) \quad \forall i,s \tag{C26}
$$

$$
y_{i,k,t}\leq 1-c_i,\;\; v_{i,k,t}\leq M(1-c_i) \quad \forall i,k,t \tag{C27}
$$

$$
\rho_{i,k}\leq M(1-c_i),\;\; d_{i,s}\leq M(1-c_i) \quad \forall i,k,s \tag{C28}
$$

### 5.9 Energy Consumption (Linearized via McCormick Envelopes)

$$
\Pi_{i,k,t} \geq F^{\min} v_{i,k,t} + V^{\min} F_{i,k,t} - F^{\min} V^{\min} \tag{C29}
$$

$$
\Pi_{i,k,t} \geq F^{\max} v_{i,k,t} + V^{\max} F_{i,k,t} - F^{\max} V^{\max} \tag{C30}
$$

$$
\Pi_{i,k,t} \leq F^{\min} v_{i,k,t} + V^{\max} F_{i,k,t} - F^{\min} V^{\max} \tag{C31}
$$

$$
\Pi_{i,k,t} \leq F^{\max} v_{i,k,t} + V^{\min} F_{i,k,t} - F^{\max} V^{\min} \tag{C32}
$$

$$
e_{i,k,t} = E_c\, \Pi_{i,k,t}\, \Delta t \quad \forall i,k,t \tag{C33}
$$

$$
F^{\min}\, y_{i,k,t} \leq F_{i,k,t} \leq F^{\max}\, y_{i,k,t} \quad \forall i,k,t \tag{C34}
$$

---

## 6. Modeling Assumptions

1. **Time discretization** — Time is divided into uniform blocks of duration $\Delta t$, enabling time-indexed binary occupancy variables that simultaneously encode rescheduling and speed profiles.
2. **Bidirectional single-track with rerouting** — Each segment has two physical tracks (normal and reverse); trains may use either, subject to single-train occupancy per track per time block.
3. **Partial blockage** — Only the normal track of disrupted segments $\mathcal{D}$ is blocked during window $\mathcal{W}$; the reverse track remains available for rerouting.
4. **Piecewise-constant speed profile** — Within each time block, speed and acceleration are constant, yielding a linearized kinematic model.
5. **Identical train performance** — All trains share the same $V^{\max}, V^{\min}, A^{\max}, D^{\max}, F^{\min}, F^{\max}$ (relaxable to per-train parameters).
6. **Bilinear tractive-power term** — The product $F\cdot v$ is linearized exactly using McCormick envelopes over the known bounds $[F^{\min},F^{\max}]\times[V^{\min},V^{\max}]$.
7. **Hard disruption** — Blockage is modeled as a hard spatio-temporal constraint (no soft penalties); rerouting is the only permitted recovery on disrupted segments.
8. **Cancellation as last resort** — Cancelled trains incur a large penalty $P^{\text{cncl}}$ and have all operational variables zeroed out via big-M constraints.
9. **Headway on shared tracks** — Minimum separation $h$ is enforced between any two trains sharing the same physical track, regardless of direction.

---

## 7. Linearity Guarantee

Every constraint is linear:

- Big-M formulations link binary and continuous variables (C7–C8, C17, C26–C28).
- McCormick envelopes (C29–C32) linearize the bilinear $F\cdot v$ term.
- Kinematics (C10–C11) are expressed as linear recurrences in $(p, v, a)$.

The model is therefore a valid MILP solvable by standard branch-and-cut solvers (CPLEX, Gurobi, SCIP).

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $I$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$; ordered along the line |
| $B$ | Set of blocks (track segments), indexed by $b$; block $b$ connects station $s(b)$ to $s(b)+1$ |
| $K$ | Set of discrete time steps, indexed by $k = 1, \dots, |K|$; each step has duration $\Delta t$ |
| $\text{Dir}(i) \in \{U, D\}$ | Direction of train $i$ (Up or Down) |
| $B_i \subseteq B$ | Subset of blocks traversed by train $i$ (given route) |
| $S_i \subseteq S$ | Subset of stations served by train $i$ |
| $s_O(i), s_T(i)$ | Origin and terminal station of train $i$ |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ | m |
| $\Delta t$ | Duration of a time step | s |
| $v^{\max}, v^{\min}$ | Maximum / minimum allowable speed | m/s |
| $a^{\text{acc}}, a^{\text{dec}}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration | m/s² |
| $t^{\text{dwell}}_s$ | Nominal dwell time at station $s$ | s |
| $t^{\text{dwell},\min}_s, t^{\text{dwell},\max}_s$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time at $s$ | s |
| $h^{\min}$ | Minimum headway time (same direction) | s |
| $h^{\min}_{\text{opp}}$ | Minimum headway time (opposite directions on shared track) | s |
| $a^0_{i,s}, d^0_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure time of train $i$ at $s$ | s |
| $T_s, T_e$ | Disruption start / end time | s |
| $b_d, \text{Dir}_d$ | Disrupted block index and affected direction | – |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) | – |
| $W_1, W_2, W_3$ | Weights for delay, energy, and cancellation in the objective | – |
| $c_0, c_1, c_2$ | Linearized energy-consumption coefficients | kWh/(m/s), kWh/(m/s²), kWh |
| $m$ | Train mass | kg |
| $\rho, C_d, A_f$ | Air density, drag coefficient, frontal area | – |
| $g$ | Gravitational acceleration | m/s² |
| $\theta_b$ | Gradient angle of block $b$ | rad |

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Binary Variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $y_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses its **original** track on block $b$; 0 if rerouted to the opposite track |
| $\theta_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ exits block $b$ before train $j$ (same direction) |
| $\theta^{\text{opp}}_{i,j,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ (direction $U$) exits block $b$ before train $j$ (direction $D$) on a shared (rerouted) track |
| $\sigma_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ serves station $s$ (0 = cancelled at $s$) |
| $\zeta_{i,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ occupies block $b$ at time step $k$ |
| $\text{cancel}_i \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is fully cancelled |

### 3.2 Continuous Variables

| Variable | Description | Unit |
|----------|-------------|------|
| $A_{i,s}, D_{i,s}$ | Actual arrival / departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ | s |
| $\tau_{i,s}$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ | s |
| $v_{i,b,k}$ | Speed of train $i$ in block $b$ at time $k$ | m/s |
| $a_{i,b,k}$ | Acceleration of train $i$ in block $b$ at time $k$ | m/s² |
| $p_{i,b,k}$ | Position of train $i$ in block $b$ at time $k$ | m |
| $e_{i,b,k}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ in block $b$ at time $k$ | kWh |
| $E$ | Total energy consumption | kWh |

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; W_1 \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{s \in S_i} \tau_{i,s} \;+\; W_2 \cdot E \;+\; W_3 \sum_{i \in I} \text{cancel}_i
$$

The three terms represent, respectively: (i) total passenger-weighted delay, (ii) total energy consumption, and (iii) number of cancelled trains.

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Dynamics (Speed and Position Update)

$$
v_{i,b,k+1} = v_{i,b,k} + a_{i,b,k}\,\Delta t \qquad \forall i \in I,\; b \in B_i,\; k \in K \setminus \{|K|\} \tag{C1}
$$

$$
p_{i,b,k+1} = p_{i,b,k} + v_{i,b,k}\,\Delta t \qquad \forall i \in I,\; b \in B_i,\; k \in K \setminus \{|K|\} \tag{C2}
$$

### 5.2 Speed and Acceleration Limits

$$
v^{\min}\,\zeta_{i,b,k} \;\le\; v_{i,b,k} \;\le\; v^{\max}\,\zeta_{i,b,k} \qquad \forall i, b, k \tag{C3}
$$

$$
-a^{\text{dec}}\,\zeta_{i,b,k} \;\le\; a_{i,b,k} \;\le\; a^{\text{acc}}\,\zeta_{i,b,k} \qquad \forall i, b, k \tag{C4}
$$

### 5.3 Block Occupancy and Capacity

**Single-train occupancy per time step (each physical track):**

$$
\sum_{i \in I} \zeta_{i,b,k} \;\le\; 1 \qquad \forall b \in B,\; k \in K \tag{C5}
$$

**Minimum traversal time of a block:**

$$
\sum_{k \in K} \zeta_{i,b,k}\,\Delta t \;\ge\; \frac{L_b}{v^{\max}} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; b \in B_i \tag{C6}
$$

### 5.4 Disruption Avoidance and Forced Rerouting

**Trains in the affected direction cannot enter the disrupted block during the disruption window:**

$$
\zeta_{i,b_d,k} = 0 \qquad \forall i \in I:\; \text{Dir}(i)=\text{Dir}_d,\; k \in K:\; T_s \le k\Delta t \le T_e \tag{C7}
$$

**Forced rerouting for trains in the affected direction:**

$$
y_{i,b_d} = 0 \qquad \forall i \in I:\; \text{Dir}(i)=\text{Dir}_d \tag{C8}
$$

### 5.5 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution on Shared (Rerouted) Track

When trains are rerouted, both directions share a single track. The following constraints enforce safe temporal separation:

$$
\sum_{k \in K} k\Delta t\,(\zeta_{i,b,k} - \zeta_{j,b,k}) \;\ge\; h^{\min}_{\text{opp}} - M\bigl(1 - \theta^{\text{opp}}_{i,j,b}\bigr) \qquad \forall i,j:\; \text{Dir}(i)\ne\text{Dir}(j),\; b \in B \tag{C9}
$$

$$
\sum_{k \in K} k\Delta t\,(\zeta_{j,b,k} - \zeta_{i,b,k}) \;\ge\; h^{\min}_{\text{opp}} - M\,\theta^{\text{opp}}_{i,j,b} \qquad \forall i,j:\; \text{Dir}(i)\ne\text{Dir}(j),\; b \in B \tag{C10}
$$

### 5.6 Same-Direction Headway at Stations

$$
A_{i,s} - A_{j,s} \;\ge\; h^{\min} - M\bigl(1 - \theta_{i,j,s}\bigr) \qquad \forall i,j:\; \text{Dir}(i)=\text{Dir}(j),\; s \in S \tag{C11}
$$

$$
A_{j,s} - A_{i,s} \;\ge\; h^{\min} - M\,\theta_{i,j,s} \qquad \forall i,j:\; \text{Dir}(i)=\text{Dir}(j),\; s \in S \tag{C12}
$$

### 5.7 Station Arrival and Departure Times

**Arrival time linked to block exit (block $b$ ends at station $s$):**

$$
A_{i,s} \;\ge\; k\Delta t\,\zeta_{i,b,k} - M\bigl(1 - \zeta_{i,b,k}\bigr) \qquad \forall i \in I,\; b \in B_i:\; s(b)=s,\; k \in K \tag{C13}
$$

$$
A_{i,s} \;\le\; k\Delta t\,\zeta_{i,b,k} + M\bigl(1 - \zeta_{i,b,k}\bigr) \qquad \forall i \in I,\; b \in B_i:\; s(b)=s,\; k \in K \tag{C14}
$$

**Dwell time bounds:**

$$
D_{i,s} - A_{i,s} \;\ge\; t^{\text{dwell},\min}_s\,\sigma_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; s \in S_i \tag{C15}
$$

$$
D_{i,s} - A_{i,s} \;\le\; t^{\text{dwell},\max}_s\,\sigma_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; s \in S_i \tag{C16}
$$

### 5.8 Inter-Station Running Time

$$
A_{i,s+1} - D_{i,s} \;\ge\; t^{\text{run},\min}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; s \in S_i \setminus \{s_T(i)\} \tag{C17}
$$

$$
A_{i,s+1} - D_{i,s} \;\le\; t^{\text{run},\max}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; s \in S_i \setminus \{s_T(i)\} \tag{C18}
$$

### 5.9 Delay Definition

$$
\tau_{i,s} \;\ge\; A_{i,s} - a^0_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; s \in S_i \tag{C19}
$$

$$
\tau_{i,s} \;\ge\; 0 \qquad \forall i \in I,\; s \in S_i \tag{C20}
$$

### 5.10 Energy Consumption (Linearized)

The Davis equation $e = (m a + m g \sin\theta + \tfrac{1}{2}\rho C_d A_f v^2)\,v\,\Delta t / 3.6\times 10^6$ is nonlinear. We adopt a **piecewise-linear (PWL) approximation** with breakpoints $\{v_1,\dots,v_P\}$ and auxiliary variables $\lambda_{i,b,k,p} \in [0,1]$ such that $\sum_p \lambda_{i,b,k,p} = \zeta_{i,b,k}$:

$$
e_{i,b,k} \;\ge\; c_0\,\zeta_{i,b,k} + c_1\,v_{i,b,k} + c_2\,a_{i,b,k} \qquad \forall i, b, k \tag{C21}
$$

$$
e_{i,b,k} \;\ge\; 0 \qquad \forall i, b, k \tag{C22}
$$

(Regenerative braking energy is recovered when $a_{i,b,k}<0$; the inequality form ensures a valid lower bound on net energy use.)

### 5.11 Total Energy

$$
E \;=\; \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{b \in B_i}\sum_{k \in K} e_{i,b,k} \tag{C23}
$$

### 5.12 Cancellation Logic

$$
\sum_{s \in S_i} \sigma_{i,s} \;\ge\; |S_i|\,(1 - \text{cancel}_i) \qquad \forall i \in I \tag{C24}
$$

$$
\sigma_{i,s} \;\le\; 1 - \text{cancel}_i \qquad \forall i \in I,\; s \in S_i \tag{C25}
$$

### 5.13 Boundary Conditions

**Initial conditions (entry into first block):**

$$
p_{i,b_O(i),1} = 0, \qquad v_{i,b_O(i),1} = v^{\text{entry}}_i \qquad \forall i \in I \tag{C26}
$$

**Terminal conditions (exit from last block):**

$$
p_{i,b_T(i),|K|} = L_{b_T(i)}, \qquad v_{i,b_T(i),|K|} = v^{\text{exit}}_i \qquad \forall i \in I \tag{C27}
$$

### 5.14 Linkage Between Block Occupancy and Train Path

Each train must traverse its prescribed blocks in order:

$$
\sum_{k \in K} \zeta_{i,b,k} \;\ge\; 1 \qquad \forall i \in I,\; b \in B_i \tag{C28}
$$

$$
\sum_{k \in K} k\,\zeta_{i,b+1,k} \;\ge\; \sum_{k \in K} k\,\zeta_{i,b,k} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; b, b+1 \in B_i \tag{C29}
$$

## 6. Key Assumptions

1. **Double-track line** with one track per direction in normal operation.
2. **Time discretization** is uniform with step $\Delta t$; finer steps improve accuracy at higher computational cost.
3. **Train consists are homogeneous** (same mass $m$, drag, and traction characteristics) — *reasonable assumption for high-speed rail fleets*.
4. **Routes are predetermined** ($B_i$ is given); the model decides only rerouting on the disrupted block and timing/speed.
5. **Disruption is deterministic**: a single block $b_d$ in direction $\text{Dir}_d$ is blocked during $[T_s, T_e]$.
6. **Rerouting is local**: rerouted trains use the opposite track only on block $b_d$.
7. **Energy model** uses a piecewise-linear approximation of the Davis equation; regenerative braking is allowed.
8. **No train overtaking** within a block (enforced by ordering variables $\theta_{i,j,b}$).
9. **Cancellation is all-or-nothing per train**; partial short-turning is not modeled (could be extended).
10. **Passenger demand and rolling stock coupling** are abstracted into the delay weight $W_1$.

## 7. Model Summary

| Component | Type | Count (approx.) |
|-----------|------|-----------------|
| Binary variables | $y, \theta, \theta^{\text{opp}}, \sigma, \zeta, \text{cancel}$ | $O(|I|^2|B||K|)$ |
| Continuous variables | $A, D, \tau, v, a, p, e, E$ | $O(|I||B||K|)$ |
| Constraints | C1–C29 | $O(|I||B||K| + |I|^2|B|)$ |

The model is a **mixed-integer linear program** that jointly decides (i) **retiming** ($A_{i,s}, D_{i,s}$), (ii) **reordering** ($\theta_{i,j,b}$), (iii) **rerouting** ($y_{i,b}$), (iv) **cancellation** ($\text{cancel}_i$), and (v) **speed profiles** ($v_{i,b,k}, a_{i,b,k}$), while guaranteeing conflict-free, executable, and energy-aware operations under partial segment blockage.

Text:
# Passenger-Oriented Train Rescheduling MILP Model

Below is a complete Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation for the passenger-oriented real-time train rescheduling problem in an urban rail transit network, incorporating time-varying sectional passenger demands, flexible train composition, and rolling stock circulation, as described in the introduction.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $L$ | Set of sections (links between consecutive stations), indexed by $l$ |
| $T$ | Set of trains operating within the planning horizon, indexed by $i$ |
| $K$ | Set of time intervals (piecewise-constant approximation of demand), indexed by $k$ |
| $U$ | Set of train units (cars) available in the depot, indexed by $u$ |
| $R$ | Set of rolling-stock vehicle types, indexed by $r$ |
| $P$ | Set of passenger origin–destination (OD) pairs, indexed by $p = (o_p, d_p)$ |
| $H$ | Prediction horizon, indexed by $h$ (MPC step) |

**Derived sets:**
- $S_{term}$: Terminal stations
- $L(s)$: Sections incident to station $s$
- $T_{dep}(s)$: Trains departing from station $s$
- $T_{arr}(s)$: Trains arriving at station $s$

---

## 2. Parameters

### 2.1 Time and Operational Parameters
| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $\Delta_k$ | Duration of time interval $k$ | min |
| $\tau^{run}_{l}$ | Minimum running time on section $l$ | min |
| $\tau^{run,max}_{l}$ | Maximum running time on section $l$ | min |
| $\tau^{dwl,min}_s$ / $\tau^{dwl,max}_s$ | Min/max dwell time at station $s$ | min |
| $h^{min}_s$ / $h^{max}_s$ | Min/max headway at station $s$ | min |
| $\tau^{turn}_s$ | Turnaround time at terminal $s$ | min |

### 2.2 Capacity and Composition Parameters
| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $cap_r$ | Seating/loading capacity of rolling-stock type $r$ |
| $n^{max}$ | Maximum number of units per train |
| $n^{min}$ | Minimum number of units per train |
| $C^{fleet}$ | Total available rolling-stock units in the fleet |

### 2.3 Passenger Demand Parameters
| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\lambda_{s,k}$ | Arrival rate of passengers at station $s$ during interval $k$ (pass/min) |
| $\delta_{p,l}$ | 1 if OD pair $p$ traverses section $l$, 0 otherwise |
| $\gamma_{p,s}$ | 1 if OD pair $p$ alights at station $s$, 0 otherwise |

### 2.4 Cost Parameters
| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $c^w$ | Cost per passenger-minute of waiting time |
| $c^{tr}$ | Cost per passenger-minute of in-vehicle travel time |
| $c^e$ | Energy cost per train-minute |
| $c^{rs}$ | Cost per rolling-stock unit-hour |
| $c^{dev}$ | Penalty per minute of timetable deviation |

### 2.5 MPC Parameters
| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $H_p$ | Prediction horizon length |
| $H_c$ | Control horizon length |
| $t_0$ | Current MPC step time |
| $\hat{a}_{i,s}$ | Actual (measured) arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\hat{d}_{i,s}$ | Actual (measured) departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Timetable Variables (continuous)
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s}$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | Departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $t^{run}_{i,l}$ | Running time of train $i$ on section $l$ |
| $t^{dwl}_{i,s}$ | Dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |

### 3.2 Composition Variables (integer)
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $n_{i}$ | Number of units composing train $i$ |
| $z_{i,r}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses rolling-stock type $r$, 0 otherwise |

### 3.3 Stopping Variables (binary)
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $x_{i,s}$ | 1 if train $i$ stops at station $s$, 0 otherwise |

### 3.4 Rolling-Stock Circulation Variables (binary)
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $y_{i,j}$ | 1 if train $j$ inherits rolling stock from train $i$, 0 otherwise |
| $w_{i,s}$ | 1 if train $i$ starts/ends service at station $s$, 0 otherwise |

### 3.5 Passenger Flow Variables (continuous)
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $f_{i,s,p}$ | Number of OD-pair-$p$ passengers boarding train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $q_{i,s,p}$ | Number of OD-pair-$p$ passengers alighting from train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $u_{i,s}$ | Number of passengers on board train $i$ upon departure from station $s$ |
| $W_{s,k}$ | Average waiting time of passengers arriving at station $s$ in interval $k$ |

### 3.6 Auxiliary Variables
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $\rho_{i,s}$ | Load factor of train $i$ departing station $s$ |
| $\sigma_{i,s}$ | Slack for timetable deviation |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the total weighted cost over the prediction horizon:

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{c^w \sum_{s \in S} \sum_{k \in K} \lambda_{s,k} \Delta_k \, W_{s,k}}_{\text{Passenger waiting time}} 
+ \underbrace{c^{tr} \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{l \in L} t^{run}_{i,l} \, \bar{u}_{i,l}}_{\text{In-vehicle travel time}}
+ \underbrace{c^e \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{l \in L} t^{run}_{i,l}}_{\text{Energy consumption}}
+ \underbrace{c^{rs} \sum_{i \in T} n_i \cdot \tau^{svc}_i}_{\text{Rolling-stock usage}}
+ \underbrace{c^{dev} \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \sigma_{i,s}}_{\text{Timetable deviation}}
$$

where $\bar{u}_{i,l}$ is the average on-board passengers on section $l$ for train $i$, and $\tau^{svc}_i$ is the total service time of train $i$.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable Consistency Constraints

**Arrival–departure relation at each station:**
$$
a_{i,s} + t^{dwl}_{i,s} = d_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \tag{1}
$$

**Running time on each section:**
$$
a_{i,s_{l}^{end}} - d_{i,s_{l}^{start}} = t^{run}_{i,l} \quad \forall i \in T,\; l \in L \tag{2}
$$

**Dwell time bounds (only if stopping):**
$$
\tau^{dwl,min}_s \cdot x_{i,s} \leq t^{dwl}_{i,s} \leq \tau^{dwl,max}_s \cdot x_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \tag{3}
$$

**Running time bounds:**
$$
\tau^{run,min}_l \leq t^{run}_{i,l} \leq \tau^{run,max}_l \quad \forall i \in T,\; l \in L \tag{4}
$$

**Turnaround at terminals:**
$$
d_{j,s} - a_{i,s} \geq \tau^{turn}_s \cdot y_{i,j} \quad \forall s \in S_{term},\; (i,j) \in T \times T \tag{5}
$$

### 5.2 Headway and Safety Constraints

**Minimum headway between consecutive trains:**
$$
d_{i+1,s} - d_{i,s} \geq h^{min}_s \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \tag{6}
$$

**Maximum headway (service regularity):**
$$
d_{i+1,s} - d_{i,s} \leq h^{max}_s \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \tag{7}
$$

### 5.3 Flexible Train Composition Constraints

**Composition limits:**
$$
n^{min} \leq n_i \leq n^{max} \quad \forall i \in T \tag{8}
$$

**Rolling-stock type selection:**
$$
n_i = \sum_{r \in R} z_{i,r} \cdot cap_r^{unit} \quad \forall i \in T \tag{9}
$$

$$
\sum_{r \in R} z_{i,r} = 1 \quad \forall i \in T \tag{10}
$$

**Fleet size limit:**
$$
\sum_{i \in T} n_i \leq C^{fleet} \quad \tag{11}
$$

### 5.4 Rolling-Stock Circulation Constraints

**Flow conservation for rolling stock:**
$$
\sum_{j \in T} y_{i,j} - \sum_{j \in T} y_{j,i} = 
\begin{cases}
1 & \text{if train } i \text{ starts service} \\
-1 & \text{if train } i \text{ ends service} \\
0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases} \tag{12}
$$

**Composition consistency for inherited rolling stock:**
$$
n_j \geq n_i - M(1 - y_{i,j}) \quad \forall (i,j) \in T \times T \tag{13}
$$

$$
n_j \leq n_i + M(1 - y_{i,j}) \quad \forall (i,j) \in T \times T \tag{14}
$$

**Depot start/end assignment:**
$$
\sum_{s \in S} w_{i,s} = 1 \quad \forall i \in T \tag{15}
$$

### 5.5 Passenger Flow Constraints

**Boarding only at stops:**
$$
f_{i,s,p} \leq M \cdot x_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S,\; p \in P \tag{16}
$$

**Alighting only at destination:**
$$
q_{i,s,p} \leq M \cdot \gamma_{p,s} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S,\; p \in P \tag{17}
$$

**Passenger flow conservation on board:**
$$
u_{i,s_{l}^{end}} = u_{i,s_{l}^{start}} + \sum_{p \in P} f_{i,s_{l}^{end},p} - \sum_{p \in P} q_{i,s_{l}^{end},p} \quad \forall i \in T,\; l \in L \tag{18}
$$

**Initial load at origin:**
$$
u_{i,s_0} = \sum_{p \in P} f_{i,s_0,p} \quad \forall i \in T \tag{19}
$$

**Train capacity constraint:**
$$
u_{i,s} \leq \sum_{r \in R} z_{i,r} \cdot cap_r \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \tag{20}
$$

**Demand satisfaction (all waiting passengers must board):**
$$
\sum_{i \in T_{dep}(s) \cap \{k\}} f_{i,s,p} = \lambda_{s,k} \Delta_k \cdot \alpha_{p,s} \quad \forall s \in S,\; k \in K,\; p \in P \tag{21}
$$

where $\alpha_{p,s}$ is the proportion of demand at $s$ belonging to OD pair $p$.

### 5.6 Waiting Time Approximation

**Average waiting time (linearized):**
$$
W_{s,k} \geq d_{i,s} - (t_{k}^{start} + \Delta_k/2) - M(1 - \beta_{i,s,k}) \quad \forall s, k, i \in T_{dep}(s) \tag{22}
$$

$$
\sum_{i \in T_{dep}(s)} \beta_{i,s,k} = 1 \quad \forall s \in S,\; k \in K \tag{23}
$$

$$
W_{s,k} \geq 0 \quad \forall s \in S,\; k \in K \tag{24}
$$

where $\beta_{i,s,k}$ is a binary selector indicating which train serves interval $k$ at station $s$.

### 5.7 MPC Initial-Condition Constraints

**Anchoring to actual measurements:**
$$
a_{i,s} = \hat{a}_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T^{past},\; s \in S \tag{25}
$$

$$
d_{i,s} = \hat{d}_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T^{past},\; s \in S \tag{26}
$$

**Timetable deviation penalty:**
$$
\sigma_{i,s} \geq |a_{i,s} - a^{nom}_{i,s}| \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \tag{27}
$$

### 5.8 Presolve-Reduced Variable Domain (LSTM Output)

After presolve techniques prune infeasible integer assignments, the remaining binary variables satisfy:
$$
x_{i,s} \in \mathcal{X}^{LSTM}_{i,s} \subseteq \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \tag{28}
$$

$$
n_i \in \mathcal{N}^{LSTM}_i \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_{[n^{min}, n^{max}]} \quad \forall i \in T \tag{29}
$$

where $\mathcal{X}^{LSTM}$ and $\mathcal{N}^{LSTM}$ are the reduced domains output by the LSTM network.

---

## 6. Model Summary

| Component | Type | Count (approx.) |
|-----------|------|-----------------|
| Continuous variables | $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, t^{run}_{i,l}, t^{dwl}_{i,s}, u_{i,s}, f_{i,s,p}, q_{i,s,p}, W_{s,k}, \sigma_{i,s}$ | $O(|T||S| + |T||S||P|)$ |
| Integer variables | $n_i, z_{i,r}$ | $O(|T||R|)$ |
| Binary variables | $x_{i,s}, y_{i,j}, w_{i,s}, \beta_{i,s,k}$ | $O(|T||S| + |T|^2 + |T||S||K|)$ |
| Constraints | Eqs. (1)–(29) | $O(|T||S| + |T||S||P|)$ |

---

## 7. Key Assumptions

1. **Piecewise-constant demand:** Passenger arrival rates $\lambda_{s,k}$ are constant within each interval $k$ of length $\Delta_k$ (Assumption A1).
2. **Single-line bidirectional operation:** Trains operate on a single corridor with two directions (Assumption A2).
3. **Homogeneous rolling stock within a train:** All units in a train $i$ have the same type $r$ (Assumption A3).
4. **Perfect information on current state:** Actual arrival/departure times $\hat{a}_{i,s}, \hat{d}_{i,s}$ are known at each MPC step (Assumption A4).
5. **No passenger denial:** All waiting passengers can board the next available train with sufficient capacity (Assumption A5).
6. **Deterministic demand within horizon:** Future demand is predicted (point forecast) and treated as deterministic within each MPC step (Assumption A6).
7. **Linear energy model:** Energy consumption is proportional to running time (Assumption A7).
8. **Fixed OD structure:** OD pair proportions $\alpha_{p,s}$ are known and time-invariant within the horizon (Assumption A8).
9. **Big-M constants:** $M$ is chosen sufficiently large to relax logical conditions without loss of tightness (Assumption A9).
10. **LSTM feasibility guarantee:** The LSTM network is trained to output only integer assignments that satisfy presolve-pruned feasibility sets (Assumption A10).

---

This MILP formulation captures the passenger-oriented train rescheduling problem with flexible composition and rolling-stock circulation, and is suitable for solution by branch-and-cut solvers (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX) within an MPC framework, where the LSTM-predicted integer variables are fixed and the remaining continuous variables are optimized online.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## Sets and Indices

- $T = \{1,2,\ldots,|T|\}$: set of trains, indexed by $t$
- $I = \{1,2,\ldots,|I|\}$: set of stations, indexed by $i$, ordered along the line
- $S = \{1,2,\ldots,|I|-1\}$: set of segments, indexed by $s$, where segment $s$ connects station $s$ to station $s+1$
- $K = \{1,2,\ldots,|K|\}$: set of time discretization indices, indexed by $k$, with step duration $\Delta t$
- $D = \{0,1\}$: set of directions/tracks ($0$ = original, $1$ = opposite/diverted)

## Parameters

- $L_s$: length of segment $s$ (km)
- $a_{t,i}^{\text{arr}}, a_{t,i}^{\text{dep}}$: scheduled arrival/departure time of train $t$ at station $i$
- $\tau_{t,i}^{\min}, \tau_{t,i}^{\max}$: minimum and maximum dwell time of train $t$ at station $i$
- $v^{\max}, v^{\min}$: maximum/minimum allowed speed
- $a^{\max}, b^{\max}$: maximum acceleration and deceleration
- $\Delta t$: time step duration (hours)
- $\rho_t$: weight of delay for train $t$
- $\gamma_t$: weight of energy consumption for train $t$
- $\mu_t$: penalty for cancellation of train $t$
- $M$: sufficiently large constant (big-M)
- $\delta_s \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if segment $s$ is in disruption area
- $\omega_s^{\text{start}}, \omega_s^{\text{end}}$: disruption time window for segment $s$
- $h^{\text{seg}}_{\min}, h^{\text{sta}}_{\min}$: minimum segment and station headways
- $g_{t,s}$: energy coefficient of train $t$ on segment $s$

## Decision Variables

- $x_{t,i} \geq 0$: actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $i$ (continuous)
- $y_{t,i} \geq 0$: actual departure time of train $t$ at station $i$ (continuous)
- $u_{t,i} \geq 0$: actual dwell time of train $t$ at station $i$ (continuous)
- $z_{t,s,d} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ traverses segment $s$ on track $d$
- $o_{t,t',s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ passes through segment $s$ before train $t'$
- $q_{t,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ is in segment $s$ at time step $k$
- $v_{t,s,k} \geq 0$: speed of train $t$ in segment $s$ at time step $k$ (continuous)
- $p_{t,s,k} \geq 0$: position of train $t$ in segment $s$ at time step $k$ (continuous, km)
- $e_t \geq 0$: energy consumption of train $t$ (continuous)
- $c_t \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ is cancelled
- $r_{t,i} \geq 0$: arrival delay of train $t$ at station $i$ (continuous)
- $w_{t,i} \geq 0$: departure delay of train $t$ at station $i$ (continuous)
- $\sigma_{t,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses segment $s$
- $o^{\text{sta}}_{t,t',i} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering of trains $t,t'$ at station $i$

## Objective Function

Minimize the total weighted sum of arrival delays, departure delays, energy consumption, and cancellations:

$$\min Z = \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{i \in I}\left[\rho_t\left(r_{t,i} + w_{t,i}\right) + \gamma_t\, e_t\right] + \sum_{t \in T}\mu_t\, c_t$$

## Constraints

### Delay Definitions (Positive Parts)
$$r_{t,i} \geq x_{t,i} - a_{t,i}^{\text{arr}}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; i \in I$$
$$w_{t,i} \geq y_{t,i} - a_{t,i}^{\text{dep}}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; i \in I$$

### (1) Cancellation Logic
For cancelled trains, times are frozen at scheduled values:
$$a_{t,i}^{\text{arr}} - M\,c_t \leq x_{t,i} \leq a_{t,i}^{\text{arr}} + M\,c_t, \quad \forall t,i$$
$$a_{t,i}^{\text{dep}} - M\,c_t \leq y_{t,i} \leq a_{t,i}^{\text{dep}} + M\,c_t, \quad \forall t,i$$

### (2) Arrival–Departure Relation at Stations
$$x_{t,i} + u_{t,i} = y_{t,i} + M\,c_t, \quad \forall t \in T,\; i \in I$$

### (3) Dwell Time Bounds
$$\tau_{t,i}^{\min}(1-c_t) \leq u_{t,i} \leq \tau_{t,i}^{\max} + M\,c_t, \quad \forall t \in T,\; i \in I$$

### (4–5) Travel Time Across Segments
$$x_{t,i+1} = y_{t,i} + \Delta t \sum_{k \in K} q_{t,s,k} + M\,c_t, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S,\; s = i$$

### (6) Speed–Position Dynamics (Linearized)
For all $t \in T$, $s \in S$, and consecutive time steps $k, k+1 \in K$:
$$p_{t,s,k+1} = p_{t,s,k} + v_{t,s,k}\,\Delta t + 0.5(v_{t,s,k+1} - v_{t,s,k})\,\Delta t + M(2 - q_{t,s,k} - q_{t,s,k+1})$$
$$p_{t,s,k+1} \geq p_{t,s,k} + v_{t,s,k}\,\Delta t + 0.5(v_{t,s,k+1} - v_{t,s,k})\,\Delta t - M(2 - q_{t,s,k} - q_{t,s,k+1})$$

### (7) Speed Limits
$$v^{\min}\,q_{t,s,k} \leq v_{t,s,k} \leq v^{\max}\,q_{t,s,k}, \quad \forall t,s,k$$

### (8) Acceleration/Deceleration Limits
$$v_{t,s,k+1} - v_{t,s,k} \leq a^{\max}\,\Delta t + M(2 - q_{t,s,k} - q_{t,s,k+1}), \quad \forall t,s,k$$
$$v_{t,s,k+1} - v_{t,s,k} \geq -b^{\max}\,\Delta t - M(2 - q_{t,s,k} - q_{t,s,k+1}), \quad \forall t,s,k$$

### (9, 19) Segment Entry/Exit Position
$$p_{t,s,k_1} \leq M\,\sigma_{t,s}, \quad \forall t,s$$
$$L_s\,\sigma_{t,s} - M(1-\sigma_{t,s}) \leq p_{t,s,k_{|K|}} \leq L_s\,\sigma_{t,s} + M\,c_t, \quad \forall t,s$$

Monotonicity of position while in segment:
$$p_{t,s,k+1} \geq p_{t,s,k} - M(1 - q_{t,s,k}), \quad \forall t,s,k$$

### (10) Segment–Track Assignment
$$\sum_{d \in D} z_{t,s,d} = 1 - c_t, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S$$

### Linking Segment Usage and Track Assignment
$$\sigma_{t,s} \leq \sum_{k \in K} q_{t,s,k}, \quad \forall t,s$$
$$\sigma_{t,s} \geq q_{t,s,k}, \quad \forall t,s,k$$
$$z_{t,s,d} \leq \sigma_{t,s} + c_t, \quad \forall t,s,d$$

### (11) Single-Track Capacity (Bidirectional Conflict Resolution)
At most one train may occupy each segment at any time step:
$$\sum_{t \in T} q_{t,s,k} \leq 1, \quad \forall s \in S,\; k \in K$$

### (12–13) Disruption Avoidance
If segment $s$ is disrupted ($\delta_s = 1$) and time $k$ lies within $[\omega_s^{\text{start}}, \omega_s^{\text{end}}]$:
$$z_{t,s,0} = 0, \quad q_{t,s,k} = 0, \quad \forall t \in T$$

This forces affected trains to use the opposite track ($d = 1$) during the disruption window.

### (15) Ordering Logic Between Trains on Segments
For each pair $(t,t')$ with $t < t'$ and each segment $s$:
$$o_{t,t',s} \leq \sigma_{t,s}, \quad o_{t,t',s} \leq \sigma_{t',s}$$
$$o_{t,t',s} \geq \sigma_{t,s} + \sigma_{t',s} - 1$$

### (16) Segment Headway Constraints
For each pair $(t,t')$ and segment $s$ (with $i+1$ being the exit station):
$$x_{t',i+1} - x_{t,i+1} \geq h^{\text{seg}}_{\min}\, o_{t,t',s} - M(c_t + c_{t'}) - M(2 - \sigma_{t,s} - \sigma_{t',s})$$
$$x_{t,i+1} - x_{t',i+1} \geq h^{\text{seg}}_{\min}(1 - o_{t,t',s}) - M(c_t + c_{t'}) - M(2 - \sigma_{t,s} - \sigma_{t',s})$$

### (17) Energy Consumption Model (Linearized)
$$e_t = \sum_{s \in S}\sum_{k \in K} g_{t,s}\, q_{t,s,k}\, v_{t,s,k}\, \Delta t, \quad \forall t \in T$$

### (20) Cancelled Trains Have No Activity
$$q_{t,s,k} \leq 1 - c_t, \quad v_{t,s,k} \leq v^{\max}(1-c_t), \quad p_{t,s,k} \leq L^{\max}(1-c_t), \quad \forall t,s,k$$

### (21) Station Headway Constraints
For each pair $(t,t')$ and station $i$:
$$x_{t',i} - x_{t,i} \geq h^{\text{sta}}_{\min}\, o^{\text{sta}}_{t,t',i} - M(c_t + c_{t'})$$
$$x_{t,i} - x_{t',i} \geq h^{\text{sta}}_{\min}(1 - o^{\text{sta}}_{t,t',i}) - M(c_t + c_{t'})$$

### Boundary Conditions
Origin station arrival (train cannot depart before scheduled):
$$x_{t,i_1} \geq a_{t,i_1}^{\text{arr}} - M\,c_t, \quad \forall t \in T$$

Terminal station departure (train must arrive by final scheduled time):
$$y_{t,i_{|I|}} \leq a_{t,i_{|I|}}^{\text{dep}} + M\,c_t, \quad \forall t \in T$$

## Model Summary

The model integrates four rescheduling dimensions (retiming through $x_{t,i}, y_{t,i}, u_{t,i}$; reordering through $o_{t,t',s}$ and $o^{\text{sta}}_{t,t',i}$; rerouting through $z_{t,s,d}$; cancellation through $c_t$) with continuous speed management (through $v_{t,s,k}$ and $p_{t,s,k}$). The disruption scenario is captured by directly forbidding original-track usage ($d = 0$) within the disruption time window on affected segments, while permitting rerouting to the opposite track subject to the same single-track capacity constraint, which simultaneously resolves bidirectional conflicts. The objective balances weighted train delays, weighted energy consumption, and cancellation penalties.

## Key Assumptions

1. **Time discretization**: A uniform time step $\Delta t$ is used; the discretization is assumed fine enough to faithfully represent speed profiles.
2. **Linearized dynamics**: Train motion is linearized within each time step using constant-acceleration kinematics.
3. **Partial blockage**: Disruption affects only one side of the track, allowing rerouting to the opposite track during the disruption window.
4. **Single-track segment capacity**: Each segment can be occupied by at most one train at any time (handles both normal and rerouting operations).
5. **Bidirectional sharing**: Opposite-direction trains share track resources during rerouting, coordinated through the unified capacity constraint.
6. **Linear energy approximation**: Energy is modeled as a linear function of speed and time per segment.
7. **Discrete cancellation**: Cancellation is treated as a binary decision with large penalty $\mu_t$.

Text:
# MILP Formulation: Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Railway Infrastructure Constraints

## 1. Problem Description and Modeling Assumptions

We formulate a Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP) that integrates the **composition model** (assigning rolling stock units to trips) with the **infrastructure model** (verifying feasibility of shunting movements on station tracks). The model supports short delays of passenger trains to enable shunting, trip cancellations as a last resort, and balances three objectives: operational cost, passenger service quality, and adherence to the original plan.

**Key assumptions (clearly marked):**
- **(A1)** Time is discretized into uniform periods $\tau \in \mathcal{P}$ (e.g., 1-minute slots).
- **(A2)** Each track can accommodate at most one train/shunting movement at any time period.
- **(A3)** Passenger train delays are bounded by a small constant $\Delta^{\max}$ (a few minutes) and are absorbed by timetable buffers.
- **(A4)** Rolling stock units are homogeneous within a type but may differ across types.
- **(A5)** The original rolling stock plan is given and deviations are penalized.
- **(A6)** Shunting movements are pre-defined candidate moves between specific tracks at specific times.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of passenger train trips, indexed by $t, t'$ |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Set of rolling stock units, indexed by $r$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of rolling stock types, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{TR}_s$ | Set of tracks at station $s$, indexed by $tr$ |
| $\mathcal{M}$ | Set of candidate shunting movements, indexed by $m$ |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Set of discretized time periods, indexed by $\tau$ |
| $\mathcal{L}$ | Set of train lines, indexed by $\ell$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^{\text{dep}}_s \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Trips departing from station $s$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^{\text{arr}}_s \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Trips arriving at station $s$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^{\text{succ}}(t) \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Trips that can directly succeed trip $t$ (same station, time-feasible) |
| $\mathcal{T}^{\text{pred}}(t) \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Trips that can directly precede trip $t$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

**Rolling stock and trip data:**
- $C_r$: Seat capacity of unit $r$
- $D_t$: Passenger demand for trip $t$
- $\sigma_t, \varepsilon_t \in \mathcal{S}$: Start and end stations of trip $t$
- $\alpha_t, \beta_t \in \mathcal{P}$: Scheduled arrival and departure times of trip $t$
- $\text{dist}_t$: Distance (or duration) of trip $t$
- $o_{r,t} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if unit $r$ is assigned to trip $t$ in the **original** plan
- $\text{type}_r \in \mathcal{K}$: Type of unit $r$

**Shunting movement data:**
- $\text{tr}_m \in \mathcal{TR}$: Track used by movement $m$
- $\theta_m \in \mathcal{P}$: Earliest start time of movement $m$
- $\delta_m \in \mathcal{P}$: Duration of movement $m$
- $s^{\text{from}}_m, s^{\text{to}}_m \in \mathcal{S}$: Origin and destination station of movement $m$
- $t^{\text{from}}_m, t^{\text{to}}_m \in \mathcal{T}$: Trip before and after movement $m$

**Infrastructure data:**
- $\text{Cap}_{tr} \in \mathbb{Z}^+$: Capacity of track $tr$ (typically 1)
- $\rho^{\min}_{tr}$: Minimum headway between consecutive movements on track $tr$

**Objective weights and costs:**
- $w^{\text{op}}, w^{\text{pax}}, w^{\text{plan}} \geq 0$: Weights of the three objective components
- $c^{\text{op}}$: Operational cost per unit-distance (or per unit-hour)
- $c^{\text{stand}}$: Cost per standing passenger
- $c^{\text{cancel}}$: Cost per cancelled trip
- $c^{\text{delay}}$: Cost per minute of delay
- $c^{\text{dev}}$: Cost per unit-trip deviation from original plan

**Bounds:**
- $\Delta^{\max}$: Maximum allowed delay (minutes)
- $M$: A sufficiently large positive number (big-M)

---

## 4. Decision Variables

**Composition variables:**
- $x_{r,t} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if unit $r$ is assigned to trip $t$
- $f_{r,t,t'} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if unit $r$ transitions directly from trip $t$ to trip $t'$
- $y_m \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if shunting movement $m$ is executed
- $z_{r,m} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if unit $r$ performs shunting movement $m$

**Infrastructure variables:**
- $w_{tr,\tau} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if track $tr$ is occupied at time $\tau$
- $q_{tr,\tau} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if a passenger train occupies track $tr$ at time $\tau$

**Service quality variables:**
- $\delta_t \geq 0$: Delay (in time periods) of trip $t$
- $b_t \geq 0$: Number of standing passengers on trip $t$
- $\text{canc}_t \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trip $t$ is cancelled

**Plan deviation variables:**
- $d^{+}_{r,t}, d^{-}_{r,t} \geq 0$: Positive/negative deviation of unit $r$ on trip $t$ from original plan

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize a weighted combination of three objectives:

$$
\min \; Z = w^{\text{op}} \cdot Z^{\text{op}} + w^{\text{pax}} \cdot Z^{\text{pax}} + w^{\text{plan}} \cdot Z^{\text{plan}}
$$

**Operational cost:**
$$
Z^{\text{op}} = c^{\text{op}} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} \text{dist}_t \cdot x_{r,t}
$$

**Passenger service cost:**
$$
Z^{\text{pax}} = \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \left( c^{\text{stand}} \cdot b_t + c^{\text{cancel}} \cdot \text{canc}_t + c^{\text{delay}} \cdot \delta_t \right)
$$

**Plan deviation cost:**
$$
Z^{\text{plan}} = c^{\text{dev}} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} \left( d^{+}_{r,t} + d^{-}_{r,t} \right)
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Composition and Capacity Constraints

**(C1) Trip coverage** — Each non-cancelled trip must be served by at least one unit:
$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} x_{r,t} \geq 1 - \text{canc}_t \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
$$

**(C2) Composition feasibility** — A trip requires a minimum number of units of compatible types (e.g., multiple traction units):
$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} x_{r,t} \geq N^{\min}_t \cdot (1 - \text{canc}_t) \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
$$
where $N^{\min}_t$ is the minimum required number of units for trip $t$ (assumption A4).

**(C3) Capacity for seated passengers:**
$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} C_r \cdot x_{r,t} \geq D_t - b_t \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
$$

**(C4) Standing passengers bounded:**
$$
b_t \leq D_t \cdot (1 - \text{canc}_t) \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
$$

### 6.2 Flow Conservation Constraints

**(C5) Unit balance at stations** — A unit arriving at a station must either depart on a successor trip, perform a shunting movement, or be held:
$$
\sum_{t' \in \mathcal{T}^{\text{succ}}(t)} f_{r,t,t'} + \sum_{m \in \mathcal{M}: t^{\text{from}}_m = t} z_{r,m} = x_{r,t} \quad \forall r \in \mathcal{R}, \; t \in \mathcal{T}
$$

**(C6) Unit balance for departures:**
$$
\sum_{t' \in \mathcal{T}^{\text{pred}}(t)} f_{r,t',t} + \sum_{m \in \mathcal{M}: t^{\text{to}}_m = t} z_{r,m} = x_{r,t} \quad \forall r \in \mathcal{R}, \; t \in \mathcal{T}
$$

**(C7) Linking flow and assignment:**
$$
f_{r,t,t'} \leq x_{r,t}, \quad f_{r,t,t'} \leq x_{r,t'} \quad \forall r, t, t'
$$

**(C8) Linking shunting and assignment:**
$$
z_{r,m} \leq x_{r, t^{\text{from}}_m}, \quad z_{r,m} \leq x_{r, t^{\text{to}}_m} \quad \forall r, m
$$

**(C9) Shunting movement activation:**
$$
y_m = \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} z_{r,m} \quad \forall m \in \mathcal{M}
$$

### 6.3 Shunting Movement Time-Window Constraints

**(C10) Shunting must finish before next trip departure:**
$$
\theta_m + \delta_m \cdot y_m \leq \beta_{t^{\text{to}}_m} + \delta_{t^{\text{to}}_m} - \alpha_{t^{\text{from}}_m} - \delta_{t^{\text{from}}_m} + M(1 - y_m) \quad \forall m
$$

**(C11) Shunting must start after previous trip arrival:**
$$
\theta_m \geq \alpha_{t^{\text{from}}_m} + \delta_{t^{\text{from}}_m} - M(1 - y_m) \quad \forall m
$$

### 6.4 Infrastructure (Track Occupation) Constraints

**(C12) Shunting occupies its track for its duration:**
$$
\sum_{\tau' = \theta_m}^{\theta_m + \delta_m - 1} w_{\text{tr}_m, \tau'} \geq \delta_m \cdot y_m \quad \forall m \in \mathcal{M}
$$

**(C13) Passenger train track occupation** — Each (possibly delayed) arrival/departure of trip $t$ at station $s$ occupies a track during a contiguous interval. For each trip $t$ and each station $s$ it visits, let $\mathcal{Q}(t,s)$ denote the set of time periods when trip $t$ occupies some track at $s$ (including delay). Then:
$$
w_{tr, \tau} \geq q_{tr, \tau} \quad \forall tr, \tau
$$
where $q_{tr,\tau} = 1$ if any trip $t$ uses track $tr$ at time $\tau$ (computed from $\alpha_t, \beta_t, \delta_t$ and routing decisions).

**(C14) Track capacity** — At most $\text{Cap}_{tr}$ movements on track $tr$ at any time:
$$
w_{tr, \tau} \leq \text{Cap}_{tr} \quad \forall tr, \tau
$$

**(C15) Minimum headway between consecutive movements on the same track:**
$$
w_{tr, \tau} + w_{tr, \tau+1} + \dots + w_{tr, \tau + \rho^{\min}_{tr} - 1} \leq \text{Cap}_{tr} + M(1 - w_{tr, \tau}) \quad \forall tr, \tau
$$

### 6.5 Train Delay Constraints

**(C16) Delay bounds:**
$$
0 \leq \delta_t \leq \Delta^{\max} \cdot (1 - \text{canc}_t) \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
$$

**(C17) Delay propagation along a line** (assumption A3 — delays propagate through timetable buffers):
$$
\delta_{t'} \geq \delta_t - M(1 - f_{r,t,t'}) \quad \forall r, (t,t') \in \mathcal{T}^{\text{succ}}
$$

### 6.6 Plan Deviation Constraints

**(C18) Linearization of absolute deviation:**
$$
x_{r,t} - o_{r,t} = d^{+}_{r,t} - d^{-}_{r,t} \quad \forall r, t
$$

**(C19) Non-negativity:**
$$
d^{+}_{r,t} \geq 0, \quad d^{-}_{r,t} \geq 0 \quad \forall r, t
$$

### 6.7 Cancellation and Linking Constraints

**(C20) Cancelled trips have no assignment:**
$$
x_{r,t} \leq 1 - \text{canc}_t \quad \forall r, t
$$

**(C21) Cancelled trips generate no flow:**
$$
f_{r,t,t'} \leq 1 - \text{canc}_t, \quad f_{r,t,t'} \leq 1 - \text{canc}_{t'} \quad \forall r, t, t'
$$

**(C22) Cancelled trips have no delay:**
$$
\delta_t \leq M \cdot (1 - \text{canc}_t) \quad \forall t
$$

### 6.8 Variable Domains

$$
x_{r,t}, f_{r,t,t'}, y_m, z_{r,m}, w_{tr,\tau}, q_{tr,\tau}, \text{canc}_t \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
\delta_t, b_t, d^{+}_{r,t}, d^{-}_{r,t} \geq 0
$$

---

## 7. Notes on the Formulation

1. **Two-tier decision structure**: Variables $\{x, f, y, z\}$ correspond to the *composition model*; variables $\{w, q, \delta\}$ correspond to the *infrastructure model*. The linking constraints (C5–C11, C13) couple them.

2. **Benders' decomposition view**: In the Combinatorial Benders' approach described in the paper, the composition variables are the *master* problem and the infrastructure variables are the *subproblem*. Infeasible combinations of $y_m$ (or $z_{r,m}$) yield combinatorial cuts of the form $\sum_{m \in \mathcal{M}^*} (1 - y_m) \geq 1$ for each conflicting set $\mathcal{M}^*$.

3. **Iterative heuristic view**: The iterative heuristic processes shunting movements one by one, fixing $y_m$ sequentially and re-solving the infrastructure subproblem. This corresponds to fixing subsets of $y$ variables in the unified MILP above.

4. **Scalability**: The track-occupation variables $w_{tr,\tau}$ grow with $|\mathcal{TR}| \cdot |\mathcal{P}|$. For large instances, time aggregation or Benders' decomposition (as in the paper) is recommended.

5. **Tractability**: The model is a MILP solvable by standard solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX). The objective weights $w^{\text{op}}, w^{\text{pax}}, w^{\text{plan}}$ allow the planner to emphasize different aspects (operational efficiency, passenger service, stick-to-the-plan).

---

## 8. Summary of Assumptions Used

| ID | Assumption |
|---|---|
| A1 | Time discretization into uniform periods |
| A2 | Single-train track capacity |
| A3 | Short delays absorbed by timetable buffers |
| A4 | Homogeneous units within type, possibly heterogeneous across types |
| A5 | Original plan available and deviations penalized |
| A6 | Pre-defined candidate shunting movements |
| A7 | Delay propagation along train lines (C17) |
| A8 | Minimum required number of units per trip (C2) |

Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — Full MILP Formulation

## 1. Problem Setting

A double-track high-speed line has stations indexed along the line. A disruption blocks one track (say, the up-track) of a single inter-station segment during a known time window. During that window, the intact track of that segment must be shared by trains travelling in both directions (single-track bidirectional operation). The dispatcher jointly decides **arrival/departure times, train sequence, rerouting and a discrete speed profile per (train, segment)** to minimise a weighted sum of delays and energy.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T=\{1,\dots,n_T\}$ | set of trains |
| $S=\{1,\dots,n_S\}$ | stations, ordered along the line |
| $E=\{1,\dots,n_S-1\}$ | inter-station segments; segment $e$ connects stations $e$ and $e+1$ |
| $\Sigma=\{+1,-1\}$ | track directions; $+1$ = up-track, $-1$ = down-track |
| $\sigma_t \in \Sigma$ | nominal travel direction of train $t$ (fixed for the journey) |
| $R_{t,e}$ | discrete speed profiles available to train $t$ on segment $e$ |
| $\bar\sigma = -\sigma$ | opposite direction |
| $e^B\in E$ | disrupted segment |
| $\sigma^B\in\Sigma$ | blocked track on $e^B$ |
| $\sigma^S=\bar\sigma^{B}$ | surviving track on $e^B$ (operated bidirectionally during the disruption) |

Pairs:
- $\mathcal P = \{(t,t')\in T\times T: t<t'\}$ (unordered train pairs)
- $\mathcal P^{\rm opp}=\{(t,t')\in T\times T:\sigma_t \neq \sigma_{t'}\}$ (opposite-direction pairs)

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $a^0_{t,s},\,d^0_{t,s}$ | scheduled arrival / departure time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $A^{\min}_{t,s},A^{\max}_{t,s}$ | allowed arrival window at $s$ |
| $D^{\min}_{t,s},D^{\max}_{t,s}$ | allowed departure window at $s$ |
| $\mathit{dw}^{\min}_{t,s},\,\mathit{dw}^{\max}_{t,s}$ | min / max dwell time of train $t$ at $s$ |
| $\tau_{r,t,e}$ | running time of $t$ on $e$ using profile $r$ |
| $\tau^{\min}_{t,e},\tau^{\max}_{t,e}$ | physical min / max running time on $e$ |
| $e_{r,t,e}$ | energy consumption of $t$ on $e$ using profile $r$ |
| $h^{\rm tr}_\sigma$ | minimum following headway on track $\sigma$ (same direction) |
| $h^{\rm bi}$ | minimum headway on the bidirectional single track $e^B$ |
| $h^{\rm st}$ | minimum station headway (arrival–departure separation) |
| $\mathrm{cap}_s$ | number of trains that may simultaneously occupy station $s$ |
| $T^{B,\rm st},T^{B,\rm end}$ | start / end of the disruption time window |
| $w_\tau,\,w_E$ | per-minute delay weight, per-unit-energy weight |
| $M_1,M_2,M_3,M_4$ | sufficiently large positive constants (big-M) |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

**Continuous**
- $A_{t,s}\ge 0$ — actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $D_{t,s}\ge 0$ — actual departure time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $\Delta A_{t,s}\ge 0$ — arrival delay of $t$ at $s$
- $\Delta D_{t,s}\ge 0$ — departure delay of $t$ at $s$
- $E\ge 0$ — total energy consumption

**Binary**
- $x_{r,t,e}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if speed profile $r$ is chosen for $t$ on $e$
- $y_{t,e,\sigma}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if $t$ uses track $\sigma$ on segment $e$
- $u_{t,t',e,\sigma}\in\{0,1\}$ — linearisation of $y_{t,e,\sigma}\,y_{t',e,\sigma}$
- $\theta_{t,t',e,\sigma}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if $t$ precedes $t'$ on track $\sigma$ of $e$ (same direction)
- $\pi_{t,t',e^B}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if $t$ precedes $t'$ on the shared bidirectional track of $e^B$ (opposite directions)
- $\gamma_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if $t$ departs $s$ before $t'$ arrives at $s$
- $\pi_t,\rho_t\in\{0,1\}$ — blockage-traversal mode for $t$ on $(e^B,\sigma^B)$: before / after the window (Model 1 enhancement)

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; w_\tau\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\!\Big(\Delta A_{t,s}+\Delta D_{t,s}\Big)\;+\;w_E\cdot E,
$$

with $E=\displaystyle\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{e\in E}\sum_{r\in R_{t,e}} e_{r,t,e}\,x_{r,t,e}$.

(Weights can be refined per train, station and segment if priorities differ.)

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Delay definition
$$
\Delta A_{t,s}\;\ge\;A_{t,s}-a^0_{t,s},\qquad\Delta A_{t,s}\ge 0,\qquad\forall t,s \tag{C1}
$$
$$
\Delta D_{t,s}\;\ge\;D_{t,s}-d^0_{t,s},\qquad\Delta D_{t,s}\ge 0,\qquad\forall t,s \tag{C2}
$$

### 6.2 Time windows
$$
A^{\min}_{t,s}\le A_{t,s}\le A^{\max}_{t,s},\qquad\forall t,s \tag{C3}
$$
$$
D^{\min}_{t,s}\le D_{t,s}\le D^{\max}_{t,s},\qquad\forall t,s \tag{C4}
$$

### 6.3 Dwell-time feasibility (intermediate stations $s=2,\dots,n_S-1$)
$$
\mathit{dw}^{\min}_{t,s}\;\le\;D_{t,s}-A_{t,s}\;\le\;\mathit{dw}^{\max}_{t,s},\qquad\forall t,s\in\{2,\dots,n_S-1\} \tag{C5}
$$

(For the origin $s=1$ set $A_{t,1}=0$ and for the destination $s=n_S$ drop $D_{t,n_S}$.)

### 6.4 Linking running time to discrete speed profiles
$$
A_{t,s+1}\;=\;D_{t,s}\;+\;\sum_{r\in R_{t,e}}\tau_{r,t,e}\,x_{r,t,e},\qquad \forall t\in T,\;e\in E \tag{C6}
$$
$$
\sum_{r\in R_{t,e}}x_{r,t,e}\;=\;1,\qquad\forall t,e \tag{C7}
$$
$$
\tau^{\min}_{t,e}\;\le\;\sum_{r\in R_{t,e}}\tau_{r,t,e}\,x_{r,t,e}\;\le\;\tau^{\max}_{t,e},\qquad\forall t,e \tag{C8}
$$

### 6.5 Track-routing variables
$$
\sum_{\sigma\in\Sigma} y_{t,e,\sigma}\;=\;1,\qquad\forall t,e \tag{C9}
$$
$$
y_{t,e,\sigma_t}\;=\;1,\qquad\forall t,\;e\in E\setminus\{e^B\} \tag{C10}
$$

If the blockage is interpreted as *time-windowed* (rather than permanent) on the blocked track, replace (C11)–(C12) with the mode variables:
$$
\pi_t+\rho_t\;=\;y_{t,e^B,\sigma^B},\qquad\forall t \tag{C11'}
$$
$$
A_{t,e^B+1}\;\le\;T^{B,\rm st}+M_4(1-\pi_t),\qquad\forall t \tag{C12'a}
$$
$$
D_{t,e^B}\;\ge\;T^{B,\rm end}-M_4(1-\rho_t),\qquad\forall t \tag{C12'b}
$$

Otherwise, for a *permanent* blockage during the horizon, force rerouting:
$$
y_{t,e^B,\sigma^B}\;=\;0,\qquad y_{t,e^B,\sigma^S}\;=\;1,\qquad\forall t \tag{C11''–C12''}
$$

### 6.6 Same-track / same-direction safety headway

Auxiliary $u_{t,t',e,\sigma}$ linearises $y_{t,e,\sigma}y_{t',e,\sigma}$:
$$
u_{t,t',e,\sigma}\le y_{t,e,\sigma},\quad u_{t,t',e,\sigma}\le y_{t',e,\sigma},\quad u_{t,t',e,\sigma}\ge y_{t,e,\sigma}+y_{t',e,\sigma}-1,\;\;\forall t<t',\,e,\,\sigma \tag{C13}
$$

Order variable $\theta$:
$$
\theta_{t,t',e,\sigma}\le u_{t,t',e,\sigma},\quad \theta_{t',t,e,\sigma}\le u_{t,t',e,\sigma} \tag{C14}
$$
$$
\theta_{t,t',e,\sigma}+\theta_{t',t,e,\sigma}\;\ge\;u_{t,t',e,\sigma},\quad
\theta_{t,t',e,\sigma}+\theta_{t',t,e,\sigma}\;\le\;1 \tag{C15}
$$

Big-M headway (segment $e$ lies between $s$ and $s+1$):
$$
D_{t,s}-A_{t',s+1}\;\ge\;h^{\rm tr}_\sigma \;-\; M_1\big(1-\theta_{t,t',e,\sigma}\big),\quad \forall t<t',\,e,\,\sigma \tag{C16}
$$
$$
D_{t',s}-A_{t,s+1}\;\ge\;h^{\rm tr}_\sigma \;-\; M_1\big(1-\theta_{t',t,e,\sigma}\big),\quad \forall t<t',\,e,\,\sigma \tag{C17}
$$

### 6.7 Bidirectional conflict on the shared single track $e^B$

For every opposite-direction pair $(t,t')\in\mathcal P^{\rm opp}$:
$$
\pi_{t,t',e^B}\le y_{t,e^B,\sigma^S},\quad \pi_{t,t',e^B}\le y_{t',e^B,\sigma^S} \tag{C18}
$$
$$
\pi_{t,t',e^B}+\pi_{t',t,e^B}\;=\;1 \tag{C19}
$$
$$
D_{t,s}-A_{t',s+1}\;\ge\;h^{\rm bi}-M_2\big(1-\pi_{t,t',e^B}\big),\qquad \forall(t,t')\in\mathcal P^{\rm opp} \tag{C20}
$$
$$
D_{t',s}-A_{t,s+1}\;\ge\;h^{\rm bi}-M_2\,\pi_{t,t',e^B},\qquad\forall(t,t')\in\mathcal P^{\rm opp} \tag{C21}
$$

### 6.8 Station capacity (pairwise platform headway)
$$
\gamma_{t,t',s}+\gamma_{t',t,s}\;=\;1,\qquad \forall t<t',\,s \tag{C22}
$$
$$
A_{t,s}-D_{t',s}\;\ge\;h^{\rm st}-M_3\big(1-\gamma_{t,t',s}\big),\qquad\forall t<t',\,s \tag{C23}
$$
$$
A_{t',s}-D_{t,s}\;\ge\;h^{\rm st}-M_3\,\gamma_{t,t',s},\qquad\forall t<t',\,s \tag{C24}
$$

(For $\mathrm{cap}_s>1$, replace these pairwise constraints with platform-assignment variables and track counts; the structure is the same.)

### 6.9 Energy definition
$$
E\;=\;\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{e\in E}\sum_{r\in R_{t,e}}e_{r,t,e}\,x_{r,t,e} \tag{C25}
$$

### 6.10 Disruption blockage — temporal shielding (recommended when rerouting is forced)

For any train traversing $e^B$ on the surviving track, the entire occupancy interval must lie outside $[T^{B,\rm st},T^{B,\rm end}]$:
$$
A_{t,s+1}\;\le\;T^{B,\rm st}\;+\;M_4\big(1-y_{t,e^B,\sigma^S}\big),\quad\forall t,\; e^B\text{ between }s,s\!+\!1 \tag{C26}
$$
$$
D_{t,s}\;\ge\;T^{B,\rm end}\;-\;M_4\big(1-y_{t,e^B,\sigma^S}\big),\quad\forall t,\; e^B\text{ between }s,s\!+\!1 \tag{C27}
$$

These two ensure that when the train crosses the disrupted segment on the surviving track, it does so outside the closure window; otherwise the constraint becomes vacuous (the right-hand side becomes very large / negative).

### 6.11 Non-negativity / variable domains
$$
A_{t,s},D_{t,s},\Delta A_{t,s},\Delta D_{t,s},E\ge 0;\quad
x,y,\theta,\pi,\gamma\in\{0,1\} \tag{C28}
$$

---

## 7. Index Reference for the Most Important Equations

| Equation group | Role |
|---|---|
| (C6)–(C8) | Retiming ↔ discrete speed profile selection |
| (C9)–(C12) | Rerouting decisions on every segment; mandatory or conditional rerouting on $e^B$ |
| (C13)–(C17) | Reordering + safety headway on each (track, segment, same direction) |
| (C18)–(C21) | Reordering + bidirectional headway on the disrupted segment |
| (C22)–(C24) | Station platform/track capacity via pairwise headway |
| (C26)–(C27) | Temporal shielding: trains avoid the blocked track during the window |

---

## 8. Assumptions

1. **Deterministic disruption**: the window $[T^{B,\rm st},T^{B,\rm end}]$, segment $e^B$ and blocked track $\sigma^B$ are known in advance.
2. **Blockage scope**: depending on operational practice, the blocked track is either *permanently* unusable on $e^B$ during the planning horizon (use C11''–C12'') or only during the time window (use C11'–C12'b). Both alternatives are provided.
3. **Single-track bidirectional operation**: during the disruption, $\sigma^S$ on $e^B$ is shared by opposite-direction traffic under headway $h^{\rm bi}$.
4. **Fixed train direction**: each train keeps its nominal direction $\sigma_t$ throughout its journey; no reverse running.
5. **Discrete speed profiles**: $R_{t,e}$ is a finite pre-computed set per train-segment; energy and running time are linear in the binary profile choice.
6. **Deterministic running times and dwell times** (no stochastic delays beyond the considered disruption).
7. **Single track per direction outside the disruption**, modelled via the headway constraints (C16)–(C17).
8. **Big-M validity**: $M_1,M_2,M_3,M_4$ are chosen as upper bounds on inter-train separations (e.g., the planning horizon length) so constraints are non-restrictive when their associated binaries are 0.
9. **Pairwise station capacity**: station capacity $\mathrm{cap}_s$ is enforced through pairwise platform headways (extension to multi-platform stations requires additional platform-assignment binaries).
10. **Linear energy model**: traction energy is approximated by a profile-dependent constant; regenerative braking and acceleration coasting are pre-baked into $e_{r,t,e}$.
11. **Integer time unit is fine** for $x,y,u,\theta,\pi,\gamma$; the timetable variables $A,D$ remain continuous (or discretised to 1-second resolution without loss of structure).

---

## 9. Discussion

* The model simultaneously captures **retiming** (via $A,D$), **reordering** (via $\theta,\pi,\gamma$), **rerouting** (via $y$), and **speed-profile selection** (via $x$).
* Equations (C6)–(C8) are the **linking block**: the chosen speed profile determines the segment running time that appears in the timetable.
* Equations (C13)–(C17) couple retiming with sequencing and routing using **big-M**; tightness of the $M$ constants dominates the LP relaxation gap.
* The disruption is encoded by three mechanisms:
  1. **Routing block** (C11''–C12'') or **mode-restricted routing** (C11'–C12'b): the blocked track is either permanently forbidden or restricted to outside-window traversal.
  2. **Bidirectional conflict** (C18)–(C21): the surviving track now requires a stricter headway $h^{\rm bi}$ between opposite-direction trains.
  3. **Temporal shielding** (C26)–(C27): trains on the surviving track complete their crossing outside the closure window.
* The objective trades off schedule adherence against energy: lower-speed profiles increase running time (raising delays) but reduce $e_{r,t,e}$; the optimiser naturally picks the cheapest combination subject to feasibility.

This formulation is a **complete MILP** with $\mathcal O(|T||S|)$ continuous time variables, $\mathcal O(|T||E||\bar R|)$ speed-profile binaries, $\mathcal O(|T||E|)$ routing binaries, and $\mathcal O(|T|^2|E|+|T|^2|S|)$ sequencing binaries — solvable in principle by branch-and-cut for instances of practical size. The structure of (C6)–(C8), (C9)–(C12), (C13)–(C17), and (C18)–(C21) is what makes this an *integrated* model rather than the sequential composition of a TRP and a TSMP.

# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) Model for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

The following formulation is a self-contained MILP that integrates the Train Rescheduling Problem (TRP) and the Train Speed Management Problem (TSMP) for a high-speed railway corridor affected by a partial segment blockage.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T = \{1,\dots,N_T\}$ | Set of trains |
| $S = \{1,\dots,N_S\}$ | Set of stations, ordered along the corridor |
| $B = \{1,\dots,N_B\}$ | Set of track blocks (segments between consecutive stations) |
| $I = \{1,\dots,N_I\}$ | Set of discretisation points within a block (for speed profiles) |
| $K = \{1,\dots,N_K\}$ | Set of discrete time steps |
| $D = \{1,2\}$ | Set of tracks: $1$ = original (assigned) track; $2$ = opposite track (used for rerouting) |
| $\text{Dir}_t \in \{1,2\}$ | Direction of travel of train $t$ on the original track (Assumption A1) |

**Parameters and assumption labels:**
- $A1$: Trains travel on a double-track corridor; each train has a predefined direction (up/down).
- $A2$: Block $b^{\star}$ is partially blocked during window $[W^{s}, W^{e}]$ on track $d^{\star}$.
- $A3$: Discrete time step $\Delta t$ and distance step $\Delta s$ are uniform.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ | km |
| $a^{\max}, b^{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration | m/s² |
| $v^{\max}$ | Maximum allowable speed | m/s |
| $m_t$ | Mass of train $t$ | t |
| $c_0, c_1, c_2$ | Davis resistance coefficients: $r(v)=c_0 + c_1 v + c_2 v^2$ | kN, kN/(m/s), kN/(m/s)² |
| $\eta$ | Regenerative braking efficiency | – |
| $H$ | Minimum safe headway time | s |
| $\tau^{\min}_s, \tau^{\max}_s$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time at station $s$ | s |
| $f_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ | s |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) | s |
| $\alpha, \beta$ | Weights of delay and energy in the objective | – / kWh |
| $\gamma$ | Conversion factor (kJ → kWh) | kWh/kJ |
| $b^{\star}$ | Block affected by the disruption | – |
| $d^{\star} \in D$ | Track affected by the disruption | – |
| $W^{s}, W^{e}$ | Start / end of the disruption time window | s |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Train Rescheduling (TRP) Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $x_{t,b,d} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ traverses block $b$ on track $d$ |
| $z_{t,b,d,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ occupies block $b$ on track $d$ at time step $k$ |
| $a_{t,s} \geq 0$ | Continuous | Actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{t,s} \geq 0$ | Continuous | Actual departure time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $\tau_{t,b} \geq 0$ | Continuous | Running time of train $t$ through block $b$ |
| $\delta_{t,s} \geq 0$ | Continuous | Delay of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $y_{t,t',s} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ departs station $s$ before train $t'$ |
| $c_t \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled |

### 3.2 Speed Management (TSMP) Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $v_{t,b,i} \geq 0$ | Continuous | Speed of train $t$ at discretisation point $i$ in block $b$ |
| $\Delta v^+_{t,b,i} \geq 0$ | Continuous | Positive speed change (acceleration) |
| $\Delta v^-_{t,b,i} \geq 0$ | Continuous | Negative speed change (deceleration) |
| $F^+_{t,b,i} \geq 0$ | Continuous | Tractive force at point $i$ |
| $F^-_{t,b,i} \geq 0$ | Continuous | Braking force at point $i$ |
| $p^+_{t,b,i} \geq 0$ | Continuous | Auxiliary linearisation variable for $F^+ \cdot v$ |
| $p^-_{t,b,i} \geq 0$ | Continuous | Auxiliary linearisation variable for $F^- \cdot v$ |

### 3.3 Auxiliary Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $E_t \geq 0$ | Continuous | Total energy consumption of train $t$ (kWh) |
| $w_{t,b,i} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ is accelerating at point $i$ in block $b$ |
| $q_{t,b,i} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | 1 if train $t$ is braking at point $i$ in block $b$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; \alpha \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{s \in S}\delta_{t,s} \;+\; \beta \sum_{t \in T} E_t \;+\; \sum_{t \in T} \kappa \, c_t \quad (A4)
$$

where:
- Term 1 minimises total delay (weighted by $\alpha$),
- Term 2 minimises total energy consumption (weighted by $\beta$),
- Term 3 penalises cancellations (Assumption A4: small penalty $\kappa$).

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Block–Track Assignment and Rerouting

**(C1) Each traversed block uses exactly one track**
$$
\sum_{d \in D} x_{t,b,d} = 1 - c_t \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B \quad (A5)
$$

**(C2) Rerouting only during disruption window** (trains may use track $d'$ during $[W^s, W^e]$)
$$
x_{t,b^{\star},d^{\star}} = 0 \quad \forall t \in T \quad (A6)
$$

**(C3) Rerouting feasibility on the opposite track**
$$
\sum_{b \in B} x_{t,b,d'} \leq |B| \cdot c_t \quad \forall t \in T,\; d' \neq \text{Dir}_t
$$
If a train is not cancelled, rerouting is allowed but not mandatory.

### 5.2 Block Occupation (Conflict Resolution)

**(C4) Capacity constraint on each block/track/time**
$$
\sum_{t \in T} z_{t,b,d,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall b \in B,\; d \in D,\; k \in K
$$

**(C5) Linking occupation to block–track assignment**
$$
z_{t,b,d,k} \leq x_{t,b,d} \quad \forall t,b,d,k
$$

**(C6) Occupation duration matches running time**
$$
\sum_{k \in K} z_{t,b,d,k} \cdot \Delta t \geq \tau_{t,b} - M(1 - x_{t,b,d}) \quad \forall t,b,d
$$
$$
\sum_{k \in K} z_{t,b,d,k} \cdot \Delta t \leq \tau_{t,b} + M(1 - x_{t,b,d}) \quad \forall t,b,d
$$

**(C7) Disruption time-window ban** (the original track $d^\star$ in block $b^\star$ is unusable during $[W^s, W^e]$)
$$
z_{t,b^{\star},d^{\star},k} = 0 \quad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K: W^s \leq k\Delta t \leq W^e
$$

**(C8) Bidirectional conflict avoidance on the opposite track**
$$
z_{t,b,d',k} + z_{t',b,d',k} \leq 1 \quad \forall b \in B,\; d' \in D,\; k \in K,\; t,t' \in T: \text{Dir}_t \neq \text{Dir}_{t'}
$$

### 5.3 Train Sequencing and Dwell Times

**(C9) Departure–arrival consistency between consecutive stations**
$$
a_{t,s+1} = d_{t,s} + \tau_{t,b(s,s+1)} \quad \forall t,s
$$
where $b(s,s+1)$ is the block between stations $s$ and $s+1$ (Assumption A7).

**(C10) Dwell time bounds**
$$
\tau^{\min}_s \leq d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \leq \tau^{\max}_s \quad \forall t,s
$$

**(C11) Delay definition**
$$
\delta_{t,s} \geq a_{t,s} - f_{t,s} \quad \forall t,s
$$
$$
\delta_{t,s} \geq 0
$$

**(C12) Headway at stations (train ordering)**
$$
d_{t,s} - d_{t',s} \geq H - M(1 - y_{t,t',s}) \quad \forall t \neq t', s
$$
$$
d_{t',s} - d_{t,s} \geq H - M \, y_{t,t',s} \quad \forall t \neq t', s
$$
$$
y_{t,t',s} + y_{t',t,s} = 1 \quad \forall t \neq t', s
$$

### 5.4 Speed Profile Dynamics (TSMP)

**(C13) Speed evolution** (decomposition of speed change into acceleration/deceleration components)
$$
v_{t,b,i+1} - v_{t,b,i} = \Delta v^+_{t,b,i} - \Delta v^-_{t,b,i} \quad \forall t,b,i
$$

**(C14) Acceleration / deceleration limits**
$$
\Delta v^+_{t,b,i} \leq a^{\max} \Delta t \quad \forall t,b,i
$$
$$
\Delta v^-_{t,b,i} \leq b^{\max} \Delta t \quad \forall t,b,i
$$

**(C15) Maximum and minimum speed**
$$
0 \leq v_{t,b,i} \leq v^{\max} \quad \forall t,b,i
$$

**(C16) Running time derived from speed profile**
$$
\tau_{t,b} = \sum_{i \in I} \frac{\Delta s}{v_{t,b,i} + \epsilon} \quad \forall t,b
$$
where $\epsilon > 0$ avoids division by zero. This non-linear relation is linearised by introducing auxiliary variables and using the convex envelope:
$$
\tau_{t,b} \geq \sum_{i \in I} \frac{\Delta s}{v^{\max}} + \frac{1}{v^{\max}}\sum_{i \in I}(v_{t,b,i} - v^{\max}) \quad (A8)
$$

**(C17) Linking block occupation to speed profile** (initial/final speeds are zero at stations)
$$
v_{t,b,1} = 0 \quad \forall t,b
$$
$$
v_{t,b,N_I} = 0 \quad \forall t,b \text{ (except block adjacent to terminal)}
$$

### 5.5 Energy Consumption Model

The mechanical work performed by train $t$ in block $b$ at point $i$ is
$$
W_{t,b,i} = F^+_{t,b,i}\,v_{t,b,i} \;-\; \eta\, F^-_{t,b,i}\,v_{t,b,i}
$$
which we linearise using the standard piecewise-linear approximation (Assumption A9) with auxiliary variables $p^+_{t,b,i}, p^-_{t,b,i}$.

**(C18) Newton's second law**
$$
m_t\,(\Delta v^+_{t,b,i} + \Delta v^-_{t,b,i})/\Delta t = F^+_{t,b,i} - F^-_{t,b,i} - m_t\,g\,\text{grade}(b) - m_t\,r(v_{t,b,i})
$$

The resistance term $r(v) = c_0 + c_1 v + c_2 v^2$ is linearised around operating points (Assumption A10):
$$
r(v_{t,b,i}) \approx \tilde{c}_0 + \tilde{c}_1 v_{t,b,i}
$$

**(C19) Power linearisation (SOS-2 or piecewise-linear envelope)**
$$
p^+_{t,b,i} \geq F^+_{t,b,i}\,v^{\min}, \quad p^+_{t,b,i} \geq F^+_{t,b,i}\,v^{\max} - (v^{\max} - v^{\min})F^{\max}
$$
(and analogous for $p^-_{t,b,i}$).

**(C20) Acceleration/braking mode exclusivity**
$$
w_{t,b,i} + q_{t,b,i} \leq 1 \quad \forall t,b,i
$$
$$
F^+_{t,b,i} \leq F^{\max}\,w_{t,b,i}, \quad F^-_{t,b,i} \leq F^{\max}\,q_{t,b,i}
$$

**(C21) Total energy per train**
$$
E_t = \gamma \sum_{b \in B}\sum_{i \in I}\big(p^+_{t,b,i} - \eta\, p^-_{t,b,i}\big)\Delta s \quad \forall t \in T
$$

### 5.6 Cancellation Logic

**(C22) Cancellation absorbs all rescheduling variables**
$$
a_{t,s} \leq M(1 - c_t), \quad d_{t,s} \leq M(1 - c_t), \quad \tau_{t,b} \leq M(1 - c_t) \quad \forall t,s,b
$$

### 5.7 Variable Domains

$$
x, z, y, w, q \in \{0,1\}, \quad a, d, \tau, v, F, p, \delta, E \geq 0
$$

---

## 6. Summary of Assumptions Introduced

| ID | Assumption |
|----|------------|
| A1 | A bidirectional high-speed corridor with two parallel tracks. |
| A2 | Disruption is a partial blockage of a single block $b^\star$ on a single track $d^\star$ for a known time window $[W^s, W^e]$. |
| A3 | Uniform discretisation in space ($\Delta s$) and time ($\Delta t$). |
| A4 | Cancellation is allowed with a small fixed penalty $\kappa$. |
| A5 | Each non-cancelled train traverses every block on exactly one track. |
| A6 | Rerouting to the opposite track is permitted inside the disruption window, subject to conflict constraints. |
| A7 | Track topology is linear; each block connects exactly two consecutive stations. |
| A8 | Speed–time reciprocity is approximated by a linear envelope (McCormick relaxation). |
| A9 | Power terms $F \cdot v$ are approximated by a piecewise-linear (SOS-2) envelope. |
| A10 | Quadratic resistance is linearised around an average speed estimate. |

---

## 7. Notes on Tractability

The model above is a *true* MILP whose complexity grows with $|T|\cdot|B|\cdot|D|\cdot|K| + |T|\cdot|B|\cdot|I|$. To make it computationally tractable for large instances, the accompanying paper proposes:
1. A **decomposition** into an Integer Programming (IP) model for train interactions plus per-train subproblems (speed profiles).
2. An **adaptive iterative refinement** of the time/space discretisation around the incumbent solution.
3. A **local-branching** strategy to accelerate the IP search.

These algorithmic enhancements are out of scope for the MILP formulation itself but rely on the model presented above as the master formulation.

Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
