# TRSMP — Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management MILP (Equations Only)

**Assumptions (marked where not given):** double-track line with stations S and segments e between consecutive stations; a disruption blocks one track of segment e* during window [T_start, T_end]; affected trains may reroute to the opposite track (unidirectional operation); speed profiles are pre-generated discrete alternatives (running time, energy) per train/segment; cancellations allowed with penalty.

## Sets & Parameters
- I: trains, with direction dir(i) ∈ {up, down}; weight w_i
- S: stations; E: segments with entry/exit stations per direction
- P_{i,e} = {(r_{i,e,p}, E_{i,e,p})}: speed profiles (running time, energy)
- A⁰_{i,s}, D⁰_{i,s}: scheduled arrival/departure; D_{i,s}: min dwell
- h: same-direction headway; h′: opposite-direction headway on shared track
- Δ_max: max allowed delay; H: horizon; M: big-M; α: energy cost weight; M_c: cancellation penalty

## Variables
- x_{i,e,p} ∈ {0,1}: train i uses profile p on segment e
- a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} ≥ 0: actual arrival/departure times
- δ_{i,s} ≥ 0: delay at station s
- y_{i,e} ∈ {0,1}: train i reroutes to opposite track on segment e
- o_{i,j,e} ∈ {0,1}: ordering (i before j) on segment e
- z_i ∈ {0,1}: train i cancelled

## Objective
Minimize:

min Σ_i Σ_s w_i δ_{i,s} + α Σ_i Σ_e Σ_p E_{i,e,p} x_{i,e,p} + M_c Σ_i z_i

## Constraints

**(1) Profile selection / cancellation** ( ∀i, e ):
Σ_p x_{i,e,p} + z_i = 1

**(2) Running-time consistency** ( ∀i, e, with entry s_in, exit s_out ):
a_{i,s_out} − d_{i,s_in} = Σ_p r_{i,e,p} x_{i,e,p}  (relaxed by ±M·z_i if cancelled)

**(3) Dwell time** ( ∀i, intermediate s ):
d_{i,s} − a_{i,s} ≥ D_{i,s} − M·z_i

**(4) Delay definition & bound** ( ∀i, s ):
δ_{i,s} ≥ a_{i,s} − A⁰_{i,s} − M·z_i
δ_{i,s} ≥ d_{i,s} − D⁰_{i,s} − M·z_i
δ_{i,s} ≤ Δ_max·(1 − z_i)

**(5) Rerouting logic on disrupted segment e\*** ( ∀i ):
- If y_{i,e*} = 1, entry time within window:
 d_{i,s_in} ≥ T_start − M(1 − y_{i,e*}) − M·z_i
 d_{i,s_in} ≤ T_end + M(1 − y_{i,e*}) + M·z_i
- If train enters during window, it must reroute (enforced jointly with the window bounds above via big-M implications linking d_{i,s_in} and y_{i,e*}).

**(6) Same-direction headways on a shared track** ( ∀ ordered pairs i,j with same direction, ∀e, both track sides):
d_{j,s_in} − d_{i,s_in} ≥ h − M(1 − o_{i,j,e}) − M·|y_i − y_j indicator terms| − M(z_i + z_j)
d_{i,s_in} − d_{j,s_in} ≥ h − M·o_{i,j,e} − … − M(z_i + z_j)
and analogous constraints on arrival ends a_{i,s_out}, a_{j,s_out}.

**(7) Opposite-direction trains sharing the opposite track during disruption** ( ∀ pairs i,j with dir(i) ≠ dir(j), ∀e, active when y_{i,e} = y_{j,e} = 1 — unidirectional, no temporal overlap):
d_{j,s_in(j)} − a_{i,s_out(i)} ≥ h′ − M(1 − o_{i,j,e}) − M(2 − y_{i,e} − y_{j,e}) − M(z_i + z_j)
d_{i,s_in(i)} − a_{j,s_out(j)} ≥ h′ − M·o_{i,j,e} − M(2 − y_{i,e} − y_{j,e}) − M(z_i + z_j)

**(8) Station capacity** ( ∀ pairs i,j, boundary stations s ):
d_{j,s} − d_{i,s} ≥ h − M(1 − o_{i,j,e}) − M(z_i + z_j)
d_{i,s} − d_{j,s} ≥ h − M·o_{i,j,e} − M(z_i + z_j)

**(9) Horizon bounds** ( ∀i, s ):
0 ≤ a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} ≤ H − M·z_i

**(10) Cancellation relaxation:** if z_i = 1, all timing/profile constraints of train i are relaxed via big-M terms (embedded above), and δ_{i,s} ≤ Δ_max(1 − z_i).

All constraints are linear; big-M is used for ordering, rerouting-window implications, and cancellation relaxations. The model simultaneously decides train times (retiming), orders (reordering), routes (rerouting), cancellations, and speed profiles, yielding a conflict-free, energy-aware rescheduled timetable with executable speed profiles.

# MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

Below is the complete mixed-integer linear programming model for the integrated train rescheduling and speed management problem on a bidirectional high-speed railway line with a partial segment blockage.

---

## 1. Notation

**Sets**
- `T = {1,...,T_max}` : discretized time steps (Δt fixed)
- `S = {1,...,S_max}` : ordered track segments; `D ⊆ S` disrupted segments
- `I = {1,...,N}` : trains; each `i ∈ I` has `dir_i ∈ {up, down}`
- `K = {1,...,K_max}` : speed intervals per train
- `V = {1,...,V_max}` : discrete speed levels

**Parameters**
- `L_s` : length of segment `s`; `pos(s) = Σ_{s'≤s} L_{s'}` cumulative position
- `block_s^t ∈ {0,1}` : 1 if the original-direction track of segment `s` is blocked at time `t`
- `t_i^arr_sch, t_i^dep_sch` : scheduled arrival/departure times
- `t_i^arr_min/max, t_i^dep_min/max` : feasible time windows
- `v_v` : speed of level `v`; `E_v` : energy per unit distance at level `v`
- `headway_h` : minimum time headway between consecutive trains
- `dwell_i^min/max` : minimum/maximum dwell time at stations
- `delta_max` : maximum allowed delay
- `acc_max, dec_max` : maximum acceleration / deceleration
- `M` : sufficiently large big-M constant
- `P_cancel, P_reroute` : cancellation and rerouting penalties
- `α, β, γ, λ ≥ 0` : objective weights
- `Len_i = pos(d_i) − pos(o_i)` : total running distance of train `i`

**Decision Variables**
- `x_i^arr, x_i^dep ∈ [0, T_max]` : actual arrival/departure times
- `r_i ∈ {0,1}` : rerouted to opposite track in disruption zone
- `c_i ∈ {0,1}` : cancelled
- `o_{i,j} ∈ {0,1}` : train `i` departs the shared station before train `j`
- `w_{i,j}^s ∈ {0,1}` : train `i` enters segment `s` before train `j`
- `s_{i,k}^v ∈ {0,1}` : speed level `v` used in interval `k` of train `i`
- `τ_i^k ≥ 0` : duration of speed interval `k` of train `i`
- `p_i^k ≥ 0` : position at end of interval `k` (`p_i^0 = 0`)
- `e_i ≥ 0` : energy consumption of train `i`
- `delta_i ≥ 0` : arrival delay
- `z_i^s ∈ {0,1}` : train `i` traverses segment `s`
- `u_{i,s}^k ∈ {0,1}` : train `i` is inside segment `s` during speed interval `k`
- `ent_i^s ≥ 0` : time train `i` enters segment `s`
- `q_i^k ≥ 0` : distance covered by train `i` in interval `k`
- `g_{i,k}^v ≥ 0` : energy contribution of level `v` in interval `k` of train `i`
- `θ_i^k ≥ 0` : auxiliary for max(τ_i^k, τ_i^{k+1})
- `d_{i,k}^+, d_{i,k}^- ≥ 0` : positive/negative speed change between intervals

---

## 2. Objective Function

$$
\min\; \alpha \sum_{i \in I} \delta_i \;+\; \beta \sum_{i \in I} e_i \;+\; \gamma \sum_{i \in I} P_{\text{cancel}}\, c_i \;+\; \lambda \sum_{i \in I} P_{\text{reroute}}\, r_i
$$

---

## 3. Constraints

### (C1) Time Windows
$$
t_i^{\text{arr,min}} \le x_i^{\text{arr}} \le t_i^{\text{arr,max}} \quad \forall\, i \in I
$$
$$
t_i^{\text{dep,min}} \le x_i^{\text{dep}} \le t_i^{\text{dep,max}} \quad \forall\, i \in I
$$

### (C2) Dwell Time at Stations
$$
\text{dwell}_i^{\min} \le x_i^{\text{arr}} - x_i^{\text{dep}} \le \text{dwell}_i^{\max} \quad \forall\, i \in I
$$

### (C3) Delay Definition and Cap
$$
\delta_i \ge x_i^{\text{arr}} - t_i^{\text{arr,sch}} \quad \forall\, i \in I
$$
$$
\delta_i \le \delta_{\max} \quad \forall\, i \in I
$$
$$
\delta_i \ge 0 \quad \forall\, i \in I
$$

### (C4) Cancellation Logic
If cancelled, the train consumes no resources and its delay is excluded from the objective:
$$
x_i^{\text{arr}} \le T_{\max}\,(1 - c_i) \quad \forall\, i \in I
$$
$$
x_i^{\text{dep}} \le T_{\max}\,(1 - c_i) \quad \forall\, i \in I
$$
$$
\delta_i \le \delta_{\max}\,(1 - c_i) \quad \forall\, i \in I
$$
$$
z_i^s \le 1 - c_i \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S
$$
$$
s_{i,k}^v \le 1 - c_i \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K,\; v \in V
$$
$$
r_i \le 1 - c_i \quad \forall\, i \in I
$$

### (C5) Coupling — Running Time Equals Interval Sum
$$
\sum_{k \in K} \tau_i^k \;=\; x_i^{\text{arr}} - x_i^{\text{dep}} \quad \forall\, i \in I
$$

### (C6) Speed Level Selection (exactly one level per interval)
$$
\sum_{v \in V} s_{i,k}^v = 1 \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K
$$

### (C7) Kinematic Consistency (Position Progression)
Linearization of the binary × continuous product `v_v · τ_i^k` via auxiliary `q_i^k`:
$$
q_i^k \le v_v\, \tau_i^k + M\,(1 - s_{i,k}^v) \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K,\; v \in V
$$
$$
q_i^k \ge v_v\, \tau_i^k - M\,(1 - s_{i,k}^v) \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K,\; v \in V
$$
$$
q_i^k \le v_{\max}\, \tau_i^k + M\, s_{i,k}^v \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K,\; v \in V
$$
$$
p_i^k = p_i^{k-1} + q_i^k \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K
$$
$$
p_i^0 = 0,\qquad p_i^{K_{\max}} = \text{Len}_i \quad \forall\, i \in I
$$

### (C8) Energy Consumption
Linearization via `g_{i,k}^v`:
$$
g_{i,k}^v \le (E_v\, v_v)\,\tau_i^k + M\,(1 - s_{i,k}^v) \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K,\; v \in V
$$
$$
g_{i,k}^v \ge (E_v\, v_v)\,\tau_i^k - M\,(1 - s_{i,k}^v) \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K,\; v \in V
$$
$$
g_{i,k}^v \le (E_v\, v_v)\, T_{\max}\, s_{i,k}^v \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K,\; v \in V
$$
$$
e_i = \sum_{k \in K}\sum_{v \in V} g_{i,k}^v \quad \forall\, i \in I
$$

### (C9) Speed-Change (Acceleration / Deceleration) Feasibility
Define the signed average speed of interval `k`: `V_i^k = Σ_v v_v s_{i,k}^v` (linear).
$$
V_i^{k+1} - V_i^k \le d_{i,k}^+ \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K,\; k < K_{\max}
$$
$$
V_i^k - V_i^{k+1} \le d_{i,k}^- \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; k \in K,\; k < K_{\max}
$$
$$
d_{i,k}^+ + d_{i,k}^- \le \text{acc}_{\max}\, \theta_i^k \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; k < K_{\max}
$$
$$
\theta_i^k \ge \tau_i^k,\quad \theta_i^k \ge \tau_i^{k+1} \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; k < K_{\max}
$$

### (C10) Segment Occupation (Position-Based)
Train `i` occupies segment `s` iff some speed interval straddles `s`:
$$
p_i^{k-1} - \text{pos}(s-1) \le M\, u_{i,s}^k \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S,\; k \in K
$$
$$
\text{pos}(s) - p_i^k \le M\, u_{i,s}^k \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S,\; k \in K
$$
$$
z_i^s \le \sum_{k \in K} u_{i,s}^k \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S
$$
$$
z_i^s \ge u_{i,s}^k \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S,\; k \in K
$$

### (C11) Rerouting Decision
If train `i` in the affected direction uses a disrupted segment while blocked, it must either reroute or be delayed past the window:
$$
r_i \;\ge\; z_i^s - \sum_{t \in W}(1 - \text{block}_s^{\,t}) \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in D
$$
Interpretation: if `block_s^t = 1` for all `t` in the train's passage window of `s ∈ D`, then `z_i^s = 1 ⇒ r_i = 1`.

### (C12) Bidirectional Conflict Avoidance on Shared (Opposite) Track
For each segment `s` (in particular `s ∈ D`) and each pair `(i,j)` with `i < j` that may both use `s`:
$$
w_{i,j}^s + w_{j,i}^s \ge z_i^s + z_j^s - 1 \quad \forall\, s \in S,\; i < j
$$
$$
w_{i,j}^s + w_{j,i}^s \le 1 \quad \forall\, s \in S,\; i < j
$$
$$
\text{ent}_j^s \ge \text{ent}_i^s + \text{headway}_h - M(1 - w_{i,j}^s) - M(1 - z_i^s) - M(1 - z_j^s) \quad \forall\, s,\; i<j
$$
$$
\text{ent}_i^s \ge \text{ent}_j^s + \text{headway}_h - M(1 - w_{j,i}^s) - M(1 - z_i^s) - M(1 - z_j^s) \quad \forall\, s,\; i<j
$$
(When `s ∈ D` and trains travel in opposite directions on the shared opposite track, these constraints enforce single-track token-block semantics — only one train occupies `s` at any time.)

### (C13) Headway on Consecutive Same-Direction Segments
$$
\text{ent}_j^{s+1} \ge \text{ent}_i^s + \text{headway}_h - M(2 - z_i^s - z_j^s) - M(1 - w_{i,j}^s) \quad \forall\, s,\; i<j \text{ same dir.}
$$

### (C14) Station Ordering / Reordering
$$
o_{i,j} + o_{j,i} = 1 \quad \forall\, i<j \text{ at same station}
$$
$$
x_i^{\text{dep}} \le x_j^{\text{dep}} + M(1 - o_{i,j}) \quad \forall\, i<j \text{ at same station}
$$
$$
x_j^{\text{dep}} \le x_i^{\text{dep}} + M(1 - o_{j,i}) \quad \forall\, i<j \text{ at same station}
$$
$$
o_{i,j} \le 1 - c_i,\quad o_{i,j} \le 1 - c_j \quad \forall\, i,j
$$

### (C15) Disruption-Window Avoidance for Non-Rerouted Trains
A non-rerouted train must enter disrupted segments either before `t_start` or after `t_end`:
$$
\text{ent}_i^s \ge t_{\text{end}} + \text{headway}_h - M(1 - z_i^s) - M\, r_i \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in D
$$
$$
\text{ent}_i^s \le t_{\text{start}} - \text{headway}_h + M(1 - z_i^s) + M\, r_i \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in D
$$

### (C16) Entry-Time Definition
For each train `i` and segment `s`, link entry time to position progression:
$$
\text{ent}_i^s \ge x_i^{\text{dep}} + \sum_{k \in K :\, p_i^k \le \text{pos}(s-1)} \tau_i^k - M(1 - z_i^s) \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S
$$
(Implemented via the `u_{i,s}^k` auxiliary: `ent_i^s ≥ x_i^dep + Σ_{k≤k'(s)} τ_i^k − M(1−z_i^s)` where `k'(s)` is the last interval strictly before `s`.)

### (C17) Variable Domains
$$
x_i^{\text{arr}}, x_i^{\text{dep}}, \tau_i^k, p_i^k, e_i, \delta_i, q_i^k, g_{i,k}^v, \theta_i^k, \text{ent}_i^s, d_{i,k}^+, d_{i,k}^- \ge 0
$$
$$
r_i, c_i, o_{i,j}, w_{i,j}^s, s_{i,k}^v, z_i^s, u_{i,s}^k \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
0 \le p_i^k \le \text{Len}_i,\qquad 0 \le \tau_i^k \le T_{\max}
$$

---

## 4. Model Element Summary

**Traffic-level (rescheduling) layer.** Variables `x_i^arr, x_i^dep` permit retiming within the feasible windows; `o_{i,j}` and `w_{i,j}^s` permit reordering; `z_i^s` and `r_i` handle rerouting through the disruption zone on the opposite track; `c_i` enables cancellation at penalty cost. Constraints (C12)–(C15) ensure conflict-free, headway-respecting operation, including single-track bidirectional operation through the disrupted segments.

**Control-level (speed management) layer.** Each train's journey is partitioned into `K_max` intervals, each selecting one discrete speed level (`s_{i,k}^v`). Durations `τ_i^k` and positions `p_i^k` follow the kinematic law `Δp = v · Δt` (C7); energy is computed from `E_v · v_v · τ` (C8); acceleration/deceleration limits between consecutive intervals are enforced by (C9).

**Coupling between layers.** Constraint (C5) forces the sum of interval durations to equal the rescheduled running time `x_i^arr − x_i^dep`, so any traffic-level time admitted by the rescheduler is physically reachable by a valid speed profile. Constraint (C10) maps positions to segment occupancy, feeding the chosen speed profile back into the conflict-avoidance constraints. Together, (C5) and (C7)–(C8) guarantee that the timetable and the speed profiles are mutually feasible.

**Disruption handling.** The parameter `block_s^t` encodes the partial blockage. (C11) and (C15) state that a train in the affected direction traversing `s ∈ D` either (a) reroutes to the opposite track (`r_i = 1`, paying `P_reroute`) and is then subject to bidirectional single-track conflict resolution via (C12), or (b) is retimed to traverse `s` outside the disruption window. Cancellation (`c_i = 1`) removes the train entirely at cost `P_cancel`.

**Linearity.** All logical conditions use standard big-M linearizations; nonlinear products `v_v · τ_i^k` and `E_v·v_v·τ_i^k` are replaced by auxiliary continuous variables `q_i^k` and `g_{i,k}^v` bounded by four-facet McCormick-style inequalities, yielding a valid MILP directly implementable in solvers such as Gurobi, CPLEX, or via Pyomo/GAMS.

- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.

- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

Text:
# TRSMP: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem — MILP Formulation

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, ordered $1,2,\dots,|S|$, indexed by $s$ |
| $K$ | Set of track segments, indexed by $k$ |
| $K^B \subseteq K$ | Set of partially blocked segments |
| $L = \{0,1\}$ | Track index: 0 = normal direction track, 1 = opposite (rerouting) track |
| $N_k$ | Set of spatial discretization points on segment $k$ |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of time discretization intervals, indexed by $\tau$ |
| $\Omega = \{tr, br, co\}$ | Driving mode set: traction, braking, coasting |

**Assumptions:**
- Time is discretized into intervals of length $\Delta t$.
- Space is discretized along each segment into steps of length $\Delta x$.
- Bidirectional traffic is allowed only within the disruption window on blocked segments (single-track working).
- A train follows the point-mass model with Davis resistance.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_k$ | Length of segment $k$ (m) |
| $\Delta x$ | Spatial discretization step |
| $\Delta t$ | Time discretization step |
| $v_{\min}, v_{\max}$ | Speed limits (m/s) |
| $a_{\max}, b_{\max}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration (m/s²) |
| $F_{\max}$ | Maximum tractive/braking force (N) |
| $M_i$ | Mass of train $i$ (kg) |
| $R_i^0, R_i^1, R_i^2$ | Davis coefficients for train $i$ |
| $\eta$ | Regenerative braking efficiency |
| $P_{\text{aux}}$ | Auxiliary power (W) |
| $t^{\text{sch}}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $h^{\min}_s, h^{\max}_s$ | Min/max dwell time at station $s$ |
| $H$ | Minimum headway time (s) |
| $t^-, t^+$ | Disruption window start/end (s) |
| $P^{\text{cancel}}$ | Cancellation penalty |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Weights for delay, energy, cancellation |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (big-M) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Rescheduling (TRP) variables:**

- $x_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ stops at station $s$.
- $z_{i,j,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $k$.
- $r_{i,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is rerouted to the opposite track on segment $k$.
- $d_{i,k,l} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses track $l \in L$ on segment $k$.
- $c_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled.
- $a_{i,s} \geq 0$: actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $\text{dep}_{i,s} \geq 0$: actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $h_{i,s} \geq 0$: dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $\delta_{i,k} \geq 0$: running time of train $i$ on segment $k$.
- $\Delta_{i,s} \geq 0$: delay of train $i$ at station $s$ versus schedule.
- $w_{i,k,l,\tau} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ occupies track $l$ of segment $k$ during interval $\tau$.
- $\text{cf}_{i,j,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trains $i,j$ conflict on segment $k$.

**Speed management (TSMP) variables:**

- $v_{i,k,n} \geq 0$: speed of train $i$ at spatial node $n$ on segment $k$ (m/s).
- $u_{i,k,n} \geq 0$: auxiliary variable $v_{i,k,n}^2$.
- $F^{\text{tr}}_{i,k,n} \geq 0$: tractive force at node $n$ on segment $k$.
- $F^{\text{br}}_{i,k,n} \geq 0$: braking force at node $n$ on segment $k$.
- $e_{i,k,n} \geq 0$: incremental energy consumption at node $n$.
- $E_i \geq 0$: total energy consumption of train $i$.
- $m^{\text{tr}}_{i,k,n}, m^{\text{br}}_{i,k,n}, m^{\text{co}}_{i,k,n} \in \{0,1\}$: driving-mode indicators.

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \alpha \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S} \Delta_{i,s} \;+\; \beta \sum_{i \in T} E_i \;+\; \gamma \sum_{i \in T} c_i \, P^{\text{cancel}}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Station Operations
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s} \;=\; a_{i,s} + h_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T,\; \forall s \in S \text{ with } x_{i,s}=1
$$
$$
h^{\min}_s \, x_{i,s} \;\leq\; h_{i,s} \;\leq\; h^{\max}_s \, x_{i,s} \quad \forall i,s
$$
$$
a_{i,s} \;=\; \text{dep}_{i,s-1} + \delta_{i,k(s)} \quad \forall i,\; k(s) \text{ ending at } s
$$

### 5.2 Delay Definition
$$
\Delta_{i,s} \;\geq\; a_{i,s} - t^{\text{sch}}_{i,s} \quad \forall i,s
$$
$$
\Delta_{i,s} \;\geq\; 0
$$

### 5.3 Train Cancellation
$$
\sum_{s \in S} x_{i,s} \;\leq\; M\,(1 - c_i) \quad \forall i
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{i,1} \;\geq\; t^{\text{sch}}_{i,1} - M\,c_i \quad \forall i
$$

### 5.4 Track Assignment
$$
d_{i,k,0} + d_{i,k,1} \;=\; 1 \quad \forall i,\; k \in K^B
$$
$$
r_{i,k} \;=\; d_{i,k,1} \quad \forall i,\; k \in K^B
$$

### 5.5 Blockage Avoidance on Normal Track
For all $i$ and $k \in K^B$ with $d_{i,k,0} = 1$ (i.e. $r_{i,k}=0$), trains cannot traverse $k$ during the disruption window $[t^-, t^+]$:
$$
\text{dep}_{i,s(k)} \;\geq\; t^+ \;-\; M\, r_{i,k}
$$
$$
a_{i,s(k+1)} \;\leq\; t^- \;+\; M\, r_{i,k}
$$
where $s(k)$ is the origin station of segment $k$ and $s(k+1)$ the terminal station.

### 5.6 Rerouting Time Penalty
$$
\delta_{i,k} \;=\; \delta^{\text{norm}}_{i,k} + \pi^{\text{rer}}\, r_{i,k} \quad \forall i,\; k \in K^B
$$
with rerouting penalty $\pi^{\text{rer}} \geq 0$.

### 5.7 Train Ordering on Segments
$$
z_{i,j,k} + z_{j,i,k} \;=\; 1 \quad \forall i \neq j,\; k
$$
$$
a_{j,s(k+1)} + H \;\leq\; a_{i,s(k+1)} + M\,(1 - z_{i,j,k}) \quad \forall i \neq j,\; k
$$

### 5.8 Bidirectional Conflict on Shared (Opposite) Track
For trains $i,j$ travelling in opposite directions on segment $k \in K^B$ with $r_{i,k} = r_{j,k} = 1$:
$$
\text{cf}_{i,j,k} \;\geq\; r_{i,k} + r_{j,k} - 1 \quad \forall i \neq j,\; k \in K^B
$$
$$
a_{j,s(k+1)} + H \;\leq\; a_{i,s(k+1)} + M\,(1 - z_{i,j,k}) + M\,\text{cf}_{i,j,k}
$$
(ensuring temporal separation between opposing movements).

### 5.9 Occupancy–Time Linking (linearized via big-M)
$$
w_{i,k,l,\tau} \;\leq\; \frac{a_{i,s(k+1)} - \tau \Delta t + M}{M} \quad \forall i,k,l,\tau
$$
$$
w_{i,k,l,\tau} \;\leq\; \frac{\tau \Delta t - \text{dep}_{i,s(k)} + M}{M} \quad \forall i,k,l,\tau
$$
$$
w_{i,k,l,\tau} \;\geq\; \frac{\tau \Delta t - \text{dep}_{i,s(k)}}{M}
$$
$$
w_{i,k,l,\tau} \;\geq\; \frac{a_{i,s(k+1)} - \tau \Delta t}{M} - 1
$$

### 5.10 Track Capacity (Headway in Time-Space)
$$
\sum_{i \in T} w_{i,k,l,\tau} \;\leq\; 1 \quad \forall k,\; l,\; \tau
$$

### 5.11 Driving-Mode Selection
$$
m^{\text{tr}}_{i,k,n} + m^{\text{br}}_{i,k,n} + m^{\text{co}}_{i,k,n} \;=\; 1 \quad \forall i,k,n
$$

### 5.12 Speed Limits
$$
v_{\min} \;\leq\; v_{i,k,n} \;\leq\; v_{\max} \quad \forall i,k,n
$$

### 5.13 Force Bounds
$$
0 \;\leq\; F^{\text{tr}}_{i,k,n} \;\leq\; F_{\max}\, m^{\text{tr}}_{i,k,n}
$$
$$
0 \;\leq\; F^{\text{br}}_{i,k,n} \;\leq\; F_{\max}\, m^{\text{br}}_{i,k,n}
$$

### 5.14 Train Dynamics (Linearized Point-Mass Model)
Define $u_{i,k,n} = v_{i,k,n}^2$ via piecewise-linear envelope (outer approximation). The discretized kinematic equation is:
$$
u_{i,k,n+1} - u_{i,k,n} \;=\; \frac{2 \Delta x}{M_i}\!\left(F^{\text{tr}}_{i,k,n} - F^{\text{br}}_{i,k,n} - R_i(v_{i,k,n})\right)
$$
with Davis resistance linearized at segment endpoints:
$$
R_i(v) \;=\; R_i^0 + R_i^1 v + R_i^2 v^2 \;\approx\; R_i^0 + \tfrac{R_i^1}{2}(v_{i,k,n} + v_{i,k,n+1}) + \tfrac{R_i^2}{2}(u_{i,k,n} + u_{i,k,n+1})
$$

Equivalently, the Euler form:
$$
v_{i,k,n+1} - v_{i,k,n} \;=\; \frac{\Delta x}{M_i\, \bar v_{i,k,n}}\!\left(F^{\text{tr}}_{i,k,n} - F^{\text{br}}_{i,k,n} - R_i(\bar v_{i,k,n})\right)
$$
where $\bar v_{i,k,n} = (v_{i,k,n} + v_{i,k,n+1})/2$, itself substituted through auxiliary linearization.

### 5.15 Acceleration and Deceleration Limits
$$
v_{i,k,n+1} - v_{i,k,n} \;\leq\; a_{\max} \frac{\Delta x}{v_{i,k,n}} \quad \forall i,k,n
$$
$$
v_{i,k,n} - v_{i,k,n+1} \;\leq\; b_{\max} \frac{\Delta x}{v_{i,k,n}} \quad \forall i,k,n
$$

### 5.16 Boundary (Station Speed) Conditions
$$
v_{i,k,0} \;=\; v^{\text{dep}}_{i,s(k)} , \qquad v_{i,k,N_k} \;=\; v^{\text{arr}}_{i,s(k+1)}
$$
$$
0 \;\leq\; v^{\text{dep}}_{i,s} \;\leq\; v_{\max}\, x_{i,s}, \qquad 0 \;\leq\; v^{\text{arr}}_{i,s} \;\leq\; v_{\max}\, x_{i,s}
$$
$$
v_{i,k,N_k} \;=\; v_{i,k+1,0} \quad \forall i,\; \text{consecutive } k,k+1 \text{ at } s
$$

### 5.17 Running-Time and Speed-Profile Linkage
$$
\delta_{i,k} \;=\; \sum_{n=0}^{N_k-1} \frac{\Delta x}{v_{i,k,n}} \quad \forall i,k
$$
(linearized via convex envelope $1/v$).

### 5.18 Energy Computation
$$
e_{i,k,n} \;=\; F^{\text{tr}}_{i,k,n}\, \Delta x + P_{\text{aux}}\, \Delta t - \eta\, F^{\text{br}}_{i,k,n}\, \Delta x
$$
$$
E_i \;=\; \sum_{k \in K}\sum_{n=0}^{N_k} e_{i,k,n}
$$

### 5.19 Initial and Final Time Bounds
$$
\text{dep}_{i,1} \;\geq\; t^{\text{sch}}_{i,1}, \qquad a_{i,|S|} \;\leq\; t^{\text{sch}}_{i,|S|} + \Delta^{\text{tol}}_i
$$

### 5.20 Non-Negativity and Integrality
All continuous variables $\geq 0$; all binary variables in $\{0,1\}$.

---

## 6. Summary of Assumptions

1. **Discretization:** Space and time are uniformly discretized ($\Delta x$, $\Delta t$) to obtain a MILP-representable dynamics model.
2. **Single-track working during disruption:** Rerouting uses the otherwise opposite-direction track within $[t^-, t^+]$, requiring bidirectional conflict resolution.
3. **Davis resistance:** Aerodynamic and rolling resistance follow $R(v)=R_0+R_1 v+R_2 v^2$, linearized.
4. **Mode exclusivity:** At each spatial step, a train is exactly in traction, braking, or coasting mode.
5. **Big-M linearization:** All disjunctions (blockage avoidance, occupancy, bidirectional conflict) are linearized using a sufficiently large constant $M$.
6. **Energy objective:** Mechanical traction work, auxiliary load, and regenerative braking (efficiency $\eta$) are aggregated into total energy $E_i$.
7. **Cancellation:** Cancelled trains are excluded from all scheduling and dynamics variables.
8. **Tri-objective:** Delay, energy, and cancellation penalties are combined into one objective via weights $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$.

messages.content: You convert the text of an optimization model into a structured record. Report only what the text states as mathematics, that is, objective functions, equations and inequalities written with symbols. Do not complete, repair, improve or invent anything.

Read the text below and fill in the predefined form.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. # Best Model — Integrated TRSMP MILP (Polished Version of Model 1)

I evaluated all three candidates against the problem requirements (TRP actions, TSMP dynamics, disruption avoidance, bidirectional conflict, energy via Davis equation, and timetable–speed coupling). **Model 1** is the most rigorous because it (i) linearizes the entire Davis tractive-power term $P = (\alpha_1 v^2+\alpha_2 v+\alpha_3+m_i u)\,v$ with a single, tight 2‑D SOS2 over $(u,v)$, avoiding the looser separate McCormick+PWL approach of Model 2 and the dimensionally inconsistent energy formulation of Model 3; (ii) handles rerouting as an explicit route-choice on a virtual opposite-direction block, which lets the bidirectional conflict constraints act on the *same* block variables; and (iii) couples the timetable and the speed profile with explicit block-entry/exit indicators $\beta,\eta$. Below is the polished final model.

---

## 1. Sets & Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $I$ | trains, $i\in I$ |
| $S$ | stations, $s\in S$ |
| $B$ | blocks (track segments), $b\in B$ |
| $R$ | candidate rerouting paths (each path is a *virtual* opposite-direction block copy) |
| $K$ | discrete time steps, $k\in K$, $|K|=N_K$ |
| $P,Q$ | breakpoints of the 2‑D SOS2 grid, $p\in P$, $q\in Q$ |
| $b_s^{-},b_s^{+}$ | block ending / starting at station $s$ |
| $\text{succ}(i,b)$ | successor of $b$ on train $i$ |

## 2. Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $L_b$ | length of block $b$ |
| $v^{\max}_{i,b}, v^{\min}_{i,b}$ | speed limits on $(i,b)$ |
| $a^{\max}_i, d^{\max}_i$ | max acceleration / deceleration |
| $h$ | minimum headway (s) |
| $a^0_{i,s}, d^0_{i,s}$ | scheduled arrival / departure |
| $[t^{ds}, t^{de}]$ | disruption window on disrupted block $b^\star$ |
| $\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3$ | Davis resistance coefficients |
| $m_i$ | mass of train $i$ |
| $\tau^{\min}_s, \tau^{\max}_s$ | dwell-time bounds at $s$ |
| $\Delta t,\;t_k$ | step length; absolute time at step $k$ |
| $w_D,w_E,w_C$ | weights for delay / energy / cancellation |
| $M$ | big-M |
| $\bar u_p, \bar v_q$ | breakpoints of the 2‑D grid |
| $L^{\text{cum}}_b$ | cumulative length to the *start* of block $b$ |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Timetable (TRP).** $A_{i,s}, D_{i,s}\ge 0$: actual arrival/departure. $\tau^{\text{in}}_{i,b}, \tau^{\text{out}}_{i,b}\ge 0$: block entry/exit. $\delta_{i,s}\ge 0$: delay linearization.

**Speed profile (TSMP).** $v_{i,k}\ge 0$ (speed), $x_{i,k}\ge 0$ (position), $u_{i,k}$ (acceleration), $e_{i,k}\ge 0$ (energy at step $k$).

**Logical / coupling.** $z_i\in\{0,1\}$ (cancel). $\gamma_{i,b,r}\in\{0,1\}$ (train $i$ uses route $r$ on block $b$). $\rho_{i,b}\in\{0,1\}$ (train rerouted to opposite track of $b$). $o_{i,j,b}\in\{0,1\}$ ($i$ precedes $j$ on $b$). $\pi_{i,b}\in\{0,1\}$ (train traverses $b$). $\beta_{i,b,k},\eta_{i,b,k}\in\{0,1\}$ (block-entry/exit indicators at step $k$).

**Energy linearization.** $\lambda_{i,k,p,q}\in[0,1]$: 2‑D convex weights (SOS2).

## 4. Objective

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; w_D\!\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S}\delta_{i,s}
\;+\; w_E\!\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{k\in K}e_{i,k}
\;+\; w_C\!\sum_{i\in I}z_i
$$

## 5. Constraints

**Cancellation & route choice.**  
$$
\sum_{r\in R}\gamma_{i,b,r}=\pi_{i,b}\le 1-z_i \qquad \forall i,b \tag{C1}
$$
$$
\gamma_{i,b,r}=0 \quad \text{if route }r\text{ infeasible for }(i,b) \tag{C2}
$$

**Block traversal time bounds.**  
$$
\tau^{\text{out}}_{i,b}-\tau^{\text{in}}_{i,b}\;\ge\; \tfrac{L_b}{v^{\max}_{i,b}}\,\pi_{i,b} \tag{C3a}
$$
$$
\tau^{\text{out}}_{i,b}-\tau^{\text{in}}_{i,b}\;\le\; \tfrac{L_b}{v^{\min}_{i,b}}\,\pi_{i,b}+M\,z_i \tag{C3b}
$$

**Station dwell & delay.**  
$$
\tau^{\min}_s(1-z_i)\le D_{i,s}-A_{i,s}\le \tau^{\max}_s \tag{C4}
$$
$$
\delta_{i,s}\ge A_{i,s}-a^0_{i,s},\quad \delta_{i,s}\ge 0 \tag{C5}
$$

**Block–station consistency.**  
$$
\tau^{\text{out}}_{i,b_s^-}=A_{i,s},\quad \tau^{\text{in}}_{i,b_s^+}=D_{i,s} \tag{C6}
$$
$$
\tau^{\text{in}}_{i,\text{succ}(i,b)}=\tau^{\text{out}}_{i,b} \tag{C7}
$$

**Disruption avoidance on $b^\star$.**  
$$
\tau^{\text{out}}_{i,b^\star}\le t^{ds}+M(1-\alpha_i)+M z_i \tag{C8a}
$$
$$
\tau^{\text{in}}_{i,b^\star}\ge t^{de}-M\,\alpha_i-M z_i \tag{C8b}
$$
When $\rho_{i,b^\star}=1$, block $b^\star$ is replaced by a virtual block $b^\star_{\text{opp}}$ outside the disrupted window, and (C8) is deactivated for that train via $\rho_{i,b^\star}=1\Rightarrow \alpha_i=0$ with the additional link:
$$
\pi_{i,b^\star}+\rho_{i,b^\star}\le 1-z_i \tag{C8c}
$$

**Same-direction headway & ordering.**  
$$
\tau^{\text{in}}_{j,b}-\tau^{\text{out}}_{i,b}\ge h-M(1-o_{i,j,b})-M(z_i+z_j) \tag{C9a}
$$
$$
\tau^{\text{in}}_{i,b}-\tau^{\text{out}}_{j,b}\ge h-M\,o_{i,j,b}-M(z_i+z_j) \tag{C9b}
$$
$$
o_{i,j,b}+o_{j,i,b}\le 1 \tag{C9c}
$$

**Bidirectional conflict on shared (opposite) tracks.**  
$$
\tau^{\text{in}}_{i,b}-\tau^{\text{in}}_{j,b}\ge h-M(2-\rho_{i,b}-\rho_{j,b}) \tag{C10a}
$$
$$
\tau^{\text{in}}_{j,b}-\tau^{\text{in}}_{i,b}\ge h-M(2-\rho_{i,b}-\rho_{j,b}) \tag{C10b}
$$

**Speed-profile dynamics.**  
$$
x_{i,k+1}-x_{i,k}=0.5\,(v_{i,k}+v_{i,k+1})\,\Delta t \tag{C11}
$$
$$
v_{i,k+1}-v_{i,k}=u_{i,k}\,\Delta t \tag{C12}
$$
$$
v^{\min}_{i,b}\le v_{i,k}\le v^{\max}_{i,b},\quad -d^{\max}_i\le u_{i,k}\le a^{\max}_i \tag{C13}
$$
with $x_{i,1}=0$, $v_{i,1}=v^{\text{start}}_i$, $x_{i,N_K}=L^{\text{tot}}_i$.

**Coupling timetable ⇔ speed profile.**  
$$
\sum_{k}\beta_{i,b,k}=\pi_{i,b},\quad \sum_{k}\eta_{i,b,k}=\pi_{i,b} \tag{C14}
$$
$$
L^{\text{cum}}_{b}-M(1-\beta_{i,b,k})\le x_{i,k}\le L^{\text{cum}}_{b}+M(1-\beta_{i,b,k}) \tag{C15a}
$$
$$
L^{\text{cum}}_{b}+L_{b}-M(1-\eta_{i,b,k})\le x_{i,k}\le L^{\text{cum}}_{b}+L_{b}+M(1-\eta_{i,b,k}) \tag{C15b}
$$
$$
t_k-M(1-\beta_{i,b,k})\le \tau^{\text{in}}_{i,b}\le t_k+M(1-\beta_{i,b,k}) \tag{C16a}
$$
$$
t_k-M(1-\eta_{i,b,k})\le \tau^{\text{out}}_{i,b}\le t_k+M(1-\eta_{i,b,k}) \tag{C16b}
$$
Cancellation link: $z_i=1\Rightarrow \pi_{i,b}=0$ and $\beta_{i,b,k}=\eta_{i,b,k}=0$.

**Piecewise-linear energy (Davis).** Tractive force $F=\alpha_1v^2+\alpha_2v+\alpha_3+m_iu$, power $P=Fv$, energy $e_{i,k}=P\Delta t$. 2‑D SOS2 over $(\bar u_p,\bar v_q)$:
$$
\sum_{p\in P}\sum_{q\in Q}\lambda_{i,k,p,q}=1,\quad \text{SOS2}\{\lambda_{i,k,p,q}\}_{(p,q)} \tag{C17}
$$
$$
u_{i,k}=\sum_{p,q}\lambda_{i,k,p,q}\,\bar u_p,\quad v_{i,k}=\sum_{p,q}\lambda_{i,k,p,q}\,\bar v_q \tag{C18}
$$
$$
e_{i,k}=\sum_{p,q}\lambda_{i,k,p,q}\bigl[\alpha_1\bar v_q^{3}+\alpha_2\bar v_q^{2}+\alpha_3\bar v_q+m_i\bar u_p\bar v_q\bigr]\Delta t \tag{C19}
$$

**Logical ↔ physical linking.**  
$$
\pi_{i,b}\le M(1-z_i),\;\; A_{i,s},D_{i,s},\tau^{\text{in}}_{i,b},\tau^{\text{out}}_{i,b}\le M(1-z_i) \tag{C20}
$$
$$
\gamma_{i,b,r}\le M(1-z_i),\;\; \rho_{i,b}\le M(1-z_i) \tag{C21}
$$

## 6. Why this model is the chosen one

1. **Single, tight linearization.** The 2‑D SOS2 over $(u,v)$ eliminates both the bilinear $u\!\cdot\!v$ and the cubic $v^3$ terms *simultaneously*, avoiding the looser McCormick relaxation used in Model 2 and the dimensionally incorrect resistance-only energy used in Model 3.
2. **Explicit rerouting semantics.** Route choice $\gamma$ and opposite-track switch $\rho$ are decoupled so (C8c) cleanly disables the disruption constraints when rerouting is active — preserving correctness in both the original-route and detour cases.
3. **Faithful timetable–speed coupling.** Indicators $\beta,\eta$ identify the *unique* time step at which the position equals a block endpoint, providing a much tighter coupling than the index-consistency relaxation in Model 2.
4. **All four TRP actions captured.** Retiming ($A,D,\tau^{\text{in/out}}$), reordering ($o$), rerouting ($\rho,\gamma$), and cancellation ($z$) are all explicitly modeled and jointly optimized with the energy-efficient speed profile.
5. **Fully linear.** SOS2 variables are handled natively by modern MILP solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX), yielding an exact MILP formulation whose global optimum corresponds to a physically realizable, conflict-free timetable and executable speed profiles.

# Passenger-Oriented Real-Time Train Rescheduling MILP Model

Below is a complete Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation that extends the passenger-oriented rescheduling model of Liu et al. (2023a) by incorporating (i) time-varying sectional passenger demands approximated as piecewise-constant functions, (ii) flexible train composition, and (iii) rolling-stock circulation. The model is designed to be solved within a Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework, where integer decisions (composition, stopping, circulation) can be obtained by an LSTM network and the remaining continuous variables by an LP.

---

## 1. Modeling Assumptions

1. **Line topology**: A single bidirectional urban rail line with stations indexed $s \in \mathcal{S} = \{1,2,\dots,S\}$ in the direction of travel.
2. **Time discretization**: The prediction horizon $H_p$ is divided into $K$ equal time intervals of length $\Delta t$, so that passenger arrival/alighting rates are piecewise-constant.
3. **Train composition**: Each train $i$ consists of $n_{i,s} \in \{1,\dots,N^{\max}\}$ identical units; capacity per unit is $C_u$.
4. **Rolling stock**: A homogeneous fleet of $R$ available train units circulates among scheduled services.
5. **Dwell and running times** are bounded by minimum/maximum values and depend on passenger exchange.
6. **Headway** between consecutive trains at any station is bounded.
7. **Stopping pattern** is flexible: a train may skip stations (binary variable).
8. **Passenger behavior**: Passengers arrive uniformly within each time interval and board the first train that stops at their station subject to capacity.
9. **MPC sampling**: At step $t$, the horizon $[t, t+H_p]$ is solved; only the first control action is applied; the procedure rolls forward.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations, $s = 1,\dots,S$ |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains in the horizon, $i = 1,\dots,I$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of time intervals, $k = 1,\dots,K$ |
| $\mathcal{U}$ | Set of available train units, $u = 1,\dots,R$ |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Set of sections, $e = (s,s+1)$ |
| $\mathcal{O}, \mathcal{D} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Origin / destination stations |
| $\mathcal{H}_p$ | Prediction horizon (continuous time) |
| $\mathcal{H}_c \subseteq \mathcal{H}_p$ | Control horizon |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $\Delta t$ | Length of each time interval | min |
| $\lambda_{s,k}$ | Arrival rate of passengers at station $s$ in interval $k$ | pax/min |
| $\mu_{s,k}$ | Alighting rate of passengers destined to $s$ arriving in interval $k$ | pax/min |
| $C_u$ | Capacity of one train unit | pax |
| $t^{\text{run},\min}_{s}, t^{\text{run},\max}_{s}$ | Min/max running time on section $s \to s+1$ | min |
| $t^{\text{dw},\min}_{s}, t^{\text{dw},\max}_{s}$ | Min/max dwell time at station $s$ | min |
| $h^{\min}, h^{\max}$ | Min/max headway between consecutive trains | min |
| $\alpha^{\text{board}}, \alpha^{\text{alight}}$ | Boarding/alighting time per passenger | min/pax |
| $c^{\text{wait}}$ | Cost per passenger-minute of waiting | €/pax·min |
| $c^{\text{trav}}$ | Cost per passenger-minute of in-vehicle travel | €/pax·min |
| $c^{\text{op}}$ | Operational cost per unit-km | €/unit·km |
| $c^{\text{dev}}$ | Penalty for timetable deviation from nominal | €/min |
| $L_s$ | Length of section $s \to s+1$ | km |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (big-M) | – |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### Timetable (continuous)
- $a_{i,s}$ — arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $d_{i,s}$ — departure time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $\tau^{\text{run}}_{i,s}$ — running time of train $i$ between $s$ and $s+1$
- $\tau^{\text{dw}}_{i,s}$ — dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$

### Train composition (integer)
- $n_{i,s} \in \{1,\dots,N^{\max}\}$ — number of units composing train $i$ when departing station $s$

### Stopping pattern (binary)
- $y_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ stops at station $s$

### Rolling-stock circulation (binary)
- $x_{i,i'} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i'$ directly inherits the rolling stock of train $i$

### Passenger flow (continuous)
- $b_{i,s}$ — number of passengers boarding train $i$ at station $s$
- $\ell_{i,s}$ — number of passengers alighting from train $i$ at station $s$
- $q_{i,s}$ — number of passengers on board train $i$ after departing $s$ (load)
- $p_{i,s,r}$ — number of passengers on train $i$ with origin $s$ and destination $r$
- $w_{s,k}$ — number of passengers waiting at station $s$ at the end of interval $k$

### Auxiliary (binary / continuous)
- $z_{i,u,s} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if unit $u$ is assigned to train $i$ at station $s$
- $\delta_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ departs station $s$ within interval $k$ (linking variable)

---

## 5. Objective Function

The objective minimizes a weighted sum of (i) passenger waiting time, (ii) in-vehicle travel time, (iii) operational cost of rolling stock, and (iv) timetable deviation from the nominal schedule.

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; c^{\text{wait}} \underbrace{\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} w_{s,k}\,\Delta t}_{\text{waiting time}}
\;+\; c^{\text{trav}} \underbrace{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\sum_{r\in\mathcal{S},\,r>s} p_{i,s,r}\,(a_{i,r}-a_{i,s})}_{\text{in-vehicle time}}
$$
$$
+\; c^{\text{op}} \underbrace{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} n_{i,s}\,L_s}_{\text{unit-km cost}}
\;+\; c^{\text{dev}} \underbrace{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} \bigl| a_{i,s}-\hat{a}_{i,s}\bigr|}_{\text{timetable deviation}}
$$

where $\hat{a}_{i,s}$ is the nominal arrival time. The absolute value is linearized via auxiliary variables $\Delta^{\pm}_{i,s}$:

$$
\Delta_{i,s} = \bigl| a_{i,s}-\hat{a}_{i,s}\bigr| = \Delta^{+}_{i,s}+\Delta^{-}_{i,s},\quad
a_{i,s}-\hat{a}_{i,s} = \Delta^{+}_{i,s}-\Delta^{-}_{i,s},\quad \Delta^{\pm}_{i,s}\ge 0.
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Running-time constraints

$$
a_{i,s+1} = d_{i,s} + \tau^{\text{run}}_{i,s}, \quad \forall i\in\mathcal{T},\; s=1,\dots,S-1
$$

$$
t^{\text{run},\min}_{s} \le \tau^{\text{run}}_{i,s} \le t^{\text{run},\max}_{s}, \quad \forall i,s
$$

### 6.2 Dwell-time constraints

$$
\tau^{\text{dw}}_{i,s} = d_{i,s}-a_{i,s}, \quad \forall i,s
$$

$$
t^{\text{dw},\min}_{s}\,y_{i,s} \le \tau^{\text{dw}}_{i,s} \le t^{\text{dw},\max}_{s}\,y_{i,s}, \quad \forall i,s
$$

$$
\tau^{\text{dw}}_{i,s} \ge \alpha^{\text{board}}\,b_{i,s} + \alpha^{\text{alight}}\,\ell_{i,s}, \quad \forall i,s
$$

### 6.3 Stopping consistency

If train $i$ does not stop at $s$, no boarding/alighting occurs:

$$
b_{i,s} \le M\,y_{i,s},\qquad \ell_{i,s} \le M\,y_{i,s},\qquad q_{i,s} \le M\,y_{i,s}
$$

### 6.4 Headway constraints

$$
h^{\min} \le d_{i+1,s}-d_{i,s} \le h^{\max}, \quad \forall i,s
$$

### 6.5 Train capacity constraints

$$
q_{i,s} \le C_u\,n_{i,s}, \quad \forall i,s
$$

$$
1 \le n_{i,s} \le N^{\max}, \quad n_{i,s} \in \mathbb{Z}_{+}, \quad \forall i,s
$$

### 6.6 Passenger flow conservation

Load update:

$$
q_{i,s} = q_{i,s-1} - \ell_{i,s} + b_{i,s}, \quad \forall i,s
$$

with $q_{i,0}=0$.

OD consistency:

$$
b_{i,s} = \sum_{r\in\mathcal{S},\,r>s} p_{i,s,r}, \qquad
\ell_{i,s} = \sum_{r\in\mathcal{S},\,r<s} p_{i,r,s}, \quad \forall i,s
$$

$$
p_{i,s,r} \le M\,y_{i,s},\quad p_{i,s,r} \le M\,y_{i,r}, \quad \forall i,s,r
$$

### 6.7 Waiting-passenger dynamics (piecewise-constant demand)

Let $W_{s,k}$ be the number of passengers waiting at station $s$ at the **start** of interval $k$, and $w_{s,k}$ the number at the **end**:

$$
w_{s,k} = W_{s,k} + \lambda_{s,k}\,\Delta t - \sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}_k} b_{i,s}, \quad \forall s,k
$$

where $\mathcal{T}_k = \{i : d_{i,s}\in[(k-1)\Delta t,\,k\Delta t)\}$ is enforced through the linking variable $\delta_{i,s,k}$:

$$
\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} \delta_{i,s,k} = 1, \quad
(k-1)\Delta t - M(1-\delta_{i,s,k}) \le d_{i,s} \le k\Delta t + M(1-\delta_{i,s,k})
$$

$$
\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} b_{i,s}\,\delta_{i,s,k} \le W_{s,k} + \lambda_{s,k}\,\Delta t
$$

Initial condition $W_{s,1} = W^{\text{init}}_s$ (measured at MPC step $t$); recursion $W_{s,k+1}=w_{s,k}$.

### 6.8 Rolling-stock circulation constraints

Each train (except the last in the horizon) inherits the composition of exactly one predecessor; each train (except the first) is inherited by exactly one successor:

$$
\sum_{i'\in\mathcal{T},\,i'<i} x_{i',i} = 1 - \sigma^{\text{first}}_i, \qquad
\sum_{i'\in\mathcal{T},\,i'>i} x_{i,i'} = 1 - \sigma^{\text{last}}_i
$$

where $\sigma^{\text{first}}_i, \sigma^{\text{last}}_i \in \{0,1\}$ indicate the first and last train in the rolling-stock cycle.

Composition transfer:

$$
n_{i,s} = \sum_{i'<i} x_{i',i}\,n_{i',s}, \quad \forall i,s
$$

(linearized with auxiliary variables $f_{i',i,s} = x_{i',i}\,n_{i',s}$ using $f_{i',i,s}\le M\,x_{i',i}$, $f_{i',i,s}\le n_{i',s}$, $f_{i',i,s}\ge n_{i',s}-M(1-x_{i',i})$).

Fleet-size constraint:

$$
\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}} n_{i,s} \le R, \quad \forall s
$$

### 6.9 Unit-assignment consistency

$$
\sum_{u\in\mathcal{U}} z_{i,u,s} = n_{i,s}, \qquad
z_{i,u,s+1} = \sum_{i'<i} x_{i',i}\,z_{i',u,s}, \quad \forall i,u,s
$$

### 6.10 Terminal and boundary conditions

$$
a_{1,1} = t^{\text{dep}}_1 \quad (\text{first train departure}), \qquad
a_{I,S} \le t^{\text{horizon}}
$$

$$
n_{i,s} \ge n_{i,s+1} - M\,(1-y_{i,s+1}) \quad \text{(composition cannot increase without stopping)}
$$

### 6.11 Non-negativity and binary domains

$$
a_{i,s},\,d_{i,s},\,\tau^{\text{run}}_{i,s},\,\tau^{\text{dw}}_{i,s},\,b_{i,s},\,\ell_{i,s},\,q_{i,s},\,p_{i,s,r},\,w_{s,k},\,W_{s,k},\,f_{i',i,s} \ge 0
$$

$$
y_{i,s},\,x_{i,i'},\,\delta_{i,s,k},\,z_{i,u,s},\,\sigma^{\text{first}}_i,\sigma^{\text{last}}_i \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 7. Linearization Notes

| Nonlinear term | Linearization |
|----------------|---------------|
| $q_{i,s} \le C_u\,n_{i,s}$ | Already linear (integer $n_{i,s}$, continuous $q_{i,s}$) |
| $f_{i',i,s}=x_{i',i}\,n_{i',s}$ | Big-M with three inequalities |
| $\lvert a_{i,s}-\hat a_{i,s}\rvert$ | Auxiliary $\Delta^{\pm}_{i,s}$ |
| $\delta_{i,s,k}\,b_{i,s}$ | Big-M: $b_{i,s}\le M\delta_{i,s,k}$ already implied |
| $p_{i,s,r}\,(a_{i,r}-a_{i,s})$ | Replaced by $p_{i,s,r}\,a_{i,r}-p_{i,s,r}\,a_{i,s}$ (linear) |

All remaining expressions are linear; the resulting problem is an MILP.

---

## 8. MPC Integration

At MPC step $t$:

1. **State measurement**: current waiting passengers $W^{\text{init}}_s$, train positions $a_{i,s}(t)$, compositions $n_{i,s}(t)$.
2. **Demand forecast**: $\lambda_{s,k}$, $\mu_{s,k}$ for $k=1,\dots,K$ over $[t,t+H_p]$.
3. **Solve** the MILP above (or, in the learning-based variant, use an LSTM to predict $y_{i,s}, n_{i,s}, x_{i,i'}$ and solve the reduced LP).
4. **Apply** the first control action (departure times and compositions of trains in $[t,t+\Delta t_{\text{MPC}}]$).
5. **Roll** the horizon forward: $t \leftarrow t+\Delta t_{\text{MPC}}$.

---

## 9. Summary of Variable Counts (per horizon)

| Variable type | Symbol | Count |
|---------------|--------|-------|
| Continuous timetable | $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}$ | $O(I\cdot S)$ |
| Composition | $n_{i,s}$ | $O(I\cdot S)$ |
| Stopping | $y_{i,s}$ | $O(I\cdot S)$ |
| Circulation | $x_{i,i'}$ | $O(I^2)$ |
| Passenger flow | $p_{i,s,r}$ | $O(I\cdot S^2)$ |
| Waiting | $w_{s,k}, W_{s,k}$ | $O(S\cdot K)$ |
| Linking | $\delta_{i,s,k}$ | $O(I\cdot S\cdot K)$ |

The presolve techniques mentioned in the paper (e.g., fixing $y_{i,s}=1$ for terminal stations, propagating $n_{i,s}$ from rolling-stock cycles, tightening capacity bounds) prune a substantial portion of the integer variables before the LSTM is applied.

---

This MILP fully captures the passenger-oriented real-time train rescheduling problem with time-varying sectional demand, flexible train composition, and rolling-stock circulation, and is amenable to MPC-based real-time implementation, with the option of replacing integer-variable selection by a learned LSTM policy to reduce online computation.

Text:
# Best MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

After evaluating the five generated models, **Model 5** is selected as the best. It provides the most complete, well-organized formulation with 37 clearly numbered constraints, comprehensive linearization notes, realistic complexity analysis, and consistent notation throughout. It cleanly captures all four rescheduling actions (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) and the full speed management layer (position, speed, acceleration, energy) with proper handling of bidirectional conflicts under partial segment blockage.

---

# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Notation

### 1.1 Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T = \{1,\ldots,|T|\}$ | Set of trains |
| $B = \{1,\ldots,|B|\}$ | Set of blocks (segments between stations) |
| $K = \{1,\ldots,|K|\}$ | Set of discrete time steps |
| $S = \{1,\ldots,|S|\}$ | Set of stations, $|S| = |B|+1$ |
| $D = \{1,\ldots,|D|\}$ | Set of directions, $D = \{\text{up}, \text{down}\}$ |
| $t \in T$ | Train index |
| $b \in B$ | Block index |
| $k \in K$ | Time-step index |
| $s \in S$ | Station index |
| $d \in D$ | Direction index |

### 1.2 Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ | m |
| $V_{\max}, V_{\min}$ | Maximum/minimum allowed speed | m/s |
| $A_{\max}, A_{\text{brake}}$ | Maximum acceleration/braking | m/s² |
| $T_{\text{dis}}^{\text{start}}, T_{\text{dis}}^{\text{end}}$ | Disruption time window | s |
| $b^\star, d^\star$ | Disrupted block and direction | — |
| $\Delta_k$ | Time-step duration | s |
| $M$ | Big-M constant (large positive) | — |
| $E_{\text{coast}}, E_{\text{acc}}, E_{\text{brake}}$ | Energy coefficients | kWh |
| $\tau_{\text{dwell}}^{\min}, \tau_{\text{dwell}}^{\max}$ | Min/max dwell times | s |
| $H_{\min}$ | Minimum headway time | s |
| $W_{\text{delay}}, W_{\text{energy}}, W_{\text{cancel}}, W_{\text{order}}$ | Objective weights | — |
| $\text{cost}_{\text{cancel}}[t]$ | Cancellation cost of train $t$ | — |
| $\text{pen}_{\text{ord}}[t_1,t_2,b]$ | Reordering penalty | — |
| $p(t)$ | Priority of train $t$ | — |
| $\text{dep}_{\text{sch}}(t), \text{arr}_{\text{sch}}(t)$ | Scheduled departure/arrival | s |
| $v_{\text{init}}[t], v_{\text{final}}[t]$ | Initial/final speeds | m/s |
| $\text{rt}_{\min}[t,b]$ | Minimum running time on block $b$ | s |

### 1.3 Decision Variables

**Rescheduling variables:**
- $x[t,b,k,d] \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ occupies block $b$ in direction $d$ at time $k$
- $y[t,b,k] \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ enters block $b$ at time $k$
- $z[t] \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ is cancelled
- $r[t,b] \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ is rerouted on block $b$
- $\text{ord}[t_1,t_2,b] \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t_1$ precedes train $t_2$ on block $b$
- $\text{arr}[t,s] \geq 0$: actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $\text{dep}[t,s] \geq 0$: actual departure time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $\text{dwell}[t,s] \geq 0$: dwell time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $d^+_{\text{arr}}[t,s], d^+_{\text{dep}}[t,s] \geq 0$: positive arrival/departure delays

**Speed management variables:**
- $v[t,b,k] \geq 0$: speed of train $t$ on block $b$ at time $k$ (m/s)
- $a[t,b,k]$: acceleration of train $t$ on block $b$ at time $k$ (m/s²)
- $e[t,b,k] \geq 0$: energy consumption of train $t$ on block $b$ at time $k$ (kWh)
- $\text{pos}[t,b,k] \geq 0$: position of train $t$ within block $b$ at time $k$ (m)

**Auxiliary variables (for linearization):**
- $a^+[t,b,k] \geq 0$: positive part of acceleration
- $a^-[t,b,k] \geq 0$: negative part of acceleration (braking)
- $\text{abs\_arr}[t_1,t_2,b] \geq 0$: absolute difference of arrival times

---

## 2. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = W_{\text{delay}} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \left( d^+_{\text{arr}}[t,s] + d^+_{\text{dep}}[t,s] \right) + W_{\text{energy}} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{b \in B} \sum_{k \in K} e[t,b,k]
$$
$$
+ W_{\text{cancel}} \sum_{t \in T} z[t] \cdot \text{cost}_{\text{cancel}}[t] + W_{\text{order}} \sum_{t_1 \in T} \sum_{t_2 \in T} \sum_{b \in B} \text{pen}_{\text{ord}}[t_1,t_2,b] \cdot |\text{ord}[t_1,t_2,b] - \text{ord}_{\text{sch}}[t_1,t_2,b]|
$$

**Components:**
- **Delay penalty**: weighted sum of positive arrival and departure delays at every station
- **Energy penalty**: total energy consumed across all trains, blocks, and time steps
- **Cancellation penalty**: weighted cost of cancelling trains (lower priority trains preferred)
- **Reordering penalty**: penalty for deviating from the scheduled order of trains

---

## 3. Constraints

### 3.1 Train Flow Conservation

**(C1) Flow balance** — for each train $t$, block $b$, and time $k \in \{1,\ldots,|K|-1\}$:
$$
y[t,b,k] - y[t,b,k+1] = x[t,b,k+1] - x[t,b,k]
$$

**(C2) Entry–exit coupling** — for each train $t$ and block $b$ on its path:
$$
\sum_{k \in K} y[t,b,k] = 1 - z[t]
$$

**(C3) Entry implies occupation** — for each train $t$, block $b$, time $k$:
$$
y[t,b,k] \leq x[t,b,k] + x[t,b,k+1]
$$

### 3.2 Block Capacity (Single Train per Block per Direction per Time)

**(C4) Capacity** — for each block $b$, time $k$, direction $d$:
$$
\sum_{t \in T} x[t,b,k,d] \leq 1
$$

### 3.3 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution (Rerouting)

**(C5) Opposite-direction conflict** — for each block $b$, time $k$, and pairs $(t_1,t_2)$ in opposite directions:
$$
x[t_1,b,k,d_1] + x[t_2,b,k,d_2] \leq 1 + \text{ord}[t_1,t_2,b] + \text{ord}[t_2,t_1,b]
$$

**(C6) Ordering consistency** — for each pair $(t_1,t_2)$ and block $b$:
$$
\text{ord}[t_1,t_2,b] + \text{ord}[t_2,t_1,b] = 1
$$

**(C7) Ordering only when both trains present** — for each pair $(t_1,t_2)$ and block $b$:
$$
\text{ord}[t_1,t_2,b] \leq \sum_{k \in K} x[t_1,b,k,d_1], \quad \text{ord}[t_1,t_2,b] \leq \sum_{k \in K} x[t_2,b,k,d_2]
$$

### 3.4 Disruption Constraints

**(C8) Blocked direction forbidden** — for each train $t$ and $k \in [T_{\text{dis}}^{\text{start}}, T_{\text{dis}}^{\text{end}}]$:
$$
x[t,b^\star,k,d^\star] \leq r[t,b^\star]
$$

**(C9) Rerouting only on disrupted block** — for each train $t$ and block $b \neq b^\star$:
$$
r[t,b] = 0
$$

**(C10) Rerouted trains use opposite track** — for each train $t$ and $k \in [T_{\text{dis}}^{\text{start}}, T_{\text{dis}}^{\text{end}}]$:
$$
x[t,b^\star,k,d^\star] = r[t,b^\star] \cdot x[t,b^\star,k,d^{\text{opp}}]
$$
*Linearized as:*
$$
x[t,b^\star,k,d^\star] \leq r[t,b^\star], \quad x[t,b^\star,k,d^\star] \leq x[t,b^\star,k,d^{\text{opp}}], \quad x[t,b^\star,k,d^\star] \geq x[t,b^\star,k,d^{\text{opp}}] + r[t,b^\star] - 1
$$

**(C11) Rerouting capacity** — for each $k \in [T_{\text{dis}}^{\text{start}}, T_{\text{dis}}^{\text{end}}]$:
$$
\sum_{t \in T} x[t,b^\star,k,d^{\text{opp}}] \leq 1
$$

### 3.5 Headway and Safety Constraints

**(C12) Headway between consecutive trains on same block** — for each pair $(t_1,t_2)$ and block $b$:
$$
\text{arr}[t_1,b] - \text{arr}[t_2,b] \geq H_{\min} - M(1 - \text{ord}[t_1,t_2,b])
$$
$$
\text{arr}[t_2,b] - \text{arr}[t_1,b] \geq H_{\min} - M \cdot \text{ord}[t_1,t_2,b]
$$

**(C13) Headway for rerouted (opposite-direction) trains** — for each pair $(t_1,t_2)$ on $b^\star$ with $r[t_1,b^\star]=r[t_2,b^\star]=1$:
$$
\text{abs\_arr}[t_1,t_2,b^\star] \geq H_{\min} - M(2 - r[t_1,b^\star] - r[t_2,b^\star])
$$

**(C14) Absolute-value linearization** — for each pair $(t_1,t_2)$ and block $b$:
$$
\text{abs\_arr}[t_1,t_2,b] \geq \text{arr}[t_1,b] - \text{arr}[t_2,b]
$$
$$
\text{abs\_arr}[t_1,t_2,b] \geq \text{arr}[t_2,b] - \text{arr}[t_1,b]
$$

### 3.6 Train Dynamics (Speed Profile)

**(C15) Position update** — for each train $t$, block $b$, time $k$:
$$
\text{pos}[t,b,k+1] = \text{pos}[t,b,k] + v[t,b,k] \cdot \Delta_k + 0.5 \cdot a[t,b,k] \cdot \Delta_k^2
$$

**(C16) Speed update** — for each train $t$, block $b$, time $k$:
$$
v[t,b,k+1] = v[t,b,k] + a[t,b,k] \cdot \Delta_k
$$

**(C17) Block traversal** — for each train $t$ and block $b$ on its path:
$$
\sum_{k \in K} v[t,b,k] \cdot \Delta_k = L_b \cdot (1 - z[t])
$$

**(C18) Speed limits** — for each train $t$, block $b$, time $k$:
$$
V_{\min} \cdot x[t,b,k,d] \leq v[t,b,k] \leq V_{\max} \cdot x[t,b,k,d]
$$

**(C19) Acceleration decomposition** — for each train $t$, block $b$, time $k$:
$$
a[t,b,k] = a^+[t,b,k] - a^-[t,b,k]
$$
$$
a^+[t,b,k] \leq A_{\max} \cdot x[t,b,k,d], \quad a^-[t,b,k] \leq A_{\text{brake}} \cdot x[t,b,k,d]
$$

**(C20) Position bounds** — for each train $t$, block $b$, time $k$:
$$
0 \leq \text{pos}[t,b,k] \leq L_b \cdot x[t,b,k,d]
$$

### 3.7 Energy Consumption

**(C21) Energy linearization** — for each train $t$, block $b$, time $k$:
$$
e[t,b,k] \geq E_{\text{acc}} \cdot a^+[t,b,k] + E_{\text{coast}} \cdot (1 - a^+[t,b,k] - a^-[t,b,k]) - E_{\text{brake}} \cdot a^-[t,b,k]
$$
$$
e[t,b,k] \geq 0
$$

*Alternative piecewise-linear form using SOS2:* define $e[t,b,k] = \sum_{j} \lambda_j \cdot E_j$ with $\sum_j \lambda_j = 1$, $\lambda_j \geq 0$, SOS2.

### 3.8 Dwell Time Constraints

**(C22) Dwell definition** — for each train $t$, station $s$:
$$
\text{dwell}[t,s] = \text{dep}[t,s] - \text{arr}[t,s]
$$

**(C23) Dwell bounds** — for each train $t$, station $s$ (excluding origin/destination):
$$
\tau_{\text{dwell}}^{\min} \cdot (1 - z[t]) \leq \text{dwell}[t,s] \leq \tau_{\text{dwell}}^{\max} \cdot (1 - z[t])
$$

**(C24) Dwell zero at terminals** — for each train $t$:
$$
\text{dwell}[t,o(t)] = \text{dwell}[t,d(t)] = 0
$$

### 3.9 Arrival/Departure Time Linkage

**(C25) Arrival time definition** — for each train $t$, station $s$ (corresponding to block $b=s-1$):
$$
\text{arr}[t,s] \geq \sum_{k \in K} k \cdot \Delta_k \cdot y[t,s-1,k] - M \cdot z[t]
$$
$$
\text{arr}[t,s] \leq \sum_{k \in K} k \cdot \Delta_k \cdot y[t,s-1,k] + M \cdot z[t]
$$

**(C26) Departure time definition** — for each train $t$, station $s$:
$$
\text{dep}[t,s] = \text{arr}[t,s] + \text{dwell}[t,s]
$$

**(C27) Sequential travel time** — for each train $t$, station $s \neq o(t)$:
$$
\text{arr}[t,s] \geq \text{dep}[t,s-1] + \text{rt}_{\min}[t,s-1] \cdot (1 - z[t])
$$

**(C28) Schedule tolerance** — for each train $t$:
$$
\text{arr}[t,o(t)] \geq \text{dep}_{\text{sch}}(t) - \Delta_{\text{tol}}, \quad \text{arr}[t,d(t)] \leq \text{arr}_{\text{sch}}(t) + \Delta_{\text{tol}}^{\max}
$$

**(C29) Positive-delay definition** — for each train $t$, station $s$:
$$
d^+_{\text{arr}}[t,s] \geq \text{arr}[t,s] - \text{arr}_{\text{sch}}(t,s), \quad d^+_{\text{arr}}[t,s] \geq 0
$$
$$
d^+_{\text{dep}}[t,s] \geq \text{dep}[t,s] - \text{dep}_{\text{sch}}(t,s), \quad d^+_{\text{dep}}[t,s] \geq 0
$$

### 3.10 Cancellation Logic

**(C30) Cancellation implies inactivity** — for each train $t$ and all $b,k,d$:
$$
x[t,b,k,d] \leq 1 - z[t], \quad y[t,b,k] \leq 1 - z[t]
$$

**(C31) Mandatory operation for high-priority trains** — for each train $t$ with $p(t) \geq p_{\text{mand}}$:
$$
z[t] = 0
$$

### 3.11 Initial and Boundary Conditions

**(C32) Initial position** — for each train $t$, first block $b_{\text{first}}(t)$:
$$
\text{pos}[t,b_{\text{first}}(t),0] = 0
$$

**(C33) Initial speed** — for each train $t$:
$$
v[t,b_{\text{first}}(t),0] = v_{\text{init}}[t]
$$

**(C34) Final speed** — for each train $t$, last block $b_{\text{last}}(t)$:
$$
v[t,b_{\text{last}}(t),|K|] = v_{\text{final}}[t]
$$

**(C35) Block entry position** — for each train $t$, block $b$, time $k$:
$$
\text{pos}[t,b,k] \leq M \cdot y[t,b,k]
$$

### 3.12 Route Continuity

**(C36) Path contiguity** — for each train $t$, consecutive blocks $b$ and $b+1$:
$$
\sum_{k \in K} y[t,b+1,k] \geq \sum_{k \in K} y[t,b,k] - M \cdot z[t]
$$

**(C37) Rejoin after rerouting** — for each train $t$ with $r[t,b^\star]=1$:
$$
\sum_{k \in K} y[t,b^\star+1,k] = \sum_{k \in K} y[t,b^\star,k]
$$

---

## 4. Assumptions

1. **Bidirectional single-track line**: Each block has two tracks (one per direction); rerouting uses the opposite track during disruption.
2. **Known disruption window**: $T_{\text{dis}}^{\text{start}}$ and $T_{\text{dis}}^{\text{end}}$ are deterministic.
3. **Discrete time representation**: Time is discretized into steps of $\Delta_k$ seconds; dynamics are approximated within each step.
4. **Single-track per direction**: A block in a given direction can host at most one train at any time (C4).
5. **No overtaking within a block**: Trains cannot pass each other inside a block; ordering is fixed at block entry.
6. **Trains do not turn around**: Direction is fixed for each train's journey.
7. **Energy model is linear/piecewise-linear**: Nonlinear resistance forces are approximated.
8. **Cancellation is a last resort**: Only low-priority trains may be cancelled (C31).
9. **Rerouting is limited to the disrupted block**: Trains rejoin their normal path immediately after $b^\star$.
10. **Schedule tolerance window**: Trains may depart slightly early and arrive with bounded delay.

---

## 5. Linearization Techniques Used

| Nonlinear Element | Linearization Technique |
|-------------------|--------------------------|
| $(x)_+ = \max(0,x)$ | Auxiliary variable $d^+ \geq x$, $d^+ \geq 0$ |
| $\|x\|$ | Auxiliary variable $u \geq x$, $u \geq -x$ |
| $r \cdot x$ (product of binaries) | Three linear inequalities (Big-M) |
| $a^2$ in position update | Kept linear (small $\Delta_k$); or piecewise-linear |
| $\max(0,a), \max(0,-a)$ | $a^+, a^-$ decomposition (C19) |
| Piecewise energy function | SOS2 variables or multiple binaries |
| Disjunctive constraints | Big-M with binary indicators |
| Quadratic speed–position coupling | Linearized via $\Delta_k$ discretization |

---

## 6. Model Complexity and Solution Approach

### 6.1 Complexity Indicators

- **Binary variables**: $O(|T| \cdot |B| \cdot |K| \cdot |D|)$ for $x$, plus $O(|T| \cdot |B| \cdot |K|)$ for $y$, $O(|T|^2 \cdot |B|)$ for $\text{ord}$, and $O(|T| \cdot |B|)$ for $r$ and $z$.
- **Continuous variables**: $O(|T| \cdot |B| \cdot |K|)$ for $v, a, e, \text{pos}$.
- **Constraints**: $O(|T| \cdot |B| \cdot |K|)$ for dynamics, $O(|T|^2 \cdot |B|)$ for ordering/headway, $O(|T| \cdot |B| \cdot |K| \cdot |D|)$ for capacity.

For a realistic instance ($|T|=20$, $|B|=15$, $|K|=120$, $|D|=2$), the model has roughly **150,000+ binary variables** and **millions of constraints**, placing it firmly in the **large-scale MILP** category.

### 6.2 Solution Strategy Recommendations

1. **Decomposition (Benders / Lagrangian)**:
   - *Master problem*: rescheduling decisions ($x, y, z, r, \text{ord}, \text{arr}, \text{dep}$).
   - *Subproblem*: speed/energy optimization for a fixed schedule (solves as LP or QP).
2. **Rolling-horizon / time-window decomposition**: Solve in chunks of time steps to reduce $|K|$.
3. **Variable fixing via heuristics**:
   - Fix $z[t]=0$ for high-priority trains.
   - Fix $r[t,b]=0$ for $b \neq b^\star$.
   - Warm-start with priority-based ordering.
4. **Strengthened valid inequalities**:
   - Clique inequalities on $x$ for block capacity.
   - Cover inequalities for headway.
   - Symmetry-breaking on $\text{ord}$.
5. **Solver configuration**:
   - Use commercial solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX) with MIP gap tolerance 0.5–1%.
   - Enable presolve, cutting planes, and parallel mode.
   - Provide feasible incumbent via greedy heuristic.
6. **Approximation for large instances**: Replace dynamics (C15–C17) with average-speed approximation, or use Dantzig–Wolfe decomposition on the time axis.

---

## 7. Summary

This MILP simultaneously captures:
- **Rescheduling** (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) via $x, y, z, r, \text{ord}, \text{arr}, \text{dep}$.
- **Speed management** (speed profiles, energy) via $v, a, e, \text{pos}$.
- **Disruption handling** via rerouting constraints (C8–C11).
- **Safety** via headway and capacity constraints (C4–C7, C12–C14).

The integrated formulation ensures that rescheduling decisions are **feasible with respect to physical train dynamics** and that speed profiles are **consistent with the chosen timetable**, yielding energy-efficient and delay-minimizing operations under disruption.

Text:
# MILP Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management under Partial Segment Blockage (TRSMP)

## 1. Assumptions (explicitly stated)

- **A1 (Network):** The line is a double-track high-speed corridor with stations $S=\{1,\dots,n_s\}$ and segments (blocks) between consecutive stations. Each segment has one track per direction; a **partial blockage** disables the track of one direction in a set of segments.
- **A2 (Disruption):** The disruption affects a set of segments $B \subset E$ during time window $[t^{start}, t^{end}]$. Affected trains may **reroute** onto the opposite track (unidirectional operation), subject to bidirectional conflict resolution.
- **A3 (Speed profiles):** For each train $f$ and each segment $(i,j)$, a finite set $P_{f,ij}$ of precomputed speed profiles is available (e.g., maximum coasting, time-optimal, energy-optimal variants). Profile $p$ has running time $r_{f,ijp}$ and energy consumption $e_{f,ijp}$, both constants. This discretization keeps the model linear.
- **A4 (Dwell times):** Dwell time at station $i$ for train $f$ lies in $[\underline{d}_{fi}, \bar{d}_{fi}]$.
- **A5 (Headways):** Minimum headway $h$ (time) between consecutive trains entering the same segment in the same direction; on a rerouted (single-track) segment, trains of opposite directions cannot occupy the segment simultaneously (block occupancy constraint).
- **A6 (Cancellations):** Each train may be cancelled at a penalty $M_f$; cancelled trains consume no resources.
- **A7 (Delays):** Delay is measured against the original scheduled arrival/departure times; a maximum allowable delay $\Delta_{max}$ applies.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $F$ | set of trains, $f \in F$ |
| $E$ | set of segments $(i,j)$ |
| $P_{f,ij}$ | feasible speed profiles of train $f$ on segment $(i,j)$ |
| $B$ | blocked segments during $[t^{start},t^{end}]$ |
| $a^{0}_{fi}, d^{0}_{fi}$ | originally scheduled arrival/departure of train $f$ at station $i$ |
| $r_{f,ijp}, e_{f,ijp}$ | running time / energy of profile $p$ |
| $h$ | minimum headway |
| $T$ | discrete time horizon, $\tau \in T$ |
| $M_f$ | cancellation penalty |
| $\omega^{arr}, \omega^{dep}, \omega^{en}$ | weights for arrival delay, departure delay, energy |

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{fi}, d_{fi} \ge 0$ | continuous | actual arrival/departure time of $f$ at $i$ |
| $x_{f,ijp} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $f$ uses profile $p$ on segment $(i,j)$ |
| $y_{f,ij} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $f$ traverses segment $(i,j)$ |
| $z_{f} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $f$ is cancelled |
| $u_{f,ij} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if $f$ uses the **opposite** (rerouted) track on $(i,j)$ |
| $o_{f,ij,\tau} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $f$ occupies segment $(i,j)$ (in its chosen direction) during time unit $\tau$ |
| $w^{arr}_{fi}, w^{dep}_{fi} \ge 0$ | continuous | arrival/departure delay |

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{f\in F}\sum_{i\in S}\left(\omega^{arr} w^{arr}_{fi} + \omega^{dep} w^{dep}_{fi}\right) + \omega^{en}\sum_{f\in F}\sum_{(i,j)\in E}\sum_{p\in P_{f,ij}} e_{f,ijp}\, x_{f,ijp} + \sum_{f\in F} M_f z_f
$$

## 5. Constraints

**Delay definition:**
$$
w^{arr}_{fi} \ge a_{fi} - a^{0}_{fi}, \qquad w^{dep}_{fi} \ge d_{fi} - d^{0}_{fi} \qquad \forall f, i \tag{1}
$$
$$
w^{arr}_{fi}, w^{dep}_{fi} \le \Delta_{max}(1-z_f) \qquad \forall f,i \tag{2}
$$

**Timetable consistency (running and dwell times):**
$$
d_{fi} + \sum_{p\in P_{f,ij}} r_{f,ijp}\, x_{f,ijp} \le a_{fj} \qquad \forall f,\ (i,j)\in E \tag{3}
$$
$$
a_{fi} + \underline{d}_{fi} \le d_{fi} \le a_{fi} + \bar{d}_{fi} \qquad \forall f, i \tag{4}
$$

**Profile selection (exactly one profile per traversed segment):**
$$
\sum_{p\in P_{f,ij}} x_{f,ijp} = y_{f,ij} \qquad \forall f,\ (i,j)\in E \tag{5}
$$

**Rerouting logic:** a train may use the opposite track only on blocked segments and only during the disruption window; if rerouted, it must arrive at the segment entry after $t^{start}$ (or wait):
$$
u_{f,ij} \le y_{f,ij}\cdot \mathbb{1}[(i,j)\in B] \qquad \forall f,\ (i,j)\in E \tag{6}
$$
$$
d_{fi} \ge t^{start}\, u_{f,ij} \qquad \forall f,\ (i,j)=(i,i{+}1)\in B \tag{7}
$$

**Segment occupancy timing (linearized):** train $f$ occupies $(i,j)$ during time unit $\tau$ only if it departs $i$ at or before $\tau$ and arrives at $j$ after $\tau$:
$$
o_{f,ij,\tau} \ge y_{f,ij} + \frac{d_{fi}-\tau}{T^{max}} \quad\text{and}\quad o_{f,ij,\tau} \ge y_{f,ij} + \frac{\tau - a_{fj}}{T^{max}} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad o_{f,ij,\tau}=1 \text{ iff } d_{fi}\le\tau < a_{fj} \tag{8}
$$
implemented with standard big-$M$ linearization ($M$ = horizon length $T^{max}$).

**Headway (same direction, same track):** for trains $f,g$ on segment $(i,j)$ with $f$ preceding $g$ (order variable $v_{fg,ij}\in\{0,1\}$, 1 if $f$ enters first):
$$
d_{gi} \ge d_{fi} + h - T^{max}(1 - v_{fg,ij}) - T^{max}(1-y_{f,ij}) - T^{max}(1-y_{g,ij}) - T^{max}(u_{f,ij}\oplus u_{g,ij}) \tag{9}
$$
$$
d_{fi} \ge d_{gi} + h - T^{max}\, v_{fg,ij} - T^{max}(1-y_{f,ij}) - T^{max}(1-y_{g,ij}) - T^{max}(u_{f,ij}\oplus u_{g,ij}) \tag{10}
$$
(the $\oplus$ term is linearized with two auxiliary binaries, ensuring headways apply only when both trains use the **same** physical track).

**Single-track conflict (rerouted segments):** opposite-direction trains on the same physical segment may never overlap in time:
$$
o_{f,ij,\tau} + o_{g,ij,\tau} \le 1 \qquad \forall f<g,\ \tau\in T,\ (i,j)\in B,\ \text{with } u_{f,ij}\neq u_{g,ij} \tag{11}
$$

**Disruption window closure:** a train whose own track is blocked cannot occupy the segment during $[t^{start},t^{end}]$ unless rerouted:
$$
o_{f,ij,\tau} \le u_{f,ij} + (1 - \mathbb{1}[\tau \in [t^{start},t^{end}]]\cdot \mathbb{1}[(i,j)\in B]) \qquad \forall f,\tau \tag{12}
$$

**Cancellation:** a cancelled train traverses no segment:
$$
y_{f,ij} \le 1 - z_f \qquad \forall f,\ (i,j)\in E \tag{13}
$$

**Variable domains:**
$$
a_{fi}, d_{fi}, w^{arr}_{fi}, w^{dep}_{fi} \ge 0;\quad x,y,z,u,o,v \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 6. Remarks

- Constraint (3) couples **timetable and speed profiles**: the chosen profile's running time determines feasible arrival times — the core of the TRP–TSMP integration.
- Constraints (9)–(11) jointly guarantee conflict-free operation under bidirectional sharing of rerouted segments.
- The model is a standard MILP; the referenced paper decomposes it into a train-plan selection IP plus per-train speed profile subproblems, with an adaptive plan-refinement and local-branching algorithm — the MILP above serves as the exact reference formulation.
