Text:
# MILP Model for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Below is a complete, linearized MILP formulation for the integrated train rescheduling and speed management problem under partial segment blockages. All nonlinear terms (products, $v^2$, $v^3$, $1/v$) are replaced by auxiliary variables with McCormick envelopes and/or Special Ordered Set (SOS2) piecewise-linear approximations, so the final model is a pure MILP.

---

## 1. Sets

| Set | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$, ordered along the line |
| $B$ | Set of track blocks, indexed by $b$; block $b$ lies between stations $s(b)$ and $s(b)+1$ |
| $K$ | Set of discrete time periods, $K=\{1,\dots,|K|\}$, each of duration $\Delta$ |
| $D=\{U,D\}$ | Directions (Up, Down) |
| $\text{path}(t)\subseteq B$ | Ordered set of blocks traversed by train $t$ |
| $B^D\subseteq B$ | Disrupted blocks |
| $K^D\subseteq K$ | Disruption time periods |
| $I=\{1,\dots,N\}$ | Piecewise-linear breakpoints for speed |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Parameter | Description | Unit |
|-----------|-------------|-----|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ | m |
| $\Delta$ | Duration of one time period | s |
| $v_{\max}, v_{\min}$ | Maximum / minimum allowable speed | m/s |
| $a_{\text{acc}}, a_{\text{dec}}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration (positive values) | m/s² |
| $\tau_h$ | Minimum headway between consecutive trains | s |
| $\tau_{d,\min}, \tau_{d,\max}$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time at stations | s |
| $\pi^a_{t,s}, \pi^d_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure time of train $t$ at station $s$ | s |
| $\text{dir}(t)\in\{U,D\}$ | Direction of train $t$ | – |
| $m_t$ | Mass of train $t$ | kg |
| $c_0, c_1, c_2$ | Davis resistance coefficients ($R(v)=c_0+c_1v+c_2v^2$) | – |
| $\eta_{\text{reg}}$ | Regenerative braking efficiency | – |
| $\theta_b$ | Gradient of block $b$ | rad |
| $g$ | Gravitational acceleration (9.81) | m/s² |
| $\alpha_{\text{delay}}, \beta_{\text{energy}}$ | Objective weights for delay and energy | – |
| $P_{\text{cancel}}$ | Cancellation penalty | – |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large big-M constant | – |
| $\rho_{b,k}\in\{0,1\}$ | 1 if block $b$ is disrupted at time $k$ (i.e., $b\in B^D$ and $k\in K^D$) | – |
| $K_{\text{end}}=|K|\cdot\Delta$ | End of the time horizon | s |
| $T_{\max}=L_b/v_{\min}$ | Maximum traversal time of block $b$ | s |
| $v_i$ | $i$-th speed breakpoint, $v_1=v_{\min}, v_N=v_{\max}$ | m/s |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### Primary (physical) variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $x_{t,b,k}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ occupies block $b$ at time $k$ on its **normal** track |
| $y_{t,b,k}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ occupies block $b$ at time $k$ on the **rerouted (opposite)** track |
| $o_{t,b,k}=x_{t,b,k}+y_{t,b,k}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ is present in block $b$ at time $k$ |
| $z_t$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled |
| $a_{t,s}\ge 0$ | continuous | Actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{t,s}\ge 0$ | continuous | Actual departure time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $\delta_{t,s}\ge 0$ | continuous | Delay of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $v_{t,b,k}\ge 0$ | continuous | Speed of train $t$ in block $b$ at time $k$ |
| $a_{t,b,k}$ | continuous | Acceleration of train $t$ in block $b$ at time $k$ (may be negative) |
| $a^{+}_{t,b,k}, a^{-}_{t,b,k}\ge 0$ | continuous | Positive / negative parts of acceleration ($a=a^+-a^-$) |
| $\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,b}, \tau^{\text{out}}_{t,b}\ge 0$ | continuous | Entry / exit times of train $t$ to/from block $b$ |
| $f_{t,b,k}, \ell_{t,b,k}$ | binary | 1 if $k$ is the **first** / **last** occupied period of train $t$ in block $b$ |
| $w_{t,t',b}$ | binary | Ordering indicator for headway (1 if $t$ enters block $b$ after $t'$) |
| $e^{\text{trac}}_{t,b,k}, e^{\text{reg}}_{t,b,k}\ge 0$ | continuous | Tractive / regenerative-braking energy of train $t$ in block $b$ at time $k$ [kWh] |

### Auxiliary variables for linearization

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $w^2_{t,b,k}\ge 0$ | Piecewise-linear approximation of $v_{t,b,k}^2$ |
| $p_{t,b,k}\ge 0$ | McCormick envelope of $a^+_{t,b,k}\cdot v_{t,b,k}$ |
| $r_{t,b,k}\ge 0$ | McCormick envelope of $a^-_{t,b,k}\cdot v_{t,b,k}$ |
| $q_{t,b,k}\ge 0$ | McCormick envelope of $w^2_{t,b,k}\cdot v_{t,b,k}$ (≈ $v^3$) |
| $u_{t,b,k}\ge 0$ | McCormick envelope of $v_{t,b,k}\cdot(\tau^{\text{out}}_{t,b}-\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,b})$ |
| $\lambda_{t,b,k,i}\ge 0$ | SOS2 weight for breakpoint $i$ of $v$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\; Z \;=\; \alpha_{\text{delay}}\!\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\delta_{t,s}
\;+\; \beta_{\text{energy}}\!\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{b\in B}\sum_{k\in K}\!\left(e^{\text{trac}}_{t,b,k}-\eta_{\text{reg}}\,e^{\text{reg}}_{t,b,k}\right)
\;+\; P_{\text{cancel}}\!\sum_{t\in T} z_t
$$

The three terms represent: (i) total passenger delay, (ii) net electrical energy consumed (traction minus recovered braking), and (iii) cancellation penalty.

---

## 5. Constraints

### (A) Block Occupancy

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{A1:}\quad x_{t,b,k}+y_{t,b,k}\le 1-z_t &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{A2:}\quad \sum_{t\in T} x_{t,b,k}\le 1 &&\forall b,k \\
&\text{A3:}\quad \sum_{t\in T} y_{t,b,k}\le 1 &&\forall b,k
\end{aligned}
$$

A1 forbids cancelled trains from occupying any block; A2/A3 enforce that at most one train uses a block per time on each track.

### (B) Bidirectional Conflict Resolution

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{B1a:}\quad \sum_{t:\,\text{dir}(t)=U} x_{t,b,k} \;+\; \sum_{t:\,\text{dir}(t)=D} y_{t,b,k}\;\le\; 1 &&\forall b,k \\
&\text{B1b:}\quad \sum_{t:\,\text{dir}(t)=D} x_{t,b,k} \;+\; \sum_{t:\,\text{dir}(t)=U} y_{t,b,k}\;\le\; 1 &&\forall b,k
\end{aligned}
$$

B1a protects the **up-track** (normal up-trains + rerouted down-trains); B1b protects the **down-track**.

### (C) Rerouting Eligibility

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{C1:}\quad y_{t,b,k}\le \rho_{b,k} &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{C2:}\quad y_{t,b,k}\le M(1-z_t) &&\forall t,b,k
\end{aligned}
$$

A train may be rerouted **only** on a disrupted block during the disruption window, and only if it is not cancelled.

### (D) Train Movement (Space-Time Flow Conservation)

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{D1:}\quad \sum_{k'\le k}\!\big(x_{t,b+1,k'}+y_{t,b+1,k'}\big)\;\le\;\sum_{k'\le k}\!\big(x_{t,b,k'}+y_{t,b,k'}\big)+(1-z_t) &&\forall t,\;b,b+1\in\text{path}(t),\;k \\
&\text{D2:}\quad \sum_{k\in K}\!\big(x_{t,b,k}+y_{t,b,k}\big)\;=\;1-z_t &&\forall t,\;b\in\text{path}(t) \\
&\text{D3:}\quad x_{t,b,k}+y_{t,b,k}\;\le\;\mathbf{1}_{[b\in\text{path}(t)]} &&\forall t,b,k
\end{aligned}
$$

D1 prevents the train from "skipping" forward in space; D2 forces each block on the path to be traversed exactly once (if not cancelled); D3 forbids occupancy of blocks outside the train's path.

### (E) Speed Dynamics

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{E1:}\quad v_{t,b,k+1}-v_{t,b,k}-\Delta\cdot a_{t,b,k}=0 &&\forall t,b,k<|K| \\
&\text{E2:}\quad v_{\min}\le v_{t,b,k}\le v_{\max} &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{E3:}\quad -a_{\text{dec}}\le a_{t,b,k}\le a_{\text{acc}} &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{E4:}\quad a_{t,b,k}=a^{+}_{t,b,k}-a^{-}_{t,b,k},\quad a^{+}_{t,b,k},a^{-}_{t,b,k}\ge 0 &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{E5:}\quad v_{t,b,k}\le v_{\max}\,(x_{t,b,k}+y_{t,b,k}) &&\forall t,b,k
\end{aligned}
$$

E1 is the discretized kinematic equation; E5 forces $v=0$ when the train is not in the block.

### (F) Block Traversal Time

**Linking entry/exit times to occupancy** (using first/last indicators):

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{F1:}\quad f_{t,b,k}\le x_{t,b,k}+y_{t,b,k} &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{F2:}\quad f_{t,b,k}\le 1-(x_{t,b,k-1}+y_{t,b,k-1})\quad (k>1) &&\forall t,b \\
&\text{F3:}\quad \sum_{k} f_{t,b,k}=1-z_t &&\forall t,b\in\text{path}(t) \\
&\text{F4:}\quad \ell_{t,b,k}\le x_{t,b,k}+y_{t,b,k} &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{F5:}\quad \ell_{t,b,k}\le 1-(x_{t,b,k+1}+y_{t,b,k+1})\quad (k<|K|) &&\forall t,b \\
&\text{F6:}\quad \sum_{k} \ell_{t,b,k}=1-z_t &&\forall t,b\in\text{path}(t) \\
&\text{F7:}\quad \tau^{\text{in}}_{t,b}=\sum_{k} k\Delta\, f_{t,b,k},\quad \tau^{\text{out}}_{t,b}=\sum_{k} k\Delta\, \ell_{t,b,k} &&\forall t,b
\end{aligned}
$$

**Traversal-time constraint** (linearized via McCormick on $v\cdot(\tau^{\text{out}}-\tau^{\text{in}})$):

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{F8:}\quad u_{t,b,k}\;\ge\; L_b\,(x_{t,b,k}+y_{t,b,k}) &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{F9:}\quad u_{t,b,k}\;\ge\; v_{\min}(\tau^{\text{out}}_{t,b}-\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,b}) &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{F10:}\quad u_{t,b,k}\;\ge\; v_{\max}(\tau^{\text{out}}_{t,b}-\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,b})+T_{\max}\,v_{t,b,k}-v_{\max}T_{\max} &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{F11:}\quad u_{t,b,k}\;\le\; v_{\max}(\tau^{\text{out}}_{t,b}-\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,b}) &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{F12:}\quad u_{t,b,k}\;\le\; v_{\min}(\tau^{\text{out}}_{t,b}-\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,b})+T_{\max}\,v_{t,b,k}-v_{\min}T_{\max} &&\forall t,b,k
\end{aligned}
$$

F8 is the physical requirement $v\cdot\Delta t\ge L_b$; F9–F12 are the McCormick envelopes that relax the bilinear product.

### (G) Station Timing

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{G1:}\quad a_{t,s}=\tau^{\text{out}}_{t,b(s-1)} &&\forall t,\;s>s_{\text{origin}}(t) \\
&\text{G2:}\quad d_{t,s}=\tau^{\text{in}}_{t,b(s)} &&\forall t,\;s<s_{\text{dest}}(t) \\
&\text{G3:}\quad \tau_{d,\min}(1-z_t)\le d_{t,s}-a_{t,s}\le \tau_{d,\max}(1-z_t) &&\forall t,s \\
&\text{G4:}\quad \delta_{t,s}\ge a_{t,s}-\pi^a_{t,s},\quad \delta_{t,s}\ge 0 &&\forall t,s
\end{aligned}
$$

G1/G2 tie station times to block exit/entry; G3 enforces dwell-time bounds; G4 defines delay.

### (H) Headway Constraints

For every pair of trains $(t,t')$ with $\text{dir}(t)=\text{dir}(t')$ and overlapping paths on block $b$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{H1:}\quad \tau^{\text{in}}_{t,b}-\tau^{\text{out}}_{t',b}\;\ge\;\tau_h-M(1-w_{t,t',b}) &&\forall t,t',b \\
&\text{H2:}\quad \tau^{\text{in}}_{t',b}-\tau^{\text{out}}_{t,b}\;\ge\;\tau_h-M\,w_{t,t',b} &&\forall t,t',b \\
&\text{H3:}\quad w_{t,t',b}\le \sum_k(x_{t,b,k}+y_{t,b,k}),\quad w_{t,t',b}\le \sum_k(x_{t',b,k}+y_{t',b,k}) &&\forall t,t',b
\end{aligned}
$$

H1/H2 enforce a minimum $\tau_h$ separation regardless of order; H3 activates the constraint only when both trains actually traverse the block.

### (I) Energy Consumption

**SOS2 piecewise-linear approximation of $v^2$** with breakpoints $v_{\min}=v_1<v_2<\dots<v_N=v_{\max}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{I1:}\quad \sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_{t,b,k,i}=1,\quad \lambda_{t,b,k,i}\ge 0,\quad \text{SOS2} &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{I2:}\quad v_{t,b,k}=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_{t,b,k,i}\,v_i &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{I3:}\quad w^2_{t,b,k}=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_{t,b,k,i}\,v_i^{2} &&\forall t,b,k
\end{aligned}
$$

**McCormick envelopes for bilinear terms** ($a^+\!\cdot v$, $a^-\!\cdot v$, $w^2\!\cdot v$):

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{I4:}\quad p_{t,b,k}\ge v_{\min}\,a^{+}_{t,b,k} &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{I5:}\quad p_{t,b,k}\ge a_{\text{acc}}\,v_{t,b,k}+v_{\max}\,a^{+}_{t,b,k}-a_{\text{acc}}v_{\max} &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{I6:}\quad p_{t,b,k}\le v_{\max}\,a^{+}_{t,b,k} &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{I7:}\quad p_{t,b,k}\le a_{\text{acc}}\,v_{t,b,k}+v_{\min}\,a^{+}_{t,b,k}-a_{\text{acc}}v_{\min} &&\forall t,b,k \\[4pt]
&\text{I8:}\quad r_{t,b,k}\ge v_{\min}\,a^{-}_{t,b,k} &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{I9:}\quad r_{t,b,k}\ge a_{\text{dec}}\,v_{t,b,k}+v_{\max}\,a^{-}_{t,b,k}-a_{\text{dec}}v_{\max} &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{I10:}\quad r_{t,b,k}\le v_{\max}\,a^{-}_{t,b,k} &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{I11:}\quad r_{t,b,k}\le a_{\text{dec}}\,v_{t,b,k}+v_{\min}\,a^{-}_{t,b,k}-a_{\text{dec}}v_{\min} &&\forall t,b,k \\[4pt]
&\text{I12:}\quad q_{t,b,k}\ge v_{\min}\,w^2_{t,b,k} &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{I13:}\quad q_{t,b,k}\ge v_{\max}\,w^2_{t,b,k}+v_{\max}^2\,v_{t,b,k}-v_{\max}^3 &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{I14:}\quad q_{t,b,k}\le v_{\max}\,w^2_{t,b,k} &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{I15:}\quad q_{t,b,k}\le v_{\min}\,w^2_{t,b,k}+v_{\max}^2\,v_{t,b,k}-v_{\min}v_{\max}^2 &&\forall t,b,k
\end{aligned}
$$

**Tractive and regenerative energy** (with constant $C_E = \Delta / 3.6\times 10^6$ converting W·s to kWh):

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{I16:}\quad e^{\text{trac}}_{t,b,k}\;\ge\; C_E\!\left(m_t\,p_{t,b,k} + m_t\,g\sin\theta_b\,v_{t,b,k} + c_0\,v_{t,b,k} + c_1\,w^2_{t,b,k} + c_2\,q_{t,b,k}\right) &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{I17:}\quad e^{\text{reg}}_{t,b,k}\;\ge\; C_E\,m_t\,r_{t,b,k} &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{I18:}\quad e^{\text{trac}}_{t,b,k}\;\le\; M\,(x_{t,b,k}+y_{t,b,k}) &&\forall t,b,k \\
&\text{I19:}\quad e^{\text{reg}}_{t,b,k}\;\le\; M\,(x_{t,b,k}+y_{t,b,k}) &&\forall t,b,k
\end{aligned}
$$

I16/I17 define tractive and regenerative energy from the mechanical power; I18/I19 force zero energy when the train is not in the block.

### (J) Cancellation

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{J1:}\quad \sum_{b\in B}\sum_{k\in K}(x_{t,b,k}+y_{t,b,k})=0 &&\text{if } z_t=1 \\
&\text{J2:}\quad z_t\in\{0,1\} &&\forall t
\end{aligned}
$$

(J1 is enforced implicitly by A1 + D2: if $z_t=1$, then $x_{t,b,k}+y_{t,b,k}\le 0$ for all $b,k$.)

### (K) Initial and Terminal Conditions

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{K1:}\quad d_{t,s_{\text{origin}}(t)}\;\ge\;\pi^d_{t,s_{\text{origin}}(t)} &&\forall t \\
&\text{K2:}\quad a_{t,s_{\text{dest}}(t)}\;\le\;K_{\text{end}} &&\forall t \\
&\text{K3:}\quad v_{t,b,1}=v_{\text{init},t},\quad v_{t,b,|K|}=v_{\text{final},t} &&\forall t,b
\end{aligned}
$$

K1 ensures the train does not depart earlier than scheduled; K2 ensures arrival within the planning horizon; K3 fixes boundary speeds.

---

## 6. Model Summary

| Component | Type | Count (approx.) |
|-----------|------|-----------------|
| Binary variables | $x,y,z,f,\ell,w$ | $O(|T||B||K|)$ |
| Continuous variables | $a,d,v,a^\pm,\tau,e,\lambda,p,r,q,u,w^2$ | $O(|T||B||K|)$ |
| Constraints | A–K | $O(|T||B||K|)$ |

The model is a **pure MILP** because:
- All products of continuous variables are replaced by auxiliary variables with McCormick envelopes (F8–F12, I4–I15).
- All $v^2$ and $v^3$ terms are approximated by SOS2 piecewise-linear functions (I1–I3) and McCormick relaxations (I12–I15).
- All logical conditions (rerouting eligibility, cancellation, headway ordering) are encoded with big-M or indicator constraints.

---

## 7. Key Assumptions

1. **Single double-track line** with bidirectional traffic; rerouting uses the opposite track only on disrupted blocks during the disruption window.
2. **Discrete time–space representation** with uniform interval $\Delta$; finer $\Delta$ improves accuracy at the cost of more variables.
3. **Davis resistance equation** $R(v)=c_0+c_1v+c_2v^2$ captures aerodynamic and rolling resistance.
4. **Regenerative braking** recovers a fraction $\eta_{\text{reg}}$ of kinetic energy dissipated during deceleration.
5. **Cancellation** is a last-resort option with a large penalty $P_{\text{cancel}}$.
6. **Headway** is enforced block-by-block; station dwell times are bounded.
7. **Speed profiles** are constrained by $v_{\min}, v_{\max}, a_{\text{acc}}, a_{\text{dec}}$ and must be physically realizable (E1, F8).
8. **Objective weights** $\alpha_{\text{delay}}, \beta_{\text{energy}}$ allow the operator to trade off punctuality against energy efficiency.

---

## 8. Outputs

Solving the MILP yields:
- **Rescheduled timetable**: arrival/departure times $a_{t,s}, d_{t,s}$ at every station.
- **Rerouting decisions**: $y_{t,b,k}=1$ indicates a train uses the opposite track on block $b$ at time $k$.
- **Cancellation decisions**: $z_t=1$ marks cancelled trains.
- **Speed profiles**: $v_{t,b,k}$ and $a_{t,b,k}$ for every train, block, and time period.
- **Performance metrics**: total delay $\sum\delta_{t,s}$, net energy $\sum(e^{\text{trac}}-\eta_{\text{reg}}e^{\text{reg}})$, and number of cancellations.

This MILP simultaneously optimizes retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and energy-efficient speed control under partial segment blockages, providing a conflict-free and physically executable rescheduling plan.

Text:
# Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — Complete MILP Formulation

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $I$ | Set of trains, $i \in I$ |
| $J$ | Set of stations, $j \in J$ ($j=1$ origin, $j=|J|$ terminal) |
| $B$ | Set of block sections, $b \in B$ |
| $K$ | Set of discrete time steps, $k \in K$ |
| $D \subseteq B$ | Set of disrupted blocks |
| $T_d \subseteq K$ | Set of time steps during the disruption window |
| $\text{dir}_i \in \{+1,-1\}$ | Travel direction of train $i$ |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $\Delta t$ | Duration of each time step | s |
| $L_b$ | Length of block section $b$ | m |
| $V_{\max}$ | Maximum allowed speed | m/s |
| $A_{\max}$ | Maximum traction acceleration | m/s² |
| $B_{\max}$ | Maximum braking deceleration | m/s² |
| $M_i$ | Mass of train $i$ | t |
| $c_0, c_1, c_2$ | Davis rolling-resistance coefficients | – |
| $\eta_{reg}$ | Regenerative-braking efficiency | – |
| $t^{arr,sched}_{i,j}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $j$ | s |
| $t^{dep,sched}_{i,j}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ at station $j$ | s |
| $\tau_{\min}, \tau_{\max}$ | Min / max dwell time at stations | s |
| $t^{start}_d, t^{end}_d$ | Disruption start / end times | s |
| $W_{delay}, W_{energy}, E_{cancel}$ | Objective weights / cancellation penalty | – |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (Big-M) | – |
| $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3$ | Linearized energy coefficients | – |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous variables**
- $a_{i,j} \ge 0$ — actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $j$
- $d_{i,j} \ge 0$ — actual departure time of train $i$ at station $j$
- $\delta_{i,j} \ge 0$ — arrival delay of train $i$ at station $j$
- $v_{i,b,k} \ge 0$ — speed of train $i$ in block $b$ at time $k$
- $u_{i,b,k}$ — acceleration of train $i$ in block $b$ at time $k$
- $u^{+}_{i,b,k} \ge 0$ — positive part of acceleration (traction)
- $u^{-}_{i,b,k} \ge 0$ — negative part of acceleration (braking)
- $p_{i,b,k} \ge 0$ — position of train $i$ in block $b$ at time $k$
- $e_{i,b,k} \ge 0$ — energy consumption of train $i$ in block $b$ at time $k$

**Binary variables**
- $x_{i,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ occupies block $b$ at time $k$
- $y_{i,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ uses the opposite (rerouting) track in block $b$ at time $k$
- $z_{i,i',b} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ exits block $b$ before train $i'$ enters
- $c_i \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ is cancelled
- $s_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ traverses block $b$

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; W_{delay}\sum_{i \in I}\sum_{j \in J}\delta_{i,j} \;+\; W_{energy}\sum_{i \in I}\sum_{b \in B}\sum_{k \in K} e_{i,b,k}\,\Delta t \;+\; E_{cancel}\sum_{i \in I} c_i
$$

The objective balances (i) total passenger delay, (ii) total tractive energy consumption, and (iii) service cancellations.

## 5. Constraints

### (1) Delay definition
$$
a_{i,j} - t^{arr,sched}_{i,j} \;\le\; \delta_{i,j} + M(1-c_i) \quad \forall i,j
$$
$$
a_{i,j} - t^{arr,sched}_{i,j} \;\ge\; -M(1-c_i) \quad \forall i,j
$$

### (2) Dwell-time bounds at stations
$$
\tau_{\min}(1-c_i) \;\le\; d_{i,j} - a_{i,j} \;\le\; \tau_{\max}(1-c_i) \quad \forall i,j
$$

### (3) Running-time link between consecutive stations
For each train $i$ and consecutive stations $j, j+1$ along its travel direction, with $P(i,j)$ the set of blocks on the path:
$$
a_{i,j+1} - d_{i,j} \;\ge\; \Delta t \sum_{b \in P(i,j)}\sum_{k \in K} x_{i,b,k} - M\,c_i \quad \forall i, j \ne |J|
$$
$$
a_{i,j+1} - d_{i,j} \;\le\; \Delta t \sum_{b \in P(i,j)}\sum_{k \in K} x_{i,b,k} + M\,c_i \quad \forall i, j \ne |J|
$$

### (4) Block-section capacity (headway)
$$
\sum_{i \in I} x_{i,b,k} \;\le\; 1 \quad \forall b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

### (5) Train-dynamics: speed update (Big-M linearization)
$$
v_{i,b,k+1} - v_{i,b,k} - u_{i,b,k}\Delta t \;\le\; M\bigl(2 - x_{i,b,k} - x_{i,b,k+1}\bigr) \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
$$
v_{i,b,k+1} - v_{i,b,k} - u_{i,b,k}\Delta t \;\ge\; -M\bigl(2 - x_{i,b,k} - x_{i,b,k+1}\bigr) \quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### (6) Train-dynamics: position update
$$
p_{i,b,k+1} - p_{i,b,k} - v_{i,b,k}\Delta t - \tfrac{1}{2}u_{i,b,k}\Delta t^{2} \;\le\; M\bigl(2 - x_{i,b,k} - x_{i,b,k+1}\bigr) \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
$$
p_{i,b,k+1} - p_{i,b,k} - v_{i,b,k}\Delta t - \tfrac{1}{2}u_{i,b,k}\Delta t^{2} \;\ge\; -M\bigl(2 - x_{i,b,k} - x_{i,b,k+1}\bigr) \quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### (7) Speed limits
$$
0 \;\le\; v_{i,b,k} \;\le\; V_{\max}\,x_{i,b,k} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### (8) Acceleration limits and decomposition
$$
u_{i,b,k} \;\le\; A_{\max}\,x_{i,b,k} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
$$
u_{i,b,k} \;\ge\; -B_{\max}\,x_{i,b,k} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
$$
u_{i,b,k} \;=\; u^{+}_{i,b,k} - u^{-}_{i,b,k} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
$$
0 \;\le\; u^{+}_{i,b,k} \;\le\; A_{\max}\,x_{i,b,k} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
$$
0 \;\le\; u^{-}_{i,b,k} \;\le\; B_{\max}\,x_{i,b,k} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### (9) Position bounds inside a block
$$
0 \;\le\; p_{i,b,k} \;\le\; L_b\,x_{i,b,k} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$

### (10) Continuity of speed and position between consecutive blocks
For each train $i$ and consecutive blocks $(b^{in}, b^{out})$ along its path:
$$
\sum_{k \in K} k\,x_{i,b^{in},k} \;\le\; \sum_{k \in K} k\,x_{i,b^{out},k} + M(1-s_{i,b^{in}}) \quad \forall i
$$
$$
v_{i,b^{in},K^{max}} - v_{i,b^{out},0} \;\le\; M\bigl(2 - s_{i,b^{in}} - s_{i,b^{out}}\bigr) \quad \forall i
$$
$$
v_{i,b^{in},K^{max}} - v_{i,b^{out},0} \;\ge\; -M\bigl(2 - s_{i,b^{in}} - s_{i,b^{out}}\bigr) \quad \forall i
$$

### (11) Ordering of conflicting trains within a block
$$
z_{i,i',b} + z_{i',i,b} \;\le\; 1 \quad \forall i \ne i',\; b
$$
$$
\sum_{k} k\,x_{i,b,k} - \sum_{k} k\,x_{i',b,k} \;\le\; M(1-z_{i,i',b}) + M(2-s_{i,b}-s_{i',b}) \quad \forall i \ne i', b
$$
$$
\sum_{k} k\,x_{i',b,k} - \sum_{k} k\,x_{i,b,k} \;\le\; M(1-z_{i',i,b}) + M(2-s_{i,b}-s_{i',b}) \quad \forall i \ne i', b
$$
$$
z_{i,i',b} + z_{i',i,b} \;\ge\; s_{i,b} + s_{i',b} - 1 \quad \forall i \ne i', b
$$

### (12) Disruption: blocked track unusable
$$
x_{i,b,k} \;=\; 0 \quad \forall b \in D,\; k \in T_d,\; i : \text{dir}_i \text{ matches blocked direction}
$$

### (13) Rerouting feasibility
$$
y_{i,b,k} \;\le\; x_{i,b,k} \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
$$
y_{i,b,k} \;=\; 0 \quad \forall b \notin D \text{ or } k \notin T_d
$$

### (14) Bidirectional conflict on the shared opposite track
For every pair $(i,i')$ with $\text{dir}_i \ne \text{dir}_{i'}$:
$$
x_{i,b,k} + x_{i',b,k} \;\le\; 1 + M(1-y_{i,b,k}) + M(1-y_{i',b,k}) \quad \forall b \in D,\; k \in T_d
$$

### (15) Linearized energy consumption
$$
e_{i,b,k} \;\ge\; \alpha_1\,v_{i,b,k} + \alpha_2\,u^{+}_{i,b,k} - \alpha_3\,u^{-}_{i,b,k} - M(1-x_{i,b,k}) \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
with $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3$ derived from a piecewise-linear approximation of the Davis equation $F = M_i(c_0 + c_1 v + c_2 v^{2})$ plus the mechanical power $F \cdot v$, and a regenerative-braking credit $\eta_{reg} M_i u^{-} v$.

### (16) Cancellation
$$
x_{i,b,k} \;\le\; 1 - c_i \quad \forall i,b,k
$$
$$
\delta_{i,j} \;\le\; M(1-c_i) \quad \forall i,j
$$

### (17) Path consistency
$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{i,b,k} \;\ge\; s_{i,b} \quad \forall i,b
$$
$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{i,b,k} \;\le\; |K|\,s_{i,b} \quad \forall i,b
$$
$$
s_{i,b} \;\le\; 1 - c_i \quad \forall i,b
$$

## 6. Modelling Assumptions

1. **Time discretization**: The planning horizon is discretized into uniform intervals $\Delta t$; all events (arrivals, departures, block entries/exits) are aligned with the grid.
2. **Homogeneous rolling stock**: All trains share the same technical parameters ($V_{\max}, A_{\max}, B_{\max}, M_i, c_0, c_1, c_2, \eta_{reg}$) except for their mass $M_i$ and schedule.
3. **Single contiguous disruption**: Exactly one block section is blocked for a single contiguous time window $[t^{start}_d, t^{end}_d]$; the opposite track remains physically intact.
4. **Rerouting only on the opposite track**: During the disruption, affected trains may divert to the opposite track within $D$ and $T_d$; no alternative routes exist outside this window.
5. **No overtaking inside a block**: Within any block section, at most one train may be present at a time, including on the rerouted (opposite) track.
6. **Bidirectional conflict on shared track**: When trains of opposite directions both reroute onto the same track within the disruption window, they must be sequenced in time (constraint 14).
7. **Dwell-time flexibility**: Dwell times at intermediate stations may vary within $[\tau_{\min}, \tau_{\max}]$ to absorb small delays.
8. **Constant speed and acceleration limits**: Limits are independent of position, gradient, and train loading.
9. **Piecewise-linear energy model**: The cubic Davis resistance term and the bilinear traction-power term are approximated by linear envelopes to keep the formulation a MILP.
10. **Cancellation as last resort**: Cancelling a train is permitted but incurs a large penalty $E_{cancel}$, reflecting the strong operational preference for keeping service running.
11. **Full-line traversal**: A non-cancelled train traverses every block on the line between its origin and terminal stations (constraint 17 with $s_{i,b}=1-c_i$).
12. **Big-M linearization**: All disjunctive / conditional relationships (occupancy ↔ dynamics, ordering, rerouting, cancellation) are encoded with a sufficiently large constant $M$.

This MILP jointly decides **arrival/departure times**, **block occupancies**, **rerouting choices**, **train orderings**, **speed profiles**, and **cancellations**, while guaranteeing that every produced timetable is conflict-free and every speed profile is dynamically feasible.

Read the text below and fill in the predefined form.

- ContainsFormulation: true only if the text writes out at least one objective function or constraint as a mathematical expression. False if the text only describes or outlines a model in words, discusses an approach, asks a question, or contains no model.
- variablesInModel: every decision variable that appears in the written expressions, numbered from 1. Parameters, sets and indices are not decision variables. An indexed family such as x_{ij} counts once. Domain: binary, integer or continuous as the text declares it, unknown if it does not say.
- objective_functions: every objective function written as an expression, numbered from 0, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. Leave the list empty if no objective function is written out.
- constraints: every constraint written as an equation or inequality, numbered from 1, with the numbers of the decision variables it contains. A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Sets and Indices

- $S = \{1, 2, \ldots, |S|\}$: set of stations
- $T = \{1, 2, \ldots, |T|\}$: set of trains
- $\mathcal{T} = \{0, 1, \ldots, T_{\max}\}$: set of discrete time steps
- $\mathcal{A}$: set of directed segments (arcs) between consecutive stations in both directions
- $\mathcal{A}^+ \subseteq \mathcal{A}$: set of forward segments
- $\mathcal{A}^- \subseteq \mathcal{A}$: set of backward segments
- $s_d \in \mathcal{A}$: disrupted segment
- $[t_d^{\text{start}}, t_d^{\text{end}}]$: disruption time window
- $T^+ = \{i \in T : \text{dir}(i) = +1\}$: forward-direction trains
- $T^- = \{i \in T : \text{dir}(i) = -1\}$: backward-direction trains

## 2. Parameters

- $\Delta t$: time step duration (min)
- $v_{\max}$: maximum operating speed (km/h)
- $a_{\max}, a_{\min}$: maximum acceleration / deceleration (m/s²)
- $d_{\text{safe}}$: minimum safety headway distance (m)
- $\tau_{\min}$: minimum dwell time at stations (min)
- $M$: sufficiently large constant (Big-M)
- $w_1, w_2, w_3, w_4$: weights for delay, energy, cancellation, and deviation
- $\bar{t}_a(i,k), \bar{t}_d(i,k)$: scheduled arrival/departure time of train $i$ at station $k$
- $\rho(s)$: minimum running time on segment $s$
- $\alpha_e, \beta_e$: linearized energy coefficients
- $L_s$: length of segment $s$

## 3. Decision Variables

**Binary variables:**
- $x_{i,s,t} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ occupies segment $s$ at time $t$
- $y_{i,k,t} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ arrives at station $k$ at time $t$
- $z_{i,k,t} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ departs from station $k$ at time $t$
- $r_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ is rerouted on segment $s$
- $c_i \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ is cancelled
- $o_{i,i',s,t} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering indicator (train $i$ ahead of train $i'$ on segment $s$ at time $t$)

**Continuous variables:**
- $a_{i,t}$: acceleration of train $i$ at time $t$
- $v_{i,t}$: speed of train $i$ at time $t$
- $p_{i,t}$: position of train $i$ at time $t$
- $E_{i,t}$: energy consumption of train $i$ at time $t$
- $d_{i,k}$: delay of train $i$ at station $k$
- $T_a(i,k), T_d(i,k)$: actual arrival/departure times

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = w_1 \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{k \in S} d_{i,k} \;+\; w_2 \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} E_{i,t} \;+\; w_3 \sum_{i \in T} c_i \;+\; w_4 \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{k \in S}\bigl[(T_a(i,k)-\bar{t}_a(i,k)) + (T_d(i,k)-\bar{t}_d(i,k))\bigr]
$$

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Flow Conservation (Time–Space Network)

For each train $i \in T$ and intermediate station $k \in S \setminus \{o_i, d_i\}$:
$$
\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} y_{i,k,t} = \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} z_{i,k,t}
$$

For each train $i \in T$, station $k$, and time $t$:
$$
y_{i,k,t} \leq \sum_{\tau=1}^{\rho(s)} x_{i,s,t-\tau}, \quad \forall s \in \mathcal{A} \text{ incoming to } k
$$
$$
z_{i,k,t} \leq \sum_{\tau=1}^{\rho(s)} x_{i,s,t+\tau}, \quad \forall s \in \mathcal{A} \text{ outgoing from } k
$$

### 5.2 Train Dynamics (Kinematic Equations)

For each train $i \in T$ and time $t \in \mathcal{T} \setminus \{T_{\max}\}$:
$$
v_{i,t+1} = v_{i,t} + a_{i,t}\,\Delta t
$$
$$
p_{i,t+1} = p_{i,t} + v_{i,t}\,\Delta t
$$

### 5.3 Speed and Acceleration Limits

$$
0 \leq v_{i,t} \leq v_{\max}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; t \in \mathcal{T}
$$
$$
a_{\min} \leq a_{i,t} \leq a_{\max}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; t \in \mathcal{T}
$$

### 5.4 Safety Headway Between Trains

For each pair $(i,i') \in T \times T$, $i < i'$, segment $s \in \mathcal{A}$, and time $t \in \mathcal{T}$:
$$
p_{i,t} - p_{i',t} \geq d_{\text{safe}} - M(1 - o_{i,i',s,t})
$$
$$
p_{i',t} - p_{i,t} \geq d_{\text{safe}} - M\,o_{i,i',s,t}
$$
$$
o_{i,i',s,t} \leq x_{i,s,t}, \quad o_{i,i',s,t} \leq x_{i',s,t}
$$

### 5.5 Track Capacity During Disruption

For each time $t \in [t_d^{\text{start}}, t_d^{\text{end}}]$:
$$
\sum_{i \in T^+} x_{i,s_d,t} \leq 1
$$
$$
\sum_{i \in T^-} x_{i,s_d,t} \leq 1
$$

### 5.6 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution

For each time $t \in \mathcal{T}$, segment $s \in \mathcal{A}$, and pair $(i,i') \in T^+ \times T^-$:
$$
x_{i,s,t} + x_{i',s,t} \leq 1
$$

### 5.7 Rerouting Constraints

For each train $i \in T$ and segment $s \in \mathcal{A}^+ \setminus \{s_d\}$:
$$
r_{i,s} = 0
$$

For each train $i \in T$, disrupted segment $s_d$, and time $t \notin [t_d^{\text{start}}, t_d^{\text{end}}]$:
$$
x_{i,s_d,t} \leq 1 - r_{i,s_d}
$$

For each train $i \in T$ and time $t \in [t_d^{\text{start}}, t_d^{\text{end}}]$:
$$
x_{i,s_d,t} \geq r_{i,s_d} - M(1 - r_{i,s_d})
$$

### 5.8 Dwell Time Constraints

For each train $i \in T$ and station $k \in S$:
$$
T_d(i,k) - T_a(i,k) \geq \tau_{\min}
$$

### 5.9 Running Time Constraints Between Stations

For each train $i \in T$ and consecutive stations $(k, k+1)$:
$$
T_d(i,k+1) - T_a(i,k) \geq \rho(k,k+1)
$$

### 5.10 Cancellation Constraints

For each train $i \in T$:
$$
\sum_{s \in \mathcal{A}}\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} x_{i,s,t} \leq (1 - c_i)\,|\mathcal{A}|\,|\mathcal{T}|
$$
$$
\sum_{k \in S}\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} y_{i,k,t} \leq (1 - c_i)\,|S|\,|\mathcal{T}|
$$
$$
v_{i,t} \leq v_{\max}(1 - c_i), \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
$$
$$
p_{i,t} \leq M(1 - c_i), \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
$$

### 5.11 Energy Consumption (Linearized)

For each train $i \in T$ and time $t \in \mathcal{T}$:
$$
E_{i,t} \geq \alpha_e\,v_{i,t} + \beta_e\,a_{i,t}
$$
$$
E_{i,t} \geq 0
$$

### 5.12 Delay Definition

For each train $i \in T$ and station $k \in S$:
$$
d_{i,k} \geq T_a(i,k) - \bar{t}_a(i,k)
$$
$$
d_{i,k} \geq T_d(i,k) - \bar{t}_d(i,k)
$$

### 5.13 Linking Actual Times to Discrete Events

For each train $i \in T$ and station $k \in S$:
$$
T_a(i,k) = \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} t\,y_{i,k,t}
$$
$$
T_d(i,k) = \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} t\,z_{i,k,t}
$$

### 5.14 Single Occupancy per Train per Time

For each train $i \in T$ and time $t \in \mathcal{T}$:
$$
\sum_{s \in \mathcal{A}} x_{i,s,t} + \sum_{k \in S}(y_{i,k,t} + z_{i,k,t}) \leq 1
$$

## 6. Assumptions

1. **Discrete time representation**: Time is discretized into uniform intervals $\Delta t$; all events (arrivals, departures, segment occupancy) occur at integer time steps.
2. **Bidirectional single line**: The railway is a double-track line where each track normally serves one direction; during disruption, trains may use the opposite track.
3. **Fixed origin–destination**: Each train has predetermined origin and destination stations.
4. **Single disruption**: Exactly one segment is blocked during a known time window.
5. **Linearized energy model**: Energy consumption is approximated as a piecewise-linear function of speed and acceleration.
6. **Homogeneous trains**: All trains share the same kinematic parameters ($v_{\max}, a_{\max}, a_{\min}$).
7. **No track gradients or curves**: Energy model ignores track geometry effects.
8. **Perfect information**: Disruption time, location, and scheduled timetable are known in advance.
9. **Passing loops at stations**: Trains can pass each other only at stations.
10. **Safety headway**: A minimum distance $d_{\text{safe}}$ must be maintained between any two trains on the same track section.

Text:
# Integrated MILP Formulation for Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Infrastructure Constraints

Below I present a complete mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation that integrates the **composition model** (Fioole et al., 2006) and the **infrastructure model** (Van Aken et al., 2017) into a single formulation. The model determines an updated rolling stock circulation during a railway disruption, while ensuring that all shunting movements are feasible with respect to track availability at the affected stations.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of train trips in the (disrupted) timetable, indexed by $t, t'$ |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Set of rolling stock units, indexed by $r$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of feasible train compositions, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{L}$ | Set of track links (sections between stations), indexed by $\ell$ |
| $\mathcal{E}$ | Set of shunting events, indexed by $e$ |
| $\mathcal{V}$ | Set of vertices in the time–space infrastructure network, indexed by $v$ |
| $\mathcal{A}$ | Set of arcs in the time–space infrastructure network, indexed by $a$ |
| $\mathcal{Tr}_s$ | Set of tracks at station $s \in \mathcal{S}$, indexed by $tr$ |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Set of discretized time periods, indexed by $\tau$ |
| $\mathcal{D}$ | Set of disruptions, indexed by $d$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^{arr}_s \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Trips arriving at station $s$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^{dep}_s \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Trips departing from station $s$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^{aff}_d \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Trips affected by disruption $d$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $o_{t,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if composition $k$ was originally assigned to trip $t$ |
| $o_{r,t} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if unit $r$ was originally assigned to trip $t$ |
| $d_t \geq 0$ | Passenger demand for trip $t$ |
| $cap_k \geq 0$ | Seat capacity of composition $k$ |
| $len_k \geq 0$ | Number of rolling stock units in composition $k$ |
| $T^{arr}_t, T^{dep}_t$ | Scheduled arrival/departure time of trip $t$ |
| $\tau^{shunt}_s$ | Minimum time required for a shunting movement at station $s$ |
| $h^{min}$ | Minimum headway time between consecutive movements on the same track |
| $\Delta^{max}$ | Maximum delay (in minutes) allowed for non-disrupted trains |
| $c^{dev}_{t,k}$ | Cost of changing the composition of trip $t$ from $k$ to another |
| $c^{stand}$ | Cost per standing passenger per trip |
| $c^{delay}$ | Cost per minute of delay imposed on a passenger train |
| $c^{cancel}$ | Cost of canceling trip $t$ |
| $c^{shunt}$ | Cost per shunting movement |
| $c^{buffer}$ | Cost per rolling stock unit held as a buffer |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) |
| $B_{d,t} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if trip $t$ is directly affected by disruption $d$ |
| $R_k \subseteq \mathcal{R}$ | Set of rolling stock units belonging to composition $k$ |
| $type_{r,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if unit $r$ is of a type compatible with composition $k$ |
| $\rho_{tr,\tau} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if track $tr$ is occupied by a passenger train at time $\tau$ |
| $\Pi_v \in \mathbb{Z}$ | Net supply (+1) or demand (−1) of infrastructure usage at node $v$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $x_{t,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if trip $t$ uses composition $k$ |
| $y_{r,t} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if rolling stock unit $r$ operates trip $t$ |
| $z_{r,t,t'} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if unit $r$ transfers from trip $t$ to trip $t'$ via shunting |
| $w_t \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if trip $t$ is canceled |
| $\delta_t \geq 0$ | Delay (in minutes) imposed on trip $t$ |
| $s_t \geq 0$ | Number of standing passengers on trip $t$ |
| $b_r \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if rolling stock unit $r$ is held as a buffer |
| $g_e \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if shunting event $e$ is performed |
| $f_a \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if arc $a$ in the infrastructure time–space network is used |
| $\Delta_{t,k} \geq 0$ | Auxiliary variable for absolute deviation from original composition |

---

## 4. Objective Function

The objective minimizes a weighted combination of: (i) deviation from the original rolling stock plan, (ii) passenger discomfort, (iii) delays to other trains, (iv) canceled trips, (v) shunting movements, and (vi) buffer usage.

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \underbrace{\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} c^{dev}_{t,k} \, \Delta_{t,k}}_{\text{deviation from original plan}} \;+\; \underbrace{c^{stand} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} s_t}_{\text{standing passengers}} \;+\; \underbrace{c^{delay} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \delta_t}_{\text{delays to other trains}} \;+\; \underbrace{c^{cancel} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} c^{cancel}_t \, w_t}_{\text{canceled trips}} \;+\; \underbrace{c^{shunt} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}} g_e}_{\text{shunting movements}} \;+\; \underbrace{c^{buffer} \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} b_r}_{\text{buffer units}}
$$

The absolute deviation $\Delta_{t,k}$ is linearized by:

$$
\Delta_{t,k} \geq x_{t,k} - o_{t,k} \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T},\, k \in \mathcal{K}
$$
$$
\Delta_{t,k} \geq o_{t,k} - x_{t,k} \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T},\, k \in \mathcal{K}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Composition Model Constraints

**(C1) Composition assignment.** Each trip is operated by exactly one composition, unless it is canceled.

$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} x_{t,k} + w_t = 1 \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
$$

**(C2) Rolling stock unit assignment.** A unit may be assigned to a trip only if it belongs to the chosen composition and is type-compatible.

$$
y_{r,t} \leq \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} type_{r,k} \, x_{t,k} \quad \forall r \in \mathcal{R},\, t \in \mathcal{T}
$$
$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} y_{r,t} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} len_k \, x_{t,k} \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
$$

**(C3) Rolling stock flow conservation.** Each unit arriving at a station on a trip must depart on another trip (or be held as a buffer).

$$
\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}^{arr}_s} y_{r,t} = \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}^{dep}_s} y_{r,t} + b_r \quad \forall r \in \mathcal{R},\, s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(C4) Stick-to-the-plan.** Limit changes in rolling stock unit assignment relative to the original plan (soft constraint via penalty in objective).

$$
\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} |y_{r,t} - o_{r,t}| \leq \Phi^{max} \quad \text{(optional, linearized similarly to } \Delta_{t,k}\text{)}
$$

**(C5) Capacity for passengers.** The composition must provide sufficient seats; any excess demand is recorded as standing.

$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} cap_k \, x_{t,k} \geq d_t (1 - w_t) - s_t \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
$$
$$
s_t \leq M (1 - w_t) \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
$$

**(C6) Shunting transfer linking.** A shunting movement is required whenever a unit changes between consecutive trips at a station.

$$
z_{r,t,t'} \leq y_{r,t}, \quad z_{r,t,t'} \leq y_{r,t'} \quad \forall r \in \mathcal{R},\, t \in \mathcal{T}^{arr}_s,\, t' \in \mathcal{T}^{dep}_s,\, s \in \mathcal{S}
$$
$$
\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}^{arr}_s} \sum_{t' \in \mathcal{T}^{dep}_s} z_{r,t,t'} = \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}^{arr}_s} y_{r,t} - b_r \quad \forall r \in \mathcal{R},\, s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(C7) Time feasibility for shunting.** A shunting movement must fit within the available turnaround time.

$$
T^{dep}_{t'} - T^{arr}_t + \delta_{t'} \geq \tau^{shunt}_s - M(1 - z_{r,t,t'}) \quad \forall r \in \mathcal{R},\, s \in \mathcal{S},\, t \in \mathcal{T}^{arr}_s,\, t' \in \mathcal{T}^{dep}_s
$$

---

### 5.2 Infrastructure Model Constraints

**(C8) Shunting event activation.** A shunting event is performed only if the corresponding transfer is selected.

$$
g_e \leq \sum_{(r,t,t') \in \Phi_e} z_{r,t,t'} \quad \forall e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

where $\Phi_e$ is the set of $(r,t,t')$ triples corresponding to event $e$.

**(C9) Time–space network flow conservation.** For each vertex $v \in \mathcal{V}$ in the infrastructure network:

$$
\sum_{a \in \delta^+(v)} f_a - \sum_{a \in \delta^-(v)} f_a = \Pi_v \quad \forall v \in \mathcal{V}
$$

**(C10) Arc usage by shunting events.** Each shunting event must be assigned to a feasible arc in the time–space network.

$$
\sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}_e} f_a \geq g_e \quad \forall e \in \mathcal{E}
$$

where $\mathcal{A}_e \subseteq \mathcal{A}$ is the set of arcs that can realize event $e$.

**(C11) Track conflict avoidance.** At most one movement (passenger train or shunting) may occupy a given track at a given time.

$$
\sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_{tr,\tau}} g_e + \rho_{tr,\tau} \leq 1 \quad \forall tr \in \mathcal{Tr}_s,\, s \in \mathcal{S},\, \tau \in \mathcal{P}
$$

where $\mathcal{E}_{tr,\tau}$ is the set of shunting events that would use track $tr$ at time $\tau$.

**(C12) Minimum headway.** Consecutive movements on the same track must respect the minimum headway.

$$
T^{dep}_{t'} - T^{dep}_t \geq h^{min} - M(1 - x_{t,k}) - M(1 - x_{t',k'}) \quad \forall t, t' \in \mathcal{T}^{dep}_s,\, k, k' \in \mathcal{K},\, s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(C13) Bounded delays for non-disrupted trains.**

$$
\delta_t \leq \Delta^{max} \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T} \setminus \mathcal{T}^{aff}_d
$$

**(C14) Disruption constraints.** Trips directly affected by a disruption cannot be operated (or only with a specific composition, depending on the scenario).

$$
x_{t,k} = 0 \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}^{aff}_d,\, k \in \mathcal{K} \quad \text{(for fully blocked links)}
$$

For partial blockages, additional constraints restrict which links may be traversed:

$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} x_{t,k} \leq 0 \quad \forall t \text{ requiring link } \ell \text{ during disruption } d
$$

---

### 5.3 Linking and Auxiliary Constraints

**(C15) Shunting driver availability.** *(Assumption: one driver per shunting movement at a station at any given time.)*

$$
\sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_{s,\tau}} g_e \leq 1 \quad \forall s \in \mathcal{S},\, \tau \in \mathcal{P}
$$

**(C16) Track length compatibility.** *(Assumption: each station track has a maximum length.)*

$$
\sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_{tr}} len_{k_e} \, g_e \leq L^{max}_{tr} \quad \forall tr \in \mathcal{Tr}_s,\, s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

where $k_e$ is the composition associated with event $e$ and $L^{max}_{tr}$ is the maximum track length.

**(C17) Rolling stock type consistency.** A unit may only be transferred between trips that require the same (or compatible) unit type.

$$
z_{r,t,t'} \leq type_{r,k_t} \cdot type_{r,k_{t'}} \quad \forall r \in \mathcal{R},\, t, t' \in \mathcal{T}
$$

---

## 6. Notes on Solution Approach

The formulation above is the **integrated MILP**. In practice, the authors solve it via a **Combinatorial Benders' decomposition**:

- **Master problem:** Constraints (C1)–(C7) and the objective (composition model).
- **Subproblem:** Constraints (C8)–(C17) (infrastructure model), which checks feasibility of shunting movements and returns **no-good cuts** of the form

$$
\sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}^{viol}} g_e \leq |\mathcal{E}^{viol}| - 1
$$

whenever a combination of shunting movements violates track or headway constraints.

The **iterative heuristic** processes shunting events one by one, feeding each to the infrastructure model and fixing those that are feasible, mimicking the real-world interaction between rolling stock dispatchers and infrastructure dispatchers.

---

## 7. Key Assumptions

1. **Discretized time** is used for the infrastructure model; the granularity $\Delta\tau$ is a parameter (e.g., 1 minute).
2. **Short delays** ($\leq \Delta^{max}$, typically 2–5 minutes) are absorbed by timetable buffers and do not propagate.
3. **Shunting drivers** are assumed available at each station for the duration of the disruption.
4. **Track lengths** at stations are sufficient for the compositions considered (verified per station in practice).
5. **Passenger demand** $d_t$ is deterministic and known for the disruption horizon.
6. **Rolling stock units** are homogeneous within type (no individual unit failures beyond the disruption).
7. The set $\mathcal{K}$ of feasible compositions is pre-generated based on depot and coupling constraints.
8. The disruption is modeled as a complete blockage of one or more links for a known time window.

---

This integrated MILP captures the full rolling stock rescheduling problem with infrastructure-aware shunting feasibility, balancing operational costs, passenger service levels, and adherence to the original plan.

Text:
# Best Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP

I evaluated the three generated models. **Model 2** was empty, **Model 1** hand-waved the bidirectional conflict linearization ("analogous constraints cover all direction/route combinations") and introduced two auxiliary binary variables ($w, b$) without clean definitions. **Model 3** is the strongest: it explicitly linearizes the track-sharing indicator, cleanly couples rerouting to physical track usage, properly enforces bidirectional conflicts on shared resources, and keeps every constraint in linear (Big-M) form. I present it below as the final answer.

---

## 1. Modeling Assumptions

- A double-track corridor is modeled as an ordered sequence of stations $S = \{1,\dots,|S|\}$ separated by segments $I = \{1,\dots,|S|-1\}$, with segment $i$ connecting station $i$ to station $i+1$.
- Trains travel either forward (southbound) or backward (northbound); each train has a fixed direction $\mathrm{dir}_k \in \{+1,-1\}$.
- A single **blocked segment** $i^\star \in I$ is unavailable during the disruption window $[B^{\text{start}}, B^{\text{end}}]$ on its **forward track**, but the parallel opposite track remains usable for rerouted trains.
- The continuous speed-management surface is discretized into a set of speed profiles $P$, each with a fixed running time $\tau_{i,p}$ and energy consumption $e_{i,p}$ per segment.
- Time is continuous; cancellations nullify all timing variables for a train (via Big-M).

---

## 2. Sets

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $K$ | Set of trains, $k \in K$ |
| $S$ | Ordered set of stations |
| $I$ | Set of segments, $i \in I$ (connects station $i$ to $i+1$) |
| $P$ | Discrete speed profiles, $p \in P$ |
| $S_k \subseteq S$ | Stations served by train $k$ |
| $I_k \subseteq I$ | Segments traversed by train $k$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $a_k^s, d_k^s$ | Scheduled arrival / departure time of train $k$ at station $s$ |
| $\tau_{i,p}$ | Running time of profile $p$ on segment $i$ |
| $e_{i,p}$ | Energy consumed under profile $p$ on segment $i$ |
| $\delta^{s}_{\min}, \delta^{s}_{\max}$ | Min / max dwell time at station $s$ |
| $\omega_s$ | Minimum station headway (departure–departure) |
| $\eta_i$ | Minimum segment running-time separation |
| $B^{\text{start}}, B^{\text{end}}$ | Disruption window bounds |
| $i^\star$ | Blocked segment index |
| $\kappa$ | Cancellation penalty |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3 \geq 0$ | Objective weights (delay, energy, cancellation) |
| $M$ | Big-M constant (set larger than the rescheduling horizon) |
| $\mathrm{dir}_k \in \{+1,-1\}$ | Direction of train $k$ (constant per train) |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $A_k^s$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Actual arrival time of train $k$ at station $s$ |
| $D_k^s$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Actual departure time |
| $y_{k,i,p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $k$ uses profile $p$ on segment $i$ |
| $r_{k,i}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $k$ is **rerouted** on segment $i$ (uses opposite track) |
| $\theta_{k,i}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | Physical track used by train $k$ on segment $i$ (0 = forward, 1 = backward) |
| $o_{k,k',i}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if $k$ precedes $k'$ on segment $i$ (when sharing the same physical track) |
| $c_k$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $k$ is **cancelled** |
| $\Delta_{k,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Arrival delay of train $k$ at station $s$ |

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; w_1 \sum_{k \in K}\sum_{s \in S_k} \Delta_{k,s} \;+\; w_2 \sum_{k \in K}\sum_{i \in I_k}\sum_{p \in P} e_{i,p}\, y_{k,i,p} \;+\; w_3 \sum_{k \in K} \kappa\, c_k
$$

A weighted sum of (i) **total arrival delay**, (ii) **total energy consumption** (driven by speed-profile choice), and (iii) **cancellation penalty**.

---

## 6. Constraints

### (C1) Cancellation zeroes timing
$$
A_k^s \le M(1-c_k),\qquad D_k^s \le M(1-c_k)\qquad \forall k \in K,\; s \in S_k
$$

### (C2) Exactly one speed profile per active train-segment
$$
\sum_{p \in P} y_{k,i,p} \;=\; 1 - c_k \qquad \forall k \in K,\; i \in I_k
$$

### (C3) Timetable propagation (running time = chosen profile)
$$
D_k^{i+1} - A_k^i \;=\; \sum_{p \in P} \tau_{i,p}\, y_{k,i,p} \qquad \forall k \in K,\; i \in I_k
$$

### (C4) Dwell-time bounds
$$
\delta^{s}_{\min}(1-c_k) \;\le\; A_k^{s+1} - D_k^{s} \;\le\; \delta^{s}_{\max}(1-c_k) \qquad \forall k \in K,\; s \in S_k\!\setminus\!\{s^{\text{last}}_k\}
$$

### (C5) Delay definition
$$
\Delta_{k,s} \;\ge\; A_k^{s} - a_k^{s},\qquad \Delta_{k,s} \;\ge\; 0 \qquad \forall k \in K,\; s \in S_k
$$

### (C6) Track-usage / rerouting linkage
Rerouting flips the train to the opposite physical track:
$$
\theta_{k,i} \;=\; r_{k,i}\quad\text{if }\mathrm{dir}_k=+1;\qquad \theta_{k,i}\;=\;1-r_{k,i}\quad\text{if }\mathrm{dir}_k=-1
$$
*(Equivalent to a fixed linear identity depending on the constant $\mathrm{dir}_k$.)*

### (C7) Disruption: blocked segment $i^\star$
A non-cancelled train may traverse $i^\star$ only if it (a) passes before $B^{\text{start}}$, (b) enters after $B^{\text{end}}$, or (c) is rerouted:
$$
A_k^{i^\star} \;\ge\; B^{\text{end}} - M\,r_{k,i^\star} - M\,c_k \qquad \forall k \in K,\; i^\star \in I_k
$$
$$
D_k^{i^\star} \;\le\; B^{\text{start}} + M(1-r_{k,i^\star}) + M\,c_k \qquad \forall k \in K,\; i^\star \in I_k
$$

### (C8) Station headway (departure-departure)
For each ordered pair $(k,k')$:
$$
D_k^s - D_{k'}^s \;\ge\; \omega_s - M\,o_{k',k,s} - M\,c_k - M\,c_{k'} \qquad \forall k \neq k',\; s
$$
$$
D_{k'}^s - D_k^s \;\ge\; \omega_s - M\,o_{k,k',s} - M\,c_k - M\,c_{k'} \qquad \forall k \neq k',\; s
$$
$$
o_{k,k',s} + o_{k',k,s} \;=\; 1 \qquad \forall k \neq k',\; s
$$

### (C9) Bidirectional conflict via shared-track indicator
Trains $k$ and $k'$ physically share segment $i$ iff $\theta_{k,i} = \theta_{k',i}$. Linearize:
$$
\text{share}_{k,k',i} \;\ge\; \theta_{k,i} - \theta_{k',i},\qquad \text{share}_{k,k',i} \;\ge\; \theta_{k',i} - \theta_{k,i}
$$
$$
\text{share}_{k,k',i} \;\le\; \theta_{k,i} + \theta_{k',i},\qquad \text{share}_{k,k',i} \;\le\; 2 - \theta_{k,i} - \theta_{k',i}
$$
$$
\text{share}_{k,k',i} \in \{0,1\} \qquad \forall k \neq k',\; i
$$

### (C10) Segment headway on shared tracks
$$
A_k^{i+1} \;\ge\; D_{k'}^i + \eta_i - M(1-o_{k,k',i}) - M(1-\text{share}_{k,k',i}) - M\,c_k - M\,c_{k'} \;\;\forall k \neq k',\;i
$$
$$
A_{k'}^{i+1} \;\ge\; D_k^i + \eta_i - M\,o_{k,k',i} - M(1-\text{share}_{k,k',i}) - M\,c_k - M\,c_{k'} \;\;\forall k \neq k',\;i
$$
$$
o_{k,k',i} + o_{k',k,i} \;=\; 1 \qquad \forall k \neq k',\; i
$$

### (C11) Variable domains
$$
y_{k,i,p},\; r_{k,i},\; \theta_{k,i},\; o_{k,k',i},\; c_k,\; \text{share}_{k,k',i} \in \{0,1\};\qquad A_k^s,\; D_k^s,\; \Delta_{k,s} \geq 0
$$

---

## 7. Why this Model is the Best Choice

| Required feature | Captured by |
|---|---|
| Train **arrival/departure retiming** | $A_k^s, D_k^s$ propagated by (C3) |
| **Speed-profile** selection with time–energy trade-off | $y_{k,i,p}$ via (C2)–(C3), $e_{i,p}$ in objective |
| **Reordering** of trains on shared resources | $o_{k,k',i}$ + share indicator (C9)–(C10) |
| **Rerouting** to the opposite track during disruption | $r_{k,i}$ coupled with $\theta_{k,i}$ (C6), (C7) |
| **Bidirectional** conflict resolution when rerouted | Track-sharing linearization (C9) + segment headway (C10) |
| **Cancellation** with penalty | $c_k$ zeroing timings (C1), penalized in objective |
| **Disruption window** enforcement | Big-M on blocked segment (C7) |
| Conflict-free rescheduling | Station headway (C8) + segment headway on shared tracks (C10) |
| **Linearity** (MILP-solvable) | All products are binary × constant via Big-M; share indicator linearized in (C9) |

The model is a standard MILP directly solvable by Gurobi / CPLEX / HiGHS, with practical tightening obtained by choosing the smallest valid Big-M per constraint (e.g., $M \geq B^{\text{end}} + \max_{k,i,p}\tau_{i,p}$), and is amenable to warm starts from the original timetable.

# MILP Formulation: Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Railway Infrastructure Constraints

## 1. Model Overview

This Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP) integrates a **composition model** (assigning rolling stock units to trips) with an **infrastructure model** (verifying track feasibility of shunting movements) for rescheduling rolling stock during railway disruptions. The model decides (i) which unit operates each trip, (ii) the composition (length) of each trip, (iii) shunting movements between consecutive trips, (iv) track assignments for all events, and (v) small delay allocations to passenger trains to free up track capacity for shunting.

---

## 2. Assumptions

| # | Assumption |
|---|---|
| **A1** | The planning horizon covers one service day; units start and end at depot locations. |
| **A2** | Each trip is operated by a single *coupled composition* of identical units; the composition length is a discrete choice from set *K*. |
| **A3** | Shunting movements are modeled as events occupying one track for a known duration. |
| **A4** | Two events conflict on a track if their time windows overlap. |
| **A5** | Passenger-train delays are bounded by Δ minutes (e.g., 3 min) and absorbed by timetable buffers. |
| **A6** | The set of feasible shunting arcs *A* is pre-computed using time and station compatibility. |
| **A7** | Cancelled trips and blocked tracks are exogenous inputs from the disruption scenario. |
| **A8** | All passengers who can board do board; those who cannot are "missed". |
| **A9** | Big-M constants are chosen tight enough to avoid weak relaxations (A9). |

---

## 3. Sets and Indices

| Set | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| *T* | Train trips, indexed by *t, t′* |
| *R* | Rolling stock units, indexed by *r* |
| *S* | Stations, indexed by *s* |
| *E* = *E^T* ∪ *E^S* | Events (train arrivals/departures *E^T* and shunting movements *E^S*), indexed by *e* |
| *TR* | Railway tracks, indexed by *tr* |
| *K* | Composition types (e.g., 2/4/6-car), indexed by *k* |
| *A* ⊆ *T* × *T* | Feasible shunting arcs (same station, sufficient turnaround time) |
| *TR_s* ⊆ *TR* | Tracks at station *s* |
| *L* | Train lines, indexed by *l* |
| *C* ⊆ *E* × *E* | Pairs of events that may conflict on the same track |

---

## 4. Parameters

**Trips & demand**
- `dem_t` — passenger demand on trip *t*
- `cap_k`, `len_k` — seat capacity and number of units in composition *k*
- `start_t`, `end_t` — scheduled start/end times of trip *t*
- `stat⁺_t`, `stat⁻_t` — start/end station of trip *t*
- `line_t` — line of trip *t*

**Rolling stock**
- `cost_r` — operating cost of unit *r*
- `loc⁰_r`, `time⁰_r` — initial location and availability time of unit *r*

**Shunting & infrastructure**
- `shunt_dur_{t,t′}` — duration of shunting movement from *t* to *t′*
- `min_turn` — minimum turnaround time
- `max_delay Δ` — maximum allowed delay for any train event
- `blocked_{tr,τ}` — 1 if track *tr* is blocked in time-slot *τ* (from disruption input)

**Original plan (for stick-to-the-plan objective)**
- `orig_{r,t}` — 1 if unit *r* originally operated trip *t*
- `orig_k_t` — original composition type for trip *t*

**Cost weights**
- `c_op`, `c_dev`, `c_stand`, `c_miss`, `c_delay` — unit costs for operations, plan deviation, standing passengers, missed passengers, and delay (per minute)

**Big-M constants**
- `M₁` — large constant for time disjunctions (≥ planning horizon length)
- `M₂` — large constant for linking constraints

---

## 5. Decision Variables

**Assignment & composition**
- `x_{r,t} ∈ {0,1}` — 1 if unit *r* operates trip *t*
- `y_{t,k} ∈ {0,1}` — 1 if trip *t* uses composition *k*
- `f_{r,t,t′} ∈ {0,1}` — 1 if unit *r* operates trip *t* immediately followed by *t′* (i.e., a shunting arc is used)

**Infrastructure & timing**
- `d_e ≥ 0` — delay (minutes) of event *e*
- `p_e ≥ 0` — actual start time of event *e*
- `z_{e,tr} ∈ {0,1}` — 1 if event *e* uses track *tr*
- `σ_{e,e′,tr} ∈ {0,1}` — 1 if event *e* precedes *e′* on track *tr* (ordering)

**Service quality**
- `stand_t ≥ 0` — number of standing passengers on trip *t*
- `miss_t ≥ 0` — number of passengers who cannot board trip *t*
- `dev_{r,t} ∈ {0,1}` — 1 if assignment (*r,t*) deviates from the original plan
- `u_t ∈ {0,1}` — 1 if trip *t* capacity ≥ demand (auxiliary)

---

## 6. Objective Function

Minimize a weighted sum of four cost components:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; w_1 \underbrace{\sum_{r\in R}\sum_{t\in T} c_{op}\,x_{r,t}}_{\text{Operating cost}}
\;+\; w_2 \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\bigl(c_{stand}\,stand_t + c_{miss}\,miss_t\bigr)}_{\text{Passenger service}}
\;+\; w_3 \underbrace{\sum_{r\in R}\sum_{t\in T} c_{dev}\,dev_{r,t}}_{\text{Stick-to-the-plan}}
\;+\; w_4 \underbrace{\sum_{e\in E^T} c_{delay}\,d_e}_{\text{Delay cost}}
$$

Weights `w₁…w₄ ≥ 0` reflect the dispatcher's priorities (A: any non-negative combination is valid).

---

## 7. Constraints

### 7.1 Composition Constraints

**(C1)** Each trip uses exactly one composition type:
$$
\sum_{k\in K} y_{t,k} = 1 \qquad \forall\, t\in T
$$

**(C2)** Number of units assigned to trip *t* equals the chosen composition length:
$$
\sum_{r\in R} x_{r,t} = \sum_{k\in K} len_k\, y_{t,k} \qquad \forall\, t\in T
$$

### 7.2 Rolling-Stock Flow Conservation

For each unit *r*, introduce a source `σ_r` and sink `τ_r`. Let `f_{r,σ_r,t}` and `f_{r,t,τ_r}` be binary flow variables on the source/sink arcs.

**(C3)** Each unit is used at most once and starts/ends at exactly one trip:
$$
\sum_{t\in T} f_{r,\sigma_r,t} \le 1,\qquad \sum_{t\in T} f_{r,t,\tau_r} \le 1 \qquad \forall\, r\in R
$$

**(C4)** Flow conservation at every trip node:
$$
\sum_{t'\in T} f_{r,t',t} + f_{r,\sigma_r,t} \;=\; \sum_{t'\in T} f_{r,t,t'} + f_{r,t,\tau_r} \;=\; x_{r,t} \qquad \forall\, r\in R,\; t\in T
$$

**(C5)** Initial-location compatibility (A1, A6):
$$
f_{r,\sigma_r,t} \le \mathbf{1}\!\left[\,stat^{+}_t = loc^{0}_r \;\wedge\; start_t \ge time^{0}_r\,\right] \qquad \forall\, r\in R,\; t\in T
$$

### 7.3 Shunting-Link Constraints

**(C6)** A shunting arc may only be used if both trips are operated by the same unit:
$$
f_{r,t,t'} \le x_{r,t}, \qquad f_{r,t,t'} \le x_{r,t'} \qquad \forall\, r\in R,\; (t,t')\in A
$$

**(C7)** Shunting-arc feasibility (only arcs in *A* allowed):
$$
f_{r,t,t'} = 0 \qquad \forall\, r\in R,\; (t,t')\notin A
$$

### 7.4 Infrastructure (Track) Constraints

**(C8)** Each event uses exactly one track at its station:
$$
\sum_{tr\in TR_{stat(e)}} z_{e,tr} = 1 \qquad \forall\, e\in E
$$

**(C9)** Track conflict — two events on the same track must not overlap. Using ordering variables `σ_{e,e′,tr}`:
$$
z_{e,tr} + z_{e',tr} - 1 \;\le\; \sigma_{e,e',tr} + \sigma_{e',e,tr} \qquad \forall\, (e,e')\in C,\; tr\in TR
$$
$$
p_e + dur_e \;\le\; p_{e'} + M_1\,(1-\sigma_{e,e',tr}) \qquad \forall\, (e,e'),\, tr
$$
$$
p_{e'} + dur_{e'} \;\le\; p_e + M_1\,(1-\sigma_{e',e,tr}) \qquad \forall\, (e,e'),\, tr
$$

**(C10)** Blocked tracks (disruption input, A7):
$$
z_{e,tr} = 0 \qquad \forall\, e,\; tr:\; blocked_{tr,\tau(e)} = 1
$$

### 7.5 Time and Delay Constraints

**(C11)** Actual time equals scheduled time plus delay:
$$
p_e = sched_e + d_e \qquad \forall\, e\in E
$$

**(C12)** Delay bound (A5):
$$
d_e \le \Delta \qquad \forall\, e\in E^T
$$
(Shunting events have no delay cap; they wait if necessary.)

**(C13)** Shunting timing — if unit *r* shunts from *t* to *t′*, the next trip cannot depart before shunting completes:
$$
p_{end(t)} + shunt\_dur_{t,t'} \;\le\; p_{start(t')} + M_2\,(1-f_{r,t,t'}) \qquad \forall\, r\in R,\; (t,t')\in A
$$

### 7.6 Passenger-Service Constraints

**(C14)** Capacity of trip *t*:
$$
Cap_t = \sum_{k\in K} cap_k\, y_{t,k} \qquad \forall\, t\in T
$$

**(C15)** Standing and missed passengers (A8):
$$
stand_t \;\ge\; dem_t - Cap_t \qquad \forall\, t\in T
$$
$$
miss_t \;\ge\; dem_t - Cap_t - M_2\,u_t \qquad \forall\, t\in T
$$
$$
miss_t \;\le\; dem_t\,(1-u_t) \qquad \forall\, t\in T
$$
$$
stand_t,\; miss_t \;\ge\; 0
$$

### 7.7 Plan-Deviation Constraints

**(C16)** Deviation indicator:
$$
dev_{r,t} \;\ge\; x_{r,t} - orig_{r,t}, \qquad dev_{r,t} \;\ge\; orig_{r,t} - x_{r,t} \qquad \forall\, r\in R,\; t\in T
$$

### 7.8 Disruption & Cancellation Constraints

**(C17)** Cancelled trips cannot be operated:
$$
x_{r,t} = 0 \qquad \forall\, r\in R,\; t\in T^{cancelled}
$$

**(C18)** Disrupted trips may have modified schedules (`start_t`, `end_t` reflect the new timetable).

---

## 8. Notes on Solution Approach

The integrated MILP above is the **master problem** of the exact Combinatorial-Benders' algorithm described in the paper:

1. **Master (composition)**: solve the model *without* (C8)–(C10) and (C13) → produces shunting movements `f`.
2. **Subproblem (infrastructure)**: fix `f` and solve (C8)–(C13) → if infeasible, return a * Combinatorial Benders' cut* of the form
   $\sum_{(t,t')\in A^{conf}} f_{r,t,t'} \le |A^{conf}|-1$ prohibiting the conflicting combination.
3. Iterate until feasibility is proved.

The **iterative heuristic** instead feeds shunting movements to the subproblem *one by one* (mimicking the dispatcher workflow), removing any infeasible movement and re-solving the master — yielding the same optimum in the reported instances because shunting movements rarely conflict with one another.

**Assumption (A9) on Big-M tightness.** `M₁` should be set to the length of the planning horizon (e.g., 1440 min) and `M₂` to a value just larger than the maximum of `dem_t` (for passenger constraints) and `Δ + max(shunt_dur)` (for timing constraints).

Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

# MILP Model for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

Below is the best, complete MILP formulation, synthesizing the strongest elements of the generated candidates. It captures all four levels of decision-making (retiming, reordering, rerouting, speed management), handles bidirectional conflicts and rerouting under partial blockages, and uses piecewise-linear approximations to remain linear.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $I$ | Set of trains, $i \in I$ |
| $J$ | Set of stations, $j \in J = \{0,1,\dots,|J|\}$ ($j=0$ origin, $j=|J|$ destination) |
| $B$ | Ordered set of track blocks, $b \in B = \{1,\dots,|B|\}$ with $|B|=|J|$ |
| $K$ | Discrete time intervals, $k \in K=\{0,1,\dots,|K|\}$, duration $\Delta$ |
| $P$ | Tracks per block, $p\in P=\{1,2\}$ (1 = up, 2 = down) |
| $S$ | Piecewise-linear segments of the energy–speed curve, $s\in S=\{1,\dots,|S|\}$ |
| $N$ | Speed breakpoints for $L_b/v$ convex envelope, $n\in N=\{1,\dots,|N|\}$ |
| $\bar p(i)=3-\text{orig}_i$ | Opposite track of train $i$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ | km |
| $V^{\max}_b, V^{\min}$ | Max/min allowed speed on $b$ / minimum operational speed | km/h |
| $A^{\max}, D^{\max}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration per time unit | km/h per min |
| $T^{a,\text{sch}}_{i,j}, T^{d,\text{sch}}_{i,j}$ | Scheduled arrival/departure time | min |
| $D^{\min}_{i,j}, D^{\max}_{i,j}$ | Min/max dwell time | min |
| $R^{\min}_{i,b}, R^{\max}_{i,b}$ | Min/max running time on $b$ | min |
| $H$ | Minimum headway on same block & track | min |
| $d^{\text{start}}_b, d^{\text{end}}_b$ | Start/end of disruption on $b$ | min |
| $E_s, c_s$ | Slope / intercept of energy–speed segment $s$ | kWh/km per (km/h) / kWh/km |
| $V^{\text{bp}}_s$ | Lower breakpoint speed of segment $s$ | km/h |
| $W_n$ | Speed breakpoints for $L_b/v$ convex envelope | km/h |
| $C^p_{i,b}$ | Routing cost | – |
| $\Pi^{\text{canc}}_i$ | Cancellation penalty | – |
| $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ | Weights for delay / energy / cancellation | – |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant | – |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{i,j}, d_{i,j}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Actual arrival / departure time of train $i$ at $j$ |
| $\tau_{i,b}, \sigma_{i,b}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Entry / exit time of train $i$ at block $b$ |
| $t_{i,b}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Traversal time of $i$ on $b$ |
| $v_{i,b}, v_{i,b,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Average / segment-local speed |
| $x^p_{i,b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses track $p$ on $b$ |
| $y_{i,i',b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if $i$ traverses $b$ before $i'$ |
| $z_{i,b,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if $i$ occupies $b$ in interval $k$ |
| $\mu_{i,b,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if energy segment $s$ is active for $i$ on $b$ |
| $\xi_{i,b,n}$ | $[0,1]$ | SOS1 variables for $L_b/v$ convex envelope |
| $e_{i,b}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Energy consumed by $i$ on $b$ (kWh) |
| $\delta^{a+}_{i,j}, \delta^{d+}_{i,j}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Positive arrival / departure delay |
| $w_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $\text{aff}_{i,b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if $i$'s occupancy on $b$ overlaps the disruption window |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\;\alpha\!\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{j\in J}\!\bigl(\delta^{a+}_{i,j}+\delta^{d+}_{i,j}\bigr) \;+\;\beta\!\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{b\in B}e_{i,b} \;+\;\gamma\!\sum_{i\in I}\Pi^{\text{canc}}_i\,w_i \;+\;\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{b\in B}\sum_{p\in P}C^p_{i,b}x^p_{i,b}
$$

The first three terms are the primary operational objectives (delay, energy, cancellations); the routing cost is a tie-breaker.

---

## 5. Constraints

### A. Train-Stop and Block Dynamics

**(A1) Dwell time at each station** (collapsed if cancelled):
$$
D^{\min}_{i,j}(1-w_i) \le d_{i,j}-a_{i,j} \le D^{\max}_{i,j}(1-w_i) \quad \forall i,j
$$

**(A2) Station-to-station running time bounds:**
$$
R^{\min}_{i,b}(1-w_i) \le a_{i,b}-d_{i,b-1} \le R^{\max}_{i,b}(1-w_i) \quad \forall i,b
$$

**(A3) Block traversal time** (definition + convex envelope of $L_b/v$ via SOS1):
$$
\sigma_{i,b}-\tau_{i,b}=t_{i,b}
$$
$$
t_{i,b} \ge \frac{L_b}{V^{\max}_b}+\sum_{n=1}^{|N|-1}\!\Bigl(\tfrac{L_b}{W_{n+1}}-\tfrac{L_b}{W_n}\Bigr)\xi_{i,b,n}
$$
$$
t_{i,b} \le \frac{L_b}{V^{\min}}+\sum_{n=1}^{|N|-1}\!\Bigl(\tfrac{L_b}{W_n}-\tfrac{L_b}{W_{n+1}}\Bigr)\xi_{i,b,n},\quad \xi_{i,b,n}\le \xi_{i,b,n-1}\;\;(SOS1)
$$

**(A4) Speed limits:**
$$
V^{\min}(1-w_i)\le v_{i,b}\le V^{\max}_b(1-w_i)\quad\forall i,b
$$

**(A5) Acceleration / deceleration between consecutive blocks** (finite-difference linearization):
$$
-D^{\max}\Delta \;\le\; v_{i,b+1}-v_{i,b}\;\le\;A^{\max}\Delta \quad\forall i,\;b<|B|
$$

### B. Routing and Track Assignment

**(B1) Exactly one track per train per block:**
$$
\sum_{p\in P}x^p_{i,b}=1-w_i \quad\forall i,b
$$

**(B2) Boundary track pinning:**
$$
x^{\text{orig}_i}_{i,1}\ge 1-w_i,\qquad x^{\text{dest}_i}_{i,|B|}\ge 1-w_i \quad\forall i
$$

**(B3) Track continuity** (no track teleportation between consecutive blocks):
$$
x^p_{i,b}=x^p_{i,b+1}+s^p_{i,b},\quad s^p_{i,b}\in\{0,1\},\quad \sum_{p}s^p_{i,b}\le 1
$$

**(B4) Disruption overlap indicator:**
$$
\tau_{i,b}\le d^{\text{end}}_b+M(1-\text{aff}_{i,b}),\quad \sigma_{i,b}\ge d^{\text{start}}_b-M(1-\text{aff}_{i,b}),\quad \text{aff}_{i,b}\le 1-w_i
$$

**(B5) Mandatory rerouting when overlapping disruption on original track:**
$$
x^{\text{orig}_i}_{i,b}+\text{aff}_{i,b}\le 1\quad\forall i,b
$$

**(B6) Opposite-track single-capacity during disruption window:**
$$
\sum_{i\in I}z_{i,b,k}\,x^{\bar p(i)}_{i,b}\le 1 \quad\forall b,\;k\text{ with }k\Delta\in[d^{\text{start}}_b,d^{\text{end}}_b]
$$

### C. Conflict Resolution

**(C1) Bidirectional conflict on the same block** (no headway — opposite directions must fully clear):
$$
\sigma_{i,b}\le \tau_{i',b}+M(1-y_{i,i',b})+M\bigl(2-x^{\text{orig}_i}_{i,b}-x^{\text{orig}_{i'}}_{i',b}\bigr)
$$
$$
\sigma_{i',b}\le \tau_{i,b}+M\,y_{i,i',b}+M\bigl(2-x^{\text{orig}_i}_{i,b}-x^{\text{orig}_{i'}}_{i',b}\bigr)
$$
$$
y_{i,i',b}+y_{i',i,b}=1 \quad\forall i\neq i',\,b
$$

**(C2) Same-direction headway on shared block & track:**
$$
\sigma_{i,b}+H\le \tau_{i',b}+M(1-y_{i,i',b})+M\bigl(2-x^p_{i,b}-x^p_{i',b}\bigr)\;\forall i\neq i',\,b,\,p
$$
$$
\sigma_{i',b}+H\le \tau_{i,b}+M\,y_{i,i',b}+M\bigl(2-x^p_{i,b}-x^p_{i',b}\bigr)\;\forall i\neq i',\,b,\,p
$$

**(C3) Block single-occupancy per interval:**
$$
\sum_{i\in I}z_{i,b,k}\le 1 \quad\forall b,k
$$

### D. Energy Model (Piecewise-Linear, No Bilinear Terms)

**(D1) Exactly one active energy segment per (train, block):**
$$
\sum_{s\in S}\mu_{i,b,s}=1-w_i \quad\forall i,b
$$

**(D2) Segment-conditional speed range:**
$$
V^{\text{bp}}_s\,\mu_{i,b,s}\le v_{i,b,s}\le V^{\text{bp}}_{s+1}\mu_{i,b,s}\quad\forall i,b,s
$$
$$
v_{i,b}=\sum_{s\in S}v_{i,b,s}\quad\forall i,b
$$

**(D3) Piecewise-linear energy:**
$$
e_{i,b}=\sum_{s\in S}\bigl(E_s\,v_{i,b,s}+c_s\,\mu_{i,b,s}\bigr)\quad\forall i,b
$$

### E. Time-Discretization Linking (Block Occupancy)

**(E1) Interval occupied iff $k\Delta\in[\tau_{i,b},\sigma_{i,b}]$:**
$$
\tau_{i,b}\ge k\Delta-M(1-z_{i,b,k}),\quad \sigma_{i,b}\le (k+1)\Delta+M(1-z_{i,b,k}),\quad z_{i,b,k}\le 1-w_i
$$

**(E2) Occupancy count equals traversal duration:**
$$
\sum_{k\in K}z_{i,b,k}\,\Delta=t_{i,b}\quad\forall i,b
$$

### F. Linking Constraints (Block ↔ Station)

**(F1) Block exit = station arrival:**
$$
a_{i,j}=\sigma_{i,j}\;\;(j=1,\dots,|J|-1),\qquad a_{i,|J|}=\sigma_{i,|B|}
$$

**(F2) Station departure = next block entry:**
$$
d_{i,0}=\tau_{i,1},\qquad d_{i,j}=\tau_{i,j+1}\;(j=1,\dots,|J|-1)
$$

### G. Delay, Cancellation, Domains

**(G1) Positive-delay definitions (active only for non-cancelled trains):**
$$
\delta^{a+}_{i,j}\ge a_{i,j}-T^{a,\text{sch}}_{i,j},\;\delta^{a+}_{i,j}\ge 0,\;\delta^{a+}_{i,j}\le M\,w_i
$$
$$
\delta^{d+}_{i,j}\ge d_{i,j}-T^{d,\text{sch}}_{i,j},\;\delta^{d+}_{i,j}\ge 0,\;\delta^{d+}_{i,j}\le M\,w_i
$$

**(G2) Variable domains:**
$$
x^p_{i,b},\,y_{i,i',b},\,z_{i,b,k},\,\mu_{i,b,s},\,w_i,\,\text{aff}_{i,b}\in\{0,1\}
$$
$$
\xi_{i,b,n}\in[0,1];\quad a_{i,j},d_{i,j},\tau_{i,b},\sigma_{i,b},v_{i,b},v_{i,b,s},t_{i,b},e_{i,b},\delta^{a+}_{i,j},\delta^{d+}_{i,j}\ge 0
$$

---

## 6. Modeling Assumptions

1. **Homogeneous rolling stock** — All trains share the same kinematic envelope $(A^{\max}, D^{\max}, V^{\min})$ and energy curve.
2. **Partial blockage = one direction blocked, opposite track available** — Capacity of the opposite track during the disruption window is exactly one train.
3. **Rerouting is optional but mandatory when overlapping disruption on the original track** — Trains can also reroute voluntarily to improve feasibility (B1, B3).
4. **Piecewise-linear energy function** with $|S|=5$ segments; the segment-active binary $\mu_{i,b,s}$ eliminates the bilinear $E_s v$ term without discretization.
5. **Convex envelope of $L_b/v$** with $|N|=8$ speed breakpoints — tighter than naive bound linearization.
6. **Time horizon** discretized at $\Delta=1$ min; the horizon $|K|$ is set to the planning window (e.g., 180–240 min for a realistic corridor).
7. **Single-track bidirectional** — both directions share the corridor; conflicts arise between opposing trains and headway arises between same-direction trains.
8. **Cancellation** as last-resort action, penalized via $\gamma\Pi^{\text{canc}}_i$ and disabling all active timing/speed variables through $(1-w_i)$ factors.
9. **Rerouting cost** $C^p_{i,b}$ allows the dispatcher to encode switch-overhead penalties, operational preferences, or section unavailability.

---

## 7. Model Properties

| Property | Realization |
|---|---|
| **Linearity** | Guaranteed via piecewise-linear energy, convex envelope of $L_b/v$, and indicator-based big-M constraints |
| **Decision layers** | Retiming $(a,d,\tau,\sigma)$ + Reordering $(y)$ + Rerouting $(x,\text{aff})$ + Speed profile $(v,e)$ jointly optimized |
| **Bidirectional conflict** | Explicit (C1) — opposite-direction trains must fully clear before the other enters |
| **Partial-blockage rerouting** | (B4)–(B6) — original track forbidden in disruption; opposite track capacity-constrained |
| **Energy–delay coupling** | Speed $v_{i,b}$ enters both running time (A3) and energy (D3) — true trade-off |
| **Scalability** | Dominated by $|I|\!\cdot\!|B|\!\cdot\!|K|$ binary occupancy variables; decomposition in Section 5 of the paper accelerates large instances |
| **Solver readiness** | Direct input to Gurobi/CPLEX; branch-and-cut; warm-started by the decomposition-based IP plan selection. |

---

This MILP delivers a **conflict-free timetable, feasible rerouting decisions, and executable energy-aware speed profiles** in a single integrated model, faithfully implementing the TRSMP framework for partial-segment-blockage disruptions described in the manuscript.
