Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

Below is the best of the three generated models, refined for clarity and correctness. It captures the integrated decisions of **retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and discrete speed-profile selection** under a partial segment blockage on a double-track high-speed line.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, $i,j \in T$ |
| $S$ | ordered stations, $s \in S = \{1,\dots,|S|\}$ |
| $K = \{1,\dots,|S|-1\}$ | inter-station segments; segment $k$ connects station $k$ to $k+1$ |
| $P$ | discrete speed profiles, $p \in P$ |
| $K^B \subseteq K$ | blocked segment(s) |
| $T^+, T^-$ | trains in the "up" / "down" direction ($T = T^+ \cup T^-$) |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\tau^a_{i,s}, \tau^d_{i,s}$ | scheduled arrival / departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $L_k$ | length of segment $k$ |
| $t^p_k$ | running time on segment $k$ under profile $p$ |
| $e^p_k$ | energy consumption on segment $k$ under profile $p$ |
| $h$ | minimum same-direction headway on a track |
| $h^{opp}$ | minimum opposite-direction (bidirectional) headway |
| $\theta^{\min}_{i,s}, \theta^{\max}_{i,s}$ | min / max dwell time of train $i$ at $s$ |
| $[\tau^{B}_{start}, \tau^{B}_{end}]$ | blockage time window on $K^B$ |
| $C^{canc}$ | cancellation penalty per train |
| $w_E$ | weight of energy in the objective |
| $R^{\max}_k$ | max number of trains that may use the opposite track on segment $k$ |
| $M_1, M_2, M_3$ | sufficiently large big-M constants |
| $T^{hor}$ | planning horizon |

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | actual departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $x^p_{i,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $p$ on segment $k$ |
| $y_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $r_{i,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted to the opposite track on segment $k$ |
| $w_{i,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses blocked segment $k$ **before** the blockage starts |
| $z_{i,j,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ enters segment $k$ before train $j$ (same physical track) |
| $o_{i,j,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if trains $i$ and $j$ share the same physical track on segment $k$ |
| $\delta_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | arrival delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $E_i$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | total energy consumption of train $i$ |

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; \underbrace{\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S} \delta_{i,s}}_{\text{total delay}} \;+\; \underbrace{C^{canc}\sum_{i \in T} y_i}_{\text{cancellation penalty}} \;+\; \underbrace{w_E \sum_{i \in T} E_i}_{\text{weighted energy}}
$$

## 5. Constraints

### (C1) Speed-profile selection (exactly one profile per operated segment)
$$
\sum_{p \in P} x^p_{i,k} \;=\; 1 - y_i, \qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; k \in K
$$

### (C2) Running-time coupling
$$
a_{i,k+1} \;\geq\; d_{i,k} \;+\; \sum_{p \in P} x^p_{i,k}\, t^p_k \;-\; M_1\, y_i, \qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; k \in K
$$

### (C3) Dwell-time bounds
$$
\theta^{\min}_{i,s} \;\leq\; d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \;\leq\; \theta^{\max}_{i,s} \;+\; M_1\, y_i, \qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (C4) Delay definition with cancellation relaxation
$$
\delta_{i,s} \;\geq\; a_{i,s} - \tau^a_{i,s} \;-\; M_1\, y_i, \qquad \delta_{i,s} \;\geq\; 0, \qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (C5) Cancellation: collapse times to 0 when train is cancelled
$$
a_{i,s} \;\leq\; T^{hor}\,(1 - y_i), \qquad d_{i,s} \;\leq\; T^{hor}\,(1 - y_i), \qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### (C6) Same-physical-track indicator (linearization of $o_{i,j,k} = 1 \Leftrightarrow r_{i,k} = r_{j,k}$)
$$
\begin{aligned}
o_{i,j,k} &\leq 1 - r_{i,k} + r_{j,k} \\
o_{i,j,k} &\leq 1 + r_{i,k} - r_{j,k} \\
o_{i,j,k} &\geq 1 - r_{i,k} - r_{j,k} \\
o_{i,j,k} &\geq r_{i,k} + r_{j,k} - 1
\end{aligned}
\qquad \forall\, i<j \in T,\; k \in K
$$

### (C7) Same-direction headway on shared physical track
$$
\begin{aligned}
a_{i,k+1} + h &\leq d_{j,k} + M_2\,(1 - z_{i,j,k}) + M_2\,(1 - o_{i,j,k}) + M_2\,(y_i + y_j) \\
a_{j,k+1} + h &\leq d_{i,k} + M_2\,z_{i,j,k} + M_2\,(1 - o_{i,j,k}) + M_2\,(y_i + y_j)
\end{aligned}
\qquad \forall\, i<j \in T,\; k \in K
$$

### (C8) Bidirectional conflict on a shared physical track (rerouted vs. opposite-direction train)
For $i \in T^+$, $j \in T^-$ (and symmetrically), on segment $k$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
a_{i,k+1} + h^{opp} &\leq a_{j,k} + M_3\,(1 - r_{i,k}) + M_3\,r_{j,k} + M_3\,(1 - o_{i,j,k}) + M_3\,(y_i + y_j) \\
a_{j,k} + h^{opp} &\leq a_{i,k+1} + M_3\,r_{i,k} + M_3\,(1 - r_{j,k}) + M_3\,(1 - o_{i,j,k}) + M_3\,(y_i + y_j)
\end{aligned}
$$
(Active only when one train is rerouted onto the track normally used by the opposite-direction train.)

### (C9) Disruption window — blocked segment is forbidden on the normal track during $[\tau^{B}_{start},\tau^{B}_{end}]$
For each $k \in K^B$ and $i \in T$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
a_{i,k+1} &\leq \tau^{B}_{start} + M_3\,(1 - w_{i,k}) + M_3\,r_{i,k} + M_3\,y_i \\
d_{i,k} &\geq \tau^{B}_{end} - M_3\,w_{i,k} - M_3\,r_{i,k} - M_3\,y_i \\
w_{i,k} &\leq 1 - r_{i,k} \\
w_{i,k} &\leq 1 - y_i
\end{aligned}
$$
**Interpretation:** if the train is **not** rerouted ($r_{i,k}=0$) and not cancelled ($y_i=0$), it must either finish before $\tau^{B}_{start}$ ($w_{i,k}=1$) or start after $\tau^{B}_{end}$ ($w_{i,k}=0$); if it **is** rerouted or cancelled, the constraint is relaxed.

### (C10) Energy consumption
$$
E_i \;=\; \sum_{k \in K}\sum_{p \in P} x^p_{i,k}\, e^p_k, \qquad \forall\, i \in T
$$

### (C11) Rerouting capacity on the opposite track
$$
\sum_{i \in T} r_{i,k} \;\leq\; R^{\max}_k, \qquad \forall\, k \in K
$$

### (C12) Optional rolling-stock / turnaround coupling
For each rolling-stock unit $u$ with turnaround time $\tau^{turn}_u$, introduce binary assignment variables $\rho_{i,u}$ linking successive trips:
$$
d_{i',1} \;\geq\; a_{i,|S|} + \tau^{turn}_u \;-\; M_1\,(y_i + y_{i'}), \qquad \forall\, (i,i') \text{ sharing unit } u
$$

### (C13) Variable domains
$$
a_{i,s},\, d_{i,s} \in [0,\, T^{hor}], \quad \delta_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad E_i \geq 0, \quad x^p_{i,k},\, y_i,\, r_{i,k},\, w_{i,k},\, z_{i,j,k},\, o_{i,j,k} \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

**Retiming.** Continuous variables $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}$ replace the scheduled times $\tau^a_{i,s}, \tau^d_{i,s}$. Delay $\delta_{i,s}$ is the deviation from schedule, penalized in the objective.

**Reordering.** Binary $z_{i,j,k}$ for every ordered pair $(i,j)$ and every segment $k$ enforces that exactly one ordering is chosen. Combined with (C7), this guarantees conflict-free (headway-respecting) sequencing on each shared track segment.

**Rerouting.** Binary $r_{i,k}$ decides whether train $i$ uses the opposite (normally counter-direction) track on segment $k$. The indicator $o_{i,j,k}$ (C6) ensures headway constraints (C7)–(C8) are enforced only when two trains actually share a physical track. Capacity (C11) limits simultaneous rerouting.

**Cancellation.** Binary $y_i$ allows a train to be removed from service at penalty $C^{canc}$. When $y_i = 1$, (C1) forces all profiles to 0, (C2) collapses running times, (C5) pins $a,d$ to 0, and (C4) removes the delay contribution.

**Speed-profile selection.** Discrete profiles $p \in P$ are chosen via $x^p_{i,k}$. (C1) enforces exactly one profile per operated segment. (C2) couples the chosen profile to the running time, and (C10) couples it to energy use — this is the **key link** between the rescheduling layer and the energy/speed layer.

**Disruption handling.** (C9) uses an auxiliary binary $w_{i,k}$ to linearize the "before-or-after" disjunction: a non-rerouted, non-cancelled train must clear the blocked segment before $\tau^{B}_{start}$ or enter it after $\tau^{B}_{end}$. Rerouted trains bypass the blockage entirely.

**Bidirectional conflicts.** (C8) handles the case where a rerouted train meets a counter-direction train on the same physical track, applying the larger headway $h^{opp}$.

**Big-M usage.** $M_1, M_2, M_3$ are chosen tight enough to preserve LP relaxation quality (e.g., $M_2 \approx T^{hor}$, $M_3 \approx T^{hor} + \tau^{B}_{end}$). Tightening via valid inequalities (e.g., precedence propagation, profile-based minimum traversal times) is recommended for computational tractability.

**Objective trade-off.** The three terms — delay, cancellation, weighted energy — allow the dispatcher to balance passenger impact, service preservation, and energy use. Setting $w_E = 0$ recovers a pure rescheduling model; setting $C^{canc} \to \infty$ forbids cancellation.

---

## 7. Assumptions

1. **Discrete speed profiles.** Each segment admits a finite set $P$ of pre-computed speed profiles, each with a fixed running time $t^p_k$ and energy $e^p_k$ (obtained from a lower-level train dynamics simulation).
2. **Single disruption window.** Exactly one partial blockage occurs on a single segment $k^* \in K^B$ during $[\tau^{B}_{start}, \tau^{B}_{end}]$.
3. **Double-track line.** Two parallel tracks exist; each direction normally uses its dedicated track. Rerouting allows a train to temporarily use the opposite track.
4. **Bidirectional headway.** When trains of opposite directions share a track, a larger safety headway $h^{opp} \geq h$ is required.
5. **Cancellation is terminal.** A cancelled train contributes no further service; its rolling stock may be reused subject to (C12).
6. **Fixed train routes.** Each train's sequence of stations is fixed; only the track assignment per segment may change.
7. **No-train-crossing assumption.** Trains do not overtake each other within a segment (reordering is between segments).
8. **Perfect information.** All parameters ($\tau^a, \tau^d, t^p_k, e^p_k$, etc.) are known deterministically.

Text:
# Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Sets

| Set | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| $T = \{1, \ldots, n\}$ | Set of trains |
| $S = \{1, \ldots, m\}$ | Set of stations (ordered along the line) |
| $S^{int}_i = S \setminus \{o_i, dest_i\}$ | Intermediate stations for train $i$ |
| $E = \{(s, s+1) : s \in S \setminus \{m\}\}$ | Set of track segments |
| $E^{up}, E^{dn}$ | Up-track and down-track segments |
| $K = \{0, 1, \ldots, p\}$ | Space discretization breakpoints |
| $I = \{1, \ldots, q\}$ | Time discretization intervals |
| $E_d \subseteq E^{up}$ | Set of disrupted segments |
| $T^{up} = \{i \in T : \text{dir}_i = +1\}$ | Up-direction trains |
| $T^{dn} = \{i \in T : \text{dir}_i = -1\}$ | Down-direction trains |

## 2. Parameters

| Parameter | Description | Unit |
|-----------|-------------|------|
| $L_e$ | Length of segment $e$ | km |
| $\Delta x$ | Space discretization step | km |
| $\Delta t$ | Time discretization step | min |
| $v_{\max}$ | Maximum allowable speed | km/h |
| $a_{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration | km/h² |
| $b_{\max}$ | Maximum deceleration | km/h² |
| $\tau_h$ | Minimum headway time | min |
| $\tau_d^{\min}, \tau_d^{\max}$ | Min/max dwell times | min |
| $T_{dis}^{s}, T_{dis}^{e}$ | Disruption start/end times | min |
| $a^{plan}_{i,s}, d^{plan}_{i,s}$ | Planned arrival/departure times | min |
| $\text{dir}_i \in \{+1, -1\}$ | Direction of train $i$ | — |
| $c_{delay}$ | Cost weight for delay | $/min |
| $c_{energy}$ | Cost weight for energy | $/kWh |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Energy coefficients | various |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (big-M) | — |

**Assumption A1:** All trains have identical kinematic parameters (relaxable by indexing parameters by $i$).
**Assumption A2:** Uniform space discretization $\Delta x = L_e / p$ across all segments.
**Assumption A3:** Disruption affects only the up-track during $[T_{dis}^s, T_{dis}^e]$.

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ (min) |
| $d_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ (min) |
| $\delta_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $s$ (min) |
| $y_{i,e}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $e$ |
| $w_{i,e}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted on segment $e$ |
| $z_{i,j,e}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $e$ |
| $v_{i,e,k}$ | $\geq 0$ | Speed of train $i$ at breakpoint $k$ of segment $e$ (km/h) |
| $t_{i,e,k}$ | $\geq 0$ | Time when train $i$ passes breakpoint $k$ of segment $e$ (min) |
| $E_i$ | $\geq 0$ | Total energy consumption of train $i$ (kWh) |
| $\phi_{i,e,k}$ | $\geq 0$ | Auxiliary: $v_{i,e,k} \cdot (t_{i,e,k+1} - t_{i,e,k})$ (McCormick) |
| $\eta_{i,e,k}$ | $\geq 0$ | Auxiliary: $v_{i,e,k}^2$ (piecewise linear) |
| $\theta_{i,e,k}$ | $\geq 0$ | Auxiliary: $v_{i,e,k}^3$ (piecewise linear) |

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = c_{delay} \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \delta_{i,s} \; + \; c_{energy} \sum_{i \in T} E_i
$$

The first term penalizes total delay (deviation from planned arrival times); the second term penalizes total energy consumption across all trains.

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Dwell Time Constraints

$$
\tau_d^{\min} \leq d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \leq \tau_d^{\max}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S^{int}_i
$$

### 5.2 Delay Definition

$$
\delta_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} - a^{plan}_{i,s}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\delta_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### 5.3 Speed–Time Relationship (McCormick Linearization)

The trapezoidal rule gives:
$$
2\Delta x = (v_{i,e,k} + v_{i,e,k+1}) \cdot (t_{i,e,k+1} - t_{i,e,k})
$$

Introduce $\phi_{i,e,k} = v_{i,e,k} \cdot (t_{i,e,k+1} - t_{i,e,k})$ with bounds $v \in [0, v_{\max}]$ and $\Delta t \in [\Delta t_{\min}, \Delta t_{\max}]$. The McCormick envelopes are:

$$
\phi_{i,e,k} \geq 0 \cdot (t_{i,e,k+1} - t_{i,e,k}) + \Delta t_{\min} \cdot v_{i,e,k} - 0 \cdot \Delta t_{\min}
$$
$$
\phi_{i,e,k} \geq v_{\max} \cdot (t_{i,e,k+1} - t_{i,e,k}) + \Delta t_{\max} \cdot v_{i,e,k} - v_{\max} \cdot \Delta t_{\max}
$$
$$
\phi_{i,e,k} \leq v_{\max} \cdot (t_{i,e,k+1} - t_{i,e,k}) + \Delta t_{\min} \cdot v_{i,e,k} - v_{\max} \cdot \Delta t_{\min}
$$
$$
\phi_{i,e,k} \leq 0 \cdot (t_{i,e,k+1} - t_{i,e,k}) + \Delta t_{\max} \cdot v_{i,e,k} - 0 \cdot \Delta t_{\max}
$$

The trapezoidal constraint becomes:

$$
2\Delta x = \phi_{i,e,k} + \phi_{i,e,k+1}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; e \in E,\; k \in K \setminus \{p\}
$$

### 5.4 Speed Limits

$$
0 \leq v_{i,e,k} \leq v_{\max}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; e \in E,\; k \in K
$$

### 5.5 Acceleration / Deceleration Limits

$$
v_{i,e,k+1} - v_{i,e,k} \leq a_{\max} \cdot (t_{i,e,k+1} - t_{i,e,k}), \quad \forall i, e, k
$$
$$
v_{i,e,k} - v_{i,e,k+1} \leq b_{\max} \cdot (t_{i,e,k+1} - t_{i,e,k}), \quad \forall i, e, k
$$

### 5.6 Arrival / Departure Time Consistency

Let $e_s^{in}$ denote the segment entering station $s$ and $e_s^{out}$ the segment leaving station $s$:

$$
a_{i,s} = t_{i, e_s^{in}, p}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{o_i\}
$$
$$
d_{i,s} = t_{i, e_s^{out}, 0}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{dest_i\}
$$

### 5.7 Segment Usage and Rerouting Logic

**Case 1:** $\text{dir}_i = +1$ (up-train) and $e \in E^{up}$:
$$
y_{i,e} + w_{i,e} = 1
$$

**Case 2:** $\text{dir}_i = -1$ (down-train) and $e \in E^{dn}$:
$$
y_{i,e} + w_{i,e} = 1
$$

**Case 3:** $\text{dir}_i = +1$ and $e \in E^{dn}$ (only via rerouting):
$$
y_{i,e} = w_{i,e}
$$

**Case 4:** $\text{dir}_i = -1$ and $e \in E^{up}$ (only via rerouting):
$$
y_{i,e} = w_{i,e}
$$

### 5.8 Disruption Constraints

For disrupted segments $e \in E_d$, trains cannot traverse them during $[T_{dis}^s, T_{dis}^e]$. Using big-M with auxiliary binary $\rho_{i,e} \in \{0,1\}$:

$$
t_{i,e,k} \leq T_{dis}^s + M(1 - y_{i,e}) + M\rho_{i,e}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; e \in E_d,\; k \in K
$$
$$
t_{i,e,k} \geq T_{dis}^e - M(1 - y_{i,e}) - M(1 - \rho_{i,e}), \quad \forall i \in T,\; e \in E_d,\; k \in K
$$

### 5.9 Conflict Resolution — Same Direction

For any pair of trains $i, j$ with $\text{dir}_i = \text{dir}_j$ sharing segment $e$:

$$
z_{i,j,e} + z_{j,i,e} = 1, \quad \forall i < j,\; e \in E
$$
$$
t_{j,e,0} - t_{i,e,p} \geq \tau_h - M(1 - z_{i,j,e}), \quad \forall i \neq j,\; e
$$
$$
t_{i,e,0} - t_{j,e,p} \geq \tau_h - M(1 - z_{j,i,e}), \quad \forall i \neq j,\; e
$$

### 5.10 Conflict Resolution — Bidirectional (Shared Track)

For $i \in T^{up}, j \in T^{dn}$ sharing segment $e$ (via rerouting):

$$
z_{i,j,e} + z_{j,i,e} = 1
$$
$$
t_{j,e,0} - t_{i,e,p} \geq \tau_h - M(1 - z_{i,j,e}), \quad \forall i \in T^{up}, j \in T^{dn}, e
$$
$$
t_{i,e,0} - t_{j,e,p} \geq \tau_h - M(1 - z_{j,i,e}), \quad \forall i \in T^{up}, j \in T^{dn}, e
$$

### 5.11 Energy Consumption (Piecewise Linear Approximation)

**Linearization of $v^2$:** Partition $[0, v_{\max}]$ into $N_2$ intervals with breakpoints $v^{(0)}=0 < v^{(1)} < \ldots < v^{(N_2)}=v_{\max}$. Introduce SOS2 variables $\lambda^{(r)}_{i,e,k}$:

$$
\eta_{i,e,k} = \sum_{r=0}^{N_2} (v^{(r)})^2 \cdot \lambda^{(r)}_{i,e,k}
$$
$$
v_{i,e,k} = \sum_{r=0}^{N_2} v^{(r)} \cdot \lambda^{(r)}_{i,e,k}
$$
$$
\sum_{r=0}^{N_2} \lambda^{(r)}_{i,e,k} = 1, \quad \lambda^{(r)}_{i,e,k} \geq 0, \quad \text{SOS2}
$$

**Linearization of $v^3$:** Similarly with breakpoints $(v^{(r)})^3$:

$$
\theta_{i,e,k} = \sum_{r=0}^{N_3} (v^{(r)})^3 \cdot \mu^{(r)}_{i,e,k}
$$
$$
v_{i,e,k} = \sum_{r=0}^{N_3} v^{(r)} \cdot \mu^{(r)}_{i,e,k}
$$
$$
\sum_{r=0}^{N_3} \mu^{(r)}_{i,e,k} = 1, \quad \mu^{(r)}_{i,e,k} \geq 0, \quad \text{SOS2}
$$

**Total energy:**
$$
E_i = \sum_{e \in E} \sum_{k \in K} \left[ \alpha \cdot \Delta x + \beta \cdot \eta_{i,e,k} + \gamma \cdot \theta_{i,e,k} \right], \quad \forall i \in T
$$

### 5.12 Initial and Boundary Conditions

$$
t_{i, e_0, 0} = d_{i, o_i}, \quad \forall i \in T
$$
$$
t_{i, e_{last}, p} = a_{i, dest_i}, \quad \forall i \in T
$$

### 5.13 Continuity Between Segments

For consecutive segments $e$ and $e'$ sharing station $s$:
$$
t_{i, e, p} = a_{i,s}, \quad t_{i, e', 0} = d_{i,s}
$$

### 5.14 Variable Domains

$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, t_{i,e,k} \geq 0
$$
$$
v_{i,e,k} \in [0, v_{\max}]
$$
$$
\delta_{i,s}, E_i, \eta_{i,e,k}, \theta_{i,e,k}, \phi_{i,e,k} \geq 0
$$
$$
y_{i,e}, w_{i,e}, z_{i,j,e}, \rho_{i,e} \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 6. Summary of Linearization Techniques

| Nonlinear Element | Technique | Section |
|-------------------|-----------|---------|
| $v \cdot \Delta t$ (speed-time) | McCormick envelopes | 5.3 |
| $v^2$ in energy | Piecewise linear (SOS2) | 5.11 |
| $v^3$ in energy | Piecewise linear (SOS2) | 5.11 |
| Disjunctive (if-then) for disruption | Big-M with auxiliary binary | 5.8 |
| Ordering for conflicts | Big-M with binary $z_{i,j,e}$ | 5.9, 5.10 |

## 7. Key Assumptions Summary

- **A1:** Identical kinematic parameters across trains (relaxable by indexing).
- **A2:** Uniform space discretization $\Delta x$ across all segments.
- **A3:** Disruption affects only up-track during the specified window.
- **A4:** Rerouting is permitted only to the immediately opposite track.
- **A5:** Dwell times are bounded but not fixed; the optimizer chooses within $[\tau_d^{\min}, \tau_d^{\max}]$.
- **A6:** Energy model uses tractive effort coefficients $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ that are constant (no regenerative braking modeled).
- **A7:** Minimum headway $\tau_h$ is the same for same-direction and bidirectional traffic (relaxable).
- **A8:** Trains cannot pass each other on the same track segment (ordering enforced via $z_{i,j,e}$).
- **A9:** The big-M constant is chosen as $M = \sum_e L_e / v_{\min} + T_{horizon}$, sufficiently large to not constrain feasible solutions.

## 8. Model Size Estimate

For $n$ trains, $m$ stations, $p$ breakpoints per segment, and $N_2, N_3$ piecewise segments:

- **Binary variables:** $O(n \cdot |E|) + O(n^2 \cdot |E|)$ (segment usage + ordering)
- **Continuous variables:** $O(n \cdot |E| \cdot p)$ (speeds and times) + $O(n \cdot |E| \cdot p \cdot (N_2 + N_3))$ (SOS2 auxiliaries)
- **Constraints:** $O(n \cdot |E| \cdot p)$ (kinematic) + $O(n^2 \cdot |E|)$ (conflicts)

This MILP is solvable by modern solvers (CPLEX, Gurobi) for moderate instances; for large-scale problems, decomposition methods (e.g., Benders, column generation) or heuristic/metaheuristic approaches are recommended.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

Below is a complete mixed-integer linear programming formulation. The model jointly decides **retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation** (TRP layer) and **speed profiles** (TSMP layer) on a discretized space–time network, while explicitly handling bidirectional conflicts caused by rerouting onto the opposite track during a partial blockage.

---

## 1 Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $I$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i,j$ |
| $B$ | Set of track blocks (segments between stations), indexed by $b$ |
| $S \subseteq B$ | Set of station-blocks, indexed by $s$ |
| $T = \{1,2,\dots,|T|\}$ | Set of discrete time steps, indexed by $t$ |
| $K = \{1,2\}$ | Tracks within each block: $k=1$ nominal direction, $k=2$ opposite direction |
| $D_i \in \{+1,-1\}$ | Nominal running direction of train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{O}(i),\mathcal{D}(i)$ | Origin and destination station of train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{N}^+(b),\mathcal{N}^-(b)$ | Successor and predecessor blocks of $b$ |

---

## 2 Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ (m) |
| $\Delta t$ | Length of a time step (s) |
| $v^{\max}_b, v^{\min}_b$ | Maximum/minimum allowable speed on block $b$ (m/s) |
| $a^{\max}, d^{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration (m/s²) |
| $\tau^{\min}_s$ | Minimum dwell time at station $s$ (s) |
| $\tau^{hd}$ | Minimum headway between consecutive trains (s) |
| $\bar t^0_i, \bar t^F_i$ | Scheduled departure/arrival time of train $i$ |
| $[\Omega^-_b, \Omega^+_b]$ | Disruption time window on block $b$ (s) |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Davis-type resistance coefficients: $f(v)=\alpha+\beta v+\gamma v^2$ (kN/ton) |
| $m_i$ | Mass of train $i$ (t) |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3$ | Weights of delay, energy, and cancellation in objective |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (Big-M) |
| $\varepsilon$ | A small positive constant |

**Assumptions (marked):**
- (A1) The track is double-track; each block $b$ has two parallel tracks, one per nominal direction.
- (A2) Time and space are uniformly discretized with steps $\Delta t$ and $L_b$.
- (A3) Energy consumption is approximated by the Davis formula; the quadratic term is linearized via a piecewise-linear (PWL) approximation with breakpoints $v^\ell$, $\ell=1,\dots,L$.
- (A4) Trains are homogeneous in traction/braking characteristics; only mass differs.
- (A5) A cancelled train releases all its resources and incurs a fixed penalty.

---

## 3 Decision Variables

### 3.1 Discrete (TRP layer)

$$
x_{i,b,t}\in\{0,1\} \quad \text{1 if train } i \text{ occupies block } b \text{ at time } t
$$
$$
u_{i,b,k,t}\in\{0,1\} \quad \text{1 if train } i \text{ uses track } k \text{ of block } b \text{ at time } t
$$
$$
y_{i,j,b}\in\{0,1\} \quad \text{1 if train } i \text{ exits block } b \text{ before train } j \text{ enters}
$$
$$
z_i\in\{0,1\} \quad \text{1 if train } i \text{ is cancelled}
$$
$$
\rho_{i,b}\in\{0,1\} \quad \text{1 if train } i \text{ is rerouted onto the opposite track on block } b
$$

### 3.2 Continuous (TSMP layer)

$$
v_{i,b,t}\ge 0 \quad \text{speed of train } i \text{ on block } b \text{ at time } t \text{ (m/s)}
$$
$$
p_{i,b,t}\in[0,L_b] \quad \text{position of train } i \text{ within block } b \text{ at time } t \text{ (m)}
$$
$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}\ge 0 \quad \text{actual arrival / departure time of train } i \text{ at station } s
$$
$$
\Delta_{i,s}\ge 0 \quad \text{delay of train } i \text{ at station } s \text{ (s)}
$$
$$
e_i\ge 0 \quad \text{traction energy of train } i \text{ (kWh)}
$$
$$
e^+_{i,b,t,\ell}\ge 0 \quad \text{PWL auxiliary variable for the } v^2 \text{ term at breakpoint } \ell
$$

---

## 4 Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; w_1\!\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S}\Delta_{i,s} \;+\; w_2\!\sum_{i\in I} e_i \;+\; w_3\!\sum_{i\in I} z_i \tag{Obj}
$$

The first term penalises total passenger delay, the second term penalises total traction energy, and the third term penalises cancellations.

---

## 5 Constraints

### 5.1 Linkage between occupancy and track choice

$$
u_{i,b,1,t}+u_{i,b,2,t}=x_{i,b,t}\quad \forall i,b,t \tag{1}
$$

$$
u_{i,b,k,t}\le 1-z_i \quad \forall i,b,k,t \tag{2}
$$

### 5.2 Position progression (space–time kinematics)

$$
p_{i,b,t}\;\ge\; p_{i,b,t-1}+v_{i,b,t-1}\,\Delta t - M(1-x_{i,b,t-1})-M(1-x_{i,b,t}) \quad \forall i,b,t \tag{3}
$$

$$
p_{i,b,t}\;\le\; p_{i,b,t-1}+v_{i,b,t-1}\,\Delta t + M(1-x_{i,b,t-1})+M(1_{i,b,t}) \quad \forall i,b,t \tag{4}
$$

$$
p_{i,b,t}\;\le\; L_b\,x_{i,b,t} \quad \forall i,b,t \tag{5}
$$

$$
p_{i,b,t}\;\ge\; 0 \quad \forall i,b,t \tag{6}
$$

Equations (3)–(4) ensure that the position evolves consistently with the speed when the train is in the block; (5)–(6) bound the position.

### 5.3 Speed limits and kinematic (acceleration) limits

$$
v^{\min}_b\,x_{i,b,t}\;\le\; v_{i,b,t}\;\le\; v^{\max}_b\,x_{i,b,t} \quad \forall i,b,t \tag{7}
$$

$$
v_{i,b,t}-v_{i,b,t-1}\;\le\; a^{\max}\Delta t + M(2-x_{i,b,t}-x_{i,b,t-1}) \quad \forall i,b,t \tag{8}
$$

$$
v_{i,b,t-1}-v_{i,b,t}\;\le\; d^{\max}\Delta t + M(2-x_{i,b,t}-x_{i,b,t-1}) \quad \forall i,b,t \tag{9}
$$

### 5.4 Block and track capacity (conflict-free operation)

**Single occupancy per track:**
$$
\sum_{i\in I} u_{i,b,k,t}\;\le\; 1 \quad \forall b,k,t \tag{10}
$$

**At most one train per block (regardless of track) when no rerouting occurs:**
$$
\sum_{i\in I} x_{i,b,t}\;\le\; 1+\sum_{i\in I}\rho_{i,b} \quad \forall b,t \tag{11}
$$
(Equation (11) allows at most two trains in block $b$ at time $t$ only if at least one of them is rerouted onto the opposite track.)

**Bidirectional conflict (rerouting):** if a train $i$ with $D_i=+1$ and a train $j$ with $D_j=-1$ both occupy block $b$ at time $t$, they must use opposite tracks:
$$
u_{i,b,1,t}+u_{j,b,1,t}\le 1 \quad \forall i,j\in I,\; D_i=+1,\;D_j=-1,\;b,t \tag{12}
$$
$$
u_{i,b,2,t}+u_{j,b,2,t}\le 1 \quad \forall i,j\in I,\; D_i=+1,\;D_j=-1,\;b,t \tag{13}
$$

### 5.5 Disruption (partial blockage) constraints

The blocked side of block $b$ is unavailable during $[\Omega^-_b,\Omega^+_b]$. Trains with $D_i$ matching the blocked side must either reroute or wait:

$$
\sum_{t\in[\Omega^-_b,\Omega^+_b]} u_{i,b,k_b^{\text{blocked}},t}\;\le\; M\,\rho_{i,b}+M\,z_i \quad \forall i,b,\;k_b^{\text{blocked}}= \tfrac{1+D_i}{2}\cdot 2 \tag{14}
$$

(If $\rho_{i,b}=0$ and $z_i=0$, train $i$ cannot use the blocked track during the window.)

$$
\rho_{i,b}\;\le\; 1-z_i \quad \forall i,b \tag{15}
$$

$$
\sum_{b\in B}\rho_{i,b}\;\le\; \bar R_i \quad \forall i \tag{16}
$$
where $\bar R_i$ is the maximum number of reroutings allowed for train $i$ (Assumption A6).

### 5.6 Train ordering and headway

For every pair of trains $i,j$ that both use block $b$:
$$
y_{i,j,b}+y_{j,i,b}=1 \quad \forall i\neq j,\;b \tag{17}
$$

$$
\sum_{t} t\,x_{i,b,t}\;<\;\sum_{t} t\,x_{j,b,t}-M(1-y_{i,j,b}) \quad \forall i\neq j,\;b \tag{18}
$$

(Linearised with Big-M as)
$$
\sum_{t} t\,x_{i,b,t}+M(1-y_{i,j,b})\;\le\;\sum_{t} t\,x_{j,b,t} \quad \forall i\neq j,\;b \tag{19}
$$

**Headway at stations:**
$$
d_{j,s}\;\ge\; d_{i,s}+\tau^{hd}-M(3-y_{i,j,s-1}-y_{i,j,s}-\theta_{ij}) \quad \forall i\neq j,\;s \tag{20}
$$
where $\theta_{ij}=1$ if trains $i,j$ share the same platform track (otherwise 0).

### 5.7 Dwell time and station timing

$$
d_{i,s}\;\ge\; a_{i,s}+\tau^{\min}_s \quad \forall i,s \tag{21}
$$

$$
a_{i,s}\;=\;\sum_{t} t\,x_{i,s,t} \quad \forall i,s \tag{22}
$$

$$
d_{i,s}\;=\;\sum_{t} t\,x_{i,s,t}+\tau^{\min}_s\,x_{i,s,t^{*}} \quad \forall i,s \tag{23}
$$

(where $t^{*}$ is the last time step of occupancy of station block $s$ by train $i$.)

### 5.8 Delay definition and bounds

$$
\Delta_{i,s}\;\ge\; a_{i,s}-\bar t^{F}_{i,s} \quad \forall i,s \tag{24}
$$

$$
\Delta_{i,s}\;\ge\; d_{i,s}-\bar t^{0}_{i,s} \quad \forall i,s \tag{25}
$$

$$
\Delta_{i,s}\;\le\; \Delta^{\max} \quad \forall i,s \tag{26}
$$

### 5.9 Initial and final conditions

$$
\sum_{b\in B} x_{i,b,1}=1-z_i \quad \forall i \tag{27}
$$

$$
\sum_{b\in B} x_{i,b,|T|}=1-z_i \quad \forall i \tag{28}
$$

$$
\sum_{t\in T} x_{i,b,t}\;\ge\; 1-z_i \quad \forall i,b \tag{29}
$$
(every non-cancelled train traverses every block on its path).

### 5.10 Energy consumption (linearised Davis formula)

Using PWL approximation of $v^2$ with breakpoints $v^\ell$:
$$
v_{i,b,t}^2 \;\approx\; \sum_{\ell=1}^{L} \lambda^\ell_{i,b,t}\,v^\ell, \qquad
\sum_{\ell}\lambda^\ell_{i,b,t}=1,\;\lambda^\ell_{i,b,t}\ge 0 \tag{30}
$$

$$
v_{i,b,t}=\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\lambda^\ell_{i,b,t}\,v^\ell \quad \forall i,b,t \tag{31}
$$

$$
e_i \;=\; \frac{\Delta t}{3.6\times 10^6}\sum_{b,t} m_i\!\left(\alpha+\beta v_{i,b,t}+\gamma\!\sum_{\ell}\lambda^\ell_{i,b,t}\,v^\ell\right) x_{i,b,t} \quad \forall i \tag{32}
$$

(Conversion factor $3.6\times 10^6$ converts $(\text{m/s})\cdot\text{s}$ to kJ, then to kWh.)

### 5.11 Coupling between TRP and TSMP

The following constraints ensure that the chosen discrete rescheduling decisions are *executable* by the continuous speed profile:

$$
v_{i,b,t}\;\ge\; v^{\min}_b\,x_{i,b,t} \quad \forall i,b,t \tag{33}
$$

$$
p_{i,b,t}\;\ge\; p_{i,b,t-1}+\varepsilon\,x_{i,b,t-1} \quad \forall i,b,t \tag{34}
$$

(Strict forward progress whenever the train occupies a block.)

$$
\sum_{b\in B}\sum_{t\in T} v_{i,b,t}\,\Delta t \;\ge\; (1-z_i)\sum_{b\in \mathcal{P}(i)} L_b \quad \forall i \tag{35}
$$
where $\mathcal{P}(i)$ is the set of blocks on the path of train $i$ (total distance must be covered).

### 5.12 Rerouting feasibility

A train can be rerouted onto the opposite track only on a contiguous set of blocks within the disrupted area:
$$
\rho_{i,b}-\rho_{i,b-1}\;\le\;\rho_{i,b+1}+M(1-\rho_{i,b}) \quad \forall i,b \tag{36}
$$

$$
\sum_{b\in B}\rho_{i,b}\;\le\; |B^{dis}| \quad \forall i \tag{37}
$$
where $B^{dis}$ is the set of disrupted blocks.

---

## 6 Summary of the MILP

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& w_1\!\sum_{i,s}\Delta_{i,s}+w_2\!\sum_i e_i+w_3\!\sum_i z_i \\
\text{s.t.}\;& \text{(1)–(37)} \\
& x_{i,b,t},u_{i,b,k,t},y_{i,j,b},z_i,\rho_{i,b}\in\{0,1\} \\
& v_{i,b,t},p_{i,b,t},a_{i,s},d_{i,s},\Delta_{i,s},e_i,\lambda^\ell_{i,b,t}\ge 0
\end{aligned}
$$

The model is a **mixed-integer linear program** because:
- All quadratic terms ($v^2$) are replaced by the PWL approximation (30)–(31), which is exact at the breakpoints and conservative in between;
- All disjunctions (e.g. ordering, rerouting) are linearised using Big-M;
- All kinematic relations are written as linear inequalities through (3)–(9).

---

## 7 Key Modelling Assumptions (Recap)

| # | Assumption |
|---|---|
| A1 | Double-track line; each block has two parallel tracks. |
| A2 | Uniform time and space discretisation. |
| A3 | Davis formula with PWL approximation of $v^2$. |
| A4 | Homogeneous traction/braking; only mass varies. |
| A5 | Cancelled trains release all resources and pay a fixed penalty. |
| A6 | Each train may be rerouted at most $\bar R_i$ times. |
| A7 | A blocked track is unavailable only during $[\Omega^-_b,\Omega^+_b]$; outside this window normal operation resumes. |
| A8 | Rerouting is only allowed within the disrupted area $B^{dis}$. |
| A9 | Bidirectional conflicts are resolved by enforcing opposite-track usage (12)–(13). |
| A10 | Headway is enforced at stations; running headway is absorbed by single-track occupancy (10). |

This MILP simultaneously yields a **conflict-free rescheduled timetable** (arrival/departure times, train order, routes, cancellations) and the **corresponding executable speed profiles** that minimise a weighted sum of passenger delay, traction energy, and service cancellations, under partial segment blockages with bidirectional rerouting.

Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.

Text:
# MILP: Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Infrastructure Feasibility

## 1. Problem setting and assumptions

**Setting.** A railway operator must reschedule rolling stock (train units) over a set of passenger trips after a disruption. Rolling stock may be rerouted, cancelled, or recombined at stations; additionally, shunting movements at two major stations (Utrecht Centraal, Rotterdam Centraal) may be performed, but only if the station infrastructure (tracks, routes) allows them. Short delays (a few minutes) of passenger trains are allowed to create shunting windows.

**Assumptions (marked where invented):**
- (A1) The timetable is fixed; only rolling stock assignments and shunting movements change. *(Assumption: no timetable adjustment beyond small delays.)*
- (A2) Each train unit type has a fixed number of carriages and seats; composition changes en route are only possible at stations equipped for them.
- (A3) Shunting feasibility is checked per station via a track-occupancy model; a shunting movement occupies one track section for a given time window.
- (A4) Delays of at most Δ = 5 minutes may be imposed on passenger trains to enable shunting; these are absorbed by timetable buffers.
- (A5) Shunting drivers are always available. *(Assumption.)*
- (A6) All costs, capacities and times are deterministic and known.

## 2. Sets and parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of scheduled passenger trips |
| $S$ | set of stations (with $\bar S \subseteq S$ the shunting-capable stations) |
| $V$ | set of train unit types (e.g. VIRM-4, VIRM-6, ICM-4) |
| $A$ | set of arcs $(i,j)$: a train unit can go from trip $i$ (or source $\sigma$) to trip $j$ (or sink $\tau$) at a station, compatible in time and place |
| $A^s$ | set of shunting arcs at station $s \in \bar S$ |
| $c_v$ | cost per km (or fixed cost) of train unit type $v$ |
| $n_v$ | number of carriages of type $v$; $k_v$ seats |
| $d_t$ | required number of carriages on trip $t$; $p_t$ expected passengers |
| $M$ | large constant |
| $K^s$ | set of tracks at station $s$ |
| $I$ | set of shunting movements (each $i \in I$ has station $s(i)$, track window $[a_i, b_i]$, duration $\ell_i$) |
| $\Theta$ | set of ordered pairs of shunting movements at the same station that cannot overlap on the same track |
| $P$ | set of passenger trains whose route may conflict with a shunting movement |

## 3. Decision variables

**Composition variables (rolling stock):**
- $x_{ijv} \in \{0,1\}$: a train unit of type $v$ traverses arc $(i,j) \in A$ (with $i,j \in T \cup \{\sigma,\tau\}$).
- $y_{tv} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: number of units of type $v$ on trip $t$.
- $z_t \in \{0,1\}$: trip $t$ is cancelled.

**Shunting/infrastructure variables:**
- $u_i \in \{0,1\}$: shunting movement $i \in I$ is performed.
- $w_{ik} \in \{0,1\}$: shunting movement $i$ uses track $k \in K^{s(i)}$.
- $o_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: movements $i,j$ with $i \prec j$ occupy the same track with $i$ before $j$ (ordering variable).
- $\delta_p \ge 0$: delay (minutes) imposed on passenger train $p \in P$.

## 4. Objective function

Minimize a weighted sum of operational cost, carriage shortage, cancellation, deviation from plan, and delay:

$$
\min \; \underbrace{\sum_{(i,j)\in A}\sum_{v\in V} c_v\, d_{ij}\, x_{ijv}}_{\text{operational cost}}
\;+\; \alpha \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T} \Big(d_t - \sum_{v} n_v y_{tv}\Big)^{+}}_{\text{carriage shortage}}
\;+\; \beta \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T} z_t}_{\text{cancellations}}
\;+\; \gamma \underbrace{\sum_{(i,j)\in A}\sum_{v\in V} \big|x^0_{ijv} - x_{ijv}\big|}_{\text{deviation from original plan}}
\;+\; \eta \underbrace{\sum_{p\in P}\delta_p}_{\text{delays}}
$$

Linearized: introduce $g_{ijv} \ge |x^0_{ijv}-x_{ijv}|$ with $g_{ijv} \ge x_{ijv}-x^0_{ijv}$, $g_{ijv}\ge x^0_{ijv}-x_{ijv}$; shortage via slack $s_t \ge 0$: $s_t \ge d_t - \sum_v n_v y_{tv}$.

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Flow conservation** for each type $v$ and node $i \in T\cup\{\sigma,\tau\}$:
$$
\sum_{j:(i,j)\in A} x_{ijv} - \sum_{j:(j,i)\in A} x_{jiv} = b_{iv}, \qquad \forall i, v
$$
with $b_{\sigma v} = $ available units of type $v$, $b_{\tau v} = -b_{\sigma v}$, $b_{tv}=0$.

**(C2) Composition consistency:**
$$
\sum_{i:(i,t)\in A} x_{itv} = y_{tv} = \sum_{j:(t,j)\in A} x_{tjv}, \qquad \forall t\in T,\ v\in V
$$

**(C3) Carriage demand (or cancellation):**
$$
\sum_{v\in V} n_v\, y_{tv} + s_t \ge d_t (1 - z_t), \qquad \forall t\in T
$$

**(C4) Seat capacity (soft, penalized):**
$$
\sum_{v\in V} k_v\, y_{tv} \ge p_t (1-z_t) - e_t, \quad e_t \ge 0 \ \text{(excess passengers, penalized)}
$$

**(C5) Composition change limits:** at most $r_t$ coupled/decoupled operations per trip $t$:
$$
\sum_{v} y_{tv} - \sum_{v} \sum_{i:(i,t)\in A} x_{itv} \le r_t, \qquad \forall t \quad (\text{and symmetrically for departures})
$$

**(C6) Shunting selection and track assignment:**
$$
\sum_{k\in K^{s(i)}} w_{ik} = u_i, \qquad \forall i\in I
$$

**(C7) No track overlap between shunting movements** on the same track (for conflicting pairs $(i,j)\in\Theta$):
$$
w_{ik} + w_{jk} \le 1 + o_{ij} + o_{ji}, \qquad \forall (i,j)\in\Theta,\ k\in K^{s(i)}
$$
$$
o_{ij} + o_{ji} \le 1, \qquad \forall (i,j)\in\Theta
$$
with ordering enforced by time (linearized big-M):
$$
t_j \ge t_i + \ell_i - M(1 - o_{ij}), \qquad t_i \ge t_j + \ell_j - M(1 - o_{ji})
$$
where $t_i$ is the (flexible) start time of shunting movement $i$ within its window $a_i \le t_i \le b_i - \ell_i$.

**(C8) Shunting–passenger train conflicts:** if shunting movement $i$ uses track $k$ and passenger train $p$ occupies track $k$ at time window $[a_p, b_p]$, then either the shunt is moved in time or train $p$ is delayed:
$$
w_{ik} \le 1 - \text{conflict}(t_i,\, p, k) + \delta_p / \Delta, \qquad \forall i, k, p \text{ conflicting}
$$
implemented via big-M timing constraints:
$$
t_i + \ell_i \le a_p + \delta_p + M(1 - w_{ik} + q_{ip}), \qquad
t_i \ge b_p + \delta_p - M(1 - w_{ik} + 1 - q_{ip})
$$
with binary $q_{ip}$ choosing "shunt before train" or "shunt after train".

**(C9) Delay bound:**
$$
0 \le \delta_p \le \Delta, \qquad \forall p\in P \quad (\Delta = 5 \text{ min, assumption A4})
$$

**(C10) Linking rolling stock and shunting:** a shunting movement $i$ may only be performed if its associated rolling stock arc is used:
$$
u_i \le \sum_{v} x_{\text{arc}(i),v}, \qquad \forall i \in I
$$

**(C11) Combinatorial Benders cuts (iterative framework).** Let $I^\pi \subseteq I$ be a set of shunting movements proposed by the composition model that the infrastructure model proved infeasible in combination. Add the no-good cut:
$$
\sum_{i \in I^\pi} u_i \le |I^\pi| - 1
$$
These cuts are generated lazily: solve the composition model, test feasibility of the proposed shunt set with the infrastructure feasibility subproblem, and add cuts until all proposed shunts are feasible.

## 6. Complete model summary

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min\ & \sum_{(i,j),v} c_v d_{ij}x_{ijv} + \alpha\sum_t s_t + \beta\sum_t z_t + \gamma\sum_{(i,j),v} g_{ijv} + \eta\sum_p \delta_p \\
\text{s.t. } & \text{(C1)–(C11)},\\
& x_{ijv}, z_t, u_i, w_{ik}, o_{ij}, q_{ip} \in \{0,1\};\quad y_{tv}\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0};\quad s_t, e_t, \delta_p, t_i, g_{ijv}\ge 0.
\end{aligned}
$$

## 7. Solution approach (as in the paper)

1. **Master (composition model):** solve (C1)–(C6), (C10) plus accumulated cuts (C11) → proposes shunting movements.
2. **Subproblem (infrastructure feasibility):** given fixed $u_i$, solve the track-occupancy feasibility model (C7)–(C9). If infeasible, return a minimal infeasible subset $I^\pi$ and add the no-good cut.
3. **Iterate** until the proposed plan is infrastructure-feasible. The exact variant adds all cuts per iteration (Combinatorial Benders); the heuristic variant tests shunting movements one-by-one, mimicking the split between rolling stock dispatchers and infrastructure dispatchers.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

Based on the input description, here is the complete MILP formulation. (Model 2 from the factory was selected as the most comprehensive; I have refined and finalized it below.)

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $I$ | Set of trains, $i \in I$ |
| $J$ | Set of stations (ordered along the corridor), $j \in J$ |
| $B$ | Set of track blocks (sections between stations), $b \in B$ |
| $T$ | Set of discrete time periods, $t \in T$ |
| $R$ | Set of routes, $R = \{0, 1\}$ (0 = main track, 1 = opposite track) |
| $K$ | Set of piecewise-linear segments for the energy function, $k \in K$ |

**Derived sets:**
- $B_i \subseteq B$: blocks on the path of train $i$
- $\text{pred}(b), \text{next}(b)$: previous and next blocks of $b$ on a train's path
- $B^{\text{dis}} = \{b \in B : \text{disruption}_b = 1\}$: disrupted blocks
- $T^{\text{dis}} = \{t \in T : \text{disruption}_t = 1\}$: disruption time window
- $I^{\text{up}}, I^{\text{down}} \subseteq I$: trains traveling in opposite directions

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ | km |
| $\Delta t$ | Duration of each time period | h |
| $v_{\min}, v_{\max}$ | Minimum and maximum operating speed | km/h |
| $a_{\text{acc}}, a_{\text{dec}}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration | km/h² |
| $\text{dwell}_{\min,j}, \text{dwell}_{\max,j}$ | Min/max dwell time at station $j$ | h |
| $h_{\text{headway}}$ | Minimum safety headway between consecutive trains | periods |
| $h_{\text{meet}}$ | Minimum meeting gap for opposing trains on opposite track | periods |
| $t^{\text{sched}}_{i,j}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $j$ | h |
| $t^0_i, t^f_i$ | Scheduled departure/arrival time of train $i$ at terminals | h |
| $c_0, c_1, c_2$ | Energy function coefficients ($c_2 > 0$) | kWh, kWh/(km/h), kWh/(km/h)² |
| $\text{disruption}_b \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if block $b$ is in the disruption area | – |
| $\text{disruption}_t \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if time $t$ is in the disruption window | – |
| $M$ | Big-M constant (sufficiently large) | – |
| $\alpha, \beta$ | Weights for delay and energy in the objective | – |
| $\text{delay}_{\max}$ | Maximum allowable delay | h |
| $v_k, E_k$ | Speed breakpoints and corresponding energy values | km/h, kWh |
| $m_k$ | Slope of segment $k$ of the piecewise-linear energy curve | – |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $x_{i,b,r,t}$ | $\in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ occupies block $b$ on route $r$ at time $t$ |
| $v_{i,b,r,t}$ | $\in [v_{\min}, v_{\max}]$ | Speed of train $i$ on block $b$, route $r$, time $t$ |
| $s_{i,b,r,t}$ | $\geq 0$ | Auxiliary: $s_{i,b,r,t} = v_{i,b,r,t} \cdot x_{i,b,r,t}$ |
| $\text{arr}_{i,j}$ | $\geq 0$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $j$ |
| $\text{dep}_{i,j}$ | $\geq 0$ | Departure time of train $i$ at station $j$ |
| $\text{delay}_{i,j}$ | $\geq 0$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $j$ vs. schedule |
| $\text{energy}_{i,b,r,t}$ | $\geq 0$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on block $b$, route $r$, time $t$ |
| $\text{ord}_{i,i',b,r,t}$ | $\in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $i'$ on block $b$, route $r$, time $t$ |
| $\text{reroute}_{i,b,t}$ | $\in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses opposite track on block $b$ at time $t$ |
| $\text{enter}_{i,b,r,t}$ | $\in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ enters block $b$ on route $r$ at time $t$ |
| $\text{exit}_{i,b,r,t}$ | $\in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ exits block $b$ on route $r$ at time $t$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \alpha \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{j \in J} \text{delay}_{i,j} \;+\; \beta \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{b \in B} \sum_{r \in R} \sum_{t \in T} \text{energy}_{i,b,r,t}
$$

The objective minimizes a weighted sum of total delay (rescheduling cost) and total energy consumption (operational cost), capturing the trade-off between service punctuality and energy efficiency.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Flow Conservation and Block Occupancy

**(a) Single block per train per time (spatial consistency):**
$$
\sum_{b \in B} x_{i,b,r,t} \leq 1 \quad \forall i \in I, \; r \in R, \; t \in T
$$

**(b) Single route per block per train per time:**
$$
\sum_{r \in R} x_{i,b,r,t} \leq 1 \quad \forall i \in I, \; b \in B, \; t \in T
$$

**(c) Distance traversal (linearized):**
$$
\sum_{t \in T} s_{i,b,r,t} \cdot \Delta t = L_b \quad \forall i \in I, \; b \in B_i, \; r \in R
$$

with linearization of the bilinear product:
$$
\begin{aligned}
s_{i,b,r,t} &\leq v_{\max} \cdot x_{i,b,r,t} \\
s_{i,b,r,t} &\geq v_{\min} \cdot x_{i,b,r,t} \\
s_{i,b,r,t} &\leq v_{i,b,r,t} \\
s_{i,b,r,t} &\geq v_{i,b,r,t} - v_{\max}(1 - x_{i,b,r,t})
\end{aligned}
\quad \forall i, b, r, t
$$

**(d) Sequential block movement (cumulative):**
$$
\sum_{t' \leq t} x_{i,\text{next}(b),r,t'} \leq \sum_{t' \leq t} x_{i,b,r,t'} \quad \forall i \in I, \; b \in B_i, \; r \in R, \; t \in T
$$

This ensures block $b+1$ is not entered before block $b$ is completed.

### 5.2 Speed Dynamics

**(a) Acceleration limit:**
$$
v_{i,b,r,t} - v_{i,b,r,t-1} \leq a_{\text{acc}} \cdot \Delta t + M(2 - x_{i,b,r,t} - x_{i,b,r,t-1}) \quad \forall i, b, r, t
$$

**(b) Deceleration limit:**
$$
v_{i,b,r,t-1} - v_{i,b,r,t} \leq a_{\text{dec}} \cdot \Delta t + M(2 - x_{i,b,r,t} - x_{i,b,r,t-1}) \quad \forall i, b, r, t
$$

**(c) Speed bounds:**
$$
v_{\min} \cdot x_{i,b,r,t} \leq v_{i,b,r,t} \leq v_{\max} \cdot x_{i,b,r,t} \quad \forall i, b, r, t
$$

### 5.3 Block Capacity and Headway

**(a) Main track capacity (unidirectional):**
$$
\sum_{i \in I} x_{i,b,0,t} \leq 1 \quad \forall b \in B, \; t \in T
$$

**(b) Opposite track capacity (bidirectional):**
$$
\sum_{i \in I} x_{i,b,1,t} \leq 1 \quad \forall b \in B, \; t \in T
$$

**(c) Safety headway:**
$$
\sum_{\tau = t}^{t + h_{\text{headway}} - 1} \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{r \in R} x_{i,b,r,\tau} \leq 1 \quad \forall b \in B, \; t \in T
$$

### 5.4 Disruption and Rerouting

**(a) Main track blocked during disruption:**
$$
x_{i,b,0,t} \leq 1 - \text{disruption}_b \cdot \text{disruption}_t \quad \forall i \in I, \; b \in B, \; t \in T
$$

**(b) Rerouting indicator:**
$$
\text{reroute}_{i,b,t} = x_{i,b,1,t} \quad \forall i \in I, \; b \in B, \; t \in T
$$

**(c) Opposite track availability during disruption:**
$$
x_{i,b,1,t} \leq 1 \quad \forall i \in I, \; b \in B^{\text{dis}}, \; t \in T^{\text{dis}}
$$

### 5.5 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution

**(a) Ordering definition (if both trains use opposite track):**
$$
\text{ord}_{i,i',b,1,t} + \text{ord}_{i',i,b,1,t} \geq x_{i,b,1,t} + x_{i',b,1,t} - 1 \quad \forall i \neq i', \; b, t
$$

**(b) Mutual exclusivity of ordering:**
$$
\text{ord}_{i,i',b,1,t} + \text{ord}_{i',i,b,1,t} \leq 1 \quad \forall i \neq i', \; b, t
$$

**(c) Minimum time gap for opposing trains on opposite track:**
$$
\sum_{\tau = t}^{t + h_{\text{meet}} - 1} (x_{i,b,1,\tau} + x_{i',b,1,\tau}) \leq 1 + \text{ord}_{i,i',b,1,t} + \text{ord}_{i',i,b,1,t} \quad \forall i \neq i', b, t
$$

### 5.6 Dwell Time Constraints

$$
\text{dwell}_{\min,j} \leq \text{dep}_{i,j} - \text{arr}_{i,j} \leq \text{dwell}_{\max,j} \quad \forall i \in I, \; j \in J
$$

### 5.7 Schedule Deviation

**(a) Delay definition:**
$$
\text{delay}_{i,j} \geq \text{arr}_{i,j} - t^{\text{sched}}_{i,j} \quad \forall i \in I, \; j \in J
$$
$$
\text{delay}_{i,j} \geq 0
$$

**(b) Maximum allowable delay:**
$$
\text{delay}_{i,j} \leq \text{delay}_{\max} \quad \forall i \in I, \; j \in J
$$

### 5.8 Energy Consumption (Piecewise-Linear Approximation)

For each segment $k$ of the piecewise-linear approximation of $E(v) = c_0 + c_1 v + c_2 v^2$:

$$
\text{energy}_{i,b,r,t} \geq E_k + m_k (v_{i,b,r,t} - v_k) - M(1 - x_{i,b,r,t}) \quad \forall i, b, r, t, \; k \in K
$$

where $E_k = c_0 + c_1 v_k + c_2 v_k^2$ and $m_k = c_1 + c_2(v_k + v_{k+1})$ (secant slope).

Additionally:
$$
\text{energy}_{i,b,r,t} \geq 0 \quad \forall i, b, r, t
$$

### 5.9 Linking Constraints (Block–Station Time Consistency)

**(a) Arrival time equals exit time from preceding block:**
$$
\text{arr}_{i,j} \geq t \cdot \text{exit}_{i,b,r,t} \quad \forall i, j, b = \text{block\_before}(j), r, t
$$
$$
\text{arr}_{i,j} \leq t \cdot \text{exit}_{i,b,r,t} + M(1 - \text{exit}_{i,b,r,t}) \quad \forall i, j, b = \text{block\_before}(j), r, t
$$

**(b) Departure time equals entry time to following block:**
$$
\text{dep}_{i,j} \geq t \cdot \text{enter}_{i,b,r,t} \quad \forall i, j, b = \text{block\_after}(j), r, t
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{i,j} \leq t \cdot \text{enter}_{i,b,r,t} + M(1 - \text{enter}_{i,b,r,t}) \quad \forall i, j, b = \text{block\_after}(j), r, t
$$

**(c) Entry/exit consistency with occupation:**
$$
x_{i,b,r,t} - x_{i,b,r,t-1} \leq \text{enter}_{i,b,r,t} \quad \forall i, b, r, t
$$
$$
x_{i,b,r,t-1} - x_{i,b,r,t} \leq \text{exit}_{i,b,r,t} \quad \forall i, b, r, t
$$
$$
\sum_{t \in T} \text{enter}_{i,b,r,t} = 1, \quad \sum_{t \in T} \text{exit}_{i,b,r,t} = 1 \quad \forall i, b \in B_i, r
$$

### 5.10 Initial and Final Conditions

**(a) Origin station (first station):**
$$
\text{dep}_{i,1} = t^0_i + \text{delay}_{i,1} \quad \forall i \in I
$$

**(b) Destination station (last station):**
$$
\text{arr}_{i,|J|} = t^f_i + \text{delay}_{i,|J|} \quad \forall i \in I
$$

**(c) Terminal block entry/exit:**
$$
\text{enter}_{i,b_1^i,r,t^0_i} = 1 \quad \forall i \in I, \; r \in R
$$
$$
\text{exit}_{i,b_{|B_i|}^i,r,t^f_i} = 1 \quad \forall i \in I, \; r \in R
$$

where $b_1^i$ and $b_{|B_i|}^i$ are the first and last blocks on train $i$'s path.

---

## 6. Model Explanation

### Key Components

**1. Integrated Decision Making.** The model simultaneously optimizes rescheduling (via $x$, $\text{arr}$, $\text{dep}$, $\text{delay}$) and speed profiles (via $v$), capturing the interdependence between timetabling and energy-efficient driving.

**2. Disruption Handling.** The binary parameters $\text{disruption}_b$ and $\text{disruption}_t$ define the spatiotemporal disruption window. Constraint 5.4(a) blocks the main track during disruption, forcing trains to use the opposite track (constraint 5.4(b)).

**3. Bidirectional Traffic on Opposite Track.** When trains from both directions share the opposite track to bypass disruption, constraints 5.5(a)–(c) ensure safe passing with adequate time gaps, using ordering variables $\text{ord}_{i,i',b,r,t}$.

**4. Speed–Energy Trade-off.** The piecewise-linear approximation in constraint 5.8 allows the model to balance faster traversal (reducing delay) against higher energy consumption, since $E(v)$ is convex in $v$.

**5. Flow Conservation.** Constraints 5.1(c)–(d) ensure each train traverses its path sequentially with consistent timing, while the auxiliary variable $s_{i,b,r,t}$ linearizes the bilinear speed–occupation product.

**6. Practical Operational Constraints.** Dwell time bounds (5.6), headway safety (5.3(c)), and acceleration/deceleration limits (5.2) reflect real-world railway operations.

### Model Size and Complexity

- **Binary variables:** $O(|I| \cdot |B| \cdot |R| \cdot |T|)$ for $x$, plus $O(|I|^2 \cdot |B| \cdot |T|)$ for $\text{ord}$
- **Continuous variables:** $O(|I| \cdot |B| \cdot |R| \cdot |T|)$ for $v$, $s$, $\text{energy}$
- **Constraints:** $O(|I| \cdot |B| \cdot |R| \cdot |T|)$ for most constraints

This formulation can be solved using standard MILP solvers (e.g., CPLEX, Gurobi) for moderate-sized instances, or enhanced with decomposition methods (e.g., Benders, column generation, or the adaptive iterative algorithm described in the paper) for large-scale problems.

---

## 7. Assumptions Made (Marked Explicitly)

1. **Single corridor** with stations indexed $j=1,\ldots,J$ and blocks between them.
2. **Two routes only** ($R=\{0,1\}$): main track and opposite track. No alternative detour routes.
3. **No train cancellations** are modeled (can be added via a binary cancellation variable).
4. **Piecewise-constant speed** within each block–time cell.
5. **Energy function** $E(v) = c_0 + c_1 v + c_2 v^2$ is convex and approximated by a piecewise-linear function.
6. **Dwell times** are bounded but not fixed.
7. **Bidirectional conflict** is resolved via ordering variables with a minimum meeting gap $h_{\text{meet}}$.
8. **Time discretization** is uniform with interval $\Delta t$.
9. **All trains** are assumed to be homogeneous (same speed limits, acceleration/deceleration bounds).
10. **Disruption window** is rectangular in space–time (a contiguous set of blocks during a contiguous time interval).

Text:
# MILP Formulation for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockage

After evaluating all five generated models, **Model 2** is selected as the best. It provides the most elegant and consistent formulation by using a **unified SOS2 approximation** for all nonlinear relations ($v^2$, $1/v$, and energy), ensuring perfect consistency between speed, time, and energy variables. The model is complete, well-structured, and properly handles all aspects of the problem.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Set | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j \in T$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s \in S$ |
| $K$ | Set of track segments, indexed by $k \in K$, $|K|=|S|-1$ |
| $P$ | Discretized positions along a segment, $p=0,1,\dots,|P|$ |
| $D=\{1,2\}$ | Directions: 1 = nominal, 2 = opposite |
| $Q$ | Breakpoints for piecewise-linear approximation, $q=1,\dots,|Q|$ |

Let $k(s)$ denote the segment connecting station $s$ to $s+1$.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| $L_k$ | Length of segment $k$ |
| $v_{\max}, v_{\min}$ | Maximum / minimum operating speed |
| $a_{\max}, a_{\min}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration ($a_{\min}<0$) |
| $t^{bs}, t^{be}$ | Blockage start / end time |
| $k_b, d_b$ | Blocked segment index and direction |
| $E_{acc}, E_{cru}, E_{dec}$ | Energy coefficients (acceleration, cruise, deceleration) |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) |
| $w_d, w_e$ | Weights for delay and energy |
| $arr_i^0, dep_i^0$ | Original scheduled arrival / departure times |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum headway between trains |
| $\tau_{\min}, \tau_{\max}$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time at stations |
| $\Delta_p = L_k/|P|$ | Position discretization step |
| $T_H$ | Planning horizon |
| $(v_q^{br}, e_q^{br}, u_q^{br}, \eta_q^{br})$ | Breakpoints: speed, energy, $u=v^2$, and $\eta=1/v$ |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous (timing & rescheduling):**
- $a_{i,s} \ge 0$: actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $d_{i,s} \ge 0$: actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $\delta_{i,s} \ge 0$: delay of train $i$ at station $s$

**Continuous (speed management):**
- $v_{i,k,p} \ge 0$: speed of train $i$ on segment $k$ at position $p$
- $t_{i,k,p} \ge 0$: time of train $i$ on segment $k$ at position $p$
- $e_{i,k,p} \ge 0$: energy consumption at position $p$
- $u_{i,k,p} \ge 0$: auxiliary variable equal to $v_{i,k,p}^2$
- $acc_{i,k,p} \in \mathbb{R}$: acceleration between positions $p$ and $p+1$
- $\lambda_{i,k,p,q} \ge 0$: SOS2 weight for piecewise-linear approximation

**Binary:**
- $z_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ operates (not cancelled)
- $r_{i,k,d} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses direction $d$ on segment $k$
- $y_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ departs station $s$ before train $j$
- $x_{i,j,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $k$

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; w_d \sum_{i\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\delta_{i,s} \;+\; w_e \sum_{i\in T}\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{p\in P} e_{i,k,p}
$$

The first term penalizes total delay (service quality); the second penalizes total tractive energy.

---

## 5. Constraints

### (C1) Delay Definition
$$
\delta_{i,s} \;\ge\; a_{i,s} - arr_i^0, \qquad \forall i\in T,\; s\in S
$$

### (C2) Train Flow Conservation at Stations
$$
a_{i,s+1} \;=\; d_{i,s} + \bigl(t_{i,k(s),|P|} - t_{i,k(s),0}\bigr), \qquad \forall i\in T,\; s\in S\setminus\{|S|\}
$$

### (C3) Segment Time Boundary
$$
t_{i,k,0} \;=\; d_{i,s}\cdot z_i, \qquad t_{i,k,|P|} \;=\; a_{i,s+1}\cdot z_i, \qquad \forall i\in T,\; k\in K
$$
where $s$ is the departure station of segment $k$.

### (C4) Dwell Time
$$
\tau_{\min}\, z_i \;\le\; d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \;\le\; \tau_{\max}\, z_i, \qquad \forall i\in T,\; s\in S
$$

### (C5) Initial Departure Time
$$
d_{i,1} \;\ge\; dep_i^0 \cdot z_i, \qquad \forall i\in T
$$

### (C6) Speed Bounds
$$
v_{\min}\, z_i \;\le\; v_{i,k,p} \;\le\; v_{\max}\, z_i, \qquad \forall i\in T,\; k\in K,\; p\in P
$$

### (C7) Acceleration Bounds
$$
a_{\min}\, z_i \;\le\; acc_{i,k,p} \;\le\; a_{\max}\, z_i, \qquad \forall i\in T,\; k\in K,\; p\in P\setminus\{|P|\}
$$

### (C8) Kinematic Relation (linearized via $u=v^2$)
$$
u_{i,k,p+1} - u_{i,k,p} \;=\; 2\, acc_{i,k,p}\, \Delta_p, \qquad \forall i\in T,\; k\in K,\; p\in P\setminus\{|P|\}
$$

with the convex relation $u = v^2$ enforced by piecewise-linear (SOS2) interpolation:
$$
u_{i,k,p} = \sum_{q\in Q}\lambda_{i,k,p,q}\, u_q^{br}, \qquad
v_{i,k,p} = \sum_{q\in Q}\lambda_{i,k,p,q}\, v_q^{br}, \qquad
\sum_{q\in Q}\lambda_{i,k,p,q} = z_i
$$
$$
\text{SOS2}\bigl(\{\lambda_{i,k,p,q}\}_{q\in Q}\bigr), \qquad \forall i\in T,\; k\in K,\; p\in P
$$

### (C9) Position–Time Consistency (linearized via $1/v$)
$$
t_{i,k,p+1} - t_{i,k,p} \;=\; \Delta_p \sum_{q\in Q}\lambda_{i,k,p,q}\, \eta_q^{br}, \qquad \forall i\in T,\; k\in K,\; p\in P\setminus\{|P|\}
$$
(uses the same $\lambda$ as C8 — exact because $v$ and $1/v$ are evaluated at the same breakpoints.)

### (C10) Energy Consumption (piecewise-linear in $v$)
$$
e_{i,k,p} \;=\; \sum_{q\in Q}\lambda_{i,k,p,q}\, e_q^{br}, \qquad \forall i\in T,\; k\in K,\; p\in P
$$
where $e_q^{br}$ are obtained from the convex function $e(v)=\alpha v^2+\beta v+\gamma$ (combining $E_{acc},E_{cru},E_{dec}$) evaluated at each breakpoint.

### (C11) Blockage Avoidance
For the blocked segment $k_b$ in direction $d_b$, any train using that direction must be entirely outside the blockage window:
$$
t_{i,k_b,p} \;\le\; t^{bs} + M(1-r_{i,k_b,d_b}) + M(1-z_i), \qquad \forall i\in T,\; p\in P
$$
$$
t_{i,k_b,p} \;\ge\; t^{be} - M(1-r_{i,k_b,d_b}) - M(1-z_i), \qquad \forall i\in T,\; p\in P
$$

### (C12) Direction Assignment (Rerouting)
$$
r_{i,k,1} + r_{i,k,2} \;=\; z_i, \qquad \forall i\in T,\; k\in K
$$
$$
r_{i,k_b,d_b} \;=\; 0, \qquad \forall i\in T \quad\text{(forces use of the opposite track)}
$$

### (C13) Segment Precedence
$$
x_{i,j,k} + x_{j,i,k} \;\le\; z_i\, z_j, \qquad \forall i,j\in T,\; i<j,\; k\in K
$$

### (C14) Headway — Same Direction
For trains $i,j$ using direction $d$ on segment $k$:
$$
t_{j,k,0} - t_{i,k,|P|} \;\ge\; h_{\min} - M(1-x_{i,j,k}) - M(2 - r_{i,k,d} - r_{j,k,d}), \quad \forall i<j,\; k\in K,\; d\in D
$$

### (C15) Headway — Opposite Directions (Meeting Avoidance)
For trains $i$ (direction 1) and $j$ (direction 2) on segment $k$:
$$
t_{j,k,|P|} - t_{i,k,0} \;\ge\; h_{\min} - M(1-x_{i,j,k}) - M(2 - r_{i,k,1} - r_{j,k,2})
$$
$$
t_{i,k,|P|} - t_{j,k,0} \;\ge\; h_{\min} - M\, x_{i,j,k} - M(2 - r_{i,k,2} - r_{j,k,1})
$$
$\forall i<j,\; k\in K$. The binary $x_{i,j,k}$ selects which train traverses first.

### (C16) Train Ordering at Stations
$$
y_{i,j,s} + y_{j,i,s} \;\le\; z_i\, z_j, \qquad \forall i<j,\; s\in S
$$
$$
d_{i,s} \;\le\; d_{j,s} + M(1-y_{i,j,s}) + M(2-z_i-z_j), \qquad \forall i<j,\; s\in S
$$

### (C17) Cancellation (big-M coupling)
If $z_i=0$, all operational variables are forced to zero:
$$
a_{i,s} \le M z_i,\;\; d_{i,s} \le M z_i,\;\; v_{i,k,p} \le M z_i,\;\; t_{i,k,p} \le M z_i,\;\; e_{i,k,p} \le M z_i
$$

### (C18) Time Horizon
$$
a_{i,s} \le T_H\, z_i, \qquad d_{i,s} \le T_H\, z_i, \qquad \forall i\in T,\; s\in S
$$

---

## 6. Key Modeling Elements

| Element | Role in the Model |
|---------|-------------------|
| **$a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, \delta_{i,s}$** | **Retiming**: actual arrival/departure times and resulting delay at every station. |
| **$y_{i,j,s}$** | **Reordering**: enforces a strict ordering of train departures at each station. |
| **$r_{i,k,d}$** | **Rerouting**: assigns each train to a track direction on each segment. Constraint (C12) forces rerouting onto the opposite track when the nominal track is blocked. |
| **$z_i$** | **Cancellation**: when $z_i=0$, the train is removed from the schedule (all its variables become zero via big-M). |
| **$v_{i,k,p}, t_{i,k,p}, acc_{i,k,p}$** | **Speed management**: discretized speed, time, and acceleration profiles along each segment. |
| **$e_{i,k,p}$** | Energy consumption at each position, computed from the speed profile. |
| **$x_{i,j,k}$** | **Conflict resolution**: decides which train traverses a (possibly shared) segment first. |
| **SOS2 variables $\lambda_{i,k,p,q}$** | Piecewise-linear interpolation weights used **simultaneously** for $u=v^2$ (C8), $1/v$ (C9), and $e(v)$ (C10) — guaranteeing consistency across all three nonlinear relations. |

---

## 7. Linearization Summary

| Nonlinear Relation | Linearization Technique |
|--------------------|------------------------|
| $v^2$ (kinematic) | Substitution $u=v^2$ + SOS2 over breakpoints $(v_q^{br}, u_q^{br})$ |
| $1/v$ (position-time) | SOS2 over same breakpoints, multiplying $\Delta_p$ |
| $e(v)$ quadratic (energy) | SOS2 over breakpoints $(v_q^{br}, e_q^{br})$ |
| Logical disjunctions (headway, blockage, ordering) | Big-M with binary indicators |
| Bilinear products | Avoided by sharing the same $\lambda$ across $v$, $1/v$, and $e$ |

---

## 8. Assumptions

1. **Single partial blockage**: Only one segment-direction pair is blocked during a single time window $[t^{bs}, t^{be}]$.
2. **Position-based discretization**: Each segment is divided into $|P|$ equal position intervals of length $\Delta_p = L_k/|P|$.
3. **Convex energy function**: Energy consumption is modeled as a convex quadratic function of speed, enabling accurate SOS2 approximation.
4. **Bidirectional single-track line**: The railway has two physical tracks (one per direction); during blockage, trains in both directions share the opposite track.
5. **Fixed train sequence**: Each train has a fixed origin-destination pair and visits stations in a prescribed order.
6. **No track switching outside blocked segments**: Rerouting is only allowed on the blocked segment.
7. **Discrete speed profile**: Speed is assumed constant within each position interval (valid for sufficiently fine discretization).
8. **Homogeneous trains**: All trains share the same kinematic parameters ($v_{\min}, v_{\max}, a_{\min}, a_{\max}$) unless differentiated by additional indices.

---

## 9. Model Complexity

| Element | Approximate Count |
|---------|-------------------|
| Continuous variables | $O(|T|(|S| + |K||P|) + |T||K||P||Q|)$ |
| Binary variables | $O(|T|^2|K| + |T|^2|S| + |T||K|)$ |
| SOS2 sets | $O(|T||K||P|)$ |
| Constraints | $O(|T||K||P| + |T|^2|K| + |T|^2|S|)$ |

The resulting model is a **mixed-integer linear program** solvable by standard MILP solvers (CPLEX, Gurobi, HiGHS) using branch-and-bound with SOS2 branching for the piecewise-linear approximations. The position resolution $|P|$ and breakpoint count $|Q|$ are the main levers for balancing accuracy and tractability.

Text:
# Complete MILP Model for Real-Time Railway Traffic Management (rtRTMP)

Below is a complete linear model based on the multi-stage framework described in the input. The model corresponds to the **global-optimum MILP** (Section 3.3 of the referenced paper), which extends the sub-optimal pair-wise model (Section 3.1) by incorporating delay propagation. Assumptions made to complete the formulation are explicitly marked as **[Assumption]**.

---

## 1. Model Overview

The model jointly decides:
- **Rerouting**: which feasible route each train takes,
- **Reordering**: which train passes a conflict point first,
- **Rescheduling**: the actual entry/exit times at each block, accounting for headways, safety overlaps, and propagated delays.

The objective is to minimize the weighted total (secondary) delay of all trains.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j \in T$ |
| $B$ | Set of railway blocks (sections between signals), indexed by $b \in B$ |
| $R_i$ | Set of feasible routes for train $i$, indexed by $r \in R_i$ |
| $C \subseteq T \times T$ | Set of conflicting train pairs that share at least one block |
| $B_{ij} \subseteq B$ | Set of blocks where trains $i$ and $j$ may conflict |
| $B^r_i \subseteq B$ | Set of blocks traversed by train $i$ on route $r$ **[Assumption]** |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\tau^{b}_{i,r}$ | Planned (nominal) entry time of train $i$ into block $b$ if it uses route $r$ |
| $\tau^{b,\text{out}}_{i,r}$ | Planned exit time of train $i$ from block $b$ if it uses route $r$ |
| $\rho_{i,b}$ | Nominal running time of train $i$ through block $b$ (route-independent) **[Assumption]** |
| $h_b$ | Minimum headway time between consecutive trains on block $b$ |
| $o_b$ | Safety overlap (clearance margin) behind a stop signal on block $b$ |
| $w_i$ | Priority weight of train $i$ (e.g., passenger > freight) |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) |
| $\varepsilon$ | Small positive constant to enforce strict inequalities **[Assumption]** |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Routing variables
$$
x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; r \in R_i
$$
$=1$ if train $i$ is assigned route $r$.

### 4.2 Ordering variables
$$
y_{ij} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall (i,j) \in C
$$
$=1$ if train $i$ passes the conflict point with train $j$ before train $j$ (i.e., $i$ precedes $j$).

### 4.3 Timing variables
$$
t^b_i \ge 0, \quad \forall i \in T,\; b \in B
$$
Actual entry time of train $i$ into block $b$.

$$
t^{b,\text{out}}_i \ge 0, \quad \forall i \in T,\; b \in B
$$
Actual exit time of train $i$ from block $b$.

### 4.4 Pair-wise delay variables
$$
\delta_{ij} \ge 0, \quad \forall (i,j) \in C
$$
Delay incurred by train $i$ because it has to wait for train $j$.

$$
\delta_i \ge 0, \quad \forall i \in T
$$
Total delay of train $i$.

### 4.5 Auxiliary variables
$$
z_{ij} \in \{0,1\}, \quad \forall (i,j) \in C
$$
$=1$ if train $i$ is delayed specifically by train $j$ (used to linearize the pair-wise delay definition).

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total train delays:

$$
\min \; \sum_{i \in T} w_i \, \delta_i
$$

**[Assumption]** Primary delays (initial disturbances) are fixed inputs; the model minimizes the additional secondary delays caused by conflicts and rerouting.

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Route assignment
Each train must be assigned exactly one route:
$$
\sum_{r \in R_i} x_{i,r} = 1, \quad \forall i \in T \tag{C1}
$$

### 6.2 Linking entry time to the chosen route
The actual entry time must be at least the planned time on the chosen route:
$$
t^b_i \;\ge\; \tau^{b}_{i,r} - M(1 - x_{i,r}), \quad \forall i \in T,\; b \in B,\; r \in R_i \tag{C2}
$$
$$
t^b_i \;\le\; \tau^{b}_{i,r} + M(1 - x_{i,r}), \quad \forall i \in T,\; b \in B,\; r \in R_i \tag{C3}
$$

### 6.3 Block traversal (running time)
$$
t^{b,\text{out}}_i \;\ge\; t^b_i + \rho_{i,b}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; b \in B \tag{C4}
$$

### 6.4 Ordering consistency for conflicting pairs
$$
y_{ij} + y_{ji} = 1, \quad \forall (i,j) \in C \tag{C5}
$$

### 6.5 Headway / safety-overlap constraints with ordering
For every pair of trains $(i,j) \in C$ and every shared block $b \in B_{ij}$:

If $i$ precedes $j$ ($y_{ij}=1$), then $j$ cannot enter block $b$ until $i$ has cleared it with the safety overlap:
$$
t^b_j \;\ge\; t^{b,\text{out}}_i + h_b + o_b - M(1 - y_{ij}) - M(2 - x_{i,r} - x_{j,s}), \quad \forall (i,j)\in C,\; b\in B_{ij},\; r\in R_i,\; s\in R_j \tag{C6}
$$

Conversely, if $j$ precedes $i$:
$$
t^b_i \;\ge\; t^{b,\text{out}}_j + h_b + o_b - M(1 - y_{ji}) - M(2 - x_{i,r} - x_{j,s}), \quad \forall (i,j)\in C,\; b\in B_{ij},\; r\in R_i,\; s\in R_j \tag{C7}
$$

**[Assumption]** The safety overlap $o_b$ follows Lindenmaier et al. (2022); it represents the clearance margin behind a stop signal.

### 6.6 Pair-wise delay definition (linearized)
The delay of train $i$ waiting for train $j$ at block $b$ is non-zero only if $j$ precedes $i$ on that block:
$$
\delta_{ij} \;\ge\; t^b_i - \tau^b_{i,r} - M(1 - y_{ji}) - M(2 - x_{i,r} - x_{j,s}), \quad \forall (i,j)\in C,\; b\in B_{ij},\; r\in R_i,\; s\in R_j \tag{C8}
$$
$$
\delta_{ij} \;\le\; M \cdot y_{ji}, \quad \forall (i,j) \in C \tag{C9}
$$

### 6.7 Total delay equals sum of pair-wise delays
$$
\delta_i \;\ge\; \sum_{j : (i,j) \in C} \delta_{ij}, \quad \forall i \in T \tag{C10}
$$
$$
\delta_i \;\le\; \sum_{j : (i,j) \in C} \delta_{ij} + M \sum_{j}(1 - z_{ij}), \quad \forall i \in T \tag{C11}
$$

### 6.8 Delay propagation (key extension of the sub-optimal model)
A delay absorbed at an upstream block propagates to all downstream blocks. Let $b' \prec_{i,r} b$ denote that block $b'$ is immediately upstream of block $b$ on train $i$'s route $r$ **[Assumption]**:
$$
t^b_i \;\ge\; t^{b'}_i + \rho_{i,b'} + h_{b'} + o_{b'} - M(1 - x_{i,r}), \quad \forall i \in T,\; (b',b) \text{ consecutive on route } r \tag{C12}
$$

Equivalently, the entry time at any block must be at least the entry time at the previous block plus the running time and any headway/overlap already incurred:
$$
t^b_i \;\ge\; t^{b',\text{out}}_i + h_{b'} + o_{b'}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; (b',b) \text{ consecutive on chosen route} \tag{C13}
$$

### 6.9 Non-negativity and integrality
$$
x_{i,r} \in \{0,1\},\quad y_{ij} \in \{0,1\},\quad z_{ij} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
t^b_i,\; t^{b,\text{out}}_i,\; \delta_i,\; \delta_{ij} \;\ge\; 0
$$

---

## 7. Sub-Optimal Variant (Section 3.1)

The sub-optimal model is obtained by:
1. **Removing constraint (C12)/(C13)** — i.e., dropping the explicit delay-propagation constraints, and
2. **Replacing (C10) by** $\delta_i = \sum_j \delta_{ij}$ (no propagation allowed).

This yields a fast but sub-optimal solution. The optimality analysis (Section 3.2) shows that the sub-optimal solution equals the global optimum **if and only if** no train's delay propagates through more than one downstream conflict — i.e., when the conflict graph is acyclic with respect to delay chains **[Assumption]**.

---

## 8. Summary of Assumptions Made

1. Block-level (macroscopic) infrastructure representation, following Dollevoet et al. (2015) and Kanai et al. (2011).
2. Constant running time $\rho_{i,b}$ per block (no energy-speed trade-off inside the MILP; energy could be added as in Naldini et al., 2022).
3. Symmetric headway $h_b$ and overlap $o_b$ independent of train type.
4. Primary delays are exogenous inputs; the model minimizes secondary delays only.
5. The conflict set $C$ and shared-block set $B_{ij}$ are precomputed from the route alternatives.
6. The big-M constant $M$ is chosen large enough (e.g., $M = \max_i (T^{\text{horizon}}_i)$) to not be binding when the corresponding binary is 0.
