# Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

Below is the full, integrated MILP model that couples train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with speed-profile generation and energy consumption.

---

## 0. Modeling Assumptions

1. **Double-track railway line** with unidirectional traffic per track; one track of a single segment $b_d$ is blocked in direction $d_d$ during window $[\tau_d^s, \tau_d^e]$.
2. **Homogeneous high-speed trains** with the same mass, max speed, and Davis coefficients.
3. **Fixed minimum dwell times** at all intermediate stations.
4. **Braking is non-recoverable**; only positive kinetic-energy changes consume tractive energy.
5. **Davis resistance:** $R(v) = m(c_0 + c_1 v + c_2 v^2)$.
6. **Piecewise-linear approximation** (SOS2) of $v^2$ and $1/v$ with $K_p$ breakpoints.
7. **Continuous time, space discretization** at every $\Delta x_b = L_b / n_b$.
8. **Segment-level block signalling** with minimum headway $h$.
9. **Single-trip horizon** per train; rolling horizon not modeled.
10. **Rerouting** is permitted only to bypass $b_d$; otherwise trains follow their nominal route $\Psi_t$.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, index $t, t'$ |
| $B$ | set of track segments, index $b$ |
| $I_b=\{0,\ldots,n_b\}$ | spatial points along segment $b$ (interval $i$ spans $[i\Delta x_b,(i+1)\Delta x_b]$) |
| $K=\{1,\ldots,K_p\}$ | breakpoints of the SOS2 approximation |
| $S$ | set of intermediate stations |
| $\Psi_t \subseteq B$ | nominal (ordered) route of train $t$ |
| $b_t^{\text{first}}, b_t^{\text{last}}$ | first/last segment on $\Psi_t$ |
| $d_t \in \{-1,+1\}$ | running direction of train $t$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $L_b, \Delta x_b$ | length of segment / interval | m |
| $V_b^{\max}, V_T^{\max}$ | segment / train max speed | m/s |
| $v_k, \bar v_k^2 = v_k^2, \bar t_k = \Delta x_b / v_k$ | breakpoint speed and pre-computed $v^2$ and $\Delta x/v$ | m/s, –, s |
| $m$ | train mass | kg |
| $c_0, c_1, c_2$ | Davis coefficients | – |
| $a_{\max}, d_{\max}$ | max acceleration / deceleration | m/s² |
| $\tau_d^s, \tau_d^e$ | disruption start / end | s |
| $b_d, d_d$ | blocked segment, blocked direction | – |
| $\tau_t^{\text{sch,dep}}, \tau_t^{\text{sch,arr}}$ | scheduled departure / arrival of $t$ | s |
| $\delta_s$ | dwell time at station $s$ | s |
| $C_t^{\text{cancel}}$ | cancellation penalty | – |
| $h$ | minimum headway | s |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | weights for delay / energy / cancellation | – |
| $M$ | big-$M$ constant | – |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous**

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $v_{t,b,i} \ge 0$ | speed in interval $(b,i)$ of train $t$ |
| $\tau_{t,b,i} \ge 0$ | entry time at the start of interval $(b,i)$ |
| $\tilde v^2_{t,b,i} \ge 0$ | SOS2 surrogate for $v_{t,b,i}^2$ |
| $\lambda_{t,b,i,k} \in [0,1]$ | SOS2 weight of breakpoint $k$ |
| $e^{\text{trac}}_{t,b,i}, e^{\text{res}}_{t,b,i} \ge 0$ | tractive and resistance energy in interval |
| $D_t, E_t$ | realized departure / arrival time |
| $\Delta_t^{\text{delay}} \ge 0$ | arrival delay of $t$ |
| $\rho_{t,t',b} \ge 0$ | time separation variable used in headway |

**Binary**

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $w_t \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled |
| $z_{t,b} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if $t$ uses the opposite track on $b$ (active only for $b = b_d$) |
| $\pi_{t,b_d}, \sigma_{t,b_d} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if $t$ traverses $b_d$ before $\tau_d^s$ / after $\tau_d^e$ |
| $\alpha_{t,t',b} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if $t$ and $t'$ share the same physical track on $b$ |
| $y_{t,t',b} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if $t$ precedes $t'$ on the shared track of $b$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min Z \;=\; \alpha \sum_{t \in T} \Delta_t^{\text{delay}}
\;+\; \beta \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{b \in \Psi_t} \sum_{i \in I_b} \Big( e^{\text{trac}}_{t,b,i} + e^{\text{res}}_{t,b,i} \Big)
\;+\; \gamma \sum_{t \in T} C_t^{\text{cancel}} w_t
$$

The three terms weigh **arrival delay**, **total energy consumption** (tractive + resistance), and **cancellation penalties**.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Travel-Time per Interval (TRP–TSMP coupling; $1/v$ linearized)

$$
\tau_{t,b,i+1} \;=\; \tau_{t,b,i} \;+\; \Delta x_b \sum_{k \in K} \lambda_{t,b,i,k}\, \bar t_k
\qquad \forall t \in T,\; b \in \Psi_t,\; i \in I_b \setminus \{n_b\}
$$

$$
\sum_{k \in K} \lambda_{t,b,i,k} = 1, \qquad \{\lambda_{t,b,i,k}\}_{k \in K} \text{ SOS2}
$$

### 5.2 Speed Profile (SOS2 linearization of $v$ and $v^2$)

$$
v_{t,b,i} = \sum_{k \in K} \lambda_{t,b,i,k} v_k, \qquad
\tilde v^2_{t,b,i} = \sum_{k \in K} \lambda_{t,b,i,k} \bar v_k^2
$$

$$
0 \le v_{t,b,i} \le \min\{V_b^{\max}, V_T^{\max}\},\qquad
\tilde v^2_{t,b,i} \ge 0
$$

### 5.3 Acceleration / Deceleration Bounds

$$
\tilde v^2_{t,b,i+1} - \tilde v^2_{t,b,i} \;\le\; 2 a_{\max} \Delta x_b
$$
$$
\tilde v^2_{t,b,i} - \tilde v^2_{t,b,i+1} \;\le\; 2 d_{\max} \Delta x_b
\qquad \forall t \in T,\; b \in \Psi_t,\; i \in I_b \setminus \{n_b\}
$$

### 5.4 Tractive Energy (only positive $\Delta E_k$ consumes energy)

$$
e^{\text{trac}}_{t,b,i} \;\ge\; \tfrac{1}{2} m \big( \tilde v^2_{t,b,i+1} - \tilde v^2_{t,b,i} \big),\qquad
e^{\text{trac}}_{t,b,i} \ge 0
$$

### 5.5 Resistance Energy (Davis equation, with $c_2 v^2$ linearized)

$$
e^{\text{res}}_{t,b,i} \;=\; m\, \Delta x_b \big( c_0 + c_1 v_{t,b,i} + c_2\, \tilde v^2_{t,b,i} \big)
\qquad \forall t, b, i
$$

### 5.6 Departure, Arrival, and Delay

$$
D_t = \tau_{t,\,b_t^{\text{first}},0}, \qquad D_t \ge \tau_t^{\text{sch,dep}}
$$
$$
E_t = \tau_{t,\,b_t^{\text{last}}, n_{b_t^{\text{last}}}}
$$
$$
\Delta_t^{\text{delay}} \ge E_t - \tau_t^{\text{sch,arr}}, \qquad
\Delta_t^{\text{delay}} \le M (1 - w_t)
$$

### 5.7 Fixed Dwell Times at Stations

For every train $t$ and consecutive pair $(b, b') \in \Psi_t$ separated by station $s$:

$$
\tau_{t, b', 0} = \tau_{t, b, n_b} + \delta_s
$$

### 5.8 Disruption Window — Three-Way Choice

For every $t$ with $b_d \in \Psi_t$ and $d_t = d_d$:

$$
\pi_{t,b_d} + \sigma_{t,b_d} + z_{t,b_d} = 1
$$

**(a) Pass before disruption starts:**
$$
\tau_{t, b_d, n_{b_d}} \le \tau_d^s + M (1 - \pi_{t,b_d})
$$

**(b) Pass after disruption ends:**
$$
\tau_{t, b_d, 0} \ge \tau_d^e - M (1 - \sigma_{t,b_d})
$$

**(c) Reroute to opposite track** — no temporal restriction beyond conflicts in (5.10).

For $b \neq b_d$ or $d_t \neq d_d$: $z_{t,b} = 0$.

### 5.9 Bidirectional Conflict Detection (shared physical track)

For each pair $(t,t')$, $t < t'$, and $b \in \Psi_t \cap \Psi_{t'}$:

$$
\alpha_{t,t',b} = \mathbb{1}\{d_t = d_{t'}\} \oplus \big( z_{t,b} \neq z_{t',b} \big)
$$

The XOR is linearized through an auxiliary variable $s_{t,t',b}$:

$$
s_{t,t',b} \ge z_{t,b} - z_{t',b},\qquad
s_{t,t',b} \ge z_{t',b} - z_{t,b}
$$
$$
s_{t,t',b} \le z_{t,b} + z_{t',b},\qquad
s_{t,t',b} \le 2 - z_{t,b} - z_{t',b}
$$
$$
\alpha_{t,t',b} = \mathbb{1}\{d_t=d_{t'}\} + s_{t,t',b} - 2\, \mathbb{1}\{d_t=d_{t'}\}\, s_{t,t',b}
$$

### 5.10 Ordering on Shared Track

$$
y_{t,t',b} + y_{t',t,b} = \alpha_{t,t',b} \qquad \forall t \ne t',\; b \in \Psi_t \cap \Psi_{t'}
$$

### 5.11 Headway / Safety Separation

$$
\tau_{t',b,0} \;\ge\; \tau_{t,b,n_b} + h - M (1 - y_{t,t',b}) - M (1 - \alpha_{t,t',b})
$$

$$
\tau_{t,b,0} \;\ge\; \tau_{t',b,n_b} + h - M y_{t,t',b} - M (1 - \alpha_{t,t',b})
$$

### 5.12 Cancellation

If $w_t = 1$: all $v_{t,b,i}, \tau_{t,b,i}$ are forced to zero (or excluded from sums); $\Delta_t^{\text{delay}} = 0$ via (5.6). Cancellation is allowed only if the timetable becomes infeasible; here we treat it as a model choice:

$$
\sum_{b \in \Psi_t} \sum_{i \in I_b} v_{t,b,i} \le M (1 - w_t),\qquad
\Delta_t^{\text{delay}} \le M (1 - w_t)
$$

### 5.13 Non-Negativity and Variable Domains

$$
v_{t,b,i}, \tilde v^2_{t,b,i}, e^{\text{trac}}_{t,b,i}, e^{\text{res}}_{t,b,i}, \tau_{t,b,i}, \Delta_t^{\text{delay}} \ge 0
$$
$$
\lambda_{t,b,i,k} \in [0,1], \quad
w_t, z_{t,b}, \pi_{t,b_d}, \sigma_{t,b_d}, \alpha_{t,t',b}, y_{t,t',b}, s_{t,t',b} \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Summary of the Integrated Coupling

| TRP variable | TSMP variable | Coupling constraint |
|---|---|---|
| arrival/departure ($D_t, E_t$) | entry times ($\tau_{t,b,i}$) | (5.6), (5.7) |
| rerouting $z_{t,b}$ | shared-track conflicts $\alpha_{t,t',b}$ | (5.8)–(5.10) |
| ordering $y_{t,t',b}$ | time separation $\tau_{t,b,n_b}-\tau_{t',b,0}$ | (5.10)–(5.11) |
| cancellation $w_t$ | suppression of speed/timing vars | (5.6), (5.12) |
| (none) | speed $v_{t,b,i}$ drives energy | (5.4)–(5.5) |

This MILP simultaneously yields a **conflict-free timetable** (with retiming, reordering, rerouting, and cancellation) **and the corresponding executable speed profiles** (with energy consumption) for all trains, ensuring that the dispatch decisions at the operational level are physically feasible at the train-control level.

# Final MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockages

Below is the complete, integrated MILP formulation that simultaneously optimizes train rescheduling (arrival/departure times, ordering, rerouting) and speed management (speed profiles, energy consumption) under partial segment blockages.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t, t'$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $B$ | Set of segments, indexed by $b$; segment $b$ connects stations $s(b)$ and $s(b)+1$ |
| $B^* \subseteq B$ | Set of disrupted segments |
| $K = \{1,\dots,|K|\}$ | Set of discretized time intervals of duration $\Delta$ (s) |
| $P$ | Set of breakpoints for the SOS2 approximation of $v^2$, indexed by $p$ |
| $A_t$ | Set of feasible rerouting alternatives for train $t$ |
| $D = \{+1,-1\}$ | Set of travel directions |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $L_b$ | Length of segment $b$ | m |
| $\Delta$ | Duration of a time interval | s |
| $v^{\min}, v^{\max}$ | Global min/max operating speed | m/s |
| $v^{\max,b^*}$ | Reduced speed limit on disrupted segment $b^*$ | m/s |
| $a^{\min}, a^{\max}$ | Acceleration / deceleration bounds | m/s² |
| $\tau^{\min}_s, \tau^{\max}_s$ | Min/max dwell time at station $s$ | s |
| $h$ | Minimum headway time between consecutive trains | s |
| $\theta_{b^*} \in [0,1]$ | Blockage severity on $b^*$ (fraction blocked) | – |
| $[k_1^{b^*}, k_2^{b^*}]$ | Disruption time window on $b^*$ (interval indices) | – |
| $\tau^{\text{arr},0}_{t,s}, \tau^{\text{dep},0}_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival/departure of train $t$ at $s$ | s |
| $c_1, c_2, c_3$ | Energy coefficients (quadratic, linear, constant) | – |
| $\rho_a$ | Cost of rerouting alternative $a$ | – |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Objective weights (delay, energy, rerouting) | – |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large positive constant (Big-M) | – |
| $\bar{v}_p, \bar{v}_p^{\,2}$ | Speed and squared-speed at breakpoint $p$ | m/s, (m/s)² |
| $\text{cap}_a$ | Capacity of rerouting alternative $a$ | trains |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Rescheduling Variables
- $a_{t,s} \ge 0$: actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $d_{t,s} \ge 0$: actual departure time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $\delta_{t,s} \ge 0$: delay of train $t$ at station $s$
- $\text{stop}_{t,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ stops at station $s$
- $y_{t,b} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ traverses segment $b$
- $o_{t,t',b} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ precedes train $t'$ on segment $b$
- $u_{t,a} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses rerouting alternative $a$
- $\text{track}_{t,b} \in \{0,1\}$: 0 = original track, 1 = opposite (rerouted) track

### 3.2 Speed Management Variables
- $v_{t,b,k} \ge 0$: speed of train $t$ on segment $b$ during interval $k$
- $p_{t,b,k} \ge 0$: position of train $t$ on segment $b$ at end of interval $k$
- $\text{acc}_{t,b,k}$: acceleration of train $t$ on segment $b$ during interval $k$
- $w_{t,b,k} \ge 0$: auxiliary variable approximating $v_{t,b,k}^2$
- $\lambda_{t,b,k,p} \ge 0$: SOS2 weight for breakpoint $p$

### 3.3 Performance Variables
- $D_t \ge 0$: total delay of train $t$
- $E_t \ge 0$: total energy consumption of train $t$
- $R_t \ge 0$: rerouting cost for train $t$

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \alpha \sum_{t \in T} D_t \;+\; \beta \sum_{t \in T} E_t \;+\; \gamma \sum_{t \in T} R_t
$$

The three terms represent: **(a)** total passenger-weighted delay, **(b)** total traction energy consumption, and **(c)** operational disruption cost from rerouting.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Dwell Time and Stop Decisions

**(C1) Dwell time bounds:**
$$
\tau^{\min}_s \cdot \text{stop}_{t,s} \;\le\; d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \;\le\; \tau^{\max}_s \cdot \text{stop}_{t,s}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

**(C2) Mandatory stops:**
$$
\text{stop}_{t,s} \;\ge\; \text{must\_stop}_{t,s}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

**(C3) Delay definition:**
$$
\delta_{t,s} \;\ge\; a_{t,s} - \tau^{\text{arr},0}_{t,s}, \quad \delta_{t,s} \;\ge\; 0, \quad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### 5.2 Speed Dynamics and Position

**(C4) Position update (kinematic recursion):**
$$
p_{t,b,k} \;=\; p_{t,b,k-1} \;+\; v_{t,b,k} \cdot \Delta, \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

**(C5) Boundary positions:**
$$
p_{t,b,0} \;=\; 0, \qquad p_{t,b,|K|} \;=\; L_b \cdot y_{t,b}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B
$$

**(C6) Speed bounds:**
$$
v^{\min} \cdot y_{t,b} \;\le\; v_{t,b,k} \;\le\; v^{\max} \cdot y_{t,b}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

**(C7) Acceleration bounds:**
$$
a^{\min} \cdot \Delta \;\le\; v_{t,b,k} - v_{t,b,k-1} \;\le\; a^{\max} \cdot \Delta, \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

**(C8) Acceleration definition:**
$$
\text{acc}_{t,b,k} \;=\; v_{t,b,k} - v_{t,b,k-1}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

### 5.3 Coupling Between Rescheduling and Speed Management

**(C9) Running time consistency (links schedule to speed profile):**
$$
d_{t,s+1} - d_{t,s} \;=\; \sum_{k \in K} \Delta \cdot \mathbb{1}[v_{t,b,k} > 0], \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B
$$
where $b$ connects $s$ and $s+1$. Linearized as:
$$
d_{t,s+1} - d_{t,s} \;\ge\; \frac{L_b}{v^{\max}} \cdot y_{t,b}, \qquad d_{t,s+1} - d_{t,s} \;\le\; \frac{L_b}{v^{\min}} \cdot y_{t,b} + M(1 - y_{t,b})
$$

**(C10) Origin/destination anchoring:**
$$
d_{t,1} \;\ge\; \tau^{\text{dep},0}_{t,1}, \qquad a_{t,|S|} \;\le\; \tau^{\text{arr},0}_{t,|S|} + D^{\max}_t, \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C11) Total delay:**
$$
D_t \;\ge\; a_{t,|S|} - \tau^{\text{arr},0}_{t,|S|}, \quad D_t \;\ge\; 0, \quad \forall t \in T
$$

### 5.4 Disruption Window Constraints

**(C12) Blocked segment exclusion during disruption window:** For each disrupted segment $b^* \in B^*$ with window $[k_1^{b^*}, k_2^{b^*}]$:
$$
v_{t,b^*,k} \;\le\; M \cdot (1 - \text{track}_{t,b^*}), \quad \forall t \in T,\; k \in [k_1^{b^*}, k_2^{b^*}]
$$
This forces any train on $b^*$ during the disruption to be rerouted ($\text{track}_{t,b^*} = 1$).

**(C13) Reduced speed on disrupted segment:**
$$
v_{t,b^*,k} \;\le\; v^{\max,b^*} + M(1 - y_{t,b^*}), \quad \forall t \in T,\; k \in K
$$

**(C14) Reduced usable length (partial blockage):**
$$
\sum_{k \in K} v_{t,b^*,k} \cdot \Delta \;\le\; (1 - \theta_{b^*}) \cdot L_{b^*} + M(1 - y_{t,b^*}), \quad \forall t \in T
$$

### 5.5 Rerouting Constraints

**(C15) At most one rerouting alternative per train:**
$$
\sum_{a \in A_t} u_{t,a} \;\le\; 1, \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C16) Rerouting activates opposite track:**
$$
\text{track}_{t,b} \;\le\; \sum_{a \in A_t^{b}} u_{t,a} + M(1 - y_{t,b}), \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B^*
$$

**(C17) Rerouting cost:**
$$
R_t \;=\; \sum_{a \in A_t} \rho_a \cdot u_{t,a}, \quad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C18) Rerouting capacity:**
$$
\sum_{t \in T} u_{t,a} \;\le\; \text{cap}_a, \quad \forall a \in \bigcup_{t} A_t
$$

### 5.6 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution on Shared Tracks

**(C19) Ordering exclusivity:**
$$
o_{t,t',b} + o_{t',t,b} \;=\; 1, \quad \forall t, t' \in T,\; t < t',\; b \in B
$$

**(C20) Same-direction headway:**
$$
a_{t',s+1} \;\ge\; a_{t,s+1} + h - M(1 - o_{t,t',b}) - M(2 - y_{t,b} - y_{t',b}), \quad \forall t,t',\; b \in B
$$

**(C21) Bidirectional headway on shared (rerouted) track:** When two trains use the same physical track in opposite directions:
$$
a_{t',s+1} \;\ge\; a_{t,s+1} + h^{\text{bi}} - M(1 - o_{t,t',b}) - M(2 - y_{t,b} - y_{t',b}) - M|\text{track}_{t,b} - \text{track}_{t',b}|
$$
where $h^{\text{bi}} \ge h$ is the stricter bidirectional safety headway. Linearized via auxiliary binaries.

**(C22) No simultaneous occupancy of same physical track:**
$$
\sum_{t \in T} \mathbb{1}[\text{track}_{t,b} = \tau] \cdot y_{t,b} \;\le\; 1, \quad \forall b \in B,\; \tau \in \{0,1\}
$$
Linearized using track-indexed copies of $y_{t,b}$.

### 5.7 SOS2 Piecewise-Linear Approximation of $v^2$

**(C23) Convex combination of speed breakpoints:**
$$
v_{t,b,k} \;=\; \sum_{p \in P} \bar{v}_p \cdot \lambda_{t,b,k,p}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

**(C24) Convex weights sum to one (when segment is used):**
$$
\sum_{p \in P} \lambda_{t,b,k,p} \;=\; y_{t,b}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

**(C25) SOS2 constraint (at most two adjacent $\lambda$ nonzero):**
$$
\{\lambda_{t,b,k,p}\}_{p \in P} \;\in\; \text{SOS2}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

**(C26) Auxiliary squared-speed variable:**
$$
w_{t,b,k} \;=\; \sum_{p \in P} \bar{v}_p^{\,2} \cdot \lambda_{t,b,k,p}, \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K
$$

**(C27) Non-negativity:**
$$
\lambda_{t,b,k,p} \;\ge\; 0, \quad \forall t \in T,\; b \in B,\; k \in K,\; p \in P
$$

### 5.8 Energy Consumption

**(C28) Energy per train:**
$$
E_t \;=\; \sum_{b \in B} \sum_{k \in K} \Delta \cdot \left( c_1 \cdot w_{t,b,k} \;+\; c_2 \cdot v_{t,b,k} \;+\; c_3 \cdot y_{t,b} \right), \quad \forall t \in T
$$

### 5.9 Variable Domains

$$
a_{t,s}, d_{t,s}, \delta_{t,s}, v_{t,b,k}, p_{t,b,k}, w_{t,b,k}, \lambda_{t,b,k,p}, D_t, E_t, R_t \;\ge\; 0
$$
$$
\text{stop}_{t,s}, y_{t,b}, o_{t,t',b}, u_{t,a}, \text{track}_{t,b} \;\in\; \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Linearization Details

| Nonlinear Term | Linearization Technique |
|----------------|------------------------|
| $v_{t,b,k}^2$ | SOS2 piecewise-linear approximation with breakpoints $\{\bar{v}_p\}$; exact at breakpoints, conservative between them |
| $\|v_{t,b,k} - v_{t,b,k-1}\|$ | Replaced by two-sided bound (C7) since acceleration is bounded |
| $\frac{L_b}{v_{t,b,k}}$ | Bounded between $\frac{L_b}{v^{\max}}$ and $\frac{L_b}{v^{\min}}$ using Big-M (C9) |
| $|\text{track}_{t,b} - \text{track}_{t',b}|$ | Linearized via auxiliary binary $\xi_{t,t',b} \ge \text{track}_{t,b} - \text{track}_{t',b}$ and $\xi_{t,t',b} \ge \text{track}_{t',b} - \text{track}_{t,b}$ |
| $\mathbb{1}[v_{t,b,k} > 0]$ | Replaced by $y_{t,b}$ (segment activation) |

---

## 7. Coupling Mechanisms Summary

| Coupling Aspect | Mechanism | Constraints |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| Schedule ↔ Speed | Running time equation | (C4), (C5), (C9) |
| Rerouting ↔ Conflicts | Track assignment + bidirectional headway | (C16), (C21), (C22) |
| Disruption ↔ Rerouting | Forced track switch during window | (C12), (C16) |
| Energy ↔ Delay | Shared speed variables in objective | (C23)–(C28) |
| Dwell ↔ Stop | Binary stop activates dwell bounds | (C1), (C2) |

---

## 8. Key Assumptions

1. **Single bidirectional line** with $|S|-1$ segments; no complex network topology.
2. **Homogeneous fleet**: all trains share the same performance parameters ($v^{\min}, v^{\max}, a^{\min}, a^{\max}$).
3. **Time discretization**: uniform intervals of length $\Delta$; finer $\Delta$ improves accuracy at higher computational cost.
4. **Partial blockage**: fraction $\theta_{b^*}$ of segment $b^*$ is unusable during $[k_1^{b^*}, k_2^{b^*}]$; trains must reroute or wait.
5. **Rerouting alternatives** are pre-enumerated and finite; each has a capacity $\text{cap}_a$.
6. **Energy model**: Davis-type quadratic approximation $E = c_1 v^2 + c_2 v + c_3$, linearized via SOS2.
7. **No regenerative braking** modeled (can be added as a negative $w_{t,b,k}$ term).
8. **Conflicts resolved locally per segment**; no global reordering required.
9. **Minimum headway** $h$ is constant; bidirectional headway $h^{\text{bi}} \ge h$ is stricter.
10. **Big-M values** are problem-specific and should be tightened using segment length and maximum traversal time to strengthen the LP relaxation.

---

## 9. Model Size Estimate

| Component | Approximate Count |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Binary variables | $O(|T| \cdot |B| \cdot |K| + |T|^2 \cdot |B| + |T| \cdot |A|)$ |
| Continuous variables | $O(|T| \cdot |B| \cdot |K| \cdot |P|)$ |
| Constraints | $O(|T| \cdot |B| \cdot |K| \cdot |P| + |T|^2 \cdot |B| \cdot |K|)$ |

This completes the full MILP formulation of the TRSMP, comprising **28 numbered constraints**, a tri-criteria objective, explicit disruption-window modeling, bidirectional conflict resolution on shared tracks, and tight coupling between rescheduling and speed management through time-indexed position and speed variables.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) Under Partial Segment Blockage

Below is a complete mixed-integer linear programming formulation for the integrated TRSMP. The model couples macroscopic rescheduling decisions (arrival/departure times, train ordering, rerouting) with microscopic speed management decisions (speed profiles, accelerations, energy consumption) while explicitly handling bidirectional conflicts on shared track resources during disruption-induced rerouting.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $I$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i \in I$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s \in S$, ordered along the line |
| $K$ | Set of track segments connecting consecutive stations, indexed by $k \in K$ |
| $N$ | Set of discrete time steps, $n = 0, 1, \ldots, N$ |
| $B_k$ | Set of spatial (track) blocks within segment $k$, indexed by $b$ |
| $D = \{\text{F}, \text{B}\}$ | Set of running directions (Forward, Backward) |
| $R_k = K \times D$ | Track resources: pair (segment, direction) |

---

## 2. Parameters

**Time–Space Discretization**
- $\Delta t$: duration of one time step (s)
- $\Delta x$: length of one spatial block (m)
- $L_k = |B_k| \cdot \Delta x$: length of segment $k$ (m)

**Train and Infrastructure Characteristics**
- $m_i$: mass of train $i$ (kg)
- $V^{\max}, V^{\min}$: maximum and minimum allowable speeds (m/s)
- $A^{\max}, B^{\max}$: maximum traction acceleration and braking deceleration (m/s²)
- $c_0, c_1, c_2$: Davis resistance coefficients (N, N·s/m, N·s²/m²)
- $\eta$: overall powertrain efficiency
- $\tau^{\min}, \tau^{\max}$: minimum and maximum dwell times at stations (s)
- $h_s$: minimum departure headway at station $s$ (s)
- $h^{\text{seg}}$: minimum temporal separation between consecutive trains on the same track (s)

**Scheduled Timetable**
- $t_i^{s,\text{sch}}$: scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ (s)
- $x_s$: position (chainage) of station $s$ (m)
- $o_i \in S, \; d_i \in S$: origin and destination of train $i$
- $\text{dir}(i) \in D$: nominal running direction of train $i$

**Disruption Data**
- $K^{\text{dis}} \subseteq K$: set of disrupted segments
- $[T_k^{\text{start}}, T_k^{\text{end}}]$: disruption time window on segment $k \in K^{\text{dis}}$
- $\text{track}^{\text{aff}}(k) \in D$: the blocked (affected) track on segment $k$

**Big-M Constants**
- $M_1, M_2, M_3$: sufficiently large positive constants
- $\varepsilon$: small positive constant

**Objective Weights**
- $w_1, w_2 \geq 0$: weights on total delay and total energy consumption

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Rescheduling (Macroscopic) Variables**
- $t_i^s \in \mathbb{R}_+$: actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ (s)
- $\tau_i^s \in \mathbb{R}_+$: dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ (s)
- $\delta_i^s \in \mathbb{R}_+$: delay of train $i$ at station $s$ (s)
- $y_{i,j}^s \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ departs station $s$ no later than train $j$
- $z_i^k \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $k$
- $r_i^k \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ reroutes onto the opposite track on segment $k$

**Speed Management (Microscopic) Variables**
- $x_i^n \in \mathbb{R}_+$: position of train $i$ at the end of time step $n$ (m)
- $v_i^n \in \mathbb{R}_+$: speed of train $i$ at the end of time step $n$ (m/s)
- $u_i^n \in \mathbb{R}$: acceleration of train $i$ during time step $n$ (m/s²)
- $o_i^{k,d,n} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ occupies track $(k,d)$ during time step $n$
- $e_i \in \mathbb{R}_+$: total energy consumption of train $i$ (kWh)

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; w_1 \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{s \in S} \delta_i^s \;+\; w_2 \sum_{i \in I} e_i \tag{Obj}
$$

The first term captures passenger-oriented service quality (total delay); the second term captures energy efficiency. Setting $w_1 = 1, w_2 = 0$ reduces the model to pure delay-minimizing rescheduling; $w_1 = 0, w_2 = 1$ yields pure energy-efficient speed management.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Dynamics (Kinematic Equations)

For each $i \in I$ and $n \in \{0, 1, \ldots, N-1\}$:

$$
x_i^{n+1} = x_i^n + v_i^n \Delta t + \tfrac{1}{2} u_i^n \Delta t^2 \tag{1a}
$$

$$
v_i^{n+1} = v_i^n + u_i^n \Delta t \tag{1b}
$$

$$
V^{\min} \le v_i^n \le V^{\max} \tag{1c}
$$

$$
-B^{\max} \le u_i^n \le A^{\max} \tag{1d}
$$

### 5.2 Block Occupancy and Movement

For each $i \in I$, $k \in K$, $d \in D$, $n \in N$:

$$
\sum_{d \in D} o_i^{k,d,n} \le 1 \tag{2a}
$$

(Each train occupies at most one track of each segment at any time.)

For each $i \in I$, $n \in N$:

$$
\sum_{k \in K} \sum_{d \in D} o_i^{k,d,n} \;+\; \sum_{s \in S} \sigma_i^{s,n} \;=\; 1 \tag{2b}
$$

where $\sigma_i^{s,n} \in \{0,1\}$ indicates that train $i$ is stopped at station $s$ at time $n$. This ensures the train is always in exactly one location (segment or station).

For each $i \in I$, $k \in K$, $n \in N$:

$$
x_i^n = \sum_{b \in B_k} b \cdot \Delta x \cdot o_i^{k,d_i,n} + \sum_{d \in D} (\text{offset}_k^d) \cdot o_i^{k,d,n} \tag{2c}
$$

(Position is consistent with block occupancy; $\text{offset}_k^d$ is the start chainage of segment $k$ for direction $d$.)

### 5.3 Station Operations

For each $i \in I$ and $s \in S$:

$$
t_i^s \le n \Delta t + M_1 (1 - \sigma_i^{s,n}) \quad \forall n \in N \tag{3a}
$$

$$
t_i^s \ge n \Delta t - M_1 (1 - \sigma_i^{s,n}) \quad \forall n \in N \tag{3b}
$$

$$
\tau_i^{\min} \le \tau_i^s \le \tau_i^{\max} \tag{3c}
$$

$$
\delta_i^s \ge t_i^s - t_i^{s,\text{sch}}, \quad \delta_i^s \ge 0 \tag{3d}
$$

The departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ is $t_i^{s,\text{dep}} = t_i^s + \tau_i^s$.

### 5.4 Train Ordering and Headway at Stations

For each pair $i, j \in I$ with $i \neq j$, and each station $s \in S$:

$$
y_{i,j}^s + y_{j,i}^s = 1 \tag{4a}
$$

$$
t_i^{s,\text{dep}} + h_s \le t_j^{s,\text{dep}} + M_2 (1 - y_{i,j}^s) \tag{4b}
$$

$$
t_j^{s,\text{dep}} + h_s \le t_i^{s,\text{dep}} + M_2 (1 - y_{j,i}^s) \tag{4c}
$$

These enforce that consecutive departures at each station are separated by at least $h_s$.

### 5.5 Track Capacity and Bidirectional Conflict Resolution

For each $(k, d) \in R$ and $n \in N$:

$$
\sum_{i \in I} o_i^{k,d,n} \le 1 \tag{5a}
$$

(No two trains may simultaneously occupy the same track resource.)

For each $i \in I$ and $k \in K$:

$$
\sum_{n \in N} o_i^{k,\text{dir}(i),n} \ge |B_k| \cdot z_i^k (1 - r_i^k) \tag{5b}
$$

$$
\sum_{n \in N} o_i^{k,\bar{d}(i),n} \ge |B_k| \cdot z_i^k \cdot r_i^k \tag{5c}
$$

where $\bar{d}(i)$ is the direction opposite to $\text{dir}(i)$. These ensure that if train $i$ traverses segment $k$ without rerouting, it uses its nominal track; if it reroutes, it uses the opposite track.

### 5.6 Disruption and Rerouting Constraints

For each disrupted segment $k \in K^{\text{dis}}$ and time step $n$ with $n \Delta t \in [T_k^{\text{start}}, T_k^{\text{end}}]$:

$$
o_i^{k,\text{track}^{\text{aff}}(k),n} = 0 \quad \forall i \in I \tag{6a}
$$

(The blocked track is unavailable during the disruption window.)

For each $i \in I$ and $k \in K^{\text{dis}}$:

$$
r_i^k \ge z_i^k - M_3 (1 - \rho_i^k) \tag{6b}
$$

$$
r_i^k \le z_i^k \tag{6c}
$$

$$
r_i^k \le \rho_i^k \tag{6d}
$$

where $\rho_i^k \in \{0,1\}$ indicates whether train $i$ is forced to reroute on segment $k$ (i.e., its path crosses $k$ during the disruption window). Constraint (6b) forces $r_i^k = 1$ whenever the train must traverse the disrupted segment during blockage; otherwise rerouting is optional.

For each $i \in I$ and $k \in K$:

$$
\sum_{d \in D} o_i^{k,d,n} \le z_i^k \quad \forall n \in N \tag{6e}
$$

(Traversing a segment requires the segment to be selected.)

### 5.7 Energy Consumption (Linearized)

The mechanical energy balance for train $i$ over time step $n$ is:

$$
E_i^n = \frac{\Delta t}{\eta} \left[ m_i \, u_i^n \, v_i^n + \left( c_0 + c_1 v_i^n + c_2 (v_i^n)^2 \right) v_i^n \right]
$$

The bilinear term $u_i^n v_i^n$ and the cubic term $(v_i^n)^3$ are linearized using the following auxiliary variables and piecewise-linear (SOS2) approximations:

Introduce $w_i^n = u_i^n v_i^n$ and $q_i^n = (v_i^n)^3$. Replace with:

$$
w_i^n \le V^{\max} u_i^n, \quad w_i^n \ge V^{\min} u_i^n \tag{7a}
$$

$$
w_i^n \le v_i^n A^{\max}, \quad w_i^n \ge v_i^n (-B^{\max}) \tag{7b}
$$

For $q_i^n$, define breakpoints $0 = \bar{v}_0 < \bar{v}_1 < \cdots < \bar{v}_P = V^{\max}$ and SOS2 variables $\lambda_{i,p}^n$:

$$
v_i^n = \sum_{p=0}^{P} \bar{v}_p \lambda_{i,p}^n, \quad
q_i^n = \sum_{p=0}^{P} \bar{v}_p^3 \lambda_{i,p}^n, \quad
\sum_{p=0}^{P} \lambda_{i,p}^n = 1, \quad
\lambda_{i,p}^n \ge 0 \tag{7c}
$$

with the SOS2 constraint that at most two adjacent $\lambda_{i,p}^n$ are nonzero.

Total energy:

$$
e_i = \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} \frac{\Delta t}{\eta} \left[ m_i w_i^n + c_0 v_i^n + c_1 (v_i^n)^2 + c_2 q_i^n \right] \tag{7d}
$$

where $(v_i^n)^2$ is similarly linearized via SOS2 with breakpoints $\bar{v}_p^2$.

### 5.8 Boundary and Initial Conditions

For each $i \in I$:

$$
x_i^0 = x_{o_i}, \quad v_i^0 = 0 \tag{8a}
$$

$$
x_i^N = x_{d_i}, \quad v_i^N = 0 \tag{8b}
$$

$$
\sum_{n \in N} o_i^{k,d,n} \ge |B_k| \cdot z_i^k \quad \forall k \in K, d \in D \tag{8c}
$$

(Every selected segment is fully traversed.)

### 5.9 Coupling Constraints (Rescheduling ↔ Speed Management)

For each $i \in I$ and $s \in S \setminus \{o_i\}$:

$$
t_i^s \ge \frac{x_s - x_{o_i}}{V^{\max}} \tag{9a}
$$

(Minimum running time from origin.)

$$
t_i^s \le \frac{x_s - x_{o_i}}{V^{\min}} + \sum_{s' < s} \tau_i^{s'} \tag{9b}
$$

(Maximum running time, accounting for dwells.)

For each $i \in I$, $k \in K$, $n \in N$:

$$
o_i^{k,d,n} = 1 \Rightarrow x_i^n \in [x_{s_k}, x_{s_{k+1}}] \tag{9c}
$$

(Implemented via big-M constraints linking $o_i^{k,d,n}$ to position bounds.)

---

## 6. Summary of Model Size

| Component | Variable Type | Approximate Count |
|-----------|---------------|-------------------|
| Arrival times $t_i^s$ | Continuous | $|I| \cdot |S|$ |
| Dwell times $\tau_i^s$ | Continuous | $|I| \cdot |S|$ |
| Position $x_i^n$ | Continuous | $|I| \cdot (N+1)$ |
| Speed $v_i^n$ | Continuous | $|I| \cdot (N+1)$ |
| Acceleration $u_i^n$ | Continuous | $|I| \cdot N$ |
| Block occupancy $o_i^{k,d,n}$ | Binary | $|I| \cdot 2|K| \cdot (N+1)$ |
| Ordering $y_{i,j}^s$ | Binary | $|I|^2 \cdot |S|$ |
| Rerouting $r_i^k$ | Binary | $|I| \cdot |K|$ |
| Segment selection $z_i^k$ | Binary | $|I| \cdot |K|$ |
| Energy auxiliaries | Continuous + SOS2 | $\mathcal{O}(|I| \cdot N \cdot P)$ |

---

## 7. Modeling Assumptions

1. **Double-track line with bidirectional traffic.** Each segment has two tracks (one per nominal direction). Under normal operation, trains use their nominal track; rerouting forces them onto the opposite track.
2. **Discrete time–space representation.** Time is discretized into steps of $\Delta t$; space into blocks of $\Delta x$. The discretization is fine enough that a train moves at most one block per time step.
3. **Homogeneous train dynamics.** All trains share the same resistance coefficients and speed/acceleration limits, differing only in mass $m_i$ (readily relaxed by indexing parameters per train).
4. **No train cancellation.** The model focuses on retiming, reordering, and rerouting. Cancellation can be introduced by adding a binary $c_i \in \{0,1\}$ and forcing $z_i^k = 0 \; \forall k$ when $c_i = 1$.
5. **Single disruption event.** One partial blockage affecting a contiguous set of segments over a known time window. Multiple disruptions are handled by replicating the disruption-indexed constraints.
6. **Deterministic demand and rolling stock.** All trains are pre-defined with fixed origin–destination pairs and consist sizes.
7. **Linearized energy model.** The cubic speed term is approximated via SOS2 piecewise-linear functions with $P$ breakpoints; accuracy improves with $P$.
8. **No platform/turnback conflicts.** Station throat capacity is abstracted into the headway parameter $h_s$.
9. **Instantaneous rerouting decision.** Trains commit to a route for the entire segment; partial-segment rerouting can be modeled by splitting segments.
10. **Fixed consist and no coupling/uncoupling operations** during the planning horizon.

---

## 8. Remarks on Tractability

The full MILP is large-scale and typically intractable for real-world instances. The companion paper proposes:
- **Decomposition** into an integer programming (IP) model for train interactions and per-train plans (continuous subproblems).
- **Adaptive iterative refinement** of plan granularity in the neighborhood of the previous solution.
- **Local branching** to accelerate convergence.

These algorithmic enhancements preserve the structure of the MILP above while dramatically reducing the effective search space, enabling solution of large-scale instances that cannot be solved directly by commercial MILP solvers.

# Passenger-Oriented Train Rescheduling MILP Model

Below is a complete Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation for the real-time, passenger-oriented train rescheduling problem in an urban rail transit network. The model extends Liu et al. (2023a) by incorporating (i) time-varying sectional passenger demands, (ii) flexible train composition, and (iii) rolling stock circulation. It is intended to be solved at each MPC step over a rolling prediction horizon.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $I = \{1,\dots,N_T\}$ | Set of trains in the prediction horizon (ordered by departure) |
| $S = \{1,\dots,N_S\}$ | Set of stations, ordered along the line ($s=1$ origin, $s=N_S$ terminal) |
| $L = \{1,\dots,N_S-1\}$ | Set of links/sections between consecutive stations |
| $K = \{1,\dots,N_K\}$ | Set of piecewise-constant demand intervals partitioning the horizon |
| $R = \{1,\dots,N_R\}$ | Set of available rolling-stock units (each unit = one car/train set) |
| $T = \{1,\dots,N_T-1\}$ | Set of consecutive train pairs for headway/circulation constraints |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $\Delta$ | Length of each demand interval ($\Delta = T_{hor}/N_K$) | min |
| $\lambda^{arr}_{s,k}$ | Boarding (arrival) demand rate at station $s$ in interval $k$ | pax/min |
| $\lambda^{dep}_{s,k}$ | Alighting (departure) demand rate at station $s$ in interval $k$ | pax/min |
| $\lambda^{od}_{s,s',k}$ | OD demand from $s$ to $s'$ in interval $k$ (sectional demand) | pax/min |
| $\tau^{run}_s$ | Minimum running time on link $s$ | min |
| $\tau^{dwl,min}_s, \tau^{dwl,max}_s$ | Min/max dwell time at station $s$ | min |
| $h^{min}, h^{max}$ | Min/max headway between consecutive trains | min |
| $\tau^{tb}$ | Minimum turnback time at terminals | min |
| $\bar{a}_{i,s}, \bar{d}_{i,s}$ | Nominal (planned) arrival/departure times | min |
| $cap$ | Passenger capacity of one rolling-stock unit | pax |
| $n^{min}, n^{max}$ | Min/max number of units per train | – |
| $c^{op}_r$ | Operating cost of unit $r$ (coupling, energy, wear) | $/run |
| $e^{rate}$ | Energy consumption per unit running time | kWh/min |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3, w_4$ | Weights for waiting, in-vehicle, operating, deviation costs | – |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) | – |

**Assumption (A1):** The planning horizon is discretized into $N_K$ equal intervals of length $\Delta$, and passenger demand is piecewise constant within each interval.
**Assumption (A2):** All trains run in the same direction on a single line (bidirectional handled by two coupled instances).
**Assumption (A3):** Rolling-stock units are homogeneous in capacity (extension to heterogeneous units is straightforward).

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Timetable variables
- $a_{i,s} \ge 0$: actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $d_{i,s} \ge 0$: actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$.

### 3.2 Discrete (integer) variables
- $x_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ stops at station $s$.
- $z_{i,r} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if rolling-stock unit $r$ is assigned to train $i$.
- $n_i \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: number of units composing train $i$.
- $\delta_{i,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if the departure of train $i$ from station $s$ falls in interval $k$.
- $v_{i,j,r,r'} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if unit $r$ on train $i$ is followed (after turnback) by unit $r'$ on train $j$.

### 3.3 Continuous passenger-flow variables
- $p_{i,s} \ge 0$: passengers on board train $i$ after departing $s$.
- $b_{i,s} \ge 0$: passengers boarding train $i$ at $s$.
- $al_{i,s} \ge 0$: passengers alighting from train $i$ at $s$.
- $w_{i,s,k} \ge 0$: passengers waiting at $s$ in interval $k$ who board train $i$.
- $q_{i,s,s',k} \ge 0$: passengers with OD $(s,s')$ boarding train $i$ in interval $k$.

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; w_1 \underbrace{\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{k\in K} w_{i,s,k}\,\Delta}_{\text{Passenger waiting time}}
\;+\; w_2 \underbrace{\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S} p_{i,s}\,(a_{i,s+1}-d_{i,s})}_{\text{In-vehicle travel time}}
\;+\; w_3 \underbrace{\left(\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{r\in R} c^{op}_r z_{i,r} \;+\; e^{rate}\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S}(a_{i,s+1}-d_{i,s})\right)}_{\text{Operating + energy cost}}
\;+\; w_4 \underbrace{\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s\in S}\left(|a_{i,s}-\bar{a}_{i,s}|+|d_{i,s}-\bar{d}_{i,s}|\right)}_{\text{Timetable deviation}}
$$

**Linearization of absolute values:** introduce $a^+_{i,s}, a^-_{i,s}, d^+_{i,s}, d^-_{i,s} \ge 0$ with
$a_{i,s}-\bar{a}_{i,s}=a^+_{i,s}-a^-_{i,s}$, $d_{i,s}-\bar{d}_{i,s}=d^+_{i,s}-d^-_{i,s}$.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train kinematics and dwell

**(C1) Running time (with stop at next station):**
$$
a_{i,s+1} - d_{i,s} \;\ge\; \tau^{run}_s, \qquad \forall i\in I,\; s\in L
$$

**(C2) Dwell-time bounds (active only if train stops):**
$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \;\ge\; \tau^{dwl,min}_s\, x_{i,s}, \qquad \forall i\in I,\; s\in S
$$
$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \;\le\; \tau^{dwl,max}_s\, x_{i,s}, \qquad \forall i\in I,\; s\in S
$$

**(C3) Origin/terminal stops:**
$$
x_{i,1}=1,\quad x_{i,N_S}=1, \qquad \forall i\in I
$$

### 5.2 Headway and safety

**(C4) Minimum and maximum headway at each station:**
$$
d_{i+1,s} - d_{i,s} \;\ge\; h^{min}, \qquad \forall i\in T,\; s\in S
$$
$$
d_{i+1,s} - d_{i,s} \;\le\; h^{max}, \qquad \forall i\in T,\; s\in S
$$

**(C5) Turnback time at terminals:**
$$
d_{i,1} - a_{i,N_S} \;\ge\; \tau^{tb}, \qquad \forall i\in I
$$

### 5.3 Flexible train composition

**(C6) Number of units equals assigned units:**
$$
n_i \;=\; \sum_{r\in R} z_{i,r}, \qquad \forall i\in I
$$

**(C7) Composition bounds:**
$$
n^{min} \;\le\; n_i \;\le\; n^{max}, \qquad \forall i\in I
$$

**(C8) Each unit assigned to exactly one train:**
$$
\sum_{i\in I} z_{i,r} \;=\; 1, \qquad \forall r\in R
$$

### 5.4 Rolling-stock circulation

**(C9) Coupling of consecutive services of the same physical unit:**
$$
\sum_{j\in I}\sum_{r'\in R} v_{i,j,r,r'} \;=\; z_{i,r}, \qquad \forall i\in I,\; r\in R
$$
$$
\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{r\in R} v_{i,j,r,r'} \;=\; z_{j,r'}, \qquad \forall j\in I,\; r'\in R
$$

**(C10) Sequencing of trains serviced by the same unit (chronological order):**
$$
d_{j,1} - a_{i,N_S} \;\ge\; \tau^{tb} - M\bigl(1-\sum_{r\in R} v_{i,j,r,r}\bigr), \qquad \forall i,j\in I
$$

**Assumption (A4):** A unit may serve at most two consecutive trains within the horizon; longer chains are decomposed iteratively across MPC steps.

### 5.5 Capacity and passenger flow

**(C11) Passenger conservation on board:**
$$
p_{i,s} \;=\; p_{i,s-1} + b_{i,s} - al_{i,s}, \qquad \forall i\in I,\; s\in S\setminus\{1\}
$$
$$
p_{i,1} \;=\; b_{i,1} - al_{i,1}, \qquad \forall i\in I
$$

**(C12) Capacity limit (linear in $n_i$):**
$$
p_{i,s} \;\le\; cap \cdot n_i, \qquad \forall i\in I,\; s\in S
$$

**(C13) Alighting bounded by current load:**
$$
al_{i,s} \;\le\; p_{i,s-1}, \qquad \forall i\in I,\; s\in S\setminus\{1\}
$$

**(C14) OD demand conservation:**
$$
\sum_{i\in I} q_{i,s,s',k} \;\le\; \lambda^{od}_{s,s',k}\,\Delta, \qquad \forall s,s'\in S,\; k\in K
$$
$$
b_{i,s} \;=\; \sum_{s'\in S}\sum_{k\in K} q_{i,s,s',k}, \qquad \forall i\in I,\; s\in S
$$
$$
al_{i,s} \;=\; \sum_{s'\in S}\sum_{k\in K} q_{i',s',s,k}, \qquad \forall i\in I,\; s\in S
$$
where $i'$ denotes the train that carried passengers from $s'$ to $s$ (precomputed via shortest-path routing on the timetable).

### 5.6 Linking timetable to piecewise-constant demand

**(C15) Interval assignment (exactly one interval per stop):**
$$
\sum_{k\in K} \delta_{i,s,k} \;=\; x_{i,s}, \qquad \forall i\in I,\; s\in S
$$

**(C16) Departure time bounded by interval:**
$$
d_{i,s} \;\ge\; (k-1)\Delta \,\delta_{i,s,k}, \qquad \forall i\in I,\; s\in S,\; k\in K
$$
$$
d_{i,s} \;\le\; k\Delta + M(1-\delta_{i,s,k}), \qquad \forall i\in I,\; s\in S,\; k\in K
$$

**(C17) Waiting passengers available in interval $k$:**
$$
w_{i,s,k} \;\le\; \lambda^{arr}_{s,k}\,\Delta\,\delta_{i,s,k} + M(1-\delta_{i,s,k}), \qquad \forall i\in I,\; s\in S,\; k\in K
$$

**(C18) Boarding limited by waiting passengers:**
$$
b_{i,s} \;\le\; \sum_{k\in K} w_{i,s,k}, \qquad \forall i\in I,\; s\in S
$$

### 5.7 Non-negativity and integrality

$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, p_{i,s}, b_{i,s}, al_{i,s}, w_{i,s,k}, q_{i,s,s',k} \ge 0
$$
$$
x_{i,s}, z_{i,r}, \delta_{i,s,k}, v_{i,j,r,r'} \in \{0,1\}, \qquad n_i \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}
$$

---

## 6. Presolve Reductions (model-streaming layer)

Before passing the model to the MILP solver, the following four presolve techniques prune a subset of integer variables (these are *preprocessing* steps, not part of the MILP itself, but they tighten the formulation):

| # | Technique | Effect |
|---|-----------|--------|
| **P1** | *Fixed-stop pruning:* set $x_{i,s}=1$ for all mandatory stops (terminals, transfer stations) and $x_{i,s}=0$ for skip-eligible stations where stopping is infeasible due to headway. | Removes $x_{i,s}$ binaries. |
| **P2** | *Composition bounding:* from demand forecast $\sum_k \lambda^{arr}_{s,k}\Delta$, compute lower bound $\lceil \hat{p}_{i,s}/cap\rceil$ and upper bound $\lfloor \bar{p}_{i,s}/cap\rfloor$; restrict $n_i$ accordingly. | Shrinks $n_i$ domain. |
| **P3** | *Interval collapsing:* merge consecutive intervals $k$ with identical demand rates $\lambda^{arr}_{s,k}=\lambda^{arr}_{s,k+1}$. | Reduces $|\delta_{i,s,k}|$. |
| **P4** | *Circulation fixing:* for units with predetermined next service (from rolling-stock depot plan), fix $v_{i,j,r,r'}$ directly. | Removes circulation binaries. |

After P1–P4, the remaining integer variables are predicted by an LSTM network; the continuous variables are then obtained by solving the MILP with those integers fixed (warm-started LP).

---

## 7. MPC Receding-Horizon Scheme

At MPC step $t$:
1. Observe current state $\bigl(a_{i,s}(t), d_{i,s}(t), p_{i,s}(t)\bigr)$.
2. Forecast demand $\lambda^{arr}_{s,k}, \lambda^{dep}_{s,k}$ over $[t, t+T_{hor}]$.
3. Apply presolve P1–P4 to reduce integer-variable dimension.
4. Use LSTM to predict remaining integer variables $(\hat{x}_{i,s}, \hat{z}_{i,r}, \hat{\delta}_{i,s,k}, \hat{v}_{i,j,r,r'})$.
5. Solve the MILP with integers fixed → obtain continuous timetable $(\hat{a}_{i,s}, \hat{d}_{i,s}, \hat{p}_{i,s})$.
6. Implement the first control action; shift horizon by one sampling period; repeat.

---

## 8. Summary of Assumptions

| ID | Assumption |
|----|-----------|
| A1 | Piecewise-constant demand within each interval $k$. |
| A2 | Single-line, unidirectional operation (bidirectional handled by symmetry). |
| A3 | Homogeneous rolling-stock capacity. |
| A4 | Each unit serves at most two consecutive trains within the horizon. |
| A5 | Dwell time is bounded and proportional to boarding/alighting (constant bounds used here; a more detailed model can make $\tau^{dwl}$ a function of $b_{i,s}, al_{i,s}$ via piecewise-linear approximation). |
| A6 | Energy consumption is linear in running time (a finer model can include regenerative braking and speed profiles). |
| A7 | OD matrix is exogenous and known; routing is deterministic. |
| A8 | No track maintenance or disruption within the horizon (disruptions enter via updated state at the next MPC step). |

This MILP captures all the structural elements described in the paper: time-varying sectional passenger demand (C14–C18), flexible train composition (C6–C8, C12), rolling-stock circulation (C9–C10), and timetable rescheduling (C1–C5), all within a passenger-oriented objective. The presolve layer (P1–P4) and the LSTM-based integer prediction are the learning-augmented components that make the formulation tractable in real time.

# MILP Model for Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## Sets
- **T** = {1, ..., |T|}: set of trains
- **S** = {1, ..., |S|}: set of stations
- **B** = {1, ..., |B|}: set of track blocks
- **K** = {1, ..., |K|}: set of discretized time intervals
- **D** ⊂ **B**: set of disrupted blocks
- **W** ⊂ **K**: disruption time window

## Parameters
- **L_b**: length of block *b* (km)
- **Δ**: duration of each time interval (seconds)
- **v_max, v_min**: maximum/minimum allowed speed (m/s)
- **a_max, d_max**: maximum acceleration/deceleration (m/s²)
- **h_min**: minimum safety headway time (seconds)
- **dwell_min(s), dwell_max(s)**: minimum/maximum dwell time at station *s*
- **t_arr_sched(t,s), t_dep_sched(t,s)**: scheduled arrival/departure times
- **E_0, E_1, E_2**: energy consumption coefficients (auxiliary, linear, quadratic)
- **M**: sufficiently large constant (Big-M)
- **w_delay, w_energy, w_cancel**: objective weights
- **P_t**: cancellation penalty for train *t*
- **direction(t)** ∈ {+1, −1}: direction of train *t*

## Decision Variables
- **x_{t,b,k}** ∈ {0,1}: 1 if train *t* occupies block *b* during interval *k*
- **v_{t,b,k}** ≥ 0: speed of train *t* in block *b* during interval *k* (m/s)
- **a_{t,b,k}** ∈ ℝ: acceleration of train *t* in block *b* during interval *k* (m/s²)
- **e_{t,b,k}** ≥ 0: energy consumption of train *t* in block *b* during interval *k* (kWh)
- **A_{t,s}** ≥ 0: actual arrival time of train *t* at station *s*
- **D_{t,s}** ≥ 0: actual departure time of train *t* at station *s*
- **y_{t,t',b}** ∈ {0,1}: 1 if train *t* precedes train *t'* on block *b*
- **r_{t,b}** ∈ {0,1}: 1 if train *t* uses rerouting on block *b*
- **z_t** ∈ {0,1}: 1 if train *t* is cancelled
- **δ_{t,s}** ≥ 0: delay of train *t* at station *s*

## Objective Function

$$\min Z = w_{delay} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \delta_{t,s} + w_{energy} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{b \in B} \sum_{k \in K} e_{t,b,k} + w_{cancel} \sum_{t \in T} P_t \cdot z_t$$

## Constraints

**1. Block Occupation (one block per interval):**
$$\sum_{b \in B} x_{t,b,k} \leq 1, \quad \forall t \in T, \; k \in K$$

**2. Train Movement Continuity:**
$$x_{t,b,k} + x_{t,b-1,k} + x_{t,b+1,k} \geq x_{t,b,k+1}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K \setminus \{|K|\}$$

**3. Speed Bounds:**
$$v_{min} \cdot x_{t,b,k} \leq v_{t,b,k} \leq v_{max} \cdot x_{t,b,k}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$

**4. Acceleration Bounds:**
$$-d_{max} \cdot \Delta \leq a_{t,b,k} \leq a_{max} \cdot \Delta, \quad \forall t \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$

**5. Kinematic Equation (Speed-Acceleration):**
$$v_{t,b,k+1} = v_{t,b,k} + a_{t,b,k} - M(1 - x_{t,b,k}) - M(1 - x_{t,b,k+1}), \quad \forall t \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K \setminus \{|K|\}$$

**6. Distance Traveled in Block:**
$$\sum_{k \in K} v_{t,b,k} \cdot \Delta \geq L_b \cdot x_{t,b,k}, \quad \forall t \in T, \; b \in B$$

**7. Energy Consumption (linearized via tangent line at v_nom):**
$$e_{t,b,k} \geq E_0 \cdot x_{t,b,k} + E_1 \cdot v_{t,b,k} + E_2 \cdot (2 v_{nom} v_{t,b,k} - v_{nom}^2), \quad \forall t \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$

**8. Arrival Time Definition:**
$$A_{t,s} \geq k \cdot \Delta - M(1 - x_{t,b_s,k}), \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S, \; k \in K$$
$$A_{t,s} \leq k \cdot \Delta + M(1 - x_{t,b_s,k}), \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S, \; k \in K$$

**9. Departure Time Definition:**
$$D_{t,s} \geq A_{t,s} + dwell_{min}(s) - M \cdot z_t, \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S$$
$$D_{t,s} \leq A_{t,s} + dwell_{max}(s) + M \cdot z_t, \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S$$

**10. Dwell Time Bounds:**
$$dwell_{min}(s) \cdot (1 - z_t) \leq D_{t,s} - A_{t,s} \leq dwell_{max}(s) \cdot (1 - z_t), \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S$$

**11. Delay Calculation:**
$$\delta_{t,s} \geq A_{t,s} - t^{sched}_{arr}(t,s) - M \cdot z_t, \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S$$
$$\delta_{t,s} \geq t^{sched}_{arr}(t,s) - A_{t,s} - M \cdot z_t, \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S$$

**12. Same-Direction Headway Constraint:**
$$\sum_{k \in K} k \cdot x_{t,b,k} + h_{min} \leq \sum_{k \in K} k \cdot x_{t',b,k} + M(1 - y_{t,t',b}) + M(1 - y_{t',t,b})$$
$$\forall t, t' \in T, \; t \neq t', \; direction(t) = direction(t'), \; b \in B$$

**13. Bidirectional Conflict (Rerouted Trains):**
$$x_{t,b,k} + x_{t',b,k} \leq 1 + M(1 - r_{t,b}) + M(1 - r_{t',b})$$
$$\forall t, t' \in T, \; direction(t) \neq direction(t'), \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$

**14. Disruption Constraint:**
$$x_{t,b,k} = 0, \quad \forall t \in T, \; b \in D, \; k \in W$$

**15. Rerouting Activation:**
$$r_{t,b} \leq \sum_{k \in W} x_{t,b,k} + M(1 - \sum_{k \in W} x_{t,b,k}), \quad \forall t \in T, \; b \in B$$

**16. Cancellation Logic:**
$$x_{t,b,k} \leq 1 - z_t, \quad \forall t \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$

**17. Train Ordering Consistency:**
$$y_{t,t',b} + y_{t',t,b} = 1, \quad \forall t, t' \in T, \; t \neq t', \; b \in B$$
$$y_{t,t',b} \leq \sum_{k \in K} x_{t,b,k}, \quad y_{t',t,b} \leq \sum_{k \in K} x_{t',b,k}$$

**18. Speed Continuity at Block Transitions:**
$$v_{t,b,k} - v_{t,b+1,k} \leq M(1 - x_{t,b,k}) + M(1 - x_{t,b+1,k})$$
$$v_{t,b+1,k} - v_{t,b,k} \leq M(1 - x_{t,b,k}) + M(1 - x_{t,b+1,k})$$
$$\forall t \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$

**19. Non-negativity:**
$$v_{t,b,k}, e_{t,b,k}, A_{t,s}, D_{t,s}, \delta_{t,s} \geq 0$$

## Key Assumptions
1. **Time discretization**: Time horizon is divided into equal intervals of duration Δ; speed is approximated as piecewise constant within each interval.
2. **Energy model**: Energy consumption is a convex quadratic function of speed, linearized using a tangent-line (supporting hyperplane) approximation at a nominal speed v_nom.
3. **Bidirectional track**: The line consists of two parallel tracks; partial blockage disables one track, allowing rerouting to the opposite track.
4. **Homogeneous trains**: All trains share identical kinematic parameters (acceleration, deceleration, max speed).
5. **Safety headway**: A minimum time separation h_min must be maintained between consecutive trains on the same block.
6. **Bounded dwell times**: Dwell times at stations are constrained within [dwell_min, dwell_max].
7. **Cancellation as last resort**: Trains may be cancelled at a high penalty P_t; cancelled trains occupy no blocks.
8. **Big-M linearization**: All disjunctive (if-then) constraints are linearized using a sufficiently large constant M.
9. **Conflict-free operation**: The model enforces that no two trains (same or opposite direction) occupy the same block at the same time interval, with bidirectional conflicts resolved via the rerouting variables.
10. **Integrated decision-making**: Train times, orders, routes, and speed profiles are optimized simultaneously within a single MILP framework.

Text:
# MILP Formulation for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

Below is the complete mixed-integer linear programming model that integrates train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting) with speed profile optimization for high-speed railway operations under partial segment blockages.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t \in \{1,\dots,\lvert T\rvert\}$ |
| $I$ | Set of blocks/segments along the line, indexed by $i \in \{1,\dots,N\}$ |
| $K$ | Set of discrete time steps, indexed by $k \in \{1,\dots,K\}$ |
| $I_D \subseteq I$ | Set of disrupted blocks |
| $K_D \subseteq K$ | Disruption time window |
| $S \subseteq I$ | Set of stations (subset of blocks) |
| $\text{Dir} = \{U, D\}$ | Travel directions (Up / Down) |
| $T_U, T_D$ | Trains traveling up / down |
| $O_t \in I,\; D_t \in I$ | Origin and destination block of train $t$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description | Unit |
|--------|-------------|------|
| $\Delta t$ | Time step duration | s |
| $L_i$ | Length of block $i$ | m |
| $v_{\max}$ | Maximum allowed speed | m/s |
| $v_{\min}$ | Minimum operating speed | m/s |
| $a_{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration | m/s² |
| $b_{\max}$ | Maximum deceleration | m/s² |
| $P_{\max}$ | Maximum tractive power | W |
| $m_t$ | Mass of train $t$ | kg |
| $c_d$ | Aerodynamic drag coefficient | – |
| $h$ | Minimum headway time | s |
| $d_{\min}, d_{\max}$ | Min/max dwell time at stations | s |
| $\text{schdep}_t, \text{scharr}_t$ | Scheduled departure/arrival of train $t$ | s |
| $w_D, w_E$ | Weights for delay and energy in objective | – |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (Big-M) | – |
| $\varepsilon$ | Small tolerance | – |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Binary Variables

$$
\begin{aligned}
x_{t,i,k} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } t \text{ occupies block } i \text{ at time } k \\
y_{t,i,k} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } t \text{ enters block } i \text{ at time } k \\
z_{t,i,k} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } t \text{ exits block } i \text{ at time } k \\
r_{t,i,k} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } t \text{ uses rerouting on block } i \text{ at time } k \\
o_{t,t',i,k} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } t \text{ precedes train } t' \text{ on block } i \text{ at time } k \\
s_{t,i} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } t \text{ stops at station } i
\end{aligned}
$$

### 3.2 Continuous Variables

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{arr}_{t,i} &\geq 0 && \text{arrival time of train } t \text{ at block } i \\
\text{dep}_{t,i} &\geq 0 && \text{departure time of train } t \text{ from block } i \\
v_{t,i,k} &\geq 0 && \text{speed of train } t \text{ on block } i \text{ at time } k \text{ (m/s)} \\
p_{t,i,k} &\geq 0 && \text{position of train } t \text{ within block } i \text{ at time } k \text{ (m)} \\
e_{t,i,k} &\geq 0 && \text{energy consumption of train } t \text{ on block } i \text{ at time } k \text{ (J)} \\
f_{t,i,k} &\geq 0 && \text{tractive force of train } t \text{ on block } i \text{ at time } k \text{ (N)} \\
\delta_t &\geq 0 && \text{total delay of train } t \text{ (s)} \\
E_{\text{tot}} &\geq 0 && \text{total energy consumption (J)}
\end{aligned}
$$

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; w_D \sum_{t \in T} \delta_t \;+\; w_E \, E_{\text{tot}} \tag{0}
$$

The objective minimizes a weighted sum of total delay across all trains and total energy consumption, balancing punctuality and sustainability.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Block Occupation Flow Conservation

$$
y_{t,i,k} - z_{t,i,k} = x_{t,i,k} - x_{t,i,k-1} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; i \in I,\; k \in K \tag{1}
$$

Ensures that entering/exiting a block matches the change in occupation state.

### 5.2 Single Block Occupation

$$
\sum_{i \in I} x_{t,i,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; k \in K \tag{2}
$$

Each train occupies at most one block at any time step.

### 5.3 Position Update (Linearized via Big-M)

$$
\begin{aligned}
p_{t,i,k} - p_{t,i,k-1} - v_{t,i,k} \Delta t &\leq M(1 - x_{t,i,k}) \\
p_{t,i,k} - p_{t,i,k-1} - v_{t,i,k} \Delta t &\geq -M(1 - x_{t,i,k}) \\
0 \leq p_{t,i,k} &\leq L_i \cdot x_{t,i,k}
\end{aligned}
\quad \forall\, t,i,k \tag{3}
$$

Position evolves only when the train occupies the block; otherwise it remains fixed.

### 5.4 Speed Bounds

$$
0 \leq v_{t,i,k} \leq v_{\max} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; i \in I,\; k \in K \tag{4}
$$

### 5.5 Acceleration / Deceleration Bounds

$$
-b_{\max} \Delta t \leq v_{t,i,k} - v_{t,i,k-1} \leq a_{\max} \Delta t \quad \forall\, t,i,k \tag{5}
$$

### 5.6 Block Entry/Exit Timing

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{arr}_{t,i} &\geq k \Delta t - M(1 - y_{t,i,k}) \\
\text{arr}_{t,i} &\leq k \Delta t + M(1 - y_{t,i,k}) \\
\text{dep}_{t,i} &\geq k \Delta t - M(1 - z_{t,i,k}) \\
\text{dep}_{t,i} &\leq k \Delta t + M(1 - z_{t,i,k})
\end{aligned}
\quad \forall\, t,i,k \tag{6}
$$

Arrival/departure times are anchored to the time step at which the train enters/exits.

### 5.7 Block Traversal Time

$$
\frac{L_i}{v_{\max}} \cdot x_{t,i,k} \leq \text{dep}_{t,i} - \text{arr}_{t,i} \leq \frac{L_i}{v_{\min}} + \varepsilon \quad \forall\, t,i \tag{7}
$$

### 5.8 Dwell Time at Stations

$$
d_{\min} s_{t,i} \leq \text{dep}_{t,i} - \text{arr}_{t,i} \leq d_{\max} s_{t,i} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; i \in S \tag{8}
$$

### 5.9 Headway Constraint (Same Direction, Same Track)

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{arr}_{t,i} - \text{arr}_{t',i} + M(1 - o_{t,t',i}) &\geq h \\
\text{arr}_{t',i} - \text{arr}_{t,i} + M(1 - o_{t',t,i}) &\geq h \\
o_{t,t',i} + o_{t',t,i} &= 1
\end{aligned}
\quad \forall\, t \neq t',\; i \in I \tag{9}
$$

Enforces minimum headway between consecutive trains using ordering variables.

### 5.10 Bidirectional Conflict (Opposite Directions)

$$
x_{t,i,k} + x_{t',i,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall\, t \in T_U,\; t' \in T_D,\; i \in I,\; k \in K \tag{10}
$$

Prevents two trains traveling in opposite directions from occupying the same block at the same time.

### 5.11 Disruption Constraint

$$
x_{t,i,k} \leq r_{t,i,k} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; i \in I_D,\; k \in K_D \tag{11}
$$

If a train passes through a disrupted block during the disruption window, it must use the rerouting option.

### 5.12 Rerouting Capacity on Opposite Track

$$
\sum_{t \in T} r_{t,i,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall\, i \in I_D,\; k \in K_D \tag{12}
$$

At most one rerouted train can use the opposite track within the disruption area at any time.

### 5.13 Delay Calculation

$$
\delta_t \geq \text{arr}_{t,D_t} - \text{scharr}_t \quad \forall\, t \in T \tag{13}
$$

### 5.14 Energy Consumption (Piecewise-Linear Tractive Effort)

$$
\begin{aligned}
f_{t,i,k} &\leq \frac{P_{\max}}{v_{t,i,k} + \varepsilon} \quad \text{(power limit)} \\
f_{t,i,k} &\leq m_t a_{\max} + c_d v_{t,i,k}^2 \quad \text{(force limit)} \\
e_{t,i,k} &\geq f_{t,i,k} \cdot v_{t,i,k} \cdot \Delta t \\
e_{t,i,k} &\geq \tfrac{1}{2} m_t \left( v_{t,i,k}^2 - v_{t,i,k-1}^2 \right) + c_d v_{t,i,k}^2 \Delta t
\end{aligned}
\quad \forall\, t,i,k \tag{14}
$$

Energy accounts for tractive work and kinetic/resistive losses. The bilinear term $f_{t,i,k} v_{t,i,k}$ is approximated by a piecewise-linear function over breakpoints of $v_{t,i,k}$.

### 5.15 Total Energy Aggregation

$$
E_{\text{tot}} = \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{k \in K} e_{t,i,k} \tag{15}
$$

### 5.16 Train Sequence at Each Block

$$
o_{t,t',i,k} + o_{t',t,i,k} = 1 \quad \forall\, t \neq t',\; i \in I,\; k \in K \tag{16}
$$

### 5.17 Departure–Arrival Consistency Between Consecutive Blocks

$$
\text{dep}_{t,i} = \text{arr}_{t,i+1} + \tfrac{d_{\min} + d_{\max}}{2} \cdot s_{t,i+1} \quad \forall\, t,\; i \in I \setminus \{N\} \tag{17}
$$

If the next block is a station, dwell time is added; otherwise the train moves directly.

### 5.18 Initial and Terminal Conditions

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{dep}_{t,O_t} &\geq \text{schdep}_t \quad \forall\, t \in T \tag{18a}\\
\text{arr}_{t,D_t} &\leq K \Delta t \quad \forall\, t \in T \tag{18b}
\end{aligned}
$$

### 5.19 Variable Domains

$$
\begin{aligned}
x_{t,i,k}, y_{t,i,k}, z_{t,i,k}, r_{t,i,k}, o_{t,t',i,k}, s_{t,i} &\in \{0,1\} \\
\text{arr}_{t,i}, \text{dep}_{t,i}, v_{t,i,k}, p_{t,i,k}, e_{t,i,k}, f_{t,i,k}, \delta_t, E_{\text{tot}} &\geq 0
\end{aligned} \tag{19}
$$

---

## 6. Explanation of Model Components

| Component | Role in the Model |
|-----------|-------------------|
| **Block occupation variables** $x_{t,i,k}$ | Encode the spatio-temporal trajectory of each train across the discretized railway network. |
| **Flow conservation (1)** | Guarantees logical consistency between entry, exit, and occupation states. |
| **Position update (3)** | Couples speed and movement, ensuring physical feasibility of motion. |
| **Speed & acceleration limits (4)–(5)** | Enforce kinematic constraints of the rolling stock. |
| **Timing constraints (6)–(8)** | Translate discrete occupation into continuous arrival/departure times and enforce dwell times at stations. |
| **Headway & conflict constraints (9)–(10), (16)** | Guarantee safety by preventing collisions between trains on the same or opposite tracks. |
| **Disruption & rerouting (11)–(12)** | Model the partial blockage and allow trains to use the opposite track, subject to capacity. |
| **Delay (13)** | Measures schedule deviation at the destination. |
| **Energy (14)–(15)** | Captures tractive and resistive energy using a piecewise-linear approximation, enabling MILP solvability. |
| **Objective (0)** | Balances punctuality (delay minimization) and sustainability (energy minimization) through user-defined weights $w_D$ and $w_E$. |

---

## 7. Summary

This MILP jointly optimizes:

1. **Rescheduling** — retiming, reordering, and rerouting decisions through binary variables $x, y, z, r, o, s$.
2. **Speed profile optimization** — continuous variables $v_{t,i,k}$ and $f_{t,i,k}$ subject to kinematic and power constraints.
3. **Conflict-free timetable** — enforced by headway, bidirectional, and rerouting capacity constraints.
4. **Pareto-optimal trade-off** — between delay and energy via the weighted objective.

The formulation is a **mixed-integer linear program** because all nonlinear terms (products of binary and continuous variables, bilinear force–speed terms) have been linearized using Big-M constraints and piecewise-linear approximations, making it directly solvable by standard MILP solvers such as **Gurobi**, **CPLEX**, or **HiGHS**.

Text:
# MILP Model for Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $B$ | Set of track blocks/segments, indexed by $b$ |
| $K$ | Set of discretized time intervals, indexed by $k$ |
| $D$ | Set of directions (up/down), indexed by $d$ |
| $b^*$ | The blocked segment |
| $T_d^s, T_d^e$ | Start and end of disruption time window |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_b$ | Length of block $b$ |
| $v^{max}, v^{min}$ | Maximum and minimum train speeds |
| $a^{max}, d^{max}$ | Maximum acceleration and deceleration |
| $E^{acc}, E^{cruise}, E^{dec}$ | Energy consumption rates |
| $\bar{a}_{i,s}, \bar{d}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival/departure times |
| $\tau^{min}_{i,s}$ | Minimum dwell time at station $s$ |
| $h^{min}$ | Minimum headway time |
| $\Delta t$ | Duration of a time interval |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (Big-M) |
| $\varepsilon$ | Small positive constant |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ | Objective weights |
| $P^{cancel}$ | Cancellation penalty |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Timing variables:**
- $arr_{i,s} \geq 0$: actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $dep_{i,s} \geq 0$: actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $arr^+_{i,s} \geq 0$: positive arrival delay
- $dep^+_{i,s} \geq 0$: positive departure delay

**Order variables:**
- $y_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ departs before train $j$ at station $s$
- $z_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ arrives before train $j$ at station $s$

**Route variables:**
- $r_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses block $b$
- $reroute_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is rerouted during disruption

**Cancellation variables:**
- $cancel_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled

**Speed profile variables:**
- $v_{i,b,k} \in [v^{min}, v^{max}]$: speed of train $i$ on block $b$ at interval $k$
- $pos_{i,b,k} \geq 0$: position of train $i$ on block $b$ at interval $k$
- $acc_{i,b,k} \in [-d^{max}, a^{max}]$: acceleration of train $i$ on block $b$ at interval $k$

**Energy variables:**
- $e_{i,b,k} \geq 0$: energy consumption of train $i$ on block $b$ at interval $k$
- $acc^+_{i,b,k} \in [0, a^{max}]$, $acc^-_{i,b,k} \in [0, d^{max}]$: positive/negative acceleration parts
- $cruise_{i,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cruising on block $b$ at interval $k$

**Conflict variables:**
- $occ_{i,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ occupies block $b$ at interval $k$

## 4. Objective Function

$$\min \; \alpha \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S} arr^+_{i,s} + \beta \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S} dep^+_{i,s} + \gamma \sum_{i \in T} cancel_i \cdot P^{cancel} + \delta \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{b \in B} \sum_{k \in K} e_{i,b,k}$$

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Dwell Time Constraints
$$dep_{i,s} - arr_{i,s} \geq \tau^{min}_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T, \; s \in S$$

### 5.2 Delay Linearization
$$arr^+_{i,s} \geq arr_{i,s} - \bar{a}_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T, \; s \in S$$
$$dep^+_{i,s} \geq dep_{i,s} - \bar{d}_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T, \; s \in S$$

### 5.3 Speed Dynamics
$$v_{i,b,k+1} = v_{i,b,k} + acc_{i,b,k} \cdot \Delta t \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K \setminus \{K\}$$
$$v^{min} \leq v_{i,b,k} \leq v^{max} \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$

### 5.4 Position Dynamics
$$pos_{i,b,k+1} = pos_{i,b,k} + v_{i,b,k} \cdot \Delta t + \frac{1}{2} acc_{i,b,k} \cdot (\Delta t)^2 \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K \setminus \{K\}$$
$$0 \leq pos_{i,b,k} \leq L_b \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$

### 5.5 Block Occupancy (Big-M Linearization)
$$pos_{i,b,k} \leq M \cdot occ_{i,b,k} \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$
$$L_b - pos_{i,b,k} \leq M \cdot occ_{i,b,k} \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$
$$pos_{i,b,k} \geq \varepsilon \cdot occ_{i,b,k} \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$
$$L_b - pos_{i,b,k} \geq \varepsilon \cdot occ_{i,b,k} \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$

### 5.6 Conflict-Free Constraints (Same Direction)
$$occ_{i,b,k} + occ_{j,b,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall i, j \in T, \; i \neq j, \; d_i = d_j, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$

### 5.7 Bidirectional Conflict Constraints (During Rerouting)
$$occ_{i,b,k} + occ_{j,b,k} \leq 1 \quad \forall i, j \in T, \; d_i \neq d_j, \; b \in B, \; k \in [T_d^s, T_d^e]$$

### 5.8 Disruption Constraints
$$r_{i,b^*} + reroute_i \leq 1 \quad \forall i \in T$$
$$r_{i,b^*} \cdot \mathbb{1}[k \in [T_d^s, T_d^e]] \leq 1 - reroute_i \quad \forall i \in T, \; k \in K$$

### 5.9 Train Order Constraints at Stations
$$y_{i,j,s} + y_{j,i,s} = 1 \quad \forall i, j \in T, \; i \neq j, \; s \in S$$
$$z_{i,j,s} + z_{j,i,s} = 1 \quad \forall i, j \in T, \; i \neq j, \; s \in S$$
$$dep_{i,s} + h^{min} \leq dep_{j,s} + M(1 - y_{i,j,s}) \quad \forall i, j \in T, \; i \neq j, \; s \in S$$
$$arr_{i,s} + h^{min} \leq arr_{j,s} + M(1 - z_{i,j,s}) \quad \forall i, j \in T, \; i \neq j, \; s \in S$$

### 5.10 Cancellation Constraints
$$arr_{i,s} \leq M(1 - cancel_i) \quad \forall i \in T, \; s \in S$$
$$dep_{i,s} \leq M(1 - cancel_i) \quad \forall i \in T, \; s \in S$$

### 5.11 Energy Consumption Linearization
$$acc_{i,b,k} = acc^+_{i,b,k} - acc^-_{i,b,k} \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$
$$acc^+_{i,b,k} \leq a^{max} \cdot cruise_{i,b,k} \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$
$$acc^-_{i,b,k} \leq d^{max} \cdot cruise_{i,b,k} \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$
$$e_{i,b,k} = E^{acc} \cdot acc^+_{i,b,k} + E^{cruise} \cdot v_{i,b,k} \cdot cruise_{i,b,k} + E^{dec} \cdot acc^-_{i,b,k} \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B, \; k \in K$$

### 5.12 Route Continuity Constraints
$$\sum_{b \in B} r_{i,b} = |B_i| \quad \forall i \in T$$
where $|B_i|$ is the total number of blocks on train $i$'s path.

### 5.13 Linking Constraints (Timing-Speed)
$$arr_{i,s+1} - dep_{i,s} = \sum_{b \in B} \frac{L_b \cdot r_{i,b}}{\bar{v}_{i,b}} \quad \forall i \in T, \; s \in S$$
where $\bar{v}_{i,b}$ is the average speed derived from the speed profile.

### 5.14 Boundary Conditions
$$pos_{i,b,0} = 0 \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B$$
$$pos_{i,b,|K|} = L_b \cdot r_{i,b} \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B$$
$$v_{i,b,0} = v^{start}_i, \quad v_{i,b,|K|} = v^{end}_i \quad \forall i \in T, \; b \in B$$

### 5.15 Rerouting Constraints
$$reroute_i \leq \sum_{b \in B} r_{i,b} \cdot \mathbb{1}[b = b^*] \quad \forall i \in T$$
$$\sum_{i \in T} reroute_i \leq N^{reroute}_{max}$$

## 6. Assumptions

1. **Time discretization**: The time horizon is discretized into uniform intervals of duration $\Delta t$.
2. **Bidirectional traffic**: Trains operate in two directions (up/down) on a double-track line.
3. **Partial blockage**: During the disruption window $[T_d^s, T_d^e]$, one track of segment $b^*$ is blocked; the opposite track remains available for rerouting.
4. **Conflict-free operation**: No two trains can occupy the same block at the same time interval.
5. **Speed limits**: Trains operate within prescribed speed bounds with bounded acceleration/deceleration.
6. **Energy model**: Energy consumption is decomposed into acceleration, cruising, and deceleration phases with constant rates.
7. **Cancellation**: Trains may be cancelled at a high penalty cost.
8. **Rerouting**: Rerouting is permitted only during the disruption window on the blocked segment.
9. **Headway**: Minimum time separation between consecutive trains at stations is enforced.
10. **Linearization**: Nonlinear terms (e.g., $\max(\cdot, 0)$, absolute values) are linearized using auxiliary variables and Big-M constraints.

Text:
# Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

## Sets and Indices
- $K = \{1, 2, \ldots, |K|\}$: set of trains
- $S = \{1, 2, \ldots, |S|\}$: set of stations (ordered along the line)
- $E = \{1, 2, \ldots, |E|\}$: set of segments between consecutive stations, with $|E| = |S| - 1$
- $T = \{1, 2, \ldots, |T|\}$: set of discrete time steps
- $D = \{1, 2\}$: set of directions (1 = up, 2 = down)

## Parameters
| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_e$ | Length of segment $e$ (km) |
| $v_{\max}$ | Maximum allowed speed (km/h) |
| $a_{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration (km/h per $\Delta t$) |
| $d_{\max}$ | Maximum deceleration (km/h per $\Delta t$) |
| $t^{sched}_{k,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $k$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{\min}, d_{\max}$ | Minimum/maximum dwell time |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum headway time between consecutive trains |
| $[t^{b}_{start}, t^{b}_{end}]$ | Disruption time window |
| $s^{b}$ | Blocked segment |
| $e_{acc}, e_{cru}, e_{brk}$ | Energy rates for acceleration, cruising, braking |
| $\Delta t$ | Time step duration (h) |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (Big-M) |
| $\rho \in [0,1]$ | Weight balancing delay vs. energy |

---

## Decision Variables

**Binary variables:**
- $x_{k,s,t} \in \{0,1\}$: = 1 if train $k$ departs station $s$ at time $t$
- $y_{k,s,t} \in \{0,1\}$: = 1 if train $k$ arrives at station $s$ at time $t$
- $z_{k,e,t} \in \{0,1\}$: = 1 if train $k$ occupies segment $e$ on its **normal** track at time $t$
- $r_{k,e,t} \in \{0,1\}$: = 1 if train $k$ uses the **opposite (rerouted)** track on segment $e$ at time $t$
- $o_{k_1,k_2,s} \in \{0,1\}$: = 1 if train $k_1$ departs station $s$ before train $k_2$
- $c_k \in \{0,1\}$: = 1 if train $k$ is cancelled

**Continuous variables:**
- $arr_{k,s} \geq 0$: arrival time of train $k$ at station $s$
- $dep_{k,s} \geq 0$: departure time of train $k$ from station $s$
- $pos_{k,e,t} \in [0, L_e]$: position of train $k$ on segment $e$ at time $t$ (km from entry)
- $v_{k,e,t} \in [0, v_{\max}]$: speed of train $k$ on segment $e$ at time $t$ (km/h)
- $energy_k \geq 0$: total energy consumption of train $k$
- $delay_{k,s} \geq 0$: delay of train $k$ at station $s$
- $acc_{k,e,t}, brk_{k,e,t} \geq 0$: auxiliary variables for linearized acceleration/braking energy

---

## Objective Function

$$
\min \; \rho \sum_{k \in K} \sum_{s \in S} delay_{k,s} \; + \; (1-\rho) \sum_{k \in K} energy_k
$$

---

## Constraints

### (C1) Arrival–Departure Consistency at Stations
$$
arr_{k,s} \leq dep_{k,s} + M \cdot c_k \quad \forall k \in K,\; s \in S
$$
$$
dep_{k,s} - arr_{k,s} \geq d_{\min} - M \cdot c_k \quad \forall k, s
$$
$$
dep_{k,s} - arr_{k,s} \leq d_{\max} + M \cdot c_k \quad \forall k, s
$$
$$
delay_{k,s} \geq arr_{k,s} - t^{sched}_{k,s} - M \cdot c_k \quad \forall k, s
$$
$$
delay_{k,s} \leq arr_{k,s} - t^{sched}_{k,s} + M \cdot c_k \quad \forall k, s
$$

### (C2) Train Flow Conservation at Stations
$$
\sum_{t \in T} x_{k,s,t} = 1 - c_k \quad \forall k, s
$$
$$
\sum_{t \in T} y_{k,s,t} = 1 - c_k \quad \forall k, s
$$
$$
dep_{k,s} \geq t \cdot x_{k,s,t} \quad \forall k, s, t
$$
$$
dep_{k,s} \leq t \cdot x_{k,s,t} + M(1 - x_{k,s,t}) \quad \forall k, s, t
$$
$$
arr_{k,s} \geq t \cdot y_{k,s,t} \quad \forall k, s, t
$$
$$
arr_{k,s} \leq t \cdot y_{k,s,t} + M(1 - y_{k,s,t}) \quad \forall k, s, t
$$

### (C3) Segment Traversal (Running Time)
For segment $e$ connecting station $s$ to $s+1$, with minimum running time $L_e / v_{\max}$:
$$
dep_{k,s+1} - arr_{k,s} \geq \frac{L_e}{v_{\max}} - M \cdot c_k \quad \forall k, e
$$
$$
dep_{k,s+1} - arr_{k,s} \leq M + M \cdot c_k \quad \forall k, e
$$

### (C4) Speed Profile Dynamics on Segments
$$
v_{k,e,t+1} - v_{k,e,t} \leq a_{\max} \cdot \Delta t + M \cdot c_k \quad \forall k, e, t \in T \setminus \{|T|\}
$$
$$
v_{k,e,t} - v_{k,e,t+1} \leq d_{\max} \cdot \Delta t + M \cdot c_k \quad \forall k, e, t \in T \setminus \{|T|\}
$$
$$
pos_{k,e,t+1} - pos_{k,e,t} = v_{k,e,t} \cdot \Delta t \quad \forall k, e, t \in T \setminus \{|T|\}
$$

### (C5) Segment Entry/Exit Consistency
$$
pos_{k,e,\min(T)} = 0 \quad \forall k, e
$$
$$
pos_{k,e,\max(T)} = L_e \quad \forall k, e
$$

### (C6) Disruption Constraints (Blocked Segment)
During the disruption window, no train may occupy either track of the blocked segment:
$$
z_{k, s^{b}, t} + r_{k, s^{b}, t} \leq M \cdot c_k \quad \forall k \in K,\; t \in [t^{b}_{start}, t^{b}_{end}]
$$

### (C7) Rerouting Constraints
$$
r_{k,e,t} \leq z_{k,e,t} + M \cdot c_k \quad \forall k, e, t
$$
$$
z_{k,e,t} + r_{k,e,t} \leq 1 + M \cdot c_k \quad \forall k, e, t
$$

### (C8) Bidirectional Conflict Resolution (Headway)
At most one train may use the rerouted (opposite) track of a segment at any given time:
$$
\sum_{k \in K} r_{k,e,t} \leq 1 \quad \forall e, t
$$
For any pair of trains on the same normal track at the same time:
$$
z_{k_1,e,t} + z_{k_2,e,t} \leq 1 + M(c_{k_1} + c_{k_2}) \quad \forall e, t,\; (k_1, k_2) \in K \times K,\; k_1 \neq k_2
$$

### (C9) Train Ordering at Stations
$$
o_{k_1,k_2,s} + o_{k_2,k_1,s} = 1 \quad \forall s,\; (k_1, k_2) \in K \times K,\; k_1 \neq k_2
$$
$$
dep_{k_2,s} - dep_{k_1,s} \geq h_{\min} - M(1 - o_{k_1,k_2,s}) - M(c_{k_1} + c_{k_2}) \quad \forall s, k_1 \neq k_2
$$
$$
dep_{k_1,s} - dep_{k_2,s} \geq h_{\min} - M(1 - o_{k_2,k_1,s}) - M(c_{k_1} + c_{k_2}) \quad \forall s, k_1 \neq k_2
$$
$$
arr_{k_2,s} - arr_{k_1,s} \geq h_{\min} - M(1 - o_{k_1,k_2,s}) - M(c_{k_1} + c_{k_2}) \quad \forall s, k_1 \neq k_2
$$
$$
arr_{k_1,s} - arr_{k_2,s} \geq h_{\min} - M(1 - o_{k_2,k_1,s}) - M(c_{k_1} + c_{k_2}) \quad \forall s, k_1 \neq k_2
$$

### (C10) Cancellation
$$
arr_{k,s} \leq M(1 - c_k) \quad \forall k, s
$$
$$
dep_{k,s} \leq M(1 - c_k) \quad \forall k, s
$$

### (C11) Energy Consumption (Linearized)
$$
acc_{k,e,t} - brk_{k,e,t} = v_{k,e,t+1} - v_{k,e,t} \quad \forall k, e, t \in T \setminus \{|T|\}
$$
$$
energy_k = \sum_{e \in E} \sum_{t \in T \setminus \{|T|\}} \left( e_{acc} \cdot acc_{k,e,t} + e_{cru} \cdot v_{k,e,t} - e_{brk} \cdot brk_{k,e,t} \right) \quad \forall k
$$

### (C12) Initial and Boundary Conditions
$$
arr_{k,S_0} \geq t^{sched}_{k,S_0} - M \cdot c_k \quad \forall k
$$
$$
dep_{k,S_{|S|}} \geq t^{sched}_{k,S_{|S|}} - M \cdot c_k \quad \forall k
$$

---

## Key Modeling Assumptions
1. **Discrete time representation** with uniform time step $\Delta t$, allowing linearization of train dynamics.
2. **Double-track line** with one track per direction; rerouting uses the opposite track during disruption.
3. **Linearized train dynamics** via Euler discretization: $pos_{t+1} - pos_t = v_t \cdot \Delta t$.
4. **Energy model** decomposes consumption into traction (acceleration), cruising, and regenerative braking, linearized using auxiliary variables $acc_{k,e,t}, brk_{k,e,t}$.
5. **Big-M relaxation** for all conditional constraints involving cancellation $c_k$.
6. **Single-track rerouting capacity**: at most one train may use the opposite track per segment per time step (preventing head-on collisions between bidirectional trains).
7. **Symmetric headway constraints** at stations for both arrivals and departures enforce conflict-free ordering.
8. **Schedule deviation** is measured only at arrivals ($delay_{k,s} = arr_{k,s} - t^{sched}_{k,s}$), as arrival time is the primary passenger-facing metric.
9. **Position bounds** $pos_{k,e,t} \in [0, L_e]$ ensure physical feasibility on each segment.
10. **Conflict-free operation** is guaranteed jointly by (C8) headway constraints and (C9) station ordering constraints.

constraints.equation: o_{k1,k2,s} + o_{k2,k1,s} = 1; dep_{k2,s} - dep_{k1,s} >= h_min - M(1-o_{k1,k2,s}) - M(c_{k1}+c_{k2}); ... (similar for arr)

constraints.Name: Energy Consumption
constraints.equation: acc_{k,e,t} - brk_{k,e,t} = v_{k,e,t+1} - v_{k,e,t}; energy_k = sum(e_acc*acc + e_cru*v - e_brk*brk)

constraints.Name: Boundary Conditions
constraints.equation: arr_{k,S0} >= t_sched - M*c_k; dep_{k,S|S|} >= t_sched - M*c_k

objective_functions.Name: Minimize delay and energy
objective_functions.description: Weighted sum of total delay and total energy
